**Tafsir of Surat an-Nisa'**

[It is Medinan] [[Addition from manuscript A.]] Al-'Awfi related from Ibn 'Abbas: Surat an-Nisa' was revealed in Medina. Ibn Mardawayh likewise related it from 'Abdullah ibn az-Zubayr and Zayd ibn Thabit. He also related, through the chain of 'Abdullah ibn Lahi'ah, from his brother 'Isa, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: When Surat an-Nisa' was revealed, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "No imprisonment" [[Related by al-Bayhaqi in as-Sunan al-Kubra (6/162), at-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (11/365), and ad-Daraqutni in as-Sunan (4/68), who said: "No one transmitted it with a chain except Ibn Lahi'ah from his brother, and both are weak."]].

Al-Hakim said in his al-Mustadrak: Abu al-'Abbas Muhammad ibn Ya'qub related to us; Abu al-Bakhtari ['Abdullah ibn Muhammad Shakir] [[In manuscripts J and A: "al-Bahtari."]] related to us; Muhammad ibn Bishr al-'Abdi related to us; Mis'ar ibn Kidam related to us, from Ma'n ibn 'Abd ar-Rahman ibn 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, from his father, from 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: Indeed, in Surat an-Nisa' there are five verses that would not please me if I had the world and all that is in it in exchange for them: "Indeed, Allah does not wrong (anyone) by an atom's weight" [the verse], and "If you avoid the major sins that you are forbidden" [the verse], and "Indeed, Allah does not forgive that partners be associated with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills," and "If they, when they wronged themselves, had come to you" [the verse], and "And whoever does evil or wrongs himself and then seeks Allah's forgiveness will find Allah Forgiving and Merciful." Then he said: This is a sound chain if 'Abd ar-Rahman heard from his father, but there is disagreement about that [[al-Mustadrak (2/305).]].

'Abd ar-Razzaq said: Ma'mar informed us, from a man, from Ibn Mas'ud, who said concerning five verses of an-Nisa': They are more beloved to me than the whole world: "If you avoid the major sins that you are forbidden, We will remove from you your misdeeds" and His saying: "And if there is a good deed, He multiplies it," and His saying: "Indeed, Allah does not forgive that partners be associated with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills," and His saying: "And whoever does evil or wrongs himself and then seeks Allah's forgiveness will find Allah Forgiving and Merciful," and His saying: "And those who believe in Allah and His messengers and do not differentiate between any of them—those, He will give them their rewards, and Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful." Ibn Jarir related it. Then he related, through the chain of Salih al-Murri, from Qatadah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Eight verses were revealed in Surat an-Nisa' that are better for this Ummah than everything upon which the sun rises and sets. The first of them: "Allah wants to make clear to you and guide you to the ways of those before you and to turn to you in forgiveness, and Allah is Knowing and Wise." The second: "And Allah wants to turn to you in forgiveness, but those who follow their desires want you to deviate into a great deviation." The third: "Allah wants to lighten [the burden] for you, and mankind was created weak" [[In manuscripts J and A: "for them."]].

Then he mentioned the statement of Ibn Mas'ud in the same manner, meaning regarding the remaining five [[In manuscripts R and A: "the five."]].

Al-Hakim related, through the chain of Abu Nu'aym, from Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah, from 'Ubaydullah [[In manuscript A: "'Abdullah."]] ibn Abi Yazid, from Ibn Abi Mulaykah, who said: I heard Ibn 'Abbas say: Ask me about Surat an-Nisa', for I recited the Qur'an while I was young. Then he said: This is a hadith that is sound according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim), though they did not record it [[al-Mustadrak (2/301).]].

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful

* *

Allah, the Exalted, says, commanding His creation to have taqwa (fear and awareness of Him), which is worshipping Him alone with no partner, and alerting them to His power by which He created them from one soul, which is Adam, peace be upon him, "and created from it its mate," which is Eve, peace be upon her, who was created from his left rib, from behind him while he was sleeping. He awoke and saw her, and she pleased him. He became content with her, and she became content with him.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father related to us; Muhammad ibn Muqatil related to us; Waki' related to us, from Abu Hilal, from Qatadah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The woman was created from the man, so her desire was placed in the man, and the man was created from the earth, so his desire was placed in the earth. So keep your women [confined].

And in the authentic hadith: "Indeed, the woman was created from a rib, and the most crooked part of the rib is its top. If you try to straighten it, you will break it, and if you enjoy her, you enjoy her while there is crookedness in her" [[Related by Muslim in his Sahih, no. (1468), from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him.]].

* *

As for His saying: "And He spread from both of them many men and women," meaning: He brought forth from both of them, that is, from Adam and Eve, many men and women, and dispersed them throughout the regions of the world, with their varied types, attributes, colors, and languages. Then to Him is the return and the gathering after that.

Then Allah, the Exalted, said: "And fear Allah, through whom you ask one another, and [be mindful of] the wombs." That is: fear Allah by obeying Him. Ibrahim, Mujahid, and al-Hasan said: "through whom you ask one another" means, as one says: "I ask you by Allah and by the womb (kinship)." ad-Dahhak said: Fear Allah, through whom you make contracts and covenants, and fear the wombs, that you should not sever them, but rather be dutiful to them and maintain their ties. This was said by Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, al-Hasan, ad-Dahhak, ar-Rabi' and others.

Some of them read: "wal-arhami" [with a kasra, "and the wombs"], in the genitive, as a conjunction with the pronoun in "bihi" [in him/it], meaning: you ask one another by Allah and by the wombs, as Mujahid and others said.

* *

As for His saying: "Indeed, Allah is ever watchful over you," that is: He observes all your deeds and your states, as He said: "And Allah is witness over all things" [al-Buruj: 9].

And in the authentic hadith: "Worship Allah as if you see Him, for if you do not see Him, indeed He sees you" [[Related with this wording by at-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir, and by the Hafiz Ibn 'Asakir in Tarikh Dimashq, as cited in at-Tahdhib (3/106), from the hadith of Abu ad-Darda', may Allah be pleased with him. Perhaps the Hafiz Ibn Kathir intends by this hadith the long hadith of Jibril, which was related by 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, and recorded by Muslim in his Sahih, no. (28), in which: "Inform me about ihsan (excellence). He said: That you worship Allah as if you see Him, for if you do not see Him, indeed He sees you."]]. This is a guidance and a command to be mindful of the Watchful One. For this reason, He, the Exalted, mentioned that the origin of creation is from one father and one mother, so that they might incline toward one another and be compassionate toward their weak ones. It is established in Sahih Muslim, from the hadith of Jarir ibn 'Abdullah al-Bajali, that when that group from Mudar came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, they being "mujtabu an-nimar" (wearing rough, patched cloaks), meaning in their nakedness and poverty, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood up and addressed the people after the noon prayer. In his sermon he said: "O mankind, fear your Lord who created you from one soul" [the verse], until he finished the verse, and he said: "O you who believe, fear Allah, and let every soul look to what it has put forward for tomorrow, and fear Allah" [al-Hashr: 18]. Then he urged them to give charity, saying: "A man gives from his dinar, from his dirham, from his measure of wheat, from his measure of dates..." and he mentioned the rest of the hadith [[Sahih Muslim, no. (1017).]].

Likewise, Imam Ahmad and the authors of the Sunan related it from Ibn Mas'ud in the khutbat al-hajah (the sermon of need), in which he then recites three verses, of which this is one: "O mankind, fear your Lord, who created you from one soul" [the verse] [[al-Musnad (4/358).]].

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 4, verses 2–4 (part 1 of 2):

God commands that the property of orphans be handed over to them in full and intact when they reach maturity (al-hulm), and forbids consuming it or mixing it with their own property. Therefore He said: ﴿And do not substitute the bad with the good.﴾ Sufyan al-Thawri said, from Abu Salih: "Do not hasten to take unlawful provision before the lawful provision that has been decreed for you comes to you."

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "Do not substitute the unlawful from people's property for the lawful from your own property." He means: do not squander your lawful property and consume their unlawful property.

Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab and al-Zuhri said: "Do not give a emaciated (animal) and take a fat one."

Ibrahim al-Nakha'i and al-Dahhak said: "Do not give a counterfeit (coin) and take a good one."

Al-Suddi said: "One of them would take the fat sheep from the orphan's flock and put in its place the emaciated sheep, saying, 'A sheep for a sheep.' He would take the good dirham and throw in its place the counterfeit, saying, 'A dirham for a dirham.'"

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And do not consume their property along with your own property﴾, Mujahid, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Muqatil ibn Hayyan, al-Suddi and Sufyan ibn Husayn said: that is, do not mix them, so that you consume them all together.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Indeed, that is a great sin (hoban kabiran)﴾, Ibn 'Abbas said: that is, a great and momentous sin.

Ibn Mardawayh narrated it from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked about His saying ﴿hoban kabiran﴾, and he said: "A great sin." However, in its isnad is Muhammad ibn Yunus al-Kudaymi, who is weak. [Ibn 'Adi said: he has been accused of fabricating hadith. Ibn Hibban said: he may have fabricated more than a thousand hadiths. Abu 'Ubayd al-Ajurri said: I saw Abu Dawud describe al-Kudaymi as a liar.]

The same was narrated from Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Hasan, Ibn Sirin, Qatadah, al-Dahhak, Muqatil ibn Hayyan, Abu Malik, Zayd ibn Aslam and Abu Sinan, the same as the statement of Ibn 'Abbas.

In the hadith narrated in Sunan Abi Dawud: "Forgive us our hoban (sin) and our errors."

Ibn Mardawayh narrated with his isnad to Wasil, the client of Abu 'Uyaynah, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, from Ibn 'Abbas, that Abu Ayyub divorced his wife, and the Prophet (ﷺ) said to him: "O Abu Ayyub, indeed the divorce of Umm Ayyub was a hoban." Ibn Sirin said: "Al-hoob is sin." [Al-Tabarani narrated it in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (12/196) through Yahya al-Himmani, from Hammad ibn Zayd, from Wasil the client of Abu 'Uyaynah, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, from Ibn 'Abbas, that Abu Ayyub wanted to divorce Umm Ayyub, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed the divorce of Umm Ayyub is a hoob." Ibn Sirin said: "Al-hoob is sin." Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (9/262): "In it is Yahya al-Himmani, who is weak."]

Then Ibn Mardawayh said: Abd al-Baqi narrated to us, Bishr ibn Musa narrated to us, Hawdhah ibn Khalifah informed us, 'Awf informed us, from Anas: that Abu Ayyub wanted to divorce Umm Ayyub, so he asked the permission of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he said: "Indeed the divorce of Umm Ayyub is a hoob, so keep her." [This is mursal (a narration in which the Companion is omitted from the chain). Abu Dawud recorded it in al-Marasil, no. 233, from Wahb ibn Baqiyyah, from Khalid, from 'Awf, from Anas ibn Sirin. Ibrahim al-Harbi recorded it in Gharib al-Hadith, as cited in Takhrij al-Kashshaf of al-Zayla'i (1/279), through Jarir, from Wasil, from Anas ibn Sirin.]

Then Ibn Mardawayh and al-Hakim in his Mustadrak narrated it from the hadith of Ali ibn 'Asim, from Humayd al-Tawil, who said: I heard Anas ibn Malik say: Abu Talhah wanted to divorce Umm Sulaym, and the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Indeed the divorce of Umm Sulaym is a hoob," so he refrained. [Al-Mustadrak (2/302), and from the route of al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan al-Kubra (7/323). Al-Hakim said: sahih (sound). Al-Dhahabi responded: "No, by Allah, in its chain is Ali ibn 'Asim, and he is wahi (very weak)."]

The meaning: indeed your consuming their property together with your property is a great sin and a grave error, so avoid it.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And if you fear that you will not act justly with the orphans, then marry from the women who are lawful for you, two, three or four﴾, that is: if a girl orphan is under the guardianship of one of you and he fears that he will not give her the proper bridal gift (mahr mithlaha), then let him turn to other women, for they are many, and God has not restricted him.

Al-Bukhari said: Ibrahim ibn Musa narrated to us, Hisham narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, Hisham ibn 'Urwah informed me, from his father, from 'Aisha: that a man had an orphan girl under his guardianship, whom he married, and she had a palm grove (adhq), and he would keep her to himself, and she had no say in him. So this was revealed about him: ﴿And if you fear that you will not act justly [with the orphans]﴾. I think he said: she was his partner in that palm grove and in his property.

Then al-Bukhari said: Abd al-'Aziz ibn Abd Allah narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn Sa'd narrated to us, from Salih ibn Kaysan, from Ibn Shihab, who said: 'Urwah ibn al-Zubayr informed me that he asked 'Aisha about the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And if you fear that you will not act justly with the orphans﴾. She said: "O son of my sister, this is the orphan girl who is under the guardianship of her guardian, who shares with him in his property, and he is attracted to her property and her beauty, so her guardian wants to marry her without dealing justly regarding her bridal gift, giving her what others would give her. So they were forbidden to marry them unless they deal justly with them and give them the highest of the customary bridal gifts for women. They were commanded to marry whatever women they liked other than them." 'Urwah said: 'Aisha said: "And the people asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) for a ruling after this verse, so Allah revealed: ﴿And they ask you concerning women﴾." 'Aisha said: The saying of Allah in the other verse: ﴿and you desire to marry them﴾ [al-Nisa': 127] refers to the desire of one of you to turn away from his orphan girl when she is of little property and beauty. So they were forbidden to marry those orphan women whose property and beauty they desired, except with justice, because of their aversion to them when they are of little property and beauty. [Sahih al-Bukhari, nos. 4573, 4574.]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿two, three and four [mathna wa thula waruba']﴾ [Fatir: 1], that is: marry whatever women you wish other than them: if one of you wishes two, or three, or four. Just as He said: ﴿Who made the angels messengers with wings, two, three and four﴾ [Fatir: 1], that is: among them is one with two wings, among them one with three, and among them one with four. This does not negate what is beyond that among the angels, because of the indication of evidence; unlike restricting men to four. From this verse, as Ibn 'Abbas and the majority of scholars said, [the limit of four is derived], because the context is one of favour and permission. Had it been permissible to combine more than four, He would have mentioned it.

Al-Shafi'i said: The Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), which clarifies on behalf of Allah, indicates that it is not permissible for anyone other than the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to combine more than four wives.

What al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, said is agreed upon among the scholars, except for what is reported from a group of the Shi'ah, that it is permissible to combine more than four, up to nine. Some of them said: without limit. Some of them hold on to the action of the Prophet (ﷺ) in combining more than four, up to nine, as established in the two Sahihs. As for eleven, it came in some wordings of al-Bukhari, but al-Bukhari left it as a mu'allaq (a narration with a missing chain at its start). It has been narrated to us from Anas that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) married fifteen women, consummated with thirteen of them, eleven were with him at one time, and he died leaving nine. This, according to the scholars, is one of the special privileges of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) over the rest of the Ummah, because of the hadiths we will mention which indicate the limit of four.

Mention of the hadiths on this:

Imam Ahmad said: Isma'il and Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, both said: Ma'mar narrated to us, from al-Zuhri. Ibn Ja'far said in his narration: Ibn Shihab informed us, from Salim, from his father: that Ghaylan ibn Salamah al-Thaqafi embraced Islam while he had ten wives, and the Prophet (ﷺ) said to him: "Choose four of them." When it was the time of 'Umar, he divorced his wives and divided his property among his sons. This reached 'Umar, who said: "I think that Satan, while eavesdropping, heard of your death and cast it into your soul, and perhaps you will not remain long. By Allah, you must either take back your wives or I will make them inherit from you, and I will command that your grave be stoned, just as the grave of Abu Righal was stoned." [The grave of Abu Righal is in al-Ta'if. Ibn Ishaq narrated that when the Prophet (ﷺ) went out to al-Ta'if, he passed by the grave of Abu Righal and said: "This is the grave of Abu Righal, who was the father of Thaqif, and he was from Thamud, and he was in this sanctuary defending it. When he left it, the punishment that befell his people in this place befell him, and he was buried here." It was also said: Abu Righal was the guide of Abraha on his route to demolish the Ka'bah. Al-Hafiz Ibn Kathir said: The reconciliation between them is that the later Abu Righal shared a name with his great-grandfather, and people stoned him just as they had stoned the first grave. Jarir said: "When al-Farazdaq dies, stone him, as you stoned the grave of Abu Righal." Then he said: The apparent meaning is that it is the second. (al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah, 2/159).]

It was narrated in the same way by al-Shafi'i, al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Majah, al-Daraqutni, al-Bayhaqi and others, from Isma'il ibn 'Ulayyah, Ghundar, Yazid ibn Zurayʻ, Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah, Sufyan al-Thawri, 'Isa ibn Yunus, Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad al-Muharibi, al-Fadl ibn Musa and others among the memorizers of hadith, from Ma'mar, with his isnad, the same, up to his saying: "Choose from them four." The remainder of the hadith, the story of 'Umar, is from the solitary narrations of Ahmad. [Al-Musnad (2/14); al-Shafi'i in al-Umm (5/49); Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 1128; Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 1953; Sunan al-Daraqutni (3/271); Sunan al-Bayhaqi al-Kubra (7/182). Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar elaborated on it in al-Talkhis (3/168), and Shaykh Nasir al-Albani (6/292) judged it sahih.] It is a good additional narration (ziyadah hasanah), and it weakens what al-Bukhari gave as the reason for regarding this hadith as defective, as al-Tirmidhi relayed from him, where he said after narrating it: I heard al-Bukhari say: "This is a hadith that is not preserved (ghayr mahfuz). The correct version is what Shu'ayb and others narrated from al-Zuhri: 'I was told from Muhammad ibn Suwayd al-Thaqafi that Ghaylan ibn Salamah,' and he mentioned it." Al-Bukhari said: "The hadith of al-Zuhri from Salim from his father is only: that a man from Thaqif divorced his wives, and 'Umar said to him: 'You must either take back your wives or I will stone your grave just as the grave of Abu Righal was stoned.'"

This reason (for defect) is open to question, and Allah knows best. 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated it from Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri, as a mursal narration. Likewise Malik narrated it from al-Zuhri as a mursal. Abu Zur'ah said: "And this is more sound." [Ibn Abi Hatim in al-'Ilal (1/400): Abu Zur'ah narrated to me from Abd al-'Aziz al-Uways, from Malik, from al-Zuhri, as a mursal.]

Al-Bayhaqi said: 'Uqayl narrated it from al-Zuhri: "It reached us from Uthman ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Suwayd."

Abu Hatim said: "This is a mistake. It is only al-Zuhri from Uthman ibn Abi Suwayd: 'It reached us that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ),'" and he mentioned it. [Ibn Abi Hatim, al-'Ilal (1/401).]

Al-Bayhaqi said: Yunus and Ibn 'Uyaynah narrated it from al-Zuhri, from Muhammad ibn Abi Suwayd.

This is as al-Bukhari gave its reason. The chain of narration that we cited earlier from the Musnad (the hadith collection of Imam Ahmad, arranged by companion) has narrators who are trustworthy (thiqat), meeting the conditions of the two Sahihs [[In manuscripts J, R, A: "on the condition of the two Shaykhs."]]. Moreover, it has been narrated through a route other than Ma'mar, indeed through al-Zuhri as well. The Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bayhaqi said: Abu 'Abd Allah al-Hafiz informed us, saying: Abu 'Ali [[In A: "Abu Ya'la."]] al-Hafiz told us, saying: Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Nasa'i told us, saying: Abu Burayd 'Amr ibn Yazid al-Jarmi [[In J, A: "Abu Yazid 'Amr ibn Yazid al-Harbi"; in R: "Abu Yazid 'Umar ibn Yazid al-Jarmi."]] informed us, saying: Sayf ibn 'Ubayd [[In J: "'Abd Allah."]] informed us, saying: Sarrar ibn Mujashshir told us, from Ayyub, from Nafi' and Salim, from Ibn 'Umar: that Ghaylan ibn Salama had ten wives, and he embraced Islam and they embraced Islam with him, so the Prophet ﷺ commanded him to choose four of them. Thus al-Nasa'i recorded it in his Sunan. Abu 'Ali ibn al-Sakan said: Sarrar ibn Mujashshir alone narrated it, and he is trustworthy (thiqah), and Ibn Ma'in likewise declared him trustworthy. Abu 'Ali said: Likewise al-Sumay' ibn Wahib [[In J, R, A: "Wahb."]] narrated it from Sarrar.

Al-Bayhaqi said: We have also narrated it from the hadith of Qays ibn al-Harith, or al-Harith ibn Qays, and 'Urwah ibn Mas'ud al-Thaqafi, and Safwan ibn Umayya, meaning the hadith of Ghaylan ibn Salama [[Al-Sunan al-Kubra (7/183). This narration is evidence that Ma'mar did not alone connect it, and it is a good supporting witness for the connection of the hadith.]].

The point of inference is this: if it were permissible to combine more than four, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would have permitted him to keep all of them, since the ten had embraced Islam with him. When he commanded him to retain four and separate from the rest, this shows that combining more than four is not permissible in any circumstance. And if this is so regarding continuing a marriage, then regarding beginning one it is all the more so. And Allah, glorified and exalted, knows best what is correct.

Another hadith on this matter: Abu Dawud and Ibn Majah narrated in their Sunan, by way of Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, from Humayda [[In A: "Humaysa."]] ibn al-Shamardal (in Ibn Majah: "bint al-Shamardal"; Abu Dawud related that some of them say "al-Shamarthal" with a dotted dhal), from Qays ibn al-Harith. In a narration in Abu Dawud: al-Harith ibn Qays ibn 'Umayra al-Asadi, who said: I embraced Islam while I had eight wives, so I mentioned that to the Prophet ﷺ, and he said: "Choose four of them."

This chain is good (hasan), and the mere difference of this kind does not harm it, because the hadith has supporting witnesses [[Sunan Abi Dawud, nos. 2241, 2242; Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 1952. Al-Mizzi preferred that his name is "Qays ibn al-Harith."]].

Another hadith on this matter: The Imam Abu 'Abd Allah Muhammad ibn Idris al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, said in his Musnad: I was informed by one who heard Ibn Abi al-Zinad say: 'Abd al-Majid ibn Suhayl ibn 'Abd al-Rahman informed me, from 'Awf ibn al-Harith, from Nawfal ibn Mu'awiya al-Dili, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: I embraced Islam while I had five wives, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me: "Choose four of them, whichever you wish, and separate from the other," so I went to the eldest of them in companionship, an old barren woman who had been with me for sixty years, and I divorced her [[Musnad al-Shafi'i, no. 1606, and by way of al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan al-Kubra (7/184).]].

All of these are witnesses confirming the soundness of the earlier hadith of Ghaylan, as the Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bayhaqi said, may Allah have mercy on him [[In A: "may Allah's mercy be upon him."]].

* *

His saying: ﴿And if you fear that you will not be just, then only one, or what your right hands possess﴾ means: if you fear, regarding the multiplication of wives, that you will not be equitable among them, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And you will never be able to be equitable among wives, even if you should strive to do so﴾ [An-Nisa: 129]. So whoever fears this should limit himself to one, or to the slave-concubines, for there is no obligation of equal division among them, but it is recommended. Whoever does it, it is good, and whoever does not, there is no blame.

* *

His saying: ﴿That is more suitable that you will not incline toward injustice﴾ Some of them said: [That is] more suitable that your dependents will not become numerous. This was said by Zayd ibn Aslam, Sufyan ibn 'Uyayna and al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on them. This is taken from His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And if you fear poverty [ʿaylah]﴾, meaning poverty, ﴿then Allah will enrich you from His bounty﴾ [At-Tawba: 28]. And the poet said:

"The poor man does not know when his wealth will come, / and the rich man does not know when he will become poor."

The Arabs say: "'Ala al-rajul ya'ilu 'ayla," when he became poor. But in this interpretation there is a point to consider: just as the multiplication of dependents is feared from multiplying free wives, so too it is feared from multiplying slave-concubines. The correct view is that of the majority: ﴿That is more suitable that you will not transgress﴾, meaning: that you will not act unjustly. It is said: "'Ala fi al-hukm" when he deviated, wronged and acted unjustly. Abu Talib said in his famous qasida:

"With a scale of justice that does not cheat by a single barleycorn, / having a witness from itself, not one who deviates."

'Ikrima, may Allah have mercy on him, cited the verse of Abu Talib that we mentioned earlier, but what he recited is as it is transmitted in the biography (sira), and Ibn Jarir narrated it, then recited it correctly and preferred that.

Hushaym narrated from Abu Ishaq, who said: 'Uthman ibn 'Affan wrote to the people of Kufa concerning something they had reproached him for: "I am not a scale that deviates." Ibn Jarir narrated it.

Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh, and Abu Hatim Ibn Hibban in his Sahih narrated by way of 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ibrahim Duhaym, who said: Muhammad ibn Shu'ayb told us, from 'Umar ibn Muhammad ibn Zayd, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar, from Hisham ibn 'Urwa, from his father, from 'A'isha, from the Prophet ﷺ regarding ﴿That is more suitable that you will not transgress﴾, that he said: "Do not be unjust."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father said: This is an erroneous hadith; the correct version is from 'A'isha, as a statement of hers (mawquf) [[Sahih Ibn Hibban, no. 1730 (Mawarid edition).]].

Ibn Abi Hatim also said: It is narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, 'A'isha, Mujahid, 'Ikrima, al-Hasan, Abu Malik, Abu Razin, al-Nakha'i, al-Sha'bi, al-Dahhak, 'Ata' al-Khurasani, Qatada, al-Suddi and Muqatil ibn Hayyan that they said: "do not incline" [[In A: "that you do not incline."]].

* *

His saying: ﴿And give the women their dowries as a gift [nihlah]﴾. 'Ali ibn Abi Talha narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: al-nihlah is the mahr (bridal gift).

Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated from al-Zuhri, from 'Urwa, from 'A'isha: nihlah means an obligation (fari'ah). Muqatil, Qatada and Ibn Juraij said: nihlah means fari'ah. Ibn Juraij added: its specified amount. Ibn Zayd said: In the language of the Arabs, nihlah means what is obligatory. It is said: "Do not marry her except with something obligatory due to her." It is not fitting for anyone after the Prophet ﷺ to marry a woman except with an obligatory dowry, and it is not fitting that naming the dowry be a falsehood without right.

The essence of their words is that a man is obligated to give the dowry to the woman definitively, and that he should do so willingly, just as one gives a gift (manihah) and bestows a nihlah gladly. Likewise he must give his wife her dowry gladly. If she, after it is named, or regarding some portion of it, is pleased to give it to him, then let him consume it as lawful and wholesome. For this reason He, [the Exalted], said: ﴿And if they give you willingly from it, anything of it, then consume it with satisfaction and ease﴾.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn Sinan told us, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi told us, from Sufyan, from al-Suddi, from Ya'qub ibn al-Mughira ibn Shu'ba, from 'Ali, who said: "If one of you complains of something, let him ask his wife for three dirhams or about that, and let him buy with it honey, then take rainwater, and it will come together as wholesome and easy, a blessed healing."

Hushaym said, from Sayyar, from Abu Salih, who said: When a man married off his daughter, he would take her dowry for himself, excluding her; so Allah forbade them from that, and there was revealed: ﴿And give the women their dowries as a gift﴾. Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Jarir narrated it.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Ahmasi told us, Waki' told us, from Sufyan, from 'Umayr al-Khath'ami, from 'Abd al-Malik ibn al-Mughira al-Ta'ifi, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Bayla-mani, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: ﴿And give the women their dowries as a gift﴾. They said: "O Messenger of Allah, then what are the 'ala'iq (ties/obligations) between them?" He said: "What their families agree upon" [[Also narrated by al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan al-Kubra (7/239), Ibn Abi Shayba in al-Musannaf (14/184), and Abu Dawud in al-Maraseel, no. 215.]].

Ibn Mardawayh narrated by way of Hajjaj ibn Artat, from 'Abd al-Malik ibn al-Mughira, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Bayla-mani, from 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ addressed us [[In J, R, A: "addressed us."]] and said: "Marry off the unmarried" three times. A man stood up to him and said: "O Messenger of Allah, what are the 'ala'iq between them?" He said: "What their families agree upon."

Ibn al-Bayla-mani [[In J, R, A: "al-Salmani."]] is weak, and furthermore there is also an interruption (inqita') in it [[Also narrated by Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shayba in al-Musannaf (4/186), Sa'id ibn Mansur in al-Sunan, no. 619 (al-A'zami), and al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan al-Kubra (7/239), all by way of Hajjaj ibn Artat, from 'Abd al-Malik ibn al-Mughira, from 'Abd al-Rahman al-Bayla-mani, mawla of 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, who said: and he mentioned it as a mursal report. I suspect that "mawla" was corrupted in the copies into "'an" ("from"), and I nearly confirm this from the words of the Hafiz Ibn Kathir "there is an interruption," for the interruption is due to its being mursal; had it been from 'Umar it would have been connected (mawsul).]].

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 4, verses 2–4 (part 1 of 2):

God commands that the property of orphans be handed over to them in full and intact when they reach maturity (al-hulm), and forbids consuming it or mixing it with their own property. Therefore He said: ﴿And do not substitute the bad with the good.﴾ Sufyan al-Thawri said, from Abu Salih: "Do not hasten to take unlawful provision before the lawful provision that has been decreed for you comes to you."

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "Do not substitute the unlawful from people's property for the lawful from your own property." He means: do not squander your lawful property and consume their unlawful property.

Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab and al-Zuhri said: "Do not give a emaciated (animal) and take a fat one."

Ibrahim al-Nakha'i and al-Dahhak said: "Do not give a counterfeit (coin) and take a good one."

Al-Suddi said: "One of them would take the fat sheep from the orphan's flock and put in its place the emaciated sheep, saying, 'A sheep for a sheep.' He would take the good dirham and throw in its place the counterfeit, saying, 'A dirham for a dirham.'"

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And do not consume their property along with your own property﴾, Mujahid, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Muqatil ibn Hayyan, al-Suddi and Sufyan ibn Husayn said: that is, do not mix them, so that you consume them all together.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Indeed, that is a great sin (hoban kabiran)﴾, Ibn 'Abbas said: that is, a great and momentous sin.

Ibn Mardawayh narrated it from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked about His saying ﴿hoban kabiran﴾, and he said: "A great sin." However, in its isnad is Muhammad ibn Yunus al-Kudaymi, who is weak. [Ibn 'Adi said: he has been accused of fabricating hadith. Ibn Hibban said: he may have fabricated more than a thousand hadiths. Abu 'Ubayd al-Ajurri said: I saw Abu Dawud describe al-Kudaymi as a liar.]

The same was narrated from Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Hasan, Ibn Sirin, Qatadah, al-Dahhak, Muqatil ibn Hayyan, Abu Malik, Zayd ibn Aslam and Abu Sinan, the same as the statement of Ibn 'Abbas.

In the hadith narrated in Sunan Abi Dawud: "Forgive us our hoban (sin) and our errors."

Ibn Mardawayh narrated with his isnad to Wasil, the client of Abu 'Uyaynah, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, from Ibn 'Abbas, that Abu Ayyub divorced his wife, and the Prophet (ﷺ) said to him: "O Abu Ayyub, indeed the divorce of Umm Ayyub was a hoban." Ibn Sirin said: "Al-hoob is sin." [Al-Tabarani narrated it in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (12/196) through Yahya al-Himmani, from Hammad ibn Zayd, from Wasil the client of Abu 'Uyaynah, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, from Ibn 'Abbas, that Abu Ayyub wanted to divorce Umm Ayyub, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed the divorce of Umm Ayyub is a hoob." Ibn Sirin said: "Al-hoob is sin." Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (9/262): "In it is Yahya al-Himmani, who is weak."]

Then Ibn Mardawayh said: Abd al-Baqi narrated to us, Bishr ibn Musa narrated to us, Hawdhah ibn Khalifah informed us, 'Awf informed us, from Anas: that Abu Ayyub wanted to divorce Umm Ayyub, so he asked the permission of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he said: "Indeed the divorce of Umm Ayyub is a hoob, so keep her." [This is mursal (a narration in which the Companion is omitted from the chain). Abu Dawud recorded it in al-Marasil, no. 233, from Wahb ibn Baqiyyah, from Khalid, from 'Awf, from Anas ibn Sirin. Ibrahim al-Harbi recorded it in Gharib al-Hadith, as cited in Takhrij al-Kashshaf of al-Zayla'i (1/279), through Jarir, from Wasil, from Anas ibn Sirin.]

Then Ibn Mardawayh and al-Hakim in his Mustadrak narrated it from the hadith of Ali ibn 'Asim, from Humayd al-Tawil, who said: I heard Anas ibn Malik say: Abu Talhah wanted to divorce Umm Sulaym, and the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Indeed the divorce of Umm Sulaym is a hoob," so he refrained. [Al-Mustadrak (2/302), and from the route of al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan al-Kubra (7/323). Al-Hakim said: sahih (sound). Al-Dhahabi responded: "No, by Allah, in its chain is Ali ibn 'Asim, and he is wahi (very weak)."]

The meaning: indeed your consuming their property together with your property is a great sin and a grave error, so avoid it.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And if you fear that you will not act justly with the orphans, then marry from the women who are lawful for you, two, three or four﴾, that is: if a girl orphan is under the guardianship of one of you and he fears that he will not give her the proper bridal gift (mahr mithlaha), then let him turn to other women, for they are many, and God has not restricted him.

Al-Bukhari said: Ibrahim ibn Musa narrated to us, Hisham narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, Hisham ibn 'Urwah informed me, from his father, from 'Aisha: that a man had an orphan girl under his guardianship, whom he married, and she had a palm grove (adhq), and he would keep her to himself, and she had no say in him. So this was revealed about him: ﴿And if you fear that you will not act justly [with the orphans]﴾. I think he said: she was his partner in that palm grove and in his property.

Then al-Bukhari said: Abd al-'Aziz ibn Abd Allah narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn Sa'd narrated to us, from Salih ibn Kaysan, from Ibn Shihab, who said: 'Urwah ibn al-Zubayr informed me that he asked 'Aisha about the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And if you fear that you will not act justly with the orphans﴾. She said: "O son of my sister, this is the orphan girl who is under the guardianship of her guardian, who shares with him in his property, and he is attracted to her property and her beauty, so her guardian wants to marry her without dealing justly regarding her bridal gift, giving her what others would give her. So they were forbidden to marry them unless they deal justly with them and give them the highest of the customary bridal gifts for women. They were commanded to marry whatever women they liked other than them." 'Urwah said: 'Aisha said: "And the people asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) for a ruling after this verse, so Allah revealed: ﴿And they ask you concerning women﴾." 'Aisha said: The saying of Allah in the other verse: ﴿and you desire to marry them﴾ [al-Nisa': 127] refers to the desire of one of you to turn away from his orphan girl when she is of little property and beauty. So they were forbidden to marry those orphan women whose property and beauty they desired, except with justice, because of their aversion to them when they are of little property and beauty. [Sahih al-Bukhari, nos. 4573, 4574.]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿two, three and four [mathna wa thula waruba']﴾ [Fatir: 1], that is: marry whatever women you wish other than them: if one of you wishes two, or three, or four. Just as He said: ﴿Who made the angels messengers with wings, two, three and four﴾ [Fatir: 1], that is: among them is one with two wings, among them one with three, and among them one with four. This does not negate what is beyond that among the angels, because of the indication of evidence; unlike restricting men to four. From this verse, as Ibn 'Abbas and the majority of scholars said, [the limit of four is derived], because the context is one of favour and permission. Had it been permissible to combine more than four, He would have mentioned it.

Al-Shafi'i said: The Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), which clarifies on behalf of Allah, indicates that it is not permissible for anyone other than the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to combine more than four wives.

What al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, said is agreed upon among the scholars, except for what is reported from a group of the Shi'ah, that it is permissible to combine more than four, up to nine. Some of them said: without limit. Some of them hold on to the action of the Prophet (ﷺ) in combining more than four, up to nine, as established in the two Sahihs. As for eleven, it came in some wordings of al-Bukhari, but al-Bukhari left it as a mu'allaq (a narration with a missing chain at its start). It has been narrated to us from Anas that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) married fifteen women, consummated with thirteen of them, eleven were with him at one time, and he died leaving nine. This, according to the scholars, is one of the special privileges of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) over the rest of the Ummah, because of the hadiths we will mention which indicate the limit of four.

Mention of the hadiths on this:

Imam Ahmad said: Isma'il and Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, both said: Ma'mar narrated to us, from al-Zuhri. Ibn Ja'far said in his narration: Ibn Shihab informed us, from Salim, from his father: that Ghaylan ibn Salamah al-Thaqafi embraced Islam while he had ten wives, and the Prophet (ﷺ) said to him: "Choose four of them." When it was the time of 'Umar, he divorced his wives and divided his property among his sons. This reached 'Umar, who said: "I think that Satan, while eavesdropping, heard of your death and cast it into your soul, and perhaps you will not remain long. By Allah, you must either take back your wives or I will make them inherit from you, and I will command that your grave be stoned, just as the grave of Abu Righal was stoned." [The grave of Abu Righal is in al-Ta'if. Ibn Ishaq narrated that when the Prophet (ﷺ) went out to al-Ta'if, he passed by the grave of Abu Righal and said: "This is the grave of Abu Righal, who was the father of Thaqif, and he was from Thamud, and he was in this sanctuary defending it. When he left it, the punishment that befell his people in this place befell him, and he was buried here." It was also said: Abu Righal was the guide of Abraha on his route to demolish the Ka'bah. Al-Hafiz Ibn Kathir said: The reconciliation between them is that the later Abu Righal shared a name with his great-grandfather, and people stoned him just as they had stoned the first grave. Jarir said: "When al-Farazdaq dies, stone him, as you stoned the grave of Abu Righal." Then he said: The apparent meaning is that it is the second. (al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah, 2/159).]

It was narrated in the same way by al-Shafi'i, al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Majah, al-Daraqutni, al-Bayhaqi and others, from Isma'il ibn 'Ulayyah, Ghundar, Yazid ibn Zurayʻ, Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah, Sufyan al-Thawri, 'Isa ibn Yunus, Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad al-Muharibi, al-Fadl ibn Musa and others among the memorizers of hadith, from Ma'mar, with his isnad, the same, up to his saying: "Choose from them four." The remainder of the hadith, the story of 'Umar, is from the solitary narrations of Ahmad. [Al-Musnad (2/14); al-Shafi'i in al-Umm (5/49); Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 1128; Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 1953; Sunan al-Daraqutni (3/271); Sunan al-Bayhaqi al-Kubra (7/182). Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar elaborated on it in al-Talkhis (3/168), and Shaykh Nasir al-Albani (6/292) judged it sahih.] It is a good additional narration (ziyadah hasanah), and it weakens what al-Bukhari gave as the reason for regarding this hadith as defective, as al-Tirmidhi relayed from him, where he said after narrating it: I heard al-Bukhari say: "This is a hadith that is not preserved (ghayr mahfuz). The correct version is what Shu'ayb and others narrated from al-Zuhri: 'I was told from Muhammad ibn Suwayd al-Thaqafi that Ghaylan ibn Salamah,' and he mentioned it." Al-Bukhari said: "The hadith of al-Zuhri from Salim from his father is only: that a man from Thaqif divorced his wives, and 'Umar said to him: 'You must either take back your wives or I will stone your grave just as the grave of Abu Righal was stoned.'"

This reason (for defect) is open to question, and Allah knows best. 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated it from Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri, as a mursal narration. Likewise Malik narrated it from al-Zuhri as a mursal. Abu Zur'ah said: "And this is more sound." [Ibn Abi Hatim in al-'Ilal (1/400): Abu Zur'ah narrated to me from Abd al-'Aziz al-Uways, from Malik, from al-Zuhri, as a mursal.]

Al-Bayhaqi said: 'Uqayl narrated it from al-Zuhri: "It reached us from Uthman ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Suwayd."

Abu Hatim said: "This is a mistake. It is only al-Zuhri from Uthman ibn Abi Suwayd: 'It reached us that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ),'" and he mentioned it. [Ibn Abi Hatim, al-'Ilal (1/401).]

Al-Bayhaqi said: Yunus and Ibn 'Uyaynah narrated it from al-Zuhri, from Muhammad ibn Abi Suwayd.

This is as al-Bukhari gave its reason. The chain of narration that we cited earlier from the Musnad (the hadith collection of Imam Ahmad, arranged by companion) has narrators who are trustworthy (thiqat), meeting the conditions of the two Sahihs [[In manuscripts J, R, A: "on the condition of the two Shaykhs."]]. Moreover, it has been narrated through a route other than Ma'mar, indeed through al-Zuhri as well. The Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bayhaqi said: Abu 'Abd Allah al-Hafiz informed us, saying: Abu 'Ali [[In A: "Abu Ya'la."]] al-Hafiz told us, saying: Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Nasa'i told us, saying: Abu Burayd 'Amr ibn Yazid al-Jarmi [[In J, A: "Abu Yazid 'Amr ibn Yazid al-Harbi"; in R: "Abu Yazid 'Umar ibn Yazid al-Jarmi."]] informed us, saying: Sayf ibn 'Ubayd [[In J: "'Abd Allah."]] informed us, saying: Sarrar ibn Mujashshir told us, from Ayyub, from Nafi' and Salim, from Ibn 'Umar: that Ghaylan ibn Salama had ten wives, and he embraced Islam and they embraced Islam with him, so the Prophet ﷺ commanded him to choose four of them. Thus al-Nasa'i recorded it in his Sunan. Abu 'Ali ibn al-Sakan said: Sarrar ibn Mujashshir alone narrated it, and he is trustworthy (thiqah), and Ibn Ma'in likewise declared him trustworthy. Abu 'Ali said: Likewise al-Sumay' ibn Wahib [[In J, R, A: "Wahb."]] narrated it from Sarrar.

Al-Bayhaqi said: We have also narrated it from the hadith of Qays ibn al-Harith, or al-Harith ibn Qays, and 'Urwah ibn Mas'ud al-Thaqafi, and Safwan ibn Umayya, meaning the hadith of Ghaylan ibn Salama [[Al-Sunan al-Kubra (7/183). This narration is evidence that Ma'mar did not alone connect it, and it is a good supporting witness for the connection of the hadith.]].

The point of inference is this: if it were permissible to combine more than four, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would have permitted him to keep all of them, since the ten had embraced Islam with him. When he commanded him to retain four and separate from the rest, this shows that combining more than four is not permissible in any circumstance. And if this is so regarding continuing a marriage, then regarding beginning one it is all the more so. And Allah, glorified and exalted, knows best what is correct.

Another hadith on this matter: Abu Dawud and Ibn Majah narrated in their Sunan, by way of Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, from Humayda [[In A: "Humaysa."]] ibn al-Shamardal (in Ibn Majah: "bint al-Shamardal"; Abu Dawud related that some of them say "al-Shamarthal" with a dotted dhal), from Qays ibn al-Harith. In a narration in Abu Dawud: al-Harith ibn Qays ibn 'Umayra al-Asadi, who said: I embraced Islam while I had eight wives, so I mentioned that to the Prophet ﷺ, and he said: "Choose four of them."

This chain is good (hasan), and the mere difference of this kind does not harm it, because the hadith has supporting witnesses [[Sunan Abi Dawud, nos. 2241, 2242; Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 1952. Al-Mizzi preferred that his name is "Qays ibn al-Harith."]].

Another hadith on this matter: The Imam Abu 'Abd Allah Muhammad ibn Idris al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, said in his Musnad: I was informed by one who heard Ibn Abi al-Zinad say: 'Abd al-Majid ibn Suhayl ibn 'Abd al-Rahman informed me, from 'Awf ibn al-Harith, from Nawfal ibn Mu'awiya al-Dili, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: I embraced Islam while I had five wives, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me: "Choose four of them, whichever you wish, and separate from the other," so I went to the eldest of them in companionship, an old barren woman who had been with me for sixty years, and I divorced her [[Musnad al-Shafi'i, no. 1606, and by way of al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan al-Kubra (7/184).]].

All of these are witnesses confirming the soundness of the earlier hadith of Ghaylan, as the Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bayhaqi said, may Allah have mercy on him [[In A: "may Allah's mercy be upon him."]].

* *

His saying: ﴿And if you fear that you will not be just, then only one, or what your right hands possess﴾ means: if you fear, regarding the multiplication of wives, that you will not be equitable among them, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And you will never be able to be equitable among wives, even if you should strive to do so﴾ [An-Nisa: 129]. So whoever fears this should limit himself to one, or to the slave-concubines, for there is no obligation of equal division among them, but it is recommended. Whoever does it, it is good, and whoever does not, there is no blame.

* *

His saying: ﴿That is more suitable that you will not incline toward injustice﴾ Some of them said: [That is] more suitable that your dependents will not become numerous. This was said by Zayd ibn Aslam, Sufyan ibn 'Uyayna and al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on them. This is taken from His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And if you fear poverty [ʿaylah]﴾, meaning poverty, ﴿then Allah will enrich you from His bounty﴾ [At-Tawba: 28]. And the poet said:

"The poor man does not know when his wealth will come, / and the rich man does not know when he will become poor."

The Arabs say: "'Ala al-rajul ya'ilu 'ayla," when he became poor. But in this interpretation there is a point to consider: just as the multiplication of dependents is feared from multiplying free wives, so too it is feared from multiplying slave-concubines. The correct view is that of the majority: ﴿That is more suitable that you will not transgress﴾, meaning: that you will not act unjustly. It is said: "'Ala fi al-hukm" when he deviated, wronged and acted unjustly. Abu Talib said in his famous qasida:

"With a scale of justice that does not cheat by a single barleycorn, / having a witness from itself, not one who deviates."

'Ikrima, may Allah have mercy on him, cited the verse of Abu Talib that we mentioned earlier, but what he recited is as it is transmitted in the biography (sira), and Ibn Jarir narrated it, then recited it correctly and preferred that.

Hushaym narrated from Abu Ishaq, who said: 'Uthman ibn 'Affan wrote to the people of Kufa concerning something they had reproached him for: "I am not a scale that deviates." Ibn Jarir narrated it.

Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh, and Abu Hatim Ibn Hibban in his Sahih narrated by way of 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ibrahim Duhaym, who said: Muhammad ibn Shu'ayb told us, from 'Umar ibn Muhammad ibn Zayd, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar, from Hisham ibn 'Urwa, from his father, from 'A'isha, from the Prophet ﷺ regarding ﴿That is more suitable that you will not transgress﴾, that he said: "Do not be unjust."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father said: This is an erroneous hadith; the correct version is from 'A'isha, as a statement of hers (mawquf) [[Sahih Ibn Hibban, no. 1730 (Mawarid edition).]].

Ibn Abi Hatim also said: It is narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, 'A'isha, Mujahid, 'Ikrima, al-Hasan, Abu Malik, Abu Razin, al-Nakha'i, al-Sha'bi, al-Dahhak, 'Ata' al-Khurasani, Qatada, al-Suddi and Muqatil ibn Hayyan that they said: "do not incline" [[In A: "that you do not incline."]].

* *

His saying: ﴿And give the women their dowries as a gift [nihlah]﴾. 'Ali ibn Abi Talha narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: al-nihlah is the mahr (bridal gift).

Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated from al-Zuhri, from 'Urwa, from 'A'isha: nihlah means an obligation (fari'ah). Muqatil, Qatada and Ibn Juraij said: nihlah means fari'ah. Ibn Juraij added: its specified amount. Ibn Zayd said: In the language of the Arabs, nihlah means what is obligatory. It is said: "Do not marry her except with something obligatory due to her." It is not fitting for anyone after the Prophet ﷺ to marry a woman except with an obligatory dowry, and it is not fitting that naming the dowry be a falsehood without right.

The essence of their words is that a man is obligated to give the dowry to the woman definitively, and that he should do so willingly, just as one gives a gift (manihah) and bestows a nihlah gladly. Likewise he must give his wife her dowry gladly. If she, after it is named, or regarding some portion of it, is pleased to give it to him, then let him consume it as lawful and wholesome. For this reason He, [the Exalted], said: ﴿And if they give you willingly from it, anything of it, then consume it with satisfaction and ease﴾.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn Sinan told us, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi told us, from Sufyan, from al-Suddi, from Ya'qub ibn al-Mughira ibn Shu'ba, from 'Ali, who said: "If one of you complains of something, let him ask his wife for three dirhams or about that, and let him buy with it honey, then take rainwater, and it will come together as wholesome and easy, a blessed healing."

Hushaym said, from Sayyar, from Abu Salih, who said: When a man married off his daughter, he would take her dowry for himself, excluding her; so Allah forbade them from that, and there was revealed: ﴿And give the women their dowries as a gift﴾. Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Jarir narrated it.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Ahmasi told us, Waki' told us, from Sufyan, from 'Umayr al-Khath'ami, from 'Abd al-Malik ibn al-Mughira al-Ta'ifi, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Bayla-mani, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: ﴿And give the women their dowries as a gift﴾. They said: "O Messenger of Allah, then what are the 'ala'iq (ties/obligations) between them?" He said: "What their families agree upon" [[Also narrated by al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan al-Kubra (7/239), Ibn Abi Shayba in al-Musannaf (14/184), and Abu Dawud in al-Maraseel, no. 215.]].

Ibn Mardawayh narrated by way of Hajjaj ibn Artat, from 'Abd al-Malik ibn al-Mughira, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Bayla-mani, from 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ addressed us [[In J, R, A: "addressed us."]] and said: "Marry off the unmarried" three times. A man stood up to him and said: "O Messenger of Allah, what are the 'ala'iq between them?" He said: "What their families agree upon."

Ibn al-Bayla-mani [[In J, R, A: "al-Salmani."]] is weak, and furthermore there is also an interruption (inqita') in it [[Also narrated by Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shayba in al-Musannaf (4/186), Sa'id ibn Mansur in al-Sunan, no. 619 (al-A'zami), and al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan al-Kubra (7/239), all by way of Hajjaj ibn Artat, from 'Abd al-Malik ibn al-Mughira, from 'Abd al-Rahman al-Bayla-mani, mawla of 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, who said: and he mentioned it as a mursal report. I suspect that "mawla" was corrupted in the copies into "'an" ("from"), and I nearly confirm this from the words of the Hafiz Ibn Kathir "there is an interruption," for the interruption is due to its being mursal; had it been from 'Umar it would have been connected (mawsul).]].

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 4, verses 2–4 (part 1 of 2):

God commands that the property of orphans be handed over to them in full and intact when they reach maturity (al-hulm), and forbids consuming it or mixing it with their own property. Therefore He said: ﴿And do not substitute the bad with the good.﴾ Sufyan al-Thawri said, from Abu Salih: "Do not hasten to take unlawful provision before the lawful provision that has been decreed for you comes to you."

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "Do not substitute the unlawful from people's property for the lawful from your own property." He means: do not squander your lawful property and consume their unlawful property.

Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab and al-Zuhri said: "Do not give a emaciated (animal) and take a fat one."

Ibrahim al-Nakha'i and al-Dahhak said: "Do not give a counterfeit (coin) and take a good one."

Al-Suddi said: "One of them would take the fat sheep from the orphan's flock and put in its place the emaciated sheep, saying, 'A sheep for a sheep.' He would take the good dirham and throw in its place the counterfeit, saying, 'A dirham for a dirham.'"

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And do not consume their property along with your own property﴾, Mujahid, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Muqatil ibn Hayyan, al-Suddi and Sufyan ibn Husayn said: that is, do not mix them, so that you consume them all together.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Indeed, that is a great sin (hoban kabiran)﴾, Ibn 'Abbas said: that is, a great and momentous sin.

Ibn Mardawayh narrated it from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked about His saying ﴿hoban kabiran﴾, and he said: "A great sin." However, in its isnad is Muhammad ibn Yunus al-Kudaymi, who is weak. [Ibn 'Adi said: he has been accused of fabricating hadith. Ibn Hibban said: he may have fabricated more than a thousand hadiths. Abu 'Ubayd al-Ajurri said: I saw Abu Dawud describe al-Kudaymi as a liar.]

The same was narrated from Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Hasan, Ibn Sirin, Qatadah, al-Dahhak, Muqatil ibn Hayyan, Abu Malik, Zayd ibn Aslam and Abu Sinan, the same as the statement of Ibn 'Abbas.

In the hadith narrated in Sunan Abi Dawud: "Forgive us our hoban (sin) and our errors."

Ibn Mardawayh narrated with his isnad to Wasil, the client of Abu 'Uyaynah, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, from Ibn 'Abbas, that Abu Ayyub divorced his wife, and the Prophet (ﷺ) said to him: "O Abu Ayyub, indeed the divorce of Umm Ayyub was a hoban." Ibn Sirin said: "Al-hoob is sin." [Al-Tabarani narrated it in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (12/196) through Yahya al-Himmani, from Hammad ibn Zayd, from Wasil the client of Abu 'Uyaynah, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, from Ibn 'Abbas, that Abu Ayyub wanted to divorce Umm Ayyub, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed the divorce of Umm Ayyub is a hoob." Ibn Sirin said: "Al-hoob is sin." Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (9/262): "In it is Yahya al-Himmani, who is weak."]

Then Ibn Mardawayh said: Abd al-Baqi narrated to us, Bishr ibn Musa narrated to us, Hawdhah ibn Khalifah informed us, 'Awf informed us, from Anas: that Abu Ayyub wanted to divorce Umm Ayyub, so he asked the permission of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he said: "Indeed the divorce of Umm Ayyub is a hoob, so keep her." [This is mursal (a narration in which the Companion is omitted from the chain). Abu Dawud recorded it in al-Marasil, no. 233, from Wahb ibn Baqiyyah, from Khalid, from 'Awf, from Anas ibn Sirin. Ibrahim al-Harbi recorded it in Gharib al-Hadith, as cited in Takhrij al-Kashshaf of al-Zayla'i (1/279), through Jarir, from Wasil, from Anas ibn Sirin.]

Then Ibn Mardawayh and al-Hakim in his Mustadrak narrated it from the hadith of Ali ibn 'Asim, from Humayd al-Tawil, who said: I heard Anas ibn Malik say: Abu Talhah wanted to divorce Umm Sulaym, and the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Indeed the divorce of Umm Sulaym is a hoob," so he refrained. [Al-Mustadrak (2/302), and from the route of al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan al-Kubra (7/323). Al-Hakim said: sahih (sound). Al-Dhahabi responded: "No, by Allah, in its chain is Ali ibn 'Asim, and he is wahi (very weak)."]

The meaning: indeed your consuming their property together with your property is a great sin and a grave error, so avoid it.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And if you fear that you will not act justly with the orphans, then marry from the women who are lawful for you, two, three or four﴾, that is: if a girl orphan is under the guardianship of one of you and he fears that he will not give her the proper bridal gift (mahr mithlaha), then let him turn to other women, for they are many, and God has not restricted him.

Al-Bukhari said: Ibrahim ibn Musa narrated to us, Hisham narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, Hisham ibn 'Urwah informed me, from his father, from 'Aisha: that a man had an orphan girl under his guardianship, whom he married, and she had a palm grove (adhq), and he would keep her to himself, and she had no say in him. So this was revealed about him: ﴿And if you fear that you will not act justly [with the orphans]﴾. I think he said: she was his partner in that palm grove and in his property.

Then al-Bukhari said: Abd al-'Aziz ibn Abd Allah narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn Sa'd narrated to us, from Salih ibn Kaysan, from Ibn Shihab, who said: 'Urwah ibn al-Zubayr informed me that he asked 'Aisha about the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And if you fear that you will not act justly with the orphans﴾. She said: "O son of my sister, this is the orphan girl who is under the guardianship of her guardian, who shares with him in his property, and he is attracted to her property and her beauty, so her guardian wants to marry her without dealing justly regarding her bridal gift, giving her what others would give her. So they were forbidden to marry them unless they deal justly with them and give them the highest of the customary bridal gifts for women. They were commanded to marry whatever women they liked other than them." 'Urwah said: 'Aisha said: "And the people asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) for a ruling after this verse, so Allah revealed: ﴿And they ask you concerning women﴾." 'Aisha said: The saying of Allah in the other verse: ﴿and you desire to marry them﴾ [al-Nisa': 127] refers to the desire of one of you to turn away from his orphan girl when she is of little property and beauty. So they were forbidden to marry those orphan women whose property and beauty they desired, except with justice, because of their aversion to them when they are of little property and beauty. [Sahih al-Bukhari, nos. 4573, 4574.]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿two, three and four [mathna wa thula waruba']﴾ [Fatir: 1], that is: marry whatever women you wish other than them: if one of you wishes two, or three, or four. Just as He said: ﴿Who made the angels messengers with wings, two, three and four﴾ [Fatir: 1], that is: among them is one with two wings, among them one with three, and among them one with four. This does not negate what is beyond that among the angels, because of the indication of evidence; unlike restricting men to four. From this verse, as Ibn 'Abbas and the majority of scholars said, [the limit of four is derived], because the context is one of favour and permission. Had it been permissible to combine more than four, He would have mentioned it.

Al-Shafi'i said: The Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), which clarifies on behalf of Allah, indicates that it is not permissible for anyone other than the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to combine more than four wives.

What al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, said is agreed upon among the scholars, except for what is reported from a group of the Shi'ah, that it is permissible to combine more than four, up to nine. Some of them said: without limit. Some of them hold on to the action of the Prophet (ﷺ) in combining more than four, up to nine, as established in the two Sahihs. As for eleven, it came in some wordings of al-Bukhari, but al-Bukhari left it as a mu'allaq (a narration with a missing chain at its start). It has been narrated to us from Anas that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) married fifteen women, consummated with thirteen of them, eleven were with him at one time, and he died leaving nine. This, according to the scholars, is one of the special privileges of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) over the rest of the Ummah, because of the hadiths we will mention which indicate the limit of four.

Mention of the hadiths on this:

Imam Ahmad said: Isma'il and Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, both said: Ma'mar narrated to us, from al-Zuhri. Ibn Ja'far said in his narration: Ibn Shihab informed us, from Salim, from his father: that Ghaylan ibn Salamah al-Thaqafi embraced Islam while he had ten wives, and the Prophet (ﷺ) said to him: "Choose four of them." When it was the time of 'Umar, he divorced his wives and divided his property among his sons. This reached 'Umar, who said: "I think that Satan, while eavesdropping, heard of your death and cast it into your soul, and perhaps you will not remain long. By Allah, you must either take back your wives or I will make them inherit from you, and I will command that your grave be stoned, just as the grave of Abu Righal was stoned." [The grave of Abu Righal is in al-Ta'if. Ibn Ishaq narrated that when the Prophet (ﷺ) went out to al-Ta'if, he passed by the grave of Abu Righal and said: "This is the grave of Abu Righal, who was the father of Thaqif, and he was from Thamud, and he was in this sanctuary defending it. When he left it, the punishment that befell his people in this place befell him, and he was buried here." It was also said: Abu Righal was the guide of Abraha on his route to demolish the Ka'bah. Al-Hafiz Ibn Kathir said: The reconciliation between them is that the later Abu Righal shared a name with his great-grandfather, and people stoned him just as they had stoned the first grave. Jarir said: "When al-Farazdaq dies, stone him, as you stoned the grave of Abu Righal." Then he said: The apparent meaning is that it is the second. (al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah, 2/159).]

It was narrated in the same way by al-Shafi'i, al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Majah, al-Daraqutni, al-Bayhaqi and others, from Isma'il ibn 'Ulayyah, Ghundar, Yazid ibn Zurayʻ, Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah, Sufyan al-Thawri, 'Isa ibn Yunus, Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad al-Muharibi, al-Fadl ibn Musa and others among the memorizers of hadith, from Ma'mar, with his isnad, the same, up to his saying: "Choose from them four." The remainder of the hadith, the story of 'Umar, is from the solitary narrations of Ahmad. [Al-Musnad (2/14); al-Shafi'i in al-Umm (5/49); Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 1128; Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 1953; Sunan al-Daraqutni (3/271); Sunan al-Bayhaqi al-Kubra (7/182). Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar elaborated on it in al-Talkhis (3/168), and Shaykh Nasir al-Albani (6/292) judged it sahih.] It is a good additional narration (ziyadah hasanah), and it weakens what al-Bukhari gave as the reason for regarding this hadith as defective, as al-Tirmidhi relayed from him, where he said after narrating it: I heard al-Bukhari say: "This is a hadith that is not preserved (ghayr mahfuz). The correct version is what Shu'ayb and others narrated from al-Zuhri: 'I was told from Muhammad ibn Suwayd al-Thaqafi that Ghaylan ibn Salamah,' and he mentioned it." Al-Bukhari said: "The hadith of al-Zuhri from Salim from his father is only: that a man from Thaqif divorced his wives, and 'Umar said to him: 'You must either take back your wives or I will stone your grave just as the grave of Abu Righal was stoned.'"

This reason (for defect) is open to question, and Allah knows best. 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated it from Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri, as a mursal narration. Likewise Malik narrated it from al-Zuhri as a mursal. Abu Zur'ah said: "And this is more sound." [Ibn Abi Hatim in al-'Ilal (1/400): Abu Zur'ah narrated to me from Abd al-'Aziz al-Uways, from Malik, from al-Zuhri, as a mursal.]

Al-Bayhaqi said: 'Uqayl narrated it from al-Zuhri: "It reached us from Uthman ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Suwayd."

Abu Hatim said: "This is a mistake. It is only al-Zuhri from Uthman ibn Abi Suwayd: 'It reached us that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ),'" and he mentioned it. [Ibn Abi Hatim, al-'Ilal (1/401).]

Al-Bayhaqi said: Yunus and Ibn 'Uyaynah narrated it from al-Zuhri, from Muhammad ibn Abi Suwayd.

This is as al-Bukhari gave its reason. The chain of narration that we cited earlier from the Musnad (the hadith collection of Imam Ahmad, arranged by companion) has narrators who are trustworthy (thiqat), meeting the conditions of the two Sahihs [[In manuscripts J, R, A: "on the condition of the two Shaykhs."]]. Moreover, it has been narrated through a route other than Ma'mar, indeed through al-Zuhri as well. The Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bayhaqi said: Abu 'Abd Allah al-Hafiz informed us, saying: Abu 'Ali [[In A: "Abu Ya'la."]] al-Hafiz told us, saying: Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Nasa'i told us, saying: Abu Burayd 'Amr ibn Yazid al-Jarmi [[In J, A: "Abu Yazid 'Amr ibn Yazid al-Harbi"; in R: "Abu Yazid 'Umar ibn Yazid al-Jarmi."]] informed us, saying: Sayf ibn 'Ubayd [[In J: "'Abd Allah."]] informed us, saying: Sarrar ibn Mujashshir told us, from Ayyub, from Nafi' and Salim, from Ibn 'Umar: that Ghaylan ibn Salama had ten wives, and he embraced Islam and they embraced Islam with him, so the Prophet ﷺ commanded him to choose four of them. Thus al-Nasa'i recorded it in his Sunan. Abu 'Ali ibn al-Sakan said: Sarrar ibn Mujashshir alone narrated it, and he is trustworthy (thiqah), and Ibn Ma'in likewise declared him trustworthy. Abu 'Ali said: Likewise al-Sumay' ibn Wahib [[In J, R, A: "Wahb."]] narrated it from Sarrar.

Al-Bayhaqi said: We have also narrated it from the hadith of Qays ibn al-Harith, or al-Harith ibn Qays, and 'Urwah ibn Mas'ud al-Thaqafi, and Safwan ibn Umayya, meaning the hadith of Ghaylan ibn Salama [[Al-Sunan al-Kubra (7/183). This narration is evidence that Ma'mar did not alone connect it, and it is a good supporting witness for the connection of the hadith.]].

The point of inference is this: if it were permissible to combine more than four, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would have permitted him to keep all of them, since the ten had embraced Islam with him. When he commanded him to retain four and separate from the rest, this shows that combining more than four is not permissible in any circumstance. And if this is so regarding continuing a marriage, then regarding beginning one it is all the more so. And Allah, glorified and exalted, knows best what is correct.

Another hadith on this matter: Abu Dawud and Ibn Majah narrated in their Sunan, by way of Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, from Humayda [[In A: "Humaysa."]] ibn al-Shamardal (in Ibn Majah: "bint al-Shamardal"; Abu Dawud related that some of them say "al-Shamarthal" with a dotted dhal), from Qays ibn al-Harith. In a narration in Abu Dawud: al-Harith ibn Qays ibn 'Umayra al-Asadi, who said: I embraced Islam while I had eight wives, so I mentioned that to the Prophet ﷺ, and he said: "Choose four of them."

This chain is good (hasan), and the mere difference of this kind does not harm it, because the hadith has supporting witnesses [[Sunan Abi Dawud, nos. 2241, 2242; Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 1952. Al-Mizzi preferred that his name is "Qays ibn al-Harith."]].

Another hadith on this matter: The Imam Abu 'Abd Allah Muhammad ibn Idris al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, said in his Musnad: I was informed by one who heard Ibn Abi al-Zinad say: 'Abd al-Majid ibn Suhayl ibn 'Abd al-Rahman informed me, from 'Awf ibn al-Harith, from Nawfal ibn Mu'awiya al-Dili, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: I embraced Islam while I had five wives, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me: "Choose four of them, whichever you wish, and separate from the other," so I went to the eldest of them in companionship, an old barren woman who had been with me for sixty years, and I divorced her [[Musnad al-Shafi'i, no. 1606, and by way of al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan al-Kubra (7/184).]].

All of these are witnesses confirming the soundness of the earlier hadith of Ghaylan, as the Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bayhaqi said, may Allah have mercy on him [[In A: "may Allah's mercy be upon him."]].

* *

His saying: ﴿And if you fear that you will not be just, then only one, or what your right hands possess﴾ means: if you fear, regarding the multiplication of wives, that you will not be equitable among them, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And you will never be able to be equitable among wives, even if you should strive to do so﴾ [An-Nisa: 129]. So whoever fears this should limit himself to one, or to the slave-concubines, for there is no obligation of equal division among them, but it is recommended. Whoever does it, it is good, and whoever does not, there is no blame.

* *

His saying: ﴿That is more suitable that you will not incline toward injustice﴾ Some of them said: [That is] more suitable that your dependents will not become numerous. This was said by Zayd ibn Aslam, Sufyan ibn 'Uyayna and al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on them. This is taken from His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And if you fear poverty [ʿaylah]﴾, meaning poverty, ﴿then Allah will enrich you from His bounty﴾ [At-Tawba: 28]. And the poet said:

"The poor man does not know when his wealth will come, / and the rich man does not know when he will become poor."

The Arabs say: "'Ala al-rajul ya'ilu 'ayla," when he became poor. But in this interpretation there is a point to consider: just as the multiplication of dependents is feared from multiplying free wives, so too it is feared from multiplying slave-concubines. The correct view is that of the majority: ﴿That is more suitable that you will not transgress﴾, meaning: that you will not act unjustly. It is said: "'Ala fi al-hukm" when he deviated, wronged and acted unjustly. Abu Talib said in his famous qasida:

"With a scale of justice that does not cheat by a single barleycorn, / having a witness from itself, not one who deviates."

'Ikrima, may Allah have mercy on him, cited the verse of Abu Talib that we mentioned earlier, but what he recited is as it is transmitted in the biography (sira), and Ibn Jarir narrated it, then recited it correctly and preferred that.

Hushaym narrated from Abu Ishaq, who said: 'Uthman ibn 'Affan wrote to the people of Kufa concerning something they had reproached him for: "I am not a scale that deviates." Ibn Jarir narrated it.

Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh, and Abu Hatim Ibn Hibban in his Sahih narrated by way of 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ibrahim Duhaym, who said: Muhammad ibn Shu'ayb told us, from 'Umar ibn Muhammad ibn Zayd, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar, from Hisham ibn 'Urwa, from his father, from 'A'isha, from the Prophet ﷺ regarding ﴿That is more suitable that you will not transgress﴾, that he said: "Do not be unjust."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father said: This is an erroneous hadith; the correct version is from 'A'isha, as a statement of hers (mawquf) [[Sahih Ibn Hibban, no. 1730 (Mawarid edition).]].

Ibn Abi Hatim also said: It is narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, 'A'isha, Mujahid, 'Ikrima, al-Hasan, Abu Malik, Abu Razin, al-Nakha'i, al-Sha'bi, al-Dahhak, 'Ata' al-Khurasani, Qatada, al-Suddi and Muqatil ibn Hayyan that they said: "do not incline" [[In A: "that you do not incline."]].

* *

His saying: ﴿And give the women their dowries as a gift [nihlah]﴾. 'Ali ibn Abi Talha narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: al-nihlah is the mahr (bridal gift).

Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated from al-Zuhri, from 'Urwa, from 'A'isha: nihlah means an obligation (fari'ah). Muqatil, Qatada and Ibn Juraij said: nihlah means fari'ah. Ibn Juraij added: its specified amount. Ibn Zayd said: In the language of the Arabs, nihlah means what is obligatory. It is said: "Do not marry her except with something obligatory due to her." It is not fitting for anyone after the Prophet ﷺ to marry a woman except with an obligatory dowry, and it is not fitting that naming the dowry be a falsehood without right.

The essence of their words is that a man is obligated to give the dowry to the woman definitively, and that he should do so willingly, just as one gives a gift (manihah) and bestows a nihlah gladly. Likewise he must give his wife her dowry gladly. If she, after it is named, or regarding some portion of it, is pleased to give it to him, then let him consume it as lawful and wholesome. For this reason He, [the Exalted], said: ﴿And if they give you willingly from it, anything of it, then consume it with satisfaction and ease﴾.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn Sinan told us, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi told us, from Sufyan, from al-Suddi, from Ya'qub ibn al-Mughira ibn Shu'ba, from 'Ali, who said: "If one of you complains of something, let him ask his wife for three dirhams or about that, and let him buy with it honey, then take rainwater, and it will come together as wholesome and easy, a blessed healing."

Hushaym said, from Sayyar, from Abu Salih, who said: When a man married off his daughter, he would take her dowry for himself, excluding her; so Allah forbade them from that, and there was revealed: ﴿And give the women their dowries as a gift﴾. Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Jarir narrated it.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Ahmasi told us, Waki' told us, from Sufyan, from 'Umayr al-Khath'ami, from 'Abd al-Malik ibn al-Mughira al-Ta'ifi, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Bayla-mani, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: ﴿And give the women their dowries as a gift﴾. They said: "O Messenger of Allah, then what are the 'ala'iq (ties/obligations) between them?" He said: "What their families agree upon" [[Also narrated by al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan al-Kubra (7/239), Ibn Abi Shayba in al-Musannaf (14/184), and Abu Dawud in al-Maraseel, no. 215.]].

Ibn Mardawayh narrated by way of Hajjaj ibn Artat, from 'Abd al-Malik ibn al-Mughira, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Bayla-mani, from 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ addressed us [[In J, R, A: "addressed us."]] and said: "Marry off the unmarried" three times. A man stood up to him and said: "O Messenger of Allah, what are the 'ala'iq between them?" He said: "What their families agree upon."

Ibn al-Bayla-mani [[In J, R, A: "al-Salmani."]] is weak, and furthermore there is also an interruption (inqita') in it [[Also narrated by Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shayba in al-Musannaf (4/186), Sa'id ibn Mansur in al-Sunan, no. 619 (al-A'zami), and al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan al-Kubra (7/239), all by way of Hajjaj ibn Artat, from 'Abd al-Malik ibn al-Mughira, from 'Abd al-Rahman al-Bayla-mani, mawla of 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, who said: and he mentioned it as a mursal report. I suspect that "mawla" was corrupted in the copies into "'an" ("from"), and I nearly confirm this from the words of the Hafiz Ibn Kathir "there is an interruption," for the interruption is due to its being mursal; had it been from 'Umar it would have been connected (mawsul).]].

He, may He be exalted, forbids enabling the foolish to dispose of the wealth which Allah has made for people as a means of support (qiyam), meaning that their livelihoods depend on it, through trade and other means. From this verse the restriction (hajr) on the foolish is derived. They are of several kinds. Sometimes the restriction is due to minority, since a minor lacks legal capacity (maslub al-'ibarah). Sometimes it is due to insanity. Sometimes it is due to poor management because of deficient intellect or religion. And sometimes it is due to bankruptcy (falas), which is when debts surround a man and his wealth is insufficient to repay them. If his creditors ask the judge to impose a restriction on him, he imposes it.

Al-Dahhak reported from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His saying: ﴿And do not give the foolish your property﴾, that he said: "They are your sons and the women." Ibn Mas'ud, al-Hakam ibn 'Utaybah, al-Hasan and al-Dahhak said the same: "They are the women and the children."

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "They are the orphans." Mujahid, 'Ikrimah and Qatadah said: "They are the women."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Hisham ibn 'Ammar narrated to us, Sadaqah ibn Khalid narrated to us, 'Uthman ibn Abi al-'Atikah narrated to us, from 'Ali ibn Yazid, from al-Qasim, from Abu Umamah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed the foolish women, except the one who obeys her guardian."

Ibn Mardawayh narrated it at length. [Al-Suyuti mentioned it in al-Durr (2/433), and in its chain is 'Uthman ibn Abi al-'Atikah, who is weak in his narration from 'Ali ibn Yazid al-Alhani.]

Ibn Abi Hatim also said: It was mentioned from Muslim ibn Ibrahim, who said: Harb ibn Suraij narrated to us, from Mu'awiyah ibn Qurrah, from Abu Hurayrah, concerning ﴿And do not give the foolish your property﴾, that he said: "The servants (khadam), and they are the devils of mankind, and they are the servants."

* *

His saying: ﴿And provide for them from it and clothe them, and speak to them a kind word﴾. 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah reported from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: He, may He be exalted, says: Do not intend your property, which Allah has placed under your control and made a means of living, and then give it to your wife or your sons and then look at what is in their hands. Rather, keep your property and manage it, and be yourself the one who spends on them from their clothing, their maintenance and their provision.
