Ibn Jarir said: Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Firas, from al-Sha'bi, from Abu Burdah, from Abu Musa, who said: Three people call upon Allah and He does not respond to them: a man whose wife has a bad character and he does not divorce her; a man who gives his property to a foolish person, while He has said: ﴿And do not give the foolish your property﴾; and a man who had a debt owed to him by another man and did not take a witness against him.

Mujahid said: ﴿And speak to them a kind word﴾ means in goodness and kinship.

This noble verse encompasses kindness to the family and to those who are in fact under restriction, through spending on clothing and provision, and through good speech and the beautifying of character.

* *

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And test the orphans﴾. Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, al-Hasan, al-Suddi and Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: That is, examine them, ﴿until they reach marriageable age﴾. Mujahid said: That means puberty (al-hulum). The majority of scholars said: Puberty in a boy is sometimes by wet dream (al-ihtilam), which is when he sees in his sleep what causes the discharge of the gushing fluid from which a child comes. Abu Dawud related in his Sunan from the Commander of the Faithful 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: I memorised from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "There is no orphanhood after wet dream, nor silence (sumat) of a day until night."

In another hadith, from 'A'ishah and other Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "The pen is lifted from three: from the child until he has a wet dream, from the sleeper until he awakes, and from the insane until he regains sanity," or until he completes fifteen years. They took this from the authentic hadith in the two Sahihs from 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar, who said: I was presented to the Prophet (ﷺ) on the day of Uhud when I was fourteen, and he did not permit me. I was presented to him on the day of the Trench when I was fifteen, and he permitted me. The Commander of the Faithful 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz, when this hadith reached him, said: "Indeed this is the dividing line between the young and the adult." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 2664, and Sahih Muslim, no. 1868.]

They differed concerning the growth of coarse hair around the private parts, which is the pubic hair, and whether it indicates puberty or not, in three opinions. In the third, a distinction is made between the children of Muslims, for it does not indicate puberty because it may have been induced by treatment, and the children of the protected people (ahl al-dhimmah), for it is puberty with regard to them, because they hasten it only so that the poll-tax (jizyah) may be imposed on them, and so they do not treat it. The sound view is that it is puberty with regard to all, because this is a natural matter in which people are equal, and the possibility of treatment is remote. Moreover, the Sunnah has indicated this in the hadith which Imam Ahmad related from 'Atiyyah al-Qurazi, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: We were presented to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on the day of Qurayzah, and whoever had grown hair was killed, and whoever had not grown it was released, so I was among those who had not grown it, and he released me.

The four Sunan compilers also related it in similar form. [Musnad (4/310); Sunan Abi Dawud, nos. 4404, 4405; Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 1584; Sunan al-Nasa'i (6/155); Sunan Ibn Majah, nos. 2541, 2542.] al-Tirmidhi said: Hasan sahih. That was the case because Sa'd ibn Mu'adh, may Allah be pleased with him, had judged concerning them that the fighters should be killed and the offspring taken captive.

Imam Abu 'Ubayd al-Qasim ibn Sallam said in his book al-Gharib: Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, from Isma'il ibn Umayyah, from Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Hayyan, from 'Umar: that a boy slandered a girl concerning her hair, and 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "Look at him." He was not found to have grown hair, so he averted the legal penalty (hadd) from him. Abu 'Ubayd said: Ibtahara her means he accused her (qadhafaha), and al-ibtihar is to say: "I did such and such with her" while lying. If he is truthful, it is al-ibtiyar. Al-Kumayt said in his poetry:

"It is shameful for one like me to describe a girl,
whether by false accusation or by truthful report."

* *

His saying: ﴿And if you perceive in them maturity of judgement, then hand over to them their property﴾. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: That means righteousness in their religion and preservation of their property. The same was related from Ibn 'Abbas, al-Hasan al-Basri and other imams. The jurists likewise said: When the boy reaches the state of being upright in his religion and his property, the restriction is lifted from him, and his property which is under the control of his guardian is handed over to him in its proper manner.

* *

His saying: ﴿And do not consume it wastefully and hastily, before they grow up﴾. He, may He be exalted, forbids consuming the property of orphans without genuine need, wastefully and hastily, before they reach maturity.

Then He said: ﴿And whoever is wealthy, let him abstain﴾, meaning whoever is in affluence with regard to the orphan's property, let him abstain from it and not eat anything of it. al-Sha'bi said: It is upon him like carrion and blood.

﴿And whoever is poor, let him eat in a reasonable manner﴾. Ibn Abi Hatim said: al-Ashaj narrated to us, 'Abdullah ibn Sulayman narrated to us, Hisham narrated to us, from his father, from 'A'ishah: ﴿And whoever is wealthy, let him abstain﴾ was revealed concerning the orphan's property.

al-Ashaj and Harun ibn Ishaq narrated to us, both saying: 'Abdah ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from Hisham, from his father, from [her], who said: It was revealed concerning the guardian of the orphan who looks after him and manages his affairs, that if he is in need he may eat from it.

My father narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Sa'id al-Asbahani narrated to us, 'Ali ibn Musharr narrated to us, from Hisham, from his father, from 'A'ishah, who said: This verse was revealed concerning the guardian of the orphan: ﴿And whoever is wealthy, let him abstain, and whoever is poor, let him eat in a reasonable manner﴾, according to the measure of his care for him.

al-Bukhari related it from Ishaq, from 'Abdullah ibn Numayr, from Hisham, with the same chain.

The jurists said: He may eat the lesser of two things: the wage of his equivalent (ajr mithlihi) or the amount of his need. They differed as to whether he must repay if he becomes affluent, in two opinions. One of them: No, because he ate in return for the wage of his work, and he was poor. This is the sound view according to the companions of al-Shafi'i, because the verse permitted eating without substitution.

Imam Ahmad said: 'Abd al-Wahhab narrated to us, Husayn narrated to us, from 'Amr ibn Shu'ayb, from his father, from his grandfather, that a man asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "I have no property, and I have an orphan?" He said: "Eat from the property of your orphan, without wastefulness, without extravagance, and without accumulating property for yourself, and without protecting your property with his property," or he said: "without ransoming your property with his property." Husayn was uncertain. [Musnad (3/186).]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa'id al-Ashaj narrated to us, Abu Khalid al-Ahmar narrated to us, Husayn al-Mu'allim narrated to us, from 'Amr ibn Shu'ayb, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: A man came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "Indeed I have an orphan who has property, and he has nothing. May I eat from his property?" He said: "In a reasonable manner, without extravagance."

Abu Dawud, al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah related it from the hadith of Husayn al-Mu'allim with it. [Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 2872; Sunan al-Nasa'i (6/256); Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 2718.]

Abu Hatim Ibn Hibban related in his Sahih, and Ibn Mardawayh in his Tafsir, from the hadith of Ya'la ibn Mahdi, from Ja'far ibn Sulayman, from Abu 'Amir al-Khazzaz, from 'Amr ibn Dinar, from Jabir, that a man said: "O Messenger of Allah, for what reason may I strike my orphan?" He said: "As much as you would strike your own child, without protecting your property with his property, and without accumulating property from him." [Ibn Hibban, Sahih, no. 4244 (al-Ihsan); al-Bayhaqi, al-Sunan al-Kubra (6/4); and al-Tabarani, al-Mu'jam al-Saghir (1/89), both through Abu 'Amir al-Khazzaz from 'Amr ibn Dinar.]

Ibn Jarir said: al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, al-Thawri informed us, from Yahya ibn Sa'id, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, who said: A Bedouin came to Ibn 'Abbas and said: "I have orphans in my care, and they have camels, and I have camels, and I milk my camels, and I am poor. What is lawful for me from their milk?" He said: "If you are seeking their stray animals, and you tar their mange, and you clean their watering trough, and you tend to them, then drink without harming their offspring and without over-milking."

Malik related it in his Muwatta' from Yahya ibn Sa'id with the same. [Tafsir al-Tabari (7/588); Muwatta' Malik (2/934); al-Nahhas related it through Malik in al-Nasikh wa'l-Mansukh (p. 298), then said: "This chain is sahih."]

It is with this view, namely that no substitute is to be repaid, that 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah, 'Ikrimah, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, 'Atiyyah al-'Awfi and al-Hasan al-Basri hold.

The second view: Yes, because the property of the orphan is forbidden (to be taken), and it is only permitted out of necessity, so he must return its equivalent, like the eating of another's property by one who is compelled by need. Abu Bakr Ibn Abi al-Dunya said: Ibn Khaythamah narrated to us, Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan and Isra'il, from Abu Ishaq, from Harithah ibn Mudarrib, who said: 'Umar [ibn al-Khattab] (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "I have placed myself with regard to this property in the position of the guardian of the orphan: if I am rich, I abstain; if I am in need, I borrow; and when I become well-off, I repay."

Another route: Sa'id ibn Mansur said: Abu al-Ahwas narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Bara', who said: 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) said to me: "I have placed myself with regard to the property of Allah in the position of the guardian of the orphan: if I am in need, I take from it, and when I become well-off, I return it; and if I am rich, I abstain."

Its chain is sound. Al-Bayhaqi also narrated something similar from Ibn 'Abbas. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated in the same way through 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿And whoever is poor, let him eat in accordance with what is reasonable﴾, meaning: the loan. He said: It was also narrated from 'Ubaydah, Abu al-'Aliyah, Abu Wa'il, Sa'id ibn Jubayr (in one of the narrations), Mujahid, al-Dahhak, and al-Suddi something similar to that. And it was narrated through al-Suddi, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿let him eat in accordance with what is reasonable﴾ that he said: he eats with three fingers.

Then he said: Ahmad ibn Sinan narrated to us, Ibn Mahdi narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from al-Hakam, from Miqsam, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿And whoever is poor, let him eat in accordance with what is reasonable﴾, he said: He eats from his own property, and provides for himself from his orphan's property, so that he does not need the orphan's property. He said: It was also narrated from Mujahid, Maymun ibn Mihran (in one of the narrations), and al-Hakam something similar to that.

'Amir al-Sha'bi said: He should not eat from it except when he is compelled to, just as one is compelled to eat carrion; and if he eats from it, he should repay it. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it.

Ibn Wahb said: Nafi' ibn Abi Nu'aym al-Qari' narrated to me, saying: I asked Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Ansari and Rabi'ah about the saying of Allah: ﴿let him eat in accordance with what is reasonable﴾, and they both said: That refers to the orphan; if he is poor, he is to be provided for according to his poverty, and the guardian is to take nothing from it.

This is far from the context, because He said: ﴿And whoever is rich, let him abstain﴾, meaning: from the guardians; ﴿and whoever is poor, let him eat in accordance with what is reasonable﴾, meaning: from them; ﴿let him eat in accordance with what is reasonable﴾, meaning: in the best manner, as He said in another verse: ﴿And do not approach the property of the orphan except in the way that is best, until he reaches maturity﴾ [al-Isra' 34], meaning: do not approach it except as one who seeks to improve it; and if you are in need of it, eat from it in accordance with what is reasonable.

* *

His saying: ﴿And when you give them their property﴾, meaning: after they reach puberty and sound judgment is found in them, then at that time hand over their property to them. ﴿When you give them their property, then call witnesses over them.﴾ This is a command from Allah the Exalted to the guardians to call witnesses against the orphans when they reach puberty and their property is handed over to them, so that none of them later denies or disputes what he has received and taken possession of.

Then He said: ﴿And Allah is sufficient as Reckoner﴾, meaning: Allah is sufficient as Reckoner, Witness, and Watcher over the guardians, in their conduct toward the orphans and in their handing over of the property to them: whether it is complete and intact, or diminished, unjustly withheld, its accounts falsified and its affairs deceptively arranged. Allah knows all of that. For this reason it is established in Sahih Muslim that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O Abu Dharr, I see that you are weak, and I love for you what I love for myself: do not take authority over two people, nor be in charge of the property of an orphan."

He said: "Eat from the property of your orphan, without wastefulness, without extravagance, and without accumulating property for yourself, and without protecting your property with his property," or he said: "without ransoming your property with his property." Husayn was uncertain. [Musnad (3/186).]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa'id al-Ashaj narrated to us, Abu Khalid al-Ahmar narrated to us, Husayn al-Mu'allim narrated to us, from 'Amr ibn Shu'ayb, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: A man came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "Indeed I have an orphan who has property, and he has nothing. May I eat from his property?" He said: "In a reasonable manner, without extravagance."

Abu Dawud, al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah related it from the hadith of Husayn al-Mu'allim with it. [Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 2872; Sunan al-Nasa'i (6/256); Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 2718.]

Abu Hatim Ibn Hibban related in his Sahih, and Ibn Mardawayh in his Tafsir, from the hadith of Ya'la ibn Mahdi, from Ja'far ibn Sulayman, from Abu 'Amir al-Khazzaz, from 'Amr ibn Dinar, from Jabir, that a man said: "O Messenger of Allah, for what reason may I strike my orphan?" He said: "As much as you would strike your own child, without protecting your property with his property, and without accumulating property from him." [Ibn Hibban, Sahih, no. 4244 (al-Ihsan); al-Bayhaqi, al-Sunan al-Kubra (6/4); and al-Tabarani, al-Mu'jam al-Saghir (1/89), both through Abu 'Amir al-Khazzaz from 'Amr ibn Dinar.]

Ibn Jarir said: al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, al-Thawri informed us, from Yahya ibn Sa'id, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, who said: A Bedouin came to Ibn 'Abbas and said: "I have orphans in my care, and they have camels, and I have camels, and I milk my camels, and I am poor. What is lawful for me from their milk?" He said: "If you are seeking their stray animals, and you tar their mange, and you clean their watering trough, and you tend to them, then drink without harming their offspring and without over-milking."

Malik related it in his Muwatta' from Yahya ibn Sa'id with the same. [Tafsir al-Tabari (7/588); Muwatta' Malik (2/934); al-Nahhas related it through Malik in al-Nasikh wa'l-Mansukh (p. 298), then said: "This chain is sahih."]

It is with this view, namely that no substitute is to be repaid, that 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah, 'Ikrimah, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, 'Atiyyah al-'Awfi and al-Hasan al-Basri hold.

The second view: Yes, because the property of the orphan is forbidden (to be taken), and it is only permitted out of necessity, so he must return its equivalent, like the eating of another's property by one who is compelled by need. Abu Bakr Ibn Abi al-Dunya said: Ibn Khaythamah narrated to us, Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan and Isra'il, from Abu Ishaq, from Harithah ibn Mudarrib, who said: 'Umar [ibn al-Khattab] (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "I have placed myself with regard to this property in the position of the guardian of the orphan: if I am rich, I abstain; if I am in need, I borrow; and when I become well-off, I repay."

Another route: Sa'id ibn Mansur said: Abu al-Ahwas narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Bara', who said: 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) said to me: "I have placed myself with regard to the property of Allah in the position of the guardian of the orphan: if I am in need, I take from it, and when I become well-off, I return it; and if I am rich, I abstain."

Its chain is sound. Al-Bayhaqi also narrated something similar from Ibn 'Abbas. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated in the same way through 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿And whoever is poor, let him eat in accordance with what is reasonable﴾, meaning: the loan. He said: It was also narrated from 'Ubaydah, Abu al-'Aliyah, Abu Wa'il, Sa'id ibn Jubayr (in one of the narrations), Mujahid, al-Dahhak, and al-Suddi something similar to that. And it was narrated through al-Suddi, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿let him eat in accordance with what is reasonable﴾ that he said: he eats with three fingers.

Then he said: Ahmad ibn Sinan narrated to us, Ibn Mahdi narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from al-Hakam, from Miqsam, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿And whoever is poor, let him eat in accordance with what is reasonable﴾, he said: He eats from his own property, and provides for himself from his orphan's property, so that he does not need the orphan's property. He said: It was also narrated from Mujahid, Maymun ibn Mihran (in one of the narrations), and al-Hakam something similar to that.

'Amir al-Sha'bi said: He should not eat from it except when he is compelled to, just as one is compelled to eat carrion; and if he eats from it, he should repay it. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it.

Ibn Wahb said: Nafi' ibn Abi Nu'aym al-Qari' narrated to me, saying: I asked Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Ansari and Rabi'ah about the saying of Allah: ﴿let him eat in accordance with what is reasonable﴾, and they both said: That refers to the orphan; if he is poor, he is to be provided for according to his poverty, and the guardian is to take nothing from it.

This is far from the context, because He said: ﴿And whoever is rich, let him abstain﴾, meaning: from the guardians; ﴿and whoever is poor, let him eat in accordance with what is reasonable﴾, meaning: from them; ﴿let him eat in accordance with what is reasonable﴾, meaning: in the best manner, as He said in another verse: ﴿And do not approach the property of the orphan except in the way that is best, until he reaches maturity﴾ [al-Isra' 34], meaning: do not approach it except as one who seeks to improve it; and if you are in need of it, eat from it in accordance with what is reasonable.

* *

His saying: ﴿And when you give them their property﴾, meaning: after they reach puberty and sound judgment is found in them, then at that time hand over their property to them. ﴿When you give them their property, then call witnesses over them.﴾ This is a command from Allah the Exalted to the guardians to call witnesses against the orphans when they reach puberty and their property is handed over to them, so that none of them later denies or disputes what he has received and taken possession of.

Then He said: ﴿And Allah is sufficient as Reckoner﴾, meaning: Allah is sufficient as Reckoner, Witness, and Watcher over the guardians, in their conduct toward the orphans and in their handing over of the property to them: whether it is complete and intact, or diminished, unjustly withheld, its accounts falsified and its affairs deceptively arranged. Allah knows all of that. For this reason it is established in Sahih Muslim that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O Abu Dharr, I see that you are weak, and I love for you what I love for myself: do not take authority over two people, nor be in charge of the property of an orphan."

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 4, verses 7–10 (part 1 of 2):

Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Qatadah said: The polytheists used to give the property to the grown men, and they did not give inheritance to the women or the children. So Allah revealed: ﴿For men there is a share of what the parents and the close relatives leave, and for women there is a share of what the parents and the close relatives leave, whether it is little or much, an obligatory share.﴾ That is, all of them are equal in the ruling of Allah the Exalted, they are equal in the basic principle of inheritance, even though they differ in amount according to what Allah [the Exalted] has prescribed for each of them, based on the kinship, marriage, or patronage (wala') through which they connect to the deceased. For it is a bond like the bond of lineage (nasab). Ibn Mardawayh narrated, through the route of Ibn Hirasah [in another manuscript: "Ibn Rahawayh"; in another: "Hawasah"], from Sufyan al-Thawri, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Aqil, from Jabir, who said: Umm Kujjah came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I have two daughters, their father has died, and they have nothing." So Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿For men there is a share of what the parents and the close relatives leave﴾, to the end of the verse. This hadith will come later in the verses of inheritance in a different context, and Allah knows best.

* *

And His saying: ﴿And when the division takes place, if relatives, orphans, and the needy are present, provide for them from it and speak to them with kind words.﴾ It was said: The meaning is: when those close relatives who are not heirs, and the orphans and the needy, are present at the division of the inheritance, then some portion from the estate should be given to them, and that this was obligatory at the beginning of Islam. And it was said: it is recommended (mustahabb). And they differed: is it abrogated (mansukh) or not? There are two opinions. Al-Bukhari said: Ahmad ibn Humayd narrated to us, 'Ubayd Allah al-Ash'ari informed us, from Sufyan, from al-Shaybani, from Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding ﴿And when the division takes place, the close relatives, the orphans, and the needy are present﴾, he said: It is muhkamah (established, not abrogated), and it is not abrogated. Sa'id also narrated it from Ibn 'Abbas.

Ibn Jarir said: al-Qasim narrated to us, al-Husayn narrated to us, 'Abbad ibn al-'Awwam narrated to us, from al-Hajjaj, from al-Hakam, from Miqsam, from Ibn 'Abbas who said: It is still in force and is acted upon.

Al-Thawri said, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding this verse, he said: It is obligatory upon the heirs, as much as their souls are content to give. Likewise it was narrated from Ibn Mas'ud, Abu Musa, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr, Abu al-'Aliyah, al-Sha'bi, al-Hasan, Ibn Sirin, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Makhul, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah, al-Zuhri, and Yahya ibn Ya'mur, that it is obligatory.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj, from Isma'il ibn 'Ulayyah, from Yunus ibn 'Ubayd, from Muhammad ibn Sirin who said: 'Ubaydah was entrusted with a bequest, so he ordered a sheep to be slaughtered and fed it to the people mentioned in this verse, and he said: If not for this verse, this would have come from my own wealth.

Malik said, in what is narrated from him as tafsir (exegesis) in a compiled section, from al-Zuhri: that 'Urwah gave from the wealth of Mus'ab when he divided his property. And al-Zuhri said: It is muhkamah.

Malik said, from 'Abd al-Karim, from Mujahid, who said: It is a right that is obligatory as long as the souls are content with it.

Mention of those who held that this is a command to make a bequest for them:
'Abd al-Razzaq said: Ibn Jurayj informed us, Ibn Abi Mulaykah informed me that Asma' bint 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr al-Siddiq and al-Qasim ibn Muhammad informed him that 'Abdullah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr divided the inheritance of his father 'Abd al-Rahman, while 'A'ishah was alive. They both said: He did not leave in the house any needy person or any relative except that he gave him from his father's inheritance. They both said: And he recited ﴿And when the division takes place, the close relatives...﴾ Al-Qasim said: I mentioned that to Ibn 'Abbas, and he said: He was not correct; that is not his right. Rather, it is for the bequest; this verse is about the bequest, that the deceased may bequeath to them. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it. [Al-Tabari also narrated it in his tafsir (8/10, 11) through the route of Ibn Jurayj from Ibn Abi Mulaykah with the same wording.]

Mention of those who said: This verse is abrogated entirely:
Sufyan al-Thawri said, from Muhammad ibn al-Sa'ib al-Kalbi, from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding ﴿And when the division takes place﴾, he said: It is abrogated.

Isma'il ibn Muslim al-Makki said, from Qatadah, from Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said regarding this verse: ﴿And when the division takes place, the close relatives...﴾ The verse that follows abrogated it: ﴿Allah instructs you concerning your children...﴾

Al-'Awfi said, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding this verse: ﴿And when the division takes place, the close relatives...﴾ That was before the obligatory shares (fara'id) were revealed. Then Allah revealed the shares after that, and gave every person with a right his right, and charity was made from what the deceased named. Ibn Mardawayh narrated these.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn al-Sabbah narrated to us, Hajjaj narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj and 'Uthman ibn 'Ata', from 'Ata', from Ibn 'Abbas his saying: ﴿And when the division takes place, the close relatives, the orphans, and the needy...﴾ It was abrogated by the verse of inheritance, so each person was given his share of what the parents and the close relatives leave, whether it is little or much.

And Husayn ibn 'Asim narrated to us, Sa'id ibn 'Amir narrated to us, from Hammam, from Qatadah, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib that he said: It is abrogated. It was before the obligatory shares. Whatever a man left of wealth, the orphan, the poor, the needy, and the relatives were given from it when they were present at the division. Then it was abrogated after that. The inheritance laws abrogated it, so Allah assigned to each person with a right his right, and the bequest became from his wealth, which he bequeaths to his relatives as he wishes.

Malik said, from al-Zuhri, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib: It is abrogated; the inheritance laws and the bequest abrogated it.

Likewise it was narrated from Ikrimah, Abu al-Sha'tha', al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, Abu Salih, Abu Malik, Zayd ibn Aslam, al-Dahhak, 'Ata' al-Khurasani, Muqatil ibn Hayyan, and Rabi'ah ibn Abi 'Abd al-Rahman, that they said: It is abrogated. This is the view of the majority of jurists and the four Imams and their companions.

Ibn Jarir chose here a very strange opinion, and its summary is: the meaning of the verse according to him is ﴿And when the division takes place﴾, that is: when the division of the bequeathed property takes place, the close kin of the deceased are present, ﴿then provide for them from it and speak to them﴾, to the orphans and the needy if they are present, ﴿with kind words﴾. This is the substance of what he attempted after long explanation and repetition, and there is room for objection in it, and Allah knows best.

Al-'Awfi has said, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿And when the division takes place﴾, which is the division of the inheritance. Many others have said likewise, and the meaning according to this is not what Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir followed, may Allah have mercy on him. Rather, the meaning is that when these poor relatives who do not inherit, and the orphans and the needy, are present at the division of a great amount of wealth, their souls long for some of it, when they see this one taking and that one taking and that one taking, while they are despairing with nothing given to them. So Allah the Exalted, who is the Most Kind and Most Merciful, commanded that something be given to them from the estate as a kindness to them, a charity for them, a benefit to them, and a consolation for their brokenness. As Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Eat of its fruit when it bears fruit, and give its due on the day of its harvest.﴾ [al-An'am: 141] And He censured those who carry away wealth secretly, fearing that the needy and those in want would notice them, as He told about the people of the garden: ﴿When they swore that they would surely harvest it in the morning﴾ [al-Qalam: 17], that is, by night. And He said: ﴿So they set off, whispering, that no needy person shall enter it today upon you﴾ [al-Qalam: 23-24]. ﴿Allah destroyed them, and for the disbelievers there are similar things﴾ [Muhammad: 10]. So whoever denies the right of Allah upon him, Allah punishes him in the most precious thing he possesses. For this reason it came in the hadith: "Charity never mixes with wealth except that it ruins it" [narrated by al-Bazzar in his Musnad, no. 881 (Kashf al-Astar), from the hadith of 'A'ishah; al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (3/64): "In it is 'Uthman al-Jumahi; Abu Hatim said: his hadith is written but not used as evidence."], that is, withholding it becomes the cause of the complete loss of that wealth.

* *

And His saying: ﴿And let those fear who, if they left behind them weak offspring, would be anxious for them. So let them fear Allah﴾. 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: This is about a man whose death approaches, and someone hears him making a bequest that would harm his heirs. So Allah the Exalted commands the one who hears it to fear Allah, to guide him, to make him succeed and be steadfast toward what is right, and to look out for his heirs as he would wish to be treated with his own heirs if he feared their loss.

Likewise said Mujahid and others. And it is established in the two Sahihs that when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) entered upon Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas to visit him, he said: "O Messenger of Allah, I have much wealth and only a daughter inherits from me. Should I give two-thirds of my wealth in charity?" He said: "No." He said: "Half?" He said: "No." He said: "A third?" He said: "A third, and a third is much." Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, that you leave your heirs wealthy is better than that you leave them poor, begging from people" [Sahih al-Bukhari no. 2742; Sahih Muslim no. 1628].

And in the Sahih, Ibn 'Abbas said: If only the people would reduce from a third to a quarter, for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "A third, and a third is much" [Sahih al-Bukhari no. 2743; Sahih Muslim no. 1629].

The jurists said: If the heirs of the deceased are wealthy, it is recommended for the deceased to bequeath up to a third in his bequest. And if they are poor, it is recommended that he reduce the third.

It was also said: The meaning of His saying: ﴿And let those fear who, if they left behind them weak offspring, would be anxious for them. So let them fear Allah﴾ [that is] concerning the handling of the wealth of orphans: ﴿and do not consume it extravagantly and hastily, fearing that they will grow up﴾.

Ibn Jarir narrated this through the route of al-'Awfi from Ibn 'Abbas. It is a good opinion, and it is supported by what follows of the warning against consuming the wealth of orphans unjustly. That is: just as you would like your offspring to be treated after you, so treat the people's offspring when you are in charge of them.

Then inform them that whoever consumes the wealth of an orphan unjustly, he is only eating fire into his belly. For this reason He said: ﴿Indeed, those who consume the properties of orphans unjustly are only consuming fire into their bellies, and they will burn in a Blaze﴾. That is: when they consume the wealth of orphans without right, they are only eating a fire that will blaze in their bellies on the Day of Resurrection. And it is established in the two Sahihs from the hadith of Sulayman ibn Bilal, from Thawr ibn Zayd [in another manuscript: "Yazid"], from Salim Abu al-Ghayth, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Avoid the seven destructive sins." It was asked: O Messenger of Allah, what are they? He said: "Associating partners with Allah, sorcery, killing a soul which Allah has forbidden except by right, consuming usury, consuming the wealth of an orphan, fleeing on the day of battle, and accusing chaste, believing, unaware women of adultery."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, ʿUbaydah narrated to us [in another manuscript: "ʿAbd Allah"], Abu ʿAbd al-Samad ʿAbd al-ʿAziz ibn ʿAbd al-Samad al-ʿAmmi informed us, Abu Harun al-ʿAbdi narrated to us, from Abu Saʿid al-Khudri, who said: We said, "O Messenger of Allah, what did you see on the night of the Isra'?" He said: "I was taken to a large creation of Allah, men, each man having lips like the lips of a camel. Men were appointed over them who would tear open the cheek of one of them, then a rock of fire would be brought and thrown into the mouth of one of them until it came out from his bottom, and they were making moaning and screaming. I said, 'O Jibril, who are these?' He said: 'These are the ones who consume the wealth of orphans unjustly. They only eat fire into their bellies, and they will soon burn in the Blaze.'"

[Also narrated by al-Tabari in his Tafsir (8/27) through the chain of Mamar from Abu Harun al-ʿAbdi, with the same wording.
Shaykh Ahmad Shakir, may Allah have mercy on him, said: "Abu Harun al-ʿAbdi is ʿAmarah ibn Jawin. He narrated from Abu Saʿid and Ibn ʿUmar, and he is weak. Some said: he is a liar." Al-Daraqutni said: "He was inconsistent, a Kharijite and a Shiite." Ibn Hibban said: "He used to narrate from Abu Saʿid what was not from his narrations. It is not permissible to write his hadith except as a matter of wonder."]

And al-Suddi said: The one who consumes the wealth of an orphan will be raised on the Day of Resurrection with flames of fire coming out of his mouth, his ears, his nose and his eyes, and whoever sees him will recognize him as one who consumed the orphan's wealth.

Abu Bakr Ibn Mardawayh said: Ishaq ibn Ibrahim ibn Zayd narrated to us, Ahmad ibn ʿAmr narrated to us, ʿUqbah ibn Mukram narrated to us, Yunus ibn Bukayr narrated to us, Ziyad ibn al-Mundhir narrated to us, from Nafiʿ ibn al-Harith, from Abu Barzah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "On the Day of Resurrection, people will be raised from their graves with their mouths blazing with fire." It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, who are they?" He said: "Have you not seen that Allah said: ﴿Indeed, those who consume the wealth of orphans unjustly – they only consume fire into their bellies﴾ [the verse]."

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from Abu Zurʿah, from ʿUqbah ibn Mukram. Abu Hatim Ibn Hibban also narrated it in his Sahih, from Ahmad ibn ʿAli ibn al-Muthanna, from ʿUqbah ibn Mukram.
[Sahih Ibn Hibban, no. (2580) "Mawarid," through the chain of Abu Yaʿla, and it is in his Musnad (13/434). In its chain are Ziyad ibn al-Mundhir and his shaykh Nufayʿ ibn al-Harith, both abandoned (matrukan) according to the imams.]

Ibn Mardawayh said: ʿAbd Allah ibn Jaʿfar, Ahmad ibn ʿIsam narrated to us, Abu ʿAmir al-ʿAbdi narrated to us, ʿAbd Allah ibn Jaʿfar al-Zuhri narrated to us, from ʿUthman ibn Muhammad, from al-Maqburi, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I hereby make the property of the two weak ones sacred: the woman and the orphan." [And in its chain is Ahmad ibn ʿIsam al-Mawsili, whom al-Daraqutni declared weak.] Meaning: I enjoin you to avoid their property.

It was previously mentioned in Surat al-Baqarah, through the chain of ʿAta' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: When Allah revealed: ﴿Indeed, those who consume the wealth of orphans unjustly – they only consume fire into their bellies﴾ [the verse], whoever had an orphan in his care separated the orphan's food from his own food and his drink from his own drink. Whatever was left over would be set aside for him until he ate it or it spoiled. This became difficult for them, so they mentioned it to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and Allah revealed: ﴿They ask you about orphans. Say: Reforming them is best. And if you mix with them, then they are your brothers, and Allah knows the corrupter from the reformer﴾ [al-Baqarah: 220].

* *

Sa'id also narrated it from Ibn 'Abbas.

Ibn Jarir said: al-Qasim narrated to us, al-Husayn narrated to us, 'Abbad ibn al-'Awwam narrated to us, from al-Hajjaj, from al-Hakam, from Miqsam, from Ibn 'Abbas who said: It is still in force and is acted upon.

Al-Thawri said, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding this verse, he said: It is obligatory upon the heirs, as much as their souls are content to give. Likewise it was narrated from Ibn Mas'ud, Abu Musa, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr, Abu al-'Aliyah, al-Sha'bi, al-Hasan, Ibn Sirin, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Makhul, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah, al-Zuhri, and Yahya ibn Ya'mur, that it is obligatory.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj, from Isma'il ibn 'Ulayyah, from Yunus ibn 'Ubayd, from Muhammad ibn Sirin who said: 'Ubaydah was entrusted with a bequest, so he ordered a sheep to be slaughtered and fed it to the people mentioned in this verse, and he said: If not for this verse, this would have come from my own wealth.

Malik said, in what is narrated from him as tafsir (exegesis) in a compiled section, from al-Zuhri: that 'Urwah gave from the wealth of Mus'ab when he divided his property. And al-Zuhri said: It is muhkamah.

Malik said, from 'Abd al-Karim, from Mujahid, who said: It is a right that is obligatory as long as the souls are content with it.

Mention of those who held that this is a command to make a bequest for them:
'Abd al-Razzaq said: Ibn Jurayj informed us, Ibn Abi Mulaykah informed me that Asma' bint 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr al-Siddiq and al-Qasim ibn Muhammad informed him that 'Abdullah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr divided the inheritance of his father 'Abd al-Rahman, while 'A'ishah was alive. They both said: He did not leave in the house any needy person or any relative except that he gave him from his father's inheritance. They both said: And he recited ﴿And when the division takes place, the close relatives...﴾ Al-Qasim said: I mentioned that to Ibn 'Abbas, and he said: He was not correct; that is not his right. Rather, it is for the bequest; this verse is about the bequest, that the deceased may bequeath to them. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it. [Al-Tabari also narrated it in his tafsir (8/10, 11) through the route of Ibn Jurayj from Ibn Abi Mulaykah with the same wording.]

Mention of those who said: This verse is abrogated entirely:
Sufyan al-Thawri said, from Muhammad ibn al-Sa'ib al-Kalbi, from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding ﴿And when the division takes place﴾, he said: It is abrogated.

Isma'il ibn Muslim al-Makki said, from Qatadah, from Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said regarding this verse: ﴿And when the division takes place, the close relatives...﴾ The verse that follows abrogated it: ﴿Allah instructs you concerning your children...﴾

Al-'Awfi said, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding this verse: ﴿And when the division takes place, the close relatives...﴾ That was before the obligatory shares (fara'id) were revealed. Then Allah revealed the shares after that, and gave every person with a right his right, and charity was made from what the deceased named. Ibn Mardawayh narrated these.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn al-Sabbah narrated to us, Hajjaj narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj and 'Uthman ibn 'Ata', from 'Ata', from Ibn 'Abbas his saying: ﴿And when the division takes place, the close relatives, the orphans, and the needy...﴾ It was abrogated by the verse of inheritance, so each person was given his share of what the parents and the close relatives leave, whether it is little or much.

And Husayn ibn 'Asim narrated to us, Sa'id ibn 'Amir narrated to us, from Hammam, from Qatadah, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib that he said: It is abrogated. It was before the obligatory shares. Whatever a man left of wealth, the orphan, the poor, the needy, and the relatives were given from it when they were present at the division. Then it was abrogated after that. The inheritance laws abrogated it, so Allah assigned to each person with a right his right, and the bequest became from his wealth, which he bequeaths to his relatives as he wishes.

Malik said, from al-Zuhri, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib: It is abrogated; the inheritance laws and the bequest abrogated it.

Likewise it was narrated from Ikrimah, Abu al-Sha'tha', al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, Abu Salih, Abu Malik, Zayd ibn Aslam, al-Dahhak, 'Ata' al-Khurasani, Muqatil ibn Hayyan, and Rabi'ah ibn Abi 'Abd al-Rahman, that they said: It is abrogated. This is the view of the majority of jurists and the four Imams and their companions.

Ibn Jarir chose here a very strange opinion, and its summary is: the meaning of the verse according to him is ﴿And when the division takes place﴾, that is: when the division of the bequeathed property takes place, the close kin of the deceased are present, ﴿then provide for them from it and speak to them﴾, to the orphans and the needy if they are present, ﴿with kind words﴾. This is the substance of what he attempted after long explanation and repetition, and there is room for objection in it, and Allah knows best.

Al-'Awfi has said, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿And when the division takes place﴾, which is the division of the inheritance. Many others have said likewise, and the meaning according to this is not what Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir followed, may Allah have mercy on him. Rather, the meaning is that when these poor relatives who do not inherit, and the orphans and the needy, are present at the division of a great amount of wealth, their souls long for some of it, when they see this one taking and that one taking and that one taking, while they are despairing with nothing given to them. So Allah the Exalted, who is the Most Kind and Most Merciful, commanded that something be given to them from the estate as a kindness to them, a charity for them, a benefit to them, and a consolation for their brokenness. As Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Eat of its fruit when it bears fruit, and give its due on the day of its harvest.﴾ [al-An'am: 141] And He censured those who carry away wealth secretly, fearing that the needy and those in want would notice them, as He told about the people of the garden: ﴿When they swore that they would surely harvest it in the morning﴾ [al-Qalam: 17], that is, by night. And He said: ﴿So they set off, whispering, that no needy person shall enter it today upon you﴾ [al-Qalam: 23-24]. ﴿Allah destroyed them, and for the disbelievers there are similar things﴾ [Muhammad: 10]. So whoever denies the right of Allah upon him, Allah punishes him in the most precious thing he possesses. For this reason it came in the hadith: "Charity never mixes with wealth except that it ruins it" [narrated by al-Bazzar in his Musnad, no. 881 (Kashf al-Astar), from the hadith of 'A'ishah; al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (3/64): "In it is 'Uthman al-Jumahi; Abu Hatim said: his hadith is written but not used as evidence."], that is, withholding it becomes the cause of the complete loss of that wealth.

* *

And His saying: ﴿And let those fear who, if they left behind them weak offspring, would be anxious for them. So let them fear Allah﴾. 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: This is about a man whose death approaches, and someone hears him making a bequest that would harm his heirs. So Allah the Exalted commands the one who hears it to fear Allah, to guide him, to make him succeed and be steadfast toward what is right, and to look out for his heirs as he would wish to be treated with his own heirs if he feared their loss.

Likewise said Mujahid and others. And it is established in the two Sahihs that when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) entered upon Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas to visit him, he said: "O Messenger of Allah, I have much wealth and only a daughter inherits from me. Should I give two-thirds of my wealth in charity?" He said: "No." He said: "Half?" He said: "No." He said: "A third?" He said: "A third, and a third is much." Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, that you leave your heirs wealthy is better than that you leave them poor, begging from people" [Sahih al-Bukhari no. 2742; Sahih Muslim no. 1628].

And in the Sahih, Ibn 'Abbas said: If only the people would reduce from a third to a quarter, for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "A third, and a third is much" [Sahih al-Bukhari no. 2743; Sahih Muslim no. 1629].

The jurists said: If the heirs of the deceased are wealthy, it is recommended for the deceased to bequeath up to a third in his bequest. And if they are poor, it is recommended that he reduce the third.

It was also said: The meaning of His saying: ﴿And let those fear who, if they left behind them weak offspring, would be anxious for them. So let them fear Allah﴾ [that is] concerning the handling of the wealth of orphans: ﴿and do not consume it extravagantly and hastily, fearing that they will grow up﴾.

Ibn Jarir narrated this through the route of al-'Awfi from Ibn 'Abbas. It is a good opinion, and it is supported by what follows of the warning against consuming the wealth of orphans unjustly. That is: just as you would like your offspring to be treated after you, so treat the people's offspring when you are in charge of them.

Then inform them that whoever consumes the wealth of an orphan unjustly, he is only eating fire into his belly. For this reason He said: ﴿Indeed, those who consume the properties of orphans unjustly are only consuming fire into their bellies, and they will burn in a Blaze﴾. That is: when they consume the wealth of orphans without right, they are only eating a fire that will blaze in their bellies on the Day of Resurrection. And it is established in the two Sahihs from the hadith of Sulayman ibn Bilal, from Thawr ibn Zayd [in another manuscript: "Yazid"], from Salim Abu al-Ghayth, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Avoid the seven destructive sins." It was asked: O Messenger of Allah, what are they? He said: "Associating partners with Allah, sorcery, killing a soul which Allah has forbidden except by right, consuming usury, consuming the wealth of an orphan, fleeing on the day of battle, and accusing chaste, believing, unaware women of adultery."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, ʿUbaydah narrated to us [in another manuscript: "ʿAbd Allah"], Abu ʿAbd al-Samad ʿAbd al-ʿAziz ibn ʿAbd al-Samad al-ʿAmmi informed us, Abu Harun al-ʿAbdi narrated to us, from Abu Saʿid al-Khudri, who said: We said, "O Messenger of Allah, what did you see on the night of the Isra'?" He said: "I was taken to a large creation of Allah, men, each man having lips like the lips of a camel. Men were appointed over them who would tear open the cheek of one of them, then a rock of fire would be brought and thrown into the mouth of one of them until it came out from his bottom, and they were making moaning and screaming. I said, 'O Jibril, who are these?' He said: 'These are the ones who consume the wealth of orphans unjustly. They only eat fire into their bellies, and they will soon burn in the Blaze.'"

[Also narrated by al-Tabari in his Tafsir (8/27) through the chain of Mamar from Abu Harun al-ʿAbdi, with the same wording.
Shaykh Ahmad Shakir, may Allah have mercy on him, said: "Abu Harun al-ʿAbdi is ʿAmarah ibn Jawin. He narrated from Abu Saʿid and Ibn ʿUmar, and he is weak. Some said: he is a liar." Al-Daraqutni said: "He was inconsistent, a Kharijite and a Shiite." Ibn Hibban said: "He used to narrate from Abu Saʿid what was not from his narrations. It is not permissible to write his hadith except as a matter of wonder."]

And al-Suddi said: The one who consumes the wealth of an orphan will be raised on the Day of Resurrection with flames of fire coming out of his mouth, his ears, his nose and his eyes, and whoever sees him will recognize him as one who consumed the orphan's wealth.

Abu Bakr Ibn Mardawayh said: Ishaq ibn Ibrahim ibn Zayd narrated to us, Ahmad ibn ʿAmr narrated to us, ʿUqbah ibn Mukram narrated to us, Yunus ibn Bukayr narrated to us, Ziyad ibn al-Mundhir narrated to us, from Nafiʿ ibn al-Harith, from Abu Barzah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "On the Day of Resurrection, people will be raised from their graves with their mouths blazing with fire." It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, who are they?" He said: "Have you not seen that Allah said: ﴿Indeed, those who consume the wealth of orphans unjustly – they only consume fire into their bellies﴾ [the verse]."

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from Abu Zurʿah, from ʿUqbah ibn Mukram. Abu Hatim Ibn Hibban also narrated it in his Sahih, from Ahmad ibn ʿAli ibn al-Muthanna, from ʿUqbah ibn Mukram.
[Sahih Ibn Hibban, no. (2580) "Mawarid," through the chain of Abu Yaʿla, and it is in his Musnad (13/434). In its chain are Ziyad ibn al-Mundhir and his shaykh Nufayʿ ibn al-Harith, both abandoned (matrukan) according to the imams.]

Ibn Mardawayh said: ʿAbd Allah ibn Jaʿfar, Ahmad ibn ʿIsam narrated to us, Abu ʿAmir al-ʿAbdi narrated to us, ʿAbd Allah ibn Jaʿfar al-Zuhri narrated to us, from ʿUthman ibn Muhammad, from al-Maqburi, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I hereby make the property of the two weak ones sacred: the woman and the orphan." [And in its chain is Ahmad ibn ʿIsam al-Mawsili, whom al-Daraqutni declared weak.] Meaning: I enjoin you to avoid their property.

It was previously mentioned in Surat al-Baqarah, through the chain of ʿAta' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: When Allah revealed: ﴿Indeed, those who consume the wealth of orphans unjustly – they only consume fire into their bellies﴾ [the verse], whoever had an orphan in his care separated the orphan's food from his own food and his drink from his own drink. Whatever was left over would be set aside for him until he ate it or it spoiled. This became difficult for them, so they mentioned it to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and Allah revealed: ﴿They ask you about orphans. Say: Reforming them is best. And if you mix with them, then they are your brothers, and Allah knows the corrupter from the reformer﴾ [al-Baqarah: 220].

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 4, verses 7–10 (part 1 of 2):

Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Qatadah said: The polytheists used to give the property to the grown men, and they did not give inheritance to the women or the children. So Allah revealed: ﴿For men there is a share of what the parents and the close relatives leave, and for women there is a share of what the parents and the close relatives leave, whether it is little or much, an obligatory share.﴾ That is, all of them are equal in the ruling of Allah the Exalted, they are equal in the basic principle of inheritance, even though they differ in amount according to what Allah [the Exalted] has prescribed for each of them, based on the kinship, marriage, or patronage (wala') through which they connect to the deceased. For it is a bond like the bond of lineage (nasab). Ibn Mardawayh narrated, through the route of Ibn Hirasah [in another manuscript: "Ibn Rahawayh"; in another: "Hawasah"], from Sufyan al-Thawri, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Aqil, from Jabir, who said: Umm Kujjah came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I have two daughters, their father has died, and they have nothing." So Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿For men there is a share of what the parents and the close relatives leave﴾, to the end of the verse. This hadith will come later in the verses of inheritance in a different context, and Allah knows best.

* *

And His saying: ﴿And when the division takes place, if relatives, orphans, and the needy are present, provide for them from it and speak to them with kind words.﴾ It was said: The meaning is: when those close relatives who are not heirs, and the orphans and the needy, are present at the division of the inheritance, then some portion from the estate should be given to them, and that this was obligatory at the beginning of Islam. And it was said: it is recommended (mustahabb). And they differed: is it abrogated (mansukh) or not? There are two opinions. Al-Bukhari said: Ahmad ibn Humayd narrated to us, 'Ubayd Allah al-Ash'ari informed us, from Sufyan, from al-Shaybani, from Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding ﴿And when the division takes place, the close relatives, the orphans, and the needy are present﴾, he said: It is muhkamah (established, not abrogated), and it is not abrogated. Sa'id also narrated it from Ibn 'Abbas.

Ibn Jarir said: al-Qasim narrated to us, al-Husayn narrated to us, 'Abbad ibn al-'Awwam narrated to us, from al-Hajjaj, from al-Hakam, from Miqsam, from Ibn 'Abbas who said: It is still in force and is acted upon.

Al-Thawri said, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding this verse, he said: It is obligatory upon the heirs, as much as their souls are content to give. Likewise it was narrated from Ibn Mas'ud, Abu Musa, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr, Abu al-'Aliyah, al-Sha'bi, al-Hasan, Ibn Sirin, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Makhul, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah, al-Zuhri, and Yahya ibn Ya'mur, that it is obligatory.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj, from Isma'il ibn 'Ulayyah, from Yunus ibn 'Ubayd, from Muhammad ibn Sirin who said: 'Ubaydah was entrusted with a bequest, so he ordered a sheep to be slaughtered and fed it to the people mentioned in this verse, and he said: If not for this verse, this would have come from my own wealth.

Malik said, in what is narrated from him as tafsir (exegesis) in a compiled section, from al-Zuhri: that 'Urwah gave from the wealth of Mus'ab when he divided his property. And al-Zuhri said: It is muhkamah.

Malik said, from 'Abd al-Karim, from Mujahid, who said: It is a right that is obligatory as long as the souls are content with it.

Mention of those who held that this is a command to make a bequest for them:
'Abd al-Razzaq said: Ibn Jurayj informed us, Ibn Abi Mulaykah informed me that Asma' bint 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr al-Siddiq and al-Qasim ibn Muhammad informed him that 'Abdullah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr divided the inheritance of his father 'Abd al-Rahman, while 'A'ishah was alive. They both said: He did not leave in the house any needy person or any relative except that he gave him from his father's inheritance. They both said: And he recited ﴿And when the division takes place, the close relatives...﴾ Al-Qasim said: I mentioned that to Ibn 'Abbas, and he said: He was not correct; that is not his right. Rather, it is for the bequest; this verse is about the bequest, that the deceased may bequeath to them. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it. [Al-Tabari also narrated it in his tafsir (8/10, 11) through the route of Ibn Jurayj from Ibn Abi Mulaykah with the same wording.]

Mention of those who said: This verse is abrogated entirely:
Sufyan al-Thawri said, from Muhammad ibn al-Sa'ib al-Kalbi, from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding ﴿And when the division takes place﴾, he said: It is abrogated.

Isma'il ibn Muslim al-Makki said, from Qatadah, from Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said regarding this verse: ﴿And when the division takes place, the close relatives...﴾ The verse that follows abrogated it: ﴿Allah instructs you concerning your children...﴾

Al-'Awfi said, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding this verse: ﴿And when the division takes place, the close relatives...﴾ That was before the obligatory shares (fara'id) were revealed. Then Allah revealed the shares after that, and gave every person with a right his right, and charity was made from what the deceased named. Ibn Mardawayh narrated these.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn al-Sabbah narrated to us, Hajjaj narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj and 'Uthman ibn 'Ata', from 'Ata', from Ibn 'Abbas his saying: ﴿And when the division takes place, the close relatives, the orphans, and the needy...﴾ It was abrogated by the verse of inheritance, so each person was given his share of what the parents and the close relatives leave, whether it is little or much.

And Husayn ibn 'Asim narrated to us, Sa'id ibn 'Amir narrated to us, from Hammam, from Qatadah, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib that he said: It is abrogated. It was before the obligatory shares. Whatever a man left of wealth, the orphan, the poor, the needy, and the relatives were given from it when they were present at the division. Then it was abrogated after that. The inheritance laws abrogated it, so Allah assigned to each person with a right his right, and the bequest became from his wealth, which he bequeaths to his relatives as he wishes.

Malik said, from al-Zuhri, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib: It is abrogated; the inheritance laws and the bequest abrogated it.

Likewise it was narrated from Ikrimah, Abu al-Sha'tha', al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, Abu Salih, Abu Malik, Zayd ibn Aslam, al-Dahhak, 'Ata' al-Khurasani, Muqatil ibn Hayyan, and Rabi'ah ibn Abi 'Abd al-Rahman, that they said: It is abrogated. This is the view of the majority of jurists and the four Imams and their companions.

Ibn Jarir chose here a very strange opinion, and its summary is: the meaning of the verse according to him is ﴿And when the division takes place﴾, that is: when the division of the bequeathed property takes place, the close kin of the deceased are present, ﴿then provide for them from it and speak to them﴾, to the orphans and the needy if they are present, ﴿with kind words﴾. This is the substance of what he attempted after long explanation and repetition, and there is room for objection in it, and Allah knows best.

Al-'Awfi has said, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿And when the division takes place﴾, which is the division of the inheritance. Many others have said likewise, and the meaning according to this is not what Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir followed, may Allah have mercy on him. Rather, the meaning is that when these poor relatives who do not inherit, and the orphans and the needy, are present at the division of a great amount of wealth, their souls long for some of it, when they see this one taking and that one taking and that one taking, while they are despairing with nothing given to them. So Allah the Exalted, who is the Most Kind and Most Merciful, commanded that something be given to them from the estate as a kindness to them, a charity for them, a benefit to them, and a consolation for their brokenness. As Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Eat of its fruit when it bears fruit, and give its due on the day of its harvest.﴾ [al-An'am: 141] And He censured those who carry away wealth secretly, fearing that the needy and those in want would notice them, as He told about the people of the garden: ﴿When they swore that they would surely harvest it in the morning﴾ [al-Qalam: 17], that is, by night. And He said: ﴿So they set off, whispering, that no needy person shall enter it today upon you﴾ [al-Qalam: 23-24]. ﴿Allah destroyed them, and for the disbelievers there are similar things﴾ [Muhammad: 10]. So whoever denies the right of Allah upon him, Allah punishes him in the most precious thing he possesses. For this reason it came in the hadith: "Charity never mixes with wealth except that it ruins it" [narrated by al-Bazzar in his Musnad, no. 881 (Kashf al-Astar), from the hadith of 'A'ishah; al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (3/64): "In it is 'Uthman al-Jumahi; Abu Hatim said: his hadith is written but not used as evidence."], that is, withholding it becomes the cause of the complete loss of that wealth.

* *

And His saying: ﴿And let those fear who, if they left behind them weak offspring, would be anxious for them. So let them fear Allah﴾. 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: This is about a man whose death approaches, and someone hears him making a bequest that would harm his heirs. So Allah the Exalted commands the one who hears it to fear Allah, to guide him, to make him succeed and be steadfast toward what is right, and to look out for his heirs as he would wish to be treated with his own heirs if he feared their loss.

Likewise said Mujahid and others. And it is established in the two Sahihs that when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) entered upon Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas to visit him, he said: "O Messenger of Allah, I have much wealth and only a daughter inherits from me. Should I give two-thirds of my wealth in charity?" He said: "No." He said: "Half?" He said: "No." He said: "A third?" He said: "A third, and a third is much." Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, that you leave your heirs wealthy is better than that you leave them poor, begging from people" [Sahih al-Bukhari no. 2742; Sahih Muslim no. 1628].

And in the Sahih, Ibn 'Abbas said: If only the people would reduce from a third to a quarter, for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "A third, and a third is much" [Sahih al-Bukhari no. 2743; Sahih Muslim no. 1629].

The jurists said: If the heirs of the deceased are wealthy, it is recommended for the deceased to bequeath up to a third in his bequest. And if they are poor, it is recommended that he reduce the third.

It was also said: The meaning of His saying: ﴿And let those fear who, if they left behind them weak offspring, would be anxious for them. So let them fear Allah﴾ [that is] concerning the handling of the wealth of orphans: ﴿and do not consume it extravagantly and hastily, fearing that they will grow up﴾.

Ibn Jarir narrated this through the route of al-'Awfi from Ibn 'Abbas. It is a good opinion, and it is supported by what follows of the warning against consuming the wealth of orphans unjustly. That is: just as you would like your offspring to be treated after you, so treat the people's offspring when you are in charge of them.

Then inform them that whoever consumes the wealth of an orphan unjustly, he is only eating fire into his belly. For this reason He said: ﴿Indeed, those who consume the properties of orphans unjustly are only consuming fire into their bellies, and they will burn in a Blaze﴾. That is: when they consume the wealth of orphans without right, they are only eating a fire that will blaze in their bellies on the Day of Resurrection. And it is established in the two Sahihs from the hadith of Sulayman ibn Bilal, from Thawr ibn Zayd [in another manuscript: "Yazid"], from Salim Abu al-Ghayth, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Avoid the seven destructive sins." It was asked: O Messenger of Allah, what are they? He said: "Associating partners with Allah, sorcery, killing a soul which Allah has forbidden except by right, consuming usury, consuming the wealth of an orphan, fleeing on the day of battle, and accusing chaste, believing, unaware women of adultery."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, ʿUbaydah narrated to us [in another manuscript: "ʿAbd Allah"], Abu ʿAbd al-Samad ʿAbd al-ʿAziz ibn ʿAbd al-Samad al-ʿAmmi informed us, Abu Harun al-ʿAbdi narrated to us, from Abu Saʿid al-Khudri, who said: We said, "O Messenger of Allah, what did you see on the night of the Isra'?" He said: "I was taken to a large creation of Allah, men, each man having lips like the lips of a camel. Men were appointed over them who would tear open the cheek of one of them, then a rock of fire would be brought and thrown into the mouth of one of them until it came out from his bottom, and they were making moaning and screaming. I said, 'O Jibril, who are these?' He said: 'These are the ones who consume the wealth of orphans unjustly. They only eat fire into their bellies, and they will soon burn in the Blaze.'"

[Also narrated by al-Tabari in his Tafsir (8/27) through the chain of Mamar from Abu Harun al-ʿAbdi, with the same wording.
Shaykh Ahmad Shakir, may Allah have mercy on him, said: "Abu Harun al-ʿAbdi is ʿAmarah ibn Jawin. He narrated from Abu Saʿid and Ibn ʿUmar, and he is weak. Some said: he is a liar." Al-Daraqutni said: "He was inconsistent, a Kharijite and a Shiite." Ibn Hibban said: "He used to narrate from Abu Saʿid what was not from his narrations. It is not permissible to write his hadith except as a matter of wonder."]

And al-Suddi said: The one who consumes the wealth of an orphan will be raised on the Day of Resurrection with flames of fire coming out of his mouth, his ears, his nose and his eyes, and whoever sees him will recognize him as one who consumed the orphan's wealth.

Abu Bakr Ibn Mardawayh said: Ishaq ibn Ibrahim ibn Zayd narrated to us, Ahmad ibn ʿAmr narrated to us, ʿUqbah ibn Mukram narrated to us, Yunus ibn Bukayr narrated to us, Ziyad ibn al-Mundhir narrated to us, from Nafiʿ ibn al-Harith, from Abu Barzah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "On the Day of Resurrection, people will be raised from their graves with their mouths blazing with fire." It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, who are they?" He said: "Have you not seen that Allah said: ﴿Indeed, those who consume the wealth of orphans unjustly – they only consume fire into their bellies﴾ [the verse]."

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from Abu Zurʿah, from ʿUqbah ibn Mukram. Abu Hatim Ibn Hibban also narrated it in his Sahih, from Ahmad ibn ʿAli ibn al-Muthanna, from ʿUqbah ibn Mukram.
[Sahih Ibn Hibban, no. (2580) "Mawarid," through the chain of Abu Yaʿla, and it is in his Musnad (13/434). In its chain are Ziyad ibn al-Mundhir and his shaykh Nufayʿ ibn al-Harith, both abandoned (matrukan) according to the imams.]

Ibn Mardawayh said: ʿAbd Allah ibn Jaʿfar, Ahmad ibn ʿIsam narrated to us, Abu ʿAmir al-ʿAbdi narrated to us, ʿAbd Allah ibn Jaʿfar al-Zuhri narrated to us, from ʿUthman ibn Muhammad, from al-Maqburi, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I hereby make the property of the two weak ones sacred: the woman and the orphan." [And in its chain is Ahmad ibn ʿIsam al-Mawsili, whom al-Daraqutni declared weak.] Meaning: I enjoin you to avoid their property.

It was previously mentioned in Surat al-Baqarah, through the chain of ʿAta' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: When Allah revealed: ﴿Indeed, those who consume the wealth of orphans unjustly – they only consume fire into their bellies﴾ [the verse], whoever had an orphan in his care separated the orphan's food from his own food and his drink from his own drink. Whatever was left over would be set aside for him until he ate it or it spoiled. This became difficult for them, so they mentioned it to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and Allah revealed: ﴿They ask you about orphans. Say: Reforming them is best. And if you mix with them, then they are your brothers, and Allah knows the corrupter from the reformer﴾ [al-Baqarah: 220].

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 4, verses 7–10 (part 1 of 2):

Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Qatadah said: The polytheists used to give the property to the grown men, and they did not give inheritance to the women or the children. So Allah revealed: ﴿For men there is a share of what the parents and the close relatives leave, and for women there is a share of what the parents and the close relatives leave, whether it is little or much, an obligatory share.﴾ That is, all of them are equal in the ruling of Allah the Exalted, they are equal in the basic principle of inheritance, even though they differ in amount according to what Allah [the Exalted] has prescribed for each of them, based on the kinship, marriage, or patronage (wala') through which they connect to the deceased. For it is a bond like the bond of lineage (nasab). Ibn Mardawayh narrated, through the route of Ibn Hirasah [in another manuscript: "Ibn Rahawayh"; in another: "Hawasah"], from Sufyan al-Thawri, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Aqil, from Jabir, who said: Umm Kujjah came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I have two daughters, their father has died, and they have nothing." So Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿For men there is a share of what the parents and the close relatives leave﴾, to the end of the verse. This hadith will come later in the verses of inheritance in a different context, and Allah knows best.

* *

And His saying: ﴿And when the division takes place, if relatives, orphans, and the needy are present, provide for them from it and speak to them with kind words.﴾ It was said: The meaning is: when those close relatives who are not heirs, and the orphans and the needy, are present at the division of the inheritance, then some portion from the estate should be given to them, and that this was obligatory at the beginning of Islam. And it was said: it is recommended (mustahabb). And they differed: is it abrogated (mansukh) or not? There are two opinions. Al-Bukhari said: Ahmad ibn Humayd narrated to us, 'Ubayd Allah al-Ash'ari informed us, from Sufyan, from al-Shaybani, from Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding ﴿And when the division takes place, the close relatives, the orphans, and the needy are present﴾, he said: It is muhkamah (established, not abrogated), and it is not abrogated. Sa'id also narrated it from Ibn 'Abbas.

Ibn Jarir said: al-Qasim narrated to us, al-Husayn narrated to us, 'Abbad ibn al-'Awwam narrated to us, from al-Hajjaj, from al-Hakam, from Miqsam, from Ibn 'Abbas who said: It is still in force and is acted upon.

Al-Thawri said, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding this verse, he said: It is obligatory upon the heirs, as much as their souls are content to give. Likewise it was narrated from Ibn Mas'ud, Abu Musa, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr, Abu al-'Aliyah, al-Sha'bi, al-Hasan, Ibn Sirin, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Makhul, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah, al-Zuhri, and Yahya ibn Ya'mur, that it is obligatory.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj, from Isma'il ibn 'Ulayyah, from Yunus ibn 'Ubayd, from Muhammad ibn Sirin who said: 'Ubaydah was entrusted with a bequest, so he ordered a sheep to be slaughtered and fed it to the people mentioned in this verse, and he said: If not for this verse, this would have come from my own wealth.

Malik said, in what is narrated from him as tafsir (exegesis) in a compiled section, from al-Zuhri: that 'Urwah gave from the wealth of Mus'ab when he divided his property. And al-Zuhri said: It is muhkamah.

Malik said, from 'Abd al-Karim, from Mujahid, who said: It is a right that is obligatory as long as the souls are content with it.

Mention of those who held that this is a command to make a bequest for them:
'Abd al-Razzaq said: Ibn Jurayj informed us, Ibn Abi Mulaykah informed me that Asma' bint 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr al-Siddiq and al-Qasim ibn Muhammad informed him that 'Abdullah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr divided the inheritance of his father 'Abd al-Rahman, while 'A'ishah was alive. They both said: He did not leave in the house any needy person or any relative except that he gave him from his father's inheritance. They both said: And he recited ﴿And when the division takes place, the close relatives...﴾ Al-Qasim said: I mentioned that to Ibn 'Abbas, and he said: He was not correct; that is not his right. Rather, it is for the bequest; this verse is about the bequest, that the deceased may bequeath to them. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it. [Al-Tabari also narrated it in his tafsir (8/10, 11) through the route of Ibn Jurayj from Ibn Abi Mulaykah with the same wording.]

Mention of those who said: This verse is abrogated entirely:
Sufyan al-Thawri said, from Muhammad ibn al-Sa'ib al-Kalbi, from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding ﴿And when the division takes place﴾, he said: It is abrogated.

Isma'il ibn Muslim al-Makki said, from Qatadah, from Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said regarding this verse: ﴿And when the division takes place, the close relatives...﴾ The verse that follows abrogated it: ﴿Allah instructs you concerning your children...﴾

Al-'Awfi said, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding this verse: ﴿And when the division takes place, the close relatives...﴾ That was before the obligatory shares (fara'id) were revealed. Then Allah revealed the shares after that, and gave every person with a right his right, and charity was made from what the deceased named. Ibn Mardawayh narrated these.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn al-Sabbah narrated to us, Hajjaj narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj and 'Uthman ibn 'Ata', from 'Ata', from Ibn 'Abbas his saying: ﴿And when the division takes place, the close relatives, the orphans, and the needy...﴾ It was abrogated by the verse of inheritance, so each person was given his share of what the parents and the close relatives leave, whether it is little or much.

And Husayn ibn 'Asim narrated to us, Sa'id ibn 'Amir narrated to us, from Hammam, from Qatadah, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib that he said: It is abrogated. It was before the obligatory shares. Whatever a man left of wealth, the orphan, the poor, the needy, and the relatives were given from it when they were present at the division. Then it was abrogated after that. The inheritance laws abrogated it, so Allah assigned to each person with a right his right, and the bequest became from his wealth, which he bequeaths to his relatives as he wishes.

Malik said, from al-Zuhri, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib: It is abrogated; the inheritance laws and the bequest abrogated it.

Likewise it was narrated from Ikrimah, Abu al-Sha'tha', al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, Abu Salih, Abu Malik, Zayd ibn Aslam, al-Dahhak, 'Ata' al-Khurasani, Muqatil ibn Hayyan, and Rabi'ah ibn Abi 'Abd al-Rahman, that they said: It is abrogated. This is the view of the majority of jurists and the four Imams and their companions.

Ibn Jarir chose here a very strange opinion, and its summary is: the meaning of the verse according to him is ﴿And when the division takes place﴾, that is: when the division of the bequeathed property takes place, the close kin of the deceased are present, ﴿then provide for them from it and speak to them﴾, to the orphans and the needy if they are present, ﴿with kind words﴾. This is the substance of what he attempted after long explanation and repetition, and there is room for objection in it, and Allah knows best.

Al-'Awfi has said, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿And when the division takes place﴾, which is the division of the inheritance. Many others have said likewise, and the meaning according to this is not what Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir followed, may Allah have mercy on him. Rather, the meaning is that when these poor relatives who do not inherit, and the orphans and the needy, are present at the division of a great amount of wealth, their souls long for some of it, when they see this one taking and that one taking and that one taking, while they are despairing with nothing given to them. So Allah the Exalted, who is the Most Kind and Most Merciful, commanded that something be given to them from the estate as a kindness to them, a charity for them, a benefit to them, and a consolation for their brokenness. As Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Eat of its fruit when it bears fruit, and give its due on the day of its harvest.﴾ [al-An'am: 141] And He censured those who carry away wealth secretly, fearing that the needy and those in want would notice them, as He told about the people of the garden: ﴿When they swore that they would surely harvest it in the morning﴾ [al-Qalam: 17], that is, by night. And He said: ﴿So they set off, whispering, that no needy person shall enter it today upon you﴾ [al-Qalam: 23-24]. ﴿Allah destroyed them, and for the disbelievers there are similar things﴾ [Muhammad: 10]. So whoever denies the right of Allah upon him, Allah punishes him in the most precious thing he possesses. For this reason it came in the hadith: "Charity never mixes with wealth except that it ruins it" [narrated by al-Bazzar in his Musnad, no. 881 (Kashf al-Astar), from the hadith of 'A'ishah; al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (3/64): "In it is 'Uthman al-Jumahi; Abu Hatim said: his hadith is written but not used as evidence."], that is, withholding it becomes the cause of the complete loss of that wealth.

* *

And His saying: ﴿And let those fear who, if they left behind them weak offspring, would be anxious for them. So let them fear Allah﴾. 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: This is about a man whose death approaches, and someone hears him making a bequest that would harm his heirs. So Allah the Exalted commands the one who hears it to fear Allah, to guide him, to make him succeed and be steadfast toward what is right, and to look out for his heirs as he would wish to be treated with his own heirs if he feared their loss.

Likewise said Mujahid and others. And it is established in the two Sahihs that when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) entered upon Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas to visit him, he said: "O Messenger of Allah, I have much wealth and only a daughter inherits from me. Should I give two-thirds of my wealth in charity?" He said: "No." He said: "Half?" He said: "No." He said: "A third?" He said: "A third, and a third is much." Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, that you leave your heirs wealthy is better than that you leave them poor, begging from people" [Sahih al-Bukhari no. 2742; Sahih Muslim no. 1628].

And in the Sahih, Ibn 'Abbas said: If only the people would reduce from a third to a quarter, for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "A third, and a third is much" [Sahih al-Bukhari no. 2743; Sahih Muslim no. 1629].

The jurists said: If the heirs of the deceased are wealthy, it is recommended for the deceased to bequeath up to a third in his bequest. And if they are poor, it is recommended that he reduce the third.

It was also said: The meaning of His saying: ﴿And let those fear who, if they left behind them weak offspring, would be anxious for them. So let them fear Allah﴾ [that is] concerning the handling of the wealth of orphans: ﴿and do not consume it extravagantly and hastily, fearing that they will grow up﴾.

Ibn Jarir narrated this through the route of al-'Awfi from Ibn 'Abbas. It is a good opinion, and it is supported by what follows of the warning against consuming the wealth of orphans unjustly. That is: just as you would like your offspring to be treated after you, so treat the people's offspring when you are in charge of them.

Then inform them that whoever consumes the wealth of an orphan unjustly, he is only eating fire into his belly. For this reason He said: ﴿Indeed, those who consume the properties of orphans unjustly are only consuming fire into their bellies, and they will burn in a Blaze﴾. That is: when they consume the wealth of orphans without right, they are only eating a fire that will blaze in their bellies on the Day of Resurrection. And it is established in the two Sahihs from the hadith of Sulayman ibn Bilal, from Thawr ibn Zayd [in another manuscript: "Yazid"], from Salim Abu al-Ghayth, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Avoid the seven destructive sins." It was asked: O Messenger of Allah, what are they?
