He said: "Associating partners with Allah, sorcery, killing a soul which Allah has forbidden except by right, consuming usury, consuming the wealth of an orphan, fleeing on the day of battle, and accusing chaste, believing, unaware women of adultery."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, ʿUbaydah narrated to us [in another manuscript: "ʿAbd Allah"], Abu ʿAbd al-Samad ʿAbd al-ʿAziz ibn ʿAbd al-Samad al-ʿAmmi informed us, Abu Harun al-ʿAbdi narrated to us, from Abu Saʿid al-Khudri, who said: We said, "O Messenger of Allah, what did you see on the night of the Isra'?" He said: "I was taken to a large creation of Allah, men, each man having lips like the lips of a camel. Men were appointed over them who would tear open the cheek of one of them, then a rock of fire would be brought and thrown into the mouth of one of them until it came out from his bottom, and they were making moaning and screaming. I said, 'O Jibril, who are these?' He said: 'These are the ones who consume the wealth of orphans unjustly. They only eat fire into their bellies, and they will soon burn in the Blaze.'"

[Also narrated by al-Tabari in his Tafsir (8/27) through the chain of Mamar from Abu Harun al-ʿAbdi, with the same wording.
Shaykh Ahmad Shakir, may Allah have mercy on him, said: "Abu Harun al-ʿAbdi is ʿAmarah ibn Jawin. He narrated from Abu Saʿid and Ibn ʿUmar, and he is weak. Some said: he is a liar." Al-Daraqutni said: "He was inconsistent, a Kharijite and a Shiite." Ibn Hibban said: "He used to narrate from Abu Saʿid what was not from his narrations. It is not permissible to write his hadith except as a matter of wonder."]

And al-Suddi said: The one who consumes the wealth of an orphan will be raised on the Day of Resurrection with flames of fire coming out of his mouth, his ears, his nose and his eyes, and whoever sees him will recognize him as one who consumed the orphan's wealth.

Abu Bakr Ibn Mardawayh said: Ishaq ibn Ibrahim ibn Zayd narrated to us, Ahmad ibn ʿAmr narrated to us, ʿUqbah ibn Mukram narrated to us, Yunus ibn Bukayr narrated to us, Ziyad ibn al-Mundhir narrated to us, from Nafiʿ ibn al-Harith, from Abu Barzah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "On the Day of Resurrection, people will be raised from their graves with their mouths blazing with fire." It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, who are they?" He said: "Have you not seen that Allah said: ﴿Indeed, those who consume the wealth of orphans unjustly – they only consume fire into their bellies﴾ [the verse]."

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from Abu Zurʿah, from ʿUqbah ibn Mukram. Abu Hatim Ibn Hibban also narrated it in his Sahih, from Ahmad ibn ʿAli ibn al-Muthanna, from ʿUqbah ibn Mukram.
[Sahih Ibn Hibban, no. (2580) "Mawarid," through the chain of Abu Yaʿla, and it is in his Musnad (13/434). In its chain are Ziyad ibn al-Mundhir and his shaykh Nufayʿ ibn al-Harith, both abandoned (matrukan) according to the imams.]

Ibn Mardawayh said: ʿAbd Allah ibn Jaʿfar, Ahmad ibn ʿIsam narrated to us, Abu ʿAmir al-ʿAbdi narrated to us, ʿAbd Allah ibn Jaʿfar al-Zuhri narrated to us, from ʿUthman ibn Muhammad, from al-Maqburi, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I hereby make the property of the two weak ones sacred: the woman and the orphan." [And in its chain is Ahmad ibn ʿIsam al-Mawsili, whom al-Daraqutni declared weak.] Meaning: I enjoin you to avoid their property.

It was previously mentioned in Surat al-Baqarah, through the chain of ʿAta' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: When Allah revealed: ﴿Indeed, those who consume the wealth of orphans unjustly – they only consume fire into their bellies﴾ [the verse], whoever had an orphan in his care separated the orphan's food from his own food and his drink from his own drink. Whatever was left over would be set aside for him until he ate it or it spoiled. This became difficult for them, so they mentioned it to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and Allah revealed: ﴿They ask you about orphans. Say: Reforming them is best. And if you mix with them, then they are your brothers, and Allah knows the corrupter from the reformer﴾ [al-Baqarah: 220].

This verse and the one that follows it, and the verse that ends this surah, are the verses of ʿIlm al-Farāʾid (the science of fixed inheritance shares). This science is derived from these three verses and from the hadiths that are related on the subject, which serve as an explanation of them. We will mention here only what relates to the interpretation of these verses. As for the establishing of legal questions, the presentation of disagreements and evidences, and the arguments among the imams, their place is the book "al-Aḥkām" (the legal rulings). And from Allah alone is help sought.

The encouragement to learn the farāʾid has been related, and these specific farāʾid are among the most important of that. Abu Dawud and Ibn Majah related, from the hadith of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ziyād ibn Anʿam al-Ifrīqī, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Rāfiʿ al-Tanūkhī, from ʿAbdullah ibn ʿAmr, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Knowledge is of three kinds, and whatever is beyond that is surplus: a clear verse (āyah muḥkamah), or an established sunnah, or a just obligation (farīḍah ʿādilah)."[[Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 2885; Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 54. It was also related by al-Ḥākim in al-Mustadrak (4/332), al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan al-Kubra (6/208), and al-Dāraqutni in al-Sunan (4/67), through ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ziyād al-Ifrīqī with this same wording. al-Dhahabi said regarding this hadith and the one after it: "Both hadiths are weak."]]

And from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O Abu Hurayrah, learn the farāʾid and teach them, for it is half of knowledge, and it is forgotten, and it is the first thing that will be taken away from my ummah."

Ibn Majah related it, and in its chain there is weakness.[[Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 2719. It was also related by al-Dāraqutni (4/67), al-Ḥākim (4/332), and al-Bayhaqi (6/208), through Ḥafs ibn ʿUmar ibn Abi al-ʿAṭṭāf. al-Dhahabi said: "In it is Ḥafs ibn ʿUmar ibn Abi al-ʿAṭṭāf, who is utterly unreliable (wāhin bi-marrah)."]]

It has also been related from the hadith of ʿAbdullah ibn Masʿud and Abu Saʿid, but there is scrutiny in each of them.[[The hadith of Ibn Masʿud is: "Learn the farāʾid and teach them, for I am a man who will be taken (away)..." until the end of the hadith. It was related by al-Ḥākim in al-Mustadrak (4/333).]] Sufyan ibn ʿUyaynah said: "He called the farāʾid half of knowledge only because all people are tested by it."

Al-Bukhari said, when interpreting this verse: Ibrahim ibn Musa related to us, Hisham related to us that Ibn Jurayj informed them, saying: Ibn al-Munkadir informed me, from Jabir ibn ʿAbdullah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and Abu Bakr visited me while I was ill in Banu Salamah, walking on foot. The Prophet (ﷺ) found me unable to comprehend anything, so he asked for water and performed ablution with it, then sprinkled it upon me, and I regained consciousness. I said: "O Messenger of Allah, what do you command me to do with my wealth?" Then the verse was revealed: ﴿Allah instructs you concerning your children: for the male, what is equal to the share of two females﴾.

It was also related by Muslim and al-Nasāʾi, from the hadith of Ḥajjāj ibn Muḥammad al-Aʿwar, from Ibn Jurayj with it. And the whole group (al-jamāʿah) related it from the hadith of Sufyan ibn ʿUyaynah, from Muḥammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Jabir.[[The route of Sufyan was related by al-Bukhari in his Ṣaḥīḥ (no. 5651), Muslim in his Ṣaḥīḥ (no. 1616), Abu Dawud in al-Sunan (no. 2886), al-Tirmidhi in al-Sunan (no. 2097), al-Nasāʾi in al-Sunan (1/87), and Ibn Majah in al-Sunan (no. 2728). The route of Ibn Jurayj was related by al-Bukhari (no. 4577) and Muslim (no. 1616), and al-Nasāʾi al-Kubra (no. 6323).]]

Another hadith from Jabir concerning the occasion of revelation of the verse: Imam Ahmad said: Zakariyya ibn ʿAdi related to us, ʿUbaydullah, who is Ibn ʿAmr al-Raqqi, related to us, from ʿAbdullah ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAqil, from Jabir, who said: The wife of Saʿd ibn al-Rabīʿ came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, these are the two daughters of Saʿd ibn al-Rabīʿ. Their father was killed with you at Uhud as a martyr, and their paternal uncle has taken their wealth, leaving them no wealth at all, and they cannot be married unless they have wealth." He said: So he (ﷺ) said: "Allah will decide concerning that." He said: Then the verse of inheritance was revealed, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent for their paternal uncle and said: "Give the two daughters of Saʿd two-thirds, and their mother one-eighth, and whatever remains is for you."

It was related by Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, and Ibn Majah, through several routes, from ʿAbdullah ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAqil, with it. al-Tirmidhi said: "It is not known except from his narration."[[al-Musnad (3/352); Sunan Abi Dawud, nos. 2891, 2892; Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 2092; Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 2720.]]

The apparent view is that the first hadith of Jabir was the occasion for the revelation of the last verse of this surah, as will come, for at that time he had sisters and no daughters, and he was to be inherited from as a kalālah (one with neither ascendant nor descendant heirs). But we have mentioned the hadith here following al-Bukhari, may Allah have mercy on him, for he mentioned it here. The second hadith from Jabir is more fitting for the revelation of this verse, and Allah knows best.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Allah instructs you concerning your children: for the male, what is equal to the share of two females﴾ means: He commands you to be just toward them. For the people of the Jāhiliyyah used to make all the inheritance for the males to the exclusion of the females, so Allah commanded equality between them in the basic principle of inheritance, but He differentiated between the two categories, making for the male the equivalent of the share of two females. That is because a man needs to bear the burden of maintenance, expenses, the hardship of trade and earning, and enduring difficulty, so it was fitting that he be given twice what the female receives.

Some intelligent people have deduced from His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Allah instructs you concerning your children: for the male, what is equal to the share of two females﴾ that He is more merciful to His creation than a parent is to his child, since He enjoined parents concerning their children. Thus it is known that He is more merciful to them than they are, as has come in the authentic hadith.

The Prophet (ﷺ) saw a woman among the captives searching around for her child. When she found him, she took him, pressed him to her chest, and nursed him. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to his companions: "Do you think this woman would throw her child into the fire while she is able not to?" They said: "No, by Allah, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "By Allah, Allah is more merciful to His servants than this woman is to her child."

Al-Bukhari also said here: Muḥammad ibn Yusuf related to us, from Warqāʾ, from Ibn Abi Najīḥ, from ʿAṭāʾ, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: "The wealth used to belong to the child, and the bequest was to the parents. Then Allah abrogated (naskh) from that what He willed: He made for the male the equivalent of the share of two females, and He made for each of the two parents a sixth and a third, made for the wife an eighth and a quarter, and for the husband a half and a quarter."[[Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhari, no. 4578.]]

al-ʿAwfi related from Ibn ʿAbbas concerning his saying: ﴿Allah instructs you concerning your children: for the male, what is equal to the share of two females﴾: When the shares were revealed, which Allah had prescribed, for the male and female child and the two parents, people disliked them, or some of them did, and they said: "The woman is given a quarter or an eighth, and the daughter is given a half, and the young boy is given (a share), yet none of these fights the people or takes booty. Be silent about this hadith; perhaps the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) will forget it, or we will say something to him and he will change it." Then some of them said: "O Messenger of Allah, we give the girl half of what her father left, though she does not ride a horse nor fight the people; and we give the young boy an inheritance though he is of no benefit." They were doing this in the Jāhiliyyah: they did not give inheritance except to one who fought the people, and they gave it to the eldest, then the next eldest. Ibn Abi Ḥātim and Ibn Jarir also related it.

* *

His saying: ﴿But if they (the daughters) are more than two women, then for them is two-thirds of what he left﴾. Some people said: the word "fawqa" (more than) is superfluous, and its meaning is: "If they are two women." As in His saying: ﴿So strike above the necks﴾ [al-Anfal: 12]. This is not accepted, neither here nor there, for there is nothing superfluous in the Qur'an without benefit, and this is impossible. Furthermore, His saying: ﴿then for them is two-thirds of what he left﴾ — if what they said were intended, He would have said: "then for both of them is two-thirds of what he left." The fact that the two daughters receive two-thirds is derived from the ruling concerning the two sisters in the last verse, for He, exalted is He, ruled there that the two sisters receive two-thirds. And if two sisters inherit two-thirds, then two daughters inheriting two-thirds is more fitting by way of priority (bi-ṭarīq al-awlā). And it has already passed in the hadith of Jabir that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) ruled that the two daughters of Saʿd ibn al-Rabīʿ receive two-thirds. Thus the Book and the Sunnah indicate this. Also, He said: ﴿But if there is only one, then for her is half﴾. So if the two daughters also had a half, He would have stated it explicitly. When He ruled for the single one alone with half, it indicates that two daughters are in the same ruling as three. And Allah knows best.

* *

His saying: ﴿And for his parents, to each one of them is a sixth of what he left, if he has children. But if he has no children and the parents inherit from him, then for his mother is a third. And if he has brothers, then for his mother is a sixth﴾ — to the end of it. The parents have several situations in inheritance:

The first: that they both combine with the children. Then each of them is assigned a sixth. If the deceased has only one daughter, she is assigned a half, and the two parents each receive a sixth, and the father takes the other sixth by way of ʿaṣabah (residuary). Thus, in this case, he combines the fixed share (farḍ) and ʿaṣabah.

The second situation: that the two parents alone inherit. Then the mother is assigned a third, and the father takes the remainder by pure ʿaṣabah, and he has taken twice what was assigned to the mother, which is two-thirds. If with them, in this case, there is a husband or a wife, the husband takes a half and the wife a quarter. Then the scholars differed about what the mother takes after the fixed share of the husband or wife, according to three opinions:

The first: that she takes a third of the remainder in both cases, because the remainder is considered as if it were the whole inheritance in relation to them. Allah has given her half of what He gave the father, so she takes a third of the remainder, and he takes two-thirds of it. This is the view of ʿUmar and ʿUthman, and the more sound of the two reports from ʿAli. Ibn Masʿud and Zayd ibn Thabit also hold it, and it is the view of the Seven Jurists (al-fuqahāʾ al-sabʿah), the Four Imams, and the majority of the scholars, may Allah have mercy on them all.

The second opinion: that she takes a third of the whole estate, based on the generality of His saying: ﴿But if he has no children and the parents inherit from him, then for his mother is a third﴾, for the verse is more general than whether there is a husband or wife with her or not. This is the view of Ibn ʿAbbas. It was also related from ʿAli and Muʿadh ibn Jabal something similar. Shurayḥ and Dawud ibn ʿAli al-Ẓāhiri also hold it, and Imam Abu al-Ḥusayn Muḥammad ibn ʿAbdullah ibn al-Labbān al-Basri chose it in his book "al-Ījāz fī ʿIlm al-Farāʾid."

This is open to scrutiny, rather it is weak, because the apparent meaning of the verse applies only when she inherits the entire estate alone. But in this issue, the husband or wife takes the fixed share, and the remainder is treated as if it were the whole estate, so she takes a third of it, as has passed.

The third opinion is that she takes a third of the entire estate in the case of the wife. The wife takes a quarter, which is three out of twelve, and the mother takes a third, which is four, leaving five for the father. In the case of the husband, however, the mother takes a third of the remainder, so that she does not take more than the father would have taken had she received a third of the whole estate. The case is then resolved from six: the husband receives half, which is three; the mother receives a third of what remains, which is one share; and the father receives what is left after that, which is two shares. This view is attributed to Muhammad ibn Sirin, may Allah have mercy on him. It combines the first two opinions, agreeing with each of them in one case, and it is also weak. The sound view is the first, and Allah knows best.

The third state of the parents is when they are together with siblings, whether full siblings, paternal siblings or maternal siblings. The siblings do not inherit anything alongside the father, but they still reduce the mother's share from a third to a sixth. So a sixth is prescribed for her in their presence. If there is no heir other than her and the father, the father takes the remainder.

The ruling on two brothers in what we have mentioned is the same as the ruling on siblings according to the majority of scholars. Al-Bayhaqi narrated through the chain of Shu'bah, the client (mawla) of Ibn 'Abbas, that Ibn 'Abbas came to 'Uthman and said: "Two brothers do not reduce the mother from the third." Allah the Exalted says: ﴿But if he has brothers﴾, and two brothers are not "brothers" in the language of your people. 'Uthman said: "I cannot change what was before me." He continued in the cities, and people inherited by it.

There is some doubt about the soundness of this report. Shu'bah here was criticised by Malik ibn Anas. If it were authentically from Ibn 'Abbas, his close companions would have adopted it, but what is transmitted from them is the opposite.

'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi al-Zinad narrated from Kharijah ibn Zayd, from his father, that he said: "Two brothers are called siblings (ikhwah)." I have devoted a separate treatise to this question.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn al-Mughirah narrated to us, Yazid ibn Zuray' narrated to us, from Sa'id, from Qatadah, concerning the words of Allah: ﴿But if he has brothers, then for his mother is a sixth﴾: "They harm the mother, and they do not inherit. A single brother does not reduce her from the third, but more than one does." The scholars used to hold that they reduced their mother from the third only because their father is responsible for their marriage and their maintenance, not their mother.

This is a good statement. However, it is reported from Ibn 'Abbas with a sound chain that he held that the sixth which they took from their mother belongs to them. This is an anomalous (shadh) view. Ibn Jarir narrated it in his Tafsir, saying:

Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Ma'mar informed us, from Ibn Tawus, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "The sixth which the siblings took from their mother is for them, for they only reduced their mother from it so that it would be theirs rather than their father's."

Then Ibn Jarir said: "This view contradicts the entire community." He also narrated to me: Yunus informed us, Sufyan informed us, 'Amr informed us, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad, from Ibn 'Abbas, that he said: "Kalalah is the one who has neither child nor parent."

* *

As for His words: ﴿after any bequest he makes or debt﴾, the scholars, both earlier and later, agreed that the debt takes precedence over the bequest. On careful reflection, this is understood from the implication (fahwa) of the noble verse. Imam Ahmad, al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Majah and the compilers of the exegetical works narrated, through the report of Abu Ishaq, from al-Harith ibn 'Abd Allah al-A'war, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib [may Allah be pleased with him] that he said: "You recite: ﴿after any bequest he makes or debt﴾, but the Messenger of Allah ﷺ judged the debt before the bequest. Full brothers (a'yan bani al-umm) inherit from one another to the exclusion of half-brothers from the father's side: a man inherits from his full brother rather than from his half-brother." Al-Tirmidhi then said: "We do not know it except through the hadith of al-Harith al-A'war, and some scholars have spoken about him."

[Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 2094.]

I say: However, he was a memoriser of the fara'id, careful about them and about calculation. Abu Bakr ibn Abi Dawud said: "al-Harith was the most knowledgeable, the most learned in the fara'id and the best at calculation among people; he learned the fara'id from 'Ali." It was said to al-Sha'bi: "Did you used to visit al-Harith?" He said: "Yes, I used to visit him to learn calculation; he was the best of people at it."

But he was weak in his narration of hadith. A group of scholars declared him weak, including al-Sha'bi, Jarir, Ibn Mahdi, Ibn al-Madini, Yahya ibn Ma'in, Abu Zur'ah and Abu Hatim. See Tahdhib al-Kamal (5/244).

[Allah knows best.]

* *

As for His words: ﴿Your fathers and your sons—you do not know which of them is nearer to you in benefit﴾: this means that We prescribed shares for fathers and for sons, and We made all equal in the basic principle of inheritance, in contrast to what was practised in the Jahiliyyah, and in contrast to what was the case at the beginning of Islam, when wealth belonged to the child and the bequest was for the parents, as mentioned earlier from Ibn 'Abbas. Allah abrogated (naskh) that practice in favour of this arrangement, and prescribed for each group according to their circumstances. A person may receive worldly benefit, or otherworldly benefit, or both, from his father that he does not receive from his son, and it may be the reverse. Therefore He said: ﴿Your fathers and your sons—you do not know which of them is nearer to you in benefit﴾. That is, as though the benefit is expected and hoped for from one and likewise from the other. For this reason We prescribed for this one and for that one, and We made the two categories equal in the basic principle of inheritance. Allah knows best.

* *

As for His words: ﴿an obligation from Allah﴾: this means that this detailed distribution of the inheritance that we have described, and the giving of more to some heirs than to others, is an obligation from Allah. He has decreed and judged it. Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise, who places things in their proper places and gives each what he deserves according to his circumstances. Therefore He said: ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever Knowing and Wise﴾.

He says, may He be exalted: ﴿And for you, O men, is half of what your wives leave, if they die without children.﴾ ﴿But if they have a child, then for you is a quarter of what they leave, after any bequest they make or debt.﴾ It has already been stated that debt takes precedence over bequest, and after it comes the bequest, then the inheritance. This is a matter on which the scholars agree (ijma'). The ruling for the children of sons, however far down they go, is the same as the ruling for the children of the loins (direct children).

Then He said: ﴿And for them is a quarter of what you leave, if you have no child. But if you have a child, then for them is an eighth of what you leave.﴾ [[Addition from manuscripts ja, ra, alif.]] And the wife and the two wives, the three and the four, share equally in the quarter or the eighth.

* *

His saying: ﴿after a bequest﴾, etc. The discussion of it is as previously stated.

* *

His saying: ﴿And if a man leaves an inheritance as kalalah (one who leaves neither ascendants nor descendants)...﴾ Kalalah is derived from the iklil (crown), which encircles the head from its sides. What is meant here is one who inherits from the collateral relatives (hawashi), not from his roots (usul) or branches (furu'), as al-Sha'bi narrated from Abu Bakr al-Siddiq: he was asked about the kalalah and said, "I will give my opinion on it. If it is correct, it is from Allah; if it is wrong, it is from me and from Satan, and Allah and His Messenger are innocent of it: the kalalah is one who has neither child nor parent." When 'Umar ibn al-Khattab became caliph, he said, "I am too shy to oppose Abu Bakr in an opinion he held." Ibn Jarir and others narrated it.

Ibn Abi Hatim said in his tafsir, may Allah have mercy on him: "Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Yazid related to us, Sufyan related to us, from Sulayman al-Ahwal, from Tawus, who said: I heard 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abbas say: 'I was the last of the people to have an agreement (ahd) with 'Umar ibn al-Khattab. I heard him say: The saying is what I said, and what I said, and what I said.' He said: The kalalah is one who has neither child nor parent." [[Ibn Abi Hatim, Tafsir (2/l. 115); Sa'id ibn Mansur narrated it in al-Sunan, no. 589, through Sufyan ibn 'Uyayna.]]

Likewise said 'Ali ibn Abi Talib and Ibn Mas'ud. It is reported authentically from more than one line from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abbas and Zayd ibn Thabit. This is the view of al-Sha'bi, al-Nakha'i, al-Hasan al-Basri, Qatadah, Jabir ibn Zayd, and al-Hakam. It is the view of the people of Madina, Kufa and Basra. It is the opinion of the seven jurists (fuqaha' al-sab'a), the four imams, and the majority of the early and later scholars, indeed all of them. Many have reported the consensus on this, and a marfu' hadith (one traced to the Prophet) has also been transmitted about it. Abu al-Husayn ibn al-Labban said: "It has been narrated from Ibn 'Abbas something that contradicts this, namely that the kalalah is one who has no child. But the authentic report from him is the first, and perhaps the narrator did not grasp what he meant."

* *

His saying: ﴿And he has a brother or a sister﴾, that is, from the mother's side, as is found in the recitation of some of the early scholars, among them Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas. Abu Bakr al-Siddiq also explained it this way, as narrated by Qatadah from him: ﴿Then each of the two has a sixth. But if there are more than that, they share in a third.﴾

The brothers from the mother differ from the rest of the heirs in several respects. First, they inherit together with the one through whom they are related, who is the mother. Second, their males and females are equal. Third, they inherit only if the deceased is inherited as kalalah, so they do not inherit alongside a father, a grandfather, a child, or a son's child. Fourth, they are not increased beyond a third, however many their males and females are.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Yunus related to us, Ibn Wahb related to us, Yunus informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, decided that the inheritance of the brothers from the mother is shared among them, the male equal to the female. Muhammad ibn Shihab al-Zuhri said: "I do not think 'Umar decided this until he learned it from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and (he decided it) in accordance with this verse in which Allah the Exalted said: ﴿But if there are more than that, they share in a third.﴾"

The scholars differed on the case known as al-Mushtarakah (the shared case), which is: a husband, a mother or a grandmother, two sons from the mother and one or more from both parents. According to the view of the majority: the husband has a half, the mother or grandmother a sixth, and the children of the mother a third; the children of both parents share with them in that third by the common portion, namely the brothers from the mother.

This case occurred in the time of the Commander of the Faithful 'Umar ibn al-Khattab. He gave the husband a half, the mother a sixth, and made the third for the children of the mother. The children of both parents said to him: "O Commander of the Faithful, suppose our father was a donkey; are we not from one mother?" So he made them share together.

The sharing (tashrik) was authentically reported from him and from the Commander of the Faithful 'Uthman. It is one of the two reports from Ibn Mas'ud, Zayd ibn Thabit, and Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them. This is the view of Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, Shurayh al-Qadi, Masruq, Tawus, Muhammad ibn Sirin, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz, al-Thawri, Shurayk, and it is the position of Malik, al-Shafi'i, and Ishaq ibn Rahawayh.

'Ali ibn Abi Talib did not share among them. Rather, he gave the third to the children of the mother, and nothing to the children of both parents in this situation, because they are residual heirs ('asaba). Waki' ibn al-Jarrah said: "Nothing is reported differently from him on this." This is also the view of Ubayy ibn Ka'b and Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, and it is the well-known position of Ibn 'Abbas. It is the doctrine of al-Sha'bi, Ibn Abi Layla, Abu Yusuf, Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, al-Hasan ibn Ziyad, Zufar ibn al-Hudhayl, the Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal, Yahya ibn Adam, Nu'aym ibn Hammad, Abu Thawr, and Dawud ibn 'Ali al-Zahiri. Abu al-Husayn ibn al-Labban, the expert in inheritance shares (faradi), chose it in his book al-Ijaz, may Allah have mercy on him.

* *

His saying: ﴿after a bequest that is made, or a debt, without causing harm﴾, that is, so that his bequest is according to justice, not for the purpose of harm, oppression, or injustice, such as depriving some of the heirs, reducing their share, or increasing it beyond what Allah has decreed for him in the apportioned shares. Whoever strives for that is like one who opposes Allah in His wisdom and His distribution. For this reason Ibn Abi Hatim said:

My father related to us, Abu al-Nadr al-Dimashqi al-Faradisi related to us, 'Umar ibn al-Mughira related to us, from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, from the Prophet ﷺ who said: "Harm in a bequest is among the major sins."

Ibn Jarir also narrated it through this 'Umar ibn al-Mughira. He is Abu Hafs, a Basran who settled in al-Masisa. Abu al-Qasim Ibn 'Asakir said: "He is known as the mufti of the poor." Many of the imams narrated from him. Abu Hatim al-Razi said of him: "He is a shaykh." 'Ali ibn al-Madini said: "He is unknown; I do not know him." However, al-Nasa'i narrated it in his Sunan from 'Ali ibn Hujr, from 'Ali ibn Mushir, from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, as a mawquf (a report stopping at the companion): "Harm in a bequest is among the major sins." Likewise Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj, from 'A'idh ibn Habib, from Dawud ibn Abi Hind. Ibn Jarir narrated it from the hadith of a group of memorizers (huffaz), from Dawud, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas as a mawquf. In some of these it says: "Ibn 'Abbas used to recite: ﴿without causing harm﴾."

Ibn Juraij said: "The sound report is the mawquf."

For this reason the imams differed about acknowledgement of a debt in favour of an heir: is it valid or not? There are two views. The first: it is not valid, because it is a place of suspicion that he may have bequeathed to him by the form of acknowledgement. It is established in the authentic hadith that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Allah has given every rightful person his right, so there is no bequest to an heir." This is the view of Abu Hanifa, Malik, Ahmad ibn Hanbal, and the older opinion of al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on them. In his newer opinion he held that the acknowledgement is valid. This is the view of Tawus, 'Ata', al-Hasan, and 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz.

This is also the choice of Abu 'Abd Allah al-Bukhari in his Sahih. He argued that Rafi' ibn Khadij bequeathed that the Fazariyya (his wife) should not be uncovered regarding what her door had closed upon. He said: "Some people said: his acknowledgement is not permissible because of the bad opinion about him toward the heirs. The Prophet ﷺ said: 'Beware of suspicion, for suspicion is the most false of speech.' Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, Allah commands you to render trusts to their owners﴾ [An-Nisa: 58], and did not single out an heir or anyone else." End of what he mentioned.

So whenever the acknowledgement is valid and corresponds to what is in reality, this disagreement applies. But whenever it is a trick and a means to increase some heirs and decrease others, it is forbidden by consensus and by the explicit text of this noble verse: ﴿without causing harm, as a commandment from Allah. And Allah is All-Knowing, Most Forbearing.﴾ [[Addition from manuscript alif.]] [Then Allah said.]

*That is, these are the obligatory shares and measures that Allah has set for the heirs according to their nearness to the deceased, their need for him, and their lack of him when he is absent. "They are the limits of Allah, so do not transgress them or go beyond them." For this reason He said: ﴿And whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger﴾, meaning in these matters, so that no heir increases another's share or diminishes it through a trick or a stratagem, but leaves them under the ruling of Allah, His obligation, and His division. ﴿He will admit him to gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein; and that is the great achievement. And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger and transgresses His limits, He will admit him to a Fire, abiding therein, and for him is a humiliating punishment.﴾ That is, because he has altered what Allah has ruled and opposed Allah in His judgment. This only proceeds from not being content with what Allah has apportioned and decreed, and for this reason He recompenses him with humiliation in the painful, lasting punishment.

Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Ma'mar informed us, from Ayyub, from Ash'ath ibn Abd Allah, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, a man may do the deeds of the people of goodness for seventy years, and then when he makes a bequest he deviates in his bequest, so his life ends with the evil of his deeds, and he enters the Fire. And indeed, a man may do the deeds of the people of evil for seventy years, and then he is just in his bequest, so his life ends with the good of his deeds, and he enters Paradise." He said: Then Abu Hurayrah said: "Recite if you wish: ﴿These are the limits of Allah﴾ until His words: ﴿a humiliating punishment.﴾"

[And] Abu Dawud said in the chapter on harm in bequests in his Sunan: Abdah ibn Abd Allah narrated to us, Abd al-Samad informed us, Nasr ibn Ali al-Haddani narrated to us, al-Ash'ath ibn Abd Allah ibn Jabir al-Haddani narrated to us, Shahr ibn Hawshab narrated to me, that Abu Hurayrah narrated to him that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, a man or a woman may work in obedience to Allah for sixty years, then death comes to them both, and they cause harm in the bequest, so the Fire becomes obligatory for them both." And he said: Abu Hurayrah recited from here: ﴿after any bequest that is made or debt, without causing harm﴾ until he reached: ﴿[And] that is the great achievement.﴾

Likewise it was narrated by al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah from the hadith of Ibn Abd Allah ibn Jabir al-Haddani with it. Al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan gharib" (a good hadith that is narrated through a single chain). The wording of Imam Ahmad is more complete and fuller.

*That is, these are the obligatory shares and measures that Allah has set for the heirs according to their nearness to the deceased, their need for him, and their lack of him when he is absent. "They are the limits of Allah, so do not transgress them or go beyond them." For this reason He said: ﴿And whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger﴾, meaning in these matters, so that no heir increases another's share or diminishes it through a trick or a stratagem, but leaves them under the ruling of Allah, His obligation, and His division. ﴿He will admit him to gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein; and that is the great achievement. And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger and transgresses His limits, He will admit him to a Fire, abiding therein, and for him is a humiliating punishment.﴾ That is, because he has altered what Allah has ruled and opposed Allah in His judgment. This only proceeds from not being content with what Allah has apportioned and decreed, and for this reason He recompenses him with humiliation in the painful, lasting punishment.

Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Ma'mar informed us, from Ayyub, from Ash'ath ibn Abd Allah, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, a man may do the deeds of the people of goodness for seventy years, and then when he makes a bequest he deviates in his bequest, so his life ends with the evil of his deeds, and he enters the Fire. And indeed, a man may do the deeds of the people of evil for seventy years, and then he is just in his bequest, so his life ends with the good of his deeds, and he enters Paradise." He said: Then Abu Hurayrah said: "Recite if you wish: ﴿These are the limits of Allah﴾ until His words: ﴿a humiliating punishment.﴾"

[And] Abu Dawud said in the chapter on harm in bequests in his Sunan: Abdah ibn Abd Allah narrated to us, Abd al-Samad informed us, Nasr ibn Ali al-Haddani narrated to us, al-Ash'ath ibn Abd Allah ibn Jabir al-Haddani narrated to us, Shahr ibn Hawshab narrated to me, that Abu Hurayrah narrated to him that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, a man or a woman may work in obedience to Allah for sixty years, then death comes to them both, and they cause harm in the bequest, so the Fire becomes obligatory for them both." And he said: Abu Hurayrah recited from here: ﴿after any bequest that is made or debt, without causing harm﴾ until he reached: ﴿[And] that is the great achievement.﴾

Likewise it was narrated by al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah from the hadith of Ibn Abd Allah ibn Jabir al-Haddani with it. Al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan gharib" (a good hadith that is narrated through a single chain). The wording of Imam Ahmad is more complete and fuller.

The legal ruling at the beginning of Islam was that if a married woman committed adultery and her adultery was established by the testimony of just witnesses, she was confined to a house and not allowed to leave it until she died. This is why He said: ﴿And those of your women who commit lewdness﴾, meaning adultery, ﴿call four witnesses against them from among you. And if they testify, confine them to houses until death takes them or God ordains for them a way.﴾ The "way" that God ordained is the abrogating ruling (al-nasikh, the ruling that cancels an earlier one) that replaced this.

Ibn 'Abbas said: The ruling remained so until God sent down Surat al-Nur, and it abrogated this with flogging or stoning.

Allah the Exalted says: "Allah accepts repentance only from those who do evil in ignorance and then repent soon. Those are the ones to whom Allah will turn in forgiveness, and Allah is ever Knowing and Wise." Verse 17. And He says: "And repentance is not accepted from those who commit evil deeds until, when death approaches one of them, he says, 'Indeed, I have repented now.'" Verse 18.

Allah says: Allah accepts repentance only from one who does evil in ignorance and then repents, even if it is before he sees the angel [who takes] his soul and before the death rattle (al-gharghara).

Mujahid and others said: Everyone who disobeys Allah, whether by mistake or deliberately, is ignorant until he desists from the sin.

Qatada, on the authority of Abu al-'Aliya, said that he used to narrate that the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to say: Every sin a servant commits is done in ignorance. Related by Ibn Jarir.

'Abd al-Razzaq said: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatada, who said: The Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gathered and held that everything disobeyed by which is ignorance, whether it was done deliberately or otherwise.

Ibn Jurayj said: 'Abd Allah ibn Kathir informed me, from Mujahid, who said: Everyone who acts in disobedience to Allah is ignorant at the time he does it. Ibn Jurayj said: 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah said something similar to me.

Abu Salih said, on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas: He does evil out of his ignorance.

'Ali ibn Abi Talha said, on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas, regarding ﴿then repent soon﴾: It is the period between now and when he sees the Angel of Death. Al-Dahhak said: Whatever is before death is "soon." Qatada and al-Suddi said: As long as he is in good health; this is also narrated from Ibn 'Abbas. Al-Hasan al-Basri said regarding ﴿then repent soon﴾: As long as he has not begun the death rattle. 'Ikrima said: The whole of this world is "soon."

Narrations of hadith on this matter:

Imam Ahmad said: 'Ali ibn 'Ayyash and 'Isam ibn Khalid told us, both saying: Ibn Thawban told us, from his father, from Makhul, from Jubayr ibn Nufayr, from Ibn 'Umar, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Indeed Allah accepts the repentance of the servant as long as he has not begun the death rattle."

Al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah also related it through the hadith of 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Thabit ibn Thawban, with the same chain. Al-Tirmidhi said: Hasan gharib. In the Sunan of Ibn Majah it occurs as "from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr," which is an error; it is in fact 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar ibn al-Khattab.

Another route from Ibn 'Umar: Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh said: Muhammad ibn Ma'mar told us, 'Abd Allah ibn al-Hasan al-Khurasani told us, Yahya ibn 'Abd Allah al-Babulti told us, Ayyub ibn Nahik al-Halabi told us, saying: I heard 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah say: I heard 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar say: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "No believing servant repents a month before death except that Allah accepts it from him, and less than that; and a day and an hour before his death, if Allah knows of his repentance and sincerity towards Him, He accepts it from him." (Abu Nu'aym related it in al-Hilya through Yahya ibn 'Abd Allah from Ayyub ibn Nahik, then said: This is a gharib hadith from 'Ata', narrated solely by Ayyub ibn Nahik.)

Another hadith: Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said: Shu'ba told us, Ibrahim ibn Maymun informed us, a man from Mil'han called Ayyub informed me, who said: I heard 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar say: Whoever repents a year before his death is forgiven, whoever repents a month before his death is forgiven, whoever repents a week before his death is forgiven, whoever repents a day before his death is forgiven, whoever repents an hour before his death is forgiven. I said to him: Allah only said: ﴿Allah accepts repentance only from those who do evil in ignorance and then repent soon﴾. He said: I only relate to you what I heard from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). (Tayalisi's Musnad, p. 301, where it is from the Musnad of 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As; Ahmad related it in his Musnad through 'Affan from Shu'ba similarly, from the Musnad of 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As. Al-Haythami said in al-Majma': "It contains an unnamed narrator, and the rest of its narrators are trustworthy.") Likewise Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi, Abu 'Umar al-Hawdi and Abu 'Amir al-'Aqadi related it from Shu'ba.

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Husayn ibn Muhammad told us, Muhammad ibn Mutarrif told us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Baylamani, who said: Four of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gathered, and one of them said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Indeed Allah accepts the repentance of the servant before he dies by a day." The second said: Did you hear this from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)? He said: Yes. He said: And I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Indeed Allah accepts the repentance of the servant before he dies by half a day." The third said: Did you hear this from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)? He said: Yes. He said: And I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Indeed Allah accepts the repentance of the servant before he dies by a forenoon." The fourth said: Did you hear this from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)? He said: Yes. He said: And I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Indeed Allah [the Exalted] accepts the repentance of the servant as long as he has not begun the death rattle with his soul." Sa'id ibn Mansur related it from al-Darawardi, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Baylamani, mentioning something close to it.

Another hadith: Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh said: Ishaq ibn Ibrahim ibn Zayd told us, 'Imran ibn 'Abd al-Rahim told us, 'Uthman ibn al-Haytham told us, 'Awf told us, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, from Abu Hurayra who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah accepts the repentance of His servant as long as he has not begun the death rattle." (Its chain contains 'Imran ibn 'Abd al-Rahim ibn Abi al-Ward. Al-Sulaymani said: "There is scrutiny concerning him; he is the one who fabricated the hadith of Abu Hanifa from Malik, may Allah have mercy on them both." Abu al-Shaykh said: He was accused of Rafd. Lisan al-Mizan.)

Hadiths on this matter that are mursal:

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Bashshar told us, Ibn Abi 'Adi told us, from 'Awf, from al-Hasan who said: It reached me that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah accepts the repentance of the servant as long as he has not begun the death rattle." This is a mursal, hasan, from al-Hasan al-Basri, may Allah have mercy on him.

Another: Ibn Jarir also said, may Allah have mercy on him: Ibn Bashshar told us, Mu'adh ibn Hisham told us, my father told me, from Qatada, from al-'Ala' ibn Ziyad, from Abu Ayyub Bushayr ibn Ka'b, that the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah accepts the repentance of the servant as long as he has not begun the death rattle."

And Ibn Bashshar told us, 'Abd al-A'la told us, from Sa'id, from Qatada, from 'Ubada ibn al-Samit, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, and mentioned something similar. (Qatada did not hear from 'Ubada ibn al-Samit.)

Another report: Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Bashshar told us, Abu Dawud told us, 'Imran told us, from Qatada who said: We were with Anas ibn Malik, and Abu Qilaba was present, and Abu Qilaba narrated and said: When Allah cursed Iblis, he asked Him for respite, and he said: By Your might and majesty, I will not leave the heart of the son of Adam as long as the spirit is in him. Allah said: By My might, I will not withhold repentance from him as long as the spirit is in him.

This has also come in a marfu' hadith, related by Imam Ahmad in his Musnad through 'Amr ibn Abi 'Amr and Abu al-Haytham al-'Utwari, both from Abu Sa'id, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Iblis said: By Your might, I will not cease to mislead them as long as their spirits are in their bodies. Allah, mighty and majestic, said: By My might and My majesty, I will not cease to forgive them as long as they seek My forgiveness." (Musnad, 3/76.)

These hadiths indicate that whoever repents to Allah, mighty and majestic, while still hoping for life, his repentance is accepted. For this reason Allah said: ﴿Those are the ones to whom Allah will turn in forgiveness, and Allah is ever Knowing and Wise.﴾ As for when despair of life sets in, the angel is seen, the spirit rattles in the throat, the chest becomes constricted, it reaches the windpipe, and the soul gurgles upward in the passages, then no repentance is accepted at that time, and "it is no time for escape." For this reason He said: ﴿And repentance is not accepted from those who commit evil deeds until, when death approaches one of them, he says, "Indeed, I have repented now."﴾ This is like His saying: ﴿So when they saw Our might, they said, "We believe in Allah alone and disbelieve in what we used to associate with Him." But their faith was not beneficial to them when they saw Our might.﴾ (Ghafir: 84–85). And like His judgment that the repentance of the people of the earth is not accepted when they see the sun rising from its west, as He said: ﴿On the day when some of the signs of your Lord come, no soul will benefit from its faith if it had not believed before or earned good through its faith.﴾ (al-An'am: 158).

* *

His saying: ﴿And none of those who die while they are disbelievers﴾ means: when the disbeliever dies in his disbelief and polytheism, his regret and repentance do not benefit him, and nothing will be accepted from him as ransom, even if it were the earth filled with gold.

Ibn 'Abbas, Abu al-'Aliya and al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: ﴿And none of those who die while they are disbelievers﴾ — they said: It was revealed concerning the people of polytheism.

Imam Ahmad said: Sulayman ibn Dawud told us, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Thabit ibn Thawban told us, saying: My father told me, from Makhul, that 'Umar ibn Nu'aym related to him from Usama ibn Salman, that Abu Dhar related to them that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah accepts the repentance of His servant — or forgives His servant — as long as the barrier has not fallen." It was said: And what is the falling of the barrier? He said: "That the soul leaves while it is in polytheism." (Musnad, 5/174.)

For this reason He said: ﴿For them We have prepared a painful punishment﴾, meaning: a severe, afflicting, and abiding torment.

Imam Ahmad said: 'Ali ibn 'Ayyash and 'Isam ibn Khalid told us, both saying: Ibn Thawban told us, from his father, from Makhul, from Jubayr ibn Nufayr, from Ibn 'Umar, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Indeed Allah accepts the repentance of the servant as long as he has not begun the death rattle."

Al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah also related it through the hadith of 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Thabit ibn Thawban, with the same chain. Al-Tirmidhi said: Hasan gharib. In the Sunan of Ibn Majah it occurs as "from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr," which is an error; it is in fact 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar ibn al-Khattab.

Another route from Ibn 'Umar: Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh said: Muhammad ibn Ma'mar told us, 'Abd Allah ibn al-Hasan al-Khurasani told us, Yahya ibn 'Abd Allah al-Babulti told us, Ayyub ibn Nahik al-Halabi told us, saying: I heard 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah say: I heard 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar say: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "No believing servant repents a month before death except that Allah accepts it from him, and less than that; and a day and an hour before his death, if Allah knows of his repentance and sincerity towards Him, He accepts it from him." (Abu Nu'aym related it in al-Hilya through Yahya ibn 'Abd Allah from Ayyub ibn Nahik, then said: This is a gharib hadith from 'Ata', narrated solely by Ayyub ibn Nahik.)

Another hadith: Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said: Shu'ba told us, Ibrahim ibn Maymun informed us, a man from Mil'han called Ayyub informed me, who said: I heard 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar say: Whoever repents a year before his death is forgiven, whoever repents a month before his death is forgiven, whoever repents a week before his death is forgiven, whoever repents a day before his death is forgiven, whoever repents an hour before his death is forgiven. I said to him: Allah only said: ﴿Allah accepts repentance only from those who do evil in ignorance and then repent soon﴾. He said: I only relate to you what I heard from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). (Tayalisi's Musnad, p. 301, where it is from the Musnad of 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As; Ahmad related it in his Musnad through 'Affan from Shu'ba similarly, from the Musnad of 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As. Al-Haythami said in al-Majma': "It contains an unnamed narrator, and the rest of its narrators are trustworthy.") Likewise Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi, Abu 'Umar al-Hawdi and Abu 'Amir al-'Aqadi related it from Shu'ba.

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Husayn ibn Muhammad told us, Muhammad ibn Mutarrif told us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Baylamani, who said: Four of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gathered, and one of them said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Indeed Allah accepts the repentance of the servant before he dies by a day." The second said: Did you hear this from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)? He said: Yes. He said: And I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Indeed Allah accepts the repentance of the servant before he dies by half a day." The third said: Did you hear this from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)? He said: Yes. He said: And I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Indeed Allah accepts the repentance of the servant before he dies by a forenoon." The fourth said: Did you hear this from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)? He said: Yes. He said: And I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Indeed Allah [the Exalted] accepts the repentance of the servant as long as he has not begun the death rattle with his soul." Sa'id ibn Mansur related it from al-Darawardi, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Baylamani, mentioning something close to it.

Another hadith: Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh said: Ishaq ibn Ibrahim ibn Zayd told us, 'Imran ibn 'Abd al-Rahim told us, 'Uthman ibn al-Haytham told us, 'Awf told us, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, from Abu Hurayra who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah accepts the repentance of His servant as long as he has not begun the death rattle." (Its chain contains 'Imran ibn 'Abd al-Rahim ibn Abi al-Ward. Al-Sulaymani said: "There is scrutiny concerning him; he is the one who fabricated the hadith of Abu Hanifa from Malik, may Allah have mercy on them both." Abu al-Shaykh said: He was accused of Rafd. Lisan al-Mizan.)

Hadiths on this matter that are mursal:

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Bashshar told us, Ibn Abi 'Adi told us, from 'Awf, from al-Hasan who said: It reached me that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah accepts the repentance of the servant as long as he has not begun the death rattle." This is a mursal, hasan, from al-Hasan al-Basri, may Allah have mercy on him.

Another: Ibn Jarir also said, may Allah have mercy on him: Ibn Bashshar told us, Mu'adh ibn Hisham told us, my father told me, from Qatada, from al-'Ala' ibn Ziyad, from Abu Ayyub Bushayr ibn Ka'b, that the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah accepts the repentance of the servant as long as he has not begun the death rattle."

And Ibn Bashshar told us, 'Abd al-A'la told us, from Sa'id, from Qatada, from 'Ubada ibn al-Samit, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, and mentioned something similar. (Qatada did not hear from 'Ubada ibn al-Samit.)

Another report: Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Bashshar told us, Abu Dawud told us, 'Imran told us, from Qatada who said: We were with Anas ibn Malik, and Abu Qilaba was present, and Abu Qilaba narrated and said: When Allah cursed Iblis, he asked Him for respite, and he said: By Your might and majesty, I will not leave the heart of the son of Adam as long as the spirit is in him. Allah said: By My might, I will not withhold repentance from him as long as the spirit is in him.

This has also come in a marfu' hadith, related by Imam Ahmad in his Musnad through 'Amr ibn Abi 'Amr and Abu al-Haytham al-'Utwari, both from Abu Sa'id, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Iblis said: By Your might, I will not cease to mislead them as long as their spirits are in their bodies. Allah, mighty and majestic, said: By My might and My majesty, I will not cease to forgive them as long as they seek My forgiveness." (Musnad, 3/76.)

These hadiths indicate that whoever repents to Allah, mighty and majestic, while still hoping for life, his repentance is accepted. For this reason Allah said: ﴿Those are the ones to whom Allah will turn in forgiveness, and Allah is ever Knowing and Wise.﴾ As for when despair of life sets in, the angel is seen, the spirit rattles in the throat, the chest becomes constricted, it reaches the windpipe, and the soul gurgles upward in the passages, then no repentance is accepted at that time, and "it is no time for escape." For this reason He said: ﴿And repentance is not accepted from those who commit evil deeds until, when death approaches one of them, he says, "Indeed, I have repented now."﴾ This is like His saying: ﴿So when they saw Our might, they said, "We believe in Allah alone and disbelieve in what we used to associate with Him." But their faith was not beneficial to them when they saw Our might.﴾ (Ghafir: 84–85). And like His judgment that the repentance of the people of the earth is not accepted when they see the sun rising from its west, as He said: ﴿On the day when some of the signs of your Lord come, no soul will benefit from its faith if it had not believed before or earned good through its faith.﴾ (al-An'am: 158).

* *

His saying: ﴿And none of those who die while they are disbelievers﴾ means: when the disbeliever dies in his disbelief and polytheism, his regret and repentance do not benefit him, and nothing will be accepted from him as ransom, even if it were the earth filled with gold.

Ibn 'Abbas, Abu al-'Aliya and al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: ﴿And none of those who die while they are disbelievers﴾ — they said: It was revealed concerning the people of polytheism.

Imam Ahmad said: Sulayman ibn Dawud told us, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Thabit ibn Thawban told us, saying: My father told me, from Makhul, that 'Umar ibn Nu'aym related to him from Usama ibn Salman, that Abu Dhar related to them that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah accepts the repentance of His servant — or forgives His servant — as long as the barrier has not fallen." It was said: And what is the falling of the barrier? He said: "That the soul leaves while it is in polytheism." (Musnad, 5/174.)

For this reason He said: ﴿For them We have prepared a painful punishment﴾, meaning: a severe, afflicting, and abiding torment.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 4, verses 19–22 (part 1 of 3):

Al-Bukhari said: Muhammad ibn Muqatil narrated to us, Asbat ibn Muhammad narrated to us, al-Shaybani narrated to us, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas. Al-Shaybani said: Abu al-Hasan al-Sawwai also related it, and I do not think he related it except from Ibn Abbas. [Concerning] ﴿O you who believe, it is not lawful for you to inherit women against their will﴾, he said: "When a man died, his guardians had more right to his wife. If some of them wished, they would marry her; if they wished, they would give her in marriage; and if they wished, they would not give her in marriage. So they had more right to her than her own family. Then this verse was revealed concerning that."

Thus it was narrated by al-Bukhari, Abu Dawud, al-Nasai, Ibn Mardawayh and Ibn Abi Hatim, from the hadith of Abu Ishaq al-Shaybani, whose name is Sulayman ibn Abi Sulayman, from Ikrimah, and from Abu al-Hasan al-Sawwai, whose name is Ata, a blind man of Kufa; both of them [narrated] from Ibn Abbas with what has preceded [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4579; Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 6089; Sunan al-Nasai al-Kubra, no. 11094.]].

Abu Dawud said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Thabit al-Marwazi narrated to us, Ali ibn Husayn narrated to me, from his father, from Yazid al-Nahwi, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: ﴿It is not lawful for you to inherit women against their will, nor to restrain them [from remarrying] that you may take back some of what you have given them, unless they commit a clear immorality﴾. He said: "That was because a man would inherit the wife of his relative and then restrain her until she died or returned to him her dowry. So Allah, exalted is He, prohibited that," i.e., He forbade it [[Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 2090.]].

Abu Dawud alone narrated it. Others, however, narrated from Ibn Abbas something similar to that. Waki' said, from Sufyan, from Ali ibn Budhaymah, from Miqsam, from Ibn Abbas: "In the Jahiliyyah (the pre-Islamic period of ignorance), when a woman's husband died, a man would come and throw a garment over her, and he would have more right to her. Then this was revealed: ﴿O you who believe, it is not lawful for you to inherit women against their will﴾" [[Al-Tabari narrated it in his Tafsir (8/108) through Ibn Waki' from Waki' with it, except that he stopped it at Miqsam.]].

Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn Abbas, as his own statement, concerning ﴿O you who believe, it is not lawful for you to inherit women against their will﴾: "When a man died and left a slave-girl, his close relative would throw his garment over her and keep her from people. If she was beautiful, he would marry her; if she was ugly, he would confine her until she died, and then he would inherit her."

Al-Awfi narrated from him: "A man from the people of Madinah, when a close relative of one of them died, would throw his garment over the man's wife. He thereby inherited her marriage, and no one else could marry her besides him. He would keep her with him until she ransomed herself from him with a ransom." So Allah revealed: ﴿O you who believe, it is not lawful for you to inherit women against their will﴾.

Zayd ibn Aslam said concerning the verse ﴿It is not lawful for you to inherit women against their will﴾: "The people of Yathrib, when a man of theirs died in the Jahiliyyah, his wife would be inherited by whoever inherited his property, and he would restrain her until he inherited her, or give her in marriage to whomever he wished. The people of Tihamah would treat the wife badly until the husband divorced her, and he would stipulate upon her that she could not marry except whomever he wished, until she ransomed herself from him with some of what he had given her. So Allah forbade the believers from that." Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it.

Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Musa ibn Ishaq narrated to us, Ali ibn al-Mundhir narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Fudayl narrated to us, from Yahya ibn Sa'id, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umamah ibn Sahl ibn Hunayf, from his father, who said: "When Abu Qays ibn al-Aslat died, his son wished to marry his wife, and this was permitted to them in the Jahiliyyah. So Allah revealed: ﴿It is not lawful for you to inherit women against their will﴾."

Ibn Jarir [al-Tabari] narrated it from the hadith of Muhammad ibn Fudayl with the same chain. Then it was narrated through the route of Ibn Juraij, who said: Ata informed me that the people of the Jahiliyyah, when a man died and left a wife, his family would detain her for a young boy among them. So this verse was revealed: ﴿It is not lawful for you to inherit women against their will﴾, to the end of the verse.

Ibn Juraij said: Mujahid said: "When a man died, his son had more right to his wife. He could marry her if he wished, provided she was not his own mother; or he could give her in marriage to whomever he wished, such as his brother or his nephew."

Ibn Juraij said: Ikrimah said: "It was revealed concerning Kubayshah bint Ma'n ibn Asim ibn al-Aws, whose husband Abu Qays ibn al-Aslat died. His son then pressed upon her, so she came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, I was not inherited along with my husband, nor was I left alone to be married off.' So this verse was revealed."

Al-Sudd​i narrated from Abu Malik: "In the Jahiliyyah, when a woman's husband died, his guardian would come and throw a garment over her. If he had a young son or a brother, he would detain her until [the son] grew up, or until she died and he inherited her. But if she escaped and came to her family, and he had not thrown a garment over her, she was saved. So Allah revealed [Ta'ala]: ﴿It is not lawful for you to inherit women against their will﴾."

Mujahid said concerning the verse: "A man would have an orphan girl in his care, whose affairs he managed. He would detain her, hoping that his wife would die so that he could marry her himself or give her in marriage to his son." Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it. Then he said: "Similar [statements] were also narrated from al-Sha'bi, Ata ibn Abi Rabah, Abu Mijlaz, al-Dahhak, al-Zuhri, Ata al-Khurasani and Muqatil ibn Hayyan."

I say: The verse encompasses what the people of the Jahiliyyah used to do, what Mujahid and those who agreed with him mentioned, and every instance in which some form of this occurred. And Allah knows best.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿nor restrain them [from remarrying] that you may take back some of what you have given them﴾, meaning: do not harm them in companionship so that they relinquish to you what you gave them as a dowry, or part of it, or some of their rights upon you, or something of that kind, by way of coercion and oppression.

Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn Abbas concerning His saying: ﴿nor restrain them﴾: he says, "nor oppress them." ﴿that you may take back some of what you have given them﴾, meaning: a man has a wife whom he dislikes being with, and she has a dowry from him, so he harms her so that she will ransom herself.

Al-Dahhak said likewise, and Qatadah and others [[Added from ج, أ.]], and Ibn Jarir chose this view.

Ibn al-Mubarak and Abd al-Razzaq said: Ma'mar informed us, saying: Simak ibn al-Fadl informed me, from Ibn al-Baylamani, who said: "These two verses were revealed, one concerning the affair of the Jahiliyyah and the other concerning the affair of Islam." Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak said: "He means His saying: ﴿It is not lawful for you to inherit women against their will﴾ [refers to] the Jahiliyyah, and ﴿nor restrain them﴾ [refers to] Islam."

* *

As for His saying: ﴿unless they commit a clear immorality﴾. Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn Abbas, Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, al-Sha'bi, al-Hasan al-Basri, Muhammad ibn Sirin, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Mujahid, Ikrimah, Ata al-Khurasani, al-Dahhak, Abu Qilabah, Abu Salih, al-Sudd​i, Zayd ibn Aslam and Sa'id ibn Abi Hilal said: it means adultery. That is, if she commits adultery, you have the right to reclaim from her the dowry you gave her, and to harass her until she leaves it to you and she gives you khul' (a divorce in which the wife gives something to be released). This is as He, exalted is He, said in Surat al-Baqarah: ﴿It is not lawful for you to take back anything of what you have given them, unless both fear that they will not keep within the limits of Allah. And if you fear that they will not keep within the limits of Allah, then there is no blame upon either of them concerning that by which she ransoms herself﴾ [2:229] [[Added from ر، أ.]].

Ibn Abbas, Ikrimah and al-Dahhak said: "The clear immorality is disobedience and defiance (nushuz and 'isyan)."

Ibn Jarir chose that it includes all of that: adultery, disobedience, defiance, foul speech and other things. That is, all of this permits harassing her until she releases him from her right or part of it, and he separates from her. This is good, and Allah knows best. It has already been mentioned in what Abu Dawud alone narrated through the route of Yazid al-Nahwi, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas [may Allah be pleased with them both], concerning His saying: ﴿It is not lawful for you to inherit women against their will, nor to restrain them [from remarrying] that you may take back some of what you have given them, unless they commit a clear immorality﴾. He said: "That was because a man would inherit the wife of his relative and then restrain her until she died or returned to him her dowry. So Allah forbade that, i.e., He prohibited it."

Ikrimah and al-Hasan al-Basri said: "This implies that the whole context concerned the affair of the Jahiliyyah, but the Muslims were forbidden from doing it in Islam."

Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd said: "Restraining [women] was practised among the Quraysh in Makkah. A man would marry a noble woman, and perhaps she would not agree with him, so he would separate from her on condition that she not marry except with his permission. He would bring witnesses and write that down against her and have it witnessed. Then, when a suitor proposed to her, if she gave him [the husband] something and satisfied him, he would permit her [to marry]; otherwise he would restrain her." He said: "This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿nor restrain them [from remarrying] that you may take back some of what you have given them﴾, to the end of the verse."

Mujahid, concerning His saying ﴿nor restrain them [from remarrying] that you may take back some of what you have given them﴾, said: "It is like the restraint mentioned in Surat al-Baqarah."

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And live with them in kindness﴾, meaning: speak good words to them and make your deeds and conduct toward them good, according to your ability, just as you like that from them; so do toward them the same. As Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And they have rights similar to those upon them, according to what is known﴾ [2:228]. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The best of you is the best of you to his family, and I am the best of you to my family" [[Narrated from the hadith of Ibn Abbas: Ibn Majah in his Sunan, no. 1977, and Ibn Hibban in his Sahih, no. 1315 ("Mawarid"), through the route of Ja'far ibn Yahya ibn Thawban, from his paternal uncle Umarah ibn Thawban, from Ata, from Ibn Abbas.

Al-Buseiri said in al-Zawa'id (2/117): "This chain is weak. Umarah ibn Thawban was mentioned by Ibn Hibban among the trustworthy narrators, and Abd al-Haqq said: 'He is not strong,' but Ibn al-Qattan refuted that. As for Ja'far ibn Yahya, Ibn al-Madini said: 'An unknown shaykh.' Ibn al-Qattan al-Fasi said: 'Of unknown condition,' yet Ibn Hibban mentioned him among the trustworthy narrators.

It also came from the hadith of Aisha: al-Tirmidhi in his Sunan, no. 3892, and Ibn Hibban in his Sahih, no. 1312, through the route of Sufyan, from Hisham ibn Urwah, from his father, from Aisha.

Al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a hasan sahih gharib hadith" (good, authentic, rare), from the hadith of al-Thawri; few have narrated it from al-Thawri.]]. Among his noble character (ﷺ) was that he was gracious in companionship, always cheerful, playful with his family, gentle with them, generous in spending upon them, and he joked with his wives. He even raced with Aisha, the Mother of the Believers, seeking to win her affection through that. She said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) raced me and I beat him, that was before I put on weight. Then I raced him again after I had put on weight, and he beat me, and he said: 'This is for that'" [[Narrated by al-Nasai in al-Sunan al-Kubra, no. 8942, and Ibn Majah in his Sunan, no. 1979, through the route of Sufyan, from Hisham ibn Urwah, from his father, from Aisha.]].

His wives would gather every night in the house of the one with whom the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was spending the night, and he would sometimes eat dinner with them. Then each of them would return to her own home. He would sleep with one of his wives under a single covering, removing his upper garment from his shoulders and sleeping in his lower garment. When he had prayed the 'Isha' prayer, he would enter his house and converse with his family briefly before sleeping, keeping them company in this way (ﷺ). And Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿There has certainly been for you in the Messenger of Allah an excellent example﴾ [33:21].

The rulings on marital companionship and the details related to them have their place in the book *al-Ahkam* (The Rulings), and praise be to God.

* *

God the Exalted says: ﴿And if you dislike them, perhaps you dislike a thing in which God has placed much good﴾ [[Addition from manuscripts ج، ر، أ.]]. That is: perhaps your patience with keeping them, despite your dislike of them, will bring you much good in this world and the Hereafter. As Ibn ʿAbbas said regarding this verse: it means that he should show them kindness, and so he may be granted a child from them, and in that child there will be much good [[In manuscript ر: "great".]]. And in the authentic hadith: "A believing man should not hate a believing woman; if he dislikes one of her traits, he will be pleased with another." [[Narrated by Muslim in his Sahih, no. (1469), from Abu Hurairah (may Allah be pleased with him).]]

* *

God says: ﴿But if you desire to exchange one wife for another, and you have given one of them a heap of gold, do not take anything back from it. Would you take it by slander and manifest sin?﴾. That is: if one of you wishes to part from a woman and take another in her place, he must not take back anything of what he gave the first as a dowry, even if it were a heap (qintar) of wealth.

We have already discussed the qintar in Surah Al ʿImran, with sufficient explanation, so there is no need to repeat it here.

This verse indicates the permissibility of giving a large amount of wealth as a dowry (ṣadaq). ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab had forbidden excessive dowries, but then he retracted that, as Imam Ahmad said: Ismaʿil narrated to us, Salamah ibn ʿAlqamah narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, who said: I was told by Abu al-ʿAjfa al-Sulami, who said: I heard ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab say: "Beware, do not exaggerate in the dowries of women. For if it were a source of honour in this world or piety before God, the one most entitled to it would be the Prophet (ﷺ). The Messenger of God (ﷺ) did not give any of his wives a dowry, nor was any of his daughters given a dowry, more than twelve ʿuqiyyah. And a man may be afflicted by his wife's dowry until enmity arises in his heart against her, and until he says: 'I have worn down my ropes to you' (kalifa ʿalq al-qirbah)." Then Ahmad and the authors of the Sunan narrated it through several chains, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, from Abu al-ʿAjfa, whose name is Hirm ibn Musayyib al-Basri. At-Tirmidhi said: this is a hasan sahih hadith. [[Al-Musnad (1/40); also narrated by Abu Dawud in al-Sunan, no. (2106); at-Tirmidhi, no. (1114); an-Nasa'i (6/117); and Ibn Majah, no. (1887).]]

Another route from ʿUmar: The Hafiz Abu Yaʿla said: Abu Khaythamah narrated to us, Yaʿqub ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, from my father, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman narrated to me, from al-Mujalid [[In manuscript ج: "Mujalid".]] ibn Saʿid, from al-Shaʿbi, from Masruq, who said: ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab mounted the pulpit of the Messenger of God and then said: "O people, why do you exaggerate in the dowries of women, when the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and his companions gave dowries of no more than four hundred dirhams or less? If exaggeration in this were piety before God or a mark of honour, you would not have preceded them in it. So I shall not hear of any man raising the dowry of a woman above four hundred dirhams." He said: Then he came down, and a woman of Quraysh confronted him and said: "O Commander of the Faithful, you forbade people from raising the dowries of women above four hundred dirhams?" He said: "Yes." She said: "Have you not heard what God revealed in the Qur'an?" He said: "And which is that?" She said: "Have you not heard God say: ﴿And you have given one of them a heap of gold [then do not take anything back from it. Would you take it by slander and manifest sin?]﴾ [[Addition from manuscripts ج، ر; in manuscript ه: "the verse".]] [an-Nisa: 20]?" He said: "O God, forgive me, everyone knows more than ʿUmar." Then he returned, mounted the pulpit and said: "O people, I had forbidden you to raise the dowries of women above four hundred dirhams. Whoever wishes to give from his wealth what he likes, let him do so." Abu Yaʿla said: I think he said: "Whoever is content in his soul, let him do it." Its chain is good and strong. [[Narrated by Saʿid ibn Mansur in al-Sunan, no. (598) (al-Aʿzami), and from his route al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan al-Kubra (7/233), who said: Haythem narrated to us, Mujalid narrated to us, from al-Shaʿbi, who said: ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with him) addressed the people and mentioned something similar. See: Irwa' al-Ghalil (6/348) by Shaykh Nasir al-Albani, who clarified the weakness of this report and its contradiction to what is in the Sunan.]]

Another route: Ibn al-Mundhir said: Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Razzaq, from Qays ibn Rabiʿ, from Abu Husayn, from Abu ʿAbd al-Rahman al-Sulami, who said: ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab said: "Do not exaggerate in the dowries [[In manuscript أ: "dowry".]] of women." A woman said: "That is not for you, O ʿUmar, for God the Exalted says: 'And you have given one of them a heap of gold.'" He said: "And so it is in the recitation of ʿAbd Allah ibn Masʿud: 'It is not lawful for you to take anything from it.'" Then ʿUmar said: "A woman argued against ʿUmar and defeated him." [[ʿAbd al-Razzaq narrated it in al-Musannaf, no. (10420), by way of Qays ibn Rabiʿ. Shaykh Nasir al-Albani said in Irwa' al-Ghalil (1/348): "It is a weak chain with two defects. The first: a break in the chain, for Abu ʿAbd al-Rahman al-Sulami, whose name is ʿAbd Allah ibn Habib ibn Rabiʿah, did not hear from ʿUmar, as Ibn Maʿin said. The second: the poor memory of Qays ibn Rabiʿ."]]

Another route, from ʿUmar, with a break in the chain: Al-Zubayr ibn Bakkar said: my paternal uncle Mus'ab ibn ʿAbd Allah narrated to me, from my grandfather, who said: ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab said: "Do not increase the dowries of women, even if she is the daughter of Dhu al-Ghussah, meaning Yazid ibn al-Husayn al-Harithi. Whoever increases it, I will place the increase in the House of Money (bayt al-mal)." A woman, one of the tall women of the Suffah [[Suffah: a term describing a tall, lanky woman, with a flat nose.]], said: "That is not yours to decide." He said: "Why?" She said: "Because God [the Exalted] said: ﴿And you have given one of them a heap of gold﴾, the verse." ʿUmar said: "A woman was right and a man was wrong." [[Mentioned by al-Suyuti in al-Durr (2/466), attributing it to al-Zubayr in al-Muwaffaqiyyat. The Hafiz Ibn Kathir said in Musnad ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab (2/573): "It contains a break in the chain."]]

For this reason, God says in rebuke: ﴿And how would you take it when you have lain with one another?﴾ [[Addition from manuscript أ.]] That is: how would you take the dowry from the woman when you have gone in to her and she has gone in to you?

Ibn ʿAbbas, Mujahid, al-Suddi and others said: this means intercourse (al-jima').

It is established in the two Sahihs that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said to the couple who had sworn the oath of mutual cursing (al-mutalaʿinan), after they had finished their oath: "God knows that one of you two is a liar. Will one of you repent?" He said this three times. The man said: "O Messenger of God, my wealth, meaning what I gave her as dowry?" He said: "You shall have no wealth. If you were truthful about her, then it is in return for what you made lawful of her private part; and if you were lying about her, then it is further from you than from her." [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (5312) and Sahih Muslim, no. (1493), from the hadith of ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with him).]]

In the Sunan of Abu Dawud and others, from Basrah ibn Aktam [[In manuscripts ج، ر، أ: "Basrah ibn Abi Basrah".]] that he married a virgin girl in her chamber, and then she was found to be pregnant from fornication. He came to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and told him about it. He judged for her the dowry, separated them, ordered her to be flogged, and said: "The child is a slave for you." [[Sunan Abi Dawud, no. (2131).]]

So the dowry is in exchange for the sexual relationship (al-buḍʿ), and for this reason God the Exalted says: ﴿And how would you take it when you have lain with one another?﴾

* *

God says: ﴿And they have taken from you a firm covenant﴾. It is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas, Mujahid and Saʿid ibn Jubayr that what is meant by this is the marriage contract (al-ʿaqd).
