The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The best of you is the best of you to his family, and I am the best of you to my family" [[Narrated from the hadith of Ibn Abbas: Ibn Majah in his Sunan, no. 1977, and Ibn Hibban in his Sahih, no. 1315 ("Mawarid"), through the route of Ja'far ibn Yahya ibn Thawban, from his paternal uncle Umarah ibn Thawban, from Ata, from Ibn Abbas.

Al-Buseiri said in al-Zawa'id (2/117): "This chain is weak. Umarah ibn Thawban was mentioned by Ibn Hibban among the trustworthy narrators, and Abd al-Haqq said: 'He is not strong,' but Ibn al-Qattan refuted that. As for Ja'far ibn Yahya, Ibn al-Madini said: 'An unknown shaykh.' Ibn al-Qattan al-Fasi said: 'Of unknown condition,' yet Ibn Hibban mentioned him among the trustworthy narrators.

It also came from the hadith of Aisha: al-Tirmidhi in his Sunan, no. 3892, and Ibn Hibban in his Sahih, no. 1312, through the route of Sufyan, from Hisham ibn Urwah, from his father, from Aisha.

Al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a hasan sahih gharib hadith" (good, authentic, rare), from the hadith of al-Thawri; few have narrated it from al-Thawri.]]. Among his noble character (ﷺ) was that he was gracious in companionship, always cheerful, playful with his family, gentle with them, generous in spending upon them, and he joked with his wives. He even raced with Aisha, the Mother of the Believers, seeking to win her affection through that. She said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) raced me and I beat him, that was before I put on weight. Then I raced him again after I had put on weight, and he beat me, and he said: 'This is for that'" [[Narrated by al-Nasai in al-Sunan al-Kubra, no. 8942, and Ibn Majah in his Sunan, no. 1979, through the route of Sufyan, from Hisham ibn Urwah, from his father, from Aisha.]].

His wives would gather every night in the house of the one with whom the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was spending the night, and he would sometimes eat dinner with them. Then each of them would return to her own home. He would sleep with one of his wives under a single covering, removing his upper garment from his shoulders and sleeping in his lower garment. When he had prayed the 'Isha' prayer, he would enter his house and converse with his family briefly before sleeping, keeping them company in this way (ﷺ). And Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿There has certainly been for you in the Messenger of Allah an excellent example﴾ [33:21].

The rulings on marital companionship and the details related to them have their place in the book *al-Ahkam* (The Rulings), and praise be to God.

* *

God the Exalted says: ﴿And if you dislike them, perhaps you dislike a thing in which God has placed much good﴾ [[Addition from manuscripts ج، ر، أ.]]. That is: perhaps your patience with keeping them, despite your dislike of them, will bring you much good in this world and the Hereafter. As Ibn ʿAbbas said regarding this verse: it means that he should show them kindness, and so he may be granted a child from them, and in that child there will be much good [[In manuscript ر: "great".]]. And in the authentic hadith: "A believing man should not hate a believing woman; if he dislikes one of her traits, he will be pleased with another." [[Narrated by Muslim in his Sahih, no. (1469), from Abu Hurairah (may Allah be pleased with him).]]

* *

God says: ﴿But if you desire to exchange one wife for another, and you have given one of them a heap of gold, do not take anything back from it. Would you take it by slander and manifest sin?﴾. That is: if one of you wishes to part from a woman and take another in her place, he must not take back anything of what he gave the first as a dowry, even if it were a heap (qintar) of wealth.

We have already discussed the qintar in Surah Al ʿImran, with sufficient explanation, so there is no need to repeat it here.

This verse indicates the permissibility of giving a large amount of wealth as a dowry (ṣadaq). ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab had forbidden excessive dowries, but then he retracted that, as Imam Ahmad said: Ismaʿil narrated to us, Salamah ibn ʿAlqamah narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, who said: I was told by Abu al-ʿAjfa al-Sulami, who said: I heard ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab say: "Beware, do not exaggerate in the dowries of women. For if it were a source of honour in this world or piety before God, the one most entitled to it would be the Prophet (ﷺ). The Messenger of God (ﷺ) did not give any of his wives a dowry, nor was any of his daughters given a dowry, more than twelve ʿuqiyyah. And a man may be afflicted by his wife's dowry until enmity arises in his heart against her, and until he says: 'I have worn down my ropes to you' (kalifa ʿalq al-qirbah)." Then Ahmad and the authors of the Sunan narrated it through several chains, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, from Abu al-ʿAjfa, whose name is Hirm ibn Musayyib al-Basri. At-Tirmidhi said: this is a hasan sahih hadith. [[Al-Musnad (1/40); also narrated by Abu Dawud in al-Sunan, no. (2106); at-Tirmidhi, no. (1114); an-Nasa'i (6/117); and Ibn Majah, no. (1887).]]

Another route from ʿUmar: The Hafiz Abu Yaʿla said: Abu Khaythamah narrated to us, Yaʿqub ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, from my father, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman narrated to me, from al-Mujalid [[In manuscript ج: "Mujalid".]] ibn Saʿid, from al-Shaʿbi, from Masruq, who said: ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab mounted the pulpit of the Messenger of God and then said: "O people, why do you exaggerate in the dowries of women, when the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and his companions gave dowries of no more than four hundred dirhams or less? If exaggeration in this were piety before God or a mark of honour, you would not have preceded them in it. So I shall not hear of any man raising the dowry of a woman above four hundred dirhams." He said: Then he came down, and a woman of Quraysh confronted him and said: "O Commander of the Faithful, you forbade people from raising the dowries of women above four hundred dirhams?" He said: "Yes." She said: "Have you not heard what God revealed in the Qur'an?" He said: "And which is that?" She said: "Have you not heard God say: ﴿And you have given one of them a heap of gold [then do not take anything back from it. Would you take it by slander and manifest sin?]﴾ [[Addition from manuscripts ج، ر; in manuscript ه: "the verse".]] [an-Nisa: 20]?" He said: "O God, forgive me, everyone knows more than ʿUmar." Then he returned, mounted the pulpit and said: "O people, I had forbidden you to raise the dowries of women above four hundred dirhams. Whoever wishes to give from his wealth what he likes, let him do so." Abu Yaʿla said: I think he said: "Whoever is content in his soul, let him do it." Its chain is good and strong. [[Narrated by Saʿid ibn Mansur in al-Sunan, no. (598) (al-Aʿzami), and from his route al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan al-Kubra (7/233), who said: Haythem narrated to us, Mujalid narrated to us, from al-Shaʿbi, who said: ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with him) addressed the people and mentioned something similar. See: Irwa' al-Ghalil (6/348) by Shaykh Nasir al-Albani, who clarified the weakness of this report and its contradiction to what is in the Sunan.]]

Another route: Ibn al-Mundhir said: Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Razzaq, from Qays ibn Rabiʿ, from Abu Husayn, from Abu ʿAbd al-Rahman al-Sulami, who said: ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab said: "Do not exaggerate in the dowries [[In manuscript أ: "dowry".]] of women." A woman said: "That is not for you, O ʿUmar, for God the Exalted says: 'And you have given one of them a heap of gold.'" He said: "And so it is in the recitation of ʿAbd Allah ibn Masʿud: 'It is not lawful for you to take anything from it.'" Then ʿUmar said: "A woman argued against ʿUmar and defeated him." [[ʿAbd al-Razzaq narrated it in al-Musannaf, no. (10420), by way of Qays ibn Rabiʿ. Shaykh Nasir al-Albani said in Irwa' al-Ghalil (1/348): "It is a weak chain with two defects. The first: a break in the chain, for Abu ʿAbd al-Rahman al-Sulami, whose name is ʿAbd Allah ibn Habib ibn Rabiʿah, did not hear from ʿUmar, as Ibn Maʿin said. The second: the poor memory of Qays ibn Rabiʿ."]]

Another route, from ʿUmar, with a break in the chain: Al-Zubayr ibn Bakkar said: my paternal uncle Mus'ab ibn ʿAbd Allah narrated to me, from my grandfather, who said: ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab said: "Do not increase the dowries of women, even if she is the daughter of Dhu al-Ghussah, meaning Yazid ibn al-Husayn al-Harithi. Whoever increases it, I will place the increase in the House of Money (bayt al-mal)." A woman, one of the tall women of the Suffah [[Suffah: a term describing a tall, lanky woman, with a flat nose.]], said: "That is not yours to decide." He said: "Why?" She said: "Because God [the Exalted] said: ﴿And you have given one of them a heap of gold﴾, the verse." ʿUmar said: "A woman was right and a man was wrong." [[Mentioned by al-Suyuti in al-Durr (2/466), attributing it to al-Zubayr in al-Muwaffaqiyyat. The Hafiz Ibn Kathir said in Musnad ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab (2/573): "It contains a break in the chain."]]

For this reason, God says in rebuke: ﴿And how would you take it when you have lain with one another?﴾ [[Addition from manuscript أ.]] That is: how would you take the dowry from the woman when you have gone in to her and she has gone in to you?

Ibn ʿAbbas, Mujahid, al-Suddi and others said: this means intercourse (al-jima').

It is established in the two Sahihs that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said to the couple who had sworn the oath of mutual cursing (al-mutalaʿinan), after they had finished their oath: "God knows that one of you two is a liar. Will one of you repent?" He said this three times. The man said: "O Messenger of God, my wealth, meaning what I gave her as dowry?" He said: "You shall have no wealth. If you were truthful about her, then it is in return for what you made lawful of her private part; and if you were lying about her, then it is further from you than from her." [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (5312) and Sahih Muslim, no. (1493), from the hadith of ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with him).]]

In the Sunan of Abu Dawud and others, from Basrah ibn Aktam [[In manuscripts ج، ر، أ: "Basrah ibn Abi Basrah".]] that he married a virgin girl in her chamber, and then she was found to be pregnant from fornication. He came to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and told him about it. He judged for her the dowry, separated them, ordered her to be flogged, and said: "The child is a slave for you." [[Sunan Abi Dawud, no. (2131).]]

So the dowry is in exchange for the sexual relationship (al-buḍʿ), and for this reason God the Exalted says: ﴿And how would you take it when you have lain with one another?﴾

* *

God says: ﴿And they have taken from you a firm covenant﴾. It is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas, Mujahid and Saʿid ibn Jubayr that what is meant by this is the marriage contract (al-ʿaqd).

Sufyan al-Thawri said, from Habib ibn Abi Thabit, from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding God's words: ﴿And they have taken from you a firm [[Addition from manuscripts ج، ر، أ.]] covenant﴾: he said: it is his saying: "Either retain them with kindness, or release them with grace."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: it is narrated similarly from ʿIkrimah, Mujahid, Abu al-ʿAliyah, al-Hasan, Qatadah, Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, al-Dahhak and al-Suddi.

Abu Jaʿfar al-Razi said, from al-Rabiʿ ibn Anas regarding the verse [[In manuscripts ج، ر، أ: "And they have taken from you a firm covenant."]]: it is his saying: "You have taken them by the trust of God, and you have made their private parts lawful by the word of God." The "word of God" is the tashahhud in the sermon. He said: among what the Prophet (ﷺ) was given on the night of his Isra' was that God said to him: "I have made it so that your ummah is not permitted to give a sermon until they testify that you are My servant and My Messenger." Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it.

In the Sahih of Muslim, from Jabir, regarding the sermon of the Farewell Pilgrimage, that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said in it: "Treat women well, for you have taken them by the trust of God, and you have made their private parts lawful by the word of God." [[Sahih Muslim, no. (1218).]]

* *

God the Exalted says: ﴿And do not marry those whom your fathers married of women, except what has already passed. Indeed, it was an indecency and hatred, and an evil way﴾ [[Addition from manuscripts ج، ر، أ; in manuscript ه: "the verse".]]. God forbids the wives of fathers, honouring them and showing reverence and respect for them, that they should be taken after him, so much so that she becomes forbidden to the son merely by the contract with her. This is a matter agreed upon (mujmaʿun ʿalayhi).

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Malik ibn Isma'il narrated to us, Qays ibn al-Rabiʿ narrated to us, from Ashʿath ibn Sawwar, from ʿAdi ibn Thabit, from a man of the Ansar who said: When Abu Qays, meaning Ibn al-Aslat, died, and he was one of the righteous Ansar, his son Qays proposed to his wife. She said: "I used to consider you a son, and you are among the righteous of your people. But I will go to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and ask his advice." She went to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and said: "Abu Qays has died." He said: "Good." Then she said: "His son Qays has proposed to me, and he is among the righteous of his people, but I used to consider him a son. What do you think?" He said to her: "Return to your house." He said: then this verse was revealed: ﴿And do not marry those whom your fathers married of women [except what has already passed]﴾ [[Addition from manuscripts ج، ر، أ.]], the verse.

Ibn Jarir said: al-Qasim narrated to us, Husayn narrated to us, Hajjaj narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from ʿIkrimah regarding His words: ﴿And do not marry those whom your fathers married of women, except what has already passed﴾ [[Addition from manuscript أ.]], he said: it was revealed concerning Abu Qays ibn al-Aslat, who married Umm ʿUbayd Allah, daughter of Sakhr [[In manuscripts ج، ر، أ: "Dumrah".]], and she had been married to his father al-Aslat. And [it was revealed concerning] al-Aswad ibn Khalaf, who married the daughter of Abu Talhah ibn ʿAbd al-ʿUzza ibn ʿUthman ibn ʿAbd al-Dar, and she had been with his father Khalaf; and [concerning] Fakhitah, daughter of al-Aswad ibn al-Muttalib ibn Asad, who had been with Umayyah ibn Khalaf, and then Safwan ibn Umayyah married her. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (8/133).]]

Ibn Kathir's commentary on Surah an-Nisa' 4:19-22 (part 3 of 3):

Al-Suhayli claimed that marrying the wives of one's fathers was practised in the Jahiliyyah (the pre-Islamic Age of Ignorance). For this reason Allah said: ﴿except what has already passed﴾, just as He said: ﴿and that you combine two sisters, except what has already passed﴾. He said: Kinanah ibn Khuzaymah did this. He married his father's wife, and she bore him his son al-Nadr ibn Kinanah. He said: The Prophet ﷺ said: "I was born of a marriage, not of illegitimate union (sifah)." He said: This indicates that this practice was permissible for them. If he means that they considered it a marriage among themselves, then Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Mukhar-rami [in A: "al-Mahrami"] narrated to us: Qurad narrated to us: Ibn 'Uyaynah narrated to us, from 'Umar, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The people of the Jahiliyyah used to forbid what Allah had forbidden, except marrying the wife of a father and combining two sisters. So Allah revealed: ﴿And do not marry what your fathers married of women﴾ and ﴿and that you combine two sisters﴾. Ata' and Qatadah said the same. However, there is doubt concerning al-Suhayli's account of the story of Kinanah, and Allah knows best. In any case, it is prohibited in this nation, and it is an extremely abominable matter. For this reason Allah said: ﴿Indeed, it was an indecency and hateful and an evil way﴾. For this reason He also said [Ta'ala]: ﴿And do not approach immoralities, what is apparent of them and what is concealed﴾ [Al-An'am 6:151], and He said: ﴿And do not approach unlawful sexual intercourse. Indeed, it is an immorality and evil as a way﴾ [Al-Isra' 17:32]. Here He added: ﴿and hateful﴾, meaning hatred. That is, it is a grave matter in itself, and it leads to the son hating his father after he marries his wife, since generally whoever marries a woman dislikes the man who was her husband before him. For this reason the Mothers of the Believers were made forbidden to the Ummah, because they are mothers, since they are the wives of the Prophet ﷺ. He is like a father to the Ummah; indeed, his right is greater than the rights of fathers by consensus (ijma'), and his love takes precedence over the love of one's own self, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him.

Atа' ibn Abi Rabah said concerning His words ﴿and hateful﴾: meaning Allah hates it. ﴿And an evil way﴾: meaning evil is the path for whoever takes it among the people. Whoever engages in it after this has apostatised from his religion, so he is to be killed, and his property becomes fay' (spoils) for the Bayt al-Mal (public treasury). This is related by Imam Ahmad and the authors of the Sunan, through several chains, from al-Bara' ibn 'Azib, from his maternal uncle Abu Burdah [in one version: Ibn 'Umar; in another version: from his paternal uncle], that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent him to a man who had married his father's wife after him, to kill him and take his property.

Imam Ahmad said: Hushaym narrated to us: Ash'ath narrated to us, from 'Adi ibn Thabit, from al-Bara' ibn 'Azib, who said: My paternal uncle al-Harith ibn 'Amr passed by me, and with him was a banner which the Prophet ﷺ had tied for him. I said to him: O uncle, where has the Prophet ﷺ sent you? He said: He sent me to a man who married his father's wife, and he commanded me to strike his neck.

Issue:
The scholars have agreed (ijma') on the prohibition of a woman whom the father has had intercourse with, whether by marriage, ownership, or by a doubtful union (shubhah). They differed concerning one who touched her with desire without intercourse, or looked at what is not lawful for him to look at if she were a stranger. From Imam Ahmad, may Allah have mercy on him, it is reported that she becomes forbidden by that as well. Ibn 'Asakir narrated in the biography of Khudayj al-Hisni, the client (mawla) of Mu'awiyah, who said: He bought for Mu'awiyah a beautiful white slave girl, and he brought her in to him naked while he held a staff in his hand. He began striking at her private parts with it, saying: "This private part, if only it had a private part!" Take her to Yazid ibn Mu'awiyah. Then he said: Call for me Rabi'ah ibn 'Amr al-Jurashi, who was a jurist. When he came in to him, he said: This one was brought to me naked, and I saw from her this and that, and I wanted to send her to Yazid. He said: Do not do that, O Commander of the Faithful, for she is not suitable for him. Then he said: What an excellent opinion you have! Then he said: Call for me 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'adah al-Fazari. I called him, and he was very dark-skinned. He said: Take this one; whiten your son with her. He said: This 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'adah had been given by the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to his daughter Fatimah. She raised him, then freed him. After that he was with Mu'awiyah among the people against 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him.

This noble verse is the verse on the prohibited relatives (al-mahārim) through lineage (nasab), together with what follows from fosterage (raḍāʿ) and the relatives prohibited by marriage (ṣihr). Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn Sinan narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us, from Sufyan ibn Habib, from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: "Seven are forbidden to you by lineage and seven by marriage," and he recited: ﴿Forbidden to you are your mothers and your daughters and your sisters﴾ to the end of the verse.

Abu Saʿid ibn Yahya ibn Saʿid narrated to us, Abu Ahmad narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Ismaʿil ibn Raja' [in ج and أ: "ibn Jabir"], from ʿUmayr, the freedman (mawlā) of Ibn ʿAbbas, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: "Seven are prohibited by lineage and seven by marriage." Then he recited: ﴿Forbidden to you are your mothers and your daughters and your sisters and your paternal aunts and your maternal aunts and your brother's daughters and your sister's daughters﴾. These are the lineage prohibitions.

The majority of scholars have derived the prohibition of a girl created from the water of an adulterer (the adulterer being her father) from the general wording of His statement, ﴿and your daughters﴾. She is a daughter, so she falls within the general term. This is the position of Abu Hanifa, Malik, and Ahmad ibn Hanbal. It has been reported from al-Shafiʿi that he permitted marriage to her, since she is not a legal daughter (bint sharʿiyya). Just as she is not included in His statement, ﴿Allah enjoins you concerning your children﴾, since she does not inherit by consensus, so too she is not included in this verse. And Allah knows best.

* *

As for His statement: ﴿And your mothers who have nursed you, and your sisters through fosterage﴾, meaning: just as your mother who bore you is forbidden to you, so too is your mother who nursed you forbidden to you. For this reason al-Bukhari and Muslim in the two Sahihs related, from the hadith of Malik ibn Anas, from ʿAbdullah ibn Abi Bakr ibn Muhammad ibn ʿAmr ibn Hazm, from ʿAmra bint ʿAbd al-Rahman, from ʿAʾisha, the Mother of the Believers, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Fosterage prohibits what birth prohibits." In a wording of Muslim: "What is forbidden by lineage is forbidden by fosterage" [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (3105), Sahih Muslim no. (1444), and Muwatta' Malik (in the chapter on fosterage)].

Some jurists have said: "Just as something is prohibited by lineage, so it is prohibited by fosterage, except in four cases." Others said: "Except in six cases," which are mentioned in the books of furuʿ (derivative jurisprudence). The verified position is that nothing is excepted from this, because some of these cases are similar to cases in lineage, and some are prohibited only through marriage (ṣihr). Therefore nothing at all contradicts the hadith, and all praise belongs to Allah.

Then the imams differed concerning the number of sucklings that establish the prohibition. Some held that mere nursing prohibits, by the generality of this verse. This is the view of Malik, and it is related from Ibn ʿUmar. Saʿid ibn al-Musayyab, ʿUrwa ibn al-Zubayr, and al-Zuhri also held this view.

Others said: fewer than three sucklings do not prohibit, based on what is established in Sahih Muslim, through the chain of Hisham ibn ʿUrwa from his father, from ʿAʾisha, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "A single suck (al-mașṣa) does not prohibit, nor do two sucks" [Sahih Muslim no. (1450). It is, however, in Muslim through the route of Ibn Abi Mulayka from ʿAbdullah ibn al-Zubayr from ʿAʾisha. It is also related by al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra through the route of Hisham ibn ʿUrwa from his father from ʿAʾisha and Ibn al-Zubayr, no. (5458)].

Qatada narrated from Abu al-Khalil, from ʿAbdullah ibn al-Harith, from Umm al-Fadl, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "A single nursing (raḍʿa) does not prohibit, nor do two nursings; a single suck does not prohibit, nor do two sucks." In another wording: "A single gulping (imlāja) does not prohibit, nor do two gulpings" [related by Muslim, no. (1451)].

Among those who held this view were Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal, Ishaq ibn Rahawayh, Abu ʿUbayd, and Abu Thawr. It is related from ʿAlī, ʿAʾisha, Umm al-Fadl, Ibn al-Zubayr, Sulayman ibn Yasar, and Saʿid ibn Jubayr, may Allah have mercy on them.

Others said: fewer than five sucklings do not prohibit, based on what is established in Sahih Muslim through the route of Malik, from ʿAbdullah ibn Abi Bakr, from ʿAmra [in ج، ر، أ: "from ʿUrwa"], from ʿAʾisha, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: "Among what Allah revealed of the Qur'an was: ten known sucklings make prohibition. Then they were abrogated (nusikhna, i.e., naskh: abrogation) by five known sucklings, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) died while they were still among what is recited of the Qur'an."

ʿAbd al-Razzaq related from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhri, from ʿUrwa, from ʿAʾisha something similar [Sahih Muslim no. (1452)].

In the hadith of Sahla bint Suhayl: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) instructed her to nurse the freedman of Abu Hudhayfa five sucklings [and see her story in al-Musnad (6/201)]. ʿAʾisha used to instruct anyone who wished to enter her presence to be nursed five sucklings. This is the view of al-Shafiʿi, may Allah the Exalted have mercy on him, and his companions.

Then it should be known that fosterage must occur in infancy, before two years, according to the view of the majority. As we have already discussed this matter in Surat al-Baqara, at His statement: ﴿Mothers shall nurse their children two complete years for whoever wishes to complete the nursing﴾ [the verse: 233].

They differed: does the milk of the sire (labn al-fahl, i.e., the milk of a woman impregnated by a man, which makes him a foster father) prohibit, as is the view of the majority of the four imams and others? Or is fosterage restricted to the mother only, and does it not extend to the father's side, as is the view of some of the early generation (salaf)? There are two positions. The verification of all this is in the book "al-Aḥkām al-Kabīr."

* *

As for His statement: ﴿And the mothers of your wives and your stepdaughters (rabāʾib) who are in your guardianship, born of your wives with whom you have consummated the marriage; but if you have not consummated the marriage with them, there is no blame upon you﴾. As for the mother of the woman, she is forbidden upon marriage to her daughter by the mere contract, whether or not he has consummated with her. As for the stepdaughter (rabība), who is the daughter of the woman, she is not forbidden to her mother by the mere contract until he consummates with her. If he divorces the mother before consummation, it is permissible for him to marry her daughter. For this reason He said: ﴿And your stepdaughters who are in your guardianship, born of your wives with whom you have consummated the marriage; but if you have not consummated with them, there is no blame upon you﴾ [meaning] in marrying them. This is specific to the stepdaughters alone.

Some understood the pronoun to refer to both the mothers and the stepdaughters, and said: neither the mother nor the daughter is forbidden by the mere contract to the other until he consummates with her, because of His statement: ﴿But if you have not consummated with them, there is no blame upon you﴾.

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, Ibn Abi ʿAdi and ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to us, from Saʿid, from Qatada, from Khilas ibn ʿAmr, from ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him, concerning a man who married a woman and divorced her before consummation: may he marry her mother? He said: "She is in the position of the stepdaughter."

Ibn Bashshar also narrated to us: Yahya ibn Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatada, from Saʿid ibn al-Musayyab, from Zayd ibn Thabit, who said: "If a man divorces his wife before consummating with her, there is no harm in his marrying her mother."

In a narration from Qatada, from Saʿid, from Zayd ibn Thabit: he used to say, "If she dies while he is with her and he takes her inheritance, it is disliked for him to marry her mother. But if he divorces her before consummation, he may do so if he wishes."

Ibn al-Mundhir said: Ishaq narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Razzaq, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Abu Bakr ibn Hafs informed me, from Muslim ibn ʿUwaymir al-Ajda', that Bakr ibn Kinana informed him that his father married him to a woman in Ta'if. He said: "I did not have intercourse with her until my paternal uncle died, and her mother had a great deal of wealth. My father said: 'Would you want her mother?' I asked Ibn ʿAbbas and informed him of the report, and he said: 'Marry her mother.' I asked Ibn ʿUmar, and he said: 'Do not marry her.' I informed my father of what Ibn ʿAbbas said and what Ibn ʿUmar said, so my father wrote to Muʿawiya and informed him in his letter of what Ibn ʿUmar and Ibn ʿAbbas said. Muʿawiya wrote: 'I do not make lawful what Allah has forbidden, nor do I forbid what Allah has made lawful. You and that matter; there are many women other than her.' He neither forbade it to me nor permitted it to me, so my father withdrew from her mother and did not marry her."

ʿAbd al-Razzaq said: Maʿmar informed us, from Simak ibn al-Fadl, from a man, from ʿAbdullah ibn al-Zubayr, who said: "The stepdaughter and the mother are equal; there is no harm in it if he has not consummated with the woman." In its chain there is an unnamed man (mubham) who was not identified [in أ: "a suspect man (muttahim)"].

Ibn Jurayj said: ʿIkrima ibn Khalid informed me that Mujahid said to him concerning: ﴿And the mothers of your wives and your stepdaughters who are in your guardianship﴾: "He meant by both of them consummation together." So this position is reported, as you see, from ʿAlī, Zayd ibn Thabit, ʿAbdullah ibn al-Zubayr, Mujahid, Ibn Jubayr, and Ibn ʿAbbas. Muʿawiya had reservations about it, and among the Shafiʿis Abu al-Hasan Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Sabuni held it, as reported by al-Rafiʿi from al-ʿAbbadi. [The majority of scholars from the early and later generations opposed him, holding that the stepdaughter is not forbidden by the mere contract to the mother, and that she is forbidden only by consummation with the mother, unlike the mother, who is forbidden by the mere contract to the stepdaughter.]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Jaʿfar ibn Muhammad ibn Harun ibn ʿAzra [in ج، أ: "ʿUrwa"] narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Wahhab narrated to us, from Saʿid, from Qatada, from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbas: that he used to say, "If a man divorces a woman before consummating with her, or she dies, her mother is not lawful to him." And he said: "She is a mubham (an unrestricted, general case), so he disliked it."

Then he said: It is reported from Ibn Masʿud, ʿImran ibn Husayn, Masruq, Tawus, ʿIkrima, ʿAta', al-Hasan, Makhul, Ibn Sirin, Qatada, and al-Zuhri something similar. This is the position of the four imams, the seven jurists, and the majority of jurists, past and present, and all praise and grace belong to Allah.

Ibn Jarir said: "The correct view, meaning the view of the one who said 'the mother is among the mubhamat (the general, unrestricted categories)', is that because Allah did not stipulate consummation with them as He stipulated it with the mothers of the stepdaughters. Moreover, this is also a consensus of the proof which it is not permissible to oppose, in what it has come with unanimously." It has also been related with this meaning a report from the Prophet (ﷺ), but its chain is questionable. It is what al-Muthanna narrated to me: Hibban ibn Musa narrated to us, Ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, al-Muthanna ibn al-Sabbah informed us, from ʿAmr ibn Shuʿayb, from his father, from his grandfather, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "If a man marries a woman, it is not lawful for him to marry her mother, whether or not he has consummated with the daughter. And if he marries the mother and does not consummate with her and then divorces her, he may marry the daughter if he wishes" [Tafsir al-Tabari (8/146); and al-Bayhaqi related it in al-Sunan al-Kubra (7/160) through this route, then said: "al-Muthanna ibn al-Sabbah is not strong."]

Then he said: This report, although there is in its chain what there is, nevertheless the consensus of the authorities on the soundness of the view that it is to be acted upon makes it unnecessary to cite other evidence for its soundness.

As for His saying: ﴿And your stepdaughters who are in your guardianship, born of your wives with whom you have consummated marriage﴾, the majority of the Imams (a'immah) hold that the stepdaughter (rabibah) is forbidden whether she is in the man's guardianship or not in his guardianship. They said: this address came out in the form of what is usual, so it has no implicit restriction (mafhum), like His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And do not compel your slave girls to prostitution if they desire chastity﴾ [An-Nur: 33].

In the Two Sahihs, Umm Habibah said: "O Messenger of Allah, marry my sister, the daughter of Abu Sufyan." And in a wording of Muslim: "'Izzah, the daughter of Abu Sufyan." He said: "Do you like that?" She said: "Yes. I am not exclusively yours, and I love that my sister should share in the good with me." He said: "Indeed, that is not lawful for me." She said: "We have heard that you intend to marry the daughter of Abu Salamah." He said: "The daughter of Umm Salamah?" She said: "Yes." He said: "Indeed, even if she were not my stepdaughter in my guardianship, she would still not be lawful for me. She is the daughter of my brother through nursing. Thuwaybah nursed me and Abu Salamah, so do not offer me your daughters or your sisters." And in a narration of al-Bukhari: "Indeed, if I had not married Umm Salamah, she would not have been lawful for me."

So he made the basis of the prohibition the mere fact of his marrying Umm Salamah, and ruled the prohibition on that basis. This is the position of the Four Imams, the Seven Jurists, and the majority of the later and earlier scholars. It has been said that the stepdaughter is only forbidden if she is in the man's guardianship, and if she is not in that situation she is not forbidden.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur'ah narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn Musa narrated to us, Hisham, that is Ibn Yusuf, informed us, from Ibn Juraij, Ibrahim ibn Ubayd ibn Rifa'ah narrated to me, Malik ibn Aws ibn al-Hadthan informed me, who said: I had a wife who died, and she had borne me children, and I grieved over her. Ali ibn Abi Talib met me and said: "What is the matter with you?" I said: "The woman has died." Ali said: "Does she have a daughter?" I said: "Yes, and she is in al-Ta'if." He said: "Was she in your guardianship?" I said: "No, she is in al-Ta'if." He said: "Then marry her." I said: "Then where is the saying of Allah [Mighty and Majestic] ﴿and your stepdaughters who are in your guardianship﴾?" He said: "Indeed, she was not in your guardianship; that applies only when she is in your guardianship."

This is a strong, established chain up to Ali ibn Abi Talib, on the condition of Muslim, and it is an extremely rare view. Dawud ibn Ali al-Zahiri and his companions went to this view. Abu al-Qasim al-Rafi'i related it from Malik, may Allah have mercy on him, and Ibn Hazm chose it. My shaykh, the memorizer Abu Abdullah al-Dhahabi, related to me that he presented this to the Shaykh and Imam Taqi al-Din Ibn Taymiyyah, may Allah have mercy on him, and he found it problematic and held back in that matter. And Allah knows best.

Ibn al-Mundhir said: Ali ibn Abd al-Aziz narrated to us, al-Athram narrated to us, from Abu Ubaydah concerning His saying ﴿who are in your guardianship﴾, he said: "In your houses."

As for the stepdaughter in ownership by the right hand (milk al-yamin), Imam Malik ibn Anas said, from Ibn Shihab: Umar ibn al-Khattab was asked about a woman and her daughter who were slaves in ownership, one of them being lawful to him after the other. Umar said: "I do not like to unite them both," meaning, to have intercourse with both of them by right of ownership. This report is disconnected (munqati').

Sunayd ibn Dawud said in his tafsir: Abu al-Ahwas narrated to us, from Tariq ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Qays, who said: I said to Ibn Abbas: "Can a man have intercourse with a woman and her daughter, both slaves belonging to him?" He said: "One verse made them lawful and another verse made them unlawful, and I would not do it."

Shaykh Abu Umar ibn Abd al-Barr, may Allah have mercy on him, said: There is no disagreement among the scholars that it is not lawful for anyone to have intercourse with a woman and her daughter in ownership, because Allah has prohibited that in marriage. He said: ﴿And the mothers of your wives and your stepdaughters who are in your guardianship, born of your wives...﴾ The ownership by the right hand follows marriage, except what is reported from Umar and Ibn Abbas, and none of the leading jurists or those who followed them agree with that. Hisham narrated from Qatadah: the daughter of a stepdaughter and the daughter of her daughter are not permissible, even if they are further down through many generations. Qatadah said the same on the authority of Abu al-Aliyah.

The meaning of His saying: ﴿with whom you have consummated marriage﴾ is: "with whom you have married." This was said by Ibn Abbas and others.

Ibn Juraij said, on the authority of Ata: it means that she is brought to him, and he uncovers her, examines her, and sits between her legs. I said: "What if he does that in the house of her family?" He said: "It is the same, and it is enough that her daughter has been made unlawful to him."

Ibn Jarir said: There is a consensus of all that a man's privacy (khalwah) with his wife does not make her daughter unlawful to him if he divorces her before touching or intimacy with her, or before looking at her private part with desire. This indicates that the meaning of that is reaching her through intercourse.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿and the wives of your sons who are from your loins﴾, that is: and there are made unlawful to you the wives of your sons whom you have fathered from your loins, excluding adopted sons (ad'iya') whom they used to adopt in the Jahiliyyah, as He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿So when Zayd had no more need of her, We married her to you, so that there would be no difficulty for the believers concerning the wives of their adopted sons, when they have no more need of them﴾ [Al-Ahzab: 37].

Ibn Juraij said: I asked Ata about His saying: ﴿and the wives of your sons who are from your loins﴾. He said: "We used to narrate, and Allah knows best, that when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ married the wife of Zayd, the polytheists in Makkah spoke about that, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed ﴿and the wives of your sons who are from your loins﴾, and there was revealed ﴿Nor has He made your adopted sons your sons﴾ [Al-Ahzab: 4], and there was revealed ﴿Muhammad is not the father of any one of your men﴾ [Al-Ahzab: 40]."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur'ah narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr al-Muqaddami narrated to us, al-Jarrah ibn al-Harith narrated to us, from al-Ash'ath, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad, that these verses are general (mubhamat): ﴿and the wives of your sons﴾, ﴿the mothers of your wives﴾. Then he said: Similar was narrated from Tawus, Ibrahim, al-Zuhri and Makhul.

I say: the meaning of "mubhamat" is that they are general, applying to those with whom marriage was consummated and those with whom it was not, so that marriage is made unlawful merely by the contract itself, and this is agreed upon. If it is said: from where is the wife of one's son by nursing made unlawful, as is the view of the majority, while some people report it as a consensus although she is not of one's loins? The answer is from His saying, peace and blessings be upon him: "What is unlawful by birth is unlawful by nursing."

* *

As for His saying: ﴿and that you should combine two sisters, except what has already passed [Indeed, Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful]﴾, that is: and there is made unlawful to you combining two sisters together in marriage, and likewise in ownership by the right hand, except what was among you in your Jahiliyyah, for We have pardoned that and forgiven it. This indicates that there is no alternative for what is yet to come and no exception for what has passed, as He said: ﴿They will not taste death therein except the first death﴾ [Ad-Dukhan: 56], which indicates that they will never taste death therein. The scholars from the Companions, the Successors, and the Imams, past and present, have agreed that combining two sisters in marriage is forbidden, and whoever embraces Islam while having two sisters as wives must choose, keeping one of them and divorcing the other without alternative.

Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal said: Musa ibn Dawud narrated to us, Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to us, from Abu Wahb al-Jayshani, from al-Dahhak ibn Fayruz, from his father, who said: "I embraced Islam while I had two wives who were sisters, and the Prophet ﷺ commanded me to divorce one of them."

Then Imam Ahmad, al-Tirmidhi, and Ibn Majah narrated it from the hadith of Ibn Lahi'ah. Abu Dawud and al-Tirmidhi also narrated it from the hadith of Yazid ibn Abi Habib, both from Abu Wahb al-Jayshani. Al-Tirmidhi said: his name is Daylam ibn al-Hawshah, from al-Dahhak ibn Fayruz al-Daylami, from his father, with the same. In a wording of al-Tirmidhi: the Prophet ﷺ said: "Choose whichever of them you wish." Then al-Tirmidhi said: this is a hasan hadith.

Ibn Majah also narrated it by another chain, saying: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, Abd al-Salam ibn Harb narrated to us, from Ishaq ibn Abd Allah ibn Abi Farwah, from Abu Wahb al-Jayshani, from Abu Khirash al-Ru'ayni, who said: "I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while I had two sisters whom I had married in the Jahiliyyah, and he said: 'When you return, divorce one of them.'"

I say: it is possible that this Abu Khirash is al-Dahhak ibn Fayruz, and it is possible that he is someone else, in which case Abu Wahb would have narrated it from two people, from Fayruz al-Daylami. And Allah knows best.

Ibn Mardawayh said: Abd Allah ibn Yahya ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated to us, Ahmad ibn Yahya al-Khawlani narrated to us, Haytham ibn Kharijah narrated to us, Yahya ibn Ishaq narrated to us, from Ishaq ibn Abd Allah ibn Abi Farwah, from Ruzayq ibn Hakim, from Kathir ibn Murrah, from al-Daylami, who said: "I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, I have two sisters under me?' He said: 'Divorce whichever of them you wish.'"

The Daylami mentioned first is al-Dahhak ibn Fayruz al-Daylami, may Allah be pleased with him. Abu Zur'ah al-Dimashqi said: he used to accompany Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan. The second is Abu Fayruz al-Daylami, may Allah be pleased with him, who was among the commanders in Yemen who were appointed to kill al-Aswad al-Ansi, the false prophet, may Allah curse him.

As for combining two sisters in ownership by the right hand, it is also unlawful, because of the generality of the verse, and Ibn Abi Hatim said:

Ibn Kathir's Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim, on Surah an-Nisa' (4), verses 23–24 (part 3 of 4):

Abu Zur'a narrated to us: Musa ibn Isma'il narrated to us: Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Abdullah ibn Abi 'Utbah (or 'Utbah), from Ibn Mas'ud: that he was asked about a man who combines between two sisters [[In A: "between the two sisters (al-ummatayn al-ukhtayn)".]], and he disliked it. The questioner said to him: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿Except what your right hands possess﴾. Ibn Mas'ud said to him: And your camel is among what your right hand possesses.

This is the well-known position of the majority (al-jumhur) and the four Imams and others, although some of the early scholars (salaf) hesitated on this matter. Imam Malik said, from Ibn Shihab, from Qabisah ibn Dhu'ayb: that a man asked 'Uthman ibn 'Affan about two sisters among those owned by the right hand: may they be combined? 'Uthman said: One verse permits them and one verse forbids them, and I would not do that. So the man left his presence and met a man from the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ and asked him about that. He said: If I had any authority in the matter, and then I found anyone who did that, I would make him an example (nakal). Malik said: Ibn Shihab said: I think he meant 'Ali ibn Abi Talib. He said: And it reached me that al-Zubayr ibn al-'Awwam said the like of that.

Shaykh Abu 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-Barr al-Namari, may Allah have mercy on him, said in his book "al-Istidhkar": Qabisah ibn Dhu'ayb only referred to 'Ali ibn Abi Talib by a kunya (indirect reference) because of his companionship with 'Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan, and they disliked mentioning 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him.

Then Abu 'Umar said, may Allah have mercy on him: Khalaf ibn Ahmad, may Allah have mercy on him, narrated to me by reading to him: that Khalaf ibn Mutarrif narrated to them: Ayyub ibn Sulayman, Sa'id [[In R, A: "Ma'bad".]] ibn Sulayman and Muhammad ibn 'Umar ibn Lubabah narrated to us, saying: Abu Zayd 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ibrahim narrated to us: Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Muqri' [[In A: "al-Maqbari".]] narrated to us, from Musa ibn Ayyub al-Ghafiqi: my paternal uncle Iyas ibn 'Amir narrated to me, saying: I asked 'Ali ibn Abi Talib [may Allah be pleased with him] [[Addition from J, A.]] and said: I have two sisters from among what my right hand possesses; I took one of them as a concubine (surriyyah) and she bore me children, then I desired the other, so what should I do? 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, said: Free the one you were having intercourse with, and then have intercourse with the other. I said: But people say: rather, marry her and then have intercourse with the other. 'Ali said: Do you think that if her husband divorced her or died, she would not return to you? Freeing her is safer for you. Then 'Ali took my hand and said to me: What is forbidden to you of what your right hand possesses is what is forbidden to you in the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, of free women, except the number (or he said: except the four), and what is forbidden to you through nursing is what is forbidden to you through lineage in the Book of Allah.

Then Abu 'Umar said: This hadith is a journey (rihlah) [[In R: "a journey of a man"]]; even if the man had gained nothing from the far east or the far west to Makkah other than it, his journey would not have been in vain [[al-Istidhkar of Ibn 'Abd al-Barr (16/252).]].

I say: It has also been narrated from 'Ali something similar to what preceded from 'Uthman. Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh said:

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ibrahim narrated to us: Muhammad ibn al-'Abbas narrated to us: Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak al-Makhrimi [[In A: "al-Makhzumi".]] narrated to me: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ghazwan narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us, from 'Amr ibn Dinar, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas who said: 'Ali ibn Abi Talib said to me: One verse forbids them and one verse permits them, meaning the two sisters. Ibn 'Abbas said: The kinship of them to me forbids them for me, and the kinship of some of them to others does not forbid them for me, meaning the slave women. The Jahiliyyah used to forbid what you forbid except the wife of the father and the combining of two sisters. When Islam came, Allah sent down: ﴿And do not marry those whom your fathers married of women, except what has already passed﴾ and ﴿and that you combine between two sisters, except what has already passed﴾, meaning: in marriage.

Then Abu 'Umar said: Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal narrated: Muhammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Hisham, from Ibn Sirin, from Ibn Mas'ud who said: What is forbidden from slave women is what is forbidden from free women, except the number. And from Ibn Sirin and al-Sha'bi the like of that.

Abu 'Umar, may Allah have mercy on him, said: The like of the position of 'Uthman has been narrated from a group of the early scholars, among them Ibn 'Abbas, but they were disputed about, and none of the jurists of the cities, of the Hijaz, of Iraq and what lies beyond them to the east, nor of al-Sham, nor of the west, took notice of that, except one who departed from their community by following the literal sense (al-zahir) and rejecting analogy (al-qiyas). Whoever acts on that has abandoned what we have agreed upon. The community of jurists agree that it is not lawful to combine two sisters by ownership of the right hand for intercourse, just as it is not lawful in marriage. The Muslims have agreed that the meaning of His words, Exalted is He: ﴿Forbidden to you are your mothers, your daughters, your sisters [and your paternal aunts and your maternal aunts] ﴾ to the end of the verse, is that marriage and ownership by the right hand regarding all of these are equal; so by reasoning and analogy, combining two sisters, the mothers of women, and stepdaughters must likewise be forbidden. This is also the view of their majority, and they are the authority by which whoever opposes it and departs from it is refuted; and Allah is the One Praised [[al-Istidhkar of Ibn 'Abd al-Barr (16/250-251).]].

* *

His words, Exalted is He: ﴿And the married women among women, except what your right hands possess﴾, meaning: and there is forbidden to you the women of others who are married (al-muhsanat, i.e., those who are married), ﴿except what your right hands possess﴾, meaning: except what you have acquired of them through captivity (sabi), for it is lawful for you to have intercourse with them once you have made them undergo istibra' (a waiting period to establish they are not pregnant). The verse was revealed concerning that.

Imam Ahmad said: 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Sufyan informed us, that is al-Thawri, from 'Uthman al-Batti, from Abu al-Khalil, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri who said: We took captive women from the captives of Awtas, and they had husbands, so we disliked to have intercourse with them while they had husbands, so we asked the Prophet ﷺ, and this verse was revealed: ﴿And the married women among women, except what your right hands possess﴾. [He said:] So we made their private parts lawful to us.

Thus al-Tirmidhi narrated it from Ahmad ibn Mani', from Hushaym; al-Nasa'i narrated it from the hadith of Sufyan al-Thawri and Shu'bah ibn al-Hajjaj, all three from 'Uthman al-Batti; Ibn Jarir narrated it from the hadith of Ash'ath ibn Sawwar from 'Uthman al-Batti; and Muslim narrated it in his Sahih from the hadith of Shu'bah from Qatadah, both from Abu al-Khalil Salih ibn Abi Maryam, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, and so on. Thus 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated it from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, from Abu al-Khalil, from Abu Sa'id, likewise [[Tafsir 'Abd al-Razzaq (1/153); Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3017); Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra no. (11097); Sahih Muslim no. (1456); Tafsir al-Tabari (8/153).]].

It has also been narrated by another route from Abu al-Khalil, from Abu 'Alqamah al-Hashimi, from Abu Sa'id. Imam Ahmad said:

Ibn Abi 'Adi narrated to us, from Sa'id, from Qatadah, from Abu al-Khalil, from Abu 'Alqamah, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri: that the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ captured captive women on the day of Awtas, who had husbands from among the people of polytheism; so some of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ held back and considered it sinful (ta'ththama) to have intercourse with them. He said: So this verse was revealed concerning that: ﴿And the married women among women, except what your right hands possess﴾.

Thus Muslim, Abu Dawud and al-Nasa'i narrated it from the hadith of Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah (Muslim added: and Shu'bah), and al-Tirmidhi narrated it from the hadith of Hammam ibn Yahya; all three from Qatadah, with its chain, similar to it. Al-Tirmidhi said: This is a hasan hadith, and I do not know that anyone mentioned Abu 'Alqamah in this hadith except what Hammam narrated from Qatadah. So he said. But Sa'id and Shu'bah have followed him; and Allah knows best [[Al-Musnad (3/84); Sahih Muslim no. (1456); Sunan Abi Dawud no. (2155); Sunan al-Nasa'i (6/110); Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3016).]].

Al-Tabarani narrated through the route of al-Dahhak from Ibn 'Abbas that it was revealed concerning the captives of Khaybar, and he mentioned a hadith similar to the hadith of Abu Sa'id. A group of the early scholars went to the view that the sale of a slave woman is a divorce for her from her husband, taking by the generality of this verse. Ibn Jarir said: Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, from Shu'bah, from Mughirah, from Ibrahim: that he was asked about a slave woman who is sold while she has a husband? He said: 'Abd Allah (Ibn Mas'ud) used to say: her sale is her divorce, and he recited this verse: ﴿And the married women among women, except what your right hands possess﴾.

Similarly Sufyan narrated it from Mansur, Mughirah and al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, from Ibn Mas'ud who said: her sale is her divorce. This is a broken (munqati') chain.

Sufyan al-Thawri said, from Khalid, from Abu Qilabah, from Ibn Mas'ud who said: if a slave woman is sold while she has a husband, then her master has more right to her private part.

Sa'id narrated it from Qatadah who said: Ubayy ibn Ka'b, Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah and Ibn 'Abbas said: her sale is her divorce.

Ibn Jarir said: Ya'qub narrated to me, [narrated to us] [[Addition from J, R, A.]] Ibn 'Ulayyah, from Khalid, from Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas who said: the divorce of a slave woman is six: her sale is her divorce, her manumission is her divorce, her gifting is her divorce, her release is her divorce, and her husband's divorce is her divorce. [[What is mentioned in all manuscripts is five, not six.]]

'Abd al-Razzaq said: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from Ibn al-Musayyab, his statement: ﴿And the married women among women﴾, he said: they are those who have husbands, whose marriage Allah forbade, except what your right hand possesses, so her sale is her divorce. Ma'mar said: al-Hasan said the like of that.

Similarly Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah narrated from Qatadah, from al-Hasan, regarding His words: ﴿And the married women among women, except what your right hands possess﴾, he said: if she has a husband, then her sale is her divorce.

'Awf said, from al-Hasan: the sale of a slave woman is her divorce, and her sale is her divorce.

This is the view of these early scholars [may Allah have mercy on them]. But the majority, both in earlier and later times, disagreed with them, and held that the sale of a slave woman is not a divorce for her, because the buyer stands in the place of the seller, and the seller had removed this benefit from his ownership and sold her stripped of it. They relied in this on the hadith of Barirah, recorded in the two Sahihs and elsewhere: 'A'ishah, the Mother of the Believers, bought her and immediately freed her, and her marriage to her husband Mughith was not annulled; rather the Prophet ﷺ gave her the choice between annulment and continuation, and she chose annulment, and her story is well known. So if the sale of a slave woman were a divorce for her, as these people said, the Prophet ﷺ would not have given her the choice. Since he gave her the choice, this indicates the continuation of the marriage, and that what is meant by the verse is only the captives (al-masbiyyat); and Allah knows best.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 4, verse 23–24 (part 4 of 4):

It has been said: the meaning of His words, ﴿And the married women among women﴾, is: the chaste ones are forbidden to you until you take possession of their chastity through marriage, with witnesses, dowries, and a guardian (wali), one, two, three, or four. This is related by Ibn Jarir from Abu al-'Aliyah, Tawus and others. 'Umar and 'Ubaydah said: ﴿And the married women among women﴾ refers to all beyond the four are forbidden to you, except what your right hands possess.
* *
As for His words, ﴿The decree of Allah upon you﴾, it means: this prohibition is a decree that Allah has prescribed for you, so hold fast to His Book, do not go beyond its limits, and adhere to His law and what He has made obligatory.
'Ubaydah, 'Ata' and al-Suddi said regarding His words, ﴿The decree of Allah upon you﴾, that it means the four. Ibrahim said: ﴿The decree of Allah upon you﴾ means what He has forbidden to you.
* *
As for His words, ﴿And lawful for you is what is beyond that﴾, meaning: whoever is other than those mentioned among the forbidden women is lawful for you. This was said by 'Ata' and others. 'Ubaydah and al-Suddi said: ﴿And lawful for you is what is beyond that﴾ means what is less than the four. This is far-fetched, and the correct view is the saying of 'Ata' as already mentioned. Qatadah said: ﴿And lawful for you is what is beyond that﴾ means what your right hands possess.
This verse is the one used by those who argue for the permissibility of combining two sisters, and by the one who says: "One verse made them lawful, and another verse made them unlawful."
* *
As for His words, ﴿That you seek with your wealth, chaste, not fornicating﴾, meaning: obtain by your wealth wives, up to four, or concubines, as many as you wish, through the lawful way. Therefore He said: ﴿chaste, not fornicating﴾.
* *
As for His words, ﴿So for whatever you enjoy from them, give them their payment as an obligation﴾, meaning: just as you enjoy them, give them their dowries in return for that, like His words: ﴿And how could you take it while you have gone in unto one another?﴾ [An-Nisa: 21], and like His words: ﴿And give the women their dowries as a gift﴾, and like His words: ﴿And it is not lawful for you to take anything of what you have given them﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 229]. The generality of this verse has been used as evidence for temporary marriage (nikah al-mut'ah). There is no doubt that it was legislated at the beginning of Islam, and then it was abrogated (naskh) afterward. Al-Shafi'i and a group of scholars held that it was permitted, then abrogated, then permitted, then abrogated, twice. Others said more than that, and others said: it was permitted only once, then abrogated, and was not permitted after that.
It has been related from Ibn 'Abbas and a group of the Companions that it was permitted out of necessity, and this is a narration from Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal, may Allah have mercy on them all. Ibn 'Abbas, Ubayy ibn Ka'b, Sa'id ibn Jubayr and al-Suddi used to recite: "So for whatever you enjoy from them until a specified term, give them their payment as an obligation." Mujahid said: it was revealed concerning temporary marriage. But the majority are of a different opinion, and the reliance is on what is established in the two Sahihs from the Commander of the Faithful 'Ali ibn Abi Talib [may Allah be pleased with him] who said: The Prophet ﷺ forbade temporary marriage and the flesh of domestic donkeys on the day of Khaybar. [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4216) and Sahih Muslim no. (1407).] This hadith has established wordings which are in the book "al-Ahkam".
In Sahih Muslim, from al-Rabi' ibn Sabrah ibn Ma'bad al-Juhani, from his father: that he fought alongside the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at the conquest of Makkah, and he said: "O people, I had permitted you to enjoy women, but indeed Allah has forbidden that until the Day of Resurrection. Whoever has any of them, let him release her, and do not take anything of what you have given them." And in a narration of Muslim concerning the Farewell Pilgrimage [Sahih Muslim no. (1406)], and it has wordings whose place is the book "al-Ahkam".
* *
As for His words, ﴿And there is no blame upon you for what you mutually agree upon after the obligation﴾: whoever takes this verse as referring to temporary marriage for a specified term said: there is no blame upon you, once the term has ended, if they mutually agree upon an increase in it and an increase in the payment.
Al-Suddi said: if he wishes, he may satisfy her from after the first obligation—meaning the payment he gave her for his enjoyment of her—before the term ends between them, by saying: "I enjoy you again for such and such," and he increases it, before she has purified her womb on the day the period ends. This is His words: ﴿And there is no blame upon you for what you mutually agree upon after the obligation﴾.
Al-Suddi said: when the period has ended, he has no further claim over her, she is free from him, and she must purify what is in her womb, and there is no inheritance between them, so neither of them inherits from the other.
Those who held the first view explained it like His words: ﴿And give the women their dowries as a gift; but if they give you something of it willingly, then consume it with satisfaction and ease﴾ [An-Nisa: 4], meaning: if you have fixed a dowry for her and she releases you from it, or from some part of it, then there is no blame upon you or upon her in that.
Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, al-Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman related to us, from his father, who said: al-Hadrami claimed that men used to fix the dowry, then perhaps one of them would fall into hardship. So He said: ﴿And there is no blame upon you﴾ O people ﴿for what you mutually agree upon after the obligation﴾, meaning: if she waives some of it for you, it is lawful for you. Ibn Jarir chose this view. And 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah related from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿And there is no blame upon you for what you mutually agree upon after the obligation﴾; the mutual agreement is that he pays her dowry in full and then gives her the choice, whether to remain or to separate.
* *
As for His words, ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever Knowing and Wise﴾: the mention of these two attributes is fitting after the legislation of these prohibitions [the great ones].

This noble verse is the verse on the prohibited relatives (al-mahārim) through lineage (nasab), together with what follows from fosterage (raḍāʿ) and the relatives prohibited by marriage (ṣihr). Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn Sinan narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us, from Sufyan ibn Habib, from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: "Seven are forbidden to you by lineage and seven by marriage," and he recited: ﴿Forbidden to you are your mothers and your daughters and your sisters﴾ to the end of the verse.

Abu Saʿid ibn Yahya ibn Saʿid narrated to us, Abu Ahmad narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Ismaʿil ibn Raja' [in ج and أ: "ibn Jabir"], from ʿUmayr, the freedman (mawlā) of Ibn ʿAbbas, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: "Seven are prohibited by lineage and seven by marriage." Then he recited: ﴿Forbidden to you are your mothers and your daughters and your sisters and your paternal aunts and your maternal aunts and your brother's daughters and your sister's daughters﴾. These are the lineage prohibitions.

The majority of scholars have derived the prohibition of a girl created from the water of an adulterer (the adulterer being her father) from the general wording of His statement, ﴿and your daughters﴾. She is a daughter, so she falls within the general term. This is the position of Abu Hanifa, Malik, and Ahmad ibn Hanbal. It has been reported from al-Shafiʿi that he permitted marriage to her, since she is not a legal daughter (bint sharʿiyya). Just as she is not included in His statement, ﴿Allah enjoins you concerning your children﴾, since she does not inherit by consensus, so too she is not included in this verse. And Allah knows best.

* *

As for His statement: ﴿And your mothers who have nursed you, and your sisters through fosterage﴾, meaning: just as your mother who bore you is forbidden to you, so too is your mother who nursed you forbidden to you. For this reason al-Bukhari and Muslim in the two Sahihs related, from the hadith of Malik ibn Anas, from ʿAbdullah ibn Abi Bakr ibn Muhammad ibn ʿAmr ibn Hazm, from ʿAmra bint ʿAbd al-Rahman, from ʿAʾisha, the Mother of the Believers, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Fosterage prohibits what birth prohibits." In a wording of Muslim: "What is forbidden by lineage is forbidden by fosterage" [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (3105), Sahih Muslim no. (1444), and Muwatta' Malik (in the chapter on fosterage)].

Some jurists have said: "Just as something is prohibited by lineage, so it is prohibited by fosterage, except in four cases." Others said: "Except in six cases," which are mentioned in the books of furuʿ (derivative jurisprudence). The verified position is that nothing is excepted from this, because some of these cases are similar to cases in lineage, and some are prohibited only through marriage (ṣihr). Therefore nothing at all contradicts the hadith, and all praise belongs to Allah.

Then the imams differed concerning the number of sucklings that establish the prohibition. Some held that mere nursing prohibits, by the generality of this verse. This is the view of Malik, and it is related from Ibn ʿUmar. Saʿid ibn al-Musayyab, ʿUrwa ibn al-Zubayr, and al-Zuhri also held this view.

Others said: fewer than three sucklings do not prohibit, based on what is established in Sahih Muslim, through the chain of Hisham ibn ʿUrwa from his father, from ʿAʾisha, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "A single suck (al-mașṣa) does not prohibit, nor do two sucks" [Sahih Muslim no. (1450). It is, however, in Muslim through the route of Ibn Abi Mulayka from ʿAbdullah ibn al-Zubayr from ʿAʾisha. It is also related by al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra through the route of Hisham ibn ʿUrwa from his father from ʿAʾisha and Ibn al-Zubayr, no. (5458)].

Qatada narrated from Abu al-Khalil, from ʿAbdullah ibn al-Harith, from Umm al-Fadl, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "A single nursing (raḍʿa) does not prohibit, nor do two nursings; a single suck does not prohibit, nor do two sucks." In another wording: "A single gulping (imlāja) does not prohibit, nor do two gulpings" [related by Muslim, no. (1451)].

Among those who held this view were Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal, Ishaq ibn Rahawayh, Abu ʿUbayd, and Abu Thawr. It is related from ʿAlī, ʿAʾisha, Umm al-Fadl, Ibn al-Zubayr, Sulayman ibn Yasar, and Saʿid ibn Jubayr, may Allah have mercy on them.

Others said: fewer than five sucklings do not prohibit, based on what is established in Sahih Muslim through the route of Malik, from ʿAbdullah ibn Abi Bakr, from ʿAmra [in ج، ر، أ: "from ʿUrwa"], from ʿAʾisha, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: "Among what Allah revealed of the Qur'an was: ten known sucklings make prohibition. Then they were abrogated (nusikhna, i.e., naskh: abrogation) by five known sucklings, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) died while they were still among what is recited of the Qur'an."

ʿAbd al-Razzaq related from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhri, from ʿUrwa, from ʿAʾisha something similar [Sahih Muslim no. (1452)].

In the hadith of Sahla bint Suhayl: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) instructed her to nurse the freedman of Abu Hudhayfa five sucklings [and see her story in al-Musnad (6/201)]. ʿAʾisha used to instruct anyone who wished to enter her presence to be nursed five sucklings. This is the view of al-Shafiʿi, may Allah the Exalted have mercy on him, and his companions.

Then it should be known that fosterage must occur in infancy, before two years, according to the view of the majority. As we have already discussed this matter in Surat al-Baqara, at His statement: ﴿Mothers shall nurse their children two complete years for whoever wishes to complete the nursing﴾ [the verse: 233].

They differed: does the milk of the sire (labn al-fahl, i.e., the milk of a woman impregnated by a man, which makes him a foster father) prohibit, as is the view of the majority of the four imams and others? Or is fosterage restricted to the mother only, and does it not extend to the father's side, as is the view of some of the early generation (salaf)? There are two positions. The verification of all this is in the book "al-Aḥkām al-Kabīr."

* *

As for His statement: ﴿And the mothers of your wives and your stepdaughters (rabāʾib) who are in your guardianship, born of your wives with whom you have consummated the marriage; but if you have not consummated the marriage with them, there is no blame upon you﴾. As for the mother of the woman, she is forbidden upon marriage to her daughter by the mere contract, whether or not he has consummated with her. As for the stepdaughter (rabība), who is the daughter of the woman, she is not forbidden to her mother by the mere contract until he consummates with her. If he divorces the mother before consummation, it is permissible for him to marry her daughter. For this reason He said: ﴿And your stepdaughters who are in your guardianship, born of your wives with whom you have consummated the marriage; but if you have not consummated with them, there is no blame upon you﴾ [meaning] in marrying them. This is specific to the stepdaughters alone.

Some understood the pronoun to refer to both the mothers and the stepdaughters, and said: neither the mother nor the daughter is forbidden by the mere contract to the other until he consummates with her, because of His statement: ﴿But if you have not consummated with them, there is no blame upon you﴾.

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, Ibn Abi ʿAdi and ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to us, from Saʿid, from Qatada, from Khilas ibn ʿAmr, from ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him, concerning a man who married a woman and divorced her before consummation: may he marry her mother? He said: "She is in the position of the stepdaughter."

Ibn Bashshar also narrated to us: Yahya ibn Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatada, from Saʿid ibn al-Musayyab, from Zayd ibn Thabit, who said: "If a man divorces his wife before consummating with her, there is no harm in his marrying her mother."

In a narration from Qatada, from Saʿid, from Zayd ibn Thabit: he used to say, "If she dies while he is with her and he takes her inheritance, it is disliked for him to marry her mother. But if he divorces her before consummation, he may do so if he wishes."

Ibn al-Mundhir said: Ishaq narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Razzaq, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Abu Bakr ibn Hafs informed me, from Muslim ibn ʿUwaymir al-Ajda', that Bakr ibn Kinana informed him that his father married him to a woman in Ta'if. He said: "I did not have intercourse with her until my paternal uncle died, and her mother had a great deal of wealth. My father said: 'Would you want her mother?' I asked Ibn ʿAbbas and informed him of the report, and he said: 'Marry her mother.' I asked Ibn ʿUmar, and he said: 'Do not marry her.' I informed my father of what Ibn ʿAbbas said and what Ibn ʿUmar said, so my father wrote to Muʿawiya and informed him in his letter of what Ibn ʿUmar and Ibn ʿAbbas said. Muʿawiya wrote: 'I do not make lawful what Allah has forbidden, nor do I forbid what Allah has made lawful. You and that matter; there are many women other than her.' He neither forbade it to me nor permitted it to me, so my father withdrew from her mother and did not marry her."

ʿAbd al-Razzaq said: Maʿmar informed us, from Simak ibn al-Fadl, from a man, from ʿAbdullah ibn al-Zubayr, who said: "The stepdaughter and the mother are equal; there is no harm in it if he has not consummated with the woman." In its chain there is an unnamed man (mubham) who was not identified [in أ: "a suspect man (muttahim)"].

Ibn Jurayj said: ʿIkrima ibn Khalid informed me that Mujahid said to him concerning: ﴿And the mothers of your wives and your stepdaughters who are in your guardianship﴾: "He meant by both of them consummation together." So this position is reported, as you see, from ʿAlī, Zayd ibn Thabit, ʿAbdullah ibn al-Zubayr, Mujahid, Ibn Jubayr, and Ibn ʿAbbas. Muʿawiya had reservations about it, and among the Shafiʿis Abu al-Hasan Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Sabuni held it, as reported by al-Rafiʿi from al-ʿAbbadi. [The majority of scholars from the early and later generations opposed him, holding that the stepdaughter is not forbidden by the mere contract to the mother, and that she is forbidden only by consummation with the mother, unlike the mother, who is forbidden by the mere contract to the stepdaughter.]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Jaʿfar ibn Muhammad ibn Harun ibn ʿAzra [in ج، أ: "ʿUrwa"] narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Wahhab narrated to us, from Saʿid, from Qatada, from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbas: that he used to say, "If a man divorces a woman before consummating with her, or she dies, her mother is not lawful to him." And he said: "She is a mubham (an unrestricted, general case), so he disliked it."

Then he said: It is reported from Ibn Masʿud, ʿImran ibn Husayn, Masruq, Tawus, ʿIkrima, ʿAta', al-Hasan, Makhul, Ibn Sirin, Qatada, and al-Zuhri something similar. This is the position of the four imams, the seven jurists, and the majority of jurists, past and present, and all praise and grace belong to Allah.

Ibn Jarir said: "The correct view, meaning the view of the one who said 'the mother is among the mubhamat (the general, unrestricted categories)', is that because Allah did not stipulate consummation with them as He stipulated it with the mothers of the stepdaughters. Moreover, this is also a consensus of the proof which it is not permissible to oppose, in what it has come with unanimously." It has also been related with this meaning a report from the Prophet (ﷺ), but its chain is questionable. It is what al-Muthanna narrated to me: Hibban ibn Musa narrated to us, Ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, al-Muthanna ibn al-Sabbah informed us, from ʿAmr ibn Shuʿayb, from his father, from his grandfather, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "If a man marries a woman, it is not lawful for him to marry her mother, whether or not he has consummated with the daughter. And if he marries the mother and does not consummate with her and then divorces her, he may marry the daughter if he wishes" [Tafsir al-Tabari (8/146); and al-Bayhaqi related it in al-Sunan al-Kubra (7/160) through this route, then said: "al-Muthanna ibn al-Sabbah is not strong."]

Then he said: This report, although there is in its chain what there is, nevertheless the consensus of the authorities on the soundness of the view that it is to be acted upon makes it unnecessary to cite other evidence for its soundness.

As for His saying: ﴿And your stepdaughters who are in your guardianship, born of your wives with whom you have consummated marriage﴾, the majority of the Imams (a'immah) hold that the stepdaughter (rabibah) is forbidden whether she is in the man's guardianship or not in his guardianship. They said: this address came out in the form of what is usual, so it has no implicit restriction (mafhum), like His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And do not compel your slave girls to prostitution if they desire chastity﴾ [An-Nur: 33].

In the Two Sahihs, Umm Habibah said: "O Messenger of Allah, marry my sister, the daughter of Abu Sufyan." And in a wording of Muslim: "'Izzah, the daughter of Abu Sufyan." He said: "Do you like that?" She said: "Yes. I am not exclusively yours, and I love that my sister should share in the good with me." He said: "Indeed, that is not lawful for me." She said: "We have heard that you intend to marry the daughter of Abu Salamah." He said: "The daughter of Umm Salamah?" She said: "Yes." He said: "Indeed, even if she were not my stepdaughter in my guardianship, she would still not be lawful for me. She is the daughter of my brother through nursing. Thuwaybah nursed me and Abu Salamah, so do not offer me your daughters or your sisters." And in a narration of al-Bukhari: "Indeed, if I had not married Umm Salamah, she would not have been lawful for me."

So he made the basis of the prohibition the mere fact of his marrying Umm Salamah, and ruled the prohibition on that basis. This is the position of the Four Imams, the Seven Jurists, and the majority of the later and earlier scholars. It has been said that the stepdaughter is only forbidden if she is in the man's guardianship, and if she is not in that situation she is not forbidden.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur'ah narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn Musa narrated to us, Hisham, that is Ibn Yusuf, informed us, from Ibn Juraij, Ibrahim ibn Ubayd ibn Rifa'ah narrated to me, Malik ibn Aws ibn al-Hadthan informed me, who said: I had a wife who died, and she had borne me children, and I grieved over her. Ali ibn Abi Talib met me and said: "What is the matter with you?" I said: "The woman has died." Ali said: "Does she have a daughter?" I said: "Yes, and she is in al-Ta'if." He said: "Was she in your guardianship?" I said: "No, she is in al-Ta'if." He said: "Then marry her." I said: "Then where is the saying of Allah [Mighty and Majestic] ﴿and your stepdaughters who are in your guardianship﴾?" He said: "Indeed, she was not in your guardianship; that applies only when she is in your guardianship."

This is a strong, established chain up to Ali ibn Abi Talib, on the condition of Muslim, and it is an extremely rare view. Dawud ibn Ali al-Zahiri and his companions went to this view. Abu al-Qasim al-Rafi'i related it from Malik, may Allah have mercy on him, and Ibn Hazm chose it. My shaykh, the memorizer Abu Abdullah al-Dhahabi, related to me that he presented this to the Shaykh and Imam Taqi al-Din Ibn Taymiyyah, may Allah have mercy on him, and he found it problematic and held back in that matter. And Allah knows best.

Ibn al-Mundhir said: Ali ibn Abd al-Aziz narrated to us, al-Athram narrated to us, from Abu Ubaydah concerning His saying ﴿who are in your guardianship﴾, he said: "In your houses."

As for the stepdaughter in ownership by the right hand (milk al-yamin), Imam Malik ibn Anas said, from Ibn Shihab: Umar ibn al-Khattab was asked about a woman and her daughter who were slaves in ownership, one of them being lawful to him after the other. Umar said: "I do not like to unite them both," meaning, to have intercourse with both of them by right of ownership. This report is disconnected (munqati').

Sunayd ibn Dawud said in his tafsir: Abu al-Ahwas narrated to us, from Tariq ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Qays, who said: I said to Ibn Abbas: "Can a man have intercourse with a woman and her daughter, both slaves belonging to him?" He said: "One verse made them lawful and another verse made them unlawful, and I would not do it."

Shaykh Abu Umar ibn Abd al-Barr, may Allah have mercy on him, said: There is no disagreement among the scholars that it is not lawful for anyone to have intercourse with a woman and her daughter in ownership, because Allah has prohibited that in marriage. He said: ﴿And the mothers of your wives and your stepdaughters who are in your guardianship, born of your wives...﴾ The ownership by the right hand follows marriage, except what is reported from Umar and Ibn Abbas, and none of the leading jurists or those who followed them agree with that. Hisham narrated from Qatadah: the daughter of a stepdaughter and the daughter of her daughter are not permissible, even if they are further down through many generations. Qatadah said the same on the authority of Abu al-Aliyah.

The meaning of His saying: ﴿with whom you have consummated marriage﴾ is: "with whom you have married." This was said by Ibn Abbas and others.

Ibn Juraij said, on the authority of Ata: it means that she is brought to him, and he uncovers her, examines her, and sits between her legs. I said: "What if he does that in the house of her family?" He said: "It is the same, and it is enough that her daughter has been made unlawful to him."

Ibn Jarir said: There is a consensus of all that a man's privacy (khalwah) with his wife does not make her daughter unlawful to him if he divorces her before touching or intimacy with her, or before looking at her private part with desire. This indicates that the meaning of that is reaching her through intercourse.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿and the wives of your sons who are from your loins﴾, that is: and there are made unlawful to you the wives of your sons whom you have fathered from your loins, excluding adopted sons (ad'iya') whom they used to adopt in the Jahiliyyah, as He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿So when Zayd had no more need of her, We married her to you, so that there would be no difficulty for the believers concerning the wives of their adopted sons, when they have no more need of them﴾ [Al-Ahzab: 37].

Ibn Juraij said: I asked Ata about His saying: ﴿and the wives of your sons who are from your loins﴾.
