He said: "We used to narrate, and Allah knows best, that when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ married the wife of Zayd, the polytheists in Makkah spoke about that, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed ﴿and the wives of your sons who are from your loins﴾, and there was revealed ﴿Nor has He made your adopted sons your sons﴾ [Al-Ahzab: 4], and there was revealed ﴿Muhammad is not the father of any one of your men﴾ [Al-Ahzab: 40]."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur'ah narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr al-Muqaddami narrated to us, al-Jarrah ibn al-Harith narrated to us, from al-Ash'ath, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad, that these verses are general (mubhamat): ﴿and the wives of your sons﴾, ﴿the mothers of your wives﴾. Then he said: Similar was narrated from Tawus, Ibrahim, al-Zuhri and Makhul.

I say: the meaning of "mubhamat" is that they are general, applying to those with whom marriage was consummated and those with whom it was not, so that marriage is made unlawful merely by the contract itself, and this is agreed upon. If it is said: from where is the wife of one's son by nursing made unlawful, as is the view of the majority, while some people report it as a consensus although she is not of one's loins? The answer is from His saying, peace and blessings be upon him: "What is unlawful by birth is unlawful by nursing."

* *

As for His saying: ﴿and that you should combine two sisters, except what has already passed [Indeed, Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful]﴾, that is: and there is made unlawful to you combining two sisters together in marriage, and likewise in ownership by the right hand, except what was among you in your Jahiliyyah, for We have pardoned that and forgiven it. This indicates that there is no alternative for what is yet to come and no exception for what has passed, as He said: ﴿They will not taste death therein except the first death﴾ [Ad-Dukhan: 56], which indicates that they will never taste death therein. The scholars from the Companions, the Successors, and the Imams, past and present, have agreed that combining two sisters in marriage is forbidden, and whoever embraces Islam while having two sisters as wives must choose, keeping one of them and divorcing the other without alternative.

Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal said: Musa ibn Dawud narrated to us, Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to us, from Abu Wahb al-Jayshani, from al-Dahhak ibn Fayruz, from his father, who said: "I embraced Islam while I had two wives who were sisters, and the Prophet ﷺ commanded me to divorce one of them."

Then Imam Ahmad, al-Tirmidhi, and Ibn Majah narrated it from the hadith of Ibn Lahi'ah. Abu Dawud and al-Tirmidhi also narrated it from the hadith of Yazid ibn Abi Habib, both from Abu Wahb al-Jayshani. Al-Tirmidhi said: his name is Daylam ibn al-Hawshah, from al-Dahhak ibn Fayruz al-Daylami, from his father, with the same. In a wording of al-Tirmidhi: the Prophet ﷺ said: "Choose whichever of them you wish." Then al-Tirmidhi said: this is a hasan hadith.

Ibn Majah also narrated it by another chain, saying: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, Abd al-Salam ibn Harb narrated to us, from Ishaq ibn Abd Allah ibn Abi Farwah, from Abu Wahb al-Jayshani, from Abu Khirash al-Ru'ayni, who said: "I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while I had two sisters whom I had married in the Jahiliyyah, and he said: 'When you return, divorce one of them.'"

I say: it is possible that this Abu Khirash is al-Dahhak ibn Fayruz, and it is possible that he is someone else, in which case Abu Wahb would have narrated it from two people, from Fayruz al-Daylami. And Allah knows best.

Ibn Mardawayh said: Abd Allah ibn Yahya ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated to us, Ahmad ibn Yahya al-Khawlani narrated to us, Haytham ibn Kharijah narrated to us, Yahya ibn Ishaq narrated to us, from Ishaq ibn Abd Allah ibn Abi Farwah, from Ruzayq ibn Hakim, from Kathir ibn Murrah, from al-Daylami, who said: "I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, I have two sisters under me?' He said: 'Divorce whichever of them you wish.'"

The Daylami mentioned first is al-Dahhak ibn Fayruz al-Daylami, may Allah be pleased with him. Abu Zur'ah al-Dimashqi said: he used to accompany Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan. The second is Abu Fayruz al-Daylami, may Allah be pleased with him, who was among the commanders in Yemen who were appointed to kill al-Aswad al-Ansi, the false prophet, may Allah curse him.

As for combining two sisters in ownership by the right hand, it is also unlawful, because of the generality of the verse, and Ibn Abi Hatim said:

Ibn Kathir's Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim, on Surah an-Nisa' (4), verses 23–24 (part 3 of 4):

Abu Zur'a narrated to us: Musa ibn Isma'il narrated to us: Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Abdullah ibn Abi 'Utbah (or 'Utbah), from Ibn Mas'ud: that he was asked about a man who combines between two sisters [[In A: "between the two sisters (al-ummatayn al-ukhtayn)".]], and he disliked it. The questioner said to him: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿Except what your right hands possess﴾. Ibn Mas'ud said to him: And your camel is among what your right hand possesses.

This is the well-known position of the majority (al-jumhur) and the four Imams and others, although some of the early scholars (salaf) hesitated on this matter. Imam Malik said, from Ibn Shihab, from Qabisah ibn Dhu'ayb: that a man asked 'Uthman ibn 'Affan about two sisters among those owned by the right hand: may they be combined? 'Uthman said: One verse permits them and one verse forbids them, and I would not do that. So the man left his presence and met a man from the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ and asked him about that. He said: If I had any authority in the matter, and then I found anyone who did that, I would make him an example (nakal). Malik said: Ibn Shihab said: I think he meant 'Ali ibn Abi Talib. He said: And it reached me that al-Zubayr ibn al-'Awwam said the like of that.

Shaykh Abu 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-Barr al-Namari, may Allah have mercy on him, said in his book "al-Istidhkar": Qabisah ibn Dhu'ayb only referred to 'Ali ibn Abi Talib by a kunya (indirect reference) because of his companionship with 'Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan, and they disliked mentioning 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him.

Then Abu 'Umar said, may Allah have mercy on him: Khalaf ibn Ahmad, may Allah have mercy on him, narrated to me by reading to him: that Khalaf ibn Mutarrif narrated to them: Ayyub ibn Sulayman, Sa'id [[In R, A: "Ma'bad".]] ibn Sulayman and Muhammad ibn 'Umar ibn Lubabah narrated to us, saying: Abu Zayd 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ibrahim narrated to us: Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Muqri' [[In A: "al-Maqbari".]] narrated to us, from Musa ibn Ayyub al-Ghafiqi: my paternal uncle Iyas ibn 'Amir narrated to me, saying: I asked 'Ali ibn Abi Talib [may Allah be pleased with him] [[Addition from J, A.]] and said: I have two sisters from among what my right hand possesses; I took one of them as a concubine (surriyyah) and she bore me children, then I desired the other, so what should I do? 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, said: Free the one you were having intercourse with, and then have intercourse with the other. I said: But people say: rather, marry her and then have intercourse with the other. 'Ali said: Do you think that if her husband divorced her or died, she would not return to you? Freeing her is safer for you. Then 'Ali took my hand and said to me: What is forbidden to you of what your right hand possesses is what is forbidden to you in the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, of free women, except the number (or he said: except the four), and what is forbidden to you through nursing is what is forbidden to you through lineage in the Book of Allah.

Then Abu 'Umar said: This hadith is a journey (rihlah) [[In R: "a journey of a man"]]; even if the man had gained nothing from the far east or the far west to Makkah other than it, his journey would not have been in vain [[al-Istidhkar of Ibn 'Abd al-Barr (16/252).]].

I say: It has also been narrated from 'Ali something similar to what preceded from 'Uthman. Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh said:

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ibrahim narrated to us: Muhammad ibn al-'Abbas narrated to us: Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak al-Makhrimi [[In A: "al-Makhzumi".]] narrated to me: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ghazwan narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us, from 'Amr ibn Dinar, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas who said: 'Ali ibn Abi Talib said to me: One verse forbids them and one verse permits them, meaning the two sisters. Ibn 'Abbas said: The kinship of them to me forbids them for me, and the kinship of some of them to others does not forbid them for me, meaning the slave women. The Jahiliyyah used to forbid what you forbid except the wife of the father and the combining of two sisters. When Islam came, Allah sent down: ﴿And do not marry those whom your fathers married of women, except what has already passed﴾ and ﴿and that you combine between two sisters, except what has already passed﴾, meaning: in marriage.

Then Abu 'Umar said: Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal narrated: Muhammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Hisham, from Ibn Sirin, from Ibn Mas'ud who said: What is forbidden from slave women is what is forbidden from free women, except the number. And from Ibn Sirin and al-Sha'bi the like of that.

Abu 'Umar, may Allah have mercy on him, said: The like of the position of 'Uthman has been narrated from a group of the early scholars, among them Ibn 'Abbas, but they were disputed about, and none of the jurists of the cities, of the Hijaz, of Iraq and what lies beyond them to the east, nor of al-Sham, nor of the west, took notice of that, except one who departed from their community by following the literal sense (al-zahir) and rejecting analogy (al-qiyas). Whoever acts on that has abandoned what we have agreed upon. The community of jurists agree that it is not lawful to combine two sisters by ownership of the right hand for intercourse, just as it is not lawful in marriage. The Muslims have agreed that the meaning of His words, Exalted is He: ﴿Forbidden to you are your mothers, your daughters, your sisters [and your paternal aunts and your maternal aunts] ﴾ to the end of the verse, is that marriage and ownership by the right hand regarding all of these are equal; so by reasoning and analogy, combining two sisters, the mothers of women, and stepdaughters must likewise be forbidden. This is also the view of their majority, and they are the authority by which whoever opposes it and departs from it is refuted; and Allah is the One Praised [[al-Istidhkar of Ibn 'Abd al-Barr (16/250-251).]].

* *

His words, Exalted is He: ﴿And the married women among women, except what your right hands possess﴾, meaning: and there is forbidden to you the women of others who are married (al-muhsanat, i.e., those who are married), ﴿except what your right hands possess﴾, meaning: except what you have acquired of them through captivity (sabi), for it is lawful for you to have intercourse with them once you have made them undergo istibra' (a waiting period to establish they are not pregnant). The verse was revealed concerning that.

Imam Ahmad said: 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Sufyan informed us, that is al-Thawri, from 'Uthman al-Batti, from Abu al-Khalil, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri who said: We took captive women from the captives of Awtas, and they had husbands, so we disliked to have intercourse with them while they had husbands, so we asked the Prophet ﷺ, and this verse was revealed: ﴿And the married women among women, except what your right hands possess﴾. [He said:] So we made their private parts lawful to us.

Thus al-Tirmidhi narrated it from Ahmad ibn Mani', from Hushaym; al-Nasa'i narrated it from the hadith of Sufyan al-Thawri and Shu'bah ibn al-Hajjaj, all three from 'Uthman al-Batti; Ibn Jarir narrated it from the hadith of Ash'ath ibn Sawwar from 'Uthman al-Batti; and Muslim narrated it in his Sahih from the hadith of Shu'bah from Qatadah, both from Abu al-Khalil Salih ibn Abi Maryam, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, and so on. Thus 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated it from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, from Abu al-Khalil, from Abu Sa'id, likewise [[Tafsir 'Abd al-Razzaq (1/153); Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3017); Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra no. (11097); Sahih Muslim no. (1456); Tafsir al-Tabari (8/153).]].

It has also been narrated by another route from Abu al-Khalil, from Abu 'Alqamah al-Hashimi, from Abu Sa'id. Imam Ahmad said:

Ibn Abi 'Adi narrated to us, from Sa'id, from Qatadah, from Abu al-Khalil, from Abu 'Alqamah, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri: that the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ captured captive women on the day of Awtas, who had husbands from among the people of polytheism; so some of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ held back and considered it sinful (ta'ththama) to have intercourse with them. He said: So this verse was revealed concerning that: ﴿And the married women among women, except what your right hands possess﴾.

Thus Muslim, Abu Dawud and al-Nasa'i narrated it from the hadith of Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah (Muslim added: and Shu'bah), and al-Tirmidhi narrated it from the hadith of Hammam ibn Yahya; all three from Qatadah, with its chain, similar to it. Al-Tirmidhi said: This is a hasan hadith, and I do not know that anyone mentioned Abu 'Alqamah in this hadith except what Hammam narrated from Qatadah. So he said. But Sa'id and Shu'bah have followed him; and Allah knows best [[Al-Musnad (3/84); Sahih Muslim no. (1456); Sunan Abi Dawud no. (2155); Sunan al-Nasa'i (6/110); Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3016).]].

Al-Tabarani narrated through the route of al-Dahhak from Ibn 'Abbas that it was revealed concerning the captives of Khaybar, and he mentioned a hadith similar to the hadith of Abu Sa'id. A group of the early scholars went to the view that the sale of a slave woman is a divorce for her from her husband, taking by the generality of this verse. Ibn Jarir said: Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, from Shu'bah, from Mughirah, from Ibrahim: that he was asked about a slave woman who is sold while she has a husband? He said: 'Abd Allah (Ibn Mas'ud) used to say: her sale is her divorce, and he recited this verse: ﴿And the married women among women, except what your right hands possess﴾.

Similarly Sufyan narrated it from Mansur, Mughirah and al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, from Ibn Mas'ud who said: her sale is her divorce. This is a broken (munqati') chain.

Sufyan al-Thawri said, from Khalid, from Abu Qilabah, from Ibn Mas'ud who said: if a slave woman is sold while she has a husband, then her master has more right to her private part.

Sa'id narrated it from Qatadah who said: Ubayy ibn Ka'b, Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah and Ibn 'Abbas said: her sale is her divorce.

Ibn Jarir said: Ya'qub narrated to me, [narrated to us] [[Addition from J, R, A.]] Ibn 'Ulayyah, from Khalid, from Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas who said: the divorce of a slave woman is six: her sale is her divorce, her manumission is her divorce, her gifting is her divorce, her release is her divorce, and her husband's divorce is her divorce. [[What is mentioned in all manuscripts is five, not six.]]

'Abd al-Razzaq said: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from Ibn al-Musayyab, his statement: ﴿And the married women among women﴾, he said: they are those who have husbands, whose marriage Allah forbade, except what your right hand possesses, so her sale is her divorce. Ma'mar said: al-Hasan said the like of that.

Similarly Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah narrated from Qatadah, from al-Hasan, regarding His words: ﴿And the married women among women, except what your right hands possess﴾, he said: if she has a husband, then her sale is her divorce.

'Awf said, from al-Hasan: the sale of a slave woman is her divorce, and her sale is her divorce.

This is the view of these early scholars [may Allah have mercy on them]. But the majority, both in earlier and later times, disagreed with them, and held that the sale of a slave woman is not a divorce for her, because the buyer stands in the place of the seller, and the seller had removed this benefit from his ownership and sold her stripped of it. They relied in this on the hadith of Barirah, recorded in the two Sahihs and elsewhere: 'A'ishah, the Mother of the Believers, bought her and immediately freed her, and her marriage to her husband Mughith was not annulled; rather the Prophet ﷺ gave her the choice between annulment and continuation, and she chose annulment, and her story is well known. So if the sale of a slave woman were a divorce for her, as these people said, the Prophet ﷺ would not have given her the choice. Since he gave her the choice, this indicates the continuation of the marriage, and that what is meant by the verse is only the captives (al-masbiyyat); and Allah knows best.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 4, verse 23–24 (part 4 of 4):

It has been said: the meaning of His words, ﴿And the married women among women﴾, is: the chaste ones are forbidden to you until you take possession of their chastity through marriage, with witnesses, dowries, and a guardian (wali), one, two, three, or four. This is related by Ibn Jarir from Abu al-'Aliyah, Tawus and others. 'Umar and 'Ubaydah said: ﴿And the married women among women﴾ refers to all beyond the four are forbidden to you, except what your right hands possess.
* *
As for His words, ﴿The decree of Allah upon you﴾, it means: this prohibition is a decree that Allah has prescribed for you, so hold fast to His Book, do not go beyond its limits, and adhere to His law and what He has made obligatory.
'Ubaydah, 'Ata' and al-Suddi said regarding His words, ﴿The decree of Allah upon you﴾, that it means the four. Ibrahim said: ﴿The decree of Allah upon you﴾ means what He has forbidden to you.
* *
As for His words, ﴿And lawful for you is what is beyond that﴾, meaning: whoever is other than those mentioned among the forbidden women is lawful for you. This was said by 'Ata' and others. 'Ubaydah and al-Suddi said: ﴿And lawful for you is what is beyond that﴾ means what is less than the four. This is far-fetched, and the correct view is the saying of 'Ata' as already mentioned. Qatadah said: ﴿And lawful for you is what is beyond that﴾ means what your right hands possess.
This verse is the one used by those who argue for the permissibility of combining two sisters, and by the one who says: "One verse made them lawful, and another verse made them unlawful."
* *
As for His words, ﴿That you seek with your wealth, chaste, not fornicating﴾, meaning: obtain by your wealth wives, up to four, or concubines, as many as you wish, through the lawful way. Therefore He said: ﴿chaste, not fornicating﴾.
* *
As for His words, ﴿So for whatever you enjoy from them, give them their payment as an obligation﴾, meaning: just as you enjoy them, give them their dowries in return for that, like His words: ﴿And how could you take it while you have gone in unto one another?﴾ [An-Nisa: 21], and like His words: ﴿And give the women their dowries as a gift﴾, and like His words: ﴿And it is not lawful for you to take anything of what you have given them﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 229]. The generality of this verse has been used as evidence for temporary marriage (nikah al-mut'ah). There is no doubt that it was legislated at the beginning of Islam, and then it was abrogated (naskh) afterward. Al-Shafi'i and a group of scholars held that it was permitted, then abrogated, then permitted, then abrogated, twice. Others said more than that, and others said: it was permitted only once, then abrogated, and was not permitted after that.
It has been related from Ibn 'Abbas and a group of the Companions that it was permitted out of necessity, and this is a narration from Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal, may Allah have mercy on them all. Ibn 'Abbas, Ubayy ibn Ka'b, Sa'id ibn Jubayr and al-Suddi used to recite: "So for whatever you enjoy from them until a specified term, give them their payment as an obligation." Mujahid said: it was revealed concerning temporary marriage. But the majority are of a different opinion, and the reliance is on what is established in the two Sahihs from the Commander of the Faithful 'Ali ibn Abi Talib [may Allah be pleased with him] who said: The Prophet ﷺ forbade temporary marriage and the flesh of domestic donkeys on the day of Khaybar. [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4216) and Sahih Muslim no. (1407).] This hadith has established wordings which are in the book "al-Ahkam".
In Sahih Muslim, from al-Rabi' ibn Sabrah ibn Ma'bad al-Juhani, from his father: that he fought alongside the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at the conquest of Makkah, and he said: "O people, I had permitted you to enjoy women, but indeed Allah has forbidden that until the Day of Resurrection. Whoever has any of them, let him release her, and do not take anything of what you have given them." And in a narration of Muslim concerning the Farewell Pilgrimage [Sahih Muslim no. (1406)], and it has wordings whose place is the book "al-Ahkam".
* *
As for His words, ﴿And there is no blame upon you for what you mutually agree upon after the obligation﴾: whoever takes this verse as referring to temporary marriage for a specified term said: there is no blame upon you, once the term has ended, if they mutually agree upon an increase in it and an increase in the payment.
Al-Suddi said: if he wishes, he may satisfy her from after the first obligation—meaning the payment he gave her for his enjoyment of her—before the term ends between them, by saying: "I enjoy you again for such and such," and he increases it, before she has purified her womb on the day the period ends. This is His words: ﴿And there is no blame upon you for what you mutually agree upon after the obligation﴾.
Al-Suddi said: when the period has ended, he has no further claim over her, she is free from him, and she must purify what is in her womb, and there is no inheritance between them, so neither of them inherits from the other.
Those who held the first view explained it like His words: ﴿And give the women their dowries as a gift; but if they give you something of it willingly, then consume it with satisfaction and ease﴾ [An-Nisa: 4], meaning: if you have fixed a dowry for her and she releases you from it, or from some part of it, then there is no blame upon you or upon her in that.
Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, al-Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman related to us, from his father, who said: al-Hadrami claimed that men used to fix the dowry, then perhaps one of them would fall into hardship. So He said: ﴿And there is no blame upon you﴾ O people ﴿for what you mutually agree upon after the obligation﴾, meaning: if she waives some of it for you, it is lawful for you. Ibn Jarir chose this view. And 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah related from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿And there is no blame upon you for what you mutually agree upon after the obligation﴾; the mutual agreement is that he pays her dowry in full and then gives her the choice, whether to remain or to separate.
* *
As for His words, ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever Knowing and Wise﴾: the mention of these two attributes is fitting after the legislation of these prohibitions [the great ones].

He says, [may He be exalted]: "And whoever cannot afford [ṭawl], that is, has no means or ability, to marry the free believing women [al-muḥṣanāt al-mu'mināt], that is, the free women [al-ḥarā'ir]..."

Ibn Wahb said: Abd al-Jabbar informed me, from Rabi'ah, regarding ﴿And whoever among you cannot afford ṭawl to marry the chaste women﴾. Rabi'ah said: "Ṭawl is desire (al-hawa). He marries the slave woman if his desire is for her." Related by Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim.

Then he began to criticize this view and refute it: ﴿So from what your right hands possess of your believing young women﴾, that is: marry the believing slave women whom believing men own. For this reason He said: ﴿of your believing young women﴾. Ibn Abbas and others said: "Let him marry from the slave women of the believers." Al-Suddi and Muqatil ibn Hayyan said the same.

Then he interjected with His words: ﴿And Allah knows best your faith; you are of one another﴾, that is: He is the One who knows the realities of matters and their inner secrets, while for you, O people, there is only the outward appearance of matters.

Then He said: ﴿So marry them with the permission of their people﴾. This indicates that the master is the guardian (wali) of his female slave, so she may not be married except with his permission. Likewise, he is the guardian of his male slave, and his slave may not marry except with his permission, as came in the hadith: "Any slave who marries without the permission of his masters is an adulterer (ʿāhir)," meaning a fornicator (zān). [Related by Abu Dawud in al-Sunan, no. 2078, and al-Tirmidhi in al-Sunan, no. 1111, through Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Aqil, from Jabir ibn Abdullah, may Allah be pleased with him. al-Tirmidhi said: the hadith of Jabir is ḥasan (good).]

If the owner of the slave woman is a woman, she is married off by the one who marries a woman on her behalf with her permission, because of what came in the hadith: "A woman should not marry a woman, nor should a woman marry herself, for the adulteress is the one who marries herself." [Related by Ibn Majah in his Sunan, no. 1882, through Muhammad ibn Marwan, from Hisham ibn Hassan, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him.]

* *

His words: ﴿And give them their wages (ujur) in a fair manner﴾, that is: pay their dowries (muhur) in a fair manner, that is, willingly from yourselves, and do not withhold any of it, belittling them because they are owned slave women.

* *

His words: ﴿chaste﴾, that is: modest, refraining from fornication (zina), not engaging in it. For this reason He said: ﴿not fornicating﴾ (musafiḥāt), and these are the prostitutes who do not refuse anyone who desires them for immorality.

* *

His words: ﴿nor taking lovers﴾. Ibn Abbas said: "The fornicators (al-musafiḥāt) are the openly lewd prostitutes (al-muʿlanāt), meaning those who do not refuse anyone who desires them for immorality." (And those who take lovers) means: friends (akhilla').

It was also related from Abu Hurayrah, Mujahid, al-Sha'bi, al-Dahhak, Ata al-Khurasani, Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, Muqatil ibn Hayyan, and al-Suddi, that they said: "Friends (akhilla')." Al-Hasan al-Basri said: "It means the close friend (al-ṣadīq)." Al-Dahhak also said: ﴿nor taking lovers﴾ refers to a woman who has one single lover (khalil) with whom she has intercourse and acknowledges it. Allah forbade that, meaning [from] marrying her as long as she is in that state.

* *

His words: ﴿So when they become married (uḥṣinna), if they commit a immoral act, then upon them is half the punishment of the free married women﴾. The reciters differed regarding ﴿uḥṣinna﴾. Some of them read it with a ḍamma on the hamza and a kasra on the ṣād, in the passive form (mabni li-ma lam yusamma fa'iluh). It was also read with a fatḥa on the hamza and the ṣād, as an intransitive verb (fi'l lāzim). It was then said that the meaning of the two readings is one. They differed about it according to two opinions:

The first: that the meaning of iḥṣān here is Islam. This was related from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, Ibn Umar, Anas, al-Aswad ibn Yazid, Zirr ibn Hubaysh, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Ata, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, al-Sha'bi, and al-Suddi. al-Zuhri related something similar from Umar ibn al-Khattab, but it is an interrupted chain (munqaṭi'). This is the view which al-Shafi'i stated explicitly, may Allah the Exalted have mercy on him, in the transmission of al-Rabi', he said: "We said that only on the basis of the Sunnah and the consensus (ijma') of most scholars."

Ibn Abi Hatim related a hadith in this regard, raised to the Prophet (marfu'). He said: Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn al-Junayd related to us; Ahmad ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Abdullah al-Dimashqi related to us; my father related to us, from his father, from Abu Hamzah, from Jabir, from a man, from Abu Abd al-Rahman, from Ali, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said regarding ﴿So when they become married﴾: "Their iḥṣān is their Islam and their chastity." It was also said that the meaning here is marriage. He said: Ali said: "Flog them."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: "It is a munkar hadith."

I (Ibn Kathir) say: its chain contains weakness, and among its narrators is one who is not named, and such a report cannot serve as proof. [Mentioned by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur (2/490).]

Al-Qasim and Salim said: its iḥṣān is her Islam and her chastity.

It was also said: the meaning here is marriage. This is the view of Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Ikrimah, Tawus, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Hasan, Qatadah, and others. Abu Ali al-Tabari transmitted it in his book al-Idah from al-Shafi'i, in what Abu al-Hakam ibn Abd al-Hakam related from him. Layth ibn Abi Sulaym related from Mujahid that he said: "The iḥṣān of a slave woman is that a free man marries her, and the iḥṣān of a male slave is that he marries a free woman." Ibn Abi Talhah similarly related from Ibn Abbas. Ibn Jarir related both in his tafsir, and Ibn Abi Hatim mentioned it from al-Sha'bi and al-Nakha'i.

It was also said that the two readings have distinct meanings: whoever reads ﴿uḥṣinna﴾ with a ḍamma on the hamza, his meaning is marriage; whoever reads "aḥṣanna" with a fatḥa, his meaning is Islam. This was chosen by the Imam Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir in his tafsir, and he affirmed and supported it.

The more apparent view, and Allah knows best, is that the meaning of iḥṣān here is marriage, because the context of the verse indicates it, where He, glorified and exalted, says: ﴿And whoever among you cannot afford ṭawl to marry the believing chaste women, then from what your right hands possess of your believing young women﴾. And Allah knows best. The whole context of the noble verse is about believing young women, so it is established that the meaning of His words ﴿So when they become married (uḥṣinna)﴾ is: they marry, as Ibn Abbas explained and those who followed him.

On either of the two views there is a difficulty for the position of the majority (jumhur). That is because they say: if a slave woman commits fornication, she receives fifty lashes, whether she is Muslim or non-Muslim, married or a virgin. Yet the implied meaning (mafhum) of the verse indicates that there is no hadd (prescribed punishment) for a slave woman who commits fornication without being chaste (muḥṣana). They have differed in their answers to this.

As for the majority, they said: there is no doubt that the explicit meaning (manṭuq) takes precedence over the implied meaning. General hadiths have come concerning the imposition of the hadd on slave women, and we give these precedence over the implied meaning of the verse. Among these is what Muslim related in his Sahih from Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, that he gave a sermon and said: "O people, impose the hadd upon your slaves, whether they are chaste or not, for a slave woman of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) committed fornication, and he ordered me to flog her. When I found her to be recently post-natal bleeding, I feared that if I flogged her I would kill her. So I mentioned that to the Prophet (ﷺ), and he said: 'You did well, leave her until she recovers.'" [Sahih Muslim, no. 1705.]

In the narration of Abdullah ibn Ahmad, from someone other than his father: "When she has become elevated from her post-natal bleeding, flog her fifty lashes."

And from Abu Hurayrah who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "If the slave woman of one of you commits fornication and her fornication is evident, let him flog her the hadd and not reproach her. Then if she commits it a second time, let him flog her the hadd and not reproach her. Then if she commits it a third time and her fornication is evident, let him sell her, even for a rope of hair." And in Muslim's version: "If she commits it three times, let him sell her in the fourth." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 3167; Sahih Muslim, no. 1765.]

Malik said, from Yahya ibn Sa'id, from Sulayman ibn Yasar, from Abdullah ibn Ayyash ibn Abi Rabi'ah al-Makhzumi, who said: Umar ibn al-Khattab commanded me, with a group of young men from Quraysh, and we flogged the slave women of the government fifty lashes each for fornication.

The second answer: the answer of those who held that if a slave woman commits fornication without being chaste, there is no hadd upon her, but she is disciplined (yuḍrabu ta'dīban). This is what is related from Abdullah ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him. Tawus, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Abu Ubayd al-Qasim ibn Sallam, and Dawud ibn Ali al-Zahiri in one narration from him also held this view. Their basis is the implied meaning of the verse, which is among the implied meanings of conditional statements (mafahim al-shart), and which is a proof according to most of them; so it takes precedence over the general text in their view. And the hadith of Abu Hurayrah and Zayd ibn Khalid, may Allah be pleased with them both: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked about a slave woman who commits fornication without being chaste. He said: "If she commits fornication, impose the hadd upon her; then if she commits it again, flog her; then sell her, even for a braid (ḍafīr)." Ibn Shihab said: "I do not know whether it was after the third or the fourth." [They both recorded it in the two Sahihs: Sahih al-Bukhari, nos. 2153, 455; Sahih Muslim, no. 1704, from the hadith of Zayd ibn Khalid, may Allah be pleased with him.] In Muslim's version: Ibn Shihab said: "The ḍafīr is the rope."

They said: In this hadith no number is specified as it is specified for the chaste woman, with half the punishment of the free married women. Therefore it is obligatory to reconcile the verse and the hadith in this way, and Allah knows best.

Even more explicit than this is what Sa'id ibn Mansur related from Sufyan, from Mis'ar, from Amr ibn Murrah, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "There is no hadd upon a slave woman until she is made chaste (uḥṣinat) — or until she is married (yu'an: or until she is married) — and when she is made chaste by a husband, upon her is half of what is upon the free married women."

Ibn Khuzaymah related it from Abdullah ibn Imran al-Abidi, from Sufyan, with the same wording, raised to the Prophet. He said: "Its raising (rafʿ) is an error; it is only the statement of Ibn Abbas." Likewise al-Bayhaqi related it from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Imran and said the same as Ibn Khuzaymah. [Al-Bayhaqi, al-Sunan al-Kubra (8/424), ed. al-Kutub al-Ilmiyyah, said: "Its raising is an error, and the mawquf (stopped at a companion) version is more correct." And Sa'id ibn Mansur related it in al-Sunan as mawquf on Ibn Abbas by this route, no. 616.]

They said: The hadith of Ali and Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, are particular cases (qaḍāyā a'yān). As for the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, there are several answers to it:

The first: that it is to be understood as referring to the married slave woman, reconciling it with this hadith.

The second: that the word hadd in his saying "let him flog her the hadd" is an inserted word (lafẓ muqḥam) from one of the narrators, as shown by the third answer, which is:

This is not a direct continuation of the earlier part I was given, but I have translated the passage as it stands.

Narrated by two Companions, and this is from the narration of Abu Hurairah alone. What is narrated from two is more deserving of precedence than what is narrated from one.[[In A: "bi-al-taqdim" (with precedence).]] Also, al-Nasa'i narrated it with a chain that meets the conditions of Muslim, from the hadith of 'Abbad ibn Tamim, from his paternal uncle, who had witnessed Badr, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "If a slave woman commits adultery, flog her. If she commits adultery again, flog her. If she commits adultery again, flog her. If she commits adultery again, sell her, even for a braided rope of hair."

**The fourth answer:** It is not improbable that some narrators used the word *hadd* (prescribed punishment) in the hadith to mean flogging, either because flogging was the punishment in question and they believed it to be a *hadd*, or because they applied the word *hadd* to discipline, just as the word *hadd* was applied to striking a sick person who had committed adultery with a bunch of palm fronds containing one hundred shoots, and to flogging a man who had committed adultery with his wife's slave girl, one hundred lashes, when she gave him permission. This is only a *ta'zir* (discretionary discipline) and *ta'dib* (correction) according to those who hold this view, such as Imam Ahmad and others among the early scholars. The true *hadd* is the flogging of an unmarried person with one hundred lashes, and the stoning of a married person or a sodomite. And Allah knows best.

Ibn Jarir narrated in his Tafsir: Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from 'Amr ibn Murrah, that he heard Sa'id ibn Jubair say: "A slave girl is not to be flogged if she commits adultery so long as she has not married."

This is a sound chain from him, and it is a strange position if he meant that she is not to be flogged at all, not even as a *hadd*. It seems he took this from the implied meaning (*mafhum*) of the verse and had not received the hadith. But if he meant that she is not to be flogged as a *hadd*, and that this does not negate discretionary flogging for correction, then his position is like the statement of Ibn 'Abbas and those who followed him in this. And Allah knows best.

**The third answer:** The verse indicates that a married slave girl receives half the *hadd* of a free woman. As for before marriage, the general statements of the Book and the Sunnah include her in the punishment of one hundred lashes, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿The adulterous woman and the adulterous man, flog each one of them with one hundred lashes﴾ (al-Nur 24:2). And as in the hadith of 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit: "Take from me, take from me, Allah has made a way for them: the unmarried with the unmarried, one hundred lashes and exile for a year; the married with one hundred lashes and stoning with stones." The hadith is in Sahih Muslim and elsewhere.

This view is the well-known position of Dawud ibn 'Ali al-Zahiri, and it is extremely weak. For if Allah had commanded that a married slave girl be punished with half of what is due to a free woman, which is fifty lashes, how could her ruling before marriage be harsher than after marriage? The principle of the Shari'ah is the reverse of what he said. The Lawgiver (peace be upon him) was asked by his Companions about a slave girl who commits adultery while not married, and he said: "Flog her," and did not say "one hundred." If her ruling were as Dawud claimed, it would have been necessary to explain this to them, because they only asked about it due to the lack of explanation of the ruling of one hundred lashes for married slave girls. Otherwise, what is the benefit in their saying "while not married" if there were no difference between the two states before the verse was revealed? But when they knew the ruling of one of the two states, they asked about the ruling of the other, and he explained it to them. As in the two Sahihs, when they asked him about sending blessings upon him, he taught them and then said: "And peace, as you already know." In another wording: when Allah revealed His words: ﴿O you who have believed, send blessings upon him and greet him with peace﴾ (al-Ahzab 33:56), they said: "This is the greeting of peace upon you, we already know it; so how are the blessings upon you?" And he mentioned the hadith. In the same way, this question is alike.[[In A: "same."]]

**The fourth answer, regarding the implied meaning of the verse:** This is the answer of Abu Thawr, for among his positions is one stranger than the view of Dawud in several respects. He says: when she is married, then the penalty for them is half of what is upon married women, which is stoning, and this cannot be halved; therefore, a married slave girl who commits adultery must be stoned. As for before marriage, she must be flogged fifty lashes. He thus erred in understanding the verse and opposed the majority in the ruling. Indeed, Abu 'Abdullah al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, said: "The Muslims have not disagreed that there is no stoning upon a slave in adultery. That is because the verse indicates that upon them is half of the punishment upon married women. The definite article in *al-muhsanat* (the married women) is for a specific reference, and they are the married women mentioned at the beginning of the verse: ﴿And whoever among you cannot afford to marry free believing women﴾ (al-Nisa 4:25). By them is meant only free women, without addressing the marriage of others. And His saying: ﴿half of what is upon the married women of the punishment﴾ indicates that the punishment intended is that which can be halved, which is flogging, not stoning." And Allah knows best.

Then Imam Ahmad narrated a clear text refuting the position of Abu Thawr, from the narration of al-Hasan ibn Sa'd, from his father: that Safiyyah, a young girl, had committed adultery with a man from the Hums,[[The Hums were a group of Quraysh tribes who held strict practices during Hajj.]] and she gave birth to a boy. The adulterer claimed him, and they disputed before 'Uthman ibn 'Affan, who referred them to 'Ali ibn Abi Talib. 'Ali said: "I will judge between them by the judgment of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): 'The child belongs to the bed, and for the adulterer is the stone.'" And he flogged them both fifty lashes each.[[Al-Musnad (1/104).]]

It has also been said: rather, the intended meaning of the implied sense is an alerting from the higher to the lower, that is: slave girls are half of free women in the *hadd* even if they are married, and there is no stoning upon them at all, neither before marriage nor after it. Rather, upon them is flogging in both states, by the Sunnah. This was said by the author of al-Ifsah on al-Shafi'i, in what Ibn 'Abd al-Hakam narrated from him. Al-Bayhaqi also mentioned it in his book al-Sunan wa al-Athar. But this is far from the wording of the verse, for we only derived the halving of the *hadd* from the verse and not from anything else. How, then, can halving be understood from it regarding other matters?

It was also said: rather, what is meant is that when she is married, only the Imam may establish the *hadd* upon her, and her master may not establish the *hadd* upon her in this state. This is an opinion in the school of Imam Ahmad, may Allah have mercy on him. But before marriage, he may do so, and the *hadd* in both cases is half of the free woman's *hadd*. This is also far-fetched, because there is nothing in the wording of the verse that indicates it.

Had it not been for these narrations, we would not know the ruling of the Imam regarding halving, and it would be obligatory to include them in the general wording of the verse regarding completing the *hadd* to one hundred lashes or stoning them, as has been established in the evidence for it. It has already been reported from 'Ali that he said: "O people, establish the *hadd* upon your slaves, whether they are married or not." The general wording of the previous hadiths contains no distinction between a married woman and others, based on the hadith of Abu Hurairah which the majority used as evidence: "If the slave girl of one of you commits adultery and her adultery is established, let him flog her the *hadd* and not reproach her."

**Summary of the verse:** When a slave girl commits adultery, there are several opinions:

First: she is to be flogged fifty lashes, both before and after marriage. Is she to be exiled? On this there are three opinions:
(a) She is exiled for a year. 
(b) She is not exiled at all. This is the view of 'Ali and the jurists of Madinah.
(c) She is exiled for half a year, which is half the exile of a free woman.

This disagreement is in the school of al-Shafi'i. As for Abu Hanifah, his position is that exile is a *ta'zir* (discretionary punishment), not part of the *hadd*, and is rather a matter of the Imam's judgment: if he wishes he may carry it out, and if he wishes he may omit it, both for men and women. According to Malik, exile applies only to men, while for women it does not, because it contradicts their protection. None of the hadiths regarding exile mention men specifically or women specifically, except that the hadith of 'Ubadah and the hadith of Abu Hurairah state that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) ruled regarding the unmarried person who commits adultery with one year of exile and the establishment of the *hadd* upon him, narrated by al-Bukhari. All of this is restricted by the meaning, which is that the purpose of exile is protection, and this is absent in the exile of women. And Allah knows best.

Second: a slave girl who commits adultery is flogged fifty lashes after marriage, and is disciplined before marriage with discretionary correction not limited to a fixed number. Earlier, what Ibn Jarir narrated from Sa'id ibn Jubair was mentioned: that she is not to be flogged before marriage. If he meant to negate that entirely, then this is a position reached by interpretation (*ta'wil*). Otherwise, it is like the second opinion.

The other opinion: she is flogged one hundred lashes before marriage and fifty after it, as is the well-known view of Dawud. This is the weakest of the opinions: that she is flogged fifty lashes before marriage and stoned after it. This is the view of Abu Thawr, and it is also weak. And Allah, glory be to Him and exalted, knows best what is correct.

* *

His saying: ﴿That is for whoever among you fears falling into sin﴾ means: the permission to marry slave girls, under the conditions previously mentioned, applies only to one who fears for himself falling into adultery, and who finds patience against intercourse difficult, and who is distressed by this, so that he is pressed by it. Then he marries the slave girl. But if he refrains from marrying a slave girl and struggles against himself in abstaining from adultery, that is better for him, because if he marries her, his children will be slaves of her master. However, if the husband is an Arab, then his children from her are not slaves, according to an earlier opinion of al-Shafi'i. For this reason He said: ﴿But that you be patient is better for you. And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

From this noble verse, the majority of scholars (jumhur al-'ulama') derived evidence regarding the permissibility of marrying slave women (nikah al-ima'), namely that it is necessary that one lacks the means (tawl) to marry free women and fears falling into sin (al-'anat). This is because marrying them entails the harm of children being born into slavery, and because of the baseness (al-dana'a) involved in turning away from free women to them. [[In manuscript A: "from fornication (al-zina')".]]

Abu Hanifa and his companions differed with the majority regarding the requirement of both conditions. They said: whenever a man is not married to a free woman, it is permissible for him to marry a believing slave woman, and also a women of the People of the Book, whether or not he has the means to marry a free woman, and whether or not he fears sin. Their basis for what they held is the general sense (umum) of the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And the chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture before you﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 5], meaning the chaste ones (al-'afa'if), which encompasses both free women and slave women. This verse is also general, and this verse [[In manuscripts J and A: "specific, and it"]] is likewise clear in indicating what the majority said. And Allah knows best.

Allah, may He be exalted, informs that He wishes to make clear to you, O believers, what He has permitted for you and what He has forbidden for you, of what has been mentioned earlier in this surah and elsewhere; "and to guide you to the ways (sunan) of those before you," meaning their praiseworthy methods and following His laws which He loves and is pleased with; "and to turn to you in repentance," that is, from sin and the things that are forbidden; "and Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise," that is, in His legislation, His decree, His actions and His words.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Allah wishes to turn to you in repentance, but those who follow their desires wish that you should incline a tremendous inclination﴾, meaning: the followers of the devils, from among the Jews, the Christians and the adulterers, wish that you would incline ﴿a tremendous inclination﴾, that is, away from the truth towards falsehood. ﴿Allah wishes to lighten [the burden] for you﴾, that is, in His laws, His commands, His prohibitions and what He decrees for you. For this reason He permitted the marrying of slave-women (imā’) under its conditions, as Mujahid and others said. ﴿Man was created weak﴾, so lightening (al-takhfif) is fitting for him, because of his weakness in himself and the weakness of his resolve and determination.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn Isma'il (al-Ahmasi) related to us: Waki' related to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Tawus, from his father: ﴿Man was created weak﴾, meaning: in the matter of women. Waki' said: his intellect departs from him in their presence.

Musa the Speaker (Kalim, upon him be peace) said to our Prophet, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him, on the night of the Isra' (Night Journey), when he passed by him returning from Sidrat al-Muntaha, "What did your Lord enjoin upon you?" He said: "He commanded me fifty prayers each day and night." Musa said to him: "Return to your Lord and ask Him for lightening, for your Ummah cannot bear that. I have already tested the people before you with something less than that, and they became unable. Your Ummah is weaker in hearing, sight and hearts." So he returned, and He reduced it by ten. Then he came back to Musa, and it kept being so until five remained. [Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: "They are five, and they are fifty; the good deed is multiplied tenfold."] The hadith...

For this reason He permitted the marrying of slave-women (imā’) under its conditions, as Mujahid and others said. ﴿Man was created weak﴾, so lightening (al-takhfif) is fitting for him, because of his weakness in himself and the weakness of his resolve and determination.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn Isma'il (al-Ahmasi) related to us: Waki' related to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Tawus, from his father: ﴿Man was created weak﴾, meaning: in the matter of women. Waki' said: his intellect departs from him in their presence.

Musa the Speaker (Kalim, upon him be peace) said to our Prophet, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him, on the night of the Isra' (Night Journey), when he passed by him returning from Sidrat al-Muntaha, "What did your Lord enjoin upon you?" He said: "He commanded me fifty prayers each day and night." Musa said to him: "Return to your Lord and ask Him for lightening, for your Ummah cannot bear that. I have already tested the people before you with something less than that, and they became unable. Your Ummah is weaker in hearing, sight and hearts." So he returned, and He reduced it by ten. Then he came back to Musa, and it kept being so until five remained. [Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: "They are five, and they are fifty; the good deed is multiplied tenfold."] The hadith...

Allah, may He be exalted, informs that He wishes to make clear to you, O believers, what He has permitted for you and what He has forbidden for you, of what has been mentioned earlier in this surah and elsewhere; "and to guide you to the ways (sunan) of those before you," meaning their praiseworthy methods and following His laws which He loves and is pleased with; "and to turn to you in repentance," that is, from sin and the things that are forbidden; "and Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise," that is, in His legislation, His decree, His actions and His words.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Allah wishes to turn to you in repentance, but those who follow their desires wish that you should incline a tremendous inclination﴾, meaning: the followers of the devils, from among the Jews, the Christians and the adulterers, wish that you would incline ﴿a tremendous inclination﴾, that is, away from the truth towards falsehood. ﴿Allah wishes to lighten [the burden] for you﴾, that is, in His laws, His commands, His prohibitions and what He decrees for you. For this reason He permitted the marrying of slave-women (imā’) under its conditions, as Mujahid and others said. ﴿Man was created weak﴾, so lightening (al-takhfif) is fitting for him, because of his weakness in himself and the weakness of his resolve and determination.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn Isma'il (al-Ahmasi) related to us: Waki' related to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Tawus, from his father: ﴿Man was created weak﴾, meaning: in the matter of women. Waki' said: his intellect departs from him in their presence.

Musa the Speaker (Kalim, upon him be peace) said to our Prophet, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him, on the night of the Isra' (Night Journey), when he passed by him returning from Sidrat al-Muntaha, "What did your Lord enjoin upon you?" He said: "He commanded me fifty prayers each day and night." Musa said to him: "Return to your Lord and ask Him for lightening, for your Ummah cannot bear that. I have already tested the people before you with something less than that, and they became unable. Your Ummah is weaker in hearing, sight and hearts." So he returned, and He reduced it by ten. Then he came back to Musa, and it kept being so until five remained. [Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: "They are five, and they are fifty; the good deed is multiplied tenfold."] The hadith...

Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim, on Surah 4, verses 29–31 (part 1 of 6):

Allah, may He be blessed and exalted, forbade His believing servants from consuming one another's wealth unjustly (bil-batil), that is, through kinds of gain that are not legally permitted, such as the various forms of riba (usury) and gambling, and whatever follows their course among all the other kinds of stratagems. This applies even when such stratagems appear to conform to the outward ruling of the Sharia, if Allah knows that the one practising them intends only a trick to obtain riba. Ibn Jarir said:

Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to me: 'Abd al-Wahhab narrated to us: Dawud narrated to us, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning a man who buys a garment from another man and says: "If I like it, I will take it; otherwise I will return it and return a dirham with it." He said: "This is what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, meant by: ﴿And do not consume your wealth among yourselves unjustly﴾."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: 'Ali ibn Harb al-Mawsili narrated to us: Ibn Fudayl narrated to us, from Dawud al-Awdi, from 'Amir, from 'Alqamah, from 'Abdullah [ ﴿O you who have believed, do not consume your wealth among yourselves unjustly﴾ ] [[Addition from J, R, A.]] He said: "It is a firm (muhkam) statement; it has not been abrogated (nusikha) and will not be abrogated until the Day of Resurrection."

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated, from Ibn 'Abbas: When Allah revealed ﴿O you who have believed, do not consume your wealth among yourselves unjustly﴾, the Muslims said: "Allah has forbidden us to consume our wealth among ourselves unjustly, and food is the best of wealth. So it is not lawful for any of us to eat at someone else's home. How then [can we eat] with people?!" Then Allah revealed afterwards: ﴿There is no blame upon the blind﴾ [An-Nur: 61], and the verse. [Likewise Qatadah ibn Di'amah said.] [[Addition from A.]]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿except that it be trade by mutual consent among you﴾ [[In A: "among you" (bbaynakum).]] it was read as tijaratun with a nominative (raf') and with an accusative (nasb). It is an exception of the disconnected type (istithna' munqati'), as if He said: Do not engage in the prohibited means of acquiring wealth, but permitted trade that is by mutual consent of the seller and the buyer, then do it, and use it to obtain wealth. Just as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿and do not kill the soul which Allah has forbidden, except by right﴾ [Al-An'am: 151], and as in His saying ﴿They will not taste death therein, except the first death﴾ [Ad-Dukhan: 56].

From this noble verse, al-Shafi'i (may Allah have mercy on him) argued that a sale is not valid except with acceptance (qabul), because it explicitly indicates mutual consent, unlike mu'atah (a sale concluded by exchange of goods and money without words), which may not indicate consent, and it must. Malik, Abu Hanifah, Ahmad and their companions disagreed with the majority on this point. They held that statements indicate mutual consent, and in some situations actions also indicate it with certainty. So they validated the mu'atah sale absolutely. Some of them said it is valid for trivial items and for whatever people regard as a sale, and this is a precautionary view of the scholars of the school who investigate its principles. And Allah knows best.

Mujahid said: ﴿except that it be trade by mutual consent among you﴾ means a sale [[In A: "sale" (bay').]] or a gift one person gives another. Ibn Jarir narrated it, [then] [[Addition from J, A.]] he said:

Ibn Wakic narrated to us: my father narrated to us, from al-Qasim, from Sulayman al-Ju'fi, from his father, from Maymun ibn Mihran who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Sale is by mutual consent, and the option (khiyar) is after the transaction, and it is not lawful for a Muslim to deceive a Muslim." This is a mursal (a hadith whose chain omits the Companion) narration. [Tafsir al-Tabari (8/221).]

Part of complete consent is the establishment of khiyar al-majlis (the option of the session, the right of the parties to cancel while still in the meeting), as established in the Two Sahihs (al-Bukhari and Muslim): that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The two parties to a sale have the option as long as they have not separated." In the wording of al-Bukhari: "When two men engage in a sale, each of them has the option as long as they have not separated." [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (2109) and Sahih Muslim no. (1531).]

Al-Shafi'i, Ahmad ibn Hanbal [[Addition from A.]] and their companions, along with the majority of the early and later scholars (al-salaf wa'l-khalaf), acted according to the meaning of this hadith. From this is the legitimacy of khiyar al-shart (the option stipulated in the contract) after the contract for up to three days, as is agreed among the scholars, and beyond three days according to what is needed to determine the value of the sale. Even up to a year in a village or similar, as is well known from Malik, may Allah have mercy on him. Some validated the mu'atah sale absolutely, and this is a view within the school of al-Shafi'i. Others said that the mu'atah sale is valid for trivial items that people regard as a sale, and this is the choice of a group of the companions of the school. [[In R: "So they validated."]]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿and do not kill yourselves﴾, that is: by committing the prohibitions of Allah and engaging in His disobediences, and by consuming your wealth among yourselves unjustly. ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever Merciful to you﴾, that is: in what He commanded you and what He forbade you.

Imam Ahmad said: Hasan [[In J, A: "Husayn".]] ibn Musa narrated to us: Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to us: Yazid ibn Abi Habib narrated to us, from 'Imran ibn Abi Anas, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr, from 'Amr ibn al-'As, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: When the Prophet (ﷺ) sent him in the year of Dhat al-Salasil, he said: "I had a wet dream on a night that was extremely cold, and I feared that if I bathed I would perish. So I performed tayammum, then led my companions in the dawn prayer." He said: "When I came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), I mentioned that to him, and he said: 'O 'Amr, you led your companions in prayer while you were junub (in a state of major impurity)!' I said: 'Yes, O Messenger of Allah, I had a wet dream on a night that was extremely cold, and I feared that if I bathed [[In A: "that I bathe."]] I would perish. So I remembered the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿And do not kill yourselves; indeed Allah is ever Merciful to you﴾, so I performed tayammum and prayed.'" Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) laughed and said nothing.

Abu Dawud related it in the same way from the hadith of Yahya ibn Ayyub, from Yazid ibn Abi Habib, with the same chain. He also related it from Muhammad ibn Abi Salamah, from Ibn Wahb, from Ibn Lahi'ah and 'Umar ibn al-Harith, both from Yazid ibn Abi Habib, from 'Imran ibn Abi Anas, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr al-Misri, from Abu Qays, client of 'Amr ibn al-'As, from him, and he mentioned something similar. This, and Allah knows best, is closer to the correct version. [Musnad (4/203) and Sunan Abi Dawud no. (334).]

Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh said: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad ibn Hamid al-Balkhi narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Salih ibn Sahl al-Balkhi narrated to us: 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Umar al-Qawariri narrated to us: Yusuf ibn Khalid narrated to us: Ziyad ibn Sa'd narrated to us, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas: that 'Amr ibn al-'As led the people in prayer while he was junub. When they came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), they mentioned that to him, and he summoned him and asked him about it. He said: "O Messenger of Allah, I feared that the cold would kill me, and Allah, the Exalted, has said: ﴿and do not kill yourselves [indeed Allah is ever Merciful to you]﴾." He said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) remained silent about it." [[Al-Tabarani (11/234) narrated it through 'Ubayd Allah al-Qawariri, and al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (1/264): "In it is Yusuf ibn Khalid al-Samti, who is a liar."]]

Then Ibn Mardawayh, at this noble verse, cited a hadith from al-A'mash, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever kills himself with an iron implement, his iron will be in his hand, with which he will stab his belly on the Day of Resurrection in the Fire of Hell, abiding therein forever and ever. Whoever kills himself with poison, his poison will be in his hand, which he will sip in the Fire of Hell, abiding therein forever and ever. Whoever throws himself from a mountain and kills himself will be falling in the Fire of Hell, abiding therein forever and ever."

This hadith is established in the Two Sahihs [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (5778) and Sahih Muslim no. (109)]. Likewise Abu al-Zinad narrated it from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), with similar wording. And from Abu Qilabah, from Thabit ibn al-Dahhak, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever kills himself with something, he will be punished with it on the Day of Resurrection." The group (al-Jama'ah) recorded it in their books through the route of Abu Qilabah [Sahih al-Bukhari nos. (6047, 6105), Sahih Muslim no. (110), Sunan Abi Dawud no. (3257), Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (1543), Sunan al-Nasa'i (7/5,6), Sunan Ibn Majah no. (2098); al-Tirmidhi does not have the phrase "whoever kills himself with something," which is the point of citation here]. In the Two Sahihs, from the hadith of al-Hasan, from Jundub ibn 'Abd Allah al-Bajali, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "There was a man among those before you who had a wound, so he took a knife and cut his hand with it, and the blood did not stop until he died. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: 'My servant hastened to take his own life, so I have forbidden Paradise to him.'" [Sahih al-Bukhari nos. (1364, 3463) and Sahih Muslim no. (113).]

For this reason Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And whoever does that in transgression and wrongdoing, We will drive him into a Fire, and that is ever easy for Allah﴾, that is: whoever engages in what Allah has forbidden him, transgressing and wronging himself in doing so, knowing its prohibition and audaciously violating it. [[Addition from J, R, A.]] This is a severe threat and a firm warning, so let every wise, intelligent person who gives ear while being attentive beware of it.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿If you avoid the major sins which you are forbidden, We will remove from you your misdeeds and admit you to a noble entrance [[Addition from J, R, A.]]﴾. That is: if you avoid the grave sins that you have been forbidden, We will expiate your minor sins for you and admit you to Paradise. For this reason He said: ﴿and admit you to a noble entrance﴾.

Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said: Mu'ammal ibn Hisham narrated to us: Isma'il ibn Ibrahim narrated to us: Khalid [[In R: "al-Khald"; in A: "al-Khalid".]] ibn Ayyub narrated to us, from Mu'awiyah ibn Qurrah, from Anas, [raising it to the Prophet] [[Addition from J, R, A.]]: "[What has reached us from our Lord, Mighty and Majestic, is] that He does not bring us out, of every family and property, [except] that He forgives us what is below the major sins. Allah [the Exalted] [[Addition from J, R, A.]] says: ﴿If you avoid the major sins which you are forbidden, We will remove from you your misdeeds [and admit you to a noble entrance]﴾." [[Al-Bazzar in Musnad no. (2200), Kashf al-Astar; al-Haythami said: "In it is al-Jald ibn Ayyub, who is weak."]]

Many hadiths related to this noble verse have been transmitted, so let us mention what is easily accessible from them:

Imam Ahmad said: Husharm narrated to us, from Mughirah, from Abu Ma'shar, from Ibrahim, from Qarth' al-Dabbi, from Salman al-Farisi, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said to me: "Do you know what the Day of Jumu'ah is?" I said: "It is the day on which Allah gathered your father." He said: "But do you know what the Day of Jumu'ah is? A man purifies himself and performs his purification well, then comes to Jumu'ah and listens attentively until the imam finishes his prayer, and this will be an expiation for him for what is between it and the next Jumu'ah, so long as the major sins (al-maqtalah) are avoided." Al-Bukhari also narrated something similar from Salman through another route. [Musnad (5/439), and al-Bukhari no. (910) through Sa'id al-Maqburi from his father, from Ibn Wadi'ah, from Salman al-Farisi, with similar wording.]

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 4, verse 29–31 (part 2 of 6):

Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir said: Al-Muthanna [ibn Ibrahim] [[added from manuscripts R and A.]] narrated to me: Abu Salih narrated to us: al-Layth narrated to us: Khalid narrated to me, from Sa'id ibn Abi Hilal, from Nu'aym al-Mujmir, who said: Suhayb, the freedman of al-'Utwari, informed me that he heard from Abu Hurayrah and Abu Sa'id, both saying: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) addressed us one day and said: "By He in whose hand is my soul" three times. Then he lowered his head, and every man among us lowered his head weeping, not knowing what he had sworn about. Then he raised his head, and there was joy in his face, and it was more beloved to us than red camels. He (ﷺ) said: "There is no servant who prays the five prayers, fasts Ramadan, pays zakat, and avoids the seven major sins, except that the gates of Paradise are opened for him, and it is said to him: Enter in peace." [[in A: "al-Bushra" (the good news).]]

This was also related by al-Nasa'i and al-Hakim in his Mustadrak, through the narration of al-Layth ibn Sa'd. Al-Hakim also related it, and Ibn Hibban in his Sahih, through the narration of Abdullah ibn Wahb, from 'Amr ibn al-Harith, from Sa'id ibn Abi Hilal, with the same chain. Then al-Hakim said: "Sahih according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim), though they did not record it." [[Tafsir al-Tabari (8/238), Sunan al-Nasa'i (5/8), and al-Mustadrak (1/200).]]

The explanation of these seven:
This is based on what is established in the two Sahihs from the hadith of Sulayman ibn Bilal, from Thawr ibn Zayd, from Salim Abi al-Ghayth, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Avoid the seven destructive things." It was asked: "O Messenger of Allah, what are they?" He said: "Associating partners with Allah, killing a soul which Allah has forbidden except by right, sorcery, consuming riba, consuming the property of the orphan, fleeing on the day of battle, and slandering chaste, believing, unaware women." [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (2766) and Sahih Muslim no. (89).]]

Another route from him: Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us: Fahd ibn 'Awf narrated to us: Abu 'Awanah narrated to us, from 'Amr ibn Abi Salamah, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The major sins are seven: the first of them is associating partners with Allah, then killing a soul without right, consuming riba, consuming the property of the orphan until he grows up, fleeing from the battle line, slandering (chaste women), and reverting to the Bedouin life after the emigration (hijrah)." [[Musnad al-Bazzar no. (109), Kashf al-Astar. Al-Haythami said in Majma' al-Zawa'id (1/103): "In it is 'Umar ibn Abi Salamah, whom Shu'bah and others declared weak, but Abu Hatim, Ibn Hibban and others declared trustworthy."]]

The explicit statement that these seven are major sins does not negate what is beyond them, except according to those who hold the principle of mafhum al-laqab (the implication drawn from naming a specific item, i.e., an argument from the mere mention of a term), which is weak in the absence of an indicator. This is especially so when there is evidence from an explicit text that the implication does not apply. As we will cite from the hadiths which mention major sins other than these seven, among them is what al-Hakim related in his Mustadrak, where he said:

Ahmad ibn Kamil al-Qadi narrated to us, by dictation: Abu Qilabah 'Abd al-Malik ibn Muhammad narrated to us: Mu'adh ibn Hani' narrated to us: Harb ibn Shaddad narrated to us: Yahya ibn Abi Kathir narrated to us, from Abd al-Hamid ibn Sinan, from Ubayd ibn 'Umayr, from his father, meaning 'Umayr ibn Qatadah, may Allah be pleased with him, that he related to him, and he had companionship (with the Prophet): that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said during the Farewell Pilgrimage: "Verily, the friends of Allah are those who pray, who maintain the five prayers which were prescribed for them, who fast Ramadan seeking its reward, who believe it is their duty, who give the zakat of their wealth seeking its reward, and who avoid the major sins which Allah has forbidden." Then a man asked him: "O Messenger of Allah, what are the major sins?" He said: "Nine: associating partners with Allah, killing a believing soul without right, fleeing on the day of battle, consuming the property of the orphan, consuming riba, slandering a chaste woman, disobeying the two believing parents, and violating the Sacred House, your qibla, whether they are alive or dead." Then he said: "No man dies who does not commit these major sins, while maintaining the prayer and paying zakat, except that he will be with the Prophet (ﷺ) in a house whose doors are of gold." [[in J, R, A: "its doors are its mansions (masani')"]]

Thus al-Hakim related it at length. Abu Dawud and al-Tirmidhi [[in J: "and al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i"]] related it in summary through the narration of Mu'adh ibn Hani', with the same chain. Likewise Ibn Abi Hatim related it from his narration in full. Then al-Hakim said: "All its narrators are those whose narrations are used in the two Sahihs, except 'Abd al-Hamid ibn Sinan." [[Al-Mustadrak (1/59), Sunan Abi Dawud no. (2875), and I did not find it in al-Tirmidhi. Al-Bayhaqi related it in al-Sunan al-Kubra from al-Hakim's route (3/408) and said: "The word 'sorcery' fell out of my book or out of my Shaykh's book (meaning al-Hakim)."
And 'Abd al-Hamid ibn Sinan. Al-Dhahabi said: "He is counted among the Tabi'un, not well known. Some declared him trustworthy. Al-Bukhari said: 'In his narration from Ubayd there is consideration.' I say: His narration from Ubayd from his father, 'The major sins are nine...' the hadith..."]]

I say: He is a Hijazi who is known only through this hadith. Ibn Hibban mentioned him in the book al-Thiqat (the Trustworthy), while al-Bukhari said: "In his hadith there is consideration."

Ibn Jarir also related it from Sulayman ibn Thabit al-Jahdari, from Salm ibn Salam, from Ayyub ibn 'Utbah, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from Ubayd ibn 'Umayr, from his father, and mentioned it. But he did not mention 'Abd al-Hamid ibn Sinan in the chain. And Allah knows best. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (8/241).]]

Another hadith with the same meaning: Ibn Mardawayh said: 'Abdullah ibn Ja'far narrated to us: Ahmad ibn Yunus narrated to us: Yahya ibn 'Abd al-Hamid narrated to us: 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Muslim ibn al-Walid narrated to us, from al-Muttalib, from 'Abdullah ibn Hantab, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) ascended the pulpit and said: "I do not swear, I do not swear." Then he descended and said: "Rejoice, rejoice! Whoever prays the five prayers and avoids the seven major sins, will be called from the gates of Paradise: Enter." 'Abd al-'Aziz said: "I do not know it except that he said: 'in peace.'" Al-Muttalib said: I heard someone ask 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr: "Did you hear the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) mention them?" He said: "Yes: disobedience to parents, associating partners with Allah, killing the soul, slandering chaste women, consuming the property of the orphan, fleeing from the battle line, and consuming riba." [[Al-Tabarani also related it in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir no. (3) "al-Qit'ah al-Mafqudah" through the route of 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Muhammad, from Muslim ibn al-Walid, from al-Muttalib with the same wording. In its chain is Muslim ibn al-Walid, whom al-Bukhari mentioned in al-Tarikh al-Kabir (8/153) and Ibn Abi Hatim in al-Jarh wa al-Ta'dil (8/197), and neither of them mentioned any criticism or praise of him.]]

Another hadith with a similar meaning: Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir said in his Tafsir: Ya'qub narrated to us: Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us: Zayd ibn Mikhraq informed us, from Taysalah ibn Mayyas, who said: I was with the Najdat (a Kharijite sect), and I committed sins which I considered to be among the major sins. I met Ibn 'Umar and said to him: "I have committed sins which I consider to be among the major sins." He said: "What are they?" I said: "I committed such and such." He said: "That is not among the major sins." I said: "And I committed such and such." He said: "That is not among the major sins," and he mentioned something Taysalah did not name. Then he said: "They are nine, and I will count them for you: associating partners with Allah, killing a soul without right, fleeing from the battle line, slandering a chaste woman, consuming riba, consuming the property of the orphan unjustly, violating the Sacred Mosque, one who practices sorcery, and the weeping of the parents from disobedience." Ziyad said: Taysalah said when he saw Ibn 'Umar: "He trembled." He said: "Do you fear the Fire that you would enter it?" I said: "Yes." He said: "And do you love to enter Paradise?" I said: "Yes." He said: "Are your parents alive?" I said: "My mother is with me." He said: "By Allah, if you speak gently to her and feed her, you will certainly enter Paradise so long as you avoid the sins that necessitate Hell." [[Tafsir al-Tabari (8/239). Al-Bukhari related it in al-Adab al-Mufrad no. (8) through the route of Ziyad ibn Mikhraq with the same wording.]]

Another route: Ibn Jarir said: Sulayman ibn Thabit al-Jahdari al-Wasiti narrated to us: Salm ibn Salam narrated to us: Ayyub ibn 'Utbah narrated to us, from Taysalah ibn 'Ali al-Nahdi, who said: I came to Ibn 'Umar while he was in the shade of an arak tree on the day of 'Arafah, pouring water over his head and face. I said: "Inform me about the major sins." He said: "They are nine." I said: "What are they?" He said: "Associating partners with Allah, and slandering a chaste woman." He said: I said: "Before killing?" He said: "Yes, and (it is) by force." And killing a believing soul, fleeing from the battle line, sorcery, consuming riba, consuming the property of the orphan, disobedience to the two believing parents, and violating the Sacred House, your qibla, whether they are alive or dead. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (8/240).]]

This is how he related it through these two routes, as a mawquf (a statement ending with a Companion). It was also related by 'Ali ibn al-Ja'd, from Ayyub ibn 'Utbah, from Taysalah ibn 'Ali [al-Nahdi] [[added from manuscript A.]], who said: I came to Ibn 'Umar on the evening of 'Arafah, while he was under the shade of an arak tree, pouring water over his head. I asked him about the major sins, and he said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'They are seven.'" I said: "And what are they?" He said: "Associating partners with Allah, slandering a chaste woman." I said: "Before the blood (killing)?" He said: "Yes, and by force." "And killing a believing soul, fleeing from the battle line, sorcery, consuming riba, consuming the property of the orphan, disobedience to the parents, and violating the Sacred House, your qibla, whether alive or dead."

Similarly it was related by al-Hasan ibn Musa al-Ashyab, from Ayyub ibn 'Utbah al-Yamani, and there is weakness in him. [[Al-Baghawi related it in al-Ja'diyyat. Al-Kharaiti related it in Masawi' al-Akhlaq no. (247) through the route of Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Marwazi, from Ayyub ibn 'Utbah, with similar wording, and Ayyub ibn 'Utbah is weak. 'Ikrimah ibn 'Ammar related it from Taysalah ibn 'Ali: that Ibn 'Umar used to stop at the arak trees on the day of 'Arafah. Abu Dawud related it in al-Masa'il (118).]] And Allah knows best.

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Zakariyya ibn 'Adi narrated to us: Baqiyyah narrated to us, from Bahir ibn Sa'd, from Khalid ibn Ma'dan, that Abu Ruhm al-Sama'i narrated to them, from Abu Ayyub, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever worships Allah without associating anything with Him, establishes the prayer, gives zakat, fasts Ramadan, and avoids the major sins, for him is Paradise, or he will enter Paradise." A man asked him: "What are the major sins?" He said: "Associating partners with Allah, killing a Muslim soul, and fleeing on the day of battle."

Ahmad also related it, and al-Nasa'i, through other routes, from Baqiyyah. [[Al-Musnad (5/413) and Sunan al-Nasa'i (7/88).]]

Another hadith: The hafiz Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh related in his Tafsir, through the route of Sulayman ibn Dawud al-Yamani, who is weak, from al-Zuhri, from Abu Bakr ibn Muhammad ibn 'Amr ibn Hazm, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) wrote a letter to the people of Yemen containing the obligatory duties, the Sunan and the blood-money, and sent it with 'Amr ibn Hazm. He said: In the letter was: "Verily, the greatest of the major sins before Allah on the Day of Resurrection are: associating partners with Allah, killing a believing soul without right, fleeing in the way of Allah on the day of battle, disobedience to parents, slandering a chaste woman, learning sorcery, consuming riba, and consuming the property of the orphan." [[Al-Hakim related it in al-Mustadrak (1/395) through the route of Yahya ibn Hamzah from Sulayman ibn Dawud with the same wording. Al-Hakim said: "This is a great hadith explaining this subject. Sulayman ibn Dawud al-Khawlani is known as al-Zuhri, although Yahya ibn Ma'in criticized him, others declared him reliable." He then mentioned the statement of Abu Hatim and Abu Zur'ah: "Sulayman ibn Dawud al-Khawlani is among those with no harm in them, according to us."]]

Another hadith, which mentions false testimony.
