Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far related to us, Shu'bah related to us, 'Ubaydullah ibn Abi Bakr related to me, saying: I heard Anas ibn Malik say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) mentioned the major sins, or was asked about the major sins, and said: "Associating partners with Allah, killing a soul, and disobedience to one's parents." He then said: "Shall I not inform you of the greatest of the major sins?" He said: "False speech, or false testimony." Shu'bah said: "My strong assumption is that he said 'false testimony.'"[[In J, R, A: "Abdullah," and in R: "Muhammad," which is an error; the correct reading is 'Ubaydullah. See Musnad al-Imam Ahmad 3/131.]] [[The Musnad (3/131).]]

Al-Bukhari and Muslim both recorded it through the narration of Shu'bah.[[Sahih al-Bukhari no. 5977 and Sahih Muslim no. 88.]] Ibn Mardawayh narrated it through two other chains from Anas, which are gharib (rare), with a similar wording.[[In R: "nahwuhu."]]

Another hadith: The two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim) recorded it through the narration of 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakrah, from his father, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Shall I not inform you of the greatest of the major sins?" We said: "Yes, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "Associating partners with Allah, and disobedience to one's parents." He had been reclining, then he sat up and said: "Beware, and false testimony. Beware, and false speech." He kept repeating it until we said: "I wish he would be silent."[[Sahih al-Bukhari no. 5976 and Sahih Muslim no. 87.]]

Another hadith, which mentions the killing of a child. It is established in the two Sahihs, from 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, which sin is the greatest?" In another narration: "the greatest." He said: "That you set up a rival to Allah while He created you." I said: "Then which?" He said: "That you kill your child out of fear that it will eat with you." I said: "Then which?" He said: "That you commit adultery with your neighbour's wife." Then he recited: ﴿And those who do not invoke with Allah another god, nor kill the soul which Allah has forbidden except by right, nor commit unlawful sexual intercourse, and whoever does that will meet a penalty﴾ [up to] ﴿except one who repents﴾ [al-Furqan: 68].[[Sahih al-Bukhari no. 4477 and Sahih Muslim no. 68.]]

Another hadith, which mentions the drinking of wine. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Yunus ibn 'Abd al-A'la informed us, Ibn Wahb informed us, Abu Sakhr related to me: that a man told him, from 'Amrah ibn Hazm, that he heard 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As, while he was in al-Hijr in Makkah, being asked about wine. He said: "By Allah, it is a great matter with Allah that an old man like me should lie about the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in this place." He then went and asked him, then came back and said: "I asked him about wine, and he said: 'It is the greatest of the major sins and the mother of all indecencies. Whoever drinks wine abandons the prayer, has intercourse with his mother, his maternal aunt and his paternal aunt.'"[[Al-Tabarani narrated it through another chain, as in al-Majma' (5/68), and al-Haythami said: "'Attab, whom I do not know; and Ibn Lahi'ah's hadith is good but has weakness in it."]] It is gharib from this route.

Another route: The Hafiz Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh narrated it through the hadith of 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Muhammad al-Darawardi, from Dawud ibn Salih, from Salim ibn 'Abdullah, from his father: that Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him, and 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, and some companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), may Allah be pleased with them all, were sitting after the death of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and they mentioned the greatest of the major sins, but they did not have anything they could rely upon. So they sent me to 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As to ask him about that. He informed me that the greatest of the major sins is drinking wine. I came to them and informed them, and they denied it, so they rushed to him until they reached him at his house. He informed them that they had discussed in the presence of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that a king from the Children of Israel seized a man and gave him the choice between drinking wine, killing a soul, committing adultery, eating the flesh of a pig, or being killed. He chose drinking wine. When he drank it, he did not refrain from anything that they wanted from him. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to us in reply: "No one drinks wine without his prayer not being accepted for forty nights. If anyone dies with something of it in his bladder, Allah forbids Paradise to him. If he dies within forty nights, he dies the death of the Jahiliyyah (Age of Ignorance)."

This hadith is extremely gharib from this route. Dawud ibn Salih is al-Tammar al-Madani, client of the Ansar. Imam Ahmad said: "I see no harm in him." Ibn Hibban mentioned him in al-Thiqat (the Reliable Narrators), and I have not seen anyone criticise him.[[Al-Hakim narrated it in al-Mustadrak (4/147), and al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Awsat no. 138 (Majma' al-Bahrayn), both through the route of Sa'id ibn Abi Maryam from al-Darawardi.]]

Another hadith, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr, which mentions the oath of ghamus (perjury). Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far related to us, Shu'bah related to us, from Firas, from al-Sha'bi, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr, from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he said: "The greatest of the major sins are associating partners with Allah, disobedience to one's parents, or killing a soul (Shu'bah was unsure), and the ghamus oath." Al-Bukhari, al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i narrated it through the hadith of Shu'bah; al-Bukhari added Shaybān, both from Firas, with it.[[Al-Musnad (2/201), Sahih al-Bukhari no. 6675, Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 3021, and Sunan al-Nasa'i (8/63).]]

Another hadith, concerning the ghamus oath. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father related to us, Abu Salih the scribe of al-Layth related to us, al-Layth ibn Sa'd related to us, Hisham ibn Sa'd related to us, from Muhammad ibn Yazid ibn Muhajir ibn Qunfudh al-Taymi, from Abu Umamah al-Ansari, from 'Abdullah ibn Unays al-Juhani, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "The greatest of the major sins are associating partners with Allah, disobedience to one's parents, and the ghamus oath. No one swears by Allah a sabr oath (one forced upon a person's property) and in it inserts even the wing of a mosquito, except that it becomes a stain in his heart until the Day of Resurrection." Imam Ahmad narrated it in his Musnad in the same way, and 'Abd ibn Humayd in his Tafsir; both through Yunus ibn Muhammad al-Mu'addib, from al-Layth ibn Sa'd, with it. Al-Tirmidhi also narrated it in his Tafsir from 'Abd ibn Humayd, with it. Then he said: "This is a hasan gharib hadith. Abu Umamah al-Ansari is Ibn Tha'labah, and his name is not known." He narrated hadiths from the Prophet (ﷺ).[[Sunan al-Tirmidhi (302).]]

Our Shaykh, the Hafiz Abu al-Hajjaj al-Mizzi, said: It was also narrated by 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ishaq al-Madani, from Muhammad ibn Zayd, from 'Abdullah ibn Abi Umamah, from his father, from 'Abdullah ibn Unays. He added 'Abdullah ibn Abi Umamah.

I say: This is how it occurs in the Tafsir of Ibn Mardawayh and the Sahih of Ibn Hibban, through the route of 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ishaq,[[In R: "Isma'il."]] as our Shaykh mentioned. May Allah lengthen his life.[[Tuhfat al-Ashraf (4/275) no. 5147, and Sahih Ibn Hibban no. 1191 (Mawarid).]]

Another hadith, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr, concerning causing someone to revile one's parents. Ibn Abi Hatim said: 'Amr ibn 'Abdullah al-Awdi related to us, Waki' related to us, from Mis'ar and Sufyan, from Sa'd ibn Ibrahim, from Humayd ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr. Sufyan raised it to the Prophet (ﷺ), while Mis'ar stopped it at 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr. He said: "Among the major sins is that a man should revile his parents." They said: "How can a man revile his parents?" He said: "A man curses the father of another man, and he curses his father; and he curses his mother, and he curses his mother."[[Ahmad narrated it in his Musnad (2/164) through the route of Waki'.]]

It was also narrated by al-Bukhari, through Ahmad ibn Yunus, from Ibrahim ibn Sa'd ibn Ibrahim ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf, from his father, from his paternal uncle Humayd ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Among the greatest of the major sins is that a man curses his parents." They said: "How does a man curse his parents?" He said: "A man curses the father of another man, and he curses his father; and he curses his mother, and he curses his mother."

Muslim narrated it likewise through the hadiths of Sufyan, Shu'bah and Yazid ibn al-Had, all three from Sa'd ibn Ibrahim, with it raised to the Prophet, with similar wording. Al-Tirmidhi said: "Sahih."[[Sahih al-Bukhari no. 5973, Sahih Muslim no. 90, and Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 1902.]]

It is established in the Sahih from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that he said: "Insulting a Muslim is wickedness (fusuq), and fighting him is disbelief (kufr)."[[Narrated by al-Bukhari no. 48 and Muslim no. 64, from 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him.]]

Another hadith on this: Ibn Abi Hatim said: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ibrahim Duhaym related to us, 'Amr ibn Abi Salamah related to us, Zuhayr ibn Muhammad related to us, from al-'Ala' ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Among the greatest of the major sins is violating a Muslim man's honour, and the two revilers (who abuse each other) are at fault, and the one who begins the abuse."[[Mentioned by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur.]]

This is how this hadith has been narrated. Abu Dawud also recorded it in the Book of Adab of his Sunan, from Ja'far ibn Musafir, from 'Amr ibn Abi Salamah, from Zuhayr ibn Muhammad, from al-'Ala', from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Among the greatest of the major sins is a man's taking liberties with the honour of a Muslim man without right, and among the major sins are the two revilers, who are at fault, with the one who begins the abuse."

Ibn Mardawayh likewise narrated it through the route of 'Abdullah ibn al-'Ala' ibn Zabr, from al-'Ala', from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), mentioning the like of it.[[Sunan Abi Dawud no. 4877.]]

Another hadith, concerning combining the two prayers without an excuse. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father related to us, Nu'aym ibn Hammad related to us, Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman related to us, from his father, from Hanash,[[In J: "Hubaysh," and in A: "Hunaysh."]] from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Whoever combines the two prayers without an excuse has committed one of the gates of the major sins." Abu 'Isa al-Tirmidhi also narrated it likewise from Abu Salamah Yahya ibn Khalaf, from al-Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman, with it. Then he said: "Hanash is Abu 'Ali al-Rahabi, and he is Husayn ibn Qays, and he is weak according to the people of hadith; Ahmad and others declared him weak."[[Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 188.]]

Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated: al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn al-Sabbah related to us, Isma'il ibn 'Ulayyah related to us, from Khalid al-Hadhdha', from Humayd ibn Hilal, from Abu Qatadah (meaning al-'Adawi), who said: "The letter of 'Umar was read to us: 'Among the major sins are combining the two prayers (meaning without an excuse), fleeing from the battle line, and plundering.'"

This is a sound chain of narration. The point is that if the threat applies to one who combines two prayers, such as Zuhr with 'Asr, whether early or late, and likewise Maghrib with 'Isha', which is permitted only for a legitimate reason (sabab shar'i), then one who does so without any of those reasons commits a major sin (kabirah). So what do you think of one who abandons prayer altogether? For this reason Muslim related in his Sahih from the Messenger of God (ﷺ) that he said: "Between a servant and polytheism (shirk) is the abandonment of prayer" [[Sahih Muslim, no. (82), from the hadith of Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah (may God be pleased with him).]]. In the Sunan, from him, peace be upon him, that he said: "The covenant between us and them is prayer; whoever abandons it has disbelieved" [[Related by al-Tirmidhi in the Sunan, no. (2621), al-Nasa'i in the Sunan (1/231), and Ibn Majah in the Sunan, no. (1079), from the hadith of Buraydah ibn al-Husayb (may God be pleased with him).]]. He also said: "Whoever abandons the 'Asr prayer, his deeds have been nullified" [[Related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. (553), and al-Nasa'i in the Sunan (1/236), from the hadith of Buraydah ibn al-Husayb (may God be pleased with him).]]. And he said: "Whoever misses the 'Asr prayer is as if he has lost his family and his wealth" [[Related by al-Nasa'i (1/238), from the hadith of Nawfal ibn Mu'awiyah (may God be pleased with him).]].

Another hadith: it contains despair of God's mercy (ya's min rawh Allah) and feeling safe from God's plan (amn min makr Allah). Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn 'Amr ibn Abi 'Asim al-Nabil related to us, my father related to us, Shabib ibn Bishr related to us, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas: that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) was reclining when a man entered upon him and said: "What are the major sins?" He said: "Associating partners with God (al-shirk billah), despair of God's mercy, despairing of God's compassion (al-qunut min rahmat Allah), and feeling safe from God's plan (al-amn min makr Allah). This is the greatest of the major sins."

Al-Bazzar related it from 'Abd Allah ibn Ishaq al-'Attar, from Abu 'Asim al-Nabil, from Shabib ibn Bishr, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas: that a man said: "O Messenger of God, what are the major sins?" He said: "Associating partners with God (al-ishrak billah) [[In d: "al-shirk".]], despair of the mercy of God (ya's min rawh Allah), and despairing of the compassion of God, the Mighty and Majestic (al-qunut min rahmat Allah 'azza wa jall)."

In its chain there is some doubt, and it is more likely to be a statement of Ibn 'Abbas (mawquf), for similar has been reported from Ibn Mas'ud [[Musnad al-Bazzar, no. (106), Kashf al-Astar; al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (1/104): "Its narrators are trustworthy."]]. Ibn Jarir said:

Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim related to me, Hushaym related to us, Mutarrif informed us, from Wabrah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from Abu al-Tufayl, who said: Ibn Mas'ud said: "The greatest of the major sins are associating partners with God, despair (al-iyas) [[In j, r, d, a: "al-yas".]] of God's mercy, despairing of God's compassion, and feeling safe from God's plan."

He related it similarly through the hadith of al-A'mash and Abu Ishaq, from Wabrah, from Abu al-Tufayl, from Ibn Mas'ud, and then he related it through several routes from Abu al-Tufayl, from Ibn Mas'ud. It is undoubtedly sound up to him (wa huwa sahih ilayhi bila shakk) [[Tafsir al-Tabari (8/243, 244). 'Abd al-Razzaq related it in al-Musannaf, no. (19701), and from his route al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (9/171), from the route of Abu Ishaq from Wabrah with the same wording. Ibn Abi al-Dunya related it in al-Tawbah, no. (31), from the route of al-A'mash from Wabrah with the same wording.]].

Another hadith: it contains bad opinion of God (su' al-zann billah). Ibn Mardawayh said: Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Bundar related to us, Abu Hatim Bakr ibn 'Abdan related to us, Muhammad ibn Muhajir [[In a: "Muhammad ibn 'Umar ibn Muhajir".]] related to us, Abu Hudhayfah [[In a: "Abu Hudhayfah Ishaq".]] al-Bukhari related to us, from Muhammad ibn 'Ajlan, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, that he said: [The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said [[Addition from a.]]]: "The greatest of the major sins is bad opinion of God, the Mighty and Majestic." This is a very strange hadith (gharib jiddan).

Another hadith: it contains becoming a Bedouin (ta'arrub) after emigration (hijrah). It has already been mentioned in the narration of 'Amr [[In a: "'Umar".]] ibn Abi Salamah, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, as a marfu' report. Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh said: Sulayman ibn Ahmad related to us, Ahmad ibn Rushdin related to us, 'Amr ibn Khalid al-Harrani related to us, Ibn Lahi'ah related to us, from Yazid ibn Abi Habib, from Muhammad ibn Sahl ibn Abi Hathmah [[In j, a: "Ibn Abi Khaythamah".]], from his father, who said: I heard the Prophet (ﷺ) say: "The major sins are seven. Will you not ask me about them? Associating partners with God (al-shirk billah), killing a soul, fleeing on the day of battle (al-firar yawm al-zahf), consuming the wealth of orphans, consuming usury (riba), slandering a chaste woman (qadhf al-muhsanah), and becoming a Bedouin (al-ta'arrub) after emigration."

Its chain has problems, and its attribution to the Prophet (raf') is a gross error (ghalat fahish) [[It has a supporting report from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri (may God be pleased with him) as a marfu', in which these seven are mentioned. Related by al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Awsat (126), Majma' al-Bahrayn. Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (1/104): "In it is Abu Bilal al-Ash'ari, who is weak."]]. The correct report is what Ibn Jarir related: Tamim ibn al-Muntasir related to us, Yazid informed us, Muhammad ibn Ishaq informed us, from Muhammad ibn Suhayl ibn Abi Hathmah [[In r, a: "Khaythamah".]], from his father, who said: I was in this mosque, the mosque of Kufa, and 'Ali (may God be pleased with him) was delivering a sermon to the people from the pulpit. He said: "O people, the major sins are seven." The people paid attention, so he repeated it three times. Then he said: "Why do you not ask me about them?" They said: "O Commander of the Faithful, what are they?" He said: "Associating partners with God, killing a soul which God has forbidden [[In a: "God has forbidden its killing".]], slandering a chaste woman, consuming the wealth of orphans, consuming usury, fleeing on the day of battle, and becoming a Bedouin after emigration." I said to my father: "O father, how does becoming a Bedouin after emigration fit here?" He said: "My son, what could be greater than a man who emigrates, and then when his share of the spoils (fai') falls to him and jihad becomes obligatory upon him, he removes that from his neck and returns to being a Bedouin as he was [[Tafsir al-Tabari (8/235).]]."

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Hashim related to us, Abu Mu'awiyah, that is Shayban, related to us, from Mansur, from Hilal ibn Yasaf, from Salamah ibn Qays al-Ashja'i, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said during the Farewell Pilgrimage: "Verily there are only four: that you associate nothing with God, that you do not kill the soul which God has forbidden except by right, that you do not commit adultery, and that you do not steal." He said: "So I am not more stingy with them than I am, since I heard them from the Messenger of God (ﷺ)" [[In a: "So what is for us?"]].

Then Ahmad also related it, and al-Nasa'i and Ibn Mardawayh, from the hadith of Mansur, with its chain in the same way [[Al-Musnad (4/339) and Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. (11373).]].

Another hadith: it has already been mentioned from the narration of 'Umar ibn al-Mughirah, from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he said: "Harming (al-idrar) in a bequest is among the major sins." The sound report is what others related, from Dawud, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas [as his own statement (qawluh)]. Ibn Abi Hatim said: This is the sound report from Ibn 'Abbas, as his own statement.

Another hadith on this: Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb related to us, Ahmad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman related to us, 'Abbad ibn 'Abbad related to us, from Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr, from al-Qasim, from Abu Umamah, that some of the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) [[In j, d, r: "Messenger of God".]] mentioned the major sins while he was reclining. They said: Associating partners with God, consuming the wealth of orphans, fleeing from battle, slandering a chaste woman, disobedience to parents, false speech, misappropriation of spoils (al-ghulul), sorcery, and consuming usury. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Where do you place ﴿Those who sell the covenant of God and their oaths for a small price﴾ [Al 'Imran 3:77]?!" up to the end of the verse. Its chain has weakness, but it is good (hasan) [[Tafsir al-Tabari (8/251).]].

Mention of the statements of the early generations (al-salaf) on this: What has been reported from the Commander of the Faithful 'Umar and 'Ali, may God be pleased with them both, has already been mentioned within the hadiths cited. Ibn Jarir said:

Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim related to me, Ibn 'Ulayyah related to us, from Ibn 'Awn, from al-Hasan: that some people met 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr in Egypt and said: "We see things in the Book of God which He commanded to be acted upon, but they are not acted upon, so we wish to meet the Commander of the Faithful about this." So he came, and they came with him. 'Umar, may God be pleased with him, met him and said: "When did you arrive?" He said: "Such and such a time ago." He said: "Did you come with permission?" He said: I do not know how he answered him. Then he said: "O Commander of the Faithful, some people met me in Egypt and said: 'We see things in the Book of God which He commanded to be acted upon, but they are not acted upon,' and they wished to meet you about this." He said: "Gather them for me." He said: So I gathered them for him. [Ibn 'Awn said: I think he said: in a hall.] He took the nearest of them, a man, and said: "I beseech you by God and by the right of Islam upon you, have you read the whole Qur'an?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Have you memorized it in your heart?" He said: "No, by God." He said: "If he had said yes, he would have refuted him." He said: "Have you memorized it in your sight? Have you memorized it in your recitation? Have you memorized it in your conduct?" Then he went through them until he reached the last of them. He said: So 'Umar's mother was bereaved of him [an idiom of rebuke]. Will you burden him to make people stand upon the Book of God?! Our Lord has known that there will be misdeeds (sayyi'at) among us. He said: Then he recited ﴿If you avoid the major sins that you are forbidden, We will remove from you your misdeeds and admit you to a noble entrance﴾ [4:31]. Then he said: "Do the people of Medina know, or did he say: does anyone know, what you have done?" They said: "No." He said: "If they knew, I would have admonished you."

A good chain and a good text, although it is from al-Hasan's narration from 'Umar and contains a break (inqita') in it. However, such a report has become well known (ishtahara), so its fame suffices [[Tafsir al-Tabari (8/255).]].

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn Sinan related to us, Abu Ahmad, that is al-Zubayri, related to us, 'Ali ibn Salih related to us, from 'Uthman ibn al-Mughirah, from Malik ibn Juwayn, from 'Ali, may God be pleased with him, who said: The major sins are associating partners with God, killing a soul, consuming the wealth of orphans, slandering a chaste woman, fleeing from battle, becoming a Bedouin after emigration, sorcery, disobedience to parents, consuming usury, abandoning the community (firaq al-jama'ah), and breaking the pledge of allegiance (nakth al-saf-qah).

It has already been reported from Ibn Mas'ud that he said: The greatest of the major sins are associating partners with God, despair of the mercy of God, despairing of God's compassion, and feeling safe from God's plan, the Mighty and Majestic.

Ibn Jarir related, from the hadith of al-A'mash, from Abu al-Duha, from Masruq, and al-A'mash from Ibrahim, from 'Alqamah, both from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: "The major sins are from the beginning of Surat al-Nisa' up to thirty verses of it." And from the hadith of Sufyan al-Thawri and Shu'bah, from 'Asim ibn Abi al-Najud, from Zirr ibn Hubaysh, from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: "The major sins are from the beginning of Surat al-Nisa' up to thirty verses of it," then he recited ﴿If you avoid the major sins that you are forbidden [We will remove from you your misdeeds and admit you to a noble entrance]﴾ [[Addition from j, r, a; in h: "the verse".]].

Ibn Abi Hatim said: al-Mundhir ibn Shadhan related to us, Ya'la ibn 'Ubayd related to us, Salih ibn Hayyan related to us, from Ibn Buraydah, from his father, who said: The greatest of the major sins are: associating partners with God, disobedience to parents, withholding surplus water after one has been satisfied, and withholding the stallion's service for a fee [[In d: "'urooq al-fahl" (vein of the stallion).]].

And in the two Sahihs, from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Surplus water is not to be withheld in order to withhold pasture by it." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 2353, and Sahih Muslim, no. 1566, from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him.]

And in the two Sahihs, also from him (ﷺ), that he said: "There are three whom Allah will not look at on the Day of Resurrection, nor will He purify them, and for them is a painful punishment: a man who has surplus water in the desert and withholds it from the traveller (ibn al-sabil)." He then mentioned the full hadith. [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 2358, and Sahih Muslim, no. 108, from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him.]

In Musnad Imam Ahmad, from the hadith of 'Amr ibn Shu'ayb, from his father, from his grandfather, traced to the Prophet (ﷺ): "Whoever withholds surplus water and surplus pasture, Allah will withhold His bounty from him on the Day of Resurrection." [al-Musnad (2/179).]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Shanabah [in ج, د, ر, أ: "Shaybah"] al-Wasiti narrated to us: Abu Ahmad narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Muslim, from Masruq, from 'A'ishah, who said: "Major sins (al-kaba'ir) were not taken from women." Ibn Abi Hatim said: That is, His saying: ﴿that they will not associate anything with Allah, nor steal, nor commit adultery, nor kill their children, nor bring a slander they have invented between their hands and feet, nor disobey you﴾ [al-Mumtahanah: 12], to the end of the verse. [In أ: "ta'ni" (i.e., "yacni"). Addition from ج، ر، أ.]

Ibn Jarir said: Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me: Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us: Ziyad ibn Mikhraq narrated to us, from Mu'awiyah ibn Qurrah, who said: "We came to Anas ibn Malik, and among what he related to us he said: 'I have not seen anything like what has reached us from our Lord, the Exalted [in ج: "Mighty and Majestic"], then we did not go out to Him from every family and wealth.'" Then he was silent for a moment, then said: "By Allah, what our Lord has imposed on us is easier than that. He has overlooked for us what is below the major sins, so what have we to do with them?" Then he recited: ﴿If you avoid the major sins you are forbidden, We will remove from you your misdeeds and admit you to an honourable entrance﴾ [al-Nisa': 31]. [Addition from ج، ر، أ، and in ه: "the verse".]

Views of Ibn 'Abbas on this:
Ibn Jarir narrated, from the hadith of al-Mu'tamir [in ج، ر: "Mu'tamir"] ibn Sulayman, from his father, from Tawus, who said: "They mentioned the major sins in the presence of Ibn 'Abbas and said: They are seven. He said: They are more than seven, and seven." Sulayman said: "I do not know how many times he said it."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us: Qubaysah narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us, from Layth, from Tawus, who said: "I said to Ibn 'Abbas: What are the seven major sins? He said: They are nearer to seventy than to seven."

Ibn Jarir narrated it from Ibn Humayd, from Layth, from Tawus, who said: "A man came to Ibn 'Abbas and said: Tell me about the seven major sins that Allah mentioned. What are they? He said: They are nearer to seventy than to seven."

'Abd al-Razzaq said: Ma'mar informed us, from Tawus, from his father, who said: "It was said to Ibn 'Abbas: Are the major sins seven? He said: They are nearer to seventy." And likewise said Abu al-'Aliyah al-Riyahi, may Allah have mercy on him.

Ibn Jarir said: Al-Muthanna narrated to us: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us: Shibl narrated to us, from Qays, from Sa'd, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, that a man said to Ibn 'Abbas: "How many are the major sins? Seven?" He said: "They are nearer to seven hundred than to seven, except that there is no major sin with seeking forgiveness, and no minor sin with persistence." Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated it likewise, from the hadith of Shibl, with the same chain.

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah said, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His saying: ﴿If you avoid the major sins you are forbidden﴾: "The major sins are every sin that Allah concluded with a Fire, or wrath, or a curse, or a punishment." Ibn Jarir also narrated it.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: 'Ali ibn Harb al-Mawsili narrated to us: Ibn Fudayl narrated to us: Shabib narrated to us, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "The major sins: everything for which Allah has promised the Fire is a major sin." Likewise said Sa'id ibn Jubayr and al-Hasan al-Basri.

Ibn Jarir said: Ya'qub narrated to me: Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us: Ayyub informed us, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, who said: "I was told that Ibn 'Abbas used to say: Everything Allah has forbidden is a major sin." I have already mentioned the glance (al-tarfah) [in it: "Fihi" — addition from ج، أ]. He said: "It is the [lustful] glance."

He also said: Ahmad ibn Hazim narrated to us: Abu Nu'aym informed us: 'Abd Allah ibn Ma'dan narrated to us, from Abu al-Walid, who said: "I asked Ibn 'Abbas about the major sins, and he said: They are everything in which Allah is disobeyed, so it is a major sin." [In ج: "qala" (said).]

Views of the Successors (al-tabi'un):
Ibn Jarir said: Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me: Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, from Ibn 'Awn, from Muhammad, who said: "I asked 'Ubaydah about the major sins, and he said: Associating partners with Allah, killing a soul which Allah has forbidden without right, fleeing on the day of battle, consuming the property of an orphan unjustly, consuming usury, and slander (al-buhtan)." He said: "And they say: a Bedouin matter after the emigration." Ibn 'Awn said: "I said to Muhammad: And sorcery? He said: Slander gathers great evil."

Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn 'Ubayd al-Muharibi narrated to me: Abu al-Ahwas Sallam ibn Sulaym narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from 'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr, who said: "The major sins are seven; there is not one among them except that there is a verse of the Book of Allah concerning it. Association with Allah is among them: ﴿Whoever associates with Allah, it is as if he had fallen from the sky and the birds snatched him away or the wind hurled him into a faraway place﴾ [al-Hajj: 31]; and ﴿Those who unjustly consume the property of orphans only consume fire into their bellies﴾ [al-Nisa': 10]; ﴿Those who consume usury will not stand except as one stands whom Satan has driven mad by touch﴾ [al-Baqarah: 275]; and ﴿Indeed those who accuse chaste, unwary, believing women﴾ [al-Nur: 23]; and fleeing from battle: ﴿O you who believe, when you meet those who disbelieve advancing, do not turn your backs to them﴾ [al-Anfal: 15]; and apostasy (al-ta'arrub) after emigration: ﴿Indeed those who turned back on their heels after guidance had become clear to them﴾ [Muhammad: 25]; and killing a believer: ﴿Whoever deliberately kills a believer, his recompense is Hell, abiding therein﴾, the verse [al-Nisa': 93]."

Ibn Abi Hatim likewise narrated it from the hadith of Abu Ishaq, from 'Ubayd, in similar wording.

Ibn Jarir said: Al-Muthanna narrated to us: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from 'Ata' (i.e., Ibn Abi Rabah), who said: "The major sins are seven: killing a soul, consuming usury, consuming the property of an orphan, accusing a chaste woman, bearing false witness, disobeying one's parents, and fleeing from battle."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur'ah narrated to us: 'Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Jarir narrated to us, from Mughirah, who said: "It used to be said that insulting Abu Bakr and 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, is among the major sins."

I say: A group of scholars has gone to the view of declaring disbelief (takfir) for whoever reviles the Companions, and this is a narration from Malik ibn Anas, may Allah have mercy on him. Muhammad ibn Sirin said: "I do not think anyone who disparages Abu Bakr and 'Umar, while loving the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), exists." Narrated by al-Tirmidhi.

Ibn Abi Hatim also said: Yunus narrated to us: Ibn Wahb informed us: 'Abd Allah ibn 'Ayyash informed me, who said: Zayd ibn Aslam, concerning the saying of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿If you avoid the major sins you are forbidden﴾, said: "Among the major sins are: association with Allah, disbelief in the signs of Allah and His Messenger, sorcery, killing children, one who attributes to Allah a son or a consort, and similar deeds, and a statement with which no deed is sound. As for every sin with which religion remains sound and with which a deed is accepted, Allah forgives misdeeds by good deeds."

Ibn Jarir said: Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us: Yazid narrated to us: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning ﴿If you avoid the major sins you are forbidden﴾, the verse: "Allah only promised forgiveness to one who avoids the major sins. It has been mentioned to us that the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Avoid the major sins, be upright, and receive good tidings.'"

Ibn Mardawayh has related, by several routes from Anas, and from Jabir, traced to the Prophet (ﷺ): "My intercession is for the people of major sins from among my community." [Regarding the hadith of Anas, it has several routes, among them: what Abu Bakr ibn 'Ayyash narrates from Humayd, from Anas. Ibn Abi 'Asim recorded it in al-Sunnah, no. 831. And what he narrates from Ibn al-Mubarak, from 'Asim al-Ahwal, from Anas, which al-Tabarani narrated in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (1/258) and Ibn Abi Hatim in al-'Ilal (2/222), and he said: I heard my father and Abu Zur'ah say: This is a munkar hadith. And what Ja'far ibn Sulaym al-Di'bi narrates from Malik ibn Dinar, from Anas, which Ibn Abi Hatim narrated in al-'Ilal (2/79), and he said: I heard my father say: This is a munkar hadith. And what Bastan ibn Huraith al-Sadafi narrates from Ash'ath, from Anas, which al-Qada'i narrated in Musnad al-Shihab, no. 237. And what Abu Janab narrates, having heard Ziyad al-Numayri, having heard Anas, which al-Qada'i narrated in Musnad al-Shihab (237). As for the hadith of Jabir, Ibn Majah narrated it in his Sunan, no. 4310, by the route of Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Jabir.]

However, in its chain, in all its routes, there is weakness, except what 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated: Ma'mar informed us, from Thabit, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "My intercession is for the people of major sins from among my community." This is a sound chain (isnad) on the condition of the two Shaykhs [in د: "on their two conditions"; in ر: "on the condition of the Shaykhayn"]. Abu 'Isa al-Tirmidhi narrated it alone by this route, from 'Abbas al-'Anbari, from 'Abd al-Razzaq, then said: "This is a hasan sahih hadith." [Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 2435.] In the Sahih there is a witness to its meaning: his saying (ﷺ), after mentioning intercession: "Do you think it is for the believers who are God-fearing? No, but it is for the sinners who are defiled."

The scholars of the principles (usul) and the branches (furu') of jurisprudence have differed on the definition of the major sin (kabirah). Some say: It is what carries a prescribed legal penalty (hadd) in the Shari'ah. Among them are those who say: It is what has a specific threat (wa'id) in the Qur'an and the Sunnah. And it has been said otherwise.

Abu al-Qasim 'Abd al-Karim ibn Muhammad al-Rafi'i said, in his famous book al-Sharh al-Kabir, in its chapter on testimonies: "Then the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them [ta'ala — addition from ج], and those after them differed concerning the major sins, and in distinguishing them from minor sins. And some of the companions [of al-Shafi'i] have several views in defining the major sin:

First: It is the disobedience which requires a legal penalty (hadd).

Second: It is the disobedience for which its doer incurs a severe threat by explicit text of the Book or the Sunnah. This is what is most found in their statements, and it is [in ج, أ: "they"] the first I incline to, but the second is more in agreement with what they mentioned when detailing the major sins.

Third: Imam al-Haramayn said in al-Irshad and elsewhere: Every offence that indicates little concern of its perpetrator for religion and weakness of piety is what nullifies justice ('adalah).

Fourth: Al-Qadi Abu Sa'id [in ج، ر: "Abu Sa'd"] al-Harawi mentioned that the major sin is: every act whose prohibition the Book has explicitly stated, every disobedience which in its kind requires a legal penalty such as execution or other, abandoning every obligatory duty that must be performed immediately, and lying in testimony, narration, and oath."

This is what he mentioned as a summary (dabt).

Then he said: Al-Qadi al-Ruyani made a detailed list and said: The major sins (al-kaba'ir) are seven: killing a soul without right, adultery (al-zina), sodomy (al-liwat), drinking wine, theft, seizing property unlawfully (ghasb), and false accusation of unchastity (al-qadhf). In "al-Shamil" he added to the seven mentioned: false testimony (shahadat al-zur). Sahib al-'Uddah added to them: consuming usury (riba), breaking the fast of Ramadan without excuse, the false oath (al-yamin al-fajira), severing the ties of kinship (qat' al-rahm), disobedience to parents ('uquq al-walidayn), fleeing from the battlefield (al-firar min al-zahf), consuming the property of an orphan, cheating in measure and weight, performing the prayer before its time or delaying it beyond its time without excuse, striking a Muslim without right, lying about the Prophet (ﷺ) deliberately, reviling his Companions, concealing testimony without excuse, taking bribes, procuring between men and women, informing on people to the ruler (al-si'ayah 'inda al-sultan), withholding zakat, abandoning enjoining good and forbidding evil when able, forgetting the Qur'an after having learned it, burning animals with fire, a woman refusing her husband without reason, despairing of the mercy of Allah, and feeling secure from the plan of Allah. It is also said: slandering the people of knowledge and the bearers of the Qur'an. Among what is counted as major sins: zihar, and eating the flesh of swine and carrion except in necessity.

Then al-Rafi'i said: There is room for hesitation regarding some of these traits.

I say: People have composed works on the major sins, among them what our shaykh, the hafiz Abu 'Abd Allah al-Dhahabi (it was published in Beirut, edited by the teacher Muhyi al-Din Mustu), compiled, which reached about seventy major sins. If the major sin is defined as that for which the Lawgiver specifically threatened the Fire, as Ibn 'Abbas and others said, and one traces this, a great deal is gathered. If it is said: everything Allah has forbidden, then it is very numerous indeed. And Allah knows best.

Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim, on Surah 4, verses 29–31 (part 1 of 6):

Allah, may He be blessed and exalted, forbade His believing servants from consuming one another's wealth unjustly (bil-batil), that is, through kinds of gain that are not legally permitted, such as the various forms of riba (usury) and gambling, and whatever follows their course among all the other kinds of stratagems. This applies even when such stratagems appear to conform to the outward ruling of the Sharia, if Allah knows that the one practising them intends only a trick to obtain riba. Ibn Jarir said:

Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to me: 'Abd al-Wahhab narrated to us: Dawud narrated to us, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning a man who buys a garment from another man and says: "If I like it, I will take it; otherwise I will return it and return a dirham with it." He said: "This is what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, meant by: ﴿And do not consume your wealth among yourselves unjustly﴾."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: 'Ali ibn Harb al-Mawsili narrated to us: Ibn Fudayl narrated to us, from Dawud al-Awdi, from 'Amir, from 'Alqamah, from 'Abdullah [ ﴿O you who have believed, do not consume your wealth among yourselves unjustly﴾ ] [[Addition from J, R, A.]] He said: "It is a firm (muhkam) statement; it has not been abrogated (nusikha) and will not be abrogated until the Day of Resurrection."

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated, from Ibn 'Abbas: When Allah revealed ﴿O you who have believed, do not consume your wealth among yourselves unjustly﴾, the Muslims said: "Allah has forbidden us to consume our wealth among ourselves unjustly, and food is the best of wealth. So it is not lawful for any of us to eat at someone else's home. How then [can we eat] with people?!" Then Allah revealed afterwards: ﴿There is no blame upon the blind﴾ [An-Nur: 61], and the verse. [Likewise Qatadah ibn Di'amah said.] [[Addition from A.]]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿except that it be trade by mutual consent among you﴾ [[In A: "among you" (bbaynakum).]] it was read as tijaratun with a nominative (raf') and with an accusative (nasb). It is an exception of the disconnected type (istithna' munqati'), as if He said: Do not engage in the prohibited means of acquiring wealth, but permitted trade that is by mutual consent of the seller and the buyer, then do it, and use it to obtain wealth. Just as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿and do not kill the soul which Allah has forbidden, except by right﴾ [Al-An'am: 151], and as in His saying ﴿They will not taste death therein, except the first death﴾ [Ad-Dukhan: 56].

From this noble verse, al-Shafi'i (may Allah have mercy on him) argued that a sale is not valid except with acceptance (qabul), because it explicitly indicates mutual consent, unlike mu'atah (a sale concluded by exchange of goods and money without words), which may not indicate consent, and it must. Malik, Abu Hanifah, Ahmad and their companions disagreed with the majority on this point. They held that statements indicate mutual consent, and in some situations actions also indicate it with certainty. So they validated the mu'atah sale absolutely. Some of them said it is valid for trivial items and for whatever people regard as a sale, and this is a precautionary view of the scholars of the school who investigate its principles. And Allah knows best.

Mujahid said: ﴿except that it be trade by mutual consent among you﴾ means a sale [[In A: "sale" (bay').]] or a gift one person gives another. Ibn Jarir narrated it, [then] [[Addition from J, A.]] he said:

Ibn Wakic narrated to us: my father narrated to us, from al-Qasim, from Sulayman al-Ju'fi, from his father, from Maymun ibn Mihran who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Sale is by mutual consent, and the option (khiyar) is after the transaction, and it is not lawful for a Muslim to deceive a Muslim." This is a mursal (a hadith whose chain omits the Companion) narration. [Tafsir al-Tabari (8/221).]

Part of complete consent is the establishment of khiyar al-majlis (the option of the session, the right of the parties to cancel while still in the meeting), as established in the Two Sahihs (al-Bukhari and Muslim): that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The two parties to a sale have the option as long as they have not separated." In the wording of al-Bukhari: "When two men engage in a sale, each of them has the option as long as they have not separated." [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (2109) and Sahih Muslim no. (1531).]

Al-Shafi'i, Ahmad ibn Hanbal [[Addition from A.]] and their companions, along with the majority of the early and later scholars (al-salaf wa'l-khalaf), acted according to the meaning of this hadith. From this is the legitimacy of khiyar al-shart (the option stipulated in the contract) after the contract for up to three days, as is agreed among the scholars, and beyond three days according to what is needed to determine the value of the sale. Even up to a year in a village or similar, as is well known from Malik, may Allah have mercy on him. Some validated the mu'atah sale absolutely, and this is a view within the school of al-Shafi'i. Others said that the mu'atah sale is valid for trivial items that people regard as a sale, and this is the choice of a group of the companions of the school. [[In R: "So they validated."]]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿and do not kill yourselves﴾, that is: by committing the prohibitions of Allah and engaging in His disobediences, and by consuming your wealth among yourselves unjustly. ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever Merciful to you﴾, that is: in what He commanded you and what He forbade you.

Imam Ahmad said: Hasan [[In J, A: "Husayn".]] ibn Musa narrated to us: Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to us: Yazid ibn Abi Habib narrated to us, from 'Imran ibn Abi Anas, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr, from 'Amr ibn al-'As, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: When the Prophet (ﷺ) sent him in the year of Dhat al-Salasil, he said: "I had a wet dream on a night that was extremely cold, and I feared that if I bathed I would perish. So I performed tayammum, then led my companions in the dawn prayer." He said: "When I came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), I mentioned that to him, and he said: 'O 'Amr, you led your companions in prayer while you were junub (in a state of major impurity)!' I said: 'Yes, O Messenger of Allah, I had a wet dream on a night that was extremely cold, and I feared that if I bathed [[In A: "that I bathe."]] I would perish. So I remembered the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿And do not kill yourselves; indeed Allah is ever Merciful to you﴾, so I performed tayammum and prayed.'" Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) laughed and said nothing.

Abu Dawud related it in the same way from the hadith of Yahya ibn Ayyub, from Yazid ibn Abi Habib, with the same chain. He also related it from Muhammad ibn Abi Salamah, from Ibn Wahb, from Ibn Lahi'ah and 'Umar ibn al-Harith, both from Yazid ibn Abi Habib, from 'Imran ibn Abi Anas, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr al-Misri, from Abu Qays, client of 'Amr ibn al-'As, from him, and he mentioned something similar. This, and Allah knows best, is closer to the correct version. [Musnad (4/203) and Sunan Abi Dawud no. (334).]

Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh said: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad ibn Hamid al-Balkhi narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Salih ibn Sahl al-Balkhi narrated to us: 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Umar al-Qawariri narrated to us: Yusuf ibn Khalid narrated to us: Ziyad ibn Sa'd narrated to us, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas: that 'Amr ibn al-'As led the people in prayer while he was junub. When they came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), they mentioned that to him, and he summoned him and asked him about it. He said: "O Messenger of Allah, I feared that the cold would kill me, and Allah, the Exalted, has said: ﴿and do not kill yourselves [indeed Allah is ever Merciful to you]﴾." He said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) remained silent about it." [[Al-Tabarani (11/234) narrated it through 'Ubayd Allah al-Qawariri, and al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (1/264): "In it is Yusuf ibn Khalid al-Samti, who is a liar."]]

Then Ibn Mardawayh, at this noble verse, cited a hadith from al-A'mash, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever kills himself with an iron implement, his iron will be in his hand, with which he will stab his belly on the Day of Resurrection in the Fire of Hell, abiding therein forever and ever. Whoever kills himself with poison, his poison will be in his hand, which he will sip in the Fire of Hell, abiding therein forever and ever. Whoever throws himself from a mountain and kills himself will be falling in the Fire of Hell, abiding therein forever and ever."

This hadith is established in the Two Sahihs [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (5778) and Sahih Muslim no. (109)]. Likewise Abu al-Zinad narrated it from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), with similar wording. And from Abu Qilabah, from Thabit ibn al-Dahhak, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever kills himself with something, he will be punished with it on the Day of Resurrection." The group (al-Jama'ah) recorded it in their books through the route of Abu Qilabah [Sahih al-Bukhari nos. (6047, 6105), Sahih Muslim no. (110), Sunan Abi Dawud no. (3257), Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (1543), Sunan al-Nasa'i (7/5,6), Sunan Ibn Majah no. (2098); al-Tirmidhi does not have the phrase "whoever kills himself with something," which is the point of citation here]. In the Two Sahihs, from the hadith of al-Hasan, from Jundub ibn 'Abd Allah al-Bajali, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "There was a man among those before you who had a wound, so he took a knife and cut his hand with it, and the blood did not stop until he died. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: 'My servant hastened to take his own life, so I have forbidden Paradise to him.'" [Sahih al-Bukhari nos. (1364, 3463) and Sahih Muslim no. (113).]

For this reason Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And whoever does that in transgression and wrongdoing, We will drive him into a Fire, and that is ever easy for Allah﴾, that is: whoever engages in what Allah has forbidden him, transgressing and wronging himself in doing so, knowing its prohibition and audaciously violating it. [[Addition from J, R, A.]] This is a severe threat and a firm warning, so let every wise, intelligent person who gives ear while being attentive beware of it.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿If you avoid the major sins which you are forbidden, We will remove from you your misdeeds and admit you to a noble entrance [[Addition from J, R, A.]]﴾. That is: if you avoid the grave sins that you have been forbidden, We will expiate your minor sins for you and admit you to Paradise. For this reason He said: ﴿and admit you to a noble entrance﴾.

Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said: Mu'ammal ibn Hisham narrated to us: Isma'il ibn Ibrahim narrated to us: Khalid [[In R: "al-Khald"; in A: "al-Khalid".]] ibn Ayyub narrated to us, from Mu'awiyah ibn Qurrah, from Anas, [raising it to the Prophet] [[Addition from J, R, A.]]: "[What has reached us from our Lord, Mighty and Majestic, is] that He does not bring us out, of every family and property, [except] that He forgives us what is below the major sins. Allah [the Exalted] [[Addition from J, R, A.]] says: ﴿If you avoid the major sins which you are forbidden, We will remove from you your misdeeds [and admit you to a noble entrance]﴾." [[Al-Bazzar in Musnad no. (2200), Kashf al-Astar; al-Haythami said: "In it is al-Jald ibn Ayyub, who is weak."]]

Many hadiths related to this noble verse have been transmitted, so let us mention what is easily accessible from them:

Imam Ahmad said: Husharm narrated to us, from Mughirah, from Abu Ma'shar, from Ibrahim, from Qarth' al-Dabbi, from Salman al-Farisi, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said to me: "Do you know what the Day of Jumu'ah is?" I said: "It is the day on which Allah gathered your father." He said: "But do you know what the Day of Jumu'ah is? A man purifies himself and performs his purification well, then comes to Jumu'ah and listens attentively until the imam finishes his prayer, and this will be an expiation for him for what is between it and the next Jumu'ah, so long as the major sins (al-maqtalah) are avoided." Al-Bukhari also narrated something similar from Salman through another route. [Musnad (5/439), and al-Bukhari no. (910) through Sa'id al-Maqburi from his father, from Ibn Wadi'ah, from Salman al-Farisi, with similar wording.]

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 4, verse 29–31 (part 2 of 6):

Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir said: Al-Muthanna [ibn Ibrahim] [[added from manuscripts R and A.]] narrated to me: Abu Salih narrated to us: al-Layth narrated to us: Khalid narrated to me, from Sa'id ibn Abi Hilal, from Nu'aym al-Mujmir, who said: Suhayb, the freedman of al-'Utwari, informed me that he heard from Abu Hurayrah and Abu Sa'id, both saying: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) addressed us one day and said: "By He in whose hand is my soul" three times. Then he lowered his head, and every man among us lowered his head weeping, not knowing what he had sworn about. Then he raised his head, and there was joy in his face, and it was more beloved to us than red camels. He (ﷺ) said: "There is no servant who prays the five prayers, fasts Ramadan, pays zakat, and avoids the seven major sins, except that the gates of Paradise are opened for him, and it is said to him: Enter in peace." [[in A: "al-Bushra" (the good news).]]

This was also related by al-Nasa'i and al-Hakim in his Mustadrak, through the narration of al-Layth ibn Sa'd. Al-Hakim also related it, and Ibn Hibban in his Sahih, through the narration of Abdullah ibn Wahb, from 'Amr ibn al-Harith, from Sa'id ibn Abi Hilal, with the same chain. Then al-Hakim said: "Sahih according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim), though they did not record it." [[Tafsir al-Tabari (8/238), Sunan al-Nasa'i (5/8), and al-Mustadrak (1/200).]]

The explanation of these seven:
This is based on what is established in the two Sahihs from the hadith of Sulayman ibn Bilal, from Thawr ibn Zayd, from Salim Abi al-Ghayth, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Avoid the seven destructive things." It was asked: "O Messenger of Allah, what are they?" He said: "Associating partners with Allah, killing a soul which Allah has forbidden except by right, sorcery, consuming riba, consuming the property of the orphan, fleeing on the day of battle, and slandering chaste, believing, unaware women." [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (2766) and Sahih Muslim no. (89).]]

Another route from him: Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us: Fahd ibn 'Awf narrated to us: Abu 'Awanah narrated to us, from 'Amr ibn Abi Salamah, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The major sins are seven: the first of them is associating partners with Allah, then killing a soul without right, consuming riba, consuming the property of the orphan until he grows up, fleeing from the battle line, slandering (chaste women), and reverting to the Bedouin life after the emigration (hijrah)." [[Musnad al-Bazzar no. (109), Kashf al-Astar. Al-Haythami said in Majma' al-Zawa'id (1/103): "In it is 'Umar ibn Abi Salamah, whom Shu'bah and others declared weak, but Abu Hatim, Ibn Hibban and others declared trustworthy."]]

The explicit statement that these seven are major sins does not negate what is beyond them, except according to those who hold the principle of mafhum al-laqab (the implication drawn from naming a specific item, i.e., an argument from the mere mention of a term), which is weak in the absence of an indicator. This is especially so when there is evidence from an explicit text that the implication does not apply. As we will cite from the hadiths which mention major sins other than these seven, among them is what al-Hakim related in his Mustadrak, where he said:

Ahmad ibn Kamil al-Qadi narrated to us, by dictation: Abu Qilabah 'Abd al-Malik ibn Muhammad narrated to us: Mu'adh ibn Hani' narrated to us: Harb ibn Shaddad narrated to us: Yahya ibn Abi Kathir narrated to us, from Abd al-Hamid ibn Sinan, from Ubayd ibn 'Umayr, from his father, meaning 'Umayr ibn Qatadah, may Allah be pleased with him, that he related to him, and he had companionship (with the Prophet): that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said during the Farewell Pilgrimage: "Verily, the friends of Allah are those who pray, who maintain the five prayers which were prescribed for them, who fast Ramadan seeking its reward, who believe it is their duty, who give the zakat of their wealth seeking its reward, and who avoid the major sins which Allah has forbidden." Then a man asked him: "O Messenger of Allah, what are the major sins?" He said: "Nine: associating partners with Allah, killing a believing soul without right, fleeing on the day of battle, consuming the property of the orphan, consuming riba, slandering a chaste woman, disobeying the two believing parents, and violating the Sacred House, your qibla, whether they are alive or dead." Then he said: "No man dies who does not commit these major sins, while maintaining the prayer and paying zakat, except that he will be with the Prophet (ﷺ) in a house whose doors are of gold." [[in J, R, A: "its doors are its mansions (masani')"]]

Thus al-Hakim related it at length. Abu Dawud and al-Tirmidhi [[in J: "and al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i"]] related it in summary through the narration of Mu'adh ibn Hani', with the same chain. Likewise Ibn Abi Hatim related it from his narration in full. Then al-Hakim said: "All its narrators are those whose narrations are used in the two Sahihs, except 'Abd al-Hamid ibn Sinan." [[Al-Mustadrak (1/59), Sunan Abi Dawud no. (2875), and I did not find it in al-Tirmidhi. Al-Bayhaqi related it in al-Sunan al-Kubra from al-Hakim's route (3/408) and said: "The word 'sorcery' fell out of my book or out of my Shaykh's book (meaning al-Hakim)."
And 'Abd al-Hamid ibn Sinan. Al-Dhahabi said: "He is counted among the Tabi'un, not well known. Some declared him trustworthy. Al-Bukhari said: 'In his narration from Ubayd there is consideration.' I say: His narration from Ubayd from his father, 'The major sins are nine...' the hadith..."]]

I say: He is a Hijazi who is known only through this hadith. Ibn Hibban mentioned him in the book al-Thiqat (the Trustworthy), while al-Bukhari said: "In his hadith there is consideration."

Ibn Jarir also related it from Sulayman ibn Thabit al-Jahdari, from Salm ibn Salam, from Ayyub ibn 'Utbah, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from Ubayd ibn 'Umayr, from his father, and mentioned it. But he did not mention 'Abd al-Hamid ibn Sinan in the chain. And Allah knows best. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (8/241).]]

Another hadith with the same meaning: Ibn Mardawayh said: 'Abdullah ibn Ja'far narrated to us: Ahmad ibn Yunus narrated to us: Yahya ibn 'Abd al-Hamid narrated to us: 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Muslim ibn al-Walid narrated to us, from al-Muttalib, from 'Abdullah ibn Hantab, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) ascended the pulpit and said: "I do not swear, I do not swear." Then he descended and said: "Rejoice, rejoice! Whoever prays the five prayers and avoids the seven major sins, will be called from the gates of Paradise: Enter." 'Abd al-'Aziz said: "I do not know it except that he said: 'in peace.'" Al-Muttalib said: I heard someone ask 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr: "Did you hear the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) mention them?" He said: "Yes: disobedience to parents, associating partners with Allah, killing the soul, slandering chaste women, consuming the property of the orphan, fleeing from the battle line, and consuming riba." [[Al-Tabarani also related it in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir no. (3) "al-Qit'ah al-Mafqudah" through the route of 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Muhammad, from Muslim ibn al-Walid, from al-Muttalib with the same wording. In its chain is Muslim ibn al-Walid, whom al-Bukhari mentioned in al-Tarikh al-Kabir (8/153) and Ibn Abi Hatim in al-Jarh wa al-Ta'dil (8/197), and neither of them mentioned any criticism or praise of him.]]

Another hadith with a similar meaning: Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir said in his Tafsir: Ya'qub narrated to us: Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us: Zayd ibn Mikhraq informed us, from Taysalah ibn Mayyas, who said: I was with the Najdat (a Kharijite sect), and I committed sins which I considered to be among the major sins. I met Ibn 'Umar and said to him: "I have committed sins which I consider to be among the major sins." He said: "What are they?" I said: "I committed such and such." He said: "That is not among the major sins." I said: "And I committed such and such." He said: "That is not among the major sins," and he mentioned something Taysalah did not name. Then he said: "They are nine, and I will count them for you: associating partners with Allah, killing a soul without right, fleeing from the battle line, slandering a chaste woman, consuming riba, consuming the property of the orphan unjustly, violating the Sacred Mosque, one who practices sorcery, and the weeping of the parents from disobedience." Ziyad said: Taysalah said when he saw Ibn 'Umar: "He trembled." He said: "Do you fear the Fire that you would enter it?" I said: "Yes." He said: "And do you love to enter Paradise?" I said: "Yes." He said: "Are your parents alive?" I said: "My mother is with me." He said: "By Allah, if you speak gently to her and feed her, you will certainly enter Paradise so long as you avoid the sins that necessitate Hell." [[Tafsir al-Tabari (8/239). Al-Bukhari related it in al-Adab al-Mufrad no. (8) through the route of Ziyad ibn Mikhraq with the same wording.]]

Another route: Ibn Jarir said: Sulayman ibn Thabit al-Jahdari al-Wasiti narrated to us: Salm ibn Salam narrated to us: Ayyub ibn 'Utbah narrated to us, from Taysalah ibn 'Ali al-Nahdi, who said: I came to Ibn 'Umar while he was in the shade of an arak tree on the day of 'Arafah, pouring water over his head and face. I said: "Inform me about the major sins." He said: "They are nine." I said: "What are they?" He said: "Associating partners with Allah, and slandering a chaste woman." He said: I said: "Before killing?" He said: "Yes, and (it is) by force." And killing a believing soul, fleeing from the battle line, sorcery, consuming riba, consuming the property of the orphan, disobedience to the two believing parents, and violating the Sacred House, your qibla, whether they are alive or dead. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (8/240).]]

This is how he related it through these two routes, as a mawquf (a statement ending with a Companion). It was also related by 'Ali ibn al-Ja'd, from Ayyub ibn 'Utbah, from Taysalah ibn 'Ali [al-Nahdi] [[added from manuscript A.]], who said: I came to Ibn 'Umar on the evening of 'Arafah, while he was under the shade of an arak tree, pouring water over his head. I asked him about the major sins, and he said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'They are seven.'" I said: "And what are they?" He said: "Associating partners with Allah, slandering a chaste woman." I said: "Before the blood (killing)?" He said: "Yes, and by force." "And killing a believing soul, fleeing from the battle line, sorcery, consuming riba, consuming the property of the orphan, disobedience to the parents, and violating the Sacred House, your qibla, whether alive or dead."

Similarly it was related by al-Hasan ibn Musa al-Ashyab, from Ayyub ibn 'Utbah al-Yamani, and there is weakness in him. [[Al-Baghawi related it in al-Ja'diyyat. Al-Kharaiti related it in Masawi' al-Akhlaq no. (247) through the route of Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Marwazi, from Ayyub ibn 'Utbah, with similar wording, and Ayyub ibn 'Utbah is weak. 'Ikrimah ibn 'Ammar related it from Taysalah ibn 'Ali: that Ibn 'Umar used to stop at the arak trees on the day of 'Arafah. Abu Dawud related it in al-Masa'il (118).]] And Allah knows best.

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Zakariyya ibn 'Adi narrated to us: Baqiyyah narrated to us, from Bahir ibn Sa'd, from Khalid ibn Ma'dan, that Abu Ruhm al-Sama'i narrated to them, from Abu Ayyub, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever worships Allah without associating anything with Him, establishes the prayer, gives zakat, fasts Ramadan, and avoids the major sins, for him is Paradise, or he will enter Paradise." A man asked him: "What are the major sins?" He said: "Associating partners with Allah, killing a Muslim soul, and fleeing on the day of battle."

Ahmad also related it, and al-Nasa'i, through other routes, from Baqiyyah. [[Al-Musnad (5/413) and Sunan al-Nasa'i (7/88).]]

Another hadith: The hafiz Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh related in his Tafsir, through the route of Sulayman ibn Dawud al-Yamani, who is weak, from al-Zuhri, from Abu Bakr ibn Muhammad ibn 'Amr ibn Hazm, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) wrote a letter to the people of Yemen containing the obligatory duties, the Sunan and the blood-money, and sent it with 'Amr ibn Hazm. He said: In the letter was: "Verily, the greatest of the major sins before Allah on the Day of Resurrection are: associating partners with Allah, killing a believing soul without right, fleeing in the way of Allah on the day of battle, disobedience to parents, slandering a chaste woman, learning sorcery, consuming riba, and consuming the property of the orphan." [[Al-Hakim related it in al-Mustadrak (1/395) through the route of Yahya ibn Hamzah from Sulayman ibn Dawud with the same wording. Al-Hakim said: "This is a great hadith explaining this subject. Sulayman ibn Dawud al-Khawlani is known as al-Zuhri, although Yahya ibn Ma'in criticized him, others declared him reliable." He then mentioned the statement of Abu Hatim and Abu Zur'ah: "Sulayman ibn Dawud al-Khawlani is among those with no harm in them, according to us."]]

Another hadith, which mentions false testimony. Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far related to us, Shu'bah related to us, 'Ubaydullah ibn Abi Bakr related to me, saying: I heard Anas ibn Malik say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) mentioned the major sins, or was asked about the major sins, and said: "Associating partners with Allah, killing a soul, and disobedience to one's parents." He then said: "Shall I not inform you of the greatest of the major sins?" He said: "False speech, or false testimony." Shu'bah said: "My strong assumption is that he said 'false testimony.'"[[In J, R, A: "Abdullah," and in R: "Muhammad," which is an error; the correct reading is 'Ubaydullah. See Musnad al-Imam Ahmad 3/131.]] [[The Musnad (3/131).]]

Al-Bukhari and Muslim both recorded it through the narration of Shu'bah.[[Sahih al-Bukhari no. 5977 and Sahih Muslim no. 88.]] Ibn Mardawayh narrated it through two other chains from Anas, which are gharib (rare), with a similar wording.[[In R: "nahwuhu."]]

Another hadith: The two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim) recorded it through the narration of 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakrah, from his father, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Shall I not inform you of the greatest of the major sins?" We said: "Yes, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "Associating partners with Allah, and disobedience to one's parents." He had been reclining, then he sat up and said: "Beware, and false testimony. Beware, and false speech." He kept repeating it until we said: "I wish he would be silent."[[Sahih al-Bukhari no. 5976 and Sahih Muslim no. 87.]]

Another hadith, which mentions the killing of a child. It is established in the two Sahihs, from 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, which sin is the greatest?" In another narration: "the greatest." He said: "That you set up a rival to Allah while He created you." I said: "Then which?" He said: "That you kill your child out of fear that it will eat with you." I said: "Then which?" He said: "That you commit adultery with your neighbour's wife." Then he recited: ﴿And those who do not invoke with Allah another god, nor kill the soul which Allah has forbidden except by right, nor commit unlawful sexual intercourse, and whoever does that will meet a penalty﴾ [up to] ﴿except one who repents﴾ [al-Furqan: 68].[[Sahih al-Bukhari no. 4477 and Sahih Muslim no. 68.]]

Another hadith, which mentions the drinking of wine. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Yunus ibn 'Abd al-A'la informed us, Ibn Wahb informed us, Abu Sakhr related to me: that a man told him, from 'Amrah ibn Hazm, that he heard 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As, while he was in al-Hijr in Makkah, being asked about wine. He said: "By Allah, it is a great matter with Allah that an old man like me should lie about the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in this place." He then went and asked him, then came back and said: "I asked him about wine, and he said: 'It is the greatest of the major sins and the mother of all indecencies. Whoever drinks wine abandons the prayer, has intercourse with his mother, his maternal aunt and his paternal aunt.'"[[Al-Tabarani narrated it through another chain, as in al-Majma' (5/68), and al-Haythami said: "'Attab, whom I do not know; and Ibn Lahi'ah's hadith is good but has weakness in it."]] It is gharib from this route.

Another route: The Hafiz Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh narrated it through the hadith of 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Muhammad al-Darawardi, from Dawud ibn Salih, from Salim ibn 'Abdullah, from his father: that Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him, and 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, and some companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), may Allah be pleased with them all, were sitting after the death of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and they mentioned the greatest of the major sins, but they did not have anything they could rely upon. So they sent me to 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As to ask him about that. He informed me that the greatest of the major sins is drinking wine. I came to them and informed them, and they denied it, so they rushed to him until they reached him at his house. He informed them that they had discussed in the presence of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that a king from the Children of Israel seized a man and gave him the choice between drinking wine, killing a soul, committing adultery, eating the flesh of a pig, or being killed. He chose drinking wine. When he drank it, he did not refrain from anything that they wanted from him. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to us in reply: "No one drinks wine without his prayer not being accepted for forty nights. If anyone dies with something of it in his bladder, Allah forbids Paradise to him. If he dies within forty nights, he dies the death of the Jahiliyyah (Age of Ignorance)."

This hadith is extremely gharib from this route. Dawud ibn Salih is al-Tammar al-Madani, client of the Ansar. Imam Ahmad said: "I see no harm in him." Ibn Hibban mentioned him in al-Thiqat (the Reliable Narrators), and I have not seen anyone criticise him.[[Al-Hakim narrated it in al-Mustadrak (4/147), and al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Awsat no. 138 (Majma' al-Bahrayn), both through the route of Sa'id ibn Abi Maryam from al-Darawardi.]]

Another hadith, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr, which mentions the oath of ghamus (perjury). Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far related to us, Shu'bah related to us, from Firas, from al-Sha'bi, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr, from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he said: "The greatest of the major sins are associating partners with Allah, disobedience to one's parents, or killing a soul (Shu'bah was unsure), and the ghamus oath." Al-Bukhari, al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i narrated it through the hadith of Shu'bah; al-Bukhari added Shaybān, both from Firas, with it.[[Al-Musnad (2/201), Sahih al-Bukhari no. 6675, Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 3021, and Sunan al-Nasa'i (8/63).]]

Another hadith, concerning the ghamus oath. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father related to us, Abu Salih the scribe of al-Layth related to us, al-Layth ibn Sa'd related to us, Hisham ibn Sa'd related to us, from Muhammad ibn Yazid ibn Muhajir ibn Qunfudh al-Taymi, from Abu Umamah al-Ansari, from 'Abdullah ibn Unays al-Juhani, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "The greatest of the major sins are associating partners with Allah, disobedience to one's parents, and the ghamus oath. No one swears by Allah a sabr oath (one forced upon a person's property) and in it inserts even the wing of a mosquito, except that it becomes a stain in his heart until the Day of Resurrection." Imam Ahmad narrated it in his Musnad in the same way, and 'Abd ibn Humayd in his Tafsir; both through Yunus ibn Muhammad al-Mu'addib, from al-Layth ibn Sa'd, with it. Al-Tirmidhi also narrated it in his Tafsir from 'Abd ibn Humayd, with it. Then he said: "This is a hasan gharib hadith. Abu Umamah al-Ansari is Ibn Tha'labah, and his name is not known." He narrated hadiths from the Prophet (ﷺ).[[Sunan al-Tirmidhi (302).]]

Our Shaykh, the Hafiz Abu al-Hajjaj al-Mizzi, said: It was also narrated by 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ishaq al-Madani, from Muhammad ibn Zayd, from 'Abdullah ibn Abi Umamah, from his father, from 'Abdullah ibn Unays. He added 'Abdullah ibn Abi Umamah.

I say: This is how it occurs in the Tafsir of Ibn Mardawayh and the Sahih of Ibn Hibban, through the route of 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ishaq,[[In R: "Isma'il."]] as our Shaykh mentioned. May Allah lengthen his life.[[Tuhfat al-Ashraf (4/275) no. 5147, and Sahih Ibn Hibban no. 1191 (Mawarid).]]

Another hadith, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr, concerning causing someone to revile one's parents. Ibn Abi Hatim said: 'Amr ibn 'Abdullah al-Awdi related to us, Waki' related to us, from Mis'ar and Sufyan, from Sa'd ibn Ibrahim, from Humayd ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr. Sufyan raised it to the Prophet (ﷺ), while Mis'ar stopped it at 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr. He said: "Among the major sins is that a man should revile his parents." They said: "How can a man revile his parents?" He said: "A man curses the father of another man, and he curses his father; and he curses his mother, and he curses his mother."[[Ahmad narrated it in his Musnad (2/164) through the route of Waki'.]]

It was also narrated by al-Bukhari, through Ahmad ibn Yunus, from Ibrahim ibn Sa'd ibn Ibrahim ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf, from his father, from his paternal uncle Humayd ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Among the greatest of the major sins is that a man curses his parents." They said: "How does a man curse his parents?" He said: "A man curses the father of another man, and he curses his father; and he curses his mother, and he curses his mother."

Muslim narrated it likewise through the hadiths of Sufyan, Shu'bah and Yazid ibn al-Had, all three from Sa'd ibn Ibrahim, with it raised to the Prophet, with similar wording. Al-Tirmidhi said: "Sahih."[[Sahih al-Bukhari no. 5973, Sahih Muslim no. 90, and Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 1902.]]

It is established in the Sahih from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that he said: "Insulting a Muslim is wickedness (fusuq), and fighting him is disbelief (kufr)."[[Narrated by al-Bukhari no. 48 and Muslim no. 64, from 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him.]]

Another hadith on this: Ibn Abi Hatim said: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ibrahim Duhaym related to us, 'Amr ibn Abi Salamah related to us, Zuhayr ibn Muhammad related to us, from al-'Ala' ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Among the greatest of the major sins is violating a Muslim man's honour, and the two revilers (who abuse each other) are at fault, and the one who begins the abuse."[[Mentioned by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur.]]

This is how this hadith has been narrated. Abu Dawud also recorded it in the Book of Adab of his Sunan, from Ja'far ibn Musafir, from 'Amr ibn Abi Salamah, from Zuhayr ibn Muhammad, from al-'Ala', from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Among the greatest of the major sins is a man's taking liberties with the honour of a Muslim man without right, and among the major sins are the two revilers, who are at fault, with the one who begins the abuse."

Ibn Mardawayh likewise narrated it through the route of 'Abdullah ibn al-'Ala' ibn Zabr, from al-'Ala', from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), mentioning the like of it.[[Sunan Abi Dawud no. 4877.]]

Another hadith, concerning combining the two prayers without an excuse. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father related to us, Nu'aym ibn Hammad related to us, Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman related to us, from his father, from Hanash,[[In J: "Hubaysh," and in A: "Hunaysh."]] from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Whoever combines the two prayers without an excuse has committed one of the gates of the major sins." Abu 'Isa al-Tirmidhi also narrated it likewise from Abu Salamah Yahya ibn Khalaf, from al-Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman, with it. Then he said: "Hanash is Abu 'Ali al-Rahabi, and he is Husayn ibn Qays, and he is weak according to the people of hadith; Ahmad and others declared him weak."[[Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 188.]]

Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated: al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn al-Sabbah related to us, Isma'il ibn 'Ulayyah related to us, from Khalid al-Hadhdha', from Humayd ibn Hilal, from Abu Qatadah (meaning al-'Adawi), who said: "The letter of 'Umar was read to us: 'Among the major sins are combining the two prayers (meaning without an excuse), fleeing from the battle line, and plundering.'"

This is a sound chain of narration. The point is that if the threat applies to one who combines two prayers, such as Zuhr with 'Asr, whether early or late, and likewise Maghrib with 'Isha', which is permitted only for a legitimate reason (sabab shar'i), then one who does so without any of those reasons commits a major sin (kabirah). So what do you think of one who abandons prayer altogether? For this reason Muslim related in his Sahih from the Messenger of God (ﷺ) that he said: "Between a servant and polytheism (shirk) is the abandonment of prayer" [[Sahih Muslim, no. (82), from the hadith of Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah (may God be pleased with him).]]. In the Sunan, from him, peace be upon him, that he said: "The covenant between us and them is prayer; whoever abandons it has disbelieved" [[Related by al-Tirmidhi in the Sunan, no. (2621), al-Nasa'i in the Sunan (1/231), and Ibn Majah in the Sunan, no. (1079), from the hadith of Buraydah ibn al-Husayb (may God be pleased with him).]]. He also said: "Whoever abandons the 'Asr prayer, his deeds have been nullified" [[Related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. (553), and al-Nasa'i in the Sunan (1/236), from the hadith of Buraydah ibn al-Husayb (may God be pleased with him).]]. And he said: "Whoever misses the 'Asr prayer is as if he has lost his family and his wealth" [[Related by al-Nasa'i (1/238), from the hadith of Nawfal ibn Mu'awiyah (may God be pleased with him).]].

Another hadith: it contains despair of God's mercy (ya's min rawh Allah) and feeling safe from God's plan (amn min makr Allah). Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn 'Amr ibn Abi 'Asim al-Nabil related to us, my father related to us, Shabib ibn Bishr related to us, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas: that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) was reclining when a man entered upon him and said: "What are the major sins?" He said: "Associating partners with God (al-shirk billah), despair of God's mercy, despairing of God's compassion (al-qunut min rahmat Allah), and feeling safe from God's plan (al-amn min makr Allah). This is the greatest of the major sins."

Al-Bazzar related it from 'Abd Allah ibn Ishaq al-'Attar, from Abu 'Asim al-Nabil, from Shabib ibn Bishr, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas: that a man said: "O Messenger of God, what are the major sins?" He said: "Associating partners with God (al-ishrak billah) [[In d: "al-shirk".]], despair of the mercy of God (ya's min rawh Allah), and despairing of the compassion of God, the Mighty and Majestic (al-qunut min rahmat Allah 'azza wa jall)."

In its chain there is some doubt, and it is more likely to be a statement of Ibn 'Abbas (mawquf), for similar has been reported from Ibn Mas'ud [[Musnad al-Bazzar, no. (106), Kashf al-Astar; al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (1/104): "Its narrators are trustworthy."]]. Ibn Jarir said:

Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim related to me, Hushaym related to us, Mutarrif informed us, from Wabrah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from Abu al-Tufayl, who said: Ibn Mas'ud said: "The greatest of the major sins are associating partners with God, despair (al-iyas) [[In j, r, d, a: "al-yas".]] of God's mercy, despairing of God's compassion, and feeling safe from God's plan."
