He also said: Ahmad ibn Hazim narrated to us: Abu Nu'aym informed us: 'Abd Allah ibn Ma'dan narrated to us, from Abu al-Walid, who said: "I asked Ibn 'Abbas about the major sins, and he said: They are everything in which Allah is disobeyed, so it is a major sin." [In ج: "qala" (said).]

Views of the Successors (al-tabi'un):
Ibn Jarir said: Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me: Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, from Ibn 'Awn, from Muhammad, who said: "I asked 'Ubaydah about the major sins, and he said: Associating partners with Allah, killing a soul which Allah has forbidden without right, fleeing on the day of battle, consuming the property of an orphan unjustly, consuming usury, and slander (al-buhtan)." He said: "And they say: a Bedouin matter after the emigration." Ibn 'Awn said: "I said to Muhammad: And sorcery? He said: Slander gathers great evil."

Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn 'Ubayd al-Muharibi narrated to me: Abu al-Ahwas Sallam ibn Sulaym narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from 'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr, who said: "The major sins are seven; there is not one among them except that there is a verse of the Book of Allah concerning it. Association with Allah is among them: ﴿Whoever associates with Allah, it is as if he had fallen from the sky and the birds snatched him away or the wind hurled him into a faraway place﴾ [al-Hajj: 31]; and ﴿Those who unjustly consume the property of orphans only consume fire into their bellies﴾ [al-Nisa': 10]; ﴿Those who consume usury will not stand except as one stands whom Satan has driven mad by touch﴾ [al-Baqarah: 275]; and ﴿Indeed those who accuse chaste, unwary, believing women﴾ [al-Nur: 23]; and fleeing from battle: ﴿O you who believe, when you meet those who disbelieve advancing, do not turn your backs to them﴾ [al-Anfal: 15]; and apostasy (al-ta'arrub) after emigration: ﴿Indeed those who turned back on their heels after guidance had become clear to them﴾ [Muhammad: 25]; and killing a believer: ﴿Whoever deliberately kills a believer, his recompense is Hell, abiding therein﴾, the verse [al-Nisa': 93]."

Ibn Abi Hatim likewise narrated it from the hadith of Abu Ishaq, from 'Ubayd, in similar wording.

Ibn Jarir said: Al-Muthanna narrated to us: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from 'Ata' (i.e., Ibn Abi Rabah), who said: "The major sins are seven: killing a soul, consuming usury, consuming the property of an orphan, accusing a chaste woman, bearing false witness, disobeying one's parents, and fleeing from battle."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur'ah narrated to us: 'Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Jarir narrated to us, from Mughirah, who said: "It used to be said that insulting Abu Bakr and 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, is among the major sins."

I say: A group of scholars has gone to the view of declaring disbelief (takfir) for whoever reviles the Companions, and this is a narration from Malik ibn Anas, may Allah have mercy on him. Muhammad ibn Sirin said: "I do not think anyone who disparages Abu Bakr and 'Umar, while loving the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), exists." Narrated by al-Tirmidhi.

Ibn Abi Hatim also said: Yunus narrated to us: Ibn Wahb informed us: 'Abd Allah ibn 'Ayyash informed me, who said: Zayd ibn Aslam, concerning the saying of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿If you avoid the major sins you are forbidden﴾, said: "Among the major sins are: association with Allah, disbelief in the signs of Allah and His Messenger, sorcery, killing children, one who attributes to Allah a son or a consort, and similar deeds, and a statement with which no deed is sound. As for every sin with which religion remains sound and with which a deed is accepted, Allah forgives misdeeds by good deeds."

Ibn Jarir said: Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us: Yazid narrated to us: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning ﴿If you avoid the major sins you are forbidden﴾, the verse: "Allah only promised forgiveness to one who avoids the major sins. It has been mentioned to us that the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Avoid the major sins, be upright, and receive good tidings.'"

Ibn Mardawayh has related, by several routes from Anas, and from Jabir, traced to the Prophet (ﷺ): "My intercession is for the people of major sins from among my community." [Regarding the hadith of Anas, it has several routes, among them: what Abu Bakr ibn 'Ayyash narrates from Humayd, from Anas. Ibn Abi 'Asim recorded it in al-Sunnah, no. 831. And what he narrates from Ibn al-Mubarak, from 'Asim al-Ahwal, from Anas, which al-Tabarani narrated in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (1/258) and Ibn Abi Hatim in al-'Ilal (2/222), and he said: I heard my father and Abu Zur'ah say: This is a munkar hadith. And what Ja'far ibn Sulaym al-Di'bi narrates from Malik ibn Dinar, from Anas, which Ibn Abi Hatim narrated in al-'Ilal (2/79), and he said: I heard my father say: This is a munkar hadith. And what Bastan ibn Huraith al-Sadafi narrates from Ash'ath, from Anas, which al-Qada'i narrated in Musnad al-Shihab, no. 237. And what Abu Janab narrates, having heard Ziyad al-Numayri, having heard Anas, which al-Qada'i narrated in Musnad al-Shihab (237). As for the hadith of Jabir, Ibn Majah narrated it in his Sunan, no. 4310, by the route of Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Jabir.]

However, in its chain, in all its routes, there is weakness, except what 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated: Ma'mar informed us, from Thabit, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "My intercession is for the people of major sins from among my community." This is a sound chain (isnad) on the condition of the two Shaykhs [in د: "on their two conditions"; in ر: "on the condition of the Shaykhayn"]. Abu 'Isa al-Tirmidhi narrated it alone by this route, from 'Abbas al-'Anbari, from 'Abd al-Razzaq, then said: "This is a hasan sahih hadith." [Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 2435.] In the Sahih there is a witness to its meaning: his saying (ﷺ), after mentioning intercession: "Do you think it is for the believers who are God-fearing? No, but it is for the sinners who are defiled."

The scholars of the principles (usul) and the branches (furu') of jurisprudence have differed on the definition of the major sin (kabirah). Some say: It is what carries a prescribed legal penalty (hadd) in the Shari'ah. Among them are those who say: It is what has a specific threat (wa'id) in the Qur'an and the Sunnah. And it has been said otherwise.

Abu al-Qasim 'Abd al-Karim ibn Muhammad al-Rafi'i said, in his famous book al-Sharh al-Kabir, in its chapter on testimonies: "Then the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them [ta'ala — addition from ج], and those after them differed concerning the major sins, and in distinguishing them from minor sins. And some of the companions [of al-Shafi'i] have several views in defining the major sin:

First: It is the disobedience which requires a legal penalty (hadd).

Second: It is the disobedience for which its doer incurs a severe threat by explicit text of the Book or the Sunnah. This is what is most found in their statements, and it is [in ج, أ: "they"] the first I incline to, but the second is more in agreement with what they mentioned when detailing the major sins.

Third: Imam al-Haramayn said in al-Irshad and elsewhere: Every offence that indicates little concern of its perpetrator for religion and weakness of piety is what nullifies justice ('adalah).

Fourth: Al-Qadi Abu Sa'id [in ج، ر: "Abu Sa'd"] al-Harawi mentioned that the major sin is: every act whose prohibition the Book has explicitly stated, every disobedience which in its kind requires a legal penalty such as execution or other, abandoning every obligatory duty that must be performed immediately, and lying in testimony, narration, and oath."

This is what he mentioned as a summary (dabt).

Then he said: Al-Qadi al-Ruyani made a detailed list and said: The major sins (al-kaba'ir) are seven: killing a soul without right, adultery (al-zina), sodomy (al-liwat), drinking wine, theft, seizing property unlawfully (ghasb), and false accusation of unchastity (al-qadhf). In "al-Shamil" he added to the seven mentioned: false testimony (shahadat al-zur). Sahib al-'Uddah added to them: consuming usury (riba), breaking the fast of Ramadan without excuse, the false oath (al-yamin al-fajira), severing the ties of kinship (qat' al-rahm), disobedience to parents ('uquq al-walidayn), fleeing from the battlefield (al-firar min al-zahf), consuming the property of an orphan, cheating in measure and weight, performing the prayer before its time or delaying it beyond its time without excuse, striking a Muslim without right, lying about the Prophet (ﷺ) deliberately, reviling his Companions, concealing testimony without excuse, taking bribes, procuring between men and women, informing on people to the ruler (al-si'ayah 'inda al-sultan), withholding zakat, abandoning enjoining good and forbidding evil when able, forgetting the Qur'an after having learned it, burning animals with fire, a woman refusing her husband without reason, despairing of the mercy of Allah, and feeling secure from the plan of Allah. It is also said: slandering the people of knowledge and the bearers of the Qur'an. Among what is counted as major sins: zihar, and eating the flesh of swine and carrion except in necessity.

Then al-Rafi'i said: There is room for hesitation regarding some of these traits.

I say: People have composed works on the major sins, among them what our shaykh, the hafiz Abu 'Abd Allah al-Dhahabi (it was published in Beirut, edited by the teacher Muhyi al-Din Mustu), compiled, which reached about seventy major sins. If the major sin is defined as that for which the Lawgiver specifically threatened the Fire, as Ibn 'Abbas and others said, and one traces this, a great deal is gathered. If it is said: everything Allah has forbidden, then it is very numerous indeed. And Allah knows best.

Imam Ahmad said: Sufyan narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: Umm Salamah said: "O Messenger of Allah, men go out to fight and we do not fight, and we have half the inheritance." Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿And do not wish for that by which Allah has made some of you exceed others.﴾

Al-Tirmidhi narrated it from Ibn Abi Umar, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, from Umm Salamah that she said: "I said: 'O Messenger of Allah...'" and he mentioned it [the hadith], and said: "Gharib" [[Al-Musnad (6/322) and Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3022).]]. Some narrators related it from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, that Umm Salamah said...

Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Hakim in his Mustadrak related, from the hadith of al-Thawri, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: Umm Salamah said: "O Messenger of Allah, we do not fight so that we may be martyred, and we do not get a share of the inheritance!" So this was revealed: ﴿And do not wish for that by which Allah has made some of you exceed others. For men is a share of what they have earned, and for women is a share of what they have earned.﴾ Then this was revealed: ﴿Indeed, I will not allow to be lost the work of any worker among you, whether male or female.﴾ [[Tafsir al-Tabari (8/262) and al-Mustadrak (2/305).]] [Ali 'Imran: 195].

Then Ibn Abi Hatim said: Likewise Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah narrated, meaning from Ibn Abi Najih, with this wording. Yahya al-Qattan and Waki' ibn al-Jarrah narrated, from al-Thawri, and from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, from Umm Salamah, who said: "I said: 'O Messenger of Allah...'" It is also narrated from Muqatil ibn Hayyan and Khusayf something similar.

Ibn Jarir narrated, from the hadith of Ibn Jurayj, from 'Ikrimah and Mujahid, that both of them said: It was revealed concerning Umm Salamah.

'Abd al-Razzaq said: Ma'mar informed us, from a shaykh from the people of Makkah, who said: This verse was revealed concerning the saying of women: "Would that we were men, so that we could strive as they strive and fight in the way of Allah, Mighty and Majestic."

Ibn Abi Hatim also said: Ahmad ibn al-Qasim ibn 'Atiyyah narrated to us, Ahmad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to me, my father narrated to me, al-Ash'ath ibn Ishaq narrated to us, from Ja'far, meaning Ibn Abi al-Mughirah, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His saying [[Addition from w.]] ﴿And do not wish for that by which Allah has made some of you exceed others. For men is a share of what they have earned, and for women is a share of what they have earned.﴾ He said: A woman came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: "O Prophet of Allah, the male has the share of two females, and the testimony of two women equals that of one man, so are we in deeds likewise? If a woman does a good deed, only half a good deed is written for her." So Allah revealed this verse: ﴿And do not wish﴾, for it is a just decision from Me, and I am the One who made it.

Al-Suddi said concerning His saying in the verse ﴿And do not wish for that by which Allah has made some of you exceed others﴾: men said: "We want to have double the reward of women, just as we have two shares in the inheritance." And women said: "We want to have a reward like the reward of the male martyrs, for we cannot fight; and if fighting had been prescribed for us, we would have fought." But Allah rejected that, and said to them: "Ask Me of My bounty." He said: "Not of the goods of this world."

Something similar has been narrated from Qatadah. 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His saying ﴿And do not wish for that by which Allah has made some of you exceed others﴾: a man should not wish, saying: "Would that I had the wealth of so-and-so and his family!" Allah forbade that, but rather he should ask Allah of His bounty.

Likewise Muhammad ibn Sirin, al-Hasan, al-Dahhak and 'Ata' said something similar to this, and this is the apparent meaning of the verse. This is not contradicted by what is established in the Sahih: "There is no envy except in two: a man whom Allah has given wealth and has empowered him to spend it in the truth, and a man who says: 'If only I had what so-and-so has, I would do as he does.' The two are equal in reward." [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (5026).]] For this is something other than what the verse forbids, since the hadith encourages wishing for the like of this one's blessing, whereas the verse forbids wishing for the very blessing of this one. Allah said: ﴿And do not wish for that by which Allah has made some of you exceed others﴾, meaning in worldly matters, and likewise in religious matters as well, on the basis of the hadith of Umm Salamah and Ibn 'Abbas. Thus 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah said: It was revealed concerning the prohibition of wishing for what belongs to so-and-so, and concerning women wishing that they were men so that they could go out to fight. Narrated by Ibn Jarir.

Then He said: ﴿For men is a share of what they have earned, and for women is a share of what they have earned.﴾ That is, each has a recompense for his deed according to its measure: if good, then good; if evil, then evil. This is the view of Ibn Jarir.

It was also said: the meaning of this is in inheritance, that is, each inherits according to his share. Al-Tirmidhi narrated it from Ibn 'Abbas.

Then He guided them to what would benefit them, saying: ﴿And ask Allah of His bounty﴾, meaning: do not wish for what some of you have been favoured with over others, for this is a decreed matter, and wishing achieves nothing; rather, ask Me of My bounty and I will give you, for I am Generous and Bestower.

Al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Mardawayh narrated, from the hadith of Hammad ibn Waqid: I heard Isra'il, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu al-Ahwas, from 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Ask Allah of His bounty, for Allah loves to be asked, and the best of worship is waiting for relief."

Then al-Tirmidhi said: Thus Hammad ibn Waqid narrated it, and he is not a reliable memorizer (laysa bil-hafiz). Abu Nu'aym narrated it from Isra'il, from Hakim ibn Jubayr, from a man, from the Prophet ﷺ, and the hadith of Abu Nu'aym is more likely to be sound [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3571).]].

Likewise Ibn Mardawayh narrated it from the hadith of Waki', from Isra'il. Then he narrated it from the hadith of Qays ibn al-Rabi', from Hakim ibn Jubayr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah said: "Ask Allah of His bounty, for Allah loves to be asked, and the most beloved of His servants to Him is the one who loves relief" [[Its chain contains Hakim ibn Jubayr, who is weak; al-Jawzajani accused him of lying, but that was due to his Shi'ism.]].

Then He said: ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever, of all things, Knowing.﴾ That is, He knows who deserves the world and gives him of it, and who deserves poverty and makes him poor; He knows who deserves the Hereafter and enables him to do its deeds, and who deserves abandonment and leaves him from pursuing goodness and its means. For this reason He said: ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever, of all things, Knowing.﴾

Ibn ʿAbbas, Mujahid, Saʿid ibn Jubayr, Abu Salih, Qatadah, Zayd ibn Aslam, al-Suddi, al-Dahhak, Muqatil ibn Hayyan, and others said regarding His words, ﴿And for each We have appointed heirs (mawali)﴾, that it means: heirs (warathah). And it is reported from Ibn ʿAbbas in another narration: it means ʿasabah (agnatic relatives). Ibn Jarir said: The Arabs call a paternal cousin a mawla, as al-Fadl ibn ʿAbbas said:

"Gently, sons of our paternal uncles, gently, our mawali;
do not reveal to us what had been buried."

[[The verse is in Tafsir al-Tabari (8/270) and in Lisan al-ʿArab, root (w-l-y).]]

He said: By His words, ﴿from what the parents and the relatives leave﴾, He means from the estate of their parents and close relatives as inheritance. So the meaning of the statement is: And for each of you, O people, We have appointed ʿasabah who inherit from what his parents and relatives leave of their inheritance for him.

* *

As for His words, ﴿And those with whom your oaths have bound you [[The Kufans read ʿaqadat without the alif, with a light pronunciation; Hamzah doubled the qaf; the rest read ʿaqadat with an alif. Taken from the margin of the edition of Shuʿab al-Iman.]] — give them their share﴾, meaning: those with whom you made firm covenants by solemn oaths, you and they, then give them their share of the inheritance, as you promised them in the binding oaths. Indeed Allah is a witness over you in those covenants and agreements. This was at the beginning of Islam; then it was abrogated (nuskhah) afterwards, and they were commanded to fulfill their pacts with those with whom they had contracted, and not to make a new contract after the revelation of this verse.

al-Bukhari said: Al-Salt ibn Muhammad related to us, Abu Usamah related to us, from Idris, from Talhah ibn Musarrif, from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbas: ﴿And for each We have appointed mawali﴾ — he said: heirs (warathah). ﴿And those with whom your oaths have bound you﴾: When the Emigrants came to Madinah, the Emigrant would inherit from the Helper, to the exclusion of his blood relatives, because of the brotherhood which the Prophet (ﷺ) had established between them. Then when ﴿And for each We have appointed mawali﴾ was revealed, it abrogated this. Then He said: ﴿And those with whom your oaths have bound you — give them their share﴾ of support, assistance, and counsel, and inheritance has gone, but a bequest may be made to them.

Then al-Bukhari said: Abu Usamah heard from Idris, and Idris heard from Talhah.
[[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4580).]]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Saʿid al-Ashajj related to us, Abu Usamah related to us, Idris al-Awdi related to us, Talhah ibn Musarrif informed me, from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbas concerning His words: ﴿And those with whom your oaths have bound you [then give them their share]﴾ [[Addition from A.]] — the verse. He said: When the Emigrants came to Madinah, the Emigrant would inherit from the Helper, to the exclusion of his blood relatives, by the brotherhood which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had established between them. Then when this verse was revealed: ﴿And for each We have appointed mawali from what the parents and the relatives leave﴾, it was abrogated. Then he said: ﴿And those with whom your oaths have bound you — give them their share﴾.

And al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn al-Sabbah related to us, Hajjaj related to us, from Ibn Jurayj — and Uthman ibn ʿAta, from ʿAta, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: ﴿And those with whom your oaths have bound you — give them their share﴾. Before Islam a man would make a covenant with another man, saying: "You inherit from me and I inherit from you." And tribes would make alliances with one another. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Every alliance that existed in the Jahiliyyah, which Islam encountered, Islam only increases it in strength; and there is no covenant or alliance in Islam." So this verse abrogated it: ﴿And blood relatives are more entitled to one another in the Book of Allah﴾ [al-Anfal: 75].

Then he said: It is related from Saʿid ibn al-Musayyib, Mujahid, ʿAta, al-Hasan, Saʿid ibn Jubayr, Abu Salih, al-Shaʿbi, Sulayman ibn Yasar, ʿIkrimah, al-Suddi, al-Dahhak, Qatadah, and Muqatil ibn Hayyan that they said: They are the allies (hulafa).

Imam Ahmad said: ʿAffan related to us, Shurayk related to us, from Simak, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who raised it (to the Prophet ﷺ), saying: "Whatever alliance there was in the Jahiliyyah, Islam only increased it in vehemence and strength." [[al-Musnad (1/329).]]

Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb related to us, Waki related to us, from Shurayk, from Simak, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said — and Abu Kurayb related to us, Musʿab ibn al-Miqdam related to us, from Israʾil, from Yunus, from Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman, mawla of the family of Talhah, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "There is no alliance in Islam, and every alliance that was in the Jahiliyyah, Islam only increased in strength. And it would not please me to have the best of red camels, while I had broken the alliance that was in Dar al-Nadwah." This is the wording of Ibn Jarir. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (8/282).]]

Ibn Jarir also said: Yaʿqub ibn Ibrahim related to us, Ibn ʿUlayyah related to us, from ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Ishaq, from al-Zuhri, from Muhammad ibn Jubayr ibn Mutʿim, from his father, from ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn ʿAwf, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I witnessed the alliance of al-Mutayyibin when I was a boy with my paternal uncles, and I would not love to have the best of red camels in exchange for breaking it." Al-Zuhri said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Islam has not encountered any alliance except that it increased it in strength." And he said: "There is no alliance in Islam." And the Prophet (ﷺ) had brought together the Quraysh and the Helpers. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (8/286) and al-Musnad (1/190).]]

Similarly, Imam Ahmad narrated it from Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal, from ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Ishaq, from al-Zuhri, in full. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (8/286) and al-Musnad (1/190).]]

Yaʿqub ibn Ibrahim related to me, Hushaym related to us, Mughirah informed me, from his father, from Shuʿbah ibn al-Tawam, from Qays ibn ʿAsim, that he asked the Prophet (ﷺ) about alliance, and he said: "Whatever alliance there was in the Jahiliyyah, hold fast to it; and there is no alliance in Islam."

Likewise Ahmad narrated it from Hushaym. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (8/283) and al-Musnad (5/61).]]

Abu Kurayb related to us, Waki related to us, from Dawud ibn Abi ʿAbd Allah, from Ibn Judʿan, from his grandmother, from Umm Salamah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "There is no alliance in Islam, and whatever alliance there was in the Jahiliyyah, Islam only increased it in strength." [[Tafsir al-Tabari (8/283).]]

Abu Kurayb related to us, Yunus ibn Bukayr related to us, Muhammad ibn Ishaq related to us, from ʿAmr ibn Shuʿayb, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: When the Prophet (ﷺ) was in Makkah in the year of the Conquest, he stood up to address the people and said: "O people, whatever alliance there was in the Jahiliyyah, Islam only increased it in strength, and there is no alliance in Islam."

Then he narrated it from the hadith of Husayn al-Muʿallim and ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn al-Harith, from ʿAmr ibn Shuʿayb, with the same. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (8/284).]]

Imam Ahmad said: ʿAbd Allah ibn Muhammad related to us, Ibn Numayr and Abu Usamah related to us, from Zakariyya, from Saʿd ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Jubayr ibn Mutʿim, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "There is no alliance in Islam, and whichever alliance there was in the Jahiliyyah, Islam only increased it in strength."

Likewise Muslim narrated it from ʿAbd Allah ibn Muhammad, who is Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, with its chain, the same. Abu Dawud narrated it from ʿUthman, from Muhammad ibn Abi Shaybah, from Muhammad ibn Bishr, Ibn Numayr and Abu Usamah, all three from Zakariyya, who is Ibn Abi Zaʾidah, with its chain, the same.

Ibn Jarir narrated it from the hadith of Muhammad ibn Bishr, with its chain. Al-Nasaʾi narrated it from the hadith of Ishaq ibn Yusuf al-Azraq, from Zakariyya, from Saʿd ibn Ibrahim, from Nafiʿ ibn Jubayr ibn Mutʿim, from his father, with its chain. [[al-Musnad (4/83), Sahih Muslim no. (2530), Sunan Abi Dawud no. (2925), Tafsir al-Tabari (8/285), and al-Sunan al-Kubra of al-Nasaʾi no. (6418).]]

Imam Ahmad said: Hushaym related to us, he said: Mughirah informed me, from his father, from Shuʿbah ibn al-Tawam, from Qays ibn ʿAsim: that he asked the Prophet (ﷺ) about alliance, and he said: "Whatever alliance there was in the Jahiliyyah, hold fast to it; and there is no alliance in Islam."

Likewise Shuʿbah narrated it from Mughirah, who is Ibn Miqsam, from his father, with the same.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said, from Dawud ibn al-Husayn, who said: I was reading to Umm Saʿd bint al-Rabiʿ, along with her grandson Musa ibn Saʿd — and she was an orphan in the care of Abu Bakr — and I read to her: ﴿And those whom your oaths have bound﴾, and she said: No, rather: ﴿And those with whom your oaths have bound you﴾. She said: It was only revealed concerning Abu Bakr and his son ʿAbd al-Rahman, when he refused to embrace Islam, and Abu Bakr swore that he would not give him an inheritance. Then when he embraced Islam, when he was forced to accept Islam at sword-point, Allah commanded that his share be given to him.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it, but this is a strange statement. The correct view is the first: that this was at the beginning of Islam, when they inherited by alliance; then it was abrogated, though the effect of the alliance remained after that, and they were commanded to fulfill the contracts and covenants. The alliance they had made before that was addressed in the hadith of Jubayr ibn Mutʿim and other Companions: "There is no alliance in Islam, and whatever alliance there was in the Jahiliyyah, Islam only increased it in strength."

This is an explicit text refuting those who hold that inheritance by alliance is valid today, as is the view of Abu Hanifah and his companions, and a narration from Ahmad ibn Hanbal, may Allah have mercy on them.

The correct view is that of the majority, and of Malik, al-Shafiʿi, and Ahmad according to his well-known position. For this reason He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And for each We have appointed heirs (mawali) from what the parents and the relatives leave﴾, meaning: heirs from among his kin, from his parents and close relatives, and they inherit him to the exclusion of all other people, as is established in the two Sahihs from Ibn ʿAbbas, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Give the fixed shares to their people; what remains then belongs to the nearest male." [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (6735) and Sahih Muslim no. (1615).]] That is: divide the inheritance among the people of the fixed shares whom Allah mentioned in the two verses on inheritance; then what remains after that, give it to the ʿasabah. As for His words: ﴿And those with whom your oaths have bound you﴾, meaning before the revelation of this verse, ﴿give them their share﴾, that is, of the inheritance. Whatever alliance is made after that has no effect.

It has been said that this verse abrogated the alliance for the future and also the ruling for the past, so there is no inheritance through it, as Ibn Abi Hatim said.

Abu Saʿid al-Ashajj related to us, Abu Usamah related to us, Idris al-Awdi related to us, Talhah ibn Musarrif informed me, from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbas: ﴿Then give them their share﴾ — he said: from support, counsel, and assistance, and a bequest may be made to them, though the inheritance has gone.

Ibn Jarir narrated it from Abu Kurayb, from Abu Usamah. Similarly it is related from Mujahid and Abu Malik, something similar.

ʿAli ibn Abi Talhah said, from Ibn ʿAbbas, concerning His words: ﴿And those with whom your oaths have bound you﴾: He said: A man would make a covenant with another man, that whichever of them died, the other would inherit from him. Then Allah revealed: ﴿And blood relatives are more entitled to one another in the Book of Allah than the believers and the Emigrants, except that you do kindness to your allies﴾ [al-Ahzab: 6]. He means: except that they bequeath to their allies with whom they made the covenant a bequest, which is permissible for them from one-third of the estate of the deceased, and that is the kindness.

This is the explicit statement of more than one of the early scholars: that it was abrogated by His words: ﴿And blood relatives are more entitled to one another in the Book of Allah than the believers and the Emigrants, except that you do kindness to your allies﴾.

Saʿid ibn Jubayr said: ﴿Then give them their share﴾, meaning: of the inheritance. He said: Abu Bakr made a covenant with a mawla, and he inherited from him. Ibn Jarir narrated it.

And al-Zuhri said, on the authority of Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab: This verse was revealed concerning those who used to adopt men who were not their sons, and would make them their heirs. So Allah revealed concerning them, and gave them a share in the bequest, and returned the inheritance to the mawali (clients) among the near kin and the 'asabah (male agnatic relatives). Allah refused inheritance to those who claimed [kinship with] and adopted those who were claimed, but He gave them a share of the bequest. Narrated by Ibn Jarir (al-Tabari).

Ibn Jarir (al-Tabari) chose that the meaning of His words ﴿So give them their share﴾ is: from support, sincere counsel and assistance, not that the meaning is "give them their share of the inheritance" so that the verse would be abrogated (mansukhah), nor that this was a ruling which was later abrogated. Rather, the verse only indicates fulfilling the covenant of alliance concluded for support and sincere counsel alone, so it is muhkamah (decisive) and not mansukhah (abrogated).

But what he said is open to scrutiny, for among alliances some were for mutual support and assistance, and some were for inheritance, as many of the early scholars have related, and as Ibn 'Abbas said: "The Muhajir used to inherit from the Ansari to the exclusion of his relatives and kin, until that was abrogated." So how can he say that this verse is muhkamah and not abrogated?! And Allah knows best.

[Shaykh Ahmad Shakir, may Allah have mercy on him, said in his commentary on the Tafsir of al-Tabari (8/288): "Ibn Kathir found this passage of al-Tabari's words problematic, so he related it from him and then said: 'But what he said is open to scrutiny, for among alliances some were for mutual support and assistance, and some were for inheritance, as many of the early scholars have related, and as Ibn 'Abbas said: The Muhajir used to inherit from the Ansari to the exclusion of his relatives and kin, until that was abrogated. So how can he say that this verse is muhkamah and not abrogated? And Allah knows best.'

What Ibn Kathir marvelled at has been explained by al-Tabari, who built his whole school upon it, in every case of abrogating and abrogated (verses). He repeated it many times in his tafsir, and he restated it here when mentioning the abrogating and abrogated, saying: 'When there is disagreement about whether a verse's ruling is abrogated or not, and the disputants differ over its ruling, then denying abrogation from it and affirming that it is muhkamah is a sound position. No one may rule that its ruling is abrogated except with a proof that must be accepted. Abu Ja'far has repeatedly made clear that the proof that must be accepted is: the apparent meaning of the Qur'an, and the sound report from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). As for the interpretation of Ibn 'Abbas or other imams, it is not a proof for establishing abrogation in a verse, since interpreting it as muhkamah is a sound position.'

So it is strange of Ibn Kathir that he marvelled at Abu Ja'far's interpretation and explanation. Had he been fair, he would have refuted al-Tabari's argument in his position on abrogating and abrogated, rather than objecting to him and marvelling at him with a proof that al-Tabari himself has already refuted, which he elaborated on repeatedly in this book and in his other works, as he said. May Allah have mercy on Abu Ja'far, and forgive Ibn Kathir.']

Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿Men are the protectors and maintainers of women﴾, meaning: the man is the qawwam (protector and maintainer) over the woman, that is, he is her leader, her chief, the one who judges over her, and her disciplinarian if she goes astray, ﴿because Allah has made some of them to excel over others﴾, meaning: because men are superior to women, and the man is better than the woman. For this reason prophethood is restricted to men, and so is the greatest rule (al-mulk al-a'zam), due to His ﷺ saying: "A people will never prosper who entrust their affairs to a woman." It was related by al-Bukhari from the hadith of 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakrah, from his father. [[Related by al-Bukhari under nos. (4425), (7099), through the route of al-Hasan al-Basri from Abu Bakrah.]] Likewise the office of judgeship and other things.

﴿And because they spend of their wealth﴾, meaning: from the dower-payments, the maintenance and the obligations which Allah has imposed upon them towards women in His Book and the Sunnah of His Prophet ﷺ. So the man is superior to the woman in himself, and he has the excellence over her and the bestowal of benefits, so it is fitting that he should be her qawwam, as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And the men have a degree over them﴾ [al-Baqarah: 228].

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah related from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿Men are the protectors and maintainers of women﴾ means: they are rulers over them, meaning she obeys him in what he commands her of obedience to him; and his obedience is that she be good to his family and guard his property. Likewise said Muqatil, al-Suddi and al-Dahhak.

Al-Hasan al-Basri said: A woman came to the Prophet ﷺ seeking his intervention against her husband, that he had slapped her. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Retaliation (al-qisas)." Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿Men are the protectors and maintainers of women﴾ to the end of the verse, so she returned without retaliation.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim related it through various routes from him. Likewise Qatadah, Ibn Jurayj and al-Suddi related this report with a broken chain (mursal); Ibn Jarir included all of it. Ibn Mardawayh traced it through another route, saying:

Ahmad ibn 'Ali al-Nasa'i related to us, Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Hashimi related to us, Muhammad ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ath related to us, Musa ibn Isma'il ibn Musa ibn Ja'far ibn Muhammad related to us, my father related to me, from my grandfather, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from 'Ali who said: A man of the Ansar came to the Prophet with his wife. She said: "O Messenger of Allah, her husband so-and-so son of so-and-so al-Ansari, has struck her and it left a mark on her face." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "That is not for him." Then Allah revealed: ﴿Men are the protectors and maintainers of women [because Allah has made some of them to excel over others]﴾, meaning: they are qawwamun over women in discipline. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I desired a matter and Allah desired something else." [[In its chain is Muhammad ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ath. Ibn 'Adi said: "I wrote from him in Egypt. His extreme Shi'ism led him to bring us a copy of nearly a thousand hadiths from Musa ibn Isma'il ibn Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his grandfather, from his forefathers, in his own hand, most or all of them being munkar. We mentioned his narration of these hadiths from this Musa to Abu 'Abd Allah al-Husayn ibn 'Ali al-Hasan ibn 'Ali from the Family of the Prophet in Egypt, who is the brother of al-Nasir, and he said to us: 'This Musa was my neighbour in Medina for forty years, and it was never mentioned in his presence that he narrated anything, neither from his father nor from anyone else.'"]].

Al-Sha'bi said regarding this verse: ﴿Men are the protectors and maintainers of women because Allah has made some of them to excel over others and because they spend of their wealth﴾, he said: the dower which he gave her. Do you not see that if he accuses her of adultery he performs li'an with her, and if she accuses him she is flogged?

* *

His saying: ﴿So righteous women are devoutly obedient﴾, meaning: among women. Ibn 'Abbas and others said: meaning they are obedient to their husbands. ﴿Guarding in the husband's absence﴾.

al-Suddi and others said: meaning she guards her husband in his absence in her person and his property.

* *

His saying: ﴿with what Allah has guarded﴾, meaning: what is guarded is by His guarding.

Ibn Jarir said: al-Muthanna related to me, Abu Salih related to us, Abu Ma'shar related to us, Sa'id ibn Abi Sa'id al-Maqburi related to us, from Abu Hurayrah who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The best of women is the woman who, when you look at her, pleases you; when you command her, she obeys you; and when you are absent from her, she guards you in herself and your property." He said: Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited this verse: ﴿Men are the protectors and maintainers of women﴾ to the end.

Ibn Abi Hatim related it from Yunus ibn Habib, from Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi, from Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Dhi'b, from Sa'id al-Maqburi, with the same wording. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (8/295).]]

Imam Ahmad said: Yahya ibn Ishaq related to us, Ibn Lahi'ah related to us, from 'Ubayd Allah ibn Abi Ja'far: that Ibn Qarizh informed him that 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "If a woman prays her five (prayers), fasts her month, guards her private part, and obeys her husband, it will be said to her: Enter Paradise by whichever of its gates you wish."

Ahmad alone related it through the route of 'Abd Allah ibn Qarizh from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf. [[Musnad (1/191).]]

* *

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And those from whom you fear nushuz (rebellion)﴾, meaning: the women from whom you fear that they may rebel against their husbands. Nushuz is elevation; so the nashiz woman is the one who lifts herself above her husband, abandons his command, turns away from him, and hates him. Whenever signs of nushuz appear in her, he should admonish her and warn her of Allah's punishment for disobeying Him, for Allah has made the husband's right and obedience obligatory upon her and has forbidden her to disobey him because of his excellence and bestowal over her. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "If I were to order anyone to prostrate to another, I would order the woman to prostrate to her husband, because of the greatness of his right over her." [[Related by al-Tirmidhi under no. (1159) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him; and Ahmad in the Musnad (6/76) from the hadith of 'A'ishah.]] Al-Bukhari related from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "If a man calls his wife to his bed and she refuses him, the angels curse her until morning." [[Sahih al-Bukhari under no. (3237).]] Muslim related it with the wording: "If a woman spends the night away from her husband's bed, the angels curse her until morning." [[Sahih Muslim under no. (1436).]] Therefore He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And those from whom you fear nushuz, admonish them﴾.

* *

His saying: ﴿and forsake them in the beds﴾. 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah related from Ibn 'Abbas: hijran is that he does not have intercourse with her, lies beside her on her bed, and turns his back to her. Likewise said many others, and others added — among them al-Suddi, al-Dahhak, 'Ikrimah, and Ibn 'Abbas in one report — "and he does not speak to her nor converse with her during that."

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah also related from Ibn 'Abbas: he admonishes her; if she accepts, well and good, otherwise he forsakes her in the bed, and does not speak to her, without abandoning marriage with her; and that is very hard on her.

Mujahid, al-Sha'bi, Ibrahim, Muhammad ibn Ka'b, Miqsam and Qatadah said: hajr is that he does not lie beside her.

Abu Dawud said: Musa ibn Isma'il related to us, Hammad related to us, from 'Ali ibn Zayd, from Abu Harrah al-Raqashi, from his paternal uncle, that the Prophet ﷺ said: "If you fear their nushuz, forsake them in the beds." Hammad said: meaning in marriage. [[Sunan Abi Dawud under no. (2145).]]

In the Sunan and the Musnad, from Mu'awiyah ibn Haydah al-Qushayri, that he said: O Messenger of Allah, what is the right of one of our wives? He said: "That you feed her when you eat, clothe her when you are clothed, do not strike the face, do not revile her, and do not forsake her except within the house." [[Sunan Abi Dawud under no. (2143) and the Musnad (4/447).]]

* *

His saying: ﴿and strike them﴾ [in some copies: "so strike them"], meaning: if they do not desist by the admonition nor by forsaking, then you may strike them with a non-severe strike (darban ghayra mubarrih), as is established in Sahih Muslim from Jabir, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said during the Farewell Pilgrimage: "Fear Allah concerning women, for they are with you as captives (awan); you have no rights over them except that they should not allow anyone you dislike to tread upon your bedding; but if they do that, then strike them with a non-severe strike; and they have the right to their provision and clothing according to what is customary." [[Sahih Muslim under no. (1218).]]

Likewise said Ibn 'Abbas and others: a non-severe strike. Al-Hasan al-Basri said: meaning one that does not leave a mark. The jurists said: it is that one does not break a limb of hers nor leave any lasting effect.

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah related from Ibn 'Abbas: he forsakes her in the bed; if she responds, well and good, otherwise Allah has permitted you to strike her with a non-severe strike, without breaking any bone of hers; and if she responds, well and good, otherwise the ransom (al-fidyah) from her becomes lawful for you.

Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah said, from al-Zuhri, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar, from Iyas ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Dhubab, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Do not strike the female servants of Allah." Then 'Umar came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: The women have become bold against their husbands. So he permitted striking them. Then many women came around the family of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ complaining of their husbands. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Many women have come around the family of Muhammad complaining of their husbands; those are not the best of you." Related by Abu Dawud, al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah. [[Sunan Abi Dawud under no. (2146); Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra under no. (9167); Sunan Ibn Majah under no. (1975).]]

Imam Ahmad said: Sulayman ibn Dawud, meaning Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi, related to us, Abu 'Awanah related to us, from Dawud al-Awdi, from 'Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, from al-Ash'ath ibn Qays, who said: I was a guest of 'Umar, and he took hold of his wife and struck her, and said: "O Ash'ath, memorise three things from me which I memorised from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: do not ask a man why he struck his wife; do not sleep except on an odd number (of rak'ahs of witr)..." and he forgot the third.

Likewise Abu Dawud, al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah related it from the hadith of 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi, from Abu 'Awanah, from Dawud al-Awdi, with it. [[Sunan Abi Dawud under no. (2147); Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra under no. (9168); Sunan Ibn Majah under no. (1986).]]

* *

His saying: ﴿Then if they obey you, seek no means against them﴾, meaning: when the woman obeys her husband in all that he desires from her, of what Allah has permitted him from her, then there is no way for him against her after that, and he has no right to strike her or forsake her.

* *

His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever Exalted and Grand﴾: a warning to men if they transgress against women without cause, for Allah, the Exalted, the Grand, is their Protector, and He avenges those who wrong them and oppress them.

Allah, the Exalted, mentioned the first situation, which is when the aversion and disobedience (nushuz) come from the wife. Then He mentioned the second situation, which is when the aversion comes from both spouses, so He said, the Exalted: ﴿And if you fear a breach between the two of them, then send an arbiter (hakam) from his family and an arbiter from her family﴾

The jurists said: When a breach (shiqaq) occurs between the spouses, the ruler (hakim) seats them beside a trustworthy person who looks into their affair and prevents the wrongdoer among them from wronging. If their matter becomes grave and their dispute drags on, the ruler sends a trustworthy person from the wife's people and a trustworthy person from the husband's people, so that they may meet, look into their affair, and do what is in the interest, whether that be separation or reconciliation, as they see fit. The Lawgiver (al-Shari') was keen on reconciliation; for this reason He said: ﴿If they both desire reconciliation, Allah will bring about harmony between them﴾

Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, commanded that they send a righteous man from the husband's family and a man like him from the wife's family, and they should look at which of them is at fault. If the husband is the one at fault, they keep his wife away from him and restrict him to providing maintenance (nafaqah). If the wife is the one at fault, they restrict her to her husband and withhold maintenance from her. If their opinion agrees on separating them or joining them, then their decision is permissible. If they see fit to join them, and one of the spouses agrees while the other dislikes it, and then one of them dies, the one who agreed inherits from the one who disliked it, but the one who disliked does not inherit from the one who agreed. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Jarir.

'Abd al-Razzaq said: Ma'mar informed us, from Ibn Tawus, from 'Ikrimah ibn Khalid, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: I and Mu'awiyah were sent as arbiters. Ma'mar said: It has reached me that 'Uthman sent them both, and said to them: If you see that they should be joined, then join them; and if you see that they should be separated, then separate them.

He also said: Ibn Juraij informed us, Ibn Abi Mulaykah related to me that 'Aqil ibn Abi Talib married Fatimah bint 'Utbah ibn Rabi'ah, and she said: "Come to me, and I will spend on you." Whenever he entered upon her, she would say: "Where are 'Utbah ibn Rabi'ah and Shaybah ibn Rabi'ah?" He said: "On your left in the Fire when you enter." So she drew her garments tightly around herself and went to 'Uthman and told him of that. He laughed, and sent for Ibn 'Abbas and Mu'awiyah. Ibn 'Abbas said: "I will certainly separate them." Mu'awiyah said: "I would not separate between two old men of Banu 'Abd Manaf." They came to them and found that they had shut their doors upon themselves, so they returned.

'Abd al-Razzaq said: Ma'mar informed us, from Ayyub, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, from 'Ubaydah, who said: I witnessed 'Ali when a woman and her husband came to him, each accompanied by a group of people. They brought out an arbiter from each side. 'Ali said to the two arbiters: "Do you know what is upon you? Upon you is that if you see that they should be joined, you join them." The woman said: "I am content with the Book of Allah concerning me and concerning him." The husband said: "As for separation, no." 'Ali said: "You have lied; by Allah, you will not leave until you are content with the Book of Allah, for you and against you."

Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim, and Ibn Jarir narrated it from Ya'qub, from Ibn 'Ulayyah, from Ayyub, from Ibn Sirin, from 'Ubaydah, from 'Ali, similarly. And he narrated it by another route, from Ibn Sirin, from 'Ubaydah, from 'Ali, with it.

This is the position of the majority of scholars: that the two arbiters have the authority of joining and separating. Ibrahim al-Nakha'i even said: If the two arbiters wish to separate them by one divorce, or two, or three, they may do so. This is also a narration from Malik.

Al-Hasan al-Basri said: The two arbiters are empowered to join, but not to separate. Likewise said Qatadah and Zayd ibn Aslam. Ahmad ibn Hanbal, Abu Thawr and Dawud also said so. Their basis is His saying: ﴿If they both desire reconciliation, Allah will bring about harmony between them﴾, and separation is not mentioned.

As for when they are agents (wakil) appointed by the two spouses, their ruling is implemented in joining and separating without any disagreement.

The imams have differed regarding the two arbiters: are they appointed by the ruler, so they judge even if the spouses are not content, or are they agents appointed by the spouses? There are two opinions. The majority hold the first, based on His saying: ﴿then send an arbiter from his family and an arbiter from her family﴾, where He called them "arbiters" (hakamayn), and it is part of the nature of an arbiter that he judges without the consent of the one judged against. This is the apparent meaning of the verse, and it is the newer position of al-Shafi'i's school, and the view of Abu Hanifah and his companions.

The second of the two, based on 'Ali's words, may Allah be pleased with him, to the husband, when he said, "As for separation, no," and he replied: "You have lied, until you acknowledge what she has acknowledged." They said: If they were judges, they would not need the husband's acknowledgment. And Allah knows best.

Shaykh Abu 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-Barr said: The scholars agreed that if the two arbiters differ in their view, the view of the other carries no weight. They agreed that their decision is binding in joining even if the spouses did not appoint them as agents. They differed on whether their decision is binding in separation. Then it is reported from the majority that their decision is binding in separation too.

He commands the worship of Him alone, with no partner, for He is the Creator, the Provider, the Bestower of blessings, and the Bountiful toward His creation at every moment and in every state. He is therefore the one who deserves that they affirm His oneness and not associate anything of His creation with Him. As the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to Mu'adh: "Do you know what Allah's right over the servants is?" He said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "That they worship Him and do not associate anything with Him." Then he said: "Do you know what the servants' right over Allah is if they do that? That He will not punish them." [Reported by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. 7373, and Muslim in his Sahih, no. 30.]

Then He enjoined kindness to the two parents, for Allah, glorified is He, made them the means by which you came out from non-existence into existence. Allah often joins between His worship and kindness to the parents, as in His saying: ﴿Give thanks to Me and to your parents﴾ [Luqman: 14], and His saying: ﴿And your Lord has decreed that you worship none but Him, and that you be kind to parents﴾ [al-Isra: 23].

Then, after kindness to the parents, He mentioned kindness to relatives, men and women, as came in the hadith: "Charity given to a poor person is (one) charity, and to a relative it is two: charity and maintaining the ties of kinship." [Reported by Ahmad in his Musnad (4/17) from the hadith of Salman ibn Amir, may Allah be pleased with him.]

Then He said: ﴿And the orphans﴾, because they have lost the one who manages their affairs and spends on them, so Allah commanded kindness to them and tenderness toward them.

Then He said: ﴿And the needy﴾, who are the poor among those in need who do not find what suffices for their sustenance. So Allah commanded helping them with what completes their sufficiency and removes their necessity. The discussion of the faqir and the miskin will come in Surah Bara'ah.

* *

His saying: ﴿And the near neighbour and the far neighbour﴾. Ali ibn Abi Talhah reported from Ibn Abbas: ﴿the near neighbour﴾ means the one between whom and you there is kinship, ﴿and the far neighbour﴾ the one between whom and you there is no kinship. It was similarly narrated from Ikrimah, Mujahid, Maymun ibn Mihran, al-Dahhak, Zayd ibn Aslam, Muqatil ibn Hayyan, and Qatadah.

Abu Ishaq reported from Nawf al-Bikali regarding His saying: ﴿the near neighbour﴾, meaning the Muslim, and ﴿the far neighbour﴾, meaning the Jew and the Christian. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it.

Jabir al-Ju'fi reported from al-Sha'bi, from Ali and Ibn Mas'ud: ﴿the near neighbour﴾ means the wife. Mujahid also said regarding His saying: ﴿the far neighbour﴾, it means the companion on the journey.

Hadiths have come concerning the injunction to treat the neighbour well, and we will mention what is available of them, and Allah is the One sought for help:

The first hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Umar ibn Muhammad ibn Zayd, that he heard his father Muhammad narrate from Abdullah ibn Umar that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Jibril kept enjoining me about the neighbour until I thought that he would make him an heir."
They both (al-Bukhari and Muslim) recorded it in the Sahih from the hadith of Umar ibn Muhammad ibn Zayd ibn Abdullah ibn Umar, with this wording. [Musnad (2/85); Sahih al-Bukhari no. 6015; Sahih Muslim no. 2625.]

The second hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Sufyan narrated to us, from Dawud ibn Shapur, from Mujahid, from Abdullah ibn Amr who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Jibril kept enjoining me about the neighbour until I thought that he would make him an heir." [Musnad (2/160).]
Abu Dawud and al-Tirmidhi narrated something similar from the hadith of Sufyan ibn Uyaynah, from Bashir Abu Isma'il (al-Tirmidhi added: and Dawud ibn Shapur), both from Mujahid, with the same wording. Then al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan gharib from this route." [Sunan Abi Dawud no. 5152; Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 1943.] It has been narrated from Mujahid, from Aishah and Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet ﷺ.

The third hadith, also from him (Abdullah ibn Amr): Ahmad also said: Abdullah ibn Yazid narrated to us, Haywah informed us, Sharahbil ibn Shurayk informed us that he heard Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Hubuli narrate from Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that he said: "The best of companions with Allah is the best of them to his companion, and the best of neighbours with Allah is the best of them to his neighbour."
al-Tirmidhi narrated it from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak, from Haywah ibn Shurayh, with it, and said: "[Hadith] hasan gharib." [Musnad (2/167); Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 1944.]

The fourth hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from his father, from Abayah ibn Rifa'ah, from Umar who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "A man should not be satisfied while his neighbour is hungry beside him." Ahmad alone narrated it. [Musnad (1/54). al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (8/167): "Its narrators are the narrators of the Sahih, except that Abayah ibn Rifa'ah did not hear from Umar."]

The fifth hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Ali ibn Abdullah narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Fudayl ibn Ghazwan narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Sa'd al-Ansari narrated to us, I heard Abu Zabyah al-Kala'i, I heard al-Miqdad ibn al-Aswad say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to his companions: ["What do you say about fornication?" They said: "It is forbidden; Allah and His Messenger have forbidden it, so it is forbidden until the Day of Resurrection."] Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "For a man to commit adultery with ten women is easier for him than to commit it with his neighbour's wife." He said: "What do you say about theft?" They said: "Allah and His Messenger have forbidden it, so it is forbidden." He said: "For a man to steal from ten houses is easier for him than to steal from his neighbour." [Ahmad alone narrated it. Musnad (6/8).]
It has a witness in the two Sahihs from the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, which sin is the greatest?" He said: "That you set up a rival to Allah while He created you." I said: "Then which?" He said: "That you kill your child fearing that he will share your food." I said: "Then which?" He said: "That you commit adultery with your neighbour's wife." [Sahih al-Bukhari no. 4761; Sahih Muslim no. 68.]

The sixth hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Yazid narrated to us, Hisham informed us, from Hafsah, from Abu al-Aliyah, from a man of the Ansar who said: I went out from my family intending to go to the Prophet ﷺ, and there he was standing, and a man with him was facing him. I thought they had some need. The Ansari said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood so long that I began to feel pity for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ because of the length of the standing. When he finished, I said: "O Messenger of Allah, this man stood with you so long that I began to feel pity for you because of the length of the standing." He said: "And did you see him?" I said: "Yes." He said: "Do you know who he is?" I said: "No." He said: "That was Jibril. He kept enjoining me about the neighbour until I thought that he would make him an heir. Then he said: 'Indeed, if you had greeted him with peace, he would have returned your greeting.'" [Musnad (5/32). al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (8/164): "Its narrators are the narrators of the Sahih."]

The seventh hadith: Abd ibn Humayd said in his Musnad: Ya'la ibn Ubayd narrated to us, Abu Bakr (meaning al-Madani) narrated to us, from Jabir ibn Abdullah who said: A man came from al-Awali while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and Jibril, peace be upon him, were praying where funeral prayers are prayed. When he finished, the man said: "O Messenger of Allah, who is this man whom I saw with you?" He said: "Did you see him?" He said: "Yes." He said: "You have seen much good. This is Jibril, who kept enjoining me about the neighbour until it appeared to me that he would make him an heir."
Al-Bazzar narrated it alone by this route. [Al-Bazzar in his Musnad (1897), Kashf al-Astar, by way of al-Fadl ibn Mubashshir Abu Bakr al-Madani with it. al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (8/165): "In it is al-Fadl ibn Mubashshir, whom Ibn Hibban declared trustworthy and others declared weak; the rest of its narrators are trustworthy."] It is a witness to the previous hadith.

The eighth hadith: Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said: Ubaydullah ibn Muhammad Abu al-Rabi' al-Harithi narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Abi Fudayk narrated to us, Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Fadl informed me, from Ata al-Khurasani, from al-Hasan, from Jabir ibn Abdullah who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Neighbours are of three kinds: a neighbour who has one right, and he is the least of neighbours in right; a neighbour who has two rights; and a neighbour who has three rights, and he is the best of neighbours in right. As for the one who has one right, he is a non-Muslim neighbour with no kinship, and he has the right of neighbourhood. As for the one who has two rights, he is a Muslim neighbour, who has the right of Islam and the right of neighbourhood. As for the one who has three rights, he is a Muslim neighbour who is a relative, who has the right of neighbourhood, the right of Islam, and the right of kinship."
Al-Bazzar said: "We do not know anyone who narrated from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Fudayl except Ibn Abi Fudayk." [Musnad al-Bazzar no. 1896, Kashf al-Astar. al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (8/164): "Al-Bazzar narrated it from his teacher Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Harithi, who is a fabricator (wada')."]

The ninth hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Abu Imran, from Talhah ibn Abdullah, from Aishah, that she asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, saying: "I have two neighbours; to which of them should I send a gift?" He said: "To the one whose door is nearer to you."
al-Bukhari narrated it from the hadith of Shu'bah, with it. [Musnad (6/175); Sahih al-Bukhari no. 6020.]

* *

His saying: ﴿And the companion by your side﴾. al-Thawri reported from Jabir al-Ju'fi, from al-Sha'bi, from Ali and Ibn Mas'ud, who both said: it is the wife.
Ibn Abi Hatim said: It was narrated from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, al-Hasan, and Sa'id ibn Jubayr, in one of the narrations, something similar to that.
Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Ikrimah, and Qatadah said: it is the companion on the journey. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: it is the righteous companion. Zayd ibn Aslam said: it is your companion at home and your companion on the journey.

As for ﴿the wayfarer﴾, it is reported from Ibn Abbas and a group that it means the guest.
Mujahid, Abu Ja'far al-Baqir, al-Hasan, al-Dahhak, and Muqatil said: it is the one who passes by you while travelling.
This is more apparent, though if the speaker who said "guest" meant the one who passes along the road, then they are the same. The discussion of the wayfarers will come in Surah Bara'ah, and in Allah is trust and upon Him is reliance.

* *

His saying: ﴿And what your right hands possess﴾ is an injunction concerning slaves, because the slave is weak in resources, a captive in the hands of people. For this reason it is established that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ began to enjoin his Ummah during his final illness, saying: "The prayer, the prayer, and what your right hands possess." He kept repeating it until his tongue could no longer express it. [Reported by Abu Dawud in al-Sunan no. 5154, from the hadith of Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him.]

Imam Ahmad said: Ibrahim ibn Abi al-Abbas narrated to us, Baqiyyah narrated to us, Bahir ibn Sa'd narrated to us, from Khalid ibn Ma'dan, from al-Miqdam ibn Ma'dikarib who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "What you feed yourself is a charity for you, what you feed your child is a charity for you, what you feed your wife is a charity for you, and what you feed your servant is a charity for you."
al-Nasa'i narrated it from the hadith of Baqiyyah, and its chain is sahih. [Musnad (4/131); al-Sunan al-Kubra of al-Nasa'i no. 9185.] And praise be to Allah.

It is also reported from Abdullah ibn Amr that he said to a steward of his: "Have you given the slaves their food?" He said: "No." He said: "Go and give it to them, for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'It is enough sin for a person that he withholds the food of those whose sustenance he is responsible for.'" Muslim narrated it. [Sahih Muslim no. 996.]

It is also reported from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "The slave has his food and his clothing, and he should not be burdened with work beyond what he can bear." Muslim also narrated it. [Sahih Muslim no. 1662.]

And from him (Ibn Abbas), from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "When one of you is brought his servant's food, if he does not seat him with him, then let him hand him a morsel or two morsels, or a bite or two bites, for he has taken care of its heat and its preparation."

Both (al-Bukhari and Muslim) narrated it, and the wording is that of al-Bukhari. [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (5460) and Sahih Muslim, no. (1663).] In Muslim's version: "let him seat him with him so he may eat. If the food is scanty and meagre, then let him place a bite or two bites in his hand."

And from Abu Dharr (may Allah be pleased with him), from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "They are your brothers, your servants, whom Allah has placed under your authority. Whoever has his brother under his authority, let him feed him from what he eats, and clothe him from what he wears, and do not burden them with what overwhelms them. If you do burden them, then help them." Both (al-Bukhari and Muslim) narrated it. [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (31) and Sahih Muslim, no. (1661).]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not love one who is self-deluded and boastful﴾, meaning: self-deluded within himself, conceited and arrogant, boastful over the people, seeing himself as better than them. He is great in his own soul, but small in the sight of Allah, and hateful to the people.

Mujahid said regarding His saying ﴿Indeed, Allah does not love one who is self-deluded﴾: meaning arrogant, ﴿boastful﴾: meaning he counts what he has been given, and does not thank Allah, Mighty and Majestic. That is, he boasts over the people of the blessings Allah has given him, and he is little in gratitude to Allah for that.

Ibn Jarir said: Al-Qasim narrated to me, al-Husayn narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Kathir narrated to us, from Abdullah ibn Waqid Abu Raja al-Harawi, who said: "You will not find one who treats his slaves badly except that you will find him self-deluded and boastful," and he recited: ﴿And what your right hands possess [Indeed, Allah does not love one who is self-deluded and boastful]﴾, "and you will not find one who is undutiful to his parents except that you will find him a tyrant, wretched," and he recited: ﴿and dutiful to my mother, and He has not made me a tyrant, wretched﴾ [Maryam: 32].

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated, from al-Awwam ibn Hawshab, the like of it regarding the self-deluded and boastful. He said:

My father narrated to us, Abu Nu'aym narrated to us, al-Aswad ibn Shayban narrated to us, Yazid ibn Abdullah ibn al-Shikhkhir narrated to us, who said: Mutarrif said: "A hadith used to reach me from Abu Dharr, and I longed to meet him. So I met him and said: 'O Abu Dharr, it has reached me that you claim the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) narrated to you: "Indeed Allah loves three and hates three"?' He said: 'Yes indeed; I do not suppose that I lie about my intimate friend,' three times. I said: 'Who are the three whom Allah hates?' He said: 'The self-deluded and boastful. Do you not find him in the Book of Allah that was revealed?'" Then he recited the verse: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not love one who is self-deluded and boastful﴾ [An-Nisa: 36].

[Ahmad narrated it in his Musnad (5/176) through Yazid, from al-Aswad ibn Shayban, with a longer and more complete version.]

My father narrated to us, Musa ibn Isma'il narrated to us, Wuhayb narrated to us, from Khalid, from Abu Tamima, from a man from Bal-Hujaym, who said: "I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, advise me.' He said: 'Beware of trailing the lower garment, for trailing the garment is a form of self-conceit, and Allah does not love self-conceit.'" [Ahmad narrated it in his Musnad (5/64) through Wuhayb ibn Khalid.]

Allah, exalted is He, says, censuring those who are stingy with their wealth and refuse to spend it in what Allah has commanded them: of the dutifulness to parents, kindness to relatives, orphans, the needy, the neighbour who is a relative, the neighbour who is a stranger, the companion at one's side, the wayfarer, and what your right hands possess of slaves. ﴿And do not withhold from them what Allah has given them of His bounty﴾... [Note: the passage is translated as follows.]

Let me render the text precisely:

Allah, exalted is He, says, censuring those who are stingy with their wealth in not spending it on what Allah has commanded them: of dutifulness to parents, kindness to relatives, orphans, the needy, the neighbour who is a relative, the neighbour who is a stranger, the companion at one's side, the wayfarer, and what your right hands possess of slaves; and they do not discharge the right of Allah in it, and they also command people to be stingy. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "And what disease is worse than stinginess?" And he said: "Beware of miserliness (shuh), for it destroyed those who were before you; it commanded them to sever ties and they severed them, and commanded them to commit immorality and they committed it." [Narrated by Abu Dawud in his Sunan, no. (6698), from the hadith of ʿAbdullah ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAs, may Allah be pleased with him.]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And they conceal what Allah has given them of His bounty﴾ — the stingy person is one who denies the blessing of Allah upon him; it is not manifest on him nor clear, neither in his eating, nor in his clothing, nor in his giving and spending. As Allah says: ﴿Indeed, mankind is ungrateful to his Lord. And indeed, he is a witness to that﴾ [al-ʿAdiyat: 6-7], meaning by his condition and his traits. ﴿And indeed, he is intense in his love of wealth﴾ [al-ʿAdiyat: 8]. Here He says: ﴿And they conceal what Allah has given them of His bounty﴾, and therefore He threatens them with His saying: ﴿And We have prepared for the disbelievers a humiliating punishment﴾. Kufr (disbelief, lit. covering) is concealing and veiling, so the stingy person covers up and hides the blessing of Allah upon him and denies it, and so he is a disbeliever in the blessings of Allah upon him.

In a hadith: "Indeed, when Allah bestows a blessing upon a servant, He loves to see its effect upon him." [Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in his Sunan, no. (2819), from the hadith of ʿAbdullah ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAs, may Allah be pleased with him; the wording is: "Indeed Allah loves to see the effect of His blessing upon His servant."] And in the Prophetic supplication: "Make us grateful for Your blessings, praising You for them, accepting them — and it is related: saying them — and complete them upon us." [Narrated by Abu Dawud in his Sunan, no. (969), from the hadith of ʿAbdullah ibn Masʿud, may Allah be pleased with him.]

Some of the early scholars (salaf) interpreted this verse as referring to the stinginess of the Jews in making known the knowledge they had of the description of the Prophet (ﷺ), and their concealing of that; therefore He said: ﴿And We have prepared for the disbelievers a humiliating punishment﴾. This was related by Ibn Ishaq, from Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, from ʿIkrimah or Saʿid ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbas. It was also said by Mujahid and others.

There is no doubt that the verse admits of this, but the apparent context concerns stinginess with wealth, though stinginess with knowledge is included in it by way of priority. The context of the speech concerns spending on relatives and the weak, and likewise the verse that follows it, His saying: ﴿And those who spend their wealth to be seen by people﴾. He mentioned the miserly who are blamed, who are the stingy, then He mentioned the generous ones who show off, who intend by their giving to gain reputation and to be praised for generosity, and do not intend thereby the Face of Allah. And in the hadith of the three who are the first to be cast into the Fire — the scholar, the warrior, and the one who spends, who did so ostentatiously — the owner of wealth says: "I did not leave any means of spending that You love except that I spent in Your way." Allah says: "You lie; you only wanted it to be said: 'He is generous' — and it has been said." That is: you have already received your reward in this world, and that is what you intended by your deed.

In a hadith, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to ʿAdi: "Indeed your father aimed at a matter and attained it."

In another hadith: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked about ʿAbdullah ibn Judʿan: would his giving charity and freeing slaves benefit him? He said: "No, for he never once said, 'My Lord, forgive me my sin on the Day of Recompense.'"

Therefore He said: ﴿And they do not believe in Allah or the Last Day [and whoever has Satan as a companion — what an evil companion he is]﴾, meaning: it was only Satan who drove them to this ugly conduct and their deviation from performing obedience in its proper manner; for he adorned it for them, made them hopeful, accompanied them and made the ugly things seem fair to them. ﴿And whoever has Satan as a companion — what an evil companion he is.﴾ For this reason the poet said: "Do not ask about the man, but ask about his companion, for every companion follows the one he accompanies."

Then Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And what would it harm them if they had believed in Allah and the Last Day and spent from what Allah has provided them [and Allah is ever Knowing of them]﴾. That is: what harm would come to them if they had taken the praiseworthy path, turned away from showing off to sincerity and faith in Allah, and hope for His promise in the Hereafter for those who do good deeds, and spent from what Allah had provided them in the ways that Allah loves and is pleased with.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And Allah is ever Knowing of them﴾, that is: He knows their good and corrupt intentions, and He knows who among them deserves success, so He grants them success, inspires them with right guidance, and enables them to do righteous deeds with which He is pleased; and He knows who deserves abandonment and being expelled from His great divine presence — whoever is expelled from His door has lost and suffered loss in this world and the Hereafter; we seek refuge in Allah from that, by His abundant kindness.

Allah, exalted is He, says, censuring those who are stingy with their wealth and refuse to spend it in what Allah has commanded them: of the dutifulness to parents, kindness to relatives, orphans, the needy, the neighbour who is a relative, the neighbour who is a stranger, the companion at one's side, the wayfarer, and what your right hands possess of slaves. ﴿And do not withhold from them what Allah has given them of His bounty﴾... [Note: the passage is translated as follows.]

Let me render the text precisely:

Allah, exalted is He, says, censuring those who are stingy with their wealth in not spending it on what Allah has commanded them: of dutifulness to parents, kindness to relatives, orphans, the needy, the neighbour who is a relative, the neighbour who is a stranger, the companion at one's side, the wayfarer, and what your right hands possess of slaves; and they do not discharge the right of Allah in it, and they also command people to be stingy. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "And what disease is worse than stinginess?" And he said: "Beware of miserliness (shuh), for it destroyed those who were before you; it commanded them to sever ties and they severed them, and commanded them to commit immorality and they committed it." [Narrated by Abu Dawud in his Sunan, no. (6698), from the hadith of ʿAbdullah ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAs, may Allah be pleased with him.]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And they conceal what Allah has given them of His bounty﴾ — the stingy person is one who denies the blessing of Allah upon him; it is not manifest on him nor clear, neither in his eating, nor in his clothing, nor in his giving and spending. As Allah says: ﴿Indeed, mankind is ungrateful to his Lord. And indeed, he is a witness to that﴾ [al-ʿAdiyat: 6-7], meaning by his condition and his traits. ﴿And indeed, he is intense in his love of wealth﴾ [al-ʿAdiyat: 8]. Here He says: ﴿And they conceal what Allah has given them of His bounty﴾, and therefore He threatens them with His saying: ﴿And We have prepared for the disbelievers a humiliating punishment﴾. Kufr (disbelief, lit. covering) is concealing and veiling, so the stingy person covers up and hides the blessing of Allah upon him and denies it, and so he is a disbeliever in the blessings of Allah upon him.

In a hadith: "Indeed, when Allah bestows a blessing upon a servant, He loves to see its effect upon him." [Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in his Sunan, no. (2819), from the hadith of ʿAbdullah ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAs, may Allah be pleased with him; the wording is: "Indeed Allah loves to see the effect of His blessing upon His servant."] And in the Prophetic supplication: "Make us grateful for Your blessings, praising You for them, accepting them — and it is related: saying them — and complete them upon us." [Narrated by Abu Dawud in his Sunan, no. (969), from the hadith of ʿAbdullah ibn Masʿud, may Allah be pleased with him.]

Some of the early scholars (salaf) interpreted this verse as referring to the stinginess of the Jews in making known the knowledge they had of the description of the Prophet (ﷺ), and their concealing of that; therefore He said: ﴿And We have prepared for the disbelievers a humiliating punishment﴾. This was related by Ibn Ishaq, from Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, from ʿIkrimah or Saʿid ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbas. It was also said by Mujahid and others.

There is no doubt that the verse admits of this, but the apparent context concerns stinginess with wealth, though stinginess with knowledge is included in it by way of priority. The context of the speech concerns spending on relatives and the weak, and likewise the verse that follows it, His saying: ﴿And those who spend their wealth to be seen by people﴾. He mentioned the miserly who are blamed, who are the stingy, then He mentioned the generous ones who show off, who intend by their giving to gain reputation and to be praised for generosity, and do not intend thereby the Face of Allah. And in the hadith of the three who are the first to be cast into the Fire — the scholar, the warrior, and the one who spends, who did so ostentatiously — the owner of wealth says: "I did not leave any means of spending that You love except that I spent in Your way." Allah says: "You lie; you only wanted it to be said: 'He is generous' — and it has been said." That is: you have already received your reward in this world, and that is what you intended by your deed.

In a hadith, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to ʿAdi: "Indeed your father aimed at a matter and attained it."

In another hadith: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked about ʿAbdullah ibn Judʿan: would his giving charity and freeing slaves benefit him? He said: "No, for he never once said, 'My Lord, forgive me my sin on the Day of Recompense.'"

Therefore He said: ﴿And they do not believe in Allah or the Last Day [and whoever has Satan as a companion — what an evil companion he is]﴾, meaning: it was only Satan who drove them to this ugly conduct and their deviation from performing obedience in its proper manner; for he adorned it for them, made them hopeful, accompanied them and made the ugly things seem fair to them. ﴿And whoever has Satan as a companion — what an evil companion he is.﴾ For this reason the poet said: "Do not ask about the man, but ask about his companion, for every companion follows the one he accompanies."

Then Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And what would it harm them if they had believed in Allah and the Last Day and spent from what Allah has provided them [and Allah is ever Knowing of them]﴾. That is: what harm would come to them if they had taken the praiseworthy path, turned away from showing off to sincerity and faith in Allah, and hope for His promise in the Hereafter for those who do good deeds, and spent from what Allah had provided them in the ways that Allah loves and is pleased with.

* *
