As for His saying: ﴿And Allah is ever Knowing of them﴾, that is: He knows their good and corrupt intentions, and He knows who among them deserves success, so He grants them success, inspires them with right guidance, and enables them to do righteous deeds with which He is pleased; and He knows who deserves abandonment and being expelled from His great divine presence — whoever is expelled from His door has lost and suffered loss in this world and the Hereafter; we seek refuge in Allah from that, by His abundant kindness.

Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim, on Surah An-Nisa' (4), verses 40–42 (Part 1 of 2):

Almighty God informs that He does not wrong any of His servants on the Day of Resurrection, not even to the weight of a mustard seed, nor to the weight of an atom. Rather, He will repay them in full for it and multiply it for them if it is a good deed, as He says: ﴿And We will set up the scales of justice for the Day of Resurrection, so no soul will be wronged in anything. Even if it be the weight of a mustard seed, We will bring it forth. And sufficient are We as reckoners.﴾ [Al-Anbiya': 47] [[Added from manuscripts R and A; in manuscript H: "the verse".]]

God also says, relating what Luqman said: ﴿O my son, indeed if it is the weight of a mustard seed and should be within a rock or in the heavens or in the earth, Allah will bring it forth. Indeed, Allah is Subtle and Acquainted.﴾ [Luqman: 16] [[Added from manuscripts R and A; in manuscript H: "the verse".]]

And He says: ﴿On that day mankind will depart in scattered groups to be shown their deeds. So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it.﴾

In the Two Sahihs (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim), from the hadith of Zayd ibn Aslam, from 'Ata' ibn Yasar, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), in the lengthy hadith of intercession (al-shafa'ah), in which it is said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will say: "Go back, and whoever you find in his heart the weight of a mustard seed [[In manuscripts R and A: "atom".]] of faith, bring him out of the Fire." And in another wording: "The least, the least, the least, the weight of an atom of faith, bring him out of the Fire." So they will bring out a great multitude. Then Abu Sa'id said: "Recite, if you wish: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not wrong even the weight of an atom, and if it is a good deed, He will double it and give from Himself a great reward.﴾" [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 7439; Sahih Muslim, no. 183.]]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj narrated to us, 'Isa ibn Yunus narrated to us, from Harun ibn 'Antarah [[In manuscript A: "'Anbarah".]], from 'Abdullah ibn al-Sa'ib, from Zadhan, who said: 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud said: "The slave and the slave-woman will be brought on the Day of Resurrection, and a caller will call out over the heads of the first and the last: 'This is so-and-so the son of so-and-so; whoever has a right, let him come to his right.'"

Then a woman will rejoice that she has a right against her father, her brother, or her husband. Then he recited: ﴿So there will be no ties of kinship among them that Day, nor will they ask about one another.﴾ [Al-Mu'minun: 101]. Then Allah will forgive from His rights whatever He wills, but He will not forgive any of the rights of people. So a platform will be set up for the people and a caller will call: "This is so-and-so the son of so-and-so; whoever has a right, let him come to his right." He will say: "My Lord, the world has perished; from where shall I give them their rights?" He will say: "Take from his good deeds, and give every person with a right his right according to the measure of his claim. If he was a friend of Allah, and there remains for him the weight of an atom, Allah will multiply it for him until He admits him to Paradise because of it." Then he recited to us: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not wrong the weight of an atom, and if it is a good deed, He will double it.﴾ He said: "Enter Paradise." But if he was a wretched slave, the angel will say: "My Lord, his good deeds have run out, and many claimants remain." He will say: "Take from their evil deeds and add them to his evil deeds, then write for him a document to the Fire."

Al-Tabari narrated it through another route from Zadhan, with similar wording. And part of this report has a witness in a sahih hadith.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Abu Nu'aym narrated to us, Fudayl [i.e., ibn Marzuq] narrated to us, from 'Ata' al-'Awfi, who said: 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar narrated to me, saying: This verse was revealed concerning the Bedouins: ﴿Whoever brings a good deed will have ten times its like﴾ [Al-An'am: 160]. A man said: "What about the Muhajirun, O Abu 'Abd al-Rahman?" He said: "There is something better than that: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not wrong the weight of an atom, and if it is a good deed, He will double it and give from Himself a great reward.﴾"

Abu Zur'ah narrated to us, Yahya ibn 'Abdullah ibn Bukayr narrated to us, 'Abdullah ibn Lahi'ah narrated to me, 'Ata' ibn Dinar narrated to me, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr regarding His saying: ﴿And if it is a good deed, He will double it﴾, that the polytheist will have his punishment lightened on the Day of Resurrection, but he will never be brought out of the Fire. And it has been argued for him from the sahih hadith that al-'Abbas said: "O Messenger of Allah, indeed Abu Talib used to protect you and support you; did it benefit him at all?" He said: "Yes, he is in a shallow part of the Fire, and if not for me, he would be in the lowest level of the Fire." [[Al-Bukhari, no. 3883, 6208; Muslim, no. 209.]]

This may be specific to Abu Talib among the disbelievers, based on what Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi narrated in his Sunan [[In manuscripts D, R and A: "his Musnad".]]: 'Imran narrated to us, Qatadah narrated to us, from Anas that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah does not wrong a believer in a good deed; he is rewarded for it with provision in this world and recompensed for it in the Hereafter. As for the disbeliever, he is fed for his good deeds in this world, and when the Day of Resurrection comes, he will have no good deed." [[Musnad al-Tayalisi, no. 47 (Minhat al-Ma'bud); also narrated by Muslim, no. 2808, through Yazid ibn Harun from Hammam ibn Yahya from Qatadah with similar wording.]]

Abu Hurayrah, 'Ikrimah, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Hasan, Qatadah and al-Dahhak said regarding His saying: ﴿and give from Himself a great reward﴾: it means Paradise.

Imam Ahmad said: 'Abd al-Samad narrated to us, Sulayman [i.e., ibn al-Mughirah] narrated to us, from 'Ali ibn Zayd, from Abu 'Uthman, who said: It reached me from Abu Hurayrah that he said: "It reached me that Allah, Exalted is He, gives His believing servant one thousand thousand good deeds for a single good deed." He said: Then it so happened that I set out for Hajj or 'Umrah, and I met him and said: "It has reached me that you say: 'I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: Allah gives His believing servant one thousand thousand good deeds for a single good deed.'" Abu Hurayrah said: "No, rather I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, gives him two thousand thousand good deeds.'" Then he recited: ﴿He will multiply it and give from Himself a great reward.﴾ So who can measure its measure? [[Musnad Ahmad (5/521).]]

Ahmad also narrated it in another way, saying: Yazid narrated to us, Mubarak ibn Fudalah narrated to us, from 'Ali ibn Zayd, from Abu 'Uthman, who said: I came to Abu Hurayrah and said to him: "It has reached me that you say: Indeed a good deed is multiplied by one thousand thousand good deeds?" He said: "And what amazes you about that? By Allah, I heard [meaning the Prophet (ﷺ)] — thus my father said — saying: 'Indeed Allah multiplies the good deed by two thousand thousand good deeds.'" [[Musnad Ahmad (2/296).]]

'Ali ibn Zayd has strange reports in his narrations, and Allah knows best.

* * *

As for His saying: ﴿So how will it be when We bring from every nation a witness, and We bring you as a witness against these?﴾, Almighty God says, informing of the terror of the Day of Resurrection and the severity of its matter and its affair: How will the matter and the situation be on the Day of Resurrection, when He brings from every nation a witness, meaning the prophets, peace be upon them? As He says: ﴿And the earth will shine with the light of its Lord, and the record will be placed, and the prophets and the witnesses will be brought forward, and judgment will be made between them with truth, and they will not be wronged.﴾ [Az-Zumar: 69] [[Added from manuscripts R and A; in manuscript H: "the verse".]] And He says: ﴿And the Day We raise up from every nation a witness against them from among themselves, and We bring you as a witness against these. And We have sent down to you the Book as clarification for all things, and guidance and mercy and good tidings for the Muslims.﴾ [An-Nahl: 89] [[Added from manuscripts R and A; in manuscript H: "the verse".]]

Al-Bukhari said: Muhammad ibn Yusuf narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, from 'Ubaydah, from 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said to me: "Recite to me." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, shall I recite to you when it was revealed to you?" He said: "Yes, indeed I love to hear it from others." So I recited Surah An-Nisa', until I reached this verse: ﴿So how will it be when We bring from every nation a witness, and We bring you as a witness against these?﴾ He said: "Enough for now." And his eyes were overflowing with tears.

He [al-Bukhari] and Muslim also narrated it from the hadith of al-A'mash, with the same chain. [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 5050; Sahih Muslim, no. 800.]] It has been narrated through multiple routes from Ibn Mas'ud, so it is established as a statement of his (mawquf). Ahmad narrated it through the routes of Abu Hayyan and Abu Razin, from him.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Bakr ibn Abi al-Dunya narrated to us, al-Salt ibn Mas'ud al-Jahdari narrated to us, Fudayl ibn Sulayman narrated to us, Yunus ibn Muhammad ibn Fadalah al-Ansari narrated to us, from his father, who said, and my father was among those who accompanied the Prophet (ﷺ): The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came to them in Banu Zafar, and he sat on the rock that is in Banu Zafar today, and with him were Ibn Mas'ud, Mu'adh ibn Jabal, and some of his companions. The Prophet (ﷺ) commanded a reciter, and he recited until he came to this verse: ﴿So how will it be when We bring from every nation a witness, and We bring you as a witness against these?﴾ Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) wept until his jaw and his sides trembled, and he said: "O Lord, I bore witness against those among whom I am; so how about those whom I have not seen?" [[Narrated by al-Baghawi in his Mu'jam, and from his route by al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (19/243), through al-Salt ibn Mas'ud al-Jahdari. Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (7/4): "its narrators are trustworthy (thiqat)."]]

Ibn Jarir said: 'Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Zuhri narrated to me, Sufyan narrated to us, from al-Mas'udi, from Ja'far ibn 'Amr ibn Hurayth, from his father, from 'Abdullah [i.e., Ibn Mas'ud], regarding ﴿So how will it be when We bring from every nation a witness﴾, he said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "A witness over them as long as I am among them; but when You take me, You will be the Watcher over them."

As for what Abu 'Abdullah al-Qurtubi mentioned in al-Tadhkirah [[Al-Tadhkirah fi Ahwal al-Mawta wa Umur al-Akhirah (p. 294).]], where he said: Chapter on what has come concerning the testimony of the Prophet (ﷺ) over his nation. He said: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, a man from the Ansar informed us, from al-Minhal ibn 'Amr, who narrated to him that he heard Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib say: "There is no day but that his nation is presented to the Prophet (ﷺ) morning and evening, and he recognizes them by their names and their deeds; therefore he bears witness over them." Allah, Exalted, says: ﴿So how will it be when We bring from every nation a witness, and We bring you as a witness against these?﴾ This is a report (athar), and it has a break in its chain, since in it is an unnamed man, and it is from the words of Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib and is not attributed to the Prophet (ﷺ). Al-Qurtubi did accept it, saying after citing it: "It has already been mentioned that deeds are presented to Allah every Monday and Thursday, and to the prophets, the fathers and the mothers on Friday." He said: "There is no contradiction, since it is possible that our Prophet is specially given what is presented to him every day, and on Friday with the prophets, peace be upon them."

* * *

As for His saying: ﴿On that Day those who disbelieved and disobeyed the Messenger will wish that the earth would be leveled over them﴾, meaning: if it were split open and swallowed them, because of what they see of the terrors of the place of standing, and the disgrace, scandal and rebuke that will befall them. As in His saying: ﴿The Day a man will look at what his hands have sent forth, and the disbeliever will say: "Would that I were dust!"﴾ [[Added from manuscript R; in manuscript H: "the verse".]] And His saying: ﴿and they will not conceal from Allah any statement.﴾ He informs about them that they will confess to everything they did, and they will conceal nothing from Him.

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, Hakkam narrated to us, 'Amr narrated to us, from Mutarrif, from al-Minhal ibn 'Amr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: A man came to Ibn 'Abbas and said: "I heard Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, say (reporting about the polytheists on the Day of Resurrection that they said): ﴿By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists﴾ [al-An'am: 23], and He says in another verse: ﴿and they will not conceal from Allah a [single] statement﴾." Ibn 'Abbas said: "As for His saying ﴿By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists﴾, when they saw that none would enter Paradise except the people of Islam, they said: 'Come, let us deny [our polytheism].' So they said: ﴿By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists﴾. Then Allah sealed their mouths, and their hands and their feet spoke, ﴿and they will not conceal from Allah a [single] statement﴾."

And 'Abd al-Razzaq said: Ma'mar informed us, from a man, from al-Minhal ibn 'Amr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: A man came to Ibn 'Abbas and said: "Things in the Qur'an are conflicting for me." He said: "What are they? Am I doubting the Qur'an?" He said: "It is not doubt, but apparent contradiction." He said: "Then state what conflicts for you from it." He said: "I hear Allah say: ﴿Then their trial will be only that they will say, "By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists"﴾ [al-An'am: 23], and He says ﴿and they will not conceal from Allah a [single] statement﴾; so they have concealed!" Ibn 'Abbas said: "As for His saying ﴿Then their trial will be only that they will say, "By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists"﴾, when they saw on the Day of Resurrection that Allah forgives only the people of Islam, and forgives sins, and does not forgive shirk, and no sin is too great for Him to forgive, the polytheists denied, saying ﴿By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists﴾, hoping that they would be forgiven. Then Allah sealed their mouths, and their hands and their feet spoke of what they used to do. At that point: ﴿On that Day those who disbelieved and disobeyed the Messenger will wish that the earth were leveled over them, and they will not conceal from Allah a [single] statement.﴾"

Juwaybir narrated from al-Dahhak: Nafi' ibn al-Azraq came to Ibn 'Abbas and said: "O Ibn 'Abbas, what about Allah's saying ﴿On that Day those who disbelieved and disobeyed the Messenger will wish that the earth were leveled over them, and they will not conceal from Allah a [single] statement﴾, and His saying ﴿By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists﴾?" Ibn 'Abbas said to him: "I think you got up from among your companions and said, 'Let me throw at Ibn 'Abbas the ambiguous verses of the Qur'an.' When you return to them, inform them that Allah will gather the people on the Day of Resurrection in one open plain. The polytheists will say: 'Indeed Allah does not accept anything from anyone except from those who affirmed His oneness.' So they will say: 'Come, let us deny,' and He will question them, and they will say: ﴿By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists﴾." He said: "Then their mouths will be sealed, and their limbs will be made to speak, and their limbs will testify against them that they used to be polytheists. At that point they will wish that the earth were leveled over them, ﴿and they will not conceal from Allah a [single] statement﴾." Narrated by Ibn Jarir.

Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim, on Surah An-Nisa' (4), verses 40–42 (Part 1 of 2):

Almighty God informs that He does not wrong any of His servants on the Day of Resurrection, not even to the weight of a mustard seed, nor to the weight of an atom. Rather, He will repay them in full for it and multiply it for them if it is a good deed, as He says: ﴿And We will set up the scales of justice for the Day of Resurrection, so no soul will be wronged in anything. Even if it be the weight of a mustard seed, We will bring it forth. And sufficient are We as reckoners.﴾ [Al-Anbiya': 47] [[Added from manuscripts R and A; in manuscript H: "the verse".]]

God also says, relating what Luqman said: ﴿O my son, indeed if it is the weight of a mustard seed and should be within a rock or in the heavens or in the earth, Allah will bring it forth. Indeed, Allah is Subtle and Acquainted.﴾ [Luqman: 16] [[Added from manuscripts R and A; in manuscript H: "the verse".]]

And He says: ﴿On that day mankind will depart in scattered groups to be shown their deeds. So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it.﴾

In the Two Sahihs (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim), from the hadith of Zayd ibn Aslam, from 'Ata' ibn Yasar, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), in the lengthy hadith of intercession (al-shafa'ah), in which it is said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will say: "Go back, and whoever you find in his heart the weight of a mustard seed [[In manuscripts R and A: "atom".]] of faith, bring him out of the Fire." And in another wording: "The least, the least, the least, the weight of an atom of faith, bring him out of the Fire." So they will bring out a great multitude. Then Abu Sa'id said: "Recite, if you wish: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not wrong even the weight of an atom, and if it is a good deed, He will double it and give from Himself a great reward.﴾" [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 7439; Sahih Muslim, no. 183.]]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj narrated to us, 'Isa ibn Yunus narrated to us, from Harun ibn 'Antarah [[In manuscript A: "'Anbarah".]], from 'Abdullah ibn al-Sa'ib, from Zadhan, who said: 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud said: "The slave and the slave-woman will be brought on the Day of Resurrection, and a caller will call out over the heads of the first and the last: 'This is so-and-so the son of so-and-so; whoever has a right, let him come to his right.'"

Then a woman will rejoice that she has a right against her father, her brother, or her husband. Then he recited: ﴿So there will be no ties of kinship among them that Day, nor will they ask about one another.﴾ [Al-Mu'minun: 101]. Then Allah will forgive from His rights whatever He wills, but He will not forgive any of the rights of people. So a platform will be set up for the people and a caller will call: "This is so-and-so the son of so-and-so; whoever has a right, let him come to his right." He will say: "My Lord, the world has perished; from where shall I give them their rights?" He will say: "Take from his good deeds, and give every person with a right his right according to the measure of his claim. If he was a friend of Allah, and there remains for him the weight of an atom, Allah will multiply it for him until He admits him to Paradise because of it." Then he recited to us: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not wrong the weight of an atom, and if it is a good deed, He will double it.﴾ He said: "Enter Paradise." But if he was a wretched slave, the angel will say: "My Lord, his good deeds have run out, and many claimants remain." He will say: "Take from their evil deeds and add them to his evil deeds, then write for him a document to the Fire."

Al-Tabari narrated it through another route from Zadhan, with similar wording. And part of this report has a witness in a sahih hadith.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Abu Nu'aym narrated to us, Fudayl [i.e., ibn Marzuq] narrated to us, from 'Ata' al-'Awfi, who said: 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar narrated to me, saying: This verse was revealed concerning the Bedouins: ﴿Whoever brings a good deed will have ten times its like﴾ [Al-An'am: 160]. A man said: "What about the Muhajirun, O Abu 'Abd al-Rahman?" He said: "There is something better than that: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not wrong the weight of an atom, and if it is a good deed, He will double it and give from Himself a great reward.﴾"

Abu Zur'ah narrated to us, Yahya ibn 'Abdullah ibn Bukayr narrated to us, 'Abdullah ibn Lahi'ah narrated to me, 'Ata' ibn Dinar narrated to me, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr regarding His saying: ﴿And if it is a good deed, He will double it﴾, that the polytheist will have his punishment lightened on the Day of Resurrection, but he will never be brought out of the Fire. And it has been argued for him from the sahih hadith that al-'Abbas said: "O Messenger of Allah, indeed Abu Talib used to protect you and support you; did it benefit him at all?" He said: "Yes, he is in a shallow part of the Fire, and if not for me, he would be in the lowest level of the Fire." [[Al-Bukhari, no. 3883, 6208; Muslim, no. 209.]]

This may be specific to Abu Talib among the disbelievers, based on what Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi narrated in his Sunan [[In manuscripts D, R and A: "his Musnad".]]: 'Imran narrated to us, Qatadah narrated to us, from Anas that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah does not wrong a believer in a good deed; he is rewarded for it with provision in this world and recompensed for it in the Hereafter. As for the disbeliever, he is fed for his good deeds in this world, and when the Day of Resurrection comes, he will have no good deed." [[Musnad al-Tayalisi, no. 47 (Minhat al-Ma'bud); also narrated by Muslim, no. 2808, through Yazid ibn Harun from Hammam ibn Yahya from Qatadah with similar wording.]]

Abu Hurayrah, 'Ikrimah, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Hasan, Qatadah and al-Dahhak said regarding His saying: ﴿and give from Himself a great reward﴾: it means Paradise.

Imam Ahmad said: 'Abd al-Samad narrated to us, Sulayman [i.e., ibn al-Mughirah] narrated to us, from 'Ali ibn Zayd, from Abu 'Uthman, who said: It reached me from Abu Hurayrah that he said: "It reached me that Allah, Exalted is He, gives His believing servant one thousand thousand good deeds for a single good deed." He said: Then it so happened that I set out for Hajj or 'Umrah, and I met him and said: "It has reached me that you say: 'I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: Allah gives His believing servant one thousand thousand good deeds for a single good deed.'" Abu Hurayrah said: "No, rather I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, gives him two thousand thousand good deeds.'" Then he recited: ﴿He will multiply it and give from Himself a great reward.﴾ So who can measure its measure? [[Musnad Ahmad (5/521).]]

Ahmad also narrated it in another way, saying: Yazid narrated to us, Mubarak ibn Fudalah narrated to us, from 'Ali ibn Zayd, from Abu 'Uthman, who said: I came to Abu Hurayrah and said to him: "It has reached me that you say: Indeed a good deed is multiplied by one thousand thousand good deeds?" He said: "And what amazes you about that? By Allah, I heard [meaning the Prophet (ﷺ)] — thus my father said — saying: 'Indeed Allah multiplies the good deed by two thousand thousand good deeds.'" [[Musnad Ahmad (2/296).]]

'Ali ibn Zayd has strange reports in his narrations, and Allah knows best.

* * *

As for His saying: ﴿So how will it be when We bring from every nation a witness, and We bring you as a witness against these?﴾, Almighty God says, informing of the terror of the Day of Resurrection and the severity of its matter and its affair: How will the matter and the situation be on the Day of Resurrection, when He brings from every nation a witness, meaning the prophets, peace be upon them? As He says: ﴿And the earth will shine with the light of its Lord, and the record will be placed, and the prophets and the witnesses will be brought forward, and judgment will be made between them with truth, and they will not be wronged.﴾ [Az-Zumar: 69] [[Added from manuscripts R and A; in manuscript H: "the verse".]] And He says: ﴿And the Day We raise up from every nation a witness against them from among themselves, and We bring you as a witness against these. And We have sent down to you the Book as clarification for all things, and guidance and mercy and good tidings for the Muslims.﴾ [An-Nahl: 89] [[Added from manuscripts R and A; in manuscript H: "the verse".]]

Al-Bukhari said: Muhammad ibn Yusuf narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, from 'Ubaydah, from 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said to me: "Recite to me." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, shall I recite to you when it was revealed to you?" He said: "Yes, indeed I love to hear it from others." So I recited Surah An-Nisa', until I reached this verse: ﴿So how will it be when We bring from every nation a witness, and We bring you as a witness against these?﴾ He said: "Enough for now." And his eyes were overflowing with tears.

He [al-Bukhari] and Muslim also narrated it from the hadith of al-A'mash, with the same chain. [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 5050; Sahih Muslim, no. 800.]] It has been narrated through multiple routes from Ibn Mas'ud, so it is established as a statement of his (mawquf). Ahmad narrated it through the routes of Abu Hayyan and Abu Razin, from him.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Bakr ibn Abi al-Dunya narrated to us, al-Salt ibn Mas'ud al-Jahdari narrated to us, Fudayl ibn Sulayman narrated to us, Yunus ibn Muhammad ibn Fadalah al-Ansari narrated to us, from his father, who said, and my father was among those who accompanied the Prophet (ﷺ): The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came to them in Banu Zafar, and he sat on the rock that is in Banu Zafar today, and with him were Ibn Mas'ud, Mu'adh ibn Jabal, and some of his companions. The Prophet (ﷺ) commanded a reciter, and he recited until he came to this verse: ﴿So how will it be when We bring from every nation a witness, and We bring you as a witness against these?﴾ Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) wept until his jaw and his sides trembled, and he said: "O Lord, I bore witness against those among whom I am; so how about those whom I have not seen?" [[Narrated by al-Baghawi in his Mu'jam, and from his route by al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (19/243), through al-Salt ibn Mas'ud al-Jahdari. Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (7/4): "its narrators are trustworthy (thiqat)."]]

Ibn Jarir said: 'Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Zuhri narrated to me, Sufyan narrated to us, from al-Mas'udi, from Ja'far ibn 'Amr ibn Hurayth, from his father, from 'Abdullah [i.e., Ibn Mas'ud], regarding ﴿So how will it be when We bring from every nation a witness﴾, he said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "A witness over them as long as I am among them; but when You take me, You will be the Watcher over them."

As for what Abu 'Abdullah al-Qurtubi mentioned in al-Tadhkirah [[Al-Tadhkirah fi Ahwal al-Mawta wa Umur al-Akhirah (p. 294).]], where he said: Chapter on what has come concerning the testimony of the Prophet (ﷺ) over his nation. He said: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, a man from the Ansar informed us, from al-Minhal ibn 'Amr, who narrated to him that he heard Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib say: "There is no day but that his nation is presented to the Prophet (ﷺ) morning and evening, and he recognizes them by their names and their deeds; therefore he bears witness over them." Allah, Exalted, says: ﴿So how will it be when We bring from every nation a witness, and We bring you as a witness against these?﴾ This is a report (athar), and it has a break in its chain, since in it is an unnamed man, and it is from the words of Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib and is not attributed to the Prophet (ﷺ). Al-Qurtubi did accept it, saying after citing it: "It has already been mentioned that deeds are presented to Allah every Monday and Thursday, and to the prophets, the fathers and the mothers on Friday." He said: "There is no contradiction, since it is possible that our Prophet is specially given what is presented to him every day, and on Friday with the prophets, peace be upon them."

* * *

As for His saying: ﴿On that Day those who disbelieved and disobeyed the Messenger will wish that the earth would be leveled over them﴾, meaning: if it were split open and swallowed them, because of what they see of the terrors of the place of standing, and the disgrace, scandal and rebuke that will befall them. As in His saying: ﴿The Day a man will look at what his hands have sent forth, and the disbeliever will say: "Would that I were dust!"﴾ [[Added from manuscript R; in manuscript H: "the verse".]] And His saying: ﴿and they will not conceal from Allah any statement.﴾ He informs about them that they will confess to everything they did, and they will conceal nothing from Him.

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, Hakkam narrated to us, 'Amr narrated to us, from Mutarrif, from al-Minhal ibn 'Amr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: A man came to Ibn 'Abbas and said: "I heard Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, say (reporting about the polytheists on the Day of Resurrection that they said): ﴿By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists﴾ [al-An'am: 23], and He says in another verse: ﴿and they will not conceal from Allah a [single] statement﴾." Ibn 'Abbas said: "As for His saying ﴿By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists﴾, when they saw that none would enter Paradise except the people of Islam, they said: 'Come, let us deny [our polytheism].' So they said: ﴿By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists﴾. Then Allah sealed their mouths, and their hands and their feet spoke, ﴿and they will not conceal from Allah a [single] statement﴾."

And 'Abd al-Razzaq said: Ma'mar informed us, from a man, from al-Minhal ibn 'Amr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: A man came to Ibn 'Abbas and said: "Things in the Qur'an are conflicting for me." He said: "What are they? Am I doubting the Qur'an?" He said: "It is not doubt, but apparent contradiction." He said: "Then state what conflicts for you from it." He said: "I hear Allah say: ﴿Then their trial will be only that they will say, "By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists"﴾ [al-An'am: 23], and He says ﴿and they will not conceal from Allah a [single] statement﴾; so they have concealed!" Ibn 'Abbas said: "As for His saying ﴿Then their trial will be only that they will say, "By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists"﴾, when they saw on the Day of Resurrection that Allah forgives only the people of Islam, and forgives sins, and does not forgive shirk, and no sin is too great for Him to forgive, the polytheists denied, saying ﴿By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists﴾, hoping that they would be forgiven. Then Allah sealed their mouths, and their hands and their feet spoke of what they used to do. At that point: ﴿On that Day those who disbelieved and disobeyed the Messenger will wish that the earth were leveled over them, and they will not conceal from Allah a [single] statement.﴾"

Juwaybir narrated from al-Dahhak: Nafi' ibn al-Azraq came to Ibn 'Abbas and said: "O Ibn 'Abbas, what about Allah's saying ﴿On that Day those who disbelieved and disobeyed the Messenger will wish that the earth were leveled over them, and they will not conceal from Allah a [single] statement﴾, and His saying ﴿By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists﴾?" Ibn 'Abbas said to him: "I think you got up from among your companions and said, 'Let me throw at Ibn 'Abbas the ambiguous verses of the Qur'an.' When you return to them, inform them that Allah will gather the people on the Day of Resurrection in one open plain. The polytheists will say: 'Indeed Allah does not accept anything from anyone except from those who affirmed His oneness.' So they will say: 'Come, let us deny,' and He will question them, and they will say: ﴿By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists﴾." He said: "Then their mouths will be sealed, and their limbs will be made to speak, and their limbs will testify against them that they used to be polytheists. At that point they will wish that the earth were leveled over them, ﴿and they will not conceal from Allah a [single] statement﴾." Narrated by Ibn Jarir.
