[[Narrated by al-Baghawi in his Mu'jam, and from his route by al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (19/243), through al-Salt ibn Mas'ud al-Jahdari. Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (7/4): "its narrators are trustworthy (thiqat)."]]

Ibn Jarir said: 'Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Zuhri narrated to me, Sufyan narrated to us, from al-Mas'udi, from Ja'far ibn 'Amr ibn Hurayth, from his father, from 'Abdullah [i.e., Ibn Mas'ud], regarding ﴿So how will it be when We bring from every nation a witness﴾, he said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "A witness over them as long as I am among them; but when You take me, You will be the Watcher over them."

As for what Abu 'Abdullah al-Qurtubi mentioned in al-Tadhkirah [[Al-Tadhkirah fi Ahwal al-Mawta wa Umur al-Akhirah (p. 294).]], where he said: Chapter on what has come concerning the testimony of the Prophet (ﷺ) over his nation. He said: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, a man from the Ansar informed us, from al-Minhal ibn 'Amr, who narrated to him that he heard Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib say: "There is no day but that his nation is presented to the Prophet (ﷺ) morning and evening, and he recognizes them by their names and their deeds; therefore he bears witness over them." Allah, Exalted, says: ﴿So how will it be when We bring from every nation a witness, and We bring you as a witness against these?﴾ This is a report (athar), and it has a break in its chain, since in it is an unnamed man, and it is from the words of Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib and is not attributed to the Prophet (ﷺ). Al-Qurtubi did accept it, saying after citing it: "It has already been mentioned that deeds are presented to Allah every Monday and Thursday, and to the prophets, the fathers and the mothers on Friday." He said: "There is no contradiction, since it is possible that our Prophet is specially given what is presented to him every day, and on Friday with the prophets, peace be upon them."

* * *

As for His saying: ﴿On that Day those who disbelieved and disobeyed the Messenger will wish that the earth would be leveled over them﴾, meaning: if it were split open and swallowed them, because of what they see of the terrors of the place of standing, and the disgrace, scandal and rebuke that will befall them. As in His saying: ﴿The Day a man will look at what his hands have sent forth, and the disbeliever will say: "Would that I were dust!"﴾ [[Added from manuscript R; in manuscript H: "the verse".]] And His saying: ﴿and they will not conceal from Allah any statement.﴾ He informs about them that they will confess to everything they did, and they will conceal nothing from Him.

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, Hakkam narrated to us, 'Amr narrated to us, from Mutarrif, from al-Minhal ibn 'Amr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: A man came to Ibn 'Abbas and said: "I heard Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, say (reporting about the polytheists on the Day of Resurrection that they said): ﴿By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists﴾ [al-An'am: 23], and He says in another verse: ﴿and they will not conceal from Allah a [single] statement﴾." Ibn 'Abbas said: "As for His saying ﴿By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists﴾, when they saw that none would enter Paradise except the people of Islam, they said: 'Come, let us deny [our polytheism].' So they said: ﴿By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists﴾. Then Allah sealed their mouths, and their hands and their feet spoke, ﴿and they will not conceal from Allah a [single] statement﴾."

And 'Abd al-Razzaq said: Ma'mar informed us, from a man, from al-Minhal ibn 'Amr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: A man came to Ibn 'Abbas and said: "Things in the Qur'an are conflicting for me." He said: "What are they? Am I doubting the Qur'an?" He said: "It is not doubt, but apparent contradiction." He said: "Then state what conflicts for you from it." He said: "I hear Allah say: ﴿Then their trial will be only that they will say, "By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists"﴾ [al-An'am: 23], and He says ﴿and they will not conceal from Allah a [single] statement﴾; so they have concealed!" Ibn 'Abbas said: "As for His saying ﴿Then their trial will be only that they will say, "By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists"﴾, when they saw on the Day of Resurrection that Allah forgives only the people of Islam, and forgives sins, and does not forgive shirk, and no sin is too great for Him to forgive, the polytheists denied, saying ﴿By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists﴾, hoping that they would be forgiven. Then Allah sealed their mouths, and their hands and their feet spoke of what they used to do. At that point: ﴿On that Day those who disbelieved and disobeyed the Messenger will wish that the earth were leveled over them, and they will not conceal from Allah a [single] statement.﴾"

Juwaybir narrated from al-Dahhak: Nafi' ibn al-Azraq came to Ibn 'Abbas and said: "O Ibn 'Abbas, what about Allah's saying ﴿On that Day those who disbelieved and disobeyed the Messenger will wish that the earth were leveled over them, and they will not conceal from Allah a [single] statement﴾, and His saying ﴿By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists﴾?" Ibn 'Abbas said to him: "I think you got up from among your companions and said, 'Let me throw at Ibn 'Abbas the ambiguous verses of the Qur'an.' When you return to them, inform them that Allah will gather the people on the Day of Resurrection in one open plain. The polytheists will say: 'Indeed Allah does not accept anything from anyone except from those who affirmed His oneness.' So they will say: 'Come, let us deny,' and He will question them, and they will say: ﴿By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists﴾." He said: "Then their mouths will be sealed, and their limbs will be made to speak, and their limbs will testify against them that they used to be polytheists. At that point they will wish that the earth were leveled over them, ﴿and they will not conceal from Allah a [single] statement﴾." Narrated by Ibn Jarir.

Allah forbids His believing servants from performing the prayer while intoxicated, to the point that the one praying does not know what he is saying, and from approaching its place, which is the mosques, while in a state of major impurity (junub), except for one who is passing through from one door to another without staying. This was before the prohibition of wine (khamr), as indicated by the hadith we mentioned in Surat al-Baqarah, at His words [Exalted is He] ﴿They ask you about wine and gambling. Say: In them is great sin﴾ [al-Baqarah: 219]. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited it to Umar, and he said: "O Allah, make clear to us a satisfying explanation regarding wine." Then when this verse was revealed, he recited it to him, and he said: "O Allah, make clear to us a satisfying explanation regarding wine." So they did not drink wine at the times of the prayers. Then when the saying of Allah [Exalted is He] was revealed: ﴿O you who believe, wine, gambling, stone idols, and divining arrows are only an abomination from the work of Satan, so avoid it that you may be successful﴾ up to His words: ﴿So will you not desist?﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 90-91], Umar said: "We have desisted, we have desisted."

In the narration of Isra'il, from Abu Ishaq, from Amr (who is Ibn Shurahbil), from Umar ibn al-Khattab, concerning the story of the prohibition of wine, he mentioned the hadith, and in it: Then the verse in Surat an-Nisa' was revealed: ﴿O you who believe, do not approach the prayer while you are intoxicated until you know what you are saying﴾. So the caller of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, when the prayer was about to be established (iqamah), would call out: "Let no intoxicated person approach the prayer." This is the wording of Abu Dawud.

They mentioned, regarding the occasion of revelation of this verse, what Ibn Abi Hatim narrated:

Yunus ibn Habib told us, Abu Dawud told us, Shu'bah told us, Simak ibn Harb informed me, saying: I heard Mus'ab ibn Sa'd narrating from Sa'd, who said: Four verses were revealed concerning me. A man from the Ansar prepared food and invited some of the Muhajirun and some of the Ansar. We ate and drank until we became intoxicated, then we boasted, and a man raised the jawbone of a camel and struck Sa'd's nose with it, so Sa'd's nose was disfigured. That was before wine was prohibited, and then the verse was revealed: ﴿O you who believe, do not approach the prayer while you are intoxicated﴾, to the end of the verse.

The hadith in full is in Sahih Muslim through the narration of Shu'bah. And the people of the Sunan, except Ibn Majah, narrated it through several chains from Simak with it.

Another occasion: Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn Ammar told us, Abd al-Rahman ibn Abd Allah al-Dashtaki told us, Abu Ja'far told us, from Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, from Ali ibn Abi Talib, who said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf prepared food for us, invited us, and gave us wine to drink. The wine took effect on us, the time of the prayer came, and they put forward a certain man, who recited: "Say, O you disbelievers, I do not worship what you worship, and we worship what you worship." Then Allah revealed: ﴿O you who believe, do not approach the prayer while you are intoxicated until you know what you are saying﴾.

Thus Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it, and al-Tirmidhi narrated it likewise from Abd Allah ibn Humayd, from Abd al-Rahman al-Dashtaki, with it, and said: "Hasan sahih."

Ibn Jarir also narrated it from Muhammad ibn Bashshar, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi, from Sufyan al-Thawri, from Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Abu Abd al-Rahman, from Ali, that he and Abd al-Rahman and another man drank wine, and Abd al-Rahman led them in prayer and recited: "Say, O you disbelievers," and garbled it, so the verse was revealed: ﴿Do not approach the prayer while you are intoxicated﴾.

Likewise Abu Dawud and al-Nasa'i narrated it from the hadith of al-Thawri, with it. Ibn Jarir also narrated, from Ibn Humayd, from Jarir, from Ata', from Abu Abd Allah al-Sulami, who said: Ali was among a group of the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ in the house of Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf. They ate, then wine was brought to them and they drank from it, and that was before wine was prohibited. The prayer came, and they put Ali forward, and he recited with them: "Say, O you disbelievers," but did not recite it as it should be, so Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿O you who believe, do not approach the prayer while you are intoxicated﴾.

Then he said: Al-Muthanna told me, al-Hajjaj ibn al-Minhal told us, Hammad told us, from Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Abd Allah ibn Habib, who is Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, that Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf prepared food and drink, invited a group of the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ, and led them in the Maghrib prayer, and recited: "Say, O you disbelievers. I worship not what you worship. Nor are you worshippers of what I worship. And I am not a worshipper of what you have worshipped. For you is your religion, and for me is my religion." Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed this verse: ﴿O you who believe, do not approach the prayer while you are intoxicated until you know what you are saying﴾.

Al-Awfi narrated from Ibn Abbas, concerning His words: ﴿O you who believe, do not approach the prayer while you are intoxicated [until you know what you are saying]﴾, that men used to come to the prayer while intoxicated, before wine was prohibited, so Allah said: ﴿Do not approach the prayer while you are intoxicated﴾, to the end of the verse. Ibn Jarir narrated it. Likewise Abu Razin and Mujahid said. Abd al-Razzaq said, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: "They used to avoid intoxication at the times of the prayers, then it was abrogated (nusikha) by the prohibition of wine."

Al-Dahhak said, concerning His words: ﴿O you who believe, do not approach the prayer while you are intoxicated﴾: He did not mean by it the intoxication of wine, but rather He meant the drowsiness of sleep. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it.

Then Ibn Jarir said: The correct view is that what is meant is the intoxication of drink. He said: The prohibition is not directed at the intoxicated person who does not understand the address, because that is in the category of the insane, rather the prohibition is addressed to the one who is drunk (thamil) and understands the obligation.

This is the summary of what he said. Many of the usuliyyun (jurists of legal theory) have also mentioned it, namely that address (khitab) is directed to one who understands speech, not to the intoxicated person who does not know what is said to him, for understanding is a condition of obligation (taklif). It may also be that the intended meaning is a warning (ta'rid) against intoxication entirely, since they are commanded to pray at the five times of the day and night, so the drinker of wine cannot consistently perform the prayer at its times. And Allah knows best. On this view it is like His words: ﴿O you who believe, fear Allah with the fear due to Him, and do not die except as Muslims﴾ [Al 'Imran: 102], which is a command to them to prepare for death upon Islam and to persist in obedience for that purpose.

* *

His words: ﴿until you know what you are saying﴾. This is the best that is said in defining the intoxicated person: he is the one who does not know what he is saying, for the one who is intoxicated has confusion in recitation and lack of reflection and humility in it. Imam Ahmad said:

Abd al-Samad told us, my father told us, Ayyub told us, from Abu Qilabah, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "If one of you becomes drowsy while praying, let him leave and finish until he knows what he is saying." Al-Bukhari alone narrated it without Muslim, and he and al-Nasa'i narrated it from the hadith of Ayyub with it. In some wordings of the hadith: "Perhaps he goes to seek forgiveness and ends up cursing himself."

* *

His words: ﴿nor in a state of major impurity, except for those passing through, until you have washed﴾. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn Ammar told us, Abd al-Rahman al-Dashtaki told us, Abu Ja'far al-Razi informed us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from Ata' ibn Yasar, from Ibn Abbas concerning His words: ﴿nor in a state of major impurity, except for those passing through, until you have washed﴾, he said: Do not enter the mosque while you are in a state of major impurity, except passing through, he said: one passes by it passing without sitting. Then he said: It has been related from Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, Anas, Abu Ubaydah, Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, Abu al-Duha, Ata', Mujahid, Masruq, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, Zayd ibn Aslam, Abu Malik, Amr ibn Dinar, al-Hakam ibn Utaybah, Ikrimah, al-Hasan al-Basri, Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Ansari, Ibn Shihab, and Qatadah, something similar to this.

Ibn Jarir said: Al-Muthanna told me, Abu Salih told us, al-Layth told me, Yazid ibn Abi Habib told me, concerning the words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿nor in a state of major impurity, except for those passing through﴾, that some men of the Ansar had their doors opening onto the mosque, and they would become in a state of major impurity without having water with them, so they would come to the water and find no passage except through the mosque, so Allah revealed: ﴿nor in a state of major impurity, except for those passing through﴾.

What supports the correctness of what Yazid ibn Abi Habib said, may Allah have mercy on him, is what is established in Sahih al-Bukhari: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Block every window (khawkhah) opening onto the mosque except the window of Abu Bakr." He said this at the end of his life ﷺ, knowing that Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, would succeed him in authority and would need to enter the mosque often for important matters concerning the affairs of the Muslims, so he commanded that the doors opening onto the mosque be blocked except his door, may Allah be pleased with him. As for the one who narrates "except the door of Ali," as occurs in some of the Sunan, it is an error, and the correct version is what is established in the Sahih. From this verse many of the imams have argued that it is forbidden for one in a state of major impurity to remain in the mosque, but it is permissible for him to pass through. Likewise the menstruating woman and the woman in postnatal bleeding (nifas) are in the same category; however, some said that their passing through is prohibited for fear of soiling the mosque. Others said: if each of them is safe from soiling it while passing, then passing is permitted for them, otherwise not.

It is established in Sahih Muslim from Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me: "Pass me the prayer mat (khumrah) from the mosque." I said: "I am menstruating." He said: "Indeed your menstruation is not in your hand." And he has a similar narration from Abu Hurayrah. In it is evidence for the permissibility of a menstruating woman passing through the mosque, and the woman in postnatal bleeding is in the same meaning, and Allah knows best.

And Abu Dawud related, from the hadith of Aflat ibn Khalifa [in one manuscript: "Khaliqa"] al-Amiri, from Jasra bint Dajaja, from Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Indeed I do not make the mosque lawful for a menstruating woman or for one in a state of janabah." [Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 232, and Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 645, from the hadith of Umm Salama. Al-Busiri said in al-Zawa'id (1/230): "This isnad is weak, its narrator Mahdud is not declared trustworthy, and Abu al-Khattab is unknown."] Abu Muslim al-Khattabi said: A group of scholars declared this hadith weak, and they said: Aflat is unknown. However, Ibn Majah related it from the hadith of Abu al-Khattab al-Hajari, from Mahdud al-Dhuhli, from Jasra, from Umm Salama, from the Prophet ﷺ, with it. Abu Zur'a al-Razi said: They say, "Jasra from Umm Salama," but the correct version is "Jasra from Aisha."

As for what Abu Isa al-Tirmidhi related from the hadith of Salim ibn Abi Hafsa, from Atiyya, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "O Ali, it is not lawful for anyone to be junub in this mosque except me and you." This is a weak hadith that is not established, for this Salim is abandoned (matruk), and his shaykh Atiyya is weak. [Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 3727.] And Allah knows best.

Another opinion regarding the meaning of the verse: Ibn Abi Hatim said: Al-Mundhir ibn Shadhan related to us, Ubayd Allah ibn Musa related to us, Ibn Abi Layla informed me, from al-Minhal, from Zirr ibn Hubaysh, from Ali regarding ﴿and not junub except as travellers passing through﴾: "He should not approach the prayer, unless he is a traveller who has become junub and cannot find water, so he prays [with tayammum] until he finds water."

Then he related it through another route, from al-Minhal ibn Amr, from Zirr, from Ali ibn Abi Talib, and mentioned it. He said: It is also related from Ibn Abbas in one of the narrations, and from Sa'id ibn Jubayr and al-Dahhak, something similar.

Ibn Jarir related, through the hadith of Waki', from Ibn Abi Layla, from al-Minhal, from Abbad ibn Abd Allah or from Zirr ibn Hubaysh, from Ali, and mentioned it. And he related it through the route of al-Awfi and Abu Mijlaz, from Ibn Abbas, and mentioned it. It is also related from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Mujahid, al-Hasan ibn Muslim, al-Hakam ibn Utayba, Zayd ibn Aslam, and his son Abd al-Rahman, something similar. And it is related through the route of Ibn Jurayj, from Abd Allah ibn Kathir, who said: We used to hear that it refers to [the state of] travel.

The opinion is supported by the hadith which Imam Ahmad and the authors of the Sunan related, from the hadith of Abu Qilaba, from Amr ibn Bujdan, from Abu Dharr, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The pure earth is the purification of the Muslim, even if he does not find water for ten years. When you find water, then touch it to your skin, for that is better." [Musnad Ahmad (5/180); Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 332; Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 124; Sunan al-Nasa'i (1/171).]

Then Ibn Jarir said, after relating the two opinions: "The more preferable is the view of the one who says: ﴿and not junub except as travellers passing through﴾, meaning, except those passing through a path in it. This is because He has already explained the ruling for the traveller who lacks water while junub, in His saying: ﴿or if you are ill, or on a journey, or one of you comes from the place of relieving oneself, or you have touched women, and you find no water, then perform tayammum with clean earth﴾ [al-Ma'ida: 6], to the end. So it is known from this that His saying: ﴿and not junub except as travellers passing through until you wash﴾, if it were meant to refer to the traveller, would have no understood purpose in repeating its mention in His saying: ﴿or if you are ill or on a journey﴾, and its ruling has already been mentioned before that. If this is so, then the interpretation of the verse is: O you who believe, do not approach the mosques for prayer while you are intoxicated until you know what you are saying, and do not approach them either while junub until you wash, except as travellers passing through. He said: The word al-'abir al-sabil means one who passes through and crosses [a way]. It is said of it: 'I crossed this road, so I cross it (a'buruhu) crossing ('abran) and crossing ('ububan).' From it it is said: 'So-and-so crossed the river' when he traversed it and went beyond it. And from it it is said of a camel strong for journeys: she is 'ubr asfar and 'abr asfar, because of her strength in crossing journeys."

This view which he supported is the view of the majority (jumhur), and it is the apparent meaning of the verse. It seems that He, exalted is He, forbade attempting the prayer in an incomplete state that contradicts its purpose, and forbade entering its place in an incomplete state, which is janabah, which distances one from the prayer and from its place as well. And Allah knows best.

* *

His saying: ﴿until you wash﴾ is evidence for what the three imams went to: Abu Hanifa, Malik, and al-Shafi'i, that it is forbidden for the junub to remain in the mosque until he washes or performs tayammum, if he cannot find water or is unable to use it in some way. Imam Ahmad went to the view that whenever the junub performs wudu, it is permissible for him to remain in the mosque, because of what he related, along with Sa'id ibn Mansur in his Sunan, with a sound isnad, that the Companions used to do that. Sa'id ibn Mansur said:

Abd al-Aziz ibn Muhammad [that is, al-Darawardi] related to us, from Hisham ibn Sa'd, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from Ata ibn Yasar, who said: "I saw men from among the companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sitting in the mosque while they were junub, when they had performed wudu for prayer." This isnad is sound according to the condition of Muslim. And Allah knows best.

* *

His saying: ﴿or if you are ill, or on a journey, or one of you comes from the place of relieving oneself, or you have touched women, and you find no water, then perform tayammum with clean earth﴾. As for the illness that permits tayammum, it is that in which, if one uses water, there is fear of losing a limb, or of disfigurement, or of prolonging the recovery. Some scholars permitted tayammum merely because of illness, due to the generality of the verse. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father related to us, Abu Ghassan Malik ibn Isma'il related to us, Qays related to us, from Khasif, from Mujahid regarding His saying: ﴿and if you are ill﴾, he said: It was revealed concerning a man from the Ansar who was ill and could not stand up to perform wudu, and had no servant to bring it to him, so he came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and mentioned that to him, so Allah revealed this verse.

This is a mursal narration (one in which a Successor reports directly from the Prophet ﷺ, omitting the Companion). Travel is well known, and there is no difference in it between a long and a short journey.

* *

His saying: ﴿or one of you comes from the place of relieving oneself﴾. Al-ghA'it is a lowered tract of land; it is used as a euphemism for defecation, which is the minor impurity (hadath al-asghar).

As for His saying: ﴿or you have touched women﴾, it is read as "lamastum" and as "lamastum" [with the alif, lamastum]. The commentators and scholars differed on the meaning of this, into two opinions:

One of them: That it is a euphemism for intercourse, based on His saying: ﴿And if you divorce them before you have touched them [tamassuhunna] and you have already specified for them an obligation, then half of what you specified﴾ [al-Baqara: 237], and the Exalted said: ﴿O you who believe, when you marry believing women and then divorce them before you have touched them [tamassuhunna], then you have no waiting period for them to count﴾ [al-Ahzab: 49].

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj related to us, Waki' related to us, from Sufyan, from Abu Ishaq, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿or you have touched women﴾, he said: "Intercourse." It is related from Ali, Ubayy ibn Ka'b, Mujahid, Tawus, al-Hasan, Ubayd ibn Umayr, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Sha'bi, Qatada, and Muqatil ibn Hayyan, something similar.

Ibn Jarir said: Humayd ibn Mas'ada related to me, Yazid ibn Zuray' related to us, Shu'ba related to us, from Abu Bishr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: "They mentioned al-lams (touching), and some of the mawali (non-Arab clients) said: 'It does not mean intercourse.' And some of the Arabs said: 'Al-lams is intercourse.' So I came to Ibn Abbas and said to him: 'Some of the mawali and the Arabs have disagreed about al-lams. The mawali said: "It is not intercourse," and the Arabs said: "It is intercourse."' He said: 'Which of the two groups were you from?' I said: 'I was from the mawali.' He said: 'The group of the mawali has lost. Indeed al-lams, al-mass, and al-mubasharah all mean intercourse, but Allah uses euphemism for whatever He wills by whatever He wills.'"

Then he related it from Ibn Bashshar, from Ghundar, from Shu'ba, with it, similarly. Then he related it from other routes from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, similarly.

And in the same way he said: Ya'qub related to me, Hushaym related to us, who said: Abu Bishr related to us, Sa'id ibn Jubayr informed us, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "Al-lams, al-mass, and al-mubasharah: intercourse, but Allah uses euphemism with whatever He wills."

Abd al-Hamid ibn Bayan related to us, Ishaq al-Azraq informed us, from Sufyan, from Asim al-Ahwal, from Bakr ibn Abd Allah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "Al-mulamasa is intercourse, but Allah is generous and uses euphemism with whatever He wills."

It has been authentically related through more than one route from Abd Allah ibn Abbas that he said this. Then Ibn Jarir related it from some of those whom Ibn Abi Hatim had reported from.

Then Ibn Jarir said: Others said: Allah meant by that every touching with the hand or with other parts of the human body, and He made wudu obligatory upon everyone who touches with any part of his body a part of her body in a manner that leads to something [sexual].

Then he said: Ibn Bashshar related to us, Abd al-Rahman related to us, Sufyan related to us, from Mukhariq, from Tariq [in one manuscript: "Tawus"], from Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, who said: "Al-lams is what is less than intercourse."

He related it through many routes from Ibn Mas'ud with the same wording. It is also related through the hadith of al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, from Abu Ubayda, from Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, who said: "A kiss is a touch, and in it is wudu."

And he said: Yunus related to me, Ibn Wahb informed us, Ubayd Allah ibn Umar informed me, from Nafi', that Ibn Umar used to perform wudu after kissing a woman, and he considered wudu obligatory in it, and he would say: "It is from al-lima's (touching)."

Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Jarir also related, through the route of Shu'ba, from Mukhariq, from Tariq, from Abd Allah, who said: "Al-lams is what is less than intercourse."

Then Ibn Abi Hatim said: It is related from Ibn Umar, Ubayda, Abu Uthman al-Nahdi, Abu Ubayda (meaning Ibn Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud), Amir al-Sha'bi, Thabit ibn al-Hajjaj, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, and Zayd ibn Aslam, something similar.

I say: Malik related from al-Zuhri, from Salim ibn Abd Allah ibn Umar, from his father, that he used to say: "A man's kissing of his wife and his touching her with his hand is from al-mulamasa. So whoever kisses his wife or touches her with his hand, wudu is obligatory upon him."

Al-Hafiz Abu al-Hasan al-Daraqutni [in his Sunan] related something similar from the Commander of the Believers Umar ibn al-Khattab. But we have related from him through another route that he used to kiss his wife, then pray without performing wudu. So the reports from him differ, and what he said about wudu, if it is authentically from him, is to be understood as recommended (istihbab). And Allah knows best.

The doctrine that wudu' is obligatory after touching is the view of al-Shafi'i and his companions, of Malik, and the well-known position of Ahmad ibn Hanbal, may Allah have mercy on them all. The proponent of this view said: In this verse the reading "lamastum" (you have touched) and "lamastum" (you have touched) has been recited, and in the Shari'ah "al-lams" (touching) is applied to feeling with the hand. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And even if We had sent down to you a book on paper, and they had touched it with their hands﴾ [al-An'am: 7], meaning they felt it [in r and a: "masasuh"]. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to Ma'iz, when he confessed to fornication and was being given an opportunity to retract his confession: "Perhaps you kissed, or touched." [Related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. (6824), Abu Dawud in his Sunan, no. (4427), and Ahmad in his Musnad (1/238), from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Abbas.] And in the sound hadith: "The hand's adultery is touching." 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, said: "Hardly a day passed but that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would come round to us, and kiss and touch." And among it is what is established in the two Sahihs: that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) forbade the sale of mulamasah [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (2146), and Sahih Muslim, no. (1511)], and it returns to feeling with the hand on both interpretations. They said: It is also applied in the language to feeling with the hand, just as it is applied to intercourse. The poet said:
"And I touched his palm with my palm, seeking wealth..."

They also cited the hadith related by Imam Ahmad: Abdullah [in r and a: "Abd al-Rahman"] ibn Mahdi and Abu Sa'id narrated to us, both saying: Za'idah narrated to us, from Abd al-Malik ibn Umair. And Abu Sa'id said: Abd al-Malik ibn Umair narrated to us, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, from Mu'adh, who said: A man came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, what do you say about a man who met a woman he did not know, and so he did everything with her that a man does with his wife, except that he did not have intercourse with her?" He said: Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed this verse: ﴿And establish prayer at the two ends of the day and at the approach of the night. Indeed, good deeds do away with misdeeds. That is a reminder for those who remember﴾ [Hud: 114]. He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: "Perform ablution, then pray." Mu'adh said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, is this for him alone, or for the believers in general?" He said: "Rather, it is for the believers in general."

At-Tirmidhi related it from the hadith of Za'idah with the same chain and said: "It is not connected." An-Nasa'i related it from the hadith of Shu'bah, from Abd al-Malik ibn Umair, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla as a mursal report [Related by al-Nasa'i in al-Kubra, no. (7328), but it is connected; al-Mizzi mentioned it in Tuhfat al-Ashraf, no. (11343), and attributed it to al-Nasa'i as a mursal report, and Allah knows best].

They said: So he commanded him to perform wudu' because he touched the woman and did not have intercourse with her. It is answered that it is disconnected between Abi Layla and Mu'adh, for he did not meet him. Furthermore, it is possible that he only commanded him to perform wudu' and pray for repentance, as was mentioned in the hadith of the Siddiq [may Allah be pleased with him]: "No servant commits a sin, then performs ablution and prays two rak'ahs, but Allah forgives him," and the hadith is mentioned in Surah Al 'Imran at His words: ﴿They remember Allah and ask forgiveness for their sins [and who forgives sins except Allah?]﴾ [Al 'Imran: 135].

Then Ibn Jarir said: The more correct of the two opinions regarding this is the view of the one who said: by His words ﴿or you have touched women﴾ Allah means intercourse and nothing else of the meanings of touching, because of the soundness of the report from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that he kissed some of his wives and then prayed without performing wudu'. Then he said: Ismail ibn Musa al-Suddi narrated this to me, saying: Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash informed us, from al-A'mash, from Habib ibn Abi Thabit, from Urwah, from A'ishah, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) would perform wudu', then kiss, then pray and not perform wudu' [Tafsir al-Tabari (8/396)].

Then he said: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Waki' narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Habib, from Urwah, from A'ishah: that the Prophet (ﷺ) kissed some of his wives, then went out to the prayer without performing wudu'. I said: "Who is she, other than you?" And she laughed.

Thus Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah related it from a group of their teachers, from Waki', with the same chain [Tafsir al-Tabari (8/396); Sunan Abi Dawud, no. (180); Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (86); Sunan Ibn Majah, no. (502)].

Then Abu Dawud said: It is related from al-Thawri that he said: Habib narrated to us only from Urwah al-Muzani. Yahya al-Qattan said to a man: "Relate from me that this hadith is like nothing at all." Al-Tirmidhi said: I heard al-Bukhari weaken this hadith, and he said: Habib ibn Abi Thabit did not hear from Urwah.

It occurs in the narration of Ibn Majah: from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Ali ibn Muhammad al-Tanafisi, from Waki', from al-A'mash, from Habib ibn Abi Thabit, from Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, from A'ishah.

More explicit than this is what Imam Ahmad related in his Musnad, from the hadith of Hisham ibn Urwah, from his father, from A'ishah [in a: "A'ishah with it"]. This is explicit that it is Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, and his saying "Who is she, other than you?" then she laughed supports it [Musnad (6/210), but it is through the chain of Habib ibn Abi Thabit from Urwah].

However, Abu Dawud related from Ibrahim ibn Makhlad al-Taliqani, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Maghra', from al-A'mash, who said: Companions of ours narrated to us, from Urwah al-Muzani, from A'ishah [in r: "Urwah"], and mentioned it. And Allah knows best.

Ibn Jarir also said: Abu Zayd Umar ibn Shabbah narrated to us, from Shihab ibn Abbad; Mandal ibn Ali narrated to us, from Layth, from Ata', from A'ishah. And from Abu Rawq, from Ibrahim al-Taymi, from A'ishah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would kiss me after wudu', then he would not renew the wudu' [Tafsir al-Tabari (8/397)].

Imam Ahmad said: Waki' narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu Rawq al-Hamdani, from Ibrahim al-Taymi, from A'ishah: that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) kissed, then prayed and did not perform wudu'.

Abu Dawud and al-Nasa'i related it from the hadith of Yahya al-Qattan (Abu Dawud added: and Ibn Mahdi), both from Sufyan al-Thawri with the same chain [Musnad (6/210); Sunan Abi Dawud, no. (178); Sunan al-Nasa'i (1/39)]. Then Abu Dawud and al-Nasa'i said: Ibrahim al-Taymi did not hear from A'ishah.

Ibn Jarir also said: Sa'id [in a: "Sa'd"] ibn Yahya al-Umawi narrated to us, my father narrated to us, Yazid ibn Sinan narrated to us, from Abd al-Rahman al-Awza'i, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from Abu Salamah, from Umm Salamah: that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would kiss her while fasting, and then would not break his fast, nor renew wudu' [Tafsir al-Tabari (8/399); al-Tabarani related it in al-Awsat, no. (436), Majma' al-Bahrayn, through the chain of Sa'id ibn Yahya al-Umawi. Al-Haythami said in Majma' al-Zawa'id (1/247): "In it is Yazid ibn Sinan al-Rahawi, whom Ahmad, Yahya and Ibn al-Madini weakened, while al-Bukhari and Abu Hatim declared him reliable; Marwan ibn Mu'awiyah strengthened him, and the rest of his narrators are trustworthy."]

He also said: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Hafs ibn Ghiyath narrated to us, from Hajjaj, from Amr ibn Shu'ayb, from Zaynab al-Sahmiyyah, from the Prophet (ﷺ): that he would kiss and then pray without performing wudu'.

Ahmad also related it from Muhammad ibn Fudayl, from Hajjaj ibn Artah, from Amr ibn Shu'ayb, from Zaynab al-Sahmiyyah, from A'ishah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), with it [Tafsir al-Tabari (8/397); Musnad (6/62)].

* *

As for His words: ﴿But if you find no water, then take clean earth and wipe your faces and hands with it﴾, many jurists have deduced from this verse that tayammum is not permissible for one who lacks water unless he has first searched for it; when he has searched and not found it, then tayammum is permissible for him at that time. They have mentioned the manner of searching in the books of furu' (jurisprudence), as is established in its place, just as is in the two Sahihs, from the hadith of Imran ibn Husayn: that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saw a man who had withdrawn and did not pray with the people, and said: "O so-and-so, what prevented you from praying with the people? Are you not a Muslim man?" He said: Yes, O Messenger of Allah, but I was afflicted with janabah and there was no water. He said: "Take to the clean earth, for it will suffice you." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (348), and Sahih Muslim, no. (682).]

And for this reason He, the Exalted, said: ﴿But if you find no water, then take clean earth﴾. Tayammum linguistically means intention (al-qasd). The Arabs say: "Allah has taken you into His protection (tayammamaka Allahu bi-hifzihi)," meaning He intended you. From it is the saying of Imru' al-Qays [the verse is in Lisan al-Arab by Ibn Manzur, root (d-r-j)]:
"When she saw that death was approaching her, and that the pebbles beneath her feet were crushed..."
"She intended the spring that is near Darij, over which the shade casts its shadow and its moss is thick..."

As for al-sa'id (the clean earth), it is said: it is everything that rises upon the surface of the earth, so that includes dust, sand, trees, stones and plants; this is the view of Malik. It is also said: it is what is of the kind of dust, so it is restricted to dust, sand, orpiment and lime; this is the school of Abu Hanifah. And it is said: it is dust alone; this is the school of al-Shafi'i, Ahmad ibn Hanbal and their companions. They argued with His words, the Exalted: ﴿so it becomes a smooth, barren ground﴾ [al-Kahf: 40], meaning dust that is smooth and clean; and with what is established in Sahih Muslim, from Huthayfah ibn al-Yaman, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "We have been favoured over the people in three ways: our rows have been made like the rows of the angels, the whole earth has been made a place of prostration for us, and its dust has been made a means of purification for us when we do not find water" [Sahih Muslim, no. (522)]. In another wording: "and its dust has been made a means of purification for us when we do not find water." They said: He restricted the purifying quality to dust in a context of favour, so if anything else could take its place, He would have mentioned it along with it.

As for al-tayyib (the clean) here, it is said: it means the lawful. And it is said: what is not impure, as related by Imam Ahmad and the compilers of the Sunan, except Ibn Majah, from the hadith of Abu Qilabah, from Amr ibn Bujdan, from Abu Dharr, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Clean earth is the purification of the Muslim, even if he does not find water for ten years; when he finds it, let him touch his skin with it, for that is better for him."

At-Tirmidhi said: hasan sahih, and Ibn Hibban also declared it sound [previously cited; Ibn Hibban related it in his Sahih (2/303), al-Ihsan]. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar related it in his Musnad from Abu Hurayrah [Musnad al-Bazzar, no. (310), Kashf al-Astar; al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (1/261): "al-Bazzar related it and said: we do not know it to be narrated from Abu Hurayrah except through this route." I say: its narrators are the narrators of the Sahih], and al-Hafiz Abu al-Hasan al-Qattan declared it sound. Ibn Abbas said: "The best of clean earth is the soil of tillage." Ibn Abi Hatim related it, and Ibn Mardawayh raised it to the Prophet in his Tafsir [Also related by al-Shirazi in al-Alqab, as cited in al-Durr al-Manthur of al-Suyuti (2/551)].

* *

As for His words: ﴿then wipe your faces and your hands﴾: tayammum is a substitute for wudu' in purification by it, not that it is a substitute for it in all its limbs; rather, it suffices to wipe only the face and the two hands, by consensus. But the imams differed concerning the manner of tayammum into several opinions.

The first opinion, which is the position of al-Shafi'i in his later (jadid) view, is that one must wipe the face and both hands up to the elbows with two strikes (dharbatayn), because the word "hands" (al-yadayn) is used of what reaches the shoulders and of what reaches the elbows, as in the verse of ablution. It is also used, and intended, for what reaches the palms, as in the verse on theft: ﴿Cut off their hands﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 38]. They said: applying what is unqualified here to what is qualified in the verse of ablution is more appropriate, because of the common factor of purification (al-tahuriyyah).

Some of them mentioned what al-Daraqutni narrated from Ibn 'Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Tayammum (dry ablution with clean earth) is two strikes: one strike for the face, and one strike for the two hands up to the elbows." However, it is not authentic, because its chains contain weak narrators whose narrations are not established by them. [Sunan al-Daraqutni (1/180), through 'Abdullah ibn al-Husayn, from 'Abd al-Rahim ibn Mutarrif, from 'Ali ibn Zabyan, from 'Ubaydullah ibn 'Umar, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, and so on. He then said: "'Ali ibn Zabyan narrated it as a marfu' (attributed to the Prophet) report, while Yahya ibn al-Qattan, Hushaym and others narrated it as a mawquf (ending with Ibn 'Umar), and this is the correct version."]

Abu Dawud narrated from Ibn 'Umar, in a hadith, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) struck his hands on the wall and wiped his face with them, then struck another strike and wiped his forearms with it. However, in its chain is Muhammad ibn Thabit al-'Abdi, whom some of the hadith memorizers declared weak, while others, who were trustworthy, narrated it and made it end with the action of Ibn 'Umar. Al-Bukhari, Abu Zur'ah and Ibn 'Adi said: this is the correct version. Al-Bayhaqi said: the marfu' form of this hadith is munkar (rejected). [Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 331.]

Al-Shafi'i argued with what he narrated from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad, from Abu al-Huwayrith, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mu'awiyah, from al-A'raj, from Ibn al-Summah: that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) performed tayammum and wiped his face and his forearms. [Al-Umm of al-Shafi'i (1/42).]

Ibn Jarir said: Musa ibn Sahl al-Ramli narrated to me, Na'im ibn Hammad narrated to us, Kharijah ibn Mus'ab narrated to us, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Ata', from Musa ibn 'Uqbah, from al-A'raj, from Abu Juhaym, who said: I saw the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) urinating, so I greeted him with salam, and he did not return it until he had finished. Then he went to the wall and struck it with his hands, wiped his face with them, then struck the wall again with his hands and wiped his hands up to the elbows. Then he returned the salam to me. [Tafsir al-Tabari (8/416).]

The second opinion is that it is obligatory to wipe the face and the hands up to the palms with two strikes, and this is the older (qadim) view of al-Shafi'i.

The third opinion is that it is sufficient to wipe the face and the palms with one strike. Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from al-Hakam, from Dharr, from Ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abza, from his father, that a man came to 'Umar and said: "I became junub (in a state of major ritual impurity) and found no water." 'Umar said: "Do not pray." 'Ammar said: "Do you not remember, O Commander of the Faithful, when you and I were on an expedition, became junub, and found no water? As for you, you did not pray; but as for me, I rolled in the dust and prayed. When we came to the Prophet (ﷺ), I mentioned that to him, and he said: 'It would have been sufficient for you.'" And the Prophet (ﷺ) struck the earth with his hand, then blew into it and wiped with it his face and his palms. [Al-Musnad (4/265).]

Ahmad also said: 'Affan narrated to us, Aban narrated to us, Qatadah narrated to us, from 'Azrah [in A: "'Urwah"], from Sa'id ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abza, from his father, from 'Ammar, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said concerning tayammum: "One strike for the face and the palms." [Al-Musnad (4/263).]

Another route: Ahmad said: 'Affan narrated to us, 'Abd al-Wahid narrated to us, Sulayman al-A'mash narrated to us, Shaqiq narrated to us, who said: I was sitting with 'Abdullah (ibn Mas'ud) and Abu Musa. Abu Musa said to 'Abdullah: "If a man did not find water, would he not pray?" 'Abdullah said: "No." Abu Musa said: "Do you not remember when 'Ammar said to 'Umar: 'Do you not remember when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent me and you with camels, and I became junub, so I rolled in the dust? When I returned to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), I informed him, and he laughed and said: "It would have been sufficient for you to say this," and he struck his palms on the earth, then wiped his palms together, and wiped his face with a single wiping, with one strike?" 'Abdullah said: "Indeed, I did not see 'Umar content with that." Abu Musa said to him: "Then what about this verse in Surat al-Nisa': ﴿and you find no water, then take to clean earth﴾?" He said: So 'Abdullah did not know what to say, and he said: "If we had permitted them tayammum, one of them would soon, when the water became cold on his skin, perform tayammum." [Al-Musnad (4/265).]

Allah the Exalted said in the verse of al-Ma'idah: ﴿So wipe your faces and your hands with it﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 6]. Al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, used this as evidence that tayammum must be done with clean dust that has some powder which clings to the face and hands, as he narrated with his chain mentioned earlier from Ibn al-Summah: that he passed by the Prophet (ﷺ) while he was urinating, and he greeted him with salam, but he did not return it, until he stood up to a wall and scraped it with a stick he had with him, then struck his hand on it, then wiped with it his face and forearms.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Allah does not intend to make any hardship for you﴾, meaning: in the religion which He has legislated for you, ﴿but He intends to purify you﴾. Therefore, when you do not find water, He permitted you to turn to tayammum with clean earth. ﴿And to complete His favor upon you that you may be grateful﴾.

For this reason this nation alone was granted the legislation of tayammum, not the rest of the nations, as is established in the two Sahihs (of al-Bukhari and Muslim), from Jabir ibn 'Abdullah, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I have been given five things which no one before me was given: I was made victorious through terror (a month's journey away); the earth was made for me a place of prayer (masjid) and a means of purification (tahur). So whoever among my nation is overtaken by the time of prayer, let him pray (and in another wording: his purification is with him, wherever his place of prayer is). The spoils of war were made lawful for me, though they were not lawful for anyone before me. I was given the intercession. And every prophet was sent specifically to his people, but I have been sent to all of mankind." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 335; Sahih Muslim, no. 521.]

It has also preceded in the hadith of Hudhayfah in Sahih Muslim: "We were favored over the people in three ways: our rows were made like the rows of the angels, the earth was made for us a place of prayer, and its dust is a means of purification when we do not find water."

Allah said in this noble verse: ﴿So wipe your faces and your hands; indeed, Allah is ever Pardoning and Forgiving﴾. Meaning: from His pardon toward you and His forgiveness for you is that He legislated tayammum and permitted you to perform prayer with it when you lack water, as a relief for you and a concession to you. That is because this noble verse contains the glorification of prayer, that it should not be performed in a deficient state, from intoxication until the responsible person becomes sober and understands what he says, or from major ritual impurity (janabah) until he performs ghusl (full bath), or from minor ritual impurity (hadath) until he performs wudu' (ablution), except when he is sick or without water. In that case Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has granted a concession in tayammum in such a state, out of mercy toward His servants, compassion for them, and ease for them. And to Allah belong praise and grace.

**The occasion of revelation of the legislation of tayammum:**

We mention this here because this verse in al-Nisa' was revealed earlier than the verse of al-Ma'idah. Its explanation: this (verse) was revealed before the prohibition of wine became final, and wine was prohibited only after Uhud. It is said: during the Prophet's siege of the Banu al-Nadir, shortly after Uhud. As for al-Ma'idah, it is among the last of what was revealed, especially its beginning. So it is appropriate to mention the occasion here. And with Allah is trust.

Imam Ahmad said: Ibn Numayr narrated to us, Hisham narrated to us, from his father, from 'Aishah: that she borrowed a necklace from Asma', and it was lost. So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent men to search for it, and they found it. The time of prayer came upon them and they had no water, so they prayed without wudu'. They complained of that to the Prophet (ﷺ), so Allah revealed the verse of tayammum. Then Usayd ibn al-Hudayr said to 'Aishah: "May Allah reward you with good. By Allah, no matter ever befell you that you disliked, but Allah made for you and for the Muslims in it good." [Al-Musnad (6/57).]

Another route: Al-Bukhari said: 'Abdullah ibn Yusuf narrated to us, Malik informed us, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Qasim, from his father, from 'Aishah, who said: We went out with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on some of his journeys, until when we were at al-Bayda' (or Dhat al-Jaysh), my necklace broke. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stopped to search for it, and the people stopped with him, and they were not at water, and they had no water with them. The people came to Abu Bakr and said: "Do you not see what 'Aishah has done? She has made the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the people stop, and they are not at water and have no water with them!" Abu Bakr came, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had placed his head on my thigh and was sleeping. He said: "You have detained the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the people, and they are not at water and have no water with them!" 'Aishah said: Abu Bakr reproached me and said what Allah willed him to say, and he kept striking my side with his hand. Nothing prevented me from moving except the place of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on my thigh. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) got up without water, and Allah revealed the verse of tayammum, so they performed tayammum. Usayd ibn al-Hudayr said: "This is not the first of your blessings, O family of Abu Bakr." 'Aishah said: Then we sent the camel I was riding, and we found the necklace beneath it.

Al-Bukhari also narrated it from Qutaybah and Isma'il, and Muslim narrated it from Yahya ibn Yahya, from Malik. [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4607.]

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Ya'qub narrated to us, my father narrated to us, from Salih, who said: Ibn Shihab said: 'Ubaydullah ibn 'Abdullah narrated to me, from Ibn 'Abbas, from 'Ammar ibn Yasir: that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) camped at Ulat al-Jaysh, and with him was his wife 'Aishah. A necklace of hers made of Zafar onyx broke, so he detained the people in search of her necklace, until the dawn shone, and the people had no water. So Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, sent down to His Messenger (ﷺ) the concession of purifying oneself with clean earth. The Muslims stood up with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), struck the earth with their hands, then raised their hands without having taken any dust. They wiped with them their faces and their hands up to the shoulders, and from the undersides of their hands to the armpits. [Al-Musnad (4/264).]

Ibn Jarir also narrated it: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Safi (?) [in the text: "Sayfi"] narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Dhi'b, [from al-Zuhri,] from 'Ubaydullah ibn 'Abdullah, from Abu al-Yaqzan, who said: We were with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and a necklace of 'Aishah was lost. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) remained until the dawn shone, and Abu Bakr became angry at 'Aishah, [may Allah be pleased with her,] and then the concession was revealed to him: wiping with clean earth. Abu Bakr entered and said to her: "Indeed you are blessed! A concession has been revealed because of you!" So we struck our hands with a strike for our faces, and a strike for our hands up to the shoulders and the armpits. [Tafsir al-Tabari (8/418).]

Another hadith: The Hafiz Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, al-Hasan ibn Ahmad narrated to us, al-Layth narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Marzuq narrated to us, al-Ala' [[In the manuscripts: "al-Abbas," which is an error. The correction is from the books of biographical criticism.]] ibn Abi Sawiyya narrated to us: al-Haytham narrated to me, from Zurayq [[In A: "Zurayq."]] al-Maliki, from Banu Malik ibn Ka'b ibn Sa'd, who lived one hundred and seventeen years, from his father, from al-Asla' ibn Shurayk, who said: "I used to saddle the camel of the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him). One cold night I became junub (in a state of major ritual impurity requiring a full bath). The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) wanted to set out, but I disliked saddling his camel while I was junub, and I feared that if I bathed in the cold water I would die or fall ill. So I ordered a man from the Ansar to saddle it. Then I heated stones and warmed water with them, and I bathed. Then I caught up with the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) and his companions, and he said: 'O Asla', what is wrong? I see that your saddling has changed.' I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, I did not saddle it; a man from the Ansar saddled it.' He said: 'And why?' I said: 'I became junub, and I feared the cold for myself, so I ordered him to saddle it. I heated stones and warmed water with them, and I bathed with it.' Then Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿O you who believe, do not approach the prayer while you are intoxicated, until you know what you are saying, nor while junub, except passing through, until you have bathed. And if you are ill or on a journey, or one of you comes from the place of relieving oneself, or you have touched women and you find no water, then perform tayammum with clean earth and wipe your faces and hands. Indeed, Allah is ever Pardoning and Forgiving﴾ [the bracketed portion is as it stands in the text]." And it has been narrated through another chain from him.

Ibn Kathir says that God, may He be exalted, informs about the Jews, upon whom be the curses of God that follow one another until the Day of Resurrection, that they buy misguidance in exchange for guidance, turn away from what God sent down to His Messenger (ﷺ), and abandon the knowledge that is with them from the earlier prophets concerning the description of Muhammad (ﷺ), in order to take in exchange for it a small price of the worldly goods. ﴿And they wish that you would go astray from the way﴾, meaning they wish that you, O believers, would disbelieve in what has been sent down to you and abandon the guidance and beneficial knowledge that you have.

﴿And Allah knows your enemies best﴾, meaning He knows them and warns you against them. ﴿And sufficient is Allah as Protector, and sufficient is Allah as Helper﴾, meaning He is sufficient as a Protector for whoever seeks refuge in Him, and sufficient as a Helper for whoever seeks His help.

Then He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿Among those who are Jews﴾. The ﴿min﴾ here, مِنْ, is for specifying the category, like His saying: ﴿So avoid the abomination of the idols﴾.

* *

His saying: ﴿They distort words from their places﴾, meaning they interpret them in other than their proper sense, and explain them in a way other than what God, mighty and majestic, intended, deliberately and by fabrication. ﴿And they say, "We hear and we disobey"﴾, meaning they say, "We hear what you say, O Muhammad, but we will not obey you in it." This is how Mujahid and Ibn Zayd explained it, and it is the intended meaning. This is more emphatic in their obstinacy and disbelief, since they turn away from the Book of God after they have understood it, while they know what sin and punishment await them for doing so.

* *

His saying: ﴿And "Hear, without being made to hear"﴾, meaning: hear what we say, not that you may hear. This was narrated by al-Dahhak from Ibn Abbas. Mujahid and al-Hasan said: "Hear, without [your words] being accepted from you."

Ibn Jarir said: "The first [explanation] is more correct." And it is as he said. This is mockery and contempt from them, upon them be the curse of God [and of the angels and mankind, all of them].

﴿And "Ra'ina," twisting their tongues and attacking the religion﴾, meaning they give the impression that they are saying "Ra'ina" (take care of us / attend to us) by their saying "Ra'ina," while they really intend ruʿūnah (foolishness). The discussion of this has already passed at His saying: ﴿O you who believe, do not say "Ra'ina," but say "Unzurna" (look at us)﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:104].

For this reason God, may He be exalted, said about these Jews, who intend by their speech the opposite of what they show: ﴿twisting their tongues and attacking the religion﴾, meaning by their cursing of the Prophet (ﷺ).

Then God, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And if they had said, "We hear and we obey, and hear, and look at us," it would have been better for them and more upright. But Allah has cursed them for their disbelief, so they do not believe except a little﴾, meaning their hearts are driven away from good and kept far from it, so no beneficial faith enters them. The discussion of His saying ﴿so few of them believe﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:88] has already passed. The point is that they do not believe with a beneficial faith.
