Allah the Exalted says, commanding the People of the Scripture to believe in what He has sent down upon His servant and messenger Muhammad (ﷺ), the Great Book [in A: "the Mighty"], which confirms the reports that are in their hands concerning the glad tidings, and threatening them should they not do so, with His saying: ﴿Before We obliterate faces and turn them back upon their backs﴾. Some of them said: its meaning is: "Before We obliterate faces." Obliterating them is turning them back upon their backs, and making their sight behind them. It is also possible that the intended meaning is: "Before We obliterate faces, so that no hearing, sight, or trace remains for them, and We turn them, together with that, toward the direction of their backs."

Al-Awfi narrated from Ibn Abbas: ﴿Before We obliterate faces﴾, and its obliteration is that they become blind; ﴿and turn them back upon their backs﴾ means: We make their faces to be from the direction of their napes, so they walk backwards, and We make for one of them two eyes from his nape.

Qatadah and Atiyyah al-Awfi said likewise. This is more forceful in punishment and chastisement. This is a parable that Allah struck for them regarding their turning away from the truth, their being returned to falsehood, and their returning from the clear path to the paths of misguidance, hastening and walking backwards upon their backs. This is like what some of them said concerning His saying: ﴿Indeed, We have put shackles upon their necks, and they reach to the chins, so they are held up. And We have put before them a barrier and behind them a barrier, and We have covered them, so they do not see﴾ [Ya-Sin 36:8–9]. That is a parable of evil which Allah struck for them regarding their misguidance and their being prevented from guidance.

Mujahid said: ﴿Before We obliterate faces﴾ means: from the path of truth; ﴿and turn them back upon their backs﴾, i.e., in misguidance.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: a similar statement was narrated from Ibn Abbas and al-Hasan.

As-Suddi said: ﴿and turn them back upon their backs﴾ means: We will prevent them from the truth. He said: We will return them as disbelievers, and turn them into apes.

Ibn Zayd said: We will return them to the lands of ash-Sham from the land of the Hijaz.

It has been mentioned that Ka'b al-Ahbar embraced Islam when he heard this verse. Ibn Jarir said:

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Jabir ibn Nuh narrated to us, from Isa ibn al-Mughirah, who said: We discussed in the presence of Ibrahim the Islam of Ka'b. He said: Ka'b embraced Islam in the time of Umar. He set out intending Bayt al-Maqdis, and passed by Madinah. Umar went out to him and said: "O Ka'b, embrace Islam." He said: "Do you not read in your book: ﴿The likeness of those who were entrusted with the Torah, then did not bear it, is like a donkey carrying books﴾?" And I have borne the Torah. He said: So Umar left him. Then he went out until he reached Homs, and he heard a man from its people weeping, saying: ﴿O you who have been given the Scripture, believe in what We have sent down, confirming what is with you, before We obliterate faces and turn them back upon their backs﴾, the verse. Ka'b said: "O Lord, I have believed; O Lord, I have submitted," out of fear that this verse would befall him. Then he returned and came to his family in Yemen, then brought them back as Muslims.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it through another route with different wording. He said: My father narrated to us, Ibn Nufayl narrated to us, Amr ibn Waqid narrated to us, from Yunus ibn Halbas, from Abu Idris A'idh Allah al-Khawlani, who said: Abu Muslim al-Jalili was the teacher of Ka'b, and he used to reproach him for his delay in coming to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He said: So he sent him to him to see whether he was he. Ka'b said: I rode until I came to Madinah, and behold, a reciter was reciting the Qur'an, saying: ﴿O you who have been given the Scripture, believe in what We have sent down, confirming what is with you, before We obliterate faces and turn them back upon their backs﴾. So I hurried to the water, performed ablution, and I was wiping my face out of fear that it would be obliterated, then I embraced Islam.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Or We curse them as We cursed the companions of the Sabbath﴾, it means: those who transgressed in their Sabbath by the stratagem of hunting, and they were transformed into apes and swine. The account of them will be expounded in Surat al-A'raf.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And the command of Allah is ever accomplished﴾, i.e., when He decrees a matter, it is not opposed or prevented.

Then Allah informed that He ﴿does not forgive that He be associated with﴾, i.e., He does not forgive a servant who meets Him while associating others with Him, ﴿but He forgives what is less than that﴾, i.e., of sins, ﴿for whom He wills﴾, i.e., of His servants.

Hadiths related to this noble verse have been transmitted, so we will mention from them what is feasible. The first hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Yazid narrated to us, Sadaqah ibn Musa informed us, Abu Imran al-Jawni narrated to us, from Yazid ibn Babanus, from Aishah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The registers with Allah are three: a register which Allah does not regard at all; a register from which Allah leaves nothing; and a register which Allah will not forgive. As for the register which Allah will not forgive, it is associating partners with Allah. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Indeed, whoever associates others with Allah, Allah has forbidden him Paradise﴾ [al-Ma'idah 5:72]. As for the register which Allah does not regard at all, it is the servant's wronging himself between himself and his Lord, such as fasting a day that he abandoned or a prayer that he left; Allah forgives that and overlooks it if He wills. As for the register which Allah leaves nothing from, it is the wronging of servants one another; retaliation is inevitable."

Ahmad alone narrated it.

The second hadith: The hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said in his Musnad: Ahmad ibn Malik narrated to us, Za'idah ibn Abi al-Raqqad narrated to us, from Ziyad al-Namari, from Anas ibn Malik, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Wrongdoing is of three kinds: a wrongdoing which Allah will not forgive, a wrongdoing which Allah will forgive, and a wrongdoing which Allah will not leave: As for the wrongdoing which Allah will not forgive, it is associating partners; and He said: ﴿Indeed, associating partners is a great wrong﴾ [Luqman 31:13]. As for the wrongdoing which Allah will forgive, it is the servants wronging themselves between themselves and their Lord. As for the wrongdoing which He will not leave, it is the servants wronging one another, until retaliation is taken from one for another."

[Musnad al-Bazzar no. 3439, "Kashf al-Astar"; al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (10/348): "al-Bazzar narrated it from his shaykh Ahmad ibn Malik al-Qushayri, and I did not know him, and the rest of its narrators are deemed trustworthy." It was also narrated by al-Tayalisi in his Musnad (2/60), and through him Abu Nu'aym in al-Hilyah (6/309): "al-Rabi' narrated to us from Yazid from Anas." Yazid is al-Raqashi, who is weak according to the imams.]

The third hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Safwan ibn Isa narrated to us, Thawr ibn Yazid narrated to us, from Abu Awn, from Abu Idris, who said: I heard Mu'awiyah say: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Every sin, Allah may forgive it, except a man who dies as a disbeliever, or a man who kills a believer deliberately."

Al-Nasa'i narrated it from Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna, from Safwan ibn Isa, with the same chain.

The fourth hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Hashim ibn al-Qasim narrated to us, Abd al-Hamid narrated to us, Shahr narrated to us, Ibn Ghanm narrated to us that Abu Dharr narrated to him from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "Allah says: O My servant, as long as you worship Me and hope in Me, I will forgive you for what is in you. O My servant, if you come to Me with sins nearly the size of the earth, as long as you do not associate anything with Me, I will come to you with forgiveness nearly its size."

Ahmad alone narrated it by this route.

The fifth hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Samad narrated to us, my father narrated to us, Husayn narrated to us, from Ibn Buraydah, that Yahya ibn Ya'mar narrated to him, that Abu al-Aswad al-Dili narrated to him, that Abu Dharr narrated to him, who said: I came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and he said: "There is no servant who says: 'There is no god but Allah,' and then dies upon that, except that he enters Paradise." I said: "Even if he commits adultery and steals?" He said: "Even if he commits adultery and steals." I said: "Even if he commits adultery and steals?" He said: "Even if he commits adultery and steals." Three times; then he said in the fourth: "Despite the nose of Abu Dharr!" He said: So Abu Dharr went out dragging his waistcloth, saying: "Even if the nose of Abu Dharr is rubbed in dust!" And Abu Dharr used to narrate this afterwards and say: "Even if the nose of Abu Dharr is rubbed in dust."

Both al-Bukhari and Muslim narrated it from the hadith of Husayn, with the same chain.

Another route from him: Imam Ahmad said: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us, from Zayd ibn Wahb, from Abu Dharr, who said: "I was walking with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in the stony ground of Madinah at night, and we were looking at Uhud. He said: 'O Abu Dharr.' I said: 'At your service, O Messenger of Allah.' He said: 'I would not like Uhud to be mine in gold, such that I spend three nights while I have of it a single dinar, except a dinar I set aside for a debt, unless I say with it in the service of Allah's servants like this.' And he scooped with his hands to his right, before him, and to his left. He said: Then we walked on, and he said: 'O Abu Dharr, the most numerous on the Day of Resurrection will be the least, except for one who says it and does it like this, and like this, and like this.' And he scooped to his right, before him, and to his left. He said: Then we walked on, and he said: 'O Abu Dharr, stay where you are until I come to you.' So he went off until he was hidden from me. I heard a commotion and a voice, and I said: 'Perhaps something has befallen the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).' I was about to follow him, then I remembered his saying: 'Do not leave until I come to you,' so I waited for him until he came, and I mentioned to him what I had heard. He said: 'That was Gabriel who came to me and said: Whoever of your Ummah dies without associating anything with Allah enters Paradise.' I said: 'Even if he commits adultery and steals?' He said: 'Even if he commits adultery and steals.'"

Both al-Bukhari and Muslim narrated it in their Sahihs from the hadith of al-A'mash, with the same chain.

Al-Bukhari and Muslim both also narrated it, both from Qutaybah, from Jarir ibn 'Abd al-Hamid, from 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Rufay', from Zayd ibn Wahb, from Abu Dharr, who said: "I went out one night, and suddenly the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was walking alone, with no one with him." He said: "So I thought that he disliked anyone walking with him. So I began walking in the shade of the moon. He turned around and saw me and said: 'Who is this?' I said: 'Abu Dharr. May Allah make me your ransom.' He said: 'O Abu Dharr, come here.' So I walked with him for a while, and he said: 'Indeed, the wealthy will be the poor on the Day of Resurrection, except for the one whom Allah has given good, so he spends it to his right and to his left, before him and behind him, and does good with it.'" He said: "So I walked with him for a while, and he said to me: 'Sit here.' So he had me sit in a open plain surrounded by stones, and he said to me: 'Sit here until I return to you.'" He said: "So he went off into the lava field until I could no longer see him. He stayed away from me and prolonged his stay. Then I heard him coming back while he was saying: 'Even if he steals, and even if he commits adultery.'" He said: "When he came, I could not restrain myself, and I said: 'O Prophet of Allah, may Allah make me your ransom, who was speaking on the side of the lava field? I did not hear anyone responding to you with anything.'" He said: "That was Jibril. He appeared to me from the side of the lava field and said: 'Give good news to your Ummah that whoever dies without associating anything with Allah will enter Paradise.' I said: 'O Jibril, even if he steals and even if he commits adultery?' He said: 'Yes.' I said: 'Even if he steals and even if he commits adultery?' He said: 'Yes.' I said: 'Even if he steals and even if he commits adultery?' He said: 'Yes, even if he drinks wine.'"

[Footnote: Sahih al-Bukhari no. (6443) and Sahih Muslim no. (94).]

**The Sixth Hadith:** 'Abd ibn Humayd said in his Musnad: Ubayd Allah ibn Musa informed us, from Ibn Abi Layla, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, who said: A man came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, what are the two things that necessitate (al-Mujibatan)?" He said: "Whoever dies without associating anything with Allah will be owed Paradise, and whoever dies associating something with Allah will be owed the Fire." And he mentioned the rest of the hadith.

[Footnote: Al-Muntakhab li-'Abd ibn Humayd no. (1058). Its chain includes Ibn Abi Layla, who had a poor memory. However, it is narrated through another sound route from Jabir: Muslim narrated it no. (93) through al-A'mash, from Abu Sufyan, from Jabir, with the same wording.]

**Another route:** Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, al-Hasan ibn 'Amr ibn Khalad al-Harrani narrated to us, Mansur ibn Isma'il al-Qurashi narrated to us, Musa ibn 'Ubayda al-Rabadhi narrated to us, informed me ('Abd Allah ibn 'Ubayda), from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "No soul dies without associating anything with Allah except that forgiveness becomes lawful for it. If He wills, He punishes it, and if He wills, He forgives it." Then he recited: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive that He be associated with, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills﴾.

[Footnote: Its chain includes Musa ibn 'Ubayda, whom the imams declared weak. His narration from his brother 'Abd Allah ibn 'Ubayda from Jabir is also mursal (a break in the chain).]

Abu Ya'la al-Hafiz also narrated it in his Musnad, from the hadith of Musa ibn 'Ubayda, from his brother 'Abd Allah ibn 'Ubayda, from Jabir, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Forgiveness does not cease to be upon the servant as long as the barrier has not descended." It was said: "O Prophet of Allah, what is the barrier?" He said: "Associating partners with Allah." He said: "No soul meets Allah without associating anything with Him except that forgiveness from Allah becomes lawful for it. If He wills to punish it, and if He wills to forgive it, He forgives it." Then the Prophet of Allah recited: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive that He be associated with, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills﴾.

[Footnote: Ibn Abi al-Dunya narrated it in Husn al-Zann bi-Allah no. (56), and Ibn 'Adi in al-Kamil (6/334), through Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman, from 'Ali ibn Salih, from Musa ibn 'Ubayda with the same wording.]

**The Seventh Hadith:** Imam Ahmad said: Abu Nu'aym narrated to us, Zakariyya narrated to us, from 'Atiyya, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever dies without associating anything with Allah will enter Paradise."

[Footnote: Al-Musnad (3/79). It is narrated only through this route.]

**The Eighth Hadith:** Imam Ahmad said: Hasan ibn Musa narrated to us, Ibn Lahi'a narrated to us, Abu Qubayl narrated to us, from 'Abd Allah ibn Nashir of the Bani Sarii', who said: I heard Abu Ruhm, the storyteller of the people of Syria, say: I heard Abu Ayyub al-Ansari say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out one day to them and said to them: "Your Lord, Mighty and Majestic, gave me the choice between seventy thousand who will enter Paradise without reckoning, and the treasure (al-Khabi'a) that He has for my Ummah." Some of his companions said to him: "O Messenger of Allah, does your Lord hide that?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went in, then came out while glorifying (Allahu Akbar), and said: "My Lord has increased for me, with every thousand, seventy thousand, and the treasure is with Him." Abu Ruhm said: "O Abu Ayyub, what do you think the treasure of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is?" The people spoke of it among themselves and said: "What have you to do with the treasure of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)?!" Abu Ayyub said: "Leave the man alone. I will tell you about the treasure of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) as I think, or rather as one who is certain. The treasure of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is that he says: 'Whoever testifies that there is no god but Allah, alone with no partner, and that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger, his heart confirming what his tongue says, Allah will admit him into Paradise.'"

[Footnote: Al-Musnad (5/413).]

**The Ninth Hadith:** Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, al-Mu'ammal ibn al-Fadl al-Harrani narrated to us, 'Isa ibn Yunus narrated to us (ḥ). And Hashim ibn al-Qasim al-Harrani informed us, in what he wrote to me, saying: 'Isa ibn Yunus himself narrated to us, from Wasil ibn al-Sa'ib al-Ruqashi, from Abu Sawra, the son of the brother of Abu Ayyub, from Abu Ayyub al-Ansari, who said: A man came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "I have a nephew who does not refrain from the forbidden." He said: "And what is his religion?" He said: "He prays and affirms the oneness of Allah, Exalted." He said: "Ask him to give you his religion as a gift. If he refuses, buy it from him." The man asked him for that, but he refused. So he came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and informed him. He said: "You found him stingy regarding his religion." He said: So this was revealed: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive that He be associated with, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills﴾.

[Footnote: Al-Tabarani narrated it in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (4/177) through 'Isa ibn Yunus from Wasil with the same wording. Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (7/5): "In it is Wasil ibn al-Sa'ib, and he is weak."]

**The Tenth Hadith:** Abu Ya'la al-Hafiz said: 'Amr ibn al-Dahhak narrated to us, my father narrated to us, Mastur Abu Hammam al-Hunā'i narrated to us, Thabit narrated to us, from Anas, who said: A man came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I have left no need, nor one who has a need, except that I have come to it." He said: "Do you not testify that there is no god but Allah, and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah?" Three times. He said: "Yes." He said: "Then that will come upon all of that."

[Footnote: Musnad Abi Ya'la (6/155). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (10/83): "Its narrators are trustworthy (thiqat)."]

**The Eleventh Hadith:** Imam Ahmad said: Abu 'Amir narrated to us, 'Ikrima ibn 'Ammar narrated to us, from Damdam ibn Jaws al-Yamami, who said: Abu Hurayra said to me: "O Yamami, do not say to a man: 'By Allah, Allah will not forgive you,' or 'Allah will never admit you into Paradise.'" I said: "O Abu Hurayra, this is a word that one of us says to his brother and companion when he is angry." He said: "Do not say it, for I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'Among the Children of Israel there were two men. One of them was diligent in worship, and the other was extravagant against himself, and they were brothers. The diligent one kept seeing the other committing a sin, and would say: "O you, stop!" He would say: "Leave me with my Lord! Were you sent to be a watcher over me?" Until one day he saw him commit a sin that he considered grave, and said to him: "Woe to you! Stop!" He said: "Leave me with my Lord! Were you sent to be a watcher over me?" So he said: "By Allah, Allah will not forgive you" (or "Allah will never admit you into Paradise"). Then Allah sent an angel to them both, who seized their souls, and they gathered before Him. He said to the sinner: "Go and enter Paradise by My mercy." And He said to the other: "Were you knowledgeable about Me? Were you capable over what is in My hand? Take him to the Fire." He said: "By Him in whose hand is the soul of Abu al-Qasim, he uttered a word that ruined his worldly life and his Hereafter.'"

[Footnote: Abu Dawud narrated it from the hadith of 'Ikrima ibn 'Ammar: "Damdam ibn Jaws narrated to me," with the same. Al-Musnad (2/323) and Sunan Abi Dawud no. (4901).]

**The Twelfth Hadith:** Al-Tabarani said: Abu Shaykh narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn 'Ajlan al-Asbahani, Salama ibn Shabib narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn al-Hakam ibn Aban narrated to us, from his father, from 'Ikrima, from Ibn 'Abbas, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: 'Whoever knows that I am capable of forgiving sins, I will forgive him and I do not mind, as long as he does not associate anything with Me.'"

[Footnote: In its chain is Ibrahim ibn al-Hakam ibn Aban, whom the imams declared weak. Ibn 'Adi said: "He used to connect the mursal narrations from his father, and most of what he narrates is not corroborated."]

**The Thirteenth Hadith:** The hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar and the hafiz Abu Ya'la [al-Mawsili] [addition from A] said: Hudba, i.e., Ibn Khalid, narrated to us, Sahl ibn Abi Hazm narrated to us, from Thabit, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever Allah promises a reward for a deed, He will certainly fulfill it for him, and whoever He threatens with punishment for a deed, He has the choice concerning it." Both of them narrated it alone.

[Footnote: Musnad Abi Ya'la (6/66). Al-Tabarani narrated it in al-Awsat no. (4739) and said: "No one narrated it from Thabit except Sahl, and Hudba alone narrated it from him." Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (10/211): "In it is Sahl ibn Abi Hazm, who was declared trustworthy despite his weakness, and the rest of its narrators are narrators of the Sahih."]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Bahr ibn Nasr al-Khawlani narrated to us, Khalid, meaning Ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Khurasani, narrated to us, al-Haytham ibn Jammaz narrated to us, from Sallam ibn Abi Mut'i, from Bakr ibn 'Abd Allah al-Muzani, from Ibn 'Umar, who said: "We, the companions of the Prophet (ﷺ), had no doubt about the killer of a soul, the consumer of an orphan's property, the slanderer of chaste women, and the false witness, until this verse was revealed: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive that He be associated with, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills﴾. So the companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) refrained from testifying (to the Fire for such people)."

Ibn Jarir narrated it from the hadith of al-Haytham ibn Hammad with the same.

[Footnote: Tafsir al-Tabari (8/450). Its chain includes al-Haytham ibn Jammaz, whom Ahmad, Ibn Ma'in, al-Nasa'i and others declared weak.]

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on Surah 4, verses 47–48 (part 3 of 3):

Ibn Abi Hatim also said: Abd al-Malik ibn Abi Abd al-Rahman al-Muqri [[In manuscript A: "al-Maqbari"]] narrated to us; Abdullah ibn Asim narrated to us; Salih, that is, al-Murri Abu Bishr, narrated to us, from Ayyub, from Nafi', from Ibn Umar, who said: "We would not doubt about those for whom Allah had made the Fire obligatory in the Book, until this verse was revealed to us: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive association with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills﴾." He said: "When we heard it, we refrained from declaring anyone certainly damned, and we left the matters to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic [[In manuscript D: "the Exalted"]]."

Al-Bazzar said: Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahim narrated to us; Shaiban ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us; Harb ibn Surayj narrated to us, from Ayyub, from Nafi', from Ibn Umar [may Allah be pleased with them both] [[Addition from manuscript A.]], who said: "We used to refrain from seeking forgiveness for the people of major sins, until we heard our Prophet (ﷺ) recite: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive association with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills﴾, and he said: 'I have delayed my intercession for the people of major sins from my Ummah until the Day of Resurrection.'"

Abu Ja'far al-Razi said, from al-Rabi', who said: Mujabbar informed me, from Abdullah ibn Umar, that he said: When this was revealed: ﴿Say: O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah; indeed, Allah forgives all sins; indeed, He is the Forgiving, the Merciful﴾ [Az-Zumar: 53] [[Addition from manuscript A; in manuscript H: "to the end of the verse."]], a man stood up and said: "And association with Allah, O Prophet of Allah?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) disliked that, and so he said: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive association with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills. And whoever associates others with Allah has certainly fabricated a tremendous sin﴾.

Ibn Jarir narrated it. Ibn Mardawayh also narrated it through several chains from Ibn Umar [[Tafsir al-Tabari (8/450).]].

This verse in Surat Tanzil [i.e., Surat al-Zumar] is conditioned upon repentance: whoever repents from any sin, even if it is repeated from him, Allah will accept his repentance. For this reason He said: ﴿Say: O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah; indeed, Allah forgives all sins; indeed, He is the Forgiving, the Merciful﴾ [Az-Zumar: 53], meaning: on condition of repentance. Had it not been so, association would have been included in it, and that is not valid, because He, the Exalted, has ruled here that He does not forgive association, and has ruled that He forgives what is other than it for whom He wills, meaning even if its doer does not repent. So in this respect the latter [i.e., the verse of al-Zumar] is more hopeful than the former. And Allah knows best.

* *

His saying: ﴿And whoever associates others with Allah has certainly fabricated a tremendous sin﴾ is like His saying: ﴿Indeed, association is a tremendous wrong﴾ [Luqman: 13]. It is also established in the two Sahihs, from Ibn Mas'ud, that he said: "I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, which sin is greatest?' He said: 'That you set up a rival to Allah while He created you...'" and he mentioned the rest of the hadith.

Ibn Mardawayh said: Ishaq ibn Ibrahim ibn Zayd narrated to us; Ahmad ibn Amr narrated to us; Ibrahim ibn al-Mundhir narrated to us; Ma'n narrated to us; Sa'id ibn Bashir narrated to us; Qatadah narrated to us, from al-Hasan, from Imran ibn Husayn, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Shall I inform you of the greatest of the major sins? It is association with Allah [[In manuscripts D, R, A: "ascribing partners to Allah."]]." Then he recited: ﴿And whoever associates others with Allah has certainly fabricated a tremendous sin﴾, "and disobedience to parents." Then he recited: ﴿Be grateful to Me and to your parents; to Me is the final destination﴾ [Luqman: 14] [[In its chain is Sa'id ibn Bashir, about whom some scholars spoke. Ahmad and Ibn Ma'in declared him weak, while Duhaym and others deemed him trustworthy.]]

Allah the Exalted says, commanding the People of the Scripture to believe in what He has sent down upon His servant and messenger Muhammad (ﷺ), the Great Book [in A: "the Mighty"], which confirms the reports that are in their hands concerning the glad tidings, and threatening them should they not do so, with His saying: ﴿Before We obliterate faces and turn them back upon their backs﴾. Some of them said: its meaning is: "Before We obliterate faces." Obliterating them is turning them back upon their backs, and making their sight behind them. It is also possible that the intended meaning is: "Before We obliterate faces, so that no hearing, sight, or trace remains for them, and We turn them, together with that, toward the direction of their backs."

Al-Awfi narrated from Ibn Abbas: ﴿Before We obliterate faces﴾, and its obliteration is that they become blind; ﴿and turn them back upon their backs﴾ means: We make their faces to be from the direction of their napes, so they walk backwards, and We make for one of them two eyes from his nape.

Qatadah and Atiyyah al-Awfi said likewise. This is more forceful in punishment and chastisement. This is a parable that Allah struck for them regarding their turning away from the truth, their being returned to falsehood, and their returning from the clear path to the paths of misguidance, hastening and walking backwards upon their backs. This is like what some of them said concerning His saying: ﴿Indeed, We have put shackles upon their necks, and they reach to the chins, so they are held up. And We have put before them a barrier and behind them a barrier, and We have covered them, so they do not see﴾ [Ya-Sin 36:8–9]. That is a parable of evil which Allah struck for them regarding their misguidance and their being prevented from guidance.

Mujahid said: ﴿Before We obliterate faces﴾ means: from the path of truth; ﴿and turn them back upon their backs﴾, i.e., in misguidance.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: a similar statement was narrated from Ibn Abbas and al-Hasan.

As-Suddi said: ﴿and turn them back upon their backs﴾ means: We will prevent them from the truth. He said: We will return them as disbelievers, and turn them into apes.

Ibn Zayd said: We will return them to the lands of ash-Sham from the land of the Hijaz.

It has been mentioned that Ka'b al-Ahbar embraced Islam when he heard this verse. Ibn Jarir said:

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Jabir ibn Nuh narrated to us, from Isa ibn al-Mughirah, who said: We discussed in the presence of Ibrahim the Islam of Ka'b. He said: Ka'b embraced Islam in the time of Umar. He set out intending Bayt al-Maqdis, and passed by Madinah. Umar went out to him and said: "O Ka'b, embrace Islam." He said: "Do you not read in your book: ﴿The likeness of those who were entrusted with the Torah, then did not bear it, is like a donkey carrying books﴾?" And I have borne the Torah. He said: So Umar left him. Then he went out until he reached Homs, and he heard a man from its people weeping, saying: ﴿O you who have been given the Scripture, believe in what We have sent down, confirming what is with you, before We obliterate faces and turn them back upon their backs﴾, the verse. Ka'b said: "O Lord, I have believed; O Lord, I have submitted," out of fear that this verse would befall him. Then he returned and came to his family in Yemen, then brought them back as Muslims.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it through another route with different wording. He said: My father narrated to us, Ibn Nufayl narrated to us, Amr ibn Waqid narrated to us, from Yunus ibn Halbas, from Abu Idris A'idh Allah al-Khawlani, who said: Abu Muslim al-Jalili was the teacher of Ka'b, and he used to reproach him for his delay in coming to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He said: So he sent him to him to see whether he was he. Ka'b said: I rode until I came to Madinah, and behold, a reciter was reciting the Qur'an, saying: ﴿O you who have been given the Scripture, believe in what We have sent down, confirming what is with you, before We obliterate faces and turn them back upon their backs﴾. So I hurried to the water, performed ablution, and I was wiping my face out of fear that it would be obliterated, then I embraced Islam.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Or We curse them as We cursed the companions of the Sabbath﴾, it means: those who transgressed in their Sabbath by the stratagem of hunting, and they were transformed into apes and swine. The account of them will be expounded in Surat al-A'raf.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And the command of Allah is ever accomplished﴾, i.e., when He decrees a matter, it is not opposed or prevented.

Then Allah informed that He ﴿does not forgive that He be associated with﴾, i.e., He does not forgive a servant who meets Him while associating others with Him, ﴿but He forgives what is less than that﴾, i.e., of sins, ﴿for whom He wills﴾, i.e., of His servants.

Hadiths related to this noble verse have been transmitted, so we will mention from them what is feasible. The first hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Yazid narrated to us, Sadaqah ibn Musa informed us, Abu Imran al-Jawni narrated to us, from Yazid ibn Babanus, from Aishah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The registers with Allah are three: a register which Allah does not regard at all; a register from which Allah leaves nothing; and a register which Allah will not forgive. As for the register which Allah will not forgive, it is associating partners with Allah. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Indeed, whoever associates others with Allah, Allah has forbidden him Paradise﴾ [al-Ma'idah 5:72]. As for the register which Allah does not regard at all, it is the servant's wronging himself between himself and his Lord, such as fasting a day that he abandoned or a prayer that he left; Allah forgives that and overlooks it if He wills. As for the register which Allah leaves nothing from, it is the wronging of servants one another; retaliation is inevitable."

Ahmad alone narrated it.

The second hadith: The hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said in his Musnad: Ahmad ibn Malik narrated to us, Za'idah ibn Abi al-Raqqad narrated to us, from Ziyad al-Namari, from Anas ibn Malik, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Wrongdoing is of three kinds: a wrongdoing which Allah will not forgive, a wrongdoing which Allah will forgive, and a wrongdoing which Allah will not leave: As for the wrongdoing which Allah will not forgive, it is associating partners; and He said: ﴿Indeed, associating partners is a great wrong﴾ [Luqman 31:13]. As for the wrongdoing which Allah will forgive, it is the servants wronging themselves between themselves and their Lord. As for the wrongdoing which He will not leave, it is the servants wronging one another, until retaliation is taken from one for another."

[Musnad al-Bazzar no. 3439, "Kashf al-Astar"; al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (10/348): "al-Bazzar narrated it from his shaykh Ahmad ibn Malik al-Qushayri, and I did not know him, and the rest of its narrators are deemed trustworthy." It was also narrated by al-Tayalisi in his Musnad (2/60), and through him Abu Nu'aym in al-Hilyah (6/309): "al-Rabi' narrated to us from Yazid from Anas." Yazid is al-Raqashi, who is weak according to the imams.]

The third hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Safwan ibn Isa narrated to us, Thawr ibn Yazid narrated to us, from Abu Awn, from Abu Idris, who said: I heard Mu'awiyah say: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Every sin, Allah may forgive it, except a man who dies as a disbeliever, or a man who kills a believer deliberately."

Al-Nasa'i narrated it from Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna, from Safwan ibn Isa, with the same chain.

The fourth hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Hashim ibn al-Qasim narrated to us, Abd al-Hamid narrated to us, Shahr narrated to us, Ibn Ghanm narrated to us that Abu Dharr narrated to him from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "Allah says: O My servant, as long as you worship Me and hope in Me, I will forgive you for what is in you. O My servant, if you come to Me with sins nearly the size of the earth, as long as you do not associate anything with Me, I will come to you with forgiveness nearly its size."

Ahmad alone narrated it by this route.

The fifth hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Samad narrated to us, my father narrated to us, Husayn narrated to us, from Ibn Buraydah, that Yahya ibn Ya'mar narrated to him, that Abu al-Aswad al-Dili narrated to him, that Abu Dharr narrated to him, who said: I came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and he said: "There is no servant who says: 'There is no god but Allah,' and then dies upon that, except that he enters Paradise." I said: "Even if he commits adultery and steals?" He said: "Even if he commits adultery and steals." I said: "Even if he commits adultery and steals?" He said: "Even if he commits adultery and steals." Three times; then he said in the fourth: "Despite the nose of Abu Dharr!" He said: So Abu Dharr went out dragging his waistcloth, saying: "Even if the nose of Abu Dharr is rubbed in dust!" And Abu Dharr used to narrate this afterwards and say: "Even if the nose of Abu Dharr is rubbed in dust."

Both al-Bukhari and Muslim narrated it from the hadith of Husayn, with the same chain.

Another route from him: Imam Ahmad said: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us, from Zayd ibn Wahb, from Abu Dharr, who said: "I was walking with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in the stony ground of Madinah at night, and we were looking at Uhud. He said: 'O Abu Dharr.' I said: 'At your service, O Messenger of Allah.' He said: 'I would not like Uhud to be mine in gold, such that I spend three nights while I have of it a single dinar, except a dinar I set aside for a debt, unless I say with it in the service of Allah's servants like this.' And he scooped with his hands to his right, before him, and to his left. He said: Then we walked on, and he said: 'O Abu Dharr, the most numerous on the Day of Resurrection will be the least, except for one who says it and does it like this, and like this, and like this.' And he scooped to his right, before him, and to his left. He said: Then we walked on, and he said: 'O Abu Dharr, stay where you are until I come to you.' So he went off until he was hidden from me. I heard a commotion and a voice, and I said: 'Perhaps something has befallen the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).' I was about to follow him, then I remembered his saying: 'Do not leave until I come to you,' so I waited for him until he came, and I mentioned to him what I had heard. He said: 'That was Gabriel who came to me and said: Whoever of your Ummah dies without associating anything with Allah enters Paradise.' I said: 'Even if he commits adultery and steals?' He said: 'Even if he commits adultery and steals.'"

Both al-Bukhari and Muslim narrated it in their Sahihs from the hadith of al-A'mash, with the same chain.

Al-Bukhari and Muslim both also narrated it, both from Qutaybah, from Jarir ibn 'Abd al-Hamid, from 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Rufay', from Zayd ibn Wahb, from Abu Dharr, who said: "I went out one night, and suddenly the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was walking alone, with no one with him." He said: "So I thought that he disliked anyone walking with him. So I began walking in the shade of the moon. He turned around and saw me and said: 'Who is this?' I said: 'Abu Dharr. May Allah make me your ransom.' He said: 'O Abu Dharr, come here.' So I walked with him for a while, and he said: 'Indeed, the wealthy will be the poor on the Day of Resurrection, except for the one whom Allah has given good, so he spends it to his right and to his left, before him and behind him, and does good with it.'" He said: "So I walked with him for a while, and he said to me: 'Sit here.' So he had me sit in a open plain surrounded by stones, and he said to me: 'Sit here until I return to you.'" He said: "So he went off into the lava field until I could no longer see him. He stayed away from me and prolonged his stay. Then I heard him coming back while he was saying: 'Even if he steals, and even if he commits adultery.'" He said: "When he came, I could not restrain myself, and I said: 'O Prophet of Allah, may Allah make me your ransom, who was speaking on the side of the lava field? I did not hear anyone responding to you with anything.'" He said: "That was Jibril. He appeared to me from the side of the lava field and said: 'Give good news to your Ummah that whoever dies without associating anything with Allah will enter Paradise.' I said: 'O Jibril, even if he steals and even if he commits adultery?' He said: 'Yes.' I said: 'Even if he steals and even if he commits adultery?' He said: 'Yes.' I said: 'Even if he steals and even if he commits adultery?' He said: 'Yes, even if he drinks wine.'"

[Footnote: Sahih al-Bukhari no. (6443) and Sahih Muslim no. (94).]

**The Sixth Hadith:** 'Abd ibn Humayd said in his Musnad: Ubayd Allah ibn Musa informed us, from Ibn Abi Layla, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, who said: A man came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, what are the two things that necessitate (al-Mujibatan)?" He said: "Whoever dies without associating anything with Allah will be owed Paradise, and whoever dies associating something with Allah will be owed the Fire." And he mentioned the rest of the hadith.

[Footnote: Al-Muntakhab li-'Abd ibn Humayd no. (1058). Its chain includes Ibn Abi Layla, who had a poor memory. However, it is narrated through another sound route from Jabir: Muslim narrated it no. (93) through al-A'mash, from Abu Sufyan, from Jabir, with the same wording.]

**Another route:** Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, al-Hasan ibn 'Amr ibn Khalad al-Harrani narrated to us, Mansur ibn Isma'il al-Qurashi narrated to us, Musa ibn 'Ubayda al-Rabadhi narrated to us, informed me ('Abd Allah ibn 'Ubayda), from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "No soul dies without associating anything with Allah except that forgiveness becomes lawful for it. If He wills, He punishes it, and if He wills, He forgives it." Then he recited: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive that He be associated with, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills﴾.

[Footnote: Its chain includes Musa ibn 'Ubayda, whom the imams declared weak. His narration from his brother 'Abd Allah ibn 'Ubayda from Jabir is also mursal (a break in the chain).]

Abu Ya'la al-Hafiz also narrated it in his Musnad, from the hadith of Musa ibn 'Ubayda, from his brother 'Abd Allah ibn 'Ubayda, from Jabir, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Forgiveness does not cease to be upon the servant as long as the barrier has not descended." It was said: "O Prophet of Allah, what is the barrier?" He said: "Associating partners with Allah." He said: "No soul meets Allah without associating anything with Him except that forgiveness from Allah becomes lawful for it. If He wills to punish it, and if He wills to forgive it, He forgives it." Then the Prophet of Allah recited: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive that He be associated with, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills﴾.

[Footnote: Ibn Abi al-Dunya narrated it in Husn al-Zann bi-Allah no. (56), and Ibn 'Adi in al-Kamil (6/334), through Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman, from 'Ali ibn Salih, from Musa ibn 'Ubayda with the same wording.]

**The Seventh Hadith:** Imam Ahmad said: Abu Nu'aym narrated to us, Zakariyya narrated to us, from 'Atiyya, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever dies without associating anything with Allah will enter Paradise."

[Footnote: Al-Musnad (3/79). It is narrated only through this route.]

**The Eighth Hadith:** Imam Ahmad said: Hasan ibn Musa narrated to us, Ibn Lahi'a narrated to us, Abu Qubayl narrated to us, from 'Abd Allah ibn Nashir of the Bani Sarii', who said: I heard Abu Ruhm, the storyteller of the people of Syria, say: I heard Abu Ayyub al-Ansari say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out one day to them and said to them: "Your Lord, Mighty and Majestic, gave me the choice between seventy thousand who will enter Paradise without reckoning, and the treasure (al-Khabi'a) that He has for my Ummah." Some of his companions said to him: "O Messenger of Allah, does your Lord hide that?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went in, then came out while glorifying (Allahu Akbar), and said: "My Lord has increased for me, with every thousand, seventy thousand, and the treasure is with Him." Abu Ruhm said: "O Abu Ayyub, what do you think the treasure of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is?" The people spoke of it among themselves and said: "What have you to do with the treasure of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)?!" Abu Ayyub said: "Leave the man alone. I will tell you about the treasure of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) as I think, or rather as one who is certain. The treasure of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is that he says: 'Whoever testifies that there is no god but Allah, alone with no partner, and that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger, his heart confirming what his tongue says, Allah will admit him into Paradise.'"

[Footnote: Al-Musnad (5/413).]

**The Ninth Hadith:** Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, al-Mu'ammal ibn al-Fadl al-Harrani narrated to us, 'Isa ibn Yunus narrated to us (ḥ). And Hashim ibn al-Qasim al-Harrani informed us, in what he wrote to me, saying: 'Isa ibn Yunus himself narrated to us, from Wasil ibn al-Sa'ib al-Ruqashi, from Abu Sawra, the son of the brother of Abu Ayyub, from Abu Ayyub al-Ansari, who said: A man came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "I have a nephew who does not refrain from the forbidden." He said: "And what is his religion?" He said: "He prays and affirms the oneness of Allah, Exalted." He said: "Ask him to give you his religion as a gift. If he refuses, buy it from him." The man asked him for that, but he refused. So he came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and informed him. He said: "You found him stingy regarding his religion." He said: So this was revealed: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive that He be associated with, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills﴾.

[Footnote: Al-Tabarani narrated it in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (4/177) through 'Isa ibn Yunus from Wasil with the same wording. Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (7/5): "In it is Wasil ibn al-Sa'ib, and he is weak."]

**The Tenth Hadith:** Abu Ya'la al-Hafiz said: 'Amr ibn al-Dahhak narrated to us, my father narrated to us, Mastur Abu Hammam al-Hunā'i narrated to us, Thabit narrated to us, from Anas, who said: A man came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I have left no need, nor one who has a need, except that I have come to it." He said: "Do you not testify that there is no god but Allah, and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah?" Three times. He said: "Yes." He said: "Then that will come upon all of that."

[Footnote: Musnad Abi Ya'la (6/155). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (10/83): "Its narrators are trustworthy (thiqat)."]

**The Eleventh Hadith:** Imam Ahmad said: Abu 'Amir narrated to us, 'Ikrima ibn 'Ammar narrated to us, from Damdam ibn Jaws al-Yamami, who said: Abu Hurayra said to me: "O Yamami, do not say to a man: 'By Allah, Allah will not forgive you,' or 'Allah will never admit you into Paradise.'" I said: "O Abu Hurayra, this is a word that one of us says to his brother and companion when he is angry." He said: "Do not say it, for I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'Among the Children of Israel there were two men. One of them was diligent in worship, and the other was extravagant against himself, and they were brothers. The diligent one kept seeing the other committing a sin, and would say: "O you, stop!" He would say: "Leave me with my Lord! Were you sent to be a watcher over me?" Until one day he saw him commit a sin that he considered grave, and said to him: "Woe to you! Stop!" He said: "Leave me with my Lord! Were you sent to be a watcher over me?" So he said: "By Allah, Allah will not forgive you" (or "Allah will never admit you into Paradise"). Then Allah sent an angel to them both, who seized their souls, and they gathered before Him. He said to the sinner: "Go and enter Paradise by My mercy." And He said to the other: "Were you knowledgeable about Me? Were you capable over what is in My hand? Take him to the Fire." He said: "By Him in whose hand is the soul of Abu al-Qasim, he uttered a word that ruined his worldly life and his Hereafter.'"

[Footnote: Abu Dawud narrated it from the hadith of 'Ikrima ibn 'Ammar: "Damdam ibn Jaws narrated to me," with the same. Al-Musnad (2/323) and Sunan Abi Dawud no. (4901).]

**The Twelfth Hadith:** Al-Tabarani said: Abu Shaykh narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn 'Ajlan al-Asbahani, Salama ibn Shabib narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn al-Hakam ibn Aban narrated to us, from his father, from 'Ikrima, from Ibn 'Abbas, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: 'Whoever knows that I am capable of forgiving sins, I will forgive him and I do not mind, as long as he does not associate anything with Me.'"

[Footnote: In its chain is Ibrahim ibn al-Hakam ibn Aban, whom the imams declared weak. Ibn 'Adi said: "He used to connect the mursal narrations from his father, and most of what he narrates is not corroborated."]

**The Thirteenth Hadith:** The hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar and the hafiz Abu Ya'la [al-Mawsili] [addition from A] said: Hudba, i.e., Ibn Khalid, narrated to us, Sahl ibn Abi Hazm narrated to us, from Thabit, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever Allah promises a reward for a deed, He will certainly fulfill it for him, and whoever He threatens with punishment for a deed, He has the choice concerning it." Both of them narrated it alone.

[Footnote: Musnad Abi Ya'la (6/66). Al-Tabarani narrated it in al-Awsat no. (4739) and said: "No one narrated it from Thabit except Sahl, and Hudba alone narrated it from him." Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (10/211): "In it is Sahl ibn Abi Hazm, who was declared trustworthy despite his weakness, and the rest of its narrators are narrators of the Sahih."]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Bahr ibn Nasr al-Khawlani narrated to us, Khalid, meaning Ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Khurasani, narrated to us, al-Haytham ibn Jammaz narrated to us, from Sallam ibn Abi Mut'i, from Bakr ibn 'Abd Allah al-Muzani, from Ibn 'Umar, who said: "We, the companions of the Prophet (ﷺ), had no doubt about the killer of a soul, the consumer of an orphan's property, the slanderer of chaste women, and the false witness, until this verse was revealed: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive that He be associated with, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills﴾. So the companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) refrained from testifying (to the Fire for such people)."

Ibn Jarir narrated it from the hadith of al-Haytham ibn Hammad with the same.

[Footnote: Tafsir al-Tabari (8/450). Its chain includes al-Haytham ibn Jammaz, whom Ahmad, Ibn Ma'in, al-Nasa'i and others declared weak.]

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on Surah 4, verses 47–48 (part 3 of 3):

Ibn Abi Hatim also said: Abd al-Malik ibn Abi Abd al-Rahman al-Muqri [[In manuscript A: "al-Maqbari"]] narrated to us; Abdullah ibn Asim narrated to us; Salih, that is, al-Murri Abu Bishr, narrated to us, from Ayyub, from Nafi', from Ibn Umar, who said: "We would not doubt about those for whom Allah had made the Fire obligatory in the Book, until this verse was revealed to us: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive association with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills﴾." He said: "When we heard it, we refrained from declaring anyone certainly damned, and we left the matters to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic [[In manuscript D: "the Exalted"]]."

Al-Bazzar said: Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahim narrated to us; Shaiban ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us; Harb ibn Surayj narrated to us, from Ayyub, from Nafi', from Ibn Umar [may Allah be pleased with them both] [[Addition from manuscript A.]], who said: "We used to refrain from seeking forgiveness for the people of major sins, until we heard our Prophet (ﷺ) recite: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive association with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills﴾, and he said: 'I have delayed my intercession for the people of major sins from my Ummah until the Day of Resurrection.'"

Abu Ja'far al-Razi said, from al-Rabi', who said: Mujabbar informed me, from Abdullah ibn Umar, that he said: When this was revealed: ﴿Say: O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah; indeed, Allah forgives all sins; indeed, He is the Forgiving, the Merciful﴾ [Az-Zumar: 53] [[Addition from manuscript A; in manuscript H: "to the end of the verse."]], a man stood up and said: "And association with Allah, O Prophet of Allah?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) disliked that, and so he said: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive association with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills. And whoever associates others with Allah has certainly fabricated a tremendous sin﴾.

Ibn Jarir narrated it. Ibn Mardawayh also narrated it through several chains from Ibn Umar [[Tafsir al-Tabari (8/450).]].

This verse in Surat Tanzil [i.e., Surat al-Zumar] is conditioned upon repentance: whoever repents from any sin, even if it is repeated from him, Allah will accept his repentance. For this reason He said: ﴿Say: O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah; indeed, Allah forgives all sins; indeed, He is the Forgiving, the Merciful﴾ [Az-Zumar: 53], meaning: on condition of repentance. Had it not been so, association would have been included in it, and that is not valid, because He, the Exalted, has ruled here that He does not forgive association, and has ruled that He forgives what is other than it for whom He wills, meaning even if its doer does not repent. So in this respect the latter [i.e., the verse of al-Zumar] is more hopeful than the former. And Allah knows best.

* *

His saying: ﴿And whoever associates others with Allah has certainly fabricated a tremendous sin﴾ is like His saying: ﴿Indeed, association is a tremendous wrong﴾ [Luqman: 13]. It is also established in the two Sahihs, from Ibn Mas'ud, that he said: "I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, which sin is greatest?' He said: 'That you set up a rival to Allah while He created you...'" and he mentioned the rest of the hadith.

Ibn Mardawayh said: Ishaq ibn Ibrahim ibn Zayd narrated to us; Ahmad ibn Amr narrated to us; Ibrahim ibn al-Mundhir narrated to us; Ma'n narrated to us; Sa'id ibn Bashir narrated to us; Qatadah narrated to us, from al-Hasan, from Imran ibn Husayn, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Shall I inform you of the greatest of the major sins? It is association with Allah [[In manuscripts D, R, A: "ascribing partners to Allah."]]." Then he recited: ﴿And whoever associates others with Allah has certainly fabricated a tremendous sin﴾, "and disobedience to parents." Then he recited: ﴿Be grateful to Me and to your parents; to Me is the final destination﴾ [Luqman: 14] [[In its chain is Sa'id ibn Bashir, about whom some scholars spoke. Ahmad and Ibn Ma'in declared him weak, while Duhaym and others deemed him trustworthy.]]

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 4, verses 49–52 (part 1 of 2):

Al-Hasan and Qatadah said: this verse, which is His saying, ﴿Have you not seen those who claim purity for themselves?﴾, was revealed about the Jews and Christians, when they said: ﴿We are the children of God and His beloved.﴾

Ibn Zayd said: it was revealed concerning their saying, ﴿We are the children of God and His beloved﴾ [al-Ma'idah 5:18], and concerning their saying, ﴿None will enter Paradise except those who are Jews or Christians﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:111].

Mujahid said: they used to put their children in front of them in supplication and prayer, having them lead them, and they claimed that they had no sins.

Ikrimah and Abu Malik said the same. Ibn Jarir narrated this.

Al-'Awfi narrated from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His saying, ﴿Have you not seen those who claim purity for themselves?﴾: the Jews said, "Our children have died, and they are a means of nearness for us; they will intercede for us and purify us." So God revealed to Muhammad (ﷺ), ﴿Have you not seen those who claim purity for themselves? Rather, God purifies whom He wills, and they will not be wronged even as much as a thread.﴾ Ibn Jarir narrated it.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: my father narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Musaffa narrated to us, Ibn Humayr narrated to us, from Ibn Lahi'ah, from Bishr ibn Abi 'Amr, from Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Jews used to put their children forward to lead them in prayer and to offer their sacrifices, and they claimed that they had no sins or wrongdoings. And they lied. God said, "I do not purify one who has sin by another who has no sin." And God revealed: ﴿Have you not seen those who claim purity for themselves?﴾

Then he said: it is similarly narrated from Mujahid, Abu Malik, al-Suddi, Ikrimah and al-Dahhak.

Al-Dahhak said: they said, "We have no sins, just as our children have no sins." So God revealed this concerning them.

It was also said: it was revealed in condemnation of mutual praise and self-recommendation.

There is a sound hadith in Muslim, from al-Miqdad ibn al-Aswad, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) commanded us to throw dust in the faces of those who praise excessively.

In another hadith, recorded in the two Sahihs through the route of Khalid al-Hadhdha', from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakrah, from his father: the Messenger of God (ﷺ) heard a man praising another man, so he said, "Woe to you! You have cut the neck of your companion." Then he said, "If one of you must praise his companion, let him say: I think him to be such-and-such, and let him not claim purity for anyone before God."

Imam Ahmad said: Mu'tamir narrated to us, from his father, from Nu'aym ibn Abi Hind, who said: 'Umar ibn al-Khattab said: whoever says "I am a believer" is an unbeliever; whoever says "he is a scholar" is ignorant; and whoever says "he is in Paradise" is in the Fire.

Ibn Mardawayh narrated it through the route of Musa ibn 'Ubaydah, from Talhah ibn 'Ubaydullah ibn Kurayz, from 'Umar, that he said: The thing I fear most for you is a person's self-admiration in his opinion. Whoever says "he is a believer" is an unbeliever; whoever says "he is a scholar" is ignorant; and whoever says "he is in Paradise" is in the Fire.

Ibn Kathir mentioned it in the Musnad of 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (2/574), and Talhah did not meet 'Umar, so it is disconnected (munqati').

Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Shu'bah and Hajjaj narrated to us, Shu'bah informed us, from Sa'd ibn Ibrahim, from Ma'bad al-Juhani, who said: Mu'awiyah rarely narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ), but he was almost never absent on Friday from narrating these words from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Whoever God intends good for, He gives him understanding in the religion. This wealth is sweet and green; whoever takes it with its right, it will be blessed for him in it. Beware of excessive praise, for it is slaughter."

Ibn Majah narrated from it: "Beware of excessive praise, for it is slaughter," from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, from Ghundar, from Shu'bah, with it.

Al-Busiri said in al-Zawa'id (3/181): "This is a good chain; Ma'bad is disputed, and the rest of the narrators of the chain are trustworthy."

This Ma'bad is Ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Uwaym al-Basri al-Qadari.

Ibn Jarir said: Yahya ibn Ibrahim al-Mas'udi narrated to us, my father narrated to me, from his father, from his grandfather, from al-A'mash, from Qays ibn Muslim, from Tariq ibn Shihab, who said: 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud said: A man goes out in the morning with his religion, then returns with nothing of it left. He meets a man who cannot benefit or harm him, and says to him, "By God, you are such-and-such," so he may return without having achieved anything of his need, and having angered God. Then he recited: ﴿Have you not seen those who claim purity for themselves?﴾ to the end of the verse.

The discussion of this will come at length under His saying, ﴿So do not claim purity for yourselves; He knows best who is pious﴾ [al-Najm 53:32]. Thus He said, ﴿But God purifies whom He wills﴾, meaning the matter returns to God, Mighty and Majestic, because He knows the realities of affairs and their subtleties.

Then He said, ﴿and they will not be wronged even as much as a thread﴾, meaning no reward will be withheld from anyone to the amount of the fatil (thread).

Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, Ikrimah, 'Ata', al-Hasan, Qatadah, and many of the early scholars said: it is what is in the slit of a date-stone.

It is also narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: it is what you twist between your fingers. Both statements are close in meaning.

* *

His saying, ﴿See how they invent lies against God﴾, meaning: in their self-purification and their claim that they are God's children and beloved, and their saying, ﴿None will enter Paradise except those who are Jews or Christians﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:111], and their saying, ﴿The Fire will not touch us except for a number of days﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:80], and their reliance on the righteous deeds of their forefathers. God has ruled that the deeds of fathers do not avail the children at all, in His saying: ﴿That is a community that has passed away; for them is what they earned, and for you is what you earned, and you will not be questioned about what they used to do﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:141].

Then He said, ﴿And sufficient is it as a manifest sin﴾, meaning: sufficient is their doing this as an evident lie and fabrication.

* *

His saying, ﴿Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Scripture, who believe in al-Jibt and al-Taghut?﴾ As for "al-Jibt", Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated from Hassan ibn Fa'id, from 'Umar ibn al-Khattab that he said: "al-Jibt" is sorcery, and "al-Taghut" is Satan.

It is similarly narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, Abu al-'Aliyah, Mujahid, 'Ata', Ikrimah, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Sha'bi, al-Hasan, al-Dahhak and al-Suddi.

It is also narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, Abu al-'Aliyah, Mujahid, 'Ata', Ikrimah, [Abu Malik], Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Sha'bi, al-Hasan and 'Atiyyah: "al-Jibt" is Satan. Ibn 'Abbas added: in Abyssinian (Habashi) language. Also from Ibn 'Abbas: "al-Jibt" is polytheism. And from him: "al-Jibt" is idols.

From al-Sha'bi: "al-Jibt" is the soothsayer (kahin). From Ibn 'Abbas: "al-Jibt" is Huyayy ibn Akhtab. From Mujahid: "al-Jibt" is Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf.

Al-'Allamah Abu Nasr Isma'il ibn Hammad al-Jawhari said in his book "al-Sihah": "al-Jibt" is a word applied to the idol, the soothsayer, the sorcerer and the like. In a hadith: "Augury, divination by birds, and drawing lines are from al-Jibt." He said: this is not of pure Arabic, since the letters jim and ta' come together in one word without a liquid letter (harf dhawlaqi).

This hadith which he mentioned was narrated by Imam Ahmad in his Musnad, where he said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, 'Awf narrated to us from Hayyan Abu al-'Ala', Qatan ibn Qabisah narrated to us, from his father, Qabisah ibn Mukhariq, that he heard the Prophet (ﷺ) say: "Indeed, 'iyafah, tarq and tiyarah are from al-Jibt." 'Awf said: "'Iyafah" is driving away birds, "tarq" is drawing a line in the earth, and "al-Jibt", al-Hasan said, is Satan.

Likewise Abu Dawud in his Sunan, and al-Nasa'i and Ibn Abi Hatim in their tafsirs, narrated it from the hadith of 'Awf al-A'rabi, with it.

The discussion of "al-Taghut" has already passed in Surah al-Baqarah, sufficiently to avoid repeating it here.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: my father narrated to us, Ishaq ibn al-Daif narrated to us, Hajjaj narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, Abu al-Zubayr informed me that he heard Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah being asked about "al-Tawaghit", and he said: they are soothsayers upon whom the devils descend.

Mujahid said: "al-Taghut" is Satan in the form of a human being, to whom they go for judgment, and he is the master of their affair.

Imam Malik said: "al-Taghut" is everything that is worshipped besides God, Mighty and Majestic.

* *

His saying, ﴿And they say to those who disbelieve, "These are better guided than those who believe in the way."﴾ meaning: they prefer the disbelievers over the Muslims out of their ignorance, their lack of religion, and their disbelief in the Book of God that is in their hands.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated: Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Yazid al-Muqri' narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from 'Amr, from Ikrimah, who said: Huyayy ibn Akhtab and Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf came to the people of Makkah, and they said to them, "You are the People of the Book and the People of Knowledge; inform us about us and about Muhammad." They said, "What are you and what is Muhammad?" They said, "We join the ties of kinship, slaughter the she-camels, give water with milk, free captives, and give drink to pilgrims. Muhammad is a severed one (sunbur) who has cut our ties of kinship, and the thieves of pilgrims, the Banu Ghifar, have followed him. So are we better, or is he?" They said, "You are better and more rightly guided in the way." So God revealed: ﴿Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Scripture, who believe in al-Jibt and al-Taghut and say to those who disbelieve, "These are better guided than those who believe in the way"?﴾

This has been narrated through more than one route, from Ibn 'Abbas and a group of the early scholars.

Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Abi 'Adi narrated to us, from Da'ud, from Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: When Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf came to Makkah, Quraysh said: "Do you not see this severed one (al-sunbur al-mumbatir) from his people? He claims he is better than us, while we are the people of the pilgrimage, the people of the custodianship, and the people of the watering!" He said, "You are better." So God revealed concerning them: ﴿Surely your enemy is the one cut off﴾ [al-Kawthar 108:3], and He revealed: ﴿Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Scripture?﴾ to ﴿a helper﴾.

Ibn Ishaq said: Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad narrated to me, from Ikrimah or from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Those who gathered the confederates (al-Ahzab) from Quraysh, Ghatafan and Banu Qurayzah were Huyayy ibn Akhtab, Sallam ibn Abi al-Huqayq (Abu Rafi'), al-Rabi' ibn al-Rabi' ibn Abi al-Huqayq, Abu Ammar, Wahwah [in A: "Dahrij"] ibn Amir, and Hawdhah ibn Qays. As for Wahwah, Abu Ammar and Hawdhah, they were from Banu Wa'il, and the rest of them were from Banu al-Nadir. When they came to Quraysh, they said: "These are the rabbis of the Jews and the people of knowledge of the earlier Scriptures. Ask them: Is your religion better, or the religion of Muhammad?" So they asked them, and they said: "Rather, your religion is better than his, and you are more rightly guided than he and those who follow him." Then Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Scripture? They believe in Jibt and Taghut, and say to those who disbelieve, "These are better guided than those who believe in the way."  Those are the ones whom Allah has cursed, and whomever Allah curses, you will not find for him a helper﴾ [in A: addition], up to His saying, the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿And We gave them a great kingdom﴾.

This is a curse upon them and an information that they have no helper in this world nor in the Hereafter, because they went seeking support from the polytheists. They said that to them only to incline them toward supporting them, and indeed they responded and came with them on the Day of the Confederates, until the Prophet (ﷺ) and his Companions dug the trench around Madinah, and Allah sufficed them against their evil: ﴿And Allah repelled those who disbelieved in their rage, not having obtained any good. And Allah sufficed the believers in the fighting. And Allah is ever Strong and Exalted in Might﴾ [al-Ahzab: 25].
