Imam Ahmad said: Mu'tamir narrated to us, from his father, from Nu'aym ibn Abi Hind, who said: 'Umar ibn al-Khattab said: whoever says "I am a believer" is an unbeliever; whoever says "he is a scholar" is ignorant; and whoever says "he is in Paradise" is in the Fire.

Ibn Mardawayh narrated it through the route of Musa ibn 'Ubaydah, from Talhah ibn 'Ubaydullah ibn Kurayz, from 'Umar, that he said: The thing I fear most for you is a person's self-admiration in his opinion. Whoever says "he is a believer" is an unbeliever; whoever says "he is a scholar" is ignorant; and whoever says "he is in Paradise" is in the Fire.

Ibn Kathir mentioned it in the Musnad of 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (2/574), and Talhah did not meet 'Umar, so it is disconnected (munqati').

Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Shu'bah and Hajjaj narrated to us, Shu'bah informed us, from Sa'd ibn Ibrahim, from Ma'bad al-Juhani, who said: Mu'awiyah rarely narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ), but he was almost never absent on Friday from narrating these words from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Whoever God intends good for, He gives him understanding in the religion. This wealth is sweet and green; whoever takes it with its right, it will be blessed for him in it. Beware of excessive praise, for it is slaughter."

Ibn Majah narrated from it: "Beware of excessive praise, for it is slaughter," from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, from Ghundar, from Shu'bah, with it.

Al-Busiri said in al-Zawa'id (3/181): "This is a good chain; Ma'bad is disputed, and the rest of the narrators of the chain are trustworthy."

This Ma'bad is Ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Uwaym al-Basri al-Qadari.

Ibn Jarir said: Yahya ibn Ibrahim al-Mas'udi narrated to us, my father narrated to me, from his father, from his grandfather, from al-A'mash, from Qays ibn Muslim, from Tariq ibn Shihab, who said: 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud said: A man goes out in the morning with his religion, then returns with nothing of it left. He meets a man who cannot benefit or harm him, and says to him, "By God, you are such-and-such," so he may return without having achieved anything of his need, and having angered God. Then he recited: ﴿Have you not seen those who claim purity for themselves?﴾ to the end of the verse.

The discussion of this will come at length under His saying, ﴿So do not claim purity for yourselves; He knows best who is pious﴾ [al-Najm 53:32]. Thus He said, ﴿But God purifies whom He wills﴾, meaning the matter returns to God, Mighty and Majestic, because He knows the realities of affairs and their subtleties.

Then He said, ﴿and they will not be wronged even as much as a thread﴾, meaning no reward will be withheld from anyone to the amount of the fatil (thread).

Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, Ikrimah, 'Ata', al-Hasan, Qatadah, and many of the early scholars said: it is what is in the slit of a date-stone.

It is also narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: it is what you twist between your fingers. Both statements are close in meaning.

* *

His saying, ﴿See how they invent lies against God﴾, meaning: in their self-purification and their claim that they are God's children and beloved, and their saying, ﴿None will enter Paradise except those who are Jews or Christians﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:111], and their saying, ﴿The Fire will not touch us except for a number of days﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:80], and their reliance on the righteous deeds of their forefathers. God has ruled that the deeds of fathers do not avail the children at all, in His saying: ﴿That is a community that has passed away; for them is what they earned, and for you is what you earned, and you will not be questioned about what they used to do﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:141].

Then He said, ﴿And sufficient is it as a manifest sin﴾, meaning: sufficient is their doing this as an evident lie and fabrication.

* *

His saying, ﴿Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Scripture, who believe in al-Jibt and al-Taghut?﴾ As for "al-Jibt", Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated from Hassan ibn Fa'id, from 'Umar ibn al-Khattab that he said: "al-Jibt" is sorcery, and "al-Taghut" is Satan.

It is similarly narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, Abu al-'Aliyah, Mujahid, 'Ata', Ikrimah, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Sha'bi, al-Hasan, al-Dahhak and al-Suddi.

It is also narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, Abu al-'Aliyah, Mujahid, 'Ata', Ikrimah, [Abu Malik], Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Sha'bi, al-Hasan and 'Atiyyah: "al-Jibt" is Satan. Ibn 'Abbas added: in Abyssinian (Habashi) language. Also from Ibn 'Abbas: "al-Jibt" is polytheism. And from him: "al-Jibt" is idols.

From al-Sha'bi: "al-Jibt" is the soothsayer (kahin). From Ibn 'Abbas: "al-Jibt" is Huyayy ibn Akhtab. From Mujahid: "al-Jibt" is Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf.

Al-'Allamah Abu Nasr Isma'il ibn Hammad al-Jawhari said in his book "al-Sihah": "al-Jibt" is a word applied to the idol, the soothsayer, the sorcerer and the like. In a hadith: "Augury, divination by birds, and drawing lines are from al-Jibt." He said: this is not of pure Arabic, since the letters jim and ta' come together in one word without a liquid letter (harf dhawlaqi).

This hadith which he mentioned was narrated by Imam Ahmad in his Musnad, where he said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, 'Awf narrated to us from Hayyan Abu al-'Ala', Qatan ibn Qabisah narrated to us, from his father, Qabisah ibn Mukhariq, that he heard the Prophet (ﷺ) say: "Indeed, 'iyafah, tarq and tiyarah are from al-Jibt." 'Awf said: "'Iyafah" is driving away birds, "tarq" is drawing a line in the earth, and "al-Jibt", al-Hasan said, is Satan.

Likewise Abu Dawud in his Sunan, and al-Nasa'i and Ibn Abi Hatim in their tafsirs, narrated it from the hadith of 'Awf al-A'rabi, with it.

The discussion of "al-Taghut" has already passed in Surah al-Baqarah, sufficiently to avoid repeating it here.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: my father narrated to us, Ishaq ibn al-Daif narrated to us, Hajjaj narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, Abu al-Zubayr informed me that he heard Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah being asked about "al-Tawaghit", and he said: they are soothsayers upon whom the devils descend.

Mujahid said: "al-Taghut" is Satan in the form of a human being, to whom they go for judgment, and he is the master of their affair.

Imam Malik said: "al-Taghut" is everything that is worshipped besides God, Mighty and Majestic.

* *

His saying, ﴿And they say to those who disbelieve, "These are better guided than those who believe in the way."﴾ meaning: they prefer the disbelievers over the Muslims out of their ignorance, their lack of religion, and their disbelief in the Book of God that is in their hands.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated: Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Yazid al-Muqri' narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from 'Amr, from Ikrimah, who said: Huyayy ibn Akhtab and Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf came to the people of Makkah, and they said to them, "You are the People of the Book and the People of Knowledge; inform us about us and about Muhammad." They said, "What are you and what is Muhammad?" They said, "We join the ties of kinship, slaughter the she-camels, give water with milk, free captives, and give drink to pilgrims. Muhammad is a severed one (sunbur) who has cut our ties of kinship, and the thieves of pilgrims, the Banu Ghifar, have followed him. So are we better, or is he?" They said, "You are better and more rightly guided in the way." So God revealed: ﴿Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Scripture, who believe in al-Jibt and al-Taghut and say to those who disbelieve, "These are better guided than those who believe in the way"?﴾

This has been narrated through more than one route, from Ibn 'Abbas and a group of the early scholars.

Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Abi 'Adi narrated to us, from Da'ud, from Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: When Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf came to Makkah, Quraysh said: "Do you not see this severed one (al-sunbur al-mumbatir) from his people? He claims he is better than us, while we are the people of the pilgrimage, the people of the custodianship, and the people of the watering!" He said, "You are better." So God revealed concerning them: ﴿Surely your enemy is the one cut off﴾ [al-Kawthar 108:3], and He revealed: ﴿Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Scripture?﴾ to ﴿a helper﴾.

Ibn Ishaq said: Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad narrated to me, from Ikrimah or from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Those who gathered the confederates (al-Ahzab) from Quraysh, Ghatafan and Banu Qurayzah were Huyayy ibn Akhtab, Sallam ibn Abi al-Huqayq (Abu Rafi'), al-Rabi' ibn al-Rabi' ibn Abi al-Huqayq, Abu Ammar, Wahwah [in A: "Dahrij"] ibn Amir, and Hawdhah ibn Qays. As for Wahwah, Abu Ammar and Hawdhah, they were from Banu Wa'il, and the rest of them were from Banu al-Nadir. When they came to Quraysh, they said: "These are the rabbis of the Jews and the people of knowledge of the earlier Scriptures. Ask them: Is your religion better, or the religion of Muhammad?" So they asked them, and they said: "Rather, your religion is better than his, and you are more rightly guided than he and those who follow him." Then Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Scripture? They believe in Jibt and Taghut, and say to those who disbelieve, "These are better guided than those who believe in the way."  Those are the ones whom Allah has cursed, and whomever Allah curses, you will not find for him a helper﴾ [in A: addition], up to His saying, the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿And We gave them a great kingdom﴾.

This is a curse upon them and an information that they have no helper in this world nor in the Hereafter, because they went seeking support from the polytheists. They said that to them only to incline them toward supporting them, and indeed they responded and came with them on the Day of the Confederates, until the Prophet (ﷺ) and his Companions dug the trench around Madinah, and Allah sufficed them against their evil: ﴿And Allah repelled those who disbelieved in their rage, not having obtained any good. And Allah sufficed the believers in the fighting. And Allah is ever Strong and Exalted in Might﴾ [al-Ahzab: 25].

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Or do they have a share of the dominion?﴾ This is a rhetorical question of denial, meaning: they have no share of the dominion [[In D: "They have no share of it." In R and A: "They have no share in the dominion."]]. Then He described them as stingy, saying: ﴿then they would not give the people even a speck (naqir)﴾. That is, if they had a share in dominion and control, they would not give anyone among the people, especially Muhammad (ﷺ), anything, not even what could fill the naqir, which is the spot on a date stone, according to Ibn 'Abbas and most scholars.

This verse is like His saying: ﴿Say: If you possessed the treasures of the mercy of my Lord, then you would withhold them, fearing expenditure.﴾ [al-Isra' 17:100] That is, fearing that what is in your hands would run out, although its depletion is inconceivable. It is only from your miserliness and greed. For this reason He said: ﴿And man has always been stingy.﴾ [al-Isra' 17:100] That is, miserly.

Then He said: ﴿Or do they envy the people for what Allah has given them of His bounty?﴾ By this He means: their envy of the Prophet (ﷺ) for the great prophethood that Allah granted him, and their envy of him prevented them from believing in him, because he was an Arab and not from the Children of Israel.

al-Tabarani said: Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah al-Hadrami narrated to us, Yahya al-Himmani narrated to us, Qays ibn al-Rabi' narrated to us, from al-Suddi, from 'Ata', from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿Or do they envy the people [for what Allah has given them of His bounty]﴾ [[Addition from R and A; in H: "the verse".]] to the end of the verse. Ibn 'Abbas said: "We are the people, rather than the (other) people." Allah the Exalted said: ﴿We had already given the family of Abraham the Book and wisdom, and We gave them a great kingdom.﴾ That is, We had already placed prophethood among the tribes of the Children of Israel, who are the descendants of Abraham, and We sent down the Books to them, and they judged among people by the sunan (ways), which is wisdom [[In R: "by the sinin (years)."]], and We made kings among them. And despite this, ﴿among them is one who believed in it﴾, that is, in this bestowal and this blessing, ﴿and among them is one who averted from it﴾, that is, disbelieved in it, turned away from it, and strove to turn people away from it. He was one of them and of their kind, that is, of the Children of Israel. They differed about it. So how about you, O Muhammad, when you are not from the Children of Israel?

Mujahid said: ﴿Among them is one who believed in it﴾, that is, in Muhammad (ﷺ). ﴿And among them is one who averted from it﴾. So the disbelievers among them are more intense in denying you and further from what you have brought them of guidance and the manifest truth.

For this reason He said, warning them: ﴿And sufficient is Hell as a blaze.﴾ That is, the Fire is sufficient as a punishment for them for their disbelief, their obstinacy, and their opposition to the Books of Allah and His messengers.

Ibn Kathir said: Allah informs us of what He will punish with in the Fire of Hell those who disbelieve in His signs and turn away from His messengers. He says: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve in Our signs, We will surely cast them into a Fire﴾, meaning We will make them enter a Fire that encompasses all of their bodies and parts. Then He informed of the continuance of their punishment and torment, saying: ﴿Every time their skins are roasted through, We will replace them with other skins so they may taste the punishment﴾. Al-A'mash, from Ibn Umar, said: when their skins are burned, they will be replaced with white skins like sheets of paper. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it.

Yahya ibn Yazid al-Hadrami said that it reached him regarding Allah's words ﴿Every time their skins are roasted through, We will replace them with other skins so they may taste the punishment﴾ that he said: a disbeliever will be given a hundred skins, and between every two skins there will be a kind of punishment. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: my father narrated to us, Ali ibn Muhammad al-Tanafisi narrated to us, Husayn al-Ju'fi narrated to us, from Za'idah, from Hisham, from al-Hasan, regarding his statement: ﴿Every time their skins are roasted through﴾ up to the end of the verse. He said: they will be roasted seventy thousand times in a day. Husayn said: Fudayl added to it, from Hisham, from al-Hasan: every time it roasts them and consumes their flesh, it will be said to them, "Return," and they will return.

He also said: it was mentioned from Hisham ibn Ammar: Sa'id ibn Yahya, that is Sa'dan, narrated to us: Nafi', the mawla (freedman) of Yusuf al-Sulami al-Basri, narrated to us, from Nafi', from Ibn Umar, who said: a man recited this verse in the presence of Umar: ﴿Every time their skins are roasted through, We will replace them with other skins﴾. Umar said: repeat it to me. He repeated it. Mu'adh ibn Jabal said: I have its interpretation: it will be replaced a hundred times in an hour. Umar said: that is how I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

Ibn Mardawayh narrated it from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ibrahim, from Abdan ibn Muhammad al-Marwazi, from Hisham ibn Ammar, with the same wording. He also narrated it by another route with different wording: he said: Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, from Imran, Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn al-Harith narrated to us, Shayban ibn Farrukh narrated to us, Nafi' Abu Hurmuz narrated to us, Nafi' narrated to us, from Ibn Umar, who said: a man recited in the presence of Umar this verse: ﴿Every time their skins are roasted through, We will replace them with other skins so they may taste the punishment﴾ up to the end of the verse. He said: Umar said: repeat it to me, and Ka'b was present. Ka'b said: O Commander of the Faithful, I have the interpretation of this verse; I recited it before Islam. Umar said: say it, O Ka'b. If you bring it as I heard it from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), we will confirm you; otherwise we will not pay attention to it. He said: I recited it before Islam: "Every time their skins are roasted through, We will replace them with other skins in one hour, a hundred and twenty times." Umar said: that is how I heard it from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

Al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: it is written in the first Book that the skin of one of them is forty cubits, his tooth is ninety cubits, and his belly, if a mountain were placed in it, it would contain it. So when the Fire consumes their skins, they will be replaced with other skins.

There is in a hadith what is even more eloquent than this. Imam Ahmad said: Waki' narrated to us, Abu Yahya al-Tawil narrated to us, from Abu Yahya al-Qattat, from Mujahid, from Ibn Umar, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "The people of the Fire will grow large in the Fire, so that between the lobe of one of their ears and his shoulder is a journey of seven hundred years, and the thickness of his skin is seventy cubits, and his molar is like Uhud."

Ahmad alone narrated it through this route.

It has also been said that the intended meaning of His words ﴿every time their skins are roasted through﴾ is: their garments (sarabil). Ibn Jarir related this, but it is weak, because it contradicts the apparent meaning.

* *

As for His words: ﴿And those who believed and did righteous deeds, We will admit them to gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever﴾, this is information about the end of the blessed ones in the Gardens of Eden, through which rivers flow in all their paths, places and regions, wherever they wish and wherever they desire. They will abide therein forever, not moved, not removed, and not desiring any change from it.

* *

As for His words: ﴿For them therein are purified spouses﴾, meaning purified from menstruation, postpartum bleeding, filth, base character traits and deficient attributes. As Ibn Abbas said: purified from impurities and filth. Likewise said Ata', al-Hasan, al-Dahhak, al-Nakha'i, Abu Salih, Atiyyah and al-Suddi.

Mujahid said: purified from urine, menstruation, phlegm, spittle, semen and children.

Qatadah said: purified from filth and sins, with no menstruation and no defect.

* *

As for His words: ﴿And We will admit them to shade, deep shade﴾, meaning: a deep, abundant, copious, good and pleasant shade.

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, and Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, Ibn Ja'far narrated to us, both saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, saying: I heard Abu al-Dahhak narrating, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Indeed in Paradise there is a tree in whose shade a rider travels for a hundred years without cutting through it: the Tree of Eternity (Shajarat al-Khuld)."

He also said: it was mentioned from Hisham ibn Ammar: Sa'id ibn Yahya, that is Sa'dan, narrated to us: Nafi', the mawla (freedman) of Yusuf al-Sulami al-Basri, narrated to us, from Nafi', from Ibn Umar, who said: a man recited this verse in the presence of Umar: ﴿Every time their skins are roasted through, We will replace them with other skins﴾. Umar said: repeat it to me. He repeated it. Mu'adh ibn Jabal said: I have its interpretation: it will be replaced a hundred times in an hour. Umar said: that is how I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

Ibn Mardawayh narrated it from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ibrahim, from Abdan ibn Muhammad al-Marwazi, from Hisham ibn Ammar, with the same wording. He also narrated it by another route with different wording: he said: Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, from Imran, Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn al-Harith narrated to us, Shayban ibn Farrukh narrated to us, Nafi' Abu Hurmuz narrated to us, Nafi' narrated to us, from Ibn Umar, who said: a man recited in the presence of Umar this verse: ﴿Every time their skins are roasted through, We will replace them with other skins so they may taste the punishment﴾ up to the end of the verse. He said: Umar said: repeat it to me, and Ka'b was present. Ka'b said: O Commander of the Faithful, I have the interpretation of this verse; I recited it before Islam. Umar said: say it, O Ka'b. If you bring it as I heard it from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), we will confirm you; otherwise we will not pay attention to it. He said: I recited it before Islam: "Every time their skins are roasted through, We will replace them with other skins in one hour, a hundred and twenty times." Umar said: that is how I heard it from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

Al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: it is written in the first Book that the skin of one of them is forty cubits, his tooth is ninety cubits, and his belly, if a mountain were placed in it, it would contain it. So when the Fire consumes their skins, they will be replaced with other skins.

There is in a hadith what is even more eloquent than this. Imam Ahmad said: Waki' narrated to us, Abu Yahya al-Tawil narrated to us, from Abu Yahya al-Qattat, from Mujahid, from Ibn Umar, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "The people of the Fire will grow large in the Fire, so that between the lobe of one of their ears and his shoulder is a journey of seven hundred years, and the thickness of his skin is seventy cubits, and his molar is like Uhud."

Ahmad alone narrated it through this route.

It has also been said that the intended meaning of His words ﴿every time their skins are roasted through﴾ is: their garments (sarabil). Ibn Jarir related this, but it is weak, because it contradicts the apparent meaning.

* *

As for His words: ﴿And those who believed and did righteous deeds, We will admit them to gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever﴾, this is information about the end of the blessed ones in the Gardens of Eden, through which rivers flow in all their paths, places and regions, wherever they wish and wherever they desire. They will abide therein forever, not moved, not removed, and not desiring any change from it.

* *

As for His words: ﴿For them therein are purified spouses﴾, meaning purified from menstruation, postpartum bleeding, filth, base character traits and deficient attributes. As Ibn Abbas said: purified from impurities and filth. Likewise said Ata', al-Hasan, al-Dahhak, al-Nakha'i, Abu Salih, Atiyyah and al-Suddi.

Mujahid said: purified from urine, menstruation, phlegm, spittle, semen and children.

Qatadah said: purified from filth and sins, with no menstruation and no defect.

* *

As for His words: ﴿And We will admit them to shade, deep shade﴾, meaning: a deep, abundant, copious, good and pleasant shade.

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, and Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, Ibn Ja'far narrated to us, both saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, saying: I heard Abu al-Dahhak narrating, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Indeed in Paradise there is a tree in whose shade a rider travels for a hundred years without cutting through it: the Tree of Eternity (Shajarat al-Khuld)."

God, Exalted is He, informs us that He commands the return of trusts to their rightful owners. In the hadith of al-Hasan, from Samurah, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Return the trust to the one who entrusted you, and do not betray the one who betrayed you." It was related by Imam Ahmad and the compilers of the Sunan.[[I have not found anyone who narrated it from the hadith of Samurah, may Allah be pleased with him. a- Imam Ahmad narrated it in his Musnad (3/414) from a man, from the Prophet (ﷺ). b- al-Tirmidhi narrated it in his Sunan, no. (1264), and Abu Dawud in his Sunan, no. (3535), through the route of Talq ibn Ghannam, from Shurayk and Qays, from Abu Husayn, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him. al-Tirmidhi said: "A hasan gharib hadith." Abu Hatim said: "A munkar hadith; no one narrated this hadith except Talq." (al-'Ilal (1/375)). c- al-Hakim narrated it in al-Mustadrak (2/64), and al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Saghir (1/171), through the route of Ayyub ibn Suwayd, from Ibn Shawdhab, from Abu al-Tayyah, from Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, and Ayyub ibn Suwayd is weak. d- al-Tabarani narrated it in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (8/150), through the route of Yahya ibn Uthman, the paternal uncle of Amr ibn al-Rabi', from Yahya ibn Ayyub, from Ishaq ibn Asid, from Abu Hafs, from Makhul, from Abu Umamah, may Allah be pleased with him. al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (8/128): "In it is Yahya ibn Uthman ibn Salih al-Misri. Ibn Abi Hatim said: 'They have spoken about him.'" e- al-Tabari narrated it in his tafsir (8/493) through the route of Qatadah, from al-Hasan, as a mursal report.]] This includes all the trusts that are obligatory upon a person: the rights of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, over His servants, such as the prayers, the zakat, the expiations, the vows, the fasting, and other things, which are entrusted to a person and which the servants do not witness; and the rights of servants over one another, such as deposits and other things that people entrust to one another without any clear evidence (bayyinah)[[In A: "fihi" (in it).]] of it.[[In R: "nabihi" (its warning).]] Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has commanded that they be fulfilled. Whoever does not do so in this world will have it taken from him on the Day of Resurrection, as is established in the authentic hadith that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The rights will certainly be returned to their rightful owners, until the hornless sheep is avenged against the horned one."[[Muslim in his Sahih, no. "2582".]]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Ahmasi narrated to us, Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Abdullah ibn al-Sa'ib, from Zadhan, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said: "Martyrdom expiates every sin except the trust. A man will be brought on the Day of Resurrection, even if he was killed in the way of Allah, and it will be said to him: 'Return your trust.' He will say: 'How can I return it when the world has gone?' Then the trust will be displayed to him at the bottom of Hell, and he will descend toward it and carry it on his shoulder. Then it will slip from his shoulder, and he will fall after it forever and ever." Zadhan said: "I came to al-Bara' and related this to him, and he said: 'My brother spoke the truth: ﴿Indeed, Allah commands you to render trusts to their rightful owners﴾."

Sufyan al-Thawri said, from Ibn Abi Layla, from a man, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding his statement: ﴿Indeed, Allah commands you to render trusts to their rightful owners﴾: "It is general (mubhamah) for the righteous and the wicked." Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyyah said: "It is specified (musajjalah) for the righteous and the wicked." Abu al-'Aliyah said: "The trust is what they were commanded and forbidden."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa'id narrated to us, Hafs ibn Ghiyath narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu al-Duha, from Masruq, who said: Ubayy ibn Ka'b said: "Among the trusts is that a woman has been entrusted with her private part."

al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: "It is among the trusts that are between you and the people."

Ali ibn Abi Talhah said, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding ﴿Indeed, Allah commands you to render trusts to their rightful owners﴾: "It includes the ruler's admonition to women," meaning on the day of 'Id.

Many of the exegetes have mentioned that this verse was revealed concerning 'Uthman ibn Talhah ibn Abi Talhah. The name of Abu Talhah is 'Abdullah ibn 'Abd al-'Uzza ibn 'Uthman ibn 'Abd al-Dar ibn Qusayy ibn Kilab al-Qurashi al-'Abdari, the doorkeeper (hajib) of the Sacred Ka'bah, and he is the cousin (ibn 'amm) of Shaybah ibn 'Uthman ibn Abi Talhah, whose descendants have held the office of doorkeeping (hijabah) to this day. This 'Uthman embraced Islam during the truce between the Treaty of al-Hudaybiyyah and the Conquest of Makkah, together with Khalid ibn al-Walid and 'Amr ibn al-'As. As for his paternal uncle 'Uthman ibn Abi Talhah, he carried the standard of the polytheists on the day of Uhud and was killed that day as a disbeliever. We have only pointed out this lineage because many exegetes may confuse this with that. The occasion of its revelation concerning him was when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) took the key of the Ka'bah from him on the day of the Conquest, then returned it to him.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said, regarding the Battle of the Conquest: Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr narrated to me, from Ubayd Allah ibn 'Abdullah ibn Abi Thawr, from Safiyyah bint Shaybah: that when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) alighted in Makkah and the people were reassured, he went out until he came to the House (al-Bayt), and circumambulated it seven times on his riding beast, touching the corner with a staff in his hand. When he had completed his circumambulation, he called 'Uthman ibn Talhah, and took the key of the Ka'bah from him. It was opened for him, and he entered it, and found in it a dove made of wood, so he broke it with his hand and threw it away. Then he stood at the door of the Ka'bah while the people had gathered for him in the mosque.

Ibn Ishaq said: Some of the people of knowledge narrated to me that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood at the door of the Ka'bah and said: "There is no god but Allah alone, with no partner. He fulfilled His promise, He supported His servant, and He alone defeated the confederates. Every glory, blood or wealth that is claimed is under these two feet of mine, except the custodianship of the House (sidanat al-bayt) and the provision of water to the pilgrims (siqayat al-hajj)." He mentioned the rest of the hadith of the Prophet's sermon on that day, until he said: Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sat down in the mosque, and 'Ali ibn Abi Talib came to him with the key of the Ka'bah in his hand and said: "O Messenger of Allah, combine for us the doorkeeping (hijabah) with the provision of water (siqayah), may Allah bless you." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Where is 'Uthman ibn Talhah?" He was summoned, and he said to him: "Here is your key, O 'Uthman. Today is a day of fulfilling and righteousness."[[See: al-Sirah al-Nabawiyyah of Ibn Hisham (3/413).]]

Ibn Jarir said: al-Qasim narrated to me, al-Husayn narrated to us, from Hajjaj, from Ibn Jurayj, [his statement: ﴿Indeed, Allah commands you to render trusts to their rightful owners﴾] [[An addition from R and A; in H: "in the verse".]] he said: "It was revealed concerning 'Uthman ibn Talhah. The Prophet (ﷺ) took the key of the Ka'bah from him and entered the House with it on the day of the Conquest. He came out while reciting this [[In A: "this verse".]] and called 'Uthman to him, and handed him the key." He said: 'Umar ibn al-Khattab said: "When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came out of the Ka'bah, reciting this verse, may my father and mother be his ransom, I had never heard him recite it before that."

al-Qasim narrated to us, al-Husayn narrated to us, al-Zinji ibn Khalid narrated to us, from al-Zuhri, who said: "He handed it to him and said: 'Help him.'"[[In R: "Conceal him."]]

Ibn Mardawayh narrated, through the route of al-Kalbi, from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His statement: ﴿Indeed, Allah commands you to render trusts to their rightful owners﴾, he said: "When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) conquered Makkah, he summoned 'Uthman ibn Talhah ibn Abi Talhah. When he came to him, he said: 'Show me the key.' So he brought it to him. When he extended his hand to him, al-'Abbas stood up and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, may my father and mother be your ransom, combine it for me with the provision of water.' So 'Uthman withdrew his hand. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Show me the key, O 'Uthman.' So he extended his hand to give it, and al-'Abbas said the same words as his first, so 'Uthman withdrew his hand. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'O 'Uthman, if you believe in Allah and the Last Day, then bring me the key.' He said: 'Here it is, by the trust of Allah.' He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood up and opened the door of the Ka'bah, and he found in the Ka'bah a statue of Ibrahim with arrows used for divination. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'What is wrong with the polytheists? May Allah destroy them! What is Ibrahim's concern with the arrows?' Then he called for a bowl of water, took some water and dipped it in it, then dipped those statues in it, and he took out the Station of Ibrahim, which had been in the Ka'bah, and attached it to the wall of the Ka'bah. Then he said: 'O people, this is the qiblah.'" He said: "Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out and circumambulated the House one or two rounds, then Jibril descended to him, as we have been told, with the return of the key. So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited: ﴿Indeed, Allah commands you to render trusts to their rightful owners﴾ until he finished the verse."[[Mentioned by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur (2/570), and its chain is fabricated (talif).]]

This is well known among the reports that this verse was revealed concerning that event. Whether or not it was revealed concerning that event, its ruling is general. For this reason Ibn 'Abbas and Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyyah said: "It is for the righteous and the wicked," meaning it is a command to everyone.

* *

His statement: ﴿And when you judge between people, that you judge with justice﴾ is a command from Him, Exalted, to judge between people with justice. For this reason Muhammad ibn Ka'b, Zayd ibn Aslam and Shahr ibn Hawshab said: "It was only revealed concerning the rulers," meaning the judges among the people.

And in a hadith: "Indeed Allah is with the judge as long as he does not oppress; when he oppresses, He leaves him to himself."[[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in his Sunan, no. (1330), from the hadith of 'Abdullah ibn Abi Awfa, and he said: "A hasan gharib hadith."]] And in a report: "A single day of justice is better than forty years of worship."

* *

His statement: ﴿Indeed, excellent is that with which He admonishes you﴾ means: that which He commands you with, of rendering trusts, judging with justice between people, and other of His commands and His complete, great and comprehensive laws.

* *

His statement: ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever Hearing and Seeing﴾ means: Hearing of your statements, Seeing of your actions, as Ibn Abi Hatim said:

Abu Zur'ah narrated to us, Yahya ibn Abdullah ibn Bukayr narrated to us, Abdullah ibn Lahi'ah narrated to me, from Yazid ibn Abi Habib, from Abu al-Khayr, from 'Uqbah ibn 'Amir, who said: "I saw the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) reciting this verse, ﴿Hearing, Seeing﴾, and saying: 'With everything He is Seeing.'"[[Mentioned by al-Suyuti in al-Durr (2/573).]]

Ibn Abi Hatim also said: Yahya ibn Abd al-Kadir al-Qazwini informed us, al-Muqri' informed us, meaning Abu Abd al-Rahman, Abdullah ibn Yazid narrated to us, Harmalah, meaning Ibn Imran al-Tujibi al-Misri, narrated to us, Abu Yunus narrated to us: "I heard Abu Hurayrah reciting this verse: ﴿Indeed, Allah commands you to render trusts to their rightful owners﴾ up to His statement: ﴿Indeed, excellent is that with which He admonishes you. Indeed, Allah is ever Hearing and Seeing﴾, and he placed his thumb on his ear and the finger next to it on his eye, and said: 'Thus I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recite it,' and he placed his two fingers." Abu Zakariyya said: "Al-Muqri' described it to us, and Abu Zakariyya placed his right thumb on his right eye, and the finger next to it on his right ear, and showed us, and said: 'Thus, and thus.'"[[In A: "thus and this."]]

Abu Dawud, Ibn Hibban in his Sahih, al-Hakim in his Mustadrak, and Ibn Mardawayh in his tafsir narrated it, from the hadith of Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Muqri' with its chain, similar to it.[[Sunan Abi Dawud, no. (4728); Sahih Ibn Hibban, no. (1732), "Mawarid"; al-Mustadrak (1/24); and al-Bayhaqi narrated it through al-Hakim's route in al-Asma' wa al-Sifat (p. 179).]] This Abu Yunus was the mawla of Abu Hurayrah, and his name is Sulaym ibn Jubayr.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 4, verse 59 (part 1 of 2):

Al-Bukhari said: Ṣadaqah ibn al-Faḍl narrated to us, Ḥajjāj ibn Muḥammad al-A'war narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Ya'lā ibn Muslim, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding ﴿Obey Allah, and obey the Messenger and those in authority among you﴾. He said: It was revealed concerning 'Abd Allah ibn Ḥudhafah ibn Qays ibn 'Adi, when the Prophet (ﷺ) sent him in a military detachment (sariyyah).

In this same form, the whole group of compilers (ahl al-sunan and others) related it, except Ibn Majah, through the narration of Ḥajjāj ibn Muḥammad al-A'war, with the same chain. Al-Tirmidhi said: "It is a ḥasan gharib ḥadith, and we only know it through the narration of Ibn Jurayj."¹

Imam Ahmad ibn Ḥanbal said: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn 'Ubayda, from Abu 'Abd al-Raḥman al-Sulami, from 'Ali, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent a detachment and appointed over them a man from the Ansar. When they set out, he became angry with them over something. He said: "Did the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) not command you to obey me?" They said: "Yes." He said: "Gather wood for me." Then he called for a fire, lit it, and said: "I have resolved that you must enter it." So the people intended to enter it. A young man among them said: "You only fled to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) from the Fire, so do not hasten until you meet the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). If he commands you to enter it, then enter." They returned to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and informed him, and he said: "If you had entered it, you would never have come out of it. Obedience is only in what is right (al-ma'ruf)." Both (al-Bukhari and Muslim) related it in their Ṣaḥīḥs through the narration of al-A'mash, with the same chain.²

Abu Dawud said: Musaddad narrated to us, Yaḥyā narrated to us, from 'Ubayd Allah, Nafi' narrated to us, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "Hearing and obeying is incumbent upon the Muslim person in what he loves and in what he dislikes, so long as he is not commanded to commit an act of disobedience. If he is commanded to commit an act of disobedience, then there is no hearing and no obedience."

Both (al-Bukhari and Muslim) related it through the narration of Yaḥyā al-Qaṭṭān.³

It is related from 'Ubada ibn al-Ṣamit, who said: "We pledged allegiance to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to hear and obey, in our ease and our hardship, in what we like and what we dislike, in our difficulties and our ease, and in being given preference over us, and that we would not dispute the command with its people." He said: "Except that you see open disbelief (kufr bawah), for which you have a proof from Allah." Both (al-Bukhari and Muslim) related it.⁴

In another ḥadith, from Anas, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Hear and obey, even if an Abyssinian slave is put in charge over you, whose head is like a raisin." Al-Bukhari related it.⁵

And from Abu Hurayrah, who said: "My beloved (khalil) (ﷺ) enjoined me to hear and obey, even if he were a mutilated Abyssinian slave." Muslim related it.⁶

And from Umm al-Ḥuṣayn, that she heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) delivering a sermon during the Farewell Pilgrimage, saying: "Even if a slave were appointed over you, leading you by the Book of Allah, hear him and obey." Muslim related it. In one wording of his: "an Abyssinian slave with his limbs cut off."⁷

Ibn Jarir said: 'Ali ibn Muslim al-Tusi narrated to me, Ibn Abi Fudayk narrated to us, 'Abd Allah ibn Muḥammad ibn 'Urwah narrated to me, from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from Abu Ṣāliḥ al-Sammān, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "After me, rulers will govern you. The righteous one among them will govern you with his righteousness, and the wicked one will govern you with his wickedness. So hear them and obey them in everything that agrees with the truth. Pray behind them. If they do good, it is for you and for them; and if they do wrong, it is for you and against them."⁸

And from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The Children of Israel were governed by prophets. Whenever a prophet died, another prophet succeeded him. But there is no prophet after me, and there will be caliphs who will increase in number." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, what do you command us?" He said: "Fulfil the allegiance to the first, then the first, and give them their right, for Allah will call them to account for what He entrusted them with." Both (al-Bukhari and Muslim) related it.⁹

And from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with both of them, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever sees in his ruler something he dislikes, let him be patient, for no one separates from the community (jama'ah) by a hand's span and dies except that he dies a death of jahiliyyah." Both (al-Bukhari and Muslim) related it.¹⁰

And from Ibn 'Umar, that he heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Whoever withdraws his hand from obedience will meet Allah on the Day of Resurrection without any proof, and whoever dies without a bay'ah (pledge of allegiance) around his neck dies a death of jahiliyyah." Muslim related it.¹¹

Muslim also related, from 'Abd al-Raḥman ibn 'Abd Rabb al-Ka'bah, who said: "I entered the mosque and found 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As sitting in the shade of the Ka'bah, with people gathered around him. I came to them and sat with him. He said: We were with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on a journey. We stopped at a place, and some of us were repairing their tents, some were shooting arrows, and some were among their camels, when the caller of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) called out: 'Al-Salah jami'ah' (Prayer is gathering). So we gathered around the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he said: 'No prophet came before me except that it was his duty to guide his community to the good that he knew for them, and to warn them against the evil that he knew for them. And this community of yours, its well-being was placed in its beginning, and later on it will be afflicted with trials and matters that you will find objectionable. Trials will come, one part of which will make the next seem lighter. When a trial comes, the believer will say: "This will destroy me." Then it is lifted, and another trial comes, and the believer says: "This is it, this is it." So whoever wishes to be distanced from the Fire and admitted to Paradise, let his death come upon him while he believes in Allah and the Last Day, and let him treat people as he loves to be treated. And whoever pledges allegiance to an imam, giving him the handshake of his hand and the fruit of his heart, let him obey him as far as he is able. If another comes to dispute with him, then strike the neck of the other.'" He said: "I drew close to him and said: 'I ask you by Allah, did you hear this from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)?' He pointed with his two hands to his ears and his heart and said: 'My ears heard it and my heart retained it.' I said to him: 'This is your paternal cousin Mu'awiyah, who orders us to consume our wealth among ourselves in falsehood and to kill ourselves, while Allah the Exalted says: ﴿O you who believe, do not consume one another's wealth unjustly, except through trade by mutual consent; and do not kill yourselves. Indeed, Allah is ever Merciful to you﴾ [An-Nisa: 29].'" He said: "He was silent for a while, then said: 'Obey him in obedience to Allah, and disobey him in disobedience to Allah.'"¹²

And the ḥadiths on this subject are numerous.

Ibn Jarir said: Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn narrated to us, Aḥmad ibn al-Mufaḍḍal narrated to us, Asbāṭ narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿Obey Allah, and obey the Messenger and those in authority among you﴾, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent a detachment under the command of Khalid ibn al-Walid, and among them was 'Ammar ibn Yasir. They marched toward the people they were targeting. When they reached near them, they camped for the night. Dhu al-'Uyaynatayn came to them and informed them, and in the morning they had all fled except one man. He ordered his family, and they gathered their belongings, then he went walking in the darkness of the night until he reached the camp of Khalid. He asked about 'Ammar ibn Yasir, and came to him and said: "O Abu al-Yaqẓan, I have embraced Islam and I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger. When my people heard of you, they fled, but I remained. Will my Islam benefit me tomorrow, or else I will flee?" 'Ammar said: "Rather, it will benefit you, so remain." He remained. When they woke up, Khalid raided, and found no one except that man, so he seized him and took his property. The news reached 'Ammar, so he came to Khalid and said: "Release the man, for he has embraced Islam, and he is under my protection." Khalid said: "And what business do you have granting protection?" They quarrelled and raised the matter to the Prophet (ﷺ). He upheld 'Ammar's protection, and forbade him from granting protection a second time over a commander's (men). They quarrelled again in the presence of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Khalid said: "O Messenger of Allah, will you leave this mutilated slave to insult me?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O Khalid, do not insult 'Ammar, for whoever insults 'Ammar, Allah will insult him, and whoever hates him, Allah will hate him, and whoever curses 'Ammar, Allah will curse him." 'Ammar became angry and stood up, and Khalid followed him until he took hold of his garment and apologized to him, and he was pleased with him. Then Allah the Mighty and Majestic revealed His words: ﴿Obey Allah, and obey the Messenger and those in authority among you﴾.¹³

Ibn Abi Ḥatim related it likewise through a route from al-Suddi, as a mursal (a report with a missing link). Ibn Mardawayh related it through the narration of al-Ḥakam ibn Ẓuhayr, from al-Suddi, from Abu Ṣāliḥ, from Ibn 'Abbas, and mentioned it in similar form.¹⁴ And Allah knows best.

'Ali ibn Abi Ṭalḥah related, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding ﴿those in authority among you﴾: "meaning the people of understanding (fiqh) and religion." Likewise said Mujahid, 'Ata', al-Hasan al-Basri, and Abu al-'Aliyah: ﴿those in authority among you﴾ means "the scholars."

The apparent meaning, and Allah knows best, is that the verse includes all of those in authority, both the rulers and the scholars, as has already been mentioned. Allah the Exalted has said: ﴿Why do the rabbis and the scholars not forbid them from their sayings of sin and their consuming of unlawful gain?﴾ [Al-Ma'idah: 63]. And Allah the Exalted has said: ﴿So ask the people of remembrance (ahl al-dhikr) if you do not know﴾ [An-Nahl: 43]. And in the authentic ḥadith agreed upon (muttafaq 'alayh), from Abu Hurayrah, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), that he said: "Whoever obeys me has obeyed Allah, and whoever disobeys me has disobeyed Allah. Whoever obeys my commander has obeyed me, and whoever disobeys my commander has disobeyed me."¹⁵

These are commands to obey the scholars and the rulers. Therefore Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Obey Allah﴾, meaning: follow His Book; ﴿and obey the Messenger﴾, meaning: adhere to his Sunnah; ﴿and those in authority among you﴾, meaning: in what they command you of obedience to Allah, not in disobedience to Allah. For there is no obedience to any created being in disobedience to Allah, as has already been mentioned in the authentic ḥadith: "Obedience is only in what is right (al-ma'ruf)."

Imam Ahmad said: 'Abd al-Raḥman narrated to us, Hammam narrated to us, Qatadah narrated to us, from Abu Mirabah, from 'Imran ibn Ḥuṣayn, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "There is no obedience in disobedience to Allah."¹⁶

* * *

As for His words: ﴿And if you dispute over anything, refer it back to Allah and the Messenger﴾, Mujahid and many of the early scholars (salaf) said: that is, to the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Messenger.

This is a command from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, that whatever the people dispute about, in the foundations of the religion and its branches, the dispute should be referred back to the Book and the Sunnah, as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And whatever you differ over, its ruling is with Allah﴾ [Ash-Shura: 10]. So whatever the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Messenger judge and testify to be sound, that is the truth, and what is after the truth but error? For this reason Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿If you should believe in Allah and the Last Day﴾, meaning: refer the disputes and ignorance back to the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Messenger, and seek judgment by them in what has arisen between you. ﴿If you should believe in Allah and the Last Day﴾.

This indicates that whoever does not seek judgment by the Book and the Sunnah in the matter of dispute, and does not return to them in that, then he is not a believer in Allah nor in the Last Day.

* *

And His saying: ﴿That is better﴾, meaning: seeking judgment by the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Messenger, and returning to them for the resolution of the dispute, is better. ﴿And best in result﴾, meaning: best in outcome and final destination, as said by As-Suddi and others. Mujahid said: "And best in reward." And it is close in meaning.

This is a denial from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, against one who claims to believe in what Allah sent down to His Messenger and to the earlier prophets, yet at the same time wishes to refer the settlement of disputes to other than the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Messenger. It is mentioned in the occasion of revelation (sabab al-nuzul) of this verse that it concerned a man from the Ansar and a man from the Jews who were in dispute. The Jew said: "Between me and you is Muhammad." The other said: "Between me and you is Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf." It was also said that it concerned a group of hypocrites (munafiqun), who had outwardly embraced Islam and wished to have their disputes judged by the judges of the jahiliyyah (the age of ignorance before Islam). And it was said other than this. The verse is more general than all of that, for it censures whoever turns away from the Book and the Sunnah and refers to whatever else is false, and this is what is meant here by the taghut (that which is worshipped or obeyed in defiance of Allah). For this reason He said: ﴿They wish to refer their judgment to the taghut, although they were commanded to reject it, and Satan wishes to lead them far astray. And when it is said to them, "Come to what Allah has sent down and to the Messenger," you see the hypocrites turning away from you with aversion﴾ [[Addition from A; in H: "to its end."]].

* *

His saying ﴿turning away from you with aversion﴾ means: they turn away from you with a turning away like that of the arrogant from such things. As Allah, the Exalted, said about the polytheists: ﴿And when it is said to them, "Follow what Allah has sent down," they say, "Rather, we will follow what we found our fathers upon"﴾ [Luqman: 21]. These and those are the opposite of the believers, concerning whom Allah said: ﴿The only saying of the believers, when they are called to Allah and His Messenger to judge between them, is that they say, "We hear and we obey." And it is those who are the successful﴾ [[Addition from A; in H: "the verse."]] [al-Nur: 51].

And it is those who are the successful﴾ [[Addition from A; in H: "the verse."]] [al-Nur: 51].

Then Allah the Exalted said, in condemning the hypocrites: ﴿So how [will it be] when a disaster strikes them because of what their hands have put forward?﴾ That is: how will it be with them when destiny drives them to you because of calamities that befall them as a result of their sins, and they are in need of you in that matter? ﴿Then they come to you swearing by Allah, "We intended nothing but good and reconciliation."﴾ That is: they come to you making excuses and swearing, "We intended by going elsewhere, and by bringing our dispute before your enemies, nothing but good and reconciliation" — that is, conciliation and flattery — not because we believe that ruling to be valid, just as Allah the Exalted informed us about them in His saying: ﴿So you see those in whose hearts is a disease hastening toward them, saying, "We fear that a misfortune may befall us." But perhaps Allah will bring a conquest or a decision from Him, so they will become, over what they had concealed within themselves, regretful﴾ [Al-Ma'idah: 52].

Al-Tabarani said: Abu Zayd Ahmad ibn Yazid al-Hawti narrated to us, Abu al-Yaman narrated to us, Safwan ibn Umar narrated to us, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Abu Barzah al-Aslami was a soothsayer who judged between the Jews in what they disputed, and some Muslims went to him for judgment, so Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿Have you not seen those who claim that they believe in what has been revealed to you and what was revealed before you [while they desire to refer their judgment to the Taghut]?﴾ up to His saying: ﴿We intended nothing but good and reconciliation.﴾

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Those are the ones whom Allah knows what is in their hearts﴾. That is: this type of people are the hypocrites, and Allah knows what is in their hearts and will recompense them for that, for nothing is hidden from Him. So be content with Him regarding them, O Muhammad, for Allah knows their outward and inward states. Therefore He said to him: ﴿So turn away from them﴾, that is: do not rebuke them for what is in their hearts; ﴿and admonish them﴾, that is: forbid them for the hypocrisy and the evil secrets in their hearts; ﴿and speak to them in their souls a far-reaching word﴾, that is: advise them privately between you and them with an eloquent speech that deters them.

Then Allah the Exalted said, in condemning the hypocrites: ﴿So how [will it be] when a disaster strikes them because of what their hands have put forward?﴾ That is: how will it be with them when destiny drives them to you because of calamities that befall them as a result of their sins, and they are in need of you in that matter? ﴿Then they come to you swearing by Allah, "We intended nothing but good and reconciliation."﴾ That is: they come to you making excuses and swearing, "We intended by going elsewhere, and by bringing our dispute before your enemies, nothing but good and reconciliation" — that is, conciliation and flattery — not because we believe that ruling to be valid, just as Allah the Exalted informed us about them in His saying: ﴿So you see those in whose hearts is a disease hastening toward them, saying, "We fear that a misfortune may befall us." The Most High says: ﴿And We did not send any messenger except to be obeyed, by Allah's leave﴾. That is, obedience to him is obligatory upon those to whom he was sent. As for His words ﴿by Allah's leave﴾, Mujahid said: that is, no one obeys except by My permission. Meaning, none obeys them except those whom I have granted success to do so, as in His words: ﴿And Allah had certainly fulfilled His promise to you when you were killing them by His permission﴾ [Al 'Imran: 52], that is, by His command, decree, will, and His giving you power over them.

And His words: ﴿And if they, when they had wronged themselves, had come to you and asked forgiveness of Allah and the Messenger had asked forgiveness for them, they would have found Allah Accepting of repentance and Merciful﴾. The Most High guides the disobedient and the sinners: when error and disobedience befall them, they should come to the Messenger (ﷺ), ask Allah's forgiveness in his presence, and ask him to seek forgiveness for them. If they do that, Allah will turn to them in repentance, show them mercy, and forgive them. For this reason He said: ﴿they would have found Allah Accepting of repentance and Merciful﴾.

A group of scholars, among them Shaykh Abu Nasr ibn al-Sabbagh in his book "al-Shamil", mentioned the well-known account related from al-'Utbi, who said: I was sitting by the grave of the Prophet (ﷺ) when a Bedouin came and said: "Peace be upon you, O Messenger of Allah. I heard Allah say: ﴿And if they, when they had wronged themselves, had come to you and asked forgiveness of Allah and the Messenger had asked forgiveness for them, they would have found Allah Accepting of repentance and Merciful﴾. I have come to you seeking forgiveness for my sin, seeking your intercession with my Lord." Then he recited:

"O best of those whose bones are buried in the valley,
whose fragrance has made the valley and the hills fragrant.
My soul is the ransom for a grave in which you dwell,
in which are chastity, generosity and nobility."

Then the Bedouin departed, and I was overcome by sleep, and I saw the Prophet (ﷺ) in a dream. He said: "O 'Utbi, go to the Bedouin and give him the good news that Allah has forgiven him."

[Editor's note: This account was mentioned by al-Nawawi in al-Majmu' (8/217) and in al-Idah (p. 498), and he added the following two verses: "You are the intercessor whose intercession is hoped for, over the Sirat when feet slip. And your two companions, I shall never forget them, may peace from me be upon you as long as the pen writes." He introduced it with the words: "Among the finest things said is what our companions related from al-'Utbi, praising it," and then mentioned it in full. Ibn Kathir here did not transmit it as an authority nor endorse it; rather he quoted it as he quoted some Isra'iliyyat (Israelite narratives) in his tafsir. It is a false account and a weak story, and some people use it to argue for the permissibility of seeking tawassul (intercession/means) through the Messenger (ﷺ) after his death. The reply to it is given in four points, mentioned by the honourable Shaykh Salih Al al-Shaykh in his book "Hadhihi Mafahimuna" (p. 76):

First: Since it is not from the Sunnah of the Messenger (ﷺ), nor the practice of his rightly-guided caliphs, nor his noble companions, nor the Followers and the praiseworthy generations, but is merely a report about an unknown person transmitted through a weak chain, how can it be relied upon in the doctrine of tawhid, which is the foundation of foundations? And how can it be relied upon when it contradicts the authentic hadiths that forbid exaggeration at graves, exaggeration regarding the righteous in general, and exaggeration regarding his grave and about him (ﷺ) in particular? As for those scholars who transmitted it or praised it, that is not a proof with which authentic texts may be opposed and the creed of the Salaf contradicted. Matters may be hidden from some scholars that are clear to others, and they may err in their transmission and opinion, and the proof lies with whoever opposes them.

Since we know the path of right guidance, we have no concern with what so-and-so said or what so-and-so related. Our religion is not built upon narratives and dreams, but upon sound proofs.

Second: Some matters and meanings may be hidden even from those who have cast off rivals (andad) and disavowed shirk and its people, as when some of the Companions said: "Make for us a dhat anwat (tree of hanging) just as they have a dhat anwat," and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allahu akbar! It is the ways of the past nations! You have said, by Him in whose hand is my soul, what the people of Moses said: 'Make for us a god just as they have gods.'" (Authentic hadith.)

The argument in this is that those Companions, though they were recent in their conversion from disbelief, had entered the religion by "There is no god but Allah," which casts off rivals and all kinds of shirk and affirms the One worshipped. Yet despite that, and despite the true knowledge of its meaning held by those who said it, some matters of its details were hidden from them. The point is that when the evidence is clear and the proof is made manifest, one must return to it and adhere to it. The ignorant may be excused, as those Companions were excused in their saying: "Make for us a dhat anwat." Other scholars are even more deserving of the possibility that some matters, even in tawhid and shirk, may be hidden from them.

Third: How dares anyone oppose the texts of the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Messenger (ﷺ) with the saying of someone who related it approvingly? Allah, glorified is He, says: ﴿Let those who oppose his command beware lest a trial afflict them or a painful punishment strike them﴾ [An-Nur: 63].

Imam Ahmad said: "I am amazed at people who know the chain of transmission and its authenticity, yet go to the opinion of Sufyan, while Allah the Most High says: ﴿Let those who oppose his command beware lest a trial afflict them.﴾ Do you know what the trial is? The trial is shirk. Perhaps if some of his words are rejected, something of deviation will enter his heart and he will perish." This was related from Ahmad by al-Fadl ibn Ziyad and Abu Talib, and perhaps it is in Ahmad's book "Ta'at al-Rasul (ﷺ)" (Obedience to the Messenger), may Allah have mercy on him.

So obedience to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) takes precedence over the obedience of anyone, even if the best of this Ummah are Abu Bakr and 'Umar. As Ibn 'Abbas said: "It is about to happen that stones will fall upon you from the sky. I say: the Messenger of Allah said, and you say: Abu Bakr and 'Umar said."

How then would Ibn 'Abbas view those people who oppose the established Sunnah and the clear proof with the saying of a Bedouin in the account of al-'Utbi, which is weak and rejected?

The Sunnah in the hearts of those who love it is greater and more precious than those flimsy arguments put forward by the owner of innovated notions, notions built upon dreams and abominations. So marvel at this, and devote yourself to following the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Beware, then beware, lest you reject the authentic hadiths and believe in false and weak reports, for whoever does so is about to have a trial enter his heart and perish.

Fourth: Every scholar is contradicted in matters he has chosen, either due to opinion or the weakness of his evidence, and they are excused before the path has been made clear by its proofs. If people pursued the anomalies and dispensations of the mujtahids, they would leave the religion of Islam for another religion, as it is said: "Whoever pursues dispensations becomes a heretic." If someone seeking corruption and deviation from the path were to take their dispensations as a ladder to climb toward his desires, it would be obligatory for the ruler to suppress him, prevent him, and discipline him, as is well known in the jurisprudence of the four Imams and others.

What has been mentioned indicates that whoever uses a scholar's opinion, known to be in error, to justify his offence, it is accepted from him and he is not blamed.

O Allah, preserve for us our religion and our tawhid.]
