And His words: ﴿But no, by your Lord, they will not [truly] believe until they make you judge concerning that over which they dispute among themselves, and then they find within themselves no discomfort from what you have decided and submit completely﴾. The Most High swears by His noble and sacred Self that no one truly believes until they make the Messenger (ﷺ) judge in all matters. Whatever he judges is the truth to which submission is obligatory, inwardly and outwardly. For this reason He said: ﴿then they find within themselves no discomfort from what you have decided and submit completely﴾, that is: when they make you judge, they obey you inwardly, so they find in themselves no discomfort at what you have judged, and they submit to it outwardly and inwardly, submitting entirely, without resistance, opposition, or dispute, as occurs in the hadith: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, none of you believes until his desire follows what I have brought."

Al-Bukhari said: Ali ibn 'Abd Allah narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from 'Urwa, who said: al-Zubayr disputed with a man [from the Ansar] concerning a watercourse of al-Harra, and the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Irrigate, O Zubayr, then release the water to your neighbour." The Ansari said: "O Messenger of Allah, was he the son of your paternal aunt [or: your uncle]?" Then the face of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) changed colour, and he said: "Irrigate, O Zubayr, then hold the water until it reaches the wall, then release the water to your neighbour." The Prophet (ﷺ) had given al-Zubayr his full right in the explicit judgment, after the Ansari had provoked him, although he had previously given them both advice that offered latitude. Al-Zubayr said: "I do not think this verse was revealed except concerning that: ﴿But no, by your Lord, they will not [truly] believe until they make you judge concerning that over which they dispute among themselves...﴾" to the end of the verse.

Thus al-Bukhari related it here, meaning in the Book of Tafsir of his Sahih, through the hadith of Ma'mar; and in the Book of Drinking (Shurb) through the hadith of Ibn Jurayj and Ma'mar also; and in the Book of Reconciliation (Sulh) through the hadith of Shu'ayb ibn Abi Hamza. All three transmitted from al-Zuhri, from 'Urwa, and he mentioned it. [Sahih al-Bukhari, nos. (4585), (2361), (2362), (2708).] Its form is that of a mursal report (one where the Successor omits the Companion), though it is connected in meaning.

Imam Ahmad also related it through this route and explicitly stated the omission: He said: Abu al-Yaman narrated to us, Shu'ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri: 'Urwa ibn al-Zubayr informed me that al-Zubayr used to narrate that he disputed with a man from the Ansar who had witnessed Badr, before the Prophet (ﷺ), concerning the watercourses of al-Harra, with which both of them used to irrigate. The Prophet (ﷺ) said to al-Zubayr: "Irrigate, then release [the water] to your neighbour." The Ansari became angry and said: "O Messenger of Allah, was he the son of your paternal aunt?" Then the face of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) changed colour, and he said: "Irrigate, O Zubayr, then hold the water until it reaches the wall." So the Prophet (ﷺ) gave al-Zubayr his right. The Prophet (ﷺ) had previously given al-Zubayr an opinion by which he intended latitude for him and for the Ansari. When the Ansari provoked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), the Prophet (ﷺ) gave al-Zubayr his full right in the explicit judgment. 'Urwa said: Al-Zubayr said: "By Allah, I do not think this verse was revealed except concerning that: ﴿But no, by your Lord, they will not [truly] believe until they make you judge concerning that over which they dispute among themselves, then they find within themselves no discomfort from what you have decided and submit completely﴾."

This is how Imam Ahmad related it [al-Musnad (1/165)]. It is interrupted (munqati') between 'Urwa and his father al-Zubayr, for he did not hear it from him. What is certain is that he heard it from his brother 'Abd Allah. Abu Muhammad 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hatim related it in this way in his tafsir, saying:

Yunus ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, Ibn Wahb informed us, al-Layth and Yunus narrated to us, from Ibn Shihab, that 'Urwa ibn al-Zubayr told him that 'Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr told him, from al-Zubayr ibn al-'Awwam: that he disputed with a man from the Ansar who had witnessed Badr with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), before the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), concerning watercourses in al-Harra, with which both of them irrigated the palm trees. The Ansari said: "Let the water flow." Al-Zubayr refused him. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Irrigate, O Zubayr, then release [the water] to your neighbour." The Ansari became angry and said: "O Messenger of Allah, was he the son of your paternal aunt?" The face of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) changed colour, and he said: "Irrigate, O Zubayr, then hold the water until it reaches the wall." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gave al-Zubayr his right. Before that, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had given al-Zubayr an opinion by which he intended latitude for him and for the Ansari. When the Ansari provoked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), he gave al-Zubayr his full right in the explicit judgment. Al-Zubayr said: "I do not think this verse was revealed except concerning that: ﴿But no, by your Lord, they will not [truly] believe until they make you judge concerning that over which they dispute among themselves, then they find within themselves no discomfort from what you have decided and submit completely﴾."

Thus al-Nasa'i related it through the hadith of Ibn Wahb, with the same chain. Ahmad and the whole group related it through the hadith of al-Layth, with the same chain. [al-Musnad (4/4); Sahih al-Bukhari (2359); Sahih Muslim (2357); Sunan Abi Dawud (3637); Sunan al-Tirmidhi (1363); Sunan al-Nasa'i (8/245); Sunan Ibn Majah (15).] The compilers of the Atraf (indexes of hadith by their opening portions) placed it in the Musnad of 'Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr, and Ahmad likewise included it in the Musnad of 'Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr. And Allah knows best.

What is most astonishing is al-Hakim Abu 'Abd Allah al-Nisaburi, for he related this hadith through the route of the nephew of Ibn Shihab, from his paternal uncle, from 'Urwa, from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr, from al-Zubayr, and mentioned it, then said: "Its chain is sound, but they (al-Bukhari and Muslim) did not record it." I know of no one who transmitted this chain from al-Zuhri naming 'Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr except his nephew, and he is weak in that narration. [al-Mustadrak (3/364).]

Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on Surah 4, verses 64–65 (part 2 of 2):

Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh said: Muhammad ibn 'Ali Abu Duhaym narrated to us, Ahmad ibn Hazim narrated to us, al-Fadl ibn Dukayn narrated to us, Ibn 'Uyaynah narrated to us, from 'Amr ibn Dinar, from Salamah (a man from the family of Abu Salamah), who said: al-Zubayr disputed with a man before the Prophet ﷺ, and he judged in favour of al-Zubayr. The man said: "He only judged for him because he is the son of his paternal aunt." Then the verse was revealed: ﴿But no, by your Lord, they will not believe until they make you judge concerning that over which they dispute among themselves, then find within themselves no discomfort from what you have decided⦆, and so on. [Al-Humaydi in his Musnad (no. 300) and Sa'id ibn Mansur in his Sunan (no. 660) also narrated it through Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah, as a mursal report.]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, 'Amr ibn 'Uthman narrated to us, Abu Haywah narrated to us, Sa'id ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz narrated to us, from al-Zuhri, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, concerning His saying: ﴿But no, by your Lord, they will not believe [until they make you judge]⦆ [the verse], he said: It was revealed concerning al-Zubayr ibn al-'Awwam and Hatib ibn Abi Balta'ah, who disputed over water, and the Prophet ﷺ judged that the upper land should be irrigated first, then the lower. This is a mursal report, but it contains the benefit of naming the Ansari (man).[[Mentioned by al-Suyuti in al-Durr (2/584).]]

A Very Strange Other Cause of Revelation:
Ibn Abi Hatim said: Yunus ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us by reading, Ibn Wahb informed us, 'Abdullah ibn Lahi'ah informed me, from Abu al-Aswad, who said: Two men disputed before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he judged between them. The one against whom the judgment was given said: "Send us back to 'Umar ibn al-Khattab." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Go to him." When they came to him, the man said: "O son of al-Khattab, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ judged for me against this man," and he said: "Send us back to 'Umar." So they returned to you. He said: "Is that so?" He said: "Yes." 'Umar said: "Stay where you are until I come out to you and judge between you." He came out to them with his sword unsheathed and struck the one who had said "Send us back to 'Umar," killing him. The other turned away fleeing to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "O Messenger of Allah, 'Umar has killed my companion, and by Allah, had I not overpowered him, he would have killed me." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I did not think that 'Umar would dare to kill a believer." Then Allah revealed: ﴿But no, by your Lord, they will not believe until they make you judge⦆ [the verse], so the blood of that man was nullified and 'Umar was cleared of killing him. Allah disliked that this should become a precedent thereafter, so He said: ﴿And if We had ordained for them, "Kill yourselves or leave your homes," they would not have done it, except a few of them. But if they had done what they were advised, it would have been better for them and stronger in firmness.⦆ [An-Nisa: 66].

Ibn Mardawayh also narrated it through the route of Ibn Lahi'ah, from Abu al-Aswad, with the same wording.

This is a strange report (athar), it is mursal, and Ibn Lahi'ah is weak. [Mentioned by al-Suyuti in al-Durr (2/585).] And Allah knows best.

Another route: Al-Hafiz Abu Ishaq Ibrahim ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ibrahim ibn Duhaym said in his Tafsir: Shu'ayb ibn Shu'ayb narrated to us, Abu al-Mughirah narrated to us, 'Utbah ibn Damrah narrated to us, my father narrated to me: that two men disputed before the Prophet ﷺ, and he judged in favour of the one who was in the right over the one in the wrong. The one against whom the judgment was given said: "I am not satisfied." His companion said: "What do you want then?" He said: "That we go to Abu Bakr al-Siddiq." So they both went to him, and the one in whose favour the judgment had been given said: "We disputed before the Prophet ﷺ and he judged in my favour against him," and Abu Bakr said: "You are both bound by what the Prophet ﷺ judged." But his companion refused to be satisfied. He said: "Let us go to 'Umar ibn al-Khattab." So they came to him, and the one in whose favour the judgment had been given said: "We disputed before the Prophet ﷺ, and he judged in my favour against him, and he refused to be satisfied. Then we came to Abu Bakr, and he said: 'You are both bound by what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ judged, and he refused to be satisfied.'" 'Umar asked him, and he said: "That is so." 'Umar entered his house and came out with his sword drawn, and struck the head of the one who refused to be satisfied, killing him. So Allah revealed: ﴿But no, by your Lord, they will not believe until they make you judge concerning that over which they dispute among themselves⦆ [to the end of] the verse. [Ibn Kathir, the author, also mentioned it under the Musnad of 'Umar ibn al-Khattab.]

The Most High says: ﴿And We did not send any messenger except to be obeyed, by Allah's leave﴾. That is, obedience to him is obligatory upon those to whom he was sent. As for His words ﴿by Allah's leave﴾, Mujahid said: that is, no one obeys except by My permission. Meaning, none obeys them except those whom I have granted success to do so, as in His words: ﴿And Allah had certainly fulfilled His promise to you when you were killing them by His permission﴾ [Al 'Imran: 52], that is, by His command, decree, will, and His giving you power over them.

And His words: ﴿And if they, when they had wronged themselves, had come to you and asked forgiveness of Allah and the Messenger had asked forgiveness for them, they would have found Allah Accepting of repentance and Merciful﴾. The Most High guides the disobedient and the sinners: when error and disobedience befall them, they should come to the Messenger (ﷺ), ask Allah's forgiveness in his presence, and ask him to seek forgiveness for them. If they do that, Allah will turn to them in repentance, show them mercy, and forgive them. For this reason He said: ﴿they would have found Allah Accepting of repentance and Merciful﴾.

A group of scholars, among them Shaykh Abu Nasr ibn al-Sabbagh in his book "al-Shamil", mentioned the well-known account related from al-'Utbi, who said: I was sitting by the grave of the Prophet (ﷺ) when a Bedouin came and said: "Peace be upon you, O Messenger of Allah. I heard Allah say: ﴿And if they, when they had wronged themselves, had come to you and asked forgiveness of Allah and the Messenger had asked forgiveness for them, they would have found Allah Accepting of repentance and Merciful﴾. I have come to you seeking forgiveness for my sin, seeking your intercession with my Lord." Then he recited:

"O best of those whose bones are buried in the valley,
whose fragrance has made the valley and the hills fragrant.
My soul is the ransom for a grave in which you dwell,
in which are chastity, generosity and nobility."

Then the Bedouin departed, and I was overcome by sleep, and I saw the Prophet (ﷺ) in a dream. He said: "O 'Utbi, go to the Bedouin and give him the good news that Allah has forgiven him."

[Editor's note: This account was mentioned by al-Nawawi in al-Majmu' (8/217) and in al-Idah (p. 498), and he added the following two verses: "You are the intercessor whose intercession is hoped for, over the Sirat when feet slip. And your two companions, I shall never forget them, may peace from me be upon you as long as the pen writes." He introduced it with the words: "Among the finest things said is what our companions related from al-'Utbi, praising it," and then mentioned it in full. Ibn Kathir here did not transmit it as an authority nor endorse it; rather he quoted it as he quoted some Isra'iliyyat (Israelite narratives) in his tafsir. It is a false account and a weak story, and some people use it to argue for the permissibility of seeking tawassul (intercession/means) through the Messenger (ﷺ) after his death. The reply to it is given in four points, mentioned by the honourable Shaykh Salih Al al-Shaykh in his book "Hadhihi Mafahimuna" (p. 76):

First: Since it is not from the Sunnah of the Messenger (ﷺ), nor the practice of his rightly-guided caliphs, nor his noble companions, nor the Followers and the praiseworthy generations, but is merely a report about an unknown person transmitted through a weak chain, how can it be relied upon in the doctrine of tawhid, which is the foundation of foundations? And how can it be relied upon when it contradicts the authentic hadiths that forbid exaggeration at graves, exaggeration regarding the righteous in general, and exaggeration regarding his grave and about him (ﷺ) in particular? As for those scholars who transmitted it or praised it, that is not a proof with which authentic texts may be opposed and the creed of the Salaf contradicted. Matters may be hidden from some scholars that are clear to others, and they may err in their transmission and opinion, and the proof lies with whoever opposes them.

Since we know the path of right guidance, we have no concern with what so-and-so said or what so-and-so related. Our religion is not built upon narratives and dreams, but upon sound proofs.

Second: Some matters and meanings may be hidden even from those who have cast off rivals (andad) and disavowed shirk and its people, as when some of the Companions said: "Make for us a dhat anwat (tree of hanging) just as they have a dhat anwat," and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allahu akbar! It is the ways of the past nations! You have said, by Him in whose hand is my soul, what the people of Moses said: 'Make for us a god just as they have gods.'" (Authentic hadith.)

The argument in this is that those Companions, though they were recent in their conversion from disbelief, had entered the religion by "There is no god but Allah," which casts off rivals and all kinds of shirk and affirms the One worshipped. Yet despite that, and despite the true knowledge of its meaning held by those who said it, some matters of its details were hidden from them. The point is that when the evidence is clear and the proof is made manifest, one must return to it and adhere to it. The ignorant may be excused, as those Companions were excused in their saying: "Make for us a dhat anwat." Other scholars are even more deserving of the possibility that some matters, even in tawhid and shirk, may be hidden from them.

Third: How dares anyone oppose the texts of the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Messenger (ﷺ) with the saying of someone who related it approvingly? Allah, glorified is He, says: ﴿Let those who oppose his command beware lest a trial afflict them or a painful punishment strike them﴾ [An-Nur: 63].

Imam Ahmad said: "I am amazed at people who know the chain of transmission and its authenticity, yet go to the opinion of Sufyan, while Allah the Most High says: ﴿Let those who oppose his command beware lest a trial afflict them.﴾ Do you know what the trial is? The trial is shirk. Perhaps if some of his words are rejected, something of deviation will enter his heart and he will perish." This was related from Ahmad by al-Fadl ibn Ziyad and Abu Talib, and perhaps it is in Ahmad's book "Ta'at al-Rasul (ﷺ)" (Obedience to the Messenger), may Allah have mercy on him.

So obedience to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) takes precedence over the obedience of anyone, even if the best of this Ummah are Abu Bakr and 'Umar. As Ibn 'Abbas said: "It is about to happen that stones will fall upon you from the sky. I say: the Messenger of Allah said, and you say: Abu Bakr and 'Umar said."

How then would Ibn 'Abbas view those people who oppose the established Sunnah and the clear proof with the saying of a Bedouin in the account of al-'Utbi, which is weak and rejected?

The Sunnah in the hearts of those who love it is greater and more precious than those flimsy arguments put forward by the owner of innovated notions, notions built upon dreams and abominations. So marvel at this, and devote yourself to following the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Beware, then beware, lest you reject the authentic hadiths and believe in false and weak reports, for whoever does so is about to have a trial enter his heart and perish.

Fourth: Every scholar is contradicted in matters he has chosen, either due to opinion or the weakness of his evidence, and they are excused before the path has been made clear by its proofs. If people pursued the anomalies and dispensations of the mujtahids, they would leave the religion of Islam for another religion, as it is said: "Whoever pursues dispensations becomes a heretic." If someone seeking corruption and deviation from the path were to take their dispensations as a ladder to climb toward his desires, it would be obligatory for the ruler to suppress him, prevent him, and discipline him, as is well known in the jurisprudence of the four Imams and others.

What has been mentioned indicates that whoever uses a scholar's opinion, known to be in error, to justify his offence, it is accepted from him and he is not blamed.

O Allah, preserve for us our religion and our tawhid.]

* *

And His words: ﴿But no, by your Lord, they will not [truly] believe until they make you judge concerning that over which they dispute among themselves, and then they find within themselves no discomfort from what you have decided and submit completely﴾. The Most High swears by His noble and sacred Self that no one truly believes until they make the Messenger (ﷺ) judge in all matters. Whatever he judges is the truth to which submission is obligatory, inwardly and outwardly. For this reason He said: ﴿then they find within themselves no discomfort from what you have decided and submit completely﴾, that is: when they make you judge, they obey you inwardly, so they find in themselves no discomfort at what you have judged, and they submit to it outwardly and inwardly, submitting entirely, without resistance, opposition, or dispute, as occurs in the hadith: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, none of you believes until his desire follows what I have brought."

Al-Bukhari said: Ali ibn 'Abd Allah narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from 'Urwa, who said: al-Zubayr disputed with a man [from the Ansar] concerning a watercourse of al-Harra, and the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Irrigate, O Zubayr, then release the water to your neighbour." The Ansari said: "O Messenger of Allah, was he the son of your paternal aunt [or: your uncle]?" Then the face of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) changed colour, and he said: "Irrigate, O Zubayr, then hold the water until it reaches the wall, then release the water to your neighbour." The Prophet (ﷺ) had given al-Zubayr his full right in the explicit judgment, after the Ansari had provoked him, although he had previously given them both advice that offered latitude. Al-Zubayr said: "I do not think this verse was revealed except concerning that: ﴿But no, by your Lord, they will not [truly] believe until they make you judge concerning that over which they dispute among themselves...﴾" to the end of the verse.

Thus al-Bukhari related it here, meaning in the Book of Tafsir of his Sahih, through the hadith of Ma'mar; and in the Book of Drinking (Shurb) through the hadith of Ibn Jurayj and Ma'mar also; and in the Book of Reconciliation (Sulh) through the hadith of Shu'ayb ibn Abi Hamza. All three transmitted from al-Zuhri, from 'Urwa, and he mentioned it. [Sahih al-Bukhari, nos. (4585), (2361), (2362), (2708).] Its form is that of a mursal report (one where the Successor omits the Companion), though it is connected in meaning.

Imam Ahmad also related it through this route and explicitly stated the omission: He said: Abu al-Yaman narrated to us, Shu'ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri: 'Urwa ibn al-Zubayr informed me that al-Zubayr used to narrate that he disputed with a man from the Ansar who had witnessed Badr, before the Prophet (ﷺ), concerning the watercourses of al-Harra, with which both of them used to irrigate. The Prophet (ﷺ) said to al-Zubayr: "Irrigate, then release [the water] to your neighbour." The Ansari became angry and said: "O Messenger of Allah, was he the son of your paternal aunt?" Then the face of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) changed colour, and he said: "Irrigate, O Zubayr, then hold the water until it reaches the wall." So the Prophet (ﷺ) gave al-Zubayr his right. The Prophet (ﷺ) had previously given al-Zubayr an opinion by which he intended latitude for him and for the Ansari. When the Ansari provoked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), the Prophet (ﷺ) gave al-Zubayr his full right in the explicit judgment. 'Urwa said: Al-Zubayr said: "By Allah, I do not think this verse was revealed except concerning that: ﴿But no, by your Lord, they will not [truly] believe until they make you judge concerning that over which they dispute among themselves, then they find within themselves no discomfort from what you have decided and submit completely﴾."

This is how Imam Ahmad related it [al-Musnad (1/165)]. It is interrupted (munqati') between 'Urwa and his father al-Zubayr, for he did not hear it from him. What is certain is that he heard it from his brother 'Abd Allah. Abu Muhammad 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hatim related it in this way in his tafsir, saying:

Yunus ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, Ibn Wahb informed us, al-Layth and Yunus narrated to us, from Ibn Shihab, that 'Urwa ibn al-Zubayr told him that 'Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr told him, from al-Zubayr ibn al-'Awwam: that he disputed with a man from the Ansar who had witnessed Badr with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), before the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), concerning watercourses in al-Harra, with which both of them irrigated the palm trees. The Ansari said: "Let the water flow." Al-Zubayr refused him. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Irrigate, O Zubayr, then release [the water] to your neighbour." The Ansari became angry and said: "O Messenger of Allah, was he the son of your paternal aunt?" The face of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) changed colour, and he said: "Irrigate, O Zubayr, then hold the water until it reaches the wall." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gave al-Zubayr his right. Before that, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had given al-Zubayr an opinion by which he intended latitude for him and for the Ansari. When the Ansari provoked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), he gave al-Zubayr his full right in the explicit judgment. Al-Zubayr said: "I do not think this verse was revealed except concerning that: ﴿But no, by your Lord, they will not [truly] believe until they make you judge concerning that over which they dispute among themselves, then they find within themselves no discomfort from what you have decided and submit completely﴾."

Thus al-Nasa'i related it through the hadith of Ibn Wahb, with the same chain. Ahmad and the whole group related it through the hadith of al-Layth, with the same chain. [al-Musnad (4/4); Sahih al-Bukhari (2359); Sahih Muslim (2357); Sunan Abi Dawud (3637); Sunan al-Tirmidhi (1363); Sunan al-Nasa'i (8/245); Sunan Ibn Majah (15).] The compilers of the Atraf (indexes of hadith by their opening portions) placed it in the Musnad of 'Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr, and Ahmad likewise included it in the Musnad of 'Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr. And Allah knows best.

What is most astonishing is al-Hakim Abu 'Abd Allah al-Nisaburi, for he related this hadith through the route of the nephew of Ibn Shihab, from his paternal uncle, from 'Urwa, from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr, from al-Zubayr, and mentioned it, then said: "Its chain is sound, but they (al-Bukhari and Muslim) did not record it." I know of no one who transmitted this chain from al-Zuhri naming 'Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr except his nephew, and he is weak in that narration. [al-Mustadrak (3/364).]

Ibn Kathir, the commentary on Surah an-Nisa' (4), verses 66–70 (part 1 of 2):

Allah, the Exalted, informs us about most people that if they were commanded to do the prohibited acts they commit, they would not do them. This is because their base natures are inclined to oppose the command. This is part of His knowledge, blessed and exalted is He, of what has not happened and what would have happened, and how it would have been. For this reason, He said, ﴿And if We had decreed for them, "Kill yourselves or leave your homes," they would not have done it, except a few of them.﴾

Ibn Jarir said: Al-Muthanna narrated to me, Ishaq narrated to me, Abu Zuhayr narrated to us [in one manuscript: "Abu al-Azhar"], from Isma'il, from Abu Ishaq as-Sabi'i, who said: When the verse ﴿And if We had decreed for them, "Kill yourselves or leave your homes," they would not have done it, except a few of them﴾ was revealed, a man said: "If we were commanded, we would have done it, and praise be to Allah who has spared us." This reached the Prophet (ﷺ), and he said: "Indeed, among my ummah are men whose faith is firmer in their hearts than the lofty mountains."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ja'far ibn Munir narrated to us, Rawh narrated to us, Hisham narrated to us, from al-Hasan, who said: When this verse was revealed, ﴿And if We had decreed for them, "Kill yourselves"...﴾, some people among the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "If our Lord had commanded it, we would have done it." This reached the Prophet (ﷺ), and he said: "Faith is firmer in the hearts of its people than the lofty mountains."

As-Suddi said: Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shammas and a Jewish man boasted. The Jew said: "By Allah, Allah had decreed killing for us, so we killed ourselves." Thabit said: "By Allah, if He had decreed for us, ﴿'Kill yourselves,'﴾ we would have killed ourselves." So Allah revealed this verse. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Mahmud ibn Ghaylan narrated to us, Bishr ibn as-Sari narrated to us, Mus'ab ibn Thabit narrated to us, from his paternal uncle 'Amir ibn 'Abd Allah ibn az-Zubayr, who said: When [the verse] ﴿And if We had decreed for them, "Kill yourselves"﴾ was revealed, Abu Bakr said: "O Messenger of Allah, by Allah, if you commanded me to kill myself, I would do it." He said: "You have spoken the truth, O Abu Bakr."

My father narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umar al-'Adani narrated to us, who said: Sufyan was asked about His saying ﴿And if We had decreed for them, "Kill yourselves or leave your homes," they would not have done it, except a few of them﴾. He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Had it been revealed, Ibn Umm 'Abd would have been among them."

My father narrated to us, Abu al-Yaman narrated to us, Isma'il ibn 'Ayyash narrated to us, from Safwan ibn 'Amr, from Shurayh ibn 'Ubayd, who said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited this verse, ﴿And if We had decreed for them, "Kill yourselves or leave your homes," they would not have done it, except a few of them﴾, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) pointed with his hand to 'Abd Allah ibn Rawahah and said: "If Allah had decreed that, this man would be among those few." He meant Ibn Rawahah.

For this reason, He said, ﴿And if they had done what they are admonished to do﴾, meaning: if they had done what they were commanded and abandoned what they were forbidden, ﴿it would have been better for them﴾, meaning: than opposing the command and committing the prohibition, ﴿and firmer in steadfastness﴾. As-Suddi said: meaning, "and firmer in affirmation (of the truth)."

﴿And then We would have given them from Us a great reward﴾, meaning: from Our presence, ﴿a great reward﴾, meaning Paradise. ﴿And We would have guided them to a straight path﴾, meaning in this world and the Hereafter.

Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And whoever obeys Allah and the Messenger – those will be with the ones upon whom Allah has bestowed favour: the prophets, the steadfast in truth (ṣiddīqūn), the martyrs, and the righteous. And excellent are those as companions.﴾ Meaning: whoever acts upon what Allah and His Messenger have commanded, and abandons what Allah and His Messenger have forbidden, then Allah, mighty and majestic, will settle him in the abode of His honour and make him a companion of the prophets, then of those after them in rank, namely the ṣiddīqūn (those steadfast in truth), then the martyrs, then the general body of believers, who are the righteous, whose inner and outer states are sound.

Then Allah praised them, saying: ﴿And excellent are those as companions.﴾

Al-Bukhari said: Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Hawshab narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn Sa'd narrated to us, from his father, from 'Urwah, from 'A'ishah, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "No prophet falls ill except that he is given the choice between this world and the Hereafter." During his final illness, in which he died, he was overcome by a severe hoarseness, and I heard him say: ﴿with those upon whom Allah has bestowed favour, of the prophets, the ṣiddīqūn, the martyrs, and the righteous.﴾ So I knew that he had been given the choice.

Muslim also narrated it similarly, from the hadith of Shu'bah, from Sa'd ibn Ibrahim, with the same chain.

This is the meaning of his (ﷺ) saying in another hadith: "O Allah, [grant me companionship] with the Highest Companion," three times, and then he died, may the best of prayers and peace be upon him.

Mention of the occasion of revelation of this noble verse:

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, Ya'qub al-Qummi narrated to us, from Ja'far ibn Abi al-Mughirah, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: A man from the Ansar came to the Prophet (ﷺ) while he was grieved. The Prophet (ﷺ) said to him: "O so-and-so, why do I see you grieved?" He said: "O Prophet of Allah, a matter I have been thinking about." He said: "What is it?" He said: "We visit you in the morning and evening, we look at your face and sit with you, but tomorrow you will be raised among the prophets, and we will not reach you." The Prophet (ﷺ) did not answer him at all, and then Jibril brought him this verse: ﴿And whoever obeys Allah and the Messenger – those will be with the ones upon whom Allah has bestowed favour, of the prophets, [the ṣiddīqūn, the martyrs, and the righteous, and excellent are those as companions].﴾ Then the Prophet (ﷺ) sent for him and gave him good news.

This report has been narrated as a mursal (a report in which the Companion is omitted from the chain) from Masruq, 'Ikrimah, 'Amir ash-Sha'bi, Qatadah, and from ar-Rabi' ibn Anas, and it is among the best of its chains.

Ibn Jarir said: Al-Muthanna narrated to us, Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from ar-Rabi', regarding His saying ﴿And whoever obeys Allah and the Messenger [will be with those upon whom Allah has bestowed favour from]﴾: The Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "We know that the Prophet (ﷺ) has a superiority over those who believed in him in the ranks of Paradise, among those who followed him and affirmed him. But how will they be when they gather in Paradise, that some of them may see others?" So Allah revealed concerning that—meaning this verse—and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Those on high descend to those below them, and they gather in its gardens, remember what Allah has bestowed upon them, and praise Him. The people of the higher ranks descend to them, and they strive to bring them whatever they desire and whatever they ask for. They are in a garden, rejoicing and enjoying themselves in it."

Ibn Jarir (8/535) narrated this as a mursal report; see the introduction in the exegetical manuscripts, where there is discussion of the copy of Abu Ja'far ar-Razi.

It has also been narrated as marfu' (traced to the Prophet (ﷺ)) by another route. Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh said: 'Abd ar-Rahim ibn Muhammad ibn Muslim narrated to us, Isma'il ibn Ahmad ibn Usayd narrated to us, 'Abd Allah ibn 'Imran narrated to us, Fudayl ibn 'Iyad narrated to us, from Mansur, from Ibrahim, from al-Aswad, from 'A'ishah, who said: A man came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, you are dearer to me than myself, dearer to me than my family, and dearer to me than my children. When I am in the house I remember you, and I cannot bear it until I come to you and look at you. When I remember my death and your death, I know that when you enter Paradise you will be raised with the prophets, and if I enter Paradise, I fear I will not see you." The Prophet (ﷺ) did not answer him until this was revealed to him: ﴿And whoever obeys Allah and the Messenger – those will be with the ones upon whom Allah has bestowed favour, of the prophets, the ṣiddīqūn, the martyrs, and the righteous, and excellent are those as companions.﴾

Al-Hafiz Abu 'Abd Allah al-Maqdisi likewise narrated it in his book Sifat al-Jannah (The Description of Paradise), by way of at-Tabarani, from Ahmad ibn 'Amr ibn Muslim al-Khallal, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Imran al-'Abidi, with the same chain. He then said: "I see no harm in its chain." And Allah knows best.

Ibn Mardawayh also said: Sulayman ibn Ahmad narrated to us, al-'Abbas ibn al-Fadl al-Asfati narrated to us, Abu Bakr ibn Thabit ibn 'Abbas al-Misri [in other manuscripts: "Ibn 'Ayyash al-Basri"] narrated to us, Khalid ibn 'Abd Allah narrated to us, from 'Ata' ibn as-Sa'ib, from 'Amir ash-Sha'bi, from Ibn 'Abbas, that a man came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I love you so much that I remember you in my dwelling, and it troubles me, and I wish to be with you in the same rank." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not answer him at all, and then Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed: ﴿And whoever obeys Allah and the Messenger – those will be with the ones upon whom Allah has bestowed favour, of the prophets, the ṣiddīqūn, the martyrs, and the righteous, and excellent are those as companions.﴾

Sulayman ibn Ahmad is at-Tabarani, and he narrated it in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (12/86). Al-Haythami said in Majma' al-Zawa'id (7/7): "It contains 'Ata' ibn as-Sa'ib, who became confused (in his memory)."

Ibn Jarir narrated it mursal from Ibn Humayd, from Jarir, from 'Ata', from ash-Sha'bi. And it is established in Sahih Muslim, through the hadith of Hilal ibn Ziyad, from al-Awza'i, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from Abu Salamah ibn 'Abd ar-Rahman, from Rabi'ah ibn Ka'b al-Aslami, that he said: "I used to spend the night with the Prophet (ﷺ), and I would bring him his water for ablution and his needs. He said to me: 'Ask.' I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, I ask you for your companionship in Paradise.' He said: 'Or is there anything else?' I said: 'That is it.' He said: 'Then help me against yourself by frequent prostration.'"

Ahmad said: Yahya ibn Ishaq narrated to us, Ibn Lahi'ah informed us, from 'Ubayd Allah ibn Abi Ja'far, from 'Isa ibn Talhah, from 'Amr ibn Murrah al-Juhani, who said: A man came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I bear witness that there is no god but Allah and that you are the Messenger of Allah, I have prayed the five (prayers), paid the zakat of my wealth, and fasted Ramadan." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever dies upon this will be with the prophets, the ṣiddīqūn, and the martyrs on the Day of Resurrection, like this"—and he raised his two fingers—"so long as he has not disobeyed his parents." Ahmad alone narrated it. [Note: it is not in the Musnad.]

Ahmad also said: Abu Sa'id, the client of Abu Hashim, narrated to us, Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to us, from Zabban [in another manuscript: "Ziyad"] ibn Fa'id, from Sahl ibn Mu'adh ibn Anas, from his father, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites a thousand verses in the cause of Allah will be recorded on the Day of Resurrection with the prophets, the ṣiddīqūn, the martyrs, and the righteous, and excellent are those as companions, if Allah wills." [Note: Al-Musnad (4/437) contains: "Hasan narrated to us, Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to us," and then the report. Al-Haythami (2/269) said: "It contains Ibn Lahi'ah from Zabban, and there is some discussion about it."]

The Prophet ﷺ said: "The truthful, trustworthy merchant is with the Prophets, the truthful ones (al-siddiqin) and the martyrs."

Al-Tirmidhi also narrated it through Sufyan al-Thawri, from Abu Hamza, from al-Hasan al-Basri, from Abu Sa'id, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The truthful, trustworthy merchant is with the Prophets and the truthful ones and the martyrs."

Then he said: "This is a hasan hadith. We do not know it except through this route. Abu Hamza's name is Abdullah ibn Jabir, a shaykh from Basra" [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (1209).]].

Greater than all of this is the glad tidings found in the Sahihs, the Masanid and others, through mutawatir chains from a group of the Companions: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asked about a man who loves a people but has not yet joined them. He said: "A person is with whom he loves." Anas said: "The Muslims never rejoiced more than they rejoiced at this hadith" [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. (6167), and by Muslim in his Sahih, no. (2639).]].

In another narration from Anas, he said: "Indeed, I love the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and I love Abu Bakr and Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, and I hope that Allah will resurrect me with them, even if I do not act as they acted" [[Sahih Muslim, no. (2639).]].

Imam Malik ibn Anas said, from Safwan ibn Sulaym, from Ata' ibn Yasar, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The people of Paradise will look up at the people of the upper chambers (al-ghuraf) above them, just as you look at the bright, distant star on the horizon, in the east or the west, because of the difference in their ranks." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, those are the abodes of the Prophets, which no one else can reach?" He said: "Yes, by Him in whose hand is my soul, [they are for] men who believed in Allah and affirmed the Messengers."

Al-Bukhari and Muslim both narrated it in their Sahihs from the hadith of Malik, and the wording is Muslim's.

Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal said: Fazara narrated to us, Fulayh informed me, from Hilal (i.e., Ibn Ali), from Ata', from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The people of Paradise will look at one another in Paradise as you look at the bright star that sets on the horizon or rises, because of the difference in ranks." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, are those the Prophets?" He said: "Yes, by Him in whose hand is my soul, and [also] people who believed in Allah and affirmed the Messengers."

The Hafiz Diya' al-Maqdisi said: "This hadith meets the conditions of al-Bukhari" [[al-Musnad (2/339).]]. And Allah knows best.

The Hafiz Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said in his al-Mu'jam al-Kabir: Ali ibn Abd al-Aziz narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ammar al-Mawsili narrated to us, Ufayf ibn Salim narrated to us, from Ayyub ibn Utba [[In the manuscripts: "Ayyub from Utba," which is a distortion.]], from Ata', from Ibn Umar, who said: A man from Abyssinia came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ asking him, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: "Ask and inquire." He said: "O Messenger of Allah, you have been given preference over us in form, colour and prophethood. Tell me: if I believe in what you believe in, and do what you do, will I be with you in Paradise?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Yes, by Him in whose hand is my soul, the whiteness of the black man will shine in Paradise from a distance of a thousand years." Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever says: 'There is no god but Allah,' he will have a covenant with Allah by it, and whoever says: 'Glory be to Allah and praise be to Him,' there will be written for him by it one hundred thousand and twenty-four thousand good deeds." A man said: "How then could we be destroyed after that, O Messenger of Allah?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "A man will come on the Day of Resurrection with a deed that, if placed upon a mountain, would weigh it down. Then a blessing from the blessings of Allah will stand up and nearly exhaust all of that, unless Allah extends His mercy to him."

And these verses were revealed: ﴿Has there come upon man a period of time when he was not a thing [even] worthy of mention?﴾ up to His saying: ﴿a delight and a great dominion﴾ [Al-Insan: 1-20]. The Abyssinian said: "Do my eyes see what your eyes see in Paradise?" The Prophet ﷺ said: "Yes." So he wept until his soul departed. Ibn Umar said: "I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ lowering him into his grave with his own hands."

In it there is strangeness and unfamiliarity, and its chain is weak [[al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (12/436). Its weakness is that it contains Ayyub ibn Utba, who is weak.]].

Therefore Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿That is the bounty from Allah﴾, meaning: from Allah's presence, by His mercy. It is He who qualified them for this, not by their deeds. ﴿And sufficient is Allah as Knower﴾, meaning: He knows who deserves guidance and success.

Ibn Kathir, the commentary on Surah an-Nisa' (4), verses 66–70 (part 1 of 2):

Allah, the Exalted, informs us about most people that if they were commanded to do the prohibited acts they commit, they would not do them. This is because their base natures are inclined to oppose the command. This is part of His knowledge, blessed and exalted is He, of what has not happened and what would have happened, and how it would have been. For this reason, He said, ﴿And if We had decreed for them, "Kill yourselves or leave your homes," they would not have done it, except a few of them.﴾

Ibn Jarir said: Al-Muthanna narrated to me, Ishaq narrated to me, Abu Zuhayr narrated to us [in one manuscript: "Abu al-Azhar"], from Isma'il, from Abu Ishaq as-Sabi'i, who said: When the verse ﴿And if We had decreed for them, "Kill yourselves or leave your homes," they would not have done it, except a few of them﴾ was revealed, a man said: "If we were commanded, we would have done it, and praise be to Allah who has spared us." This reached the Prophet (ﷺ), and he said: "Indeed, among my ummah are men whose faith is firmer in their hearts than the lofty mountains."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ja'far ibn Munir narrated to us, Rawh narrated to us, Hisham narrated to us, from al-Hasan, who said: When this verse was revealed, ﴿And if We had decreed for them, "Kill yourselves"...﴾, some people among the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "If our Lord had commanded it, we would have done it." This reached the Prophet (ﷺ), and he said: "Faith is firmer in the hearts of its people than the lofty mountains."

As-Suddi said: Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shammas and a Jewish man boasted. The Jew said: "By Allah, Allah had decreed killing for us, so we killed ourselves." Thabit said: "By Allah, if He had decreed for us, ﴿'Kill yourselves,'﴾ we would have killed ourselves." So Allah revealed this verse. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Mahmud ibn Ghaylan narrated to us, Bishr ibn as-Sari narrated to us, Mus'ab ibn Thabit narrated to us, from his paternal uncle 'Amir ibn 'Abd Allah ibn az-Zubayr, who said: When [the verse] ﴿And if We had decreed for them, "Kill yourselves"﴾ was revealed, Abu Bakr said: "O Messenger of Allah, by Allah, if you commanded me to kill myself, I would do it." He said: "You have spoken the truth, O Abu Bakr."

My father narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umar al-'Adani narrated to us, who said: Sufyan was asked about His saying ﴿And if We had decreed for them, "Kill yourselves or leave your homes," they would not have done it, except a few of them﴾. He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Had it been revealed, Ibn Umm 'Abd would have been among them."

My father narrated to us, Abu al-Yaman narrated to us, Isma'il ibn 'Ayyash narrated to us, from Safwan ibn 'Amr, from Shurayh ibn 'Ubayd, who said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited this verse, ﴿And if We had decreed for them, "Kill yourselves or leave your homes," they would not have done it, except a few of them﴾, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) pointed with his hand to 'Abd Allah ibn Rawahah and said: "If Allah had decreed that, this man would be among those few." He meant Ibn Rawahah.

For this reason, He said, ﴿And if they had done what they are admonished to do﴾, meaning: if they had done what they were commanded and abandoned what they were forbidden, ﴿it would have been better for them﴾, meaning: than opposing the command and committing the prohibition, ﴿and firmer in steadfastness﴾. As-Suddi said: meaning, "and firmer in affirmation (of the truth)."

﴿And then We would have given them from Us a great reward﴾, meaning: from Our presence, ﴿a great reward﴾, meaning Paradise. ﴿And We would have guided them to a straight path﴾, meaning in this world and the Hereafter.

Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And whoever obeys Allah and the Messenger – those will be with the ones upon whom Allah has bestowed favour: the prophets, the steadfast in truth (ṣiddīqūn), the martyrs, and the righteous. And excellent are those as companions.﴾ Meaning: whoever acts upon what Allah and His Messenger have commanded, and abandons what Allah and His Messenger have forbidden, then Allah, mighty and majestic, will settle him in the abode of His honour and make him a companion of the prophets, then of those after them in rank, namely the ṣiddīqūn (those steadfast in truth), then the martyrs, then the general body of believers, who are the righteous, whose inner and outer states are sound.

Then Allah praised them, saying: ﴿And excellent are those as companions.﴾

Al-Bukhari said: Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Hawshab narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn Sa'd narrated to us, from his father, from 'Urwah, from 'A'ishah, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "No prophet falls ill except that he is given the choice between this world and the Hereafter." During his final illness, in which he died, he was overcome by a severe hoarseness, and I heard him say: ﴿with those upon whom Allah has bestowed favour, of the prophets, the ṣiddīqūn, the martyrs, and the righteous.﴾ So I knew that he had been given the choice.

Muslim also narrated it similarly, from the hadith of Shu'bah, from Sa'd ibn Ibrahim, with the same chain.

This is the meaning of his (ﷺ) saying in another hadith: "O Allah, [grant me companionship] with the Highest Companion," three times, and then he died, may the best of prayers and peace be upon him.

Greater than all of this is the glad tidings found in the Sahihs, the Masanid and others, through mutawatir chains from a group of the Companions: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asked about a man who loves a people but has not yet joined them. He said: "A person is with whom he loves." Anas said: "The Muslims never rejoiced more than they rejoiced at this hadith" [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. (6167), and by Muslim in his Sahih, no. (2639).]].

In another narration from Anas, he said: "Indeed, I love the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and I love Abu Bakr and Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, and I hope that Allah will resurrect me with them, even if I do not act as they acted" [[Sahih Muslim, no. (2639).]].

Imam Malik ibn Anas said, from Safwan ibn Sulaym, from Ata' ibn Yasar, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The people of Paradise will look up at the people of the upper chambers (al-ghuraf) above them, just as you look at the bright, distant star on the horizon, in the east or the west, because of the difference in their ranks." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, those are the abodes of the Prophets, which no one else can reach?" He said: "Yes, by Him in whose hand is my soul, [they are for] men who believed in Allah and affirmed the Messengers."

Al-Bukhari and Muslim both narrated it in their Sahihs from the hadith of Malik, and the wording is Muslim's.

Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal said: Fazara narrated to us, Fulayh informed me, from Hilal (i.e., Ibn Ali), from Ata', from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The people of Paradise will look at one another in Paradise as you look at the bright star that sets on the horizon or rises, because of the difference in ranks." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, are those the Prophets?" He said: "Yes, by Him in whose hand is my soul, and [also] people who believed in Allah and affirmed the Messengers."

The Hafiz Diya' al-Maqdisi said: "This hadith meets the conditions of al-Bukhari" [[al-Musnad (2/339).]]. And Allah knows best.

The Hafiz Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said in his al-Mu'jam al-Kabir: Ali ibn Abd al-Aziz narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ammar al-Mawsili narrated to us, Ufayf ibn Salim narrated to us, from Ayyub ibn Utba [[In the manuscripts: "Ayyub from Utba," which is a distortion.]], from Ata', from Ibn Umar, who said: A man from Abyssinia came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ asking him, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: "Ask and inquire." He said: "O Messenger of Allah, you have been given preference over us in form, colour and prophethood. Tell me: if I believe in what you believe in, and do what you do, will I be with you in Paradise?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Yes, by Him in whose hand is my soul, the whiteness of the black man will shine in Paradise from a distance of a thousand years." Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever says: 'There is no god but Allah,' he will have a covenant with Allah by it, and whoever says: 'Glory be to Allah and praise be to Him,' there will be written for him by it one hundred thousand and twenty-four thousand good deeds." A man said: "How then could we be destroyed after that, O Messenger of Allah?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "A man will come on the Day of Resurrection with a deed that, if placed upon a mountain, would weigh it down. Then a blessing from the blessings of Allah will stand up and nearly exhaust all of that, unless Allah extends His mercy to him."

And these verses were revealed: ﴿Has there come upon man a period of time when he was not a thing [even] worthy of mention?﴾ up to His saying: ﴿a delight and a great dominion﴾ [Al-Insan: 1-20]. The Abyssinian said: "Do my eyes see what your eyes see in Paradise?" The Prophet ﷺ said: "Yes." So he wept until his soul departed. Ibn Umar said: "I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ lowering him into his grave with his own hands."

In it there is strangeness and unfamiliarity, and its chain is weak [[al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (12/436). Its weakness is that it contains Ayyub ibn Utba, who is weak.]].

Therefore Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿That is the bounty from Allah﴾, meaning: from Allah's presence, by His mercy. It is He who qualified them for this, not by their deeds. ﴿And sufficient is Allah as Knower﴾, meaning: He knows who deserves guidance and success.

Ibn Kathir, the commentary on Surah an-Nisa' (4), verses 66–70 (part 1 of 2):

Allah, the Exalted, informs us about most people that if they were commanded to do the prohibited acts they commit, they would not do them. This is because their base natures are inclined to oppose the command. This is part of His knowledge, blessed and exalted is He, of what has not happened and what would have happened, and how it would have been. For this reason, He said, ﴿And if We had decreed for them, "Kill yourselves or leave your homes," they would not have done it, except a few of them.﴾

Ibn Jarir said: Al-Muthanna narrated to me, Ishaq narrated to me, Abu Zuhayr narrated to us [in one manuscript: "Abu al-Azhar"], from Isma'il, from Abu Ishaq as-Sabi'i, who said: When the verse ﴿And if We had decreed for them, "Kill yourselves or leave your homes," they would not have done it, except a few of them﴾ was revealed, a man said: "If we were commanded, we would have done it, and praise be to Allah who has spared us." This reached the Prophet (ﷺ), and he said: "Indeed, among my ummah are men whose faith is firmer in their hearts than the lofty mountains."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ja'far ibn Munir narrated to us, Rawh narrated to us, Hisham narrated to us, from al-Hasan, who said: When this verse was revealed, ﴿And if We had decreed for them, "Kill yourselves"...﴾, some people among the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "If our Lord had commanded it, we would have done it." This reached the Prophet (ﷺ), and he said: "Faith is firmer in the hearts of its people than the lofty mountains."

As-Suddi said: Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shammas and a Jewish man boasted. The Jew said: "By Allah, Allah had decreed killing for us, so we killed ourselves." Thabit said: "By Allah, if He had decreed for us, ﴿'Kill yourselves,'﴾ we would have killed ourselves." So Allah revealed this verse. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Mahmud ibn Ghaylan narrated to us, Bishr ibn as-Sari narrated to us, Mus'ab ibn Thabit narrated to us, from his paternal uncle 'Amir ibn 'Abd Allah ibn az-Zubayr, who said: When [the verse] ﴿And if We had decreed for them, "Kill yourselves"﴾ was revealed, Abu Bakr said: "O Messenger of Allah, by Allah, if you commanded me to kill myself, I would do it." He said: "You have spoken the truth, O Abu Bakr."

My father narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umar al-'Adani narrated to us, who said: Sufyan was asked about His saying ﴿And if We had decreed for them, "Kill yourselves or leave your homes," they would not have done it, except a few of them﴾. He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Had it been revealed, Ibn Umm 'Abd would have been among them."

My father narrated to us, Abu al-Yaman narrated to us, Isma'il ibn 'Ayyash narrated to us, from Safwan ibn 'Amr, from Shurayh ibn 'Ubayd, who said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited this verse, ﴿And if We had decreed for them, "Kill yourselves or leave your homes," they would not have done it, except a few of them﴾, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) pointed with his hand to 'Abd Allah ibn Rawahah and said: "If Allah had decreed that, this man would be among those few." He meant Ibn Rawahah.

For this reason, He said, ﴿And if they had done what they are admonished to do﴾, meaning: if they had done what they were commanded and abandoned what they were forbidden, ﴿it would have been better for them﴾, meaning: than opposing the command and committing the prohibition, ﴿and firmer in steadfastness﴾. As-Suddi said: meaning, "and firmer in affirmation (of the truth)."

﴿And then We would have given them from Us a great reward﴾, meaning: from Our presence, ﴿a great reward﴾, meaning Paradise. ﴿And We would have guided them to a straight path﴾, meaning in this world and the Hereafter.

Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And whoever obeys Allah and the Messenger – those will be with the ones upon whom Allah has bestowed favour: the prophets, the steadfast in truth (ṣiddīqūn), the martyrs, and the righteous. And excellent are those as companions.﴾ Meaning: whoever acts upon what Allah and His Messenger have commanded, and abandons what Allah and His Messenger have forbidden, then Allah, mighty and majestic, will settle him in the abode of His honour and make him a companion of the prophets, then of those after them in rank, namely the ṣiddīqūn (those steadfast in truth), then the martyrs, then the general body of believers, who are the righteous, whose inner and outer states are sound.

Then Allah praised them, saying: ﴿And excellent are those as companions.﴾

Al-Bukhari said: Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Hawshab narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn Sa'd narrated to us, from his father, from 'Urwah, from 'A'ishah, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "No prophet falls ill except that he is given the choice between this world and the Hereafter." During his final illness, in which he died, he was overcome by a severe hoarseness, and I heard him say: ﴿with those upon whom Allah has bestowed favour, of the prophets, the ṣiddīqūn, the martyrs, and the righteous.﴾ So I knew that he had been given the choice.

Muslim also narrated it similarly, from the hadith of Shu'bah, from Sa'd ibn Ibrahim, with the same chain.

This is the meaning of his (ﷺ) saying in another hadith: "O Allah, [grant me companionship] with the Highest Companion," three times, and then he died, may the best of prayers and peace be upon him.

Mention of the occasion of revelation of this noble verse:

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, Ya'qub al-Qummi narrated to us, from Ja'far ibn Abi al-Mughirah, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: A man from the Ansar came to the Prophet (ﷺ) while he was grieved. The Prophet (ﷺ) said to him: "O so-and-so, why do I see you grieved?" He said: "O Prophet of Allah, a matter I have been thinking about." He said: "What is it?" He said: "We visit you in the morning and evening, we look at your face and sit with you, but tomorrow you will be raised among the prophets, and we will not reach you." The Prophet (ﷺ) did not answer him at all, and then Jibril brought him this verse: ﴿And whoever obeys Allah and the Messenger – those will be with the ones upon whom Allah has bestowed favour, of the prophets, [the ṣiddīqūn, the martyrs, and the righteous, and excellent are those as companions].﴾ Then the Prophet (ﷺ) sent for him and gave him good news.

This report has been narrated as a mursal (a report in which the Companion is omitted from the chain) from Masruq, 'Ikrimah, 'Amir ash-Sha'bi, Qatadah, and from ar-Rabi' ibn Anas, and it is among the best of its chains.

Ibn Jarir said: Al-Muthanna narrated to us, Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from ar-Rabi', regarding His saying ﴿And whoever obeys Allah and the Messenger [will be with those upon whom Allah has bestowed favour from]﴾: The Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "We know that the Prophet (ﷺ) has a superiority over those who believed in him in the ranks of Paradise, among those who followed him and affirmed him. But how will they be when they gather in Paradise, that some of them may see others?" So Allah revealed concerning that—meaning this verse—and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Those on high descend to those below them, and they gather in its gardens, remember what Allah has bestowed upon them, and praise Him. The people of the higher ranks descend to them, and they strive to bring them whatever they desire and whatever they ask for. They are in a garden, rejoicing and enjoying themselves in it."

Ibn Jarir (8/535) narrated this as a mursal report; see the introduction in the exegetical manuscripts, where there is discussion of the copy of Abu Ja'far ar-Razi.

It has also been narrated as marfu' (traced to the Prophet (ﷺ)) by another route. Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh said: 'Abd ar-Rahim ibn Muhammad ibn Muslim narrated to us, Isma'il ibn Ahmad ibn Usayd narrated to us, 'Abd Allah ibn 'Imran narrated to us, Fudayl ibn 'Iyad narrated to us, from Mansur, from Ibrahim, from al-Aswad, from 'A'ishah, who said: A man came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, you are dearer to me than myself, dearer to me than my family, and dearer to me than my children. When I am in the house I remember you, and I cannot bear it until I come to you and look at you. When I remember my death and your death, I know that when you enter Paradise you will be raised with the prophets, and if I enter Paradise, I fear I will not see you." The Prophet (ﷺ) did not answer him until this was revealed to him: ﴿And whoever obeys Allah and the Messenger – those will be with the ones upon whom Allah has bestowed favour, of the prophets, the ṣiddīqūn, the martyrs, and the righteous, and excellent are those as companions.﴾

Al-Hafiz Abu 'Abd Allah al-Maqdisi likewise narrated it in his book Sifat al-Jannah (The Description of Paradise), by way of at-Tabarani, from Ahmad ibn 'Amr ibn Muslim al-Khallal, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Imran al-'Abidi, with the same chain. He then said: "I see no harm in its chain." And Allah knows best.

Ibn Mardawayh also said: Sulayman ibn Ahmad narrated to us, al-'Abbas ibn al-Fadl al-Asfati narrated to us, Abu Bakr ibn Thabit ibn 'Abbas al-Misri [in other manuscripts: "Ibn 'Ayyash al-Basri"] narrated to us, Khalid ibn 'Abd Allah narrated to us, from 'Ata' ibn as-Sa'ib, from 'Amir ash-Sha'bi, from Ibn 'Abbas, that a man came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I love you so much that I remember you in my dwelling, and it troubles me, and I wish to be with you in the same rank." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not answer him at all, and then Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed: ﴿And whoever obeys Allah and the Messenger – those will be with the ones upon whom Allah has bestowed favour, of the prophets, the ṣiddīqūn, the martyrs, and the righteous, and excellent are those as companions.﴾

Sulayman ibn Ahmad is at-Tabarani, and he narrated it in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (12/86). Al-Haythami said in Majma' al-Zawa'id (7/7): "It contains 'Ata' ibn as-Sa'ib, who became confused (in his memory)."

He said: 'Then help me against yourself by frequent prostration.'"

Ahmad said: Yahya ibn Ishaq narrated to us, Ibn Lahi'ah informed us, from 'Ubayd Allah ibn Abi Ja'far, from 'Isa ibn Talhah, from 'Amr ibn Murrah al-Juhani, who said: A man came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I bear witness that there is no god but Allah and that you are the Messenger of Allah, I have prayed the five (prayers), paid the zakat of my wealth, and fasted Ramadan." Mention of the occasion of revelation of this noble verse:

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, Ya'qub al-Qummi narrated to us, from Ja'far ibn Abi al-Mughirah, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: A man from the Ansar came to the Prophet (ﷺ) while he was grieved. The Prophet (ﷺ) said to him: "O so-and-so, why do I see you grieved?" He said: "O Prophet of Allah, a matter I have been thinking about." He said: "What is it?" He said: "We visit you in the morning and evening, we look at your face and sit with you, but tomorrow you will be raised among the prophets, and we will not reach you." The Prophet (ﷺ) did not answer him at all, and then Jibril brought him this verse: ﴿And whoever obeys Allah and the Messenger – those will be with the ones upon whom Allah has bestowed favour, of the prophets, [the ṣiddīqūn, the martyrs, and the righteous, and excellent are those as companions].﴾ Then the Prophet (ﷺ) sent for him and gave him good news.

This report has been narrated as a mursal (a report in which the Companion is omitted from the chain) from Masruq, 'Ikrimah, 'Amir ash-Sha'bi, Qatadah, and from ar-Rabi' ibn Anas, and it is among the best of its chains.

Ibn Jarir said: Al-Muthanna narrated to us, Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from ar-Rabi', regarding His saying ﴿And whoever obeys Allah and the Messenger [will be with those upon whom Allah has bestowed favour from]﴾: The Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "We know that the Prophet (ﷺ) has a superiority over those who believed in him in the ranks of Paradise, among those who followed him and affirmed him. But how will they be when they gather in Paradise, that some of them may see others?" So Allah revealed concerning that—meaning this verse—and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Those on high descend to those below them, and they gather in its gardens, remember what Allah has bestowed upon them, and praise Him. The people of the higher ranks descend to them, and they strive to bring them whatever they desire and whatever they ask for. They are in a garden, rejoicing and enjoying themselves in it."

Ibn Jarir (8/535) narrated this as a mursal report; see the introduction in the exegetical manuscripts, where there is discussion of the copy of Abu Ja'far ar-Razi.

It has also been narrated as marfu' (traced to the Prophet (ﷺ)) by another route. Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh said: 'Abd ar-Rahim ibn Muhammad ibn Muslim narrated to us, Isma'il ibn Ahmad ibn Usayd narrated to us, 'Abd Allah ibn 'Imran narrated to us, Fudayl ibn 'Iyad narrated to us, from Mansur, from Ibrahim, from al-Aswad, from 'A'ishah, who said: A man came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, you are dearer to me than myself, dearer to me than my family, and dearer to me than my children. When I am in the house I remember you, and I cannot bear it until I come to you and look at you. When I remember my death and your death, I know that when you enter Paradise you will be raised with the prophets, and if I enter Paradise, I fear I will not see you." The Prophet (ﷺ) did not answer him until this was revealed to him: ﴿And whoever obeys Allah and the Messenger – those will be with the ones upon whom Allah has bestowed favour, of the prophets, the ṣiddīqūn, the martyrs, and the righteous, and excellent are those as companions.﴾

Al-Hafiz Abu 'Abd Allah al-Maqdisi likewise narrated it in his book Sifat al-Jannah (The Description of Paradise), by way of at-Tabarani, from Ahmad ibn 'Amr ibn Muslim al-Khallal, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Imran al-'Abidi, with the same chain. He then said: "I see no harm in its chain." And Allah knows best.

Ibn Mardawayh also said: Sulayman ibn Ahmad narrated to us, al-'Abbas ibn al-Fadl al-Asfati narrated to us, Abu Bakr ibn Thabit ibn 'Abbas al-Misri [in other manuscripts: "Ibn 'Ayyash al-Basri"] narrated to us, Khalid ibn 'Abd Allah narrated to us, from 'Ata' ibn as-Sa'ib, from 'Amir ash-Sha'bi, from Ibn 'Abbas, that a man came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I love you so much that I remember you in my dwelling, and it troubles me, and I wish to be with you in the same rank." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not answer him at all, and then Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed: ﴿And whoever obeys Allah and the Messenger – those will be with the ones upon whom Allah has bestowed favour, of the prophets, the ṣiddīqūn, the martyrs, and the righteous, and excellent are those as companions.﴾

And it is established in Sahih Muslim, through the hadith of Hilal ibn Ziyad, from al-Awza'i, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from Abu Salamah ibn 'Abd ar-Rahman, from Rabi'ah ibn Ka'b al-Aslami, that he said: "I used to spend the night with the Prophet (ﷺ), and I would bring him his water for ablution and his needs. He said to me: 'Ask.' I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, I ask you for your companionship in Paradise.' He said: 'Or is there anything else?' I said: 'That is it.' He said: 'Then help me against yourself by frequent prostration.'"

Ahmad said: Yahya ibn Ishaq narrated to us, Ibn Lahi'ah informed us, from 'Ubayd Allah ibn Abi Ja'far, from 'Isa ibn Talhah, from 'Amr ibn Murrah al-Juhani, who said: A man came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I bear witness that there is no god but Allah and that you are the Messenger of Allah, I have prayed the five (prayers), paid the zakat of my wealth, and fasted Ramadan." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever dies upon this will be with the prophets, the ṣiddīqūn, and the martyrs on the Day of Resurrection, like this"—and he raised his two fingers—"so long as he has not disobeyed his parents."
