Ahmad also said: Abu Sa'id, the client of Abu Hashim, narrated to us, Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to us, from Zabban [in another manuscript: "Ziyad"] ibn Fa'id, from Sahl ibn Mu'adh ibn Anas, from his father, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites a thousand verses in the cause of Allah will be recorded on the Day of Resurrection with the prophets, the ṣiddīqūn, the martyrs, and the righteous, and excellent are those as companions, if Allah wills." [Note: Al-Musnad (4/437) contains: "Hasan narrated to us, Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to us," and then the report. Al-Haythami (2/269) said: "It contains Ibn Lahi'ah from Zabban, and there is some discussion about it."]

The Prophet ﷺ said: "The truthful, trustworthy merchant is with the Prophets, the truthful ones (al-siddiqin) and the martyrs."

Al-Tirmidhi also narrated it through Sufyan al-Thawri, from Abu Hamza, from al-Hasan al-Basri, from Abu Sa'id, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The truthful, trustworthy merchant is with the Prophets and the truthful ones and the martyrs."

Then he said: "This is a hasan hadith. We do not know it except through this route. Abu Hamza's name is Abdullah ibn Jabir, a shaykh from Basra" [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (1209).]].

Greater than all of this is the glad tidings found in the Sahihs, the Masanid and others, through mutawatir chains from a group of the Companions: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asked about a man who loves a people but has not yet joined them. He said: "A person is with whom he loves." Anas said: "The Muslims never rejoiced more than they rejoiced at this hadith" [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. (6167), and by Muslim in his Sahih, no. (2639).]].

In another narration from Anas, he said: "Indeed, I love the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and I love Abu Bakr and Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, and I hope that Allah will resurrect me with them, even if I do not act as they acted" [[Sahih Muslim, no. (2639).]].

Imam Malik ibn Anas said, from Safwan ibn Sulaym, from Ata' ibn Yasar, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The people of Paradise will look up at the people of the upper chambers (al-ghuraf) above them, just as you look at the bright, distant star on the horizon, in the east or the west, because of the difference in their ranks." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, those are the abodes of the Prophets, which no one else can reach?" He said: "Yes, by Him in whose hand is my soul, [they are for] men who believed in Allah and affirmed the Messengers."

Al-Bukhari and Muslim both narrated it in their Sahihs from the hadith of Malik, and the wording is Muslim's.

Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal said: Fazara narrated to us, Fulayh informed me, from Hilal (i.e., Ibn Ali), from Ata', from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The people of Paradise will look at one another in Paradise as you look at the bright star that sets on the horizon or rises, because of the difference in ranks." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, are those the Prophets?" He said: "Yes, by Him in whose hand is my soul, and [also] people who believed in Allah and affirmed the Messengers."

The Hafiz Diya' al-Maqdisi said: "This hadith meets the conditions of al-Bukhari" [[al-Musnad (2/339).]]. And Allah knows best.

The Hafiz Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said in his al-Mu'jam al-Kabir: Ali ibn Abd al-Aziz narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ammar al-Mawsili narrated to us, Ufayf ibn Salim narrated to us, from Ayyub ibn Utba [[In the manuscripts: "Ayyub from Utba," which is a distortion.]], from Ata', from Ibn Umar, who said: A man from Abyssinia came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ asking him, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: "Ask and inquire." He said: "O Messenger of Allah, you have been given preference over us in form, colour and prophethood. Tell me: if I believe in what you believe in, and do what you do, will I be with you in Paradise?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Yes, by Him in whose hand is my soul, the whiteness of the black man will shine in Paradise from a distance of a thousand years." Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever says: 'There is no god but Allah,' he will have a covenant with Allah by it, and whoever says: 'Glory be to Allah and praise be to Him,' there will be written for him by it one hundred thousand and twenty-four thousand good deeds." A man said: "How then could we be destroyed after that, O Messenger of Allah?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "A man will come on the Day of Resurrection with a deed that, if placed upon a mountain, would weigh it down. Then a blessing from the blessings of Allah will stand up and nearly exhaust all of that, unless Allah extends His mercy to him."

And these verses were revealed: ﴿Has there come upon man a period of time when he was not a thing [even] worthy of mention?﴾ up to His saying: ﴿a delight and a great dominion﴾ [Al-Insan: 1-20]. The Abyssinian said: "Do my eyes see what your eyes see in Paradise?" The Prophet ﷺ said: "Yes." So he wept until his soul departed. Ibn Umar said: "I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ lowering him into his grave with his own hands."

In it there is strangeness and unfamiliarity, and its chain is weak [[al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (12/436). Its weakness is that it contains Ayyub ibn Utba, who is weak.]].

Therefore Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿That is the bounty from Allah﴾, meaning: from Allah's presence, by His mercy. It is He who qualified them for this, not by their deeds. ﴿And sufficient is Allah as Knower﴾, meaning: He knows who deserves guidance and success.

Ibn Kathir, the commentary on Surah an-Nisa' (4), verses 66–70 (part 1 of 2):

Allah, the Exalted, informs us about most people that if they were commanded to do the prohibited acts they commit, they would not do them. This is because their base natures are inclined to oppose the command. This is part of His knowledge, blessed and exalted is He, of what has not happened and what would have happened, and how it would have been. For this reason, He said, ﴿And if We had decreed for them, "Kill yourselves or leave your homes," they would not have done it, except a few of them.﴾

Ibn Jarir said: Al-Muthanna narrated to me, Ishaq narrated to me, Abu Zuhayr narrated to us [in one manuscript: "Abu al-Azhar"], from Isma'il, from Abu Ishaq as-Sabi'i, who said: When the verse ﴿And if We had decreed for them, "Kill yourselves or leave your homes," they would not have done it, except a few of them﴾ was revealed, a man said: "If we were commanded, we would have done it, and praise be to Allah who has spared us." This reached the Prophet (ﷺ), and he said: "Indeed, among my ummah are men whose faith is firmer in their hearts than the lofty mountains."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ja'far ibn Munir narrated to us, Rawh narrated to us, Hisham narrated to us, from al-Hasan, who said: When this verse was revealed, ﴿And if We had decreed for them, "Kill yourselves"...﴾, some people among the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "If our Lord had commanded it, we would have done it." This reached the Prophet (ﷺ), and he said: "Faith is firmer in the hearts of its people than the lofty mountains."

As-Suddi said: Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shammas and a Jewish man boasted. The Jew said: "By Allah, Allah had decreed killing for us, so we killed ourselves." Thabit said: "By Allah, if He had decreed for us, ﴿'Kill yourselves,'﴾ we would have killed ourselves." So Allah revealed this verse. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Mahmud ibn Ghaylan narrated to us, Bishr ibn as-Sari narrated to us, Mus'ab ibn Thabit narrated to us, from his paternal uncle 'Amir ibn 'Abd Allah ibn az-Zubayr, who said: When [the verse] ﴿And if We had decreed for them, "Kill yourselves"﴾ was revealed, Abu Bakr said: "O Messenger of Allah, by Allah, if you commanded me to kill myself, I would do it." He said: "You have spoken the truth, O Abu Bakr."

My father narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umar al-'Adani narrated to us, who said: Sufyan was asked about His saying ﴿And if We had decreed for them, "Kill yourselves or leave your homes," they would not have done it, except a few of them﴾. He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Had it been revealed, Ibn Umm 'Abd would have been among them."

My father narrated to us, Abu al-Yaman narrated to us, Isma'il ibn 'Ayyash narrated to us, from Safwan ibn 'Amr, from Shurayh ibn 'Ubayd, who said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited this verse, ﴿And if We had decreed for them, "Kill yourselves or leave your homes," they would not have done it, except a few of them﴾, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) pointed with his hand to 'Abd Allah ibn Rawahah and said: "If Allah had decreed that, this man would be among those few." He meant Ibn Rawahah.

For this reason, He said, ﴿And if they had done what they are admonished to do﴾, meaning: if they had done what they were commanded and abandoned what they were forbidden, ﴿it would have been better for them﴾, meaning: than opposing the command and committing the prohibition, ﴿and firmer in steadfastness﴾. As-Suddi said: meaning, "and firmer in affirmation (of the truth)."

﴿And then We would have given them from Us a great reward﴾, meaning: from Our presence, ﴿a great reward﴾, meaning Paradise. ﴿And We would have guided them to a straight path﴾, meaning in this world and the Hereafter.

Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And whoever obeys Allah and the Messenger – those will be with the ones upon whom Allah has bestowed favour: the prophets, the steadfast in truth (ṣiddīqūn), the martyrs, and the righteous. And excellent are those as companions.﴾ Meaning: whoever acts upon what Allah and His Messenger have commanded, and abandons what Allah and His Messenger have forbidden, then Allah, mighty and majestic, will settle him in the abode of His honour and make him a companion of the prophets, then of those after them in rank, namely the ṣiddīqūn (those steadfast in truth), then the martyrs, then the general body of believers, who are the righteous, whose inner and outer states are sound.

Then Allah praised them, saying: ﴿And excellent are those as companions.﴾

Al-Bukhari said: Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Hawshab narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn Sa'd narrated to us, from his father, from 'Urwah, from 'A'ishah, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "No prophet falls ill except that he is given the choice between this world and the Hereafter." During his final illness, in which he died, he was overcome by a severe hoarseness, and I heard him say: ﴿with those upon whom Allah has bestowed favour, of the prophets, the ṣiddīqūn, the martyrs, and the righteous.﴾ So I knew that he had been given the choice.

Muslim also narrated it similarly, from the hadith of Shu'bah, from Sa'd ibn Ibrahim, with the same chain.

This is the meaning of his (ﷺ) saying in another hadith: "O Allah, [grant me companionship] with the Highest Companion," three times, and then he died, may the best of prayers and peace be upon him.

The Hafiz Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said in his al-Mu'jam al-Kabir: Ali ibn Abd al-Aziz narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ammar al-Mawsili narrated to us, Ufayf ibn Salim narrated to us, from Ayyub ibn Utba [[In the manuscripts: "Ayyub from Utba," which is a distortion.]], from Ata', from Ibn Umar, who said: A man from Abyssinia came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ asking him, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: "Ask and inquire." He said: "O Messenger of Allah, you have been given preference over us in form, colour and prophethood. Tell me: if I believe in what you believe in, and do what you do, will I be with you in Paradise?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Yes, by Him in whose hand is my soul, the whiteness of the black man will shine in Paradise from a distance of a thousand years." Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever says: 'There is no god but Allah,' he will have a covenant with Allah by it, and whoever says: 'Glory be to Allah and praise be to Him,' there will be written for him by it one hundred thousand and twenty-four thousand good deeds." A man said: "How then could we be destroyed after that, O Messenger of Allah?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "A man will come on the Day of Resurrection with a deed that, if placed upon a mountain, would weigh it down. Then a blessing from the blessings of Allah will stand up and nearly exhaust all of that, unless Allah extends His mercy to him."

And these verses were revealed: ﴿Has there come upon man a period of time when he was not a thing [even] worthy of mention?﴾ up to His saying: ﴿a delight and a great dominion﴾ [Al-Insan: 1-20]. The Abyssinian said: "Do my eyes see what your eyes see in Paradise?" The Prophet ﷺ said: "Yes." So he wept until his soul departed. Ibn Umar said: "I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ lowering him into his grave with his own hands."

In it there is strangeness and unfamiliarity, and its chain is weak [[al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (12/436). Its weakness is that it contains Ayyub ibn Utba, who is weak.]].

Therefore Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿That is the bounty from Allah﴾, meaning: from Allah's presence, by His mercy. It is He who qualified them for this, not by their deeds. ﴿And sufficient is Allah as Knower﴾, meaning: He knows who deserves guidance and success.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 4, verses 71–74:

God commands His believing servants to take precautions against their enemy (al-hadhar), and this entails preparing for them by readying weapons and equipment and increasing their numbers by going forth (al-nafir) in His cause.

﴿Thubat﴾ means: group after group, company after company, and detachment after detachment. Thubat is the plural of thubah (a body of men), and thubah may also be pluralized as thubin.

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah related from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His words: ﴿So go forth in separate groups﴾, that it means: in companies (‘usab), i.e., scattered detachments (saraya) ﴿or go forth all together﴾, meaning: all of you.

Similar has been related from Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, al-Suddi, Qatadah, al-Dahhak, 'Ata' al-Khurasani, Muqatil ibn Hayyan, and Khusayf al-Jazari.

* *

As for His words: ﴿And indeed among you is one who lingers﴾, Mujahid and others said: it was revealed concerning the hypocrites. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: ﴿lingers﴾ means: he will stay behind from jihad.

It is possible that the meaning is that he himself lags behind and discourages others from jihad, as 'Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul, may Allah curse him, used to do: he would hold back from jihad and dissuade people from going out to it. This is the view of Ibn Jurayj and Ibn Jarir. For this reason, God, informing about the hypocrite, says that when he holds back from jihad he says: ﴿If a misfortune strikes you﴾, i.e., death, martyrdom, and the enemy's victory over you, for God has wisdom in that ﴿he says: Allah has blessed me, for I was not present with them as a witness﴾, i.e., I was not present with them at the battle, considering that a blessing from God upon him, and he did not realize what reward he had missed through patience or through martyrdom had he been killed.

﴿And if a bounty from Allah comes to you﴾, i.e., victory, triumph and spoils, ﴿he will surely say, as if there had never been any affection between you and him: "Oh, I wish I had been with them, so I would have achieved a great success."﴾ That is, that he would be given a share with them so that he would obtain it. This is his greatest aim and the ultimate of his desire.

Then God said: ﴿So let them fight in the cause of Allah, those who sell the worldly life for the Hereafter﴾, i.e., the believer who goes forth, those who sell their religion for a small provision of this world. That is only because of their disbelief and lack of faith.

Then God said: ﴿And whoever fights in the cause of Allah and is killed or achieves victory, We will give him a great reward﴾, i.e., everyone who fights in the cause of Allah, whether he is killed or victorious and takes spoils, has with Allah a great reward and abundant recompense, as established in the two Sahihs [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, nos. (7463, 7457), and Muslim in his Sahih, no. (1876), from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him.]] and Allah has undertaken for the one who strives in His cause that, if He takes his soul, He will admit him to Paradise, or return him to the dwelling from which he set out, bringing whatever reward or spoils he has gained.

Allah urges His believing servants to fight in His cause and to strive for the liberation of those who were oppressed in Makkah, men, women and children, who were distressed at remaining there. Therefore Allah said: ﴿Those who say, "Our Lord, bring us out from this city"﴾, meaning Makkah, as in His saying: ﴿And how many a city, mightier in strength than your city which has driven you out, have We destroyed, and there was none to help them﴾ [Muhammad: 13].

Then He described it with His saying: ﴿whose people are wrongdoers. Appoint for us from Yourself a protector, and appoint for us from Yourself a helper﴾, meaning: make for us from Yourself a protector and a helper.

Al-Bukhari said: Abdullah ibn Muhammad narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Ubayd Allah, who said: I heard Ibn Abbas say: "I and my mother were among the oppressed."

Sulayman ibn Harb narrated to us, Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to us, from Ayyub, from Ibn Abi Mulaykah, that Ibn Abbas recited ﴿except the oppressed among men, women and children﴾ and said: "I and my mother were among those whom Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has excused."

Then Allah said: ﴿Those who believe fight in the cause of Allah, and those who disbelieve fight in the cause of Taghut (false deities/the devil)﴾, meaning: the believers fight in obedience to Allah and seeking His pleasure, while the disbelievers fight in obedience to Satan.

Then Allah stirred the believers to fight His enemies by His saying: ﴿So fight against the allies of Satan. Indeed, the plot of Satan is ever weak﴾.

The Muslims, while they were in Makkah at the beginning of Islam, were commanded to pray and to give zakat, though zakat was not yet obligatory with its prescribed rates. They were commanded to share with the poor among them, and they were commanded to pardon and forgive the polytheists and to be patient until a set time. They were eager and wished they had been commanded to fight, so that they could vent their anger on their enemies. But the situation was not suitable for that at the time, for many reasons. Among them: their number was small compared with the large number of their enemies. Another reason was that they were in their own land, which is a sacred land and the most noble place on earth, so it was not fitting to begin with an order to fight there. For this reason they were not commanded to wage jihad (struggle in the way of God) until they were in Madinah, once they had a home, a stronghold and helpers. Even so, when they were commanded to do what they had wished for, some of them recoiled from it and feared confronting the people with a great fear. ﴿They said, "Our Lord, why have You prescribed fighting for us? If only You had delayed us to a near term."﴾ That is, "If only You had not postponed its obligation to another time," for in it is the shedding of blood, the orphaning of children and the widowing of women. This verse has the same meaning as His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And those who believe say, "If only a surah were sent down." But when a decisive surah is sent down in which fighting is mentioned, you see those in whose hearts is a disease looking at you with the look of one fainting from death. So woe to them. Obedience and honorable speech would have been better for them. And when the matter is resolved, if they had been true to God, it would have been better for them.﴾ [Muhammad: 20, 21]. [[Addition from manuscript R. In manuscript H: "the verse".]]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated to us; Muhammad ibn Abd al-Aziz ibn Abi Rizmah [[In manuscript A: "Zar'ah".]] and Ali ibn Zinjah narrated to us, both saying: Ali ibn al-Hasan narrated to us, from al-Husayn ibn Waqid, from Amr ibn Dinar, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas: that Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf and some companions of his came to the Prophet (ﷺ) in Makkah and said: "O Prophet of God, we were in honor while we were polytheists, but when we believed we became humiliated." He said: "I have been commanded to pardon, so do not fight the people." When God transferred him to Madinah, He commanded him to fight, but they held back. So God revealed: ﴿Have you not seen those who were told, "Hold back your hands, and establish prayer and give zakat"? But when fighting was prescribed for them, behold, a faction of them fear people as they fear God or with even greater fear.﴾ [[Addition from manuscripts R and A.]] etc.

It was also related by al-Nasa'i, al-Hakim and Ibn Mardawayh, through the narration of Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Shaqiq, with the same chain [[Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. (11112), and al-Mustadrak (2/307).]].

Asbat related from al-Suddi: "They had only prayer and zakat. So they asked God to prescribe fighting for them. But when fighting was prescribed for them: ﴿Behold, a faction of them fear people as they fear God or with even greater fear. And they say, 'Our Lord, why have You prescribed fighting for us? If only You had delayed us to a near term,'﴾ which is death. God, exalted is He, said: ﴿Say, "The enjoyment of this world is little, and the Hereafter is better for those who fear God."﴾

And from Mujahid: these verses were revealed concerning the Jews. Related by Ibn Jarir.

* *

His saying: ﴿Say, "The enjoyment of this world is little, and the Hereafter is better for those who fear God."﴾ That is, the Hereafter of the one who fears God is better than his worldly life.

﴿And you will not be wronged a thread﴾ That is, not in your deeds; rather, you will be paid their full reward. This is a consolation for them regarding the world, an encouragement for them toward the Hereafter, and an incitement for them to jihad.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: my father narrated to us; Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim al-Dawraqi narrated to us; Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us; Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to us, from Hisham, who said: al-Hasan recited: ﴿Say, "The enjoyment of this world is little,"﴾ and said: "May God have mercy on a servant who kept company with it according to its measure. The whole world, its first and its last, is only like a man who slept a nap, saw in his dream some of what he loves, and then woke up."

Ibn Ma'in said: Abu Muslihr used to recite:

"There is no good in this world for one who has no share
from God in the abode of permanence.
If the world impresses men,
it is little enjoyment, and its passing is near."

* *

His saying: ﴿Wherever you may be, death will overtake you, even if you should be in towers built up high.﴾ That is, you are certainly heading toward death, and none of you will escape it, as He said, exalted is He: ﴿Everyone upon it will perish, but there will remain the Face of your Lord, Owner of Majesty and Honor.﴾ [[Addition from manuscripts R and A; in H: "the verse".]] [Ar-Rahman: 26, 27]. He also said: ﴿Every soul will taste death﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 185], and He said: ﴿And We did not grant to any human before you eternal life﴾ [Al-Anbiya: 34]. The point is that everyone is certainly heading toward death, and nothing saves him from that, whether he fought in jihad or did not fight, for he has a determined term and an appointed time, as Khalid ibn al-Walid said when death came to him on his bed: "I have witnessed such-and-such a number of battles, and there is not a limb of mine without a wound from a spear or an arrow, and here I am dying on my bed. May the eyes of cowards never sleep!" [[Related by the hafiz Ibn Asakir in Tarikh Dimashq, as in al-Mukhtasar by Ibn al-Manzur (8/26), through the route of Abu al-Zinad that when Khalid's death approached he wept and said ... and he mentioned it.]]

* *

His saying: ﴿even if you should be in towers built up high﴾ That is, in strong, fortified, lofty and elevated fortresses. It was said that they are towers in the sky, as said by al-Suddi, but this is weak. The correct view is that they are fortresses; that is, caution and fortification do not avail against death, as Zuhayr ibn Abi Sulma said:

"Whoever fears the causes of death, it will reach him,
even if he tries to climb the causes of the sky with a ladder."

[[The verse is from the Mu'allaqah of Zuhayr ibn Abi Sulma, found in his Diwan (p. 30).]]

Then it was said: "al-Mushayyadah" is al-Mashidah, as in His saying: "and a lofty palace" [Al-Hajj: 45]. It was also said that there is a difference between them: al-Mushayyadah with the doubled letter means "prolonged," while without the doubling it means "adorned with shid," which is plaster.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim have mentioned here a lengthy account from Mujahid: that he mentioned a woman among those who came before us whom labor pains seized, so she commanded her hired man to bring her a fire. He went out and found a man standing at the door, who said: "What has the woman given birth to?" He said: "A girl." The man said: "Indeed, she will commit adultery with a hundred men, and then her hired man will marry her, and her death will be by a spider." He said: So he turned back, stabbed the girl in the belly with a knife, split it open, and then fled, thinking she had died. Her mother sewed up her belly, and she recovered, grew up and became the most beautiful woman in her land. That hired man went off to where he went and entered the seas, acquired great wealth, then returned to his land and wished to marry. He said to an old woman: "I want to marry the most beautiful woman in this land." She said to him: "There is no one more beautiful here than so-and-so." He said: "Propose her to me." She went to her, and she accepted, so he entered upon her and was greatly impressed by her. She asked him about his affair and where he had come from, so he told her his story and what had happened to him in his flight. She said: "I am the one." And she showed him the place of the knife. He became certain of it and said: "If you are indeed her, you have told me two things that must come to pass. One of them: that you have committed adultery with a hundred men." She said: "Something of that has happened, but I do not know how many they are." He said: "They are a hundred." And the second: "that you will die by a spider." So he built for her a strong, towering palace to protect her from that. One day they were there when suddenly a spider was on the ceiling. He showed it to her, and she said: "Is this the one you fear for me? By God, no one will kill it but me." So they brought it down from the ceiling, and she went to it and crushed it with the big toe of her foot, killing it. Some of its poison flew and lodged between her toenail and her flesh, so her foot turned black, and in that was her end [[Tafsir al-Tabari (8/552).]].

Here we will mention the story of the lord of al-Hadr, who was "al-Satirun," when Sabur tricked him until he besieged him in it, and killed those within it after a siege of two years. The Arabs said poems about that, among them:

"The lord of al-Hadr, when he built it, and when Dijlah
and al-Khabur were brought to him in tribute,
He built it of marble and covered it with plaster,
so birds have their nests on its heights.
The hands of death did not spare him, and kingship passed away from him,
and its gate is deserted."

When he entered upon Uthman, he began to say: "O God, unite the community of Muhammad." Then he recited the verse of the poet:

"I see death leaves no one mighty, and it has spared
for the people of 'Ad no refuge or dwelling in the lands.
The people of the fortress are attacked at night while the fortress is locked,
and it reaches the mountains together with their peaks."
[[In manuscript R: "the heights".]]

* *

His saying: ﴿And if good befalls them﴾ That is, fertility and provision from fruits, crops, children and the like. This is the meaning of the words of Ibn Abbas, Abu al-Aliyah and al-Suddi: ﴿they say, "This is from God." But if evil befalls them﴾ That is, drought, famine, loss in fruits and crops, or the death of children, offspring or other things, as Abu al-Aliyah and al-Suddi said. ﴿they say, "This is from you."﴾ That is, from your side, and because of our following you and our adherence to your religion. As He said, exalted is He, concerning the people of Pharaoh: ﴿But when good came to them, they said, "This is ours." And if evil befell them, they ascribed bad omen to Musa and those with him﴾ [Al-A'raf: 131]. And as He said: ﴿And among people is one who worships God on an edge. If good befalls him, he is content with it; but if a trial strikes him, he turns back on his face. He has lost this world and the Hereafter﴾ [Al-Hajj: 11]. Likewise these hypocrites said, who entered Islam outwardly while in reality they disliked it. Therefore, when evil befalls them, they attribute it to their following of the Prophet (ﷺ).

Al-Suddi said: ﴿And if good befalls them﴾: "The good is fertility. Their horses, livestock and herds bring forth young, their condition improves, and their women bear boys. They say: ﴿This is from God.﴾ But if evil befalls them﴾: "The evil is drought and harm to their wealth. They considered Muhammad (ﷺ) a bad omen and said: ﴿This is from you.﴾ They say: 'Because we abandoned our religion and followed Muhammad, this calamity has struck us.'" So God, mighty and majestic, revealed: ﴿Say, "All is from God."﴾ So His saying ﴿Say, "All is from God"﴾ means that everything is by the decree and destiny of God, and it takes effect upon the righteous and the wicked, the believer and the disbeliever.

Ali ibn Abi Talhah said, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿Say, "All is from God"﴾ means: the good and the evil. Likewise said al-Hasan al-Basri.

Then God, exalted is He, said, rebuking those who spoke this statement which proceeds from doubt and uncertainty, and from little understanding and knowledge, and much ignorance and wrongdoing: ﴿So what is wrong with these people that they can hardly understand any statement?﴾

Mention of a strange hadith related to His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say, "All is from God."﴾

The Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said: Al-Sakan ibn Sa'id narrated to us, 'Umar ibn Yunus narrated to us, Isma'il ibn Hammad narrated to us, from Muqatil ibn Hayyan, from 'Amr ibn Shu'ayb, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: "We were sitting with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), when Abu Bakr and 'Umar came along with two groups of people, and their voices had risen. Abu Bakr sat close to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and 'Umar sat close to Abu Bakr. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Why have your voices risen?' A man said: 'O Messenger of Allah...' Abu Bakr said: 'The good deeds are from Allah and the evil deeds are from ourselves.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'What did you say, O 'Umar?' He said: 'I said: The good deeds and the evil deeds are from Allah, Exalted is He.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'The first to speak about this were Jibril and Mika'il. Mika'il said your statement, O Abu Bakr, and Jibril said your statement, O 'Umar. He said: We differ, so the people of the heavens differ, and if the people of the heavens differ, the people of the earth will differ. They referred their dispute to Israfil, and he judged between them that the good deeds and the evil deeds are from Allah.'" Then he turned to Abu Bakr and 'Umar and said: "Memorise my judgment between you both: Had Allah wished that He not be disobeyed, He would not have created Iblis."

Shaykh al-Islam Taqi al-Din Abu al-'Abbas Ibn Taymiyyah said: This is a fabricated (mawdu') hadith, agreed upon by the people of knowledge. [The hadith is in Musnad al-Bazzar, no. (2496). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (7/191): "The Sheikh of al-Bazzar, al-Sakan ibn Sa'id, I do not know him, and the rest of al-Bazzar's narrators are trustworthy, with some remarks about some of them that do not harm." Ibn Hajar, may Allah have mercy on him, said: "This report is munkar, and there is weakness in its chain."]

Then Allah, the Exalted, said, addressing the Messenger [(ﷺ)] (the intended meaning being the human species, so that the answer is complete): ﴿Whatever good befalls you is from Allah, and whatever evil befalls you is from yourself﴾, i.e., from the bounty, favour, kindness and mercy of Allah; and ﴿whatever evil befalls you is from yourself﴾, i.e., it is from your own side and from your own deeds, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And whatever disaster strikes you, it is because of what your hands have earned, and He pardons much﴾ [Ash-Shura: 30].

Al-Suddi, al-Hasan al-Basri, Ibn Jurayj and Ibn Zayd said: ﴿from yourself﴾ means: because of your sin.

Qatadah said: ﴿Whatever good befalls you is from Allah, and whatever evil befalls you is from yourself﴾: it is a punishment, O son of Adam, for your sin. He said: It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) used to say: "No scratch from a stick, no stumble of a foot, and no twitch of a vein befalls a man except because of a sin, and what Allah pardons is greater."

This which Qatadah transmitted without a chain (mursal) has been related with a connected chain in the Sahih: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, no distress, sorrow or fatigue afflicts a believer, not even a thorn that pricks him, but Allah expiates some of his sins by it." [Related by Muslim in similar wording, no. (2572), from the hadith of 'A'ishah, and no. (2573), from the hadith of Abu Sa'id and Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with them.]

Abu Salih said: ﴿Whatever good befalls you is from Allah, and whatever evil befalls you is from yourself﴾, i.e., because of your sin, and I am the One who decreed it for you. Narrated by Ibn Jarir.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn 'Ammar narrated to us, Sahl (meaning Ibn Bakkar) narrated to us, al-Aswad ibn Shayban narrated to us, 'Uqbah ibn Wasil ibn Akhi Mutarrif narrated to me, from Mutarrif ibn 'Abdullah, who said: "What do you want from qadar? Does not the verse in Surah an-Nisa suffice you: ﴿And if good befalls them, they say, 'This is from Allah,' and if evil befalls them, they say, 'This is from you﴾", i.e., from yourself. By Allah, they were not left to qadar, and they were commanded, and to Him they will return.

This is a firm and strong statement in refutation of the Qadariyyah and also the Jabriyyah, and its elaboration has another place.

* *

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And We have sent you to mankind as a Messenger﴾, i.e., conveying to them the laws of Allah, what He loves and is pleased with, and what He dislikes and rejects.

﴿And sufficient is Allah as Witness﴾, i.e., as a witness that He sent you, and He is also a witness between you and them, and knowing of what you convey to them, and of what they return to you of rejection, out of disbelief and obstinacy.

The Muslims, while they were in Makkah at the beginning of Islam, were commanded to pray and to give zakat, though zakat was not yet obligatory with its prescribed rates. They were commanded to share with the poor among them, and they were commanded to pardon and forgive the polytheists and to be patient until a set time. They were eager and wished they had been commanded to fight, so that they could vent their anger on their enemies. But the situation was not suitable for that at the time, for many reasons. Among them: their number was small compared with the large number of their enemies. Another reason was that they were in their own land, which is a sacred land and the most noble place on earth, so it was not fitting to begin with an order to fight there. For this reason they were not commanded to wage jihad (struggle in the way of God) until they were in Madinah, once they had a home, a stronghold and helpers. Even so, when they were commanded to do what they had wished for, some of them recoiled from it and feared confronting the people with a great fear. ﴿They said, "Our Lord, why have You prescribed fighting for us? If only You had delayed us to a near term."﴾ That is, "If only You had not postponed its obligation to another time," for in it is the shedding of blood, the orphaning of children and the widowing of women. This verse has the same meaning as His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And those who believe say, "If only a surah were sent down." But when a decisive surah is sent down in which fighting is mentioned, you see those in whose hearts is a disease looking at you with the look of one fainting from death. So woe to them. Obedience and honorable speech would have been better for them. And when the matter is resolved, if they had been true to God, it would have been better for them.﴾ [Muhammad: 20, 21]. [[Addition from manuscript R. In manuscript H: "the verse".]]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated to us; Muhammad ibn Abd al-Aziz ibn Abi Rizmah [[In manuscript A: "Zar'ah".]] and Ali ibn Zinjah narrated to us, both saying: Ali ibn al-Hasan narrated to us, from al-Husayn ibn Waqid, from Amr ibn Dinar, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas: that Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf and some companions of his came to the Prophet (ﷺ) in Makkah and said: "O Prophet of God, we were in honor while we were polytheists, but when we believed we became humiliated." He said: "I have been commanded to pardon, so do not fight the people." When God transferred him to Madinah, He commanded him to fight, but they held back. So God revealed: ﴿Have you not seen those who were told, "Hold back your hands, and establish prayer and give zakat"? But when fighting was prescribed for them, behold, a faction of them fear people as they fear God or with even greater fear.﴾ [[Addition from manuscripts R and A.]] etc.

It was also related by al-Nasa'i, al-Hakim and Ibn Mardawayh, through the narration of Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Shaqiq, with the same chain [[Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. (11112), and al-Mustadrak (2/307).]].

Asbat related from al-Suddi: "They had only prayer and zakat. So they asked God to prescribe fighting for them. But when fighting was prescribed for them: ﴿Behold, a faction of them fear people as they fear God or with even greater fear. And they say, 'Our Lord, why have You prescribed fighting for us? If only You had delayed us to a near term,'﴾ which is death. God, exalted is He, said: ﴿Say, "The enjoyment of this world is little, and the Hereafter is better for those who fear God."﴾

And from Mujahid: these verses were revealed concerning the Jews. Related by Ibn Jarir.

* *

His saying: ﴿Say, "The enjoyment of this world is little, and the Hereafter is better for those who fear God."﴾ That is, the Hereafter of the one who fears God is better than his worldly life.

﴿And you will not be wronged a thread﴾ That is, not in your deeds; rather, you will be paid their full reward. This is a consolation for them regarding the world, an encouragement for them toward the Hereafter, and an incitement for them to jihad.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: my father narrated to us; Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim al-Dawraqi narrated to us; Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us; Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to us, from Hisham, who said: al-Hasan recited: ﴿Say, "The enjoyment of this world is little,"﴾ and said: "May God have mercy on a servant who kept company with it according to its measure. The whole world, its first and its last, is only like a man who slept a nap, saw in his dream some of what he loves, and then woke up."

Ibn Ma'in said: Abu Muslihr used to recite:

"There is no good in this world for one who has no share
from God in the abode of permanence.
If the world impresses men,
it is little enjoyment, and its passing is near."

* *

His saying: ﴿Wherever you may be, death will overtake you, even if you should be in towers built up high.﴾ That is, you are certainly heading toward death, and none of you will escape it, as He said, exalted is He: ﴿Everyone upon it will perish, but there will remain the Face of your Lord, Owner of Majesty and Honor.﴾ [[Addition from manuscripts R and A; in H: "the verse".]] [Ar-Rahman: 26, 27]. He also said: ﴿Every soul will taste death﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 185], and He said: ﴿And We did not grant to any human before you eternal life﴾ [Al-Anbiya: 34]. The point is that everyone is certainly heading toward death, and nothing saves him from that, whether he fought in jihad or did not fight, for he has a determined term and an appointed time, as Khalid ibn al-Walid said when death came to him on his bed: "I have witnessed such-and-such a number of battles, and there is not a limb of mine without a wound from a spear or an arrow, and here I am dying on my bed. May the eyes of cowards never sleep!" [[Related by the hafiz Ibn Asakir in Tarikh Dimashq, as in al-Mukhtasar by Ibn al-Manzur (8/26), through the route of Abu al-Zinad that when Khalid's death approached he wept and said ... and he mentioned it.]]

* *

His saying: ﴿even if you should be in towers built up high﴾ That is, in strong, fortified, lofty and elevated fortresses. It was said that they are towers in the sky, as said by al-Suddi, but this is weak. The correct view is that they are fortresses; that is, caution and fortification do not avail against death, as Zuhayr ibn Abi Sulma said:

"Whoever fears the causes of death, it will reach him,
even if he tries to climb the causes of the sky with a ladder."

[[The verse is from the Mu'allaqah of Zuhayr ibn Abi Sulma, found in his Diwan (p. 30).]]

Then it was said: "al-Mushayyadah" is al-Mashidah, as in His saying: "and a lofty palace" [Al-Hajj: 45]. It was also said that there is a difference between them: al-Mushayyadah with the doubled letter means "prolonged," while without the doubling it means "adorned with shid," which is plaster.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim have mentioned here a lengthy account from Mujahid: that he mentioned a woman among those who came before us whom labor pains seized, so she commanded her hired man to bring her a fire. He went out and found a man standing at the door, who said: "What has the woman given birth to?" He said: "A girl." The man said: "Indeed, she will commit adultery with a hundred men, and then her hired man will marry her, and her death will be by a spider." He said: So he turned back, stabbed the girl in the belly with a knife, split it open, and then fled, thinking she had died. Her mother sewed up her belly, and she recovered, grew up and became the most beautiful woman in her land. That hired man went off to where he went and entered the seas, acquired great wealth, then returned to his land and wished to marry. He said to an old woman: "I want to marry the most beautiful woman in this land." She said to him: "There is no one more beautiful here than so-and-so." He said: "Propose her to me." She went to her, and she accepted, so he entered upon her and was greatly impressed by her. She asked him about his affair and where he had come from, so he told her his story and what had happened to him in his flight. She said: "I am the one." And she showed him the place of the knife. He became certain of it and said: "If you are indeed her, you have told me two things that must come to pass. One of them: that you have committed adultery with a hundred men." She said: "Something of that has happened, but I do not know how many they are." He said: "They are a hundred." And the second: "that you will die by a spider." So he built for her a strong, towering palace to protect her from that. One day they were there when suddenly a spider was on the ceiling. He showed it to her, and she said: "Is this the one you fear for me? By God, no one will kill it but me." So they brought it down from the ceiling, and she went to it and crushed it with the big toe of her foot, killing it. Some of its poison flew and lodged between her toenail and her flesh, so her foot turned black, and in that was her end [[Tafsir al-Tabari (8/552).]].

Here we will mention the story of the lord of al-Hadr, who was "al-Satirun," when Sabur tricked him until he besieged him in it, and killed those within it after a siege of two years. The Arabs said poems about that, among them:

"The lord of al-Hadr, when he built it, and when Dijlah
and al-Khabur were brought to him in tribute,
He built it of marble and covered it with plaster,
so birds have their nests on its heights.
The hands of death did not spare him, and kingship passed away from him,
and its gate is deserted."

When he entered upon Uthman, he began to say: "O God, unite the community of Muhammad." Then he recited the verse of the poet:

"I see death leaves no one mighty, and it has spared
for the people of 'Ad no refuge or dwelling in the lands.
The people of the fortress are attacked at night while the fortress is locked,
and it reaches the mountains together with their peaks."
[[In manuscript R: "the heights".]]

* *

His saying: ﴿And if good befalls them﴾ That is, fertility and provision from fruits, crops, children and the like. This is the meaning of the words of Ibn Abbas, Abu al-Aliyah and al-Suddi: ﴿they say, "This is from God." But if evil befalls them﴾ That is, drought, famine, loss in fruits and crops, or the death of children, offspring or other things, as Abu al-Aliyah and al-Suddi said. ﴿they say, "This is from you."﴾ That is, from your side, and because of our following you and our adherence to your religion. As He said, exalted is He, concerning the people of Pharaoh: ﴿But when good came to them, they said, "This is ours." And if evil befell them, they ascribed bad omen to Musa and those with him﴾ [Al-A'raf: 131]. And as He said: ﴿And among people is one who worships God on an edge. If good befalls him, he is content with it; but if a trial strikes him, he turns back on his face. He has lost this world and the Hereafter﴾ [Al-Hajj: 11]. Likewise these hypocrites said, who entered Islam outwardly while in reality they disliked it. Therefore, when evil befalls them, they attribute it to their following of the Prophet (ﷺ).

Al-Suddi said: ﴿And if good befalls them﴾: "The good is fertility. Their horses, livestock and herds bring forth young, their condition improves, and their women bear boys. They say: ﴿This is from God.﴾ But if evil befalls them﴾: "The evil is drought and harm to their wealth. They considered Muhammad (ﷺ) a bad omen and said: ﴿This is from you.﴾ They say: 'Because we abandoned our religion and followed Muhammad, this calamity has struck us.'" So God, mighty and majestic, revealed: ﴿Say, "All is from God."﴾ So His saying ﴿Say, "All is from God"﴾ means that everything is by the decree and destiny of God, and it takes effect upon the righteous and the wicked, the believer and the disbeliever.

Ali ibn Abi Talhah said, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿Say, "All is from God"﴾ means: the good and the evil. Likewise said al-Hasan al-Basri.

Then God, exalted is He, said, rebuking those who spoke this statement which proceeds from doubt and uncertainty, and from little understanding and knowledge, and much ignorance and wrongdoing: ﴿So what is wrong with these people that they can hardly understand any statement?﴾

Mention of a strange hadith related to His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say, "All is from God."﴾

The Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said: Al-Sakan ibn Sa'id narrated to us, 'Umar ibn Yunus narrated to us, Isma'il ibn Hammad narrated to us, from Muqatil ibn Hayyan, from 'Amr ibn Shu'ayb, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: "We were sitting with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), when Abu Bakr and 'Umar came along with two groups of people, and their voices had risen. Abu Bakr sat close to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and 'Umar sat close to Abu Bakr. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Why have your voices risen?' A man said: 'O Messenger of Allah...' Abu Bakr said: 'The good deeds are from Allah and the evil deeds are from ourselves.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'What did you say, O 'Umar?' He said: 'I said: The good deeds and the evil deeds are from Allah, Exalted is He.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'The first to speak about this were Jibril and Mika'il. Mika'il said your statement, O Abu Bakr, and Jibril said your statement, O 'Umar. He said: We differ, so the people of the heavens differ, and if the people of the heavens differ, the people of the earth will differ. They referred their dispute to Israfil, and he judged between them that the good deeds and the evil deeds are from Allah.'" Then he turned to Abu Bakr and 'Umar and said: "Memorise my judgment between you both: Had Allah wished that He not be disobeyed, He would not have created Iblis."

Shaykh al-Islam Taqi al-Din Abu al-'Abbas Ibn Taymiyyah said: This is a fabricated (mawdu') hadith, agreed upon by the people of knowledge. [The hadith is in Musnad al-Bazzar, no. (2496). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (7/191): "The Sheikh of al-Bazzar, al-Sakan ibn Sa'id, I do not know him, and the rest of al-Bazzar's narrators are trustworthy, with some remarks about some of them that do not harm." Ibn Hajar, may Allah have mercy on him, said: "This report is munkar, and there is weakness in its chain."]

Then Allah, the Exalted, said, addressing the Messenger [(ﷺ)] (the intended meaning being the human species, so that the answer is complete): ﴿Whatever good befalls you is from Allah, and whatever evil befalls you is from yourself﴾, i.e., from the bounty, favour, kindness and mercy of Allah; and ﴿whatever evil befalls you is from yourself﴾, i.e., it is from your own side and from your own deeds, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And whatever disaster strikes you, it is because of what your hands have earned, and He pardons much﴾ [Ash-Shura: 30].

Al-Suddi, al-Hasan al-Basri, Ibn Jurayj and Ibn Zayd said: ﴿from yourself﴾ means: because of your sin.

Qatadah said: ﴿Whatever good befalls you is from Allah, and whatever evil befalls you is from yourself﴾: it is a punishment, O son of Adam, for your sin. He said: It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) used to say: "No scratch from a stick, no stumble of a foot, and no twitch of a vein befalls a man except because of a sin, and what Allah pardons is greater."

This which Qatadah transmitted without a chain (mursal) has been related with a connected chain in the Sahih: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, no distress, sorrow or fatigue afflicts a believer, not even a thorn that pricks him, but Allah expiates some of his sins by it." [Related by Muslim in similar wording, no. (2572), from the hadith of 'A'ishah, and no. (2573), from the hadith of Abu Sa'id and Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with them.]

Abu Salih said: ﴿Whatever good befalls you is from Allah, and whatever evil befalls you is from yourself﴾, i.e., because of your sin, and I am the One who decreed it for you. Narrated by Ibn Jarir.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn 'Ammar narrated to us, Sahl (meaning Ibn Bakkar) narrated to us, al-Aswad ibn Shayban narrated to us, 'Uqbah ibn Wasil ibn Akhi Mutarrif narrated to me, from Mutarrif ibn 'Abdullah, who said: "What do you want from qadar? Does not the verse in Surah an-Nisa suffice you: ﴿And if good befalls them, they say, 'This is from Allah,' and if evil befalls them, they say, 'This is from you﴾", i.e., from yourself. By Allah, they were not left to qadar, and they were commanded, and to Him they will return.

This is a firm and strong statement in refutation of the Qadariyyah and also the Jabriyyah, and its elaboration has another place.

* *

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And We have sent you to mankind as a Messenger﴾, i.e., conveying to them the laws of Allah, what He loves and is pleased with, and what He dislikes and rejects.

﴿And sufficient is Allah as Witness﴾, i.e., as a witness that He sent you, and He is also a witness between you and them, and knowing of what you convey to them, and of what they return to you of rejection, out of disbelief and obstinacy.

The Muslims, while they were in Makkah at the beginning of Islam, were commanded to pray and to give zakat, though zakat was not yet obligatory with its prescribed rates. They were commanded to share with the poor among them, and they were commanded to pardon and forgive the polytheists and to be patient until a set time. They were eager and wished they had been commanded to fight, so that they could vent their anger on their enemies. But the situation was not suitable for that at the time, for many reasons. Among them: their number was small compared with the large number of their enemies. Another reason was that they were in their own land, which is a sacred land and the most noble place on earth, so it was not fitting to begin with an order to fight there. For this reason they were not commanded to wage jihad (struggle in the way of God) until they were in Madinah, once they had a home, a stronghold and helpers. Even so, when they were commanded to do what they had wished for, some of them recoiled from it and feared confronting the people with a great fear. ﴿They said, "Our Lord, why have You prescribed fighting for us? If only You had delayed us to a near term."﴾ That is, "If only You had not postponed its obligation to another time," for in it is the shedding of blood, the orphaning of children and the widowing of women. This verse has the same meaning as His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And those who believe say, "If only a surah were sent down." But when a decisive surah is sent down in which fighting is mentioned, you see those in whose hearts is a disease looking at you with the look of one fainting from death. So woe to them. Obedience and honorable speech would have been better for them. And when the matter is resolved, if they had been true to God, it would have been better for them.﴾ [Muhammad: 20, 21]. [[Addition from manuscript R. In manuscript H: "the verse".]]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated to us; Muhammad ibn Abd al-Aziz ibn Abi Rizmah [[In manuscript A: "Zar'ah".]] and Ali ibn Zinjah narrated to us, both saying: Ali ibn al-Hasan narrated to us, from al-Husayn ibn Waqid, from Amr ibn Dinar, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas: that Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf and some companions of his came to the Prophet (ﷺ) in Makkah and said: "O Prophet of God, we were in honor while we were polytheists, but when we believed we became humiliated." He said: "I have been commanded to pardon, so do not fight the people." When God transferred him to Madinah, He commanded him to fight, but they held back. So God revealed: ﴿Have you not seen those who were told, "Hold back your hands, and establish prayer and give zakat"? But when fighting was prescribed for them, behold, a faction of them fear people as they fear God or with even greater fear.﴾ [[Addition from manuscripts R and A.]] etc.

It was also related by al-Nasa'i, al-Hakim and Ibn Mardawayh, through the narration of Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Shaqiq, with the same chain [[Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. (11112), and al-Mustadrak (2/307).]].

Asbat related from al-Suddi: "They had only prayer and zakat. So they asked God to prescribe fighting for them. But when fighting was prescribed for them: ﴿Behold, a faction of them fear people as they fear God or with even greater fear. And they say, 'Our Lord, why have You prescribed fighting for us? If only You had delayed us to a near term,'﴾ which is death. God, exalted is He, said: ﴿Say, "The enjoyment of this world is little, and the Hereafter is better for those who fear God."﴾

And from Mujahid: these verses were revealed concerning the Jews. Related by Ibn Jarir.

* *

His saying: ﴿Say, "The enjoyment of this world is little, and the Hereafter is better for those who fear God."﴾ That is, the Hereafter of the one who fears God is better than his worldly life.

﴿And you will not be wronged a thread﴾ That is, not in your deeds; rather, you will be paid their full reward. This is a consolation for them regarding the world, an encouragement for them toward the Hereafter, and an incitement for them to jihad.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: my father narrated to us; Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim al-Dawraqi narrated to us; Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us; Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to us, from Hisham, who said: al-Hasan recited: ﴿Say, "The enjoyment of this world is little,"﴾ and said: "May God have mercy on a servant who kept company with it according to its measure. The whole world, its first and its last, is only like a man who slept a nap, saw in his dream some of what he loves, and then woke up."

Ibn Ma'in said: Abu Muslihr used to recite:

"There is no good in this world for one who has no share
from God in the abode of permanence.
If the world impresses men,
it is little enjoyment, and its passing is near."

* *

His saying: ﴿Wherever you may be, death will overtake you, even if you should be in towers built up high.﴾ That is, you are certainly heading toward death, and none of you will escape it, as He said, exalted is He: ﴿Everyone upon it will perish, but there will remain the Face of your Lord, Owner of Majesty and Honor.﴾ [[Addition from manuscripts R and A; in H: "the verse".]] [Ar-Rahman: 26, 27]. He also said: ﴿Every soul will taste death﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 185], and He said: ﴿And We did not grant to any human before you eternal life﴾ [Al-Anbiya: 34]. The point is that everyone is certainly heading toward death, and nothing saves him from that, whether he fought in jihad or did not fight, for he has a determined term and an appointed time, as Khalid ibn al-Walid said when death came to him on his bed: "I have witnessed such-and-such a number of battles, and there is not a limb of mine without a wound from a spear or an arrow, and here I am dying on my bed. May the eyes of cowards never sleep!" [[Related by the hafiz Ibn Asakir in Tarikh Dimashq, as in al-Mukhtasar by Ibn al-Manzur (8/26), through the route of Abu al-Zinad that when Khalid's death approached he wept and said ... and he mentioned it.]]

* *

His saying: ﴿even if you should be in towers built up high﴾ That is, in strong, fortified, lofty and elevated fortresses. It was said that they are towers in the sky, as said by al-Suddi, but this is weak. The correct view is that they are fortresses; that is, caution and fortification do not avail against death, as Zuhayr ibn Abi Sulma said:

"Whoever fears the causes of death, it will reach him,
even if he tries to climb the causes of the sky with a ladder."

[[The verse is from the Mu'allaqah of Zuhayr ibn Abi Sulma, found in his Diwan (p. 30).]]

Then it was said: "al-Mushayyadah" is al-Mashidah, as in His saying: "and a lofty palace" [Al-Hajj: 45]. It was also said that there is a difference between them: al-Mushayyadah with the doubled letter means "prolonged," while without the doubling it means "adorned with shid," which is plaster.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim have mentioned here a lengthy account from Mujahid: that he mentioned a woman among those who came before us whom labor pains seized, so she commanded her hired man to bring her a fire. He went out and found a man standing at the door, who said: "What has the woman given birth to?" He said: "A girl." The man said: "Indeed, she will commit adultery with a hundred men, and then her hired man will marry her, and her death will be by a spider." He said: So he turned back, stabbed the girl in the belly with a knife, split it open, and then fled, thinking she had died. Her mother sewed up her belly, and she recovered, grew up and became the most beautiful woman in her land. That hired man went off to where he went and entered the seas, acquired great wealth, then returned to his land and wished to marry. He said to an old woman: "I want to marry the most beautiful woman in this land." She said to him: "There is no one more beautiful here than so-and-so." He said: "Propose her to me." She went to her, and she accepted, so he entered upon her and was greatly impressed by her. She asked him about his affair and where he had come from, so he told her his story and what had happened to him in his flight. She said: "I am the one." And she showed him the place of the knife. He became certain of it and said: "If you are indeed her, you have told me two things that must come to pass. One of them: that you have committed adultery with a hundred men." She said: "Something of that has happened, but I do not know how many they are." He said: "They are a hundred." And the second: "that you will die by a spider." So he built for her a strong, towering palace to protect her from that. One day they were there when suddenly a spider was on the ceiling. He showed it to her, and she said: "Is this the one you fear for me? By God, no one will kill it but me." So they brought it down from the ceiling, and she went to it and crushed it with the big toe of her foot, killing it. Some of its poison flew and lodged between her toenail and her flesh, so her foot turned black, and in that was her end [[Tafsir al-Tabari (8/552).]].

Here we will mention the story of the lord of al-Hadr, who was "al-Satirun," when Sabur tricked him until he besieged him in it, and killed those within it after a siege of two years. The Arabs said poems about that, among them:

"The lord of al-Hadr, when he built it, and when Dijlah
and al-Khabur were brought to him in tribute,
He built it of marble and covered it with plaster,
so birds have their nests on its heights.
The hands of death did not spare him, and kingship passed away from him,
and its gate is deserted."

When he entered upon Uthman, he began to say: "O God, unite the community of Muhammad." Then he recited the verse of the poet:

"I see death leaves no one mighty, and it has spared
for the people of 'Ad no refuge or dwelling in the lands.
The people of the fortress are attacked at night while the fortress is locked,
and it reaches the mountains together with their peaks."
[[In manuscript R: "the heights".]]

* *

His saying: ﴿And if good befalls them﴾ That is, fertility and provision from fruits, crops, children and the like. This is the meaning of the words of Ibn Abbas, Abu al-Aliyah and al-Suddi: ﴿they say, "This is from God." But if evil befalls them﴾ That is, drought, famine, loss in fruits and crops, or the death of children, offspring or other things, as Abu al-Aliyah and al-Suddi said. ﴿they say, "This is from you."﴾ That is, from your side, and because of our following you and our adherence to your religion. As He said, exalted is He, concerning the people of Pharaoh: ﴿But when good came to them, they said, "This is ours." And if evil befell them, they ascribed bad omen to Musa and those with him﴾ [Al-A'raf: 131]. And as He said: ﴿And among people is one who worships God on an edge. If good befalls him, he is content with it; but if a trial strikes him, he turns back on his face. He has lost this world and the Hereafter﴾ [Al-Hajj: 11]. Likewise these hypocrites said, who entered Islam outwardly while in reality they disliked it. Therefore, when evil befalls them, they attribute it to their following of the Prophet (ﷺ).

Al-Suddi said: ﴿And if good befalls them﴾: "The good is fertility. Their horses, livestock and herds bring forth young, their condition improves, and their women bear boys. They say: ﴿This is from God.﴾ But if evil befalls them﴾: "The evil is drought and harm to their wealth. They considered Muhammad (ﷺ) a bad omen and said: ﴿This is from you.﴾ They say: 'Because we abandoned our religion and followed Muhammad, this calamity has struck us.'" So God, mighty and majestic, revealed: ﴿Say, "All is from God."﴾ So His saying ﴿Say, "All is from God"﴾ means that everything is by the decree and destiny of God, and it takes effect upon the righteous and the wicked, the believer and the disbeliever.

Ali ibn Abi Talhah said, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿Say, "All is from God"﴾ means: the good and the evil. Likewise said al-Hasan al-Basri.

Then God, exalted is He, said, rebuking those who spoke this statement which proceeds from doubt and uncertainty, and from little understanding and knowledge, and much ignorance and wrongdoing: ﴿So what is wrong with these people that they can hardly understand any statement?﴾

Mention of a strange hadith related to His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say, "All is from God."﴾

The Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said: Al-Sakan ibn Sa'id narrated to us, 'Umar ibn Yunus narrated to us, Isma'il ibn Hammad narrated to us, from Muqatil ibn Hayyan, from 'Amr ibn Shu'ayb, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: "We were sitting with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), when Abu Bakr and 'Umar came along with two groups of people, and their voices had risen. Abu Bakr sat close to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and 'Umar sat close to Abu Bakr. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Why have your voices risen?' A man said: 'O Messenger of Allah...' Abu Bakr said: 'The good deeds are from Allah and the evil deeds are from ourselves.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'What did you say, O 'Umar?' He said: 'I said: The good deeds and the evil deeds are from Allah, Exalted is He.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'The first to speak about this were Jibril and Mika'il. Mika'il said your statement, O Abu Bakr, and Jibril said your statement, O 'Umar. He said: We differ, so the people of the heavens differ, and if the people of the heavens differ, the people of the earth will differ. They referred their dispute to Israfil, and he judged between them that the good deeds and the evil deeds are from Allah.'" Then he turned to Abu Bakr and 'Umar and said: "Memorise my judgment between you both: Had Allah wished that He not be disobeyed, He would not have created Iblis."

Shaykh al-Islam Taqi al-Din Abu al-'Abbas Ibn Taymiyyah said: This is a fabricated (mawdu') hadith, agreed upon by the people of knowledge. [The hadith is in Musnad al-Bazzar, no. (2496). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (7/191): "The Sheikh of al-Bazzar, al-Sakan ibn Sa'id, I do not know him, and the rest of al-Bazzar's narrators are trustworthy, with some remarks about some of them that do not harm." Ibn Hajar, may Allah have mercy on him, said: "This report is munkar, and there is weakness in its chain."]

Then Allah, the Exalted, said, addressing the Messenger [(ﷺ)] (the intended meaning being the human species, so that the answer is complete): ﴿Whatever good befalls you is from Allah, and whatever evil befalls you is from yourself﴾, i.e., from the bounty, favour, kindness and mercy of Allah; and ﴿whatever evil befalls you is from yourself﴾, i.e., it is from your own side and from your own deeds, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And whatever disaster strikes you, it is because of what your hands have earned, and He pardons much﴾ [Ash-Shura: 30].

Al-Suddi, al-Hasan al-Basri, Ibn Jurayj and Ibn Zayd said: ﴿from yourself﴾ means: because of your sin.

Qatadah said: ﴿Whatever good befalls you is from Allah, and whatever evil befalls you is from yourself﴾: it is a punishment, O son of Adam, for your sin. He said: It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) used to say: "No scratch from a stick, no stumble of a foot, and no twitch of a vein befalls a man except because of a sin, and what Allah pardons is greater."

This which Qatadah transmitted without a chain (mursal) has been related with a connected chain in the Sahih: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, no distress, sorrow or fatigue afflicts a believer, not even a thorn that pricks him, but Allah expiates some of his sins by it." [Related by Muslim in similar wording, no. (2572), from the hadith of 'A'ishah, and no. (2573), from the hadith of Abu Sa'id and Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with them.]

Abu Salih said: ﴿Whatever good befalls you is from Allah, and whatever evil befalls you is from yourself﴾, i.e., because of your sin, and I am the One who decreed it for you. Narrated by Ibn Jarir.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn 'Ammar narrated to us, Sahl (meaning Ibn Bakkar) narrated to us, al-Aswad ibn Shayban narrated to us, 'Uqbah ibn Wasil ibn Akhi Mutarrif narrated to me, from Mutarrif ibn 'Abdullah, who said: "What do you want from qadar? Does not the verse in Surah an-Nisa suffice you: ﴿And if good befalls them, they say, 'This is from Allah,' and if evil befalls them, they say, 'This is from you﴾", i.e., from yourself. By Allah, they were not left to qadar, and they were commanded, and to Him they will return.

This is a firm and strong statement in refutation of the Qadariyyah and also the Jabriyyah, and its elaboration has another place.

* *

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And We have sent you to mankind as a Messenger﴾, i.e., conveying to them the laws of Allah, what He loves and is pleased with, and what He dislikes and rejects.

﴿And sufficient is Allah as Witness﴾, i.e., as a witness that He sent you, and He is also a witness between you and them, and knowing of what you convey to them, and of what they return to you of rejection, out of disbelief and obstinacy.

Ibn Kathir's commentary on Surah 4, verses 80–81:

Allah, the Exalted, informs about His servant and Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ) that whoever obeys him has obeyed Allah, and whoever disobeys him has disobeyed Allah. That is only because he does not speak from desire; it is nothing but a revelation that is revealed.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn Sinan narrated to us, Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever obeys me has obeyed Allah, and whoever disobeys me has disobeyed Allah. Whoever obeys the commander has obeyed me, and whoever disobeys the commander has disobeyed me."

This hadith is established in both Sahihs (al-Bukhari and Muslim), from al-A'mash with this chain. [[Narrated by al-Bukhari, no. (7137), and Muslim, no. (1835), through the route of Yunus ibn Yazid, from al-Zuhri, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah with it.]]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And whoever turns away, We have not sent you as a guardian over them﴾, meaning: you are not responsible for him. Your duty is only to convey the message. Whoever follows you will be happy and saved, and you will receive a reward equal to what he attains. Whoever turns away from you will be ruined and lose, and you bear no responsibility for his affair, as came in the hadith: "Whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger has been guided aright, and whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger, indeed he harms only himself." [[Narrated by Muslim in his Sahih, no. (87), from the hadith of 'Adi ibn Hatim, may Allah be pleased with him.]]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And they say, "Obedience"﴾, Allah, the Exalted, informs about the hypocrites that they display agreement and obedience. ﴿But when they leave your presence﴾, meaning: they go out and withdraw from you, ﴿a faction of them plans by night other than what you say﴾, meaning: they secretly conspire at night among themselves, contrary to what they had displayed. Then Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And Allah records what they plan by night﴾, meaning: He knows it and records it against them, through the guardian angels (al-hafazah al-katibin) who are appointed over the servants and who know what they do. The meaning of this threat is that He, the Exalted, informs that He knows what they conceal and hide among themselves, and what they agree upon at night of opposing and disobeying the Messenger, even though they had shown him obedience and agreement, and He will repay them for that. As Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And they say, "We believe in Allah and the Messenger and we obey"; then a faction of them turn away after that. And those are not believers﴾ [An-Nur: 47].

* *

As for His saying: ﴿So turn away from them﴾, meaning: pardon them, bear patiently with them, do not take them to account, do not expose their affairs to the people, and do not fear them either. ﴿And rely upon Allah; and sufficient is Allah as Disposer of affairs﴾, meaning: sufficient is He as a Protector, Helper and Supporter for whoever relies upon Him and turns to Him.

Allah, the Exalted, informs about His servant and Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ) that whoever obeys him has obeyed Allah, and whoever disobeys him has disobeyed Allah. That is only because he does not speak from desire; it is nothing but a revelation that is revealed.

Whoever obeys the commander has obeyed me, and whoever disobeys the commander has disobeyed me."

Allah the Exalted says, commanding His servants to reflect upon the Qur'an and forbidding them to turn away from it and from understanding its meanings, which are clear and firm, and its eloquent words. He informs them that there is no discrepancy in it, no disorder, no contradiction and no conflict, because it is a revelation from the All-Wise, the Praiseworthy. So it is truth from truth. For this reason Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Do they not reflect upon the Qur'an, or are there locks upon their hearts?﴾ [Muhammad: 24]. Then He said: ﴿And if it had been from other than Allah﴾, meaning, if it were fabricated and invented, as those ignorant polytheists and hypocrites say in their inner selves, ﴿they would have found in it much discrepancy﴾, meaning, much disorder and contradiction. That is, since this is free from discrepancy, it is from Allah. As Allah the Exalted said, reporting about those firmly grounded in knowledge when they said: ﴿We believe in it; all is from our Lord﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 7], meaning its firm verses and its ambiguous verses are all true. Therefore they referred the ambiguous to the firm and were guided, while those in whose hearts is deviation referred the firm to the ambiguous and went astray. For this reason Allah the Exalted praised the firmly grounded and censured the deviators.

Imam Ahmad said: Anas ibn 'Iyad narrated to us, Abu Hazim narrated to us, from 'Amr ibn Shu'ayb, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: "I sat with my brother in a gathering that I would not wish to exchange for red camels. My brother and I came, and there were elders from the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at one of the doors, so we disliked separating them, and we sat in a corner. Then they mentioned a verse of the Qur'an and disputed about it until their voices rose. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came out angry, until his face turned red, throwing dust at them and saying: 'Slowly, O people! By this, the nations before you were destroyed, through their disagreement with their prophets and their striking the Scriptures against one another. The Qur'an was not revealed for one part of it to deny another part; rather, one part of it confirms another. So what you know of it, act upon, and what you do not know of it, refer it to its knowledgeable one.'"

It was also narrated by him from Abu Mu'awiyah, from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from 'Amr ibn Shu'ayb, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out one day while the people were speaking about divine decree, and it was as if pomegranate seeds were being squeezed out of his face from anger. He said to them: "What is the matter with you, striking the Book of Allah, one part against another? By this, those before you were destroyed." He said: "I never envied myself for a gathering in which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was present and I was not present, as I envied myself for that gathering, that I had not witnessed it."

Ibn Majah narrated it from the hadith of Dawud ibn Abi Hind, similarly.

Ahmad also said: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us, Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to us, from Abu 'Imran al-Jawni, who said: 'Abdullah ibn Rabah wrote to me, narrating from 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr, who said: "I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ one day, and while we were sitting, two men disagreed about a verse, and their voices rose. He said: 'The nations before you were destroyed only through their disagreement about the Book.'" Muslim and al-Nasa'i also narrated it, from the hadith of Hammad ibn Zayd, similarly.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And when a matter comes to them concerning security or fear, they spread it around﴾, it is a rebuke of one who hastens to matters before their verification, so he reports them, spreads them and publicizes them, though they may have no validity.

Muslim said in the "Introduction to his Sahih": Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, 'Ali ibn Hafs narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Khubayb ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from Hafs ibn 'Asim, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "It is sufficient lying for a person that he narrates everything he hears." Abu Dawud also narrated it in the "Book of Etiquette" of his Sunan, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Ishkab, from 'Ali ibn Hafs, from Shu'bah, as a musnad hadith. Muslim also narrated it from the hadith of Mu'adh ibn Hisham al-'Anbari and 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi. Abu Dawud also narrated it from the hadith of Hafs ibn 'Umar al-Namari; all three narrated from Shu'bah, from Khubayb, from Hafs ibn 'Asim, as a mursal hadith.

In the two Sahihs, from al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade "qil wa qal" (qil wa qal: idle talk, saying "he said, she said"), meaning one who excessively narrates what people say without verification, reflection or clarification.

In Sunan Abi Dawud, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Evil is the mount of a man: they claim things about him."

In the Sahih: "Whoever narrates a hadith while he sees that it is a lie, then he is one of the two liars." [Narrated by Muslim in the introduction to his Sahih (p. 9) and al-Tirmidhi in his Sunan (no. 2662) from the hadith of al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah, may Allah be pleased with him.]

Here is mentioned the agreed-upon hadith of 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, when it reached him that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had divorced his wives. He came from his home until he entered the mosque and found people saying that. He could not be patient until he sought permission to enter upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and asked him: "Have you divorced your wives?" He said: "No." So I said: "Allahu Akbar!" and he mentioned the hadith at length.

In Muslim's version: I said: "Have you divorced them?" He said: "No." So I stood at the door of the mosque and called out at the top of my voice: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ has not divorced his wives." And this verse was revealed: ﴿And when a matter comes to them concerning security or fear, they spread it around. But if they had referred it to the Messenger and to those charged with authority among them, those who infer it among them would have known it﴾. So I was the one who inferred that matter.

The meaning of His saying "yastanbitunahu" (those who infer it): that is, they extract it and seek to know it from its sources. It is said: "istanbata al-rajul al-'ayn" (the man extracted the spring), when he dug it and drew it out from its depths.

As for His saying: ﴿You would have followed Satan, except for a few﴾, 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that it means the believers.

'Abd al-Razzaq narrated from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿except for a few﴾ means: all of you. He cited in support of this view the verse of al-Tirmah ibn Hakim, praising Yazid ibn al-Muhallab:

"Noble, abundant in the hands of giving, few in blame and reproach."

That is, he has no blame, and no reproach against him.
