It was also narrated by him from Abu Mu'awiyah, from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from 'Amr ibn Shu'ayb, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out one day while the people were speaking about divine decree, and it was as if pomegranate seeds were being squeezed out of his face from anger. He said to them: "What is the matter with you, striking the Book of Allah, one part against another? By this, those before you were destroyed." He said: "I never envied myself for a gathering in which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was present and I was not present, as I envied myself for that gathering, that I had not witnessed it."

Ibn Majah narrated it from the hadith of Dawud ibn Abi Hind, similarly.

Ahmad also said: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us, Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to us, from Abu 'Imran al-Jawni, who said: 'Abdullah ibn Rabah wrote to me, narrating from 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr, who said: "I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ one day, and while we were sitting, two men disagreed about a verse, and their voices rose. He said: 'The nations before you were destroyed only through their disagreement about the Book.'" Muslim and al-Nasa'i also narrated it, from the hadith of Hammad ibn Zayd, similarly.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And when a matter comes to them concerning security or fear, they spread it around﴾, it is a rebuke of one who hastens to matters before their verification, so he reports them, spreads them and publicizes them, though they may have no validity.

Muslim said in the "Introduction to his Sahih": Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, 'Ali ibn Hafs narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Khubayb ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from Hafs ibn 'Asim, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "It is sufficient lying for a person that he narrates everything he hears." Abu Dawud also narrated it in the "Book of Etiquette" of his Sunan, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Ishkab, from 'Ali ibn Hafs, from Shu'bah, as a musnad hadith. Muslim also narrated it from the hadith of Mu'adh ibn Hisham al-'Anbari and 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi. Abu Dawud also narrated it from the hadith of Hafs ibn 'Umar al-Namari; all three narrated from Shu'bah, from Khubayb, from Hafs ibn 'Asim, as a mursal hadith.

In the two Sahihs, from al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade "qil wa qal" (qil wa qal: idle talk, saying "he said, she said"), meaning one who excessively narrates what people say without verification, reflection or clarification.

In Sunan Abi Dawud, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Evil is the mount of a man: they claim things about him."

In the Sahih: "Whoever narrates a hadith while he sees that it is a lie, then he is one of the two liars." [Narrated by Muslim in the introduction to his Sahih (p. 9) and al-Tirmidhi in his Sunan (no. 2662) from the hadith of al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah, may Allah be pleased with him.]

Here is mentioned the agreed-upon hadith of 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, when it reached him that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had divorced his wives. He came from his home until he entered the mosque and found people saying that. He could not be patient until he sought permission to enter upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and asked him: "Have you divorced your wives?" He said: "No." So I said: "Allahu Akbar!" and he mentioned the hadith at length.

In Muslim's version: I said: "Have you divorced them?" He said: "No." So I stood at the door of the mosque and called out at the top of my voice: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ has not divorced his wives." And this verse was revealed: ﴿And when a matter comes to them concerning security or fear, they spread it around. But if they had referred it to the Messenger and to those charged with authority among them, those who infer it among them would have known it﴾. So I was the one who inferred that matter.

The meaning of His saying "yastanbitunahu" (those who infer it): that is, they extract it and seek to know it from its sources. It is said: "istanbata al-rajul al-'ayn" (the man extracted the spring), when he dug it and drew it out from its depths.

As for His saying: ﴿You would have followed Satan, except for a few﴾, 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that it means the believers.

'Abd al-Razzaq narrated from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿except for a few﴾ means: all of you. He cited in support of this view the verse of al-Tirmah ibn Hakim, praising Yazid ibn al-Muhallab:

"Noble, abundant in the hands of giving, few in blame and reproach."

That is, he has no blame, and no reproach against him.

Allah, Exalted is He, commands His servant and Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ) to engage in fighting personally, and whoever holds back, there is no burden on him for it; for this reason He said: ﴿You are not burdened except with yourself﴾.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Muhammad ibn 'Amr ibn Nubayh narrated to us, Hakkam narrated to us, al-Jarrah al-Kindi narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, who said: I asked al-Bara' ibn 'Azib about a man who meets a hundred of the enemy and fights them: is he among those of whom Allah says: ﴿And do not throw yourselves with your own hands into destruction﴾ [al-Baqarah: 195]? He said: Allah Almighty said to His Prophet (ﷺ): ﴿So fight in the way of Allah; you are not burdened except with yourself, and urge on the believers﴾.

Imam Ahmad also narrated it, from Sulayman ibn Dawud, from Abu Bakr ibn 'Ayyash, from Abu Ishaq, who said: I said to al-Bara': A man charges against the polytheists, is he among those who cast themselves with their own hands into destruction? He said: No, because Allah sent His Messenger (ﷺ) and said: ﴿So fight in the way of Allah; you are not burdened except with yourself﴾. That [prohibition] applies only to spending (wealth).

Likewise Ibn Mardawayh narrated it, through the chain of Abu Bakr ibn 'Ayyash and 'Ali ibn Salih, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Bara' with the same wording.

Then Ibn Mardawayh said: Sulayman ibn Ahmad narrated to us, Ahmad ibn al-Nadr al-'Askari narrated to us, Muslim ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Jarmi narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Himyar narrated to us, Sufyan al-Thawri narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Bara', who said: When this was revealed to the Prophet (ﷺ): ﴿So fight in the way of Allah; you are not burdened except with yourself, and urge on the believers [Perhaps Allah will restrain the might of those who disbelieve]﴾ — the verse — he said to his Companions: "My Lord has commanded me to fight, so fight." This is a gharib (unusual) hadith [Al-Suyuti mentioned it in al-Durr (2/602); its unusualness is that it is transmitted as a statement of al-Bara' from several routes, and it is not narrated as a marfu' (Prophetic) report except through this route].

* *

As for His words: ﴿and urge on the believers﴾, meaning: encourage them to fight, make them eager for it, and cheer them on in it, just as the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to them at Badr while he was straightening the rows: "Rise up to a Paradise whose breadth is the heavens and the earth."

Many hadiths have come concerning encouragement to this. Among them is what al-Bukhari narrated from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever believes in Allah and His Messenger, establishes the prayer, pays the zakat, and fasts Ramadan, it is a right upon Allah to admit him into Paradise, whether he emigrates in the way of Allah or sits in the land in which he was born." They said: O Messenger of Allah, shall we not inform the people of this? He said: "Indeed, in Paradise there are a hundred levels, which Allah has prepared for those who strive in the way of Allah; between each two levels is as the distance between the heaven and the earth. So when you ask Allah, ask Him for al-Firdaws, for it is the middle and highest part of Paradise, and above it is the Throne of the Most Merciful, and from it the rivers of Paradise gush forth" [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 2790].

It has been narrated with similar wording from the hadiths of Mu'adh, Abu al-Darda' and 'Ubadah.

And from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O Abu Sa'id, whoever is pleased with Allah as Lord, with Islam as religion, and with Muhammad as Prophet, Paradise is obligatory for him." Abu Sa'id marvelled at it and said: Repeat it to me, O Messenger of Allah. So he did. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "And another [deed], by which Allah raises the servant a hundred levels in Paradise, between each two levels is as the distance between the heaven and the earth." He said: What is it, O Messenger of Allah? He said: "Jihad in the way of Allah." Narrated by Muslim [Sahih Muslim, no. 1884].

* *

As for His words: ﴿Perhaps Allah will restrain the might of those who disbelieve﴾, meaning: by your urging them to fight, their resolves are roused to confront the enemies, to defend the territory of Islam and its people, and to resist and persevere against them.

* *

As for His words: ﴿And Allah is stronger in might and stronger in punishment﴾, meaning: He is capable of [punishing] them in this world and the Hereafter, as He said: ﴿That, and if Allah had willed, He could have taken revenge upon them, but [He wills] to test some of you by means of others. And those who are killed in the way of Allah — He will never waste their deeds﴾ [Muhammad: 4].

* *

As for His words: ﴿Whoever intercedes with a good intercession will have a share of it, and whoever intercedes with a bad intercession will bear a portion of it﴾, meaning: whoever strives in a matter from which good results, he will have a share of that; and whoever intercedes for an evil matter will bear a burden from that matter which results from his effort and intention, as is established in the Sahih that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Intercede, and you will be rewarded, and Allah decrees through the tongue of His Prophet what He wills."

Mujahid ibn Jabr said: This verse was revealed concerning the intercessions of people for one another.

Al-Hasan al-Basri said: Allah said ﴿yashfa'[ مَنْ يَشْفَعْ ]﴾ and did not say "yushaffa'".

* *

As for His words: ﴿And Allah is ever Controlling over all things﴾, Ibn 'Abbas, 'Ata', 'Atiyyah, Qatadah and Mattar al-Warraq said: ﴿Muqita﴾ means watchful (hafiz). Mujahid said: witness (shahid). In another report from him: reckoner (hasib). Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Suddi and Ibn Zayd said: capable (qadir). 'Abd Allah ibn Kathir said: al-Muqit is the one who is constant (al-wasib). al-Dahhak said: al-Muqit is the Provider (al-Razzaq).

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, 'Abd al-Rahim ibn Mutarrif narrated to us, 'Isa ibn Yunus narrated to us, from Isma'il, from a man, from 'Abd Allah ibn Rawahah, when a man asked him about the words of Allah: ﴿And Allah is ever Controlling over all things﴾, he said: He sustains every person according to the measure of his deeds.

* *

As for His words: ﴿When you are greeted with a greeting, greet with better than it or return it﴾, meaning: when a Muslim greets you, respond with something better than his greeting, or return it with the same as his greeting. The addition is recommended, while returning the equivalent is obligatory.

Ibn Jarir said: Musa ibn Sahl al-Ramli narrated to me, 'Abd Allah ibn al-Sarri al-Antaki narrated to us, Hisham ibn Lahiq narrated to us, from 'Asim al-Ahwal, from Abu 'Uthman al-Nahdi, from Salman al-Farisi, who said: A man came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "As-salamu 'alayka, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "Wa 'alayka as-salam wa rahmat Allah." Then another came and said: "As-salamu 'alayka, O Messenger of Allah, wa rahmat Allah." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: "Wa 'alayka as-salam wa rahmat Allah wa barakatuh." Then another came and said: "As-salamu 'alayka, O Messenger of Allah, wa rahmat Allah wa barakatuh," and he said to him: "Wa 'alayk." The man said to him: O Prophet of Allah, may my father and mother be your ransom, so-and-so and so-and-so came to you and greeted you, and you returned more to them than you returned to me. He said: "You have left nothing for us; Allah the Exalted said: ﴿When you are greeted with a greeting, greet with better than it or return it﴾, so we returned it to you."

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it in a suspended (mu'allaq) form in the same way, saying: It was mentioned from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Tirmidhi, 'Abd Allah ibn al-Sarri, Abu Muhammad al-Antaki — Abu al-Hasan said: he was a righteous man — narrated to us, Hisham ibn Lahiq narrated to us, and he mentioned its chain with the like of it.

Ibn Mardawayh narrated it: 'Abd al-Baqi ibn Qani' narrated to us, 'Abd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Hanbal narrated to us, my father narrated to us, Hisham ibn Lahiq Abu 'Uthman narrated to us, and he mentioned it with the like of it, but I did not find it in the Musnad [al-Tabari in his Tafsir (8/589); its chain includes 'Abd Allah ibn al-Sarri, of whom Abu Nu'aym said: "He narrates the munkar; he is nothing." Imam Ahmad said: "He raised reports from 'Asim which were not raised, attributing them to Salman."] And Allah knows best.

He returned his greeting, then he sat down. He said: "Ten [good deeds]." Then another came and said: "As-salamu 'alaykum wa rahmat Allah." He returned his greeting, then he sat down. He said: "Twenty." Then another came and said: "As-salamu 'alaykum wa rahmat Allah wa barakatuh." He returned his greeting, then he sat down. He said: "Thirty."

Abu Dawud narrated it likewise from Muhammad ibn Kathir, and al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i and al-Bazzar transmitted it from his hadith. Al-Tirmidhi then said: "Hasan gharib from this route; and on the subject there are reports from Abu Sa'id, 'Ali and Sahl ibn Hunayf [may Allah be pleased with them]."

Al-Bazzar said: This has been narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) through several routes; this is the best of them in chain.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: 'Ali ibn Harb al-Mawsili narrated to us, Humayd ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Ru'asi narrated to us, from al-Hasan ibn Salih, from Simak, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas who said: Whoever among Allah's creation greets you, return his greeting even if he is a Magian; that is because Allah says: ﴿so greet with better than it or return it﴾.

Qatadah said: ﴿so greet with better than it﴾ means: for Muslims; ﴿or return it﴾ means: for the People of the Covenant (dhimmis).

This interpretation is open to question; rather, as has preceded in the hadith, the intended meaning is to return with something better than what was given. If a Muslim reaches the furthest extent of what is prescribed in greeting, then one returns to him just what he said. As for the People of the Covenant, they are not to be greeted first with salam, nor is their greeting to be increased; rather, they are answered with what is established in the two Sahihs from Ibn 'Umar that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When the Jews greet you, one of them only says: 'As-sam 'alayka' (death upon you); so say: 'Wa 'alayka'" [narrated by al-Bukhari, no. 6257, and Muslim, no. 2164].

In Sahih Muslim, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Do not begin the Jews and Christians with salam, and when you meet them on a road, force them to its narrowest part" [Sahih Muslim, no. 2167].

Sufyan al-Thawri said, from a man, from al-Hasan al-Basri: "Greeting is voluntary (tatawwu'), and returning it is obligatory (fard)."

What he said is the statement of all the scholars: that returning the greeting is obligatory upon the one greeted, so he is sinful if he does not do it, for he has opposed Allah's command in His words: ﴿so greet with better than it or return it﴾. And there has come in the hadith which [Abu Dawud] narrated [blank in all copies; in one supporting copy: Abu Dawud with his chain to Abu Hurayrah who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, you will not enter Paradise until you believe, and you will not believe until you love one another. Shall I not direct you to something which, if you do it, you will love one another? Spread the greeting among you."]

* *

As for His words: ﴿Allah — there is no deity except Him﴾, it is a report of His oneness and His singularity in divinity over all creation, and it implies an oath, by His words: ﴿He will surely gather you to the Day of Resurrection, about which there is no doubt﴾. This lam is a preparatory lam for the oath. So His words: ﴿Allah — there is no deity except Him﴾ are a statement and an oath that He will surely gather the first and the last in one plain, and will recompense every doer for his deeds.

* *

Al-Bazzar said: This has been narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) through several routes; this is the best of them in chain.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: 'Ali ibn Harb al-Mawsili narrated to us, Humayd ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Ru'asi narrated to us, from al-Hasan ibn Salih, from Simak, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas who said: Whoever among Allah's creation greets you, return his greeting even if he is a Magian; that is because Allah says: ﴿so greet with better than it or return it﴾.

Qatadah said: ﴿so greet with better than it﴾ means: for Muslims; ﴿or return it﴾ means: for the People of the Covenant (dhimmis).

This interpretation is open to question; rather, as has preceded in the hadith, the intended meaning is to return with something better than what was given. If a Muslim reaches the furthest extent of what is prescribed in greeting, then one returns to him just what he said. As for the People of the Covenant, they are not to be greeted first with salam, nor is their greeting to be increased; rather, they are answered with what is established in the two Sahihs from Ibn 'Umar that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When the Jews greet you, one of them only says: 'As-sam 'alayka' (death upon you); so say: 'Wa 'alayka'" [narrated by al-Bukhari, no. 6257, and Muslim, no. 2164].

In Sahih Muslim, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Do not begin the Jews and Christians with salam, and when you meet them on a road, force them to its narrowest part" [Sahih Muslim, no. 2167].

Sufyan al-Thawri said, from a man, from al-Hasan al-Basri: "Greeting is voluntary (tatawwu'), and returning it is obligatory (fard)."

What he said is the statement of all the scholars: that returning the greeting is obligatory upon the one greeted, so he is sinful if he does not do it, for he has opposed Allah's command in His words: ﴿so greet with better than it or return it﴾. And there has come in the hadith which [Abu Dawud] narrated [blank in all copies; in one supporting copy: Abu Dawud with his chain to Abu Hurayrah who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, you will not enter Paradise until you believe, and you will not believe until you love one another. Shall I not direct you to something which, if you do it, you will love one another? Spread the greeting among you."]

* *

As for His words: ﴿Allah — there is no deity except Him﴾, it is a report of His oneness and His singularity in divinity over all creation, and it implies an oath, by His words: ﴿He will surely gather you to the Day of Resurrection, about which there is no doubt﴾. This lam is a preparatory lam for the oath. So His words: ﴿Allah — there is no deity except Him﴾ are a statement and an oath that He will surely gather the first and the last in one plain, and will recompense every doer for his deeds.

* *

As for His words, Exalted is He: ﴿And who is more truthful in statement than Allah?﴾, meaning: none is more truthful than Him in His speech and report, in His promise and threat. There is no deity except Him, and no lord besides Him.

He, exalted is He, says, rebuking the believers for their disagreement about the hypocrites, who were of two opinions. There is also disagreement over the cause of this. The Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) divided into two groups about them: one group said, "Let us kill them," and another group said, "No." So Allah revealed: ﴿So what is the matter with you that you have become two groups concerning the hypocrites?﴾ Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "It is Taybah (Medina), and it expels impurity as the fire expels the dross of silver."

Al-Bukhari and Muslim both recorded it in their Sahihs, from the narration of Shu'bah.

When the believers were told that they had left Mecca, a group of the believers said: "Ride out against those cowards and kill them, for they are supporting your enemy against you." Another group of the believers said: "Glory be to Allah! Or as they said: Will you kill people who have spoken the same words as you have spoken? Is it because they did not emigrate and did not leave their homes, that their blood and property are made lawful?" Thus they were two groups, while the Messenger was among them and did not forbid either of the two groups from anything. So Allah revealed: ﴿So what is the matter with you that you have become two groups concerning the hypocrites?﴾

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it. Similar reports have also been transmitted from Abu Salamah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, 'Ikrimah, Mujahid, al-Dahhak and others.

Zayd ibn Aslam said, from a son of Sa'd ibn Mu'adh: It was revealed concerning the dispute between the Aws and the Khazraj about 'Abdullah ibn Ubayy, when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) asked for his removal from the pulpit in the affair of the slander.

This is a strange report, and it has been said that it was other than this.

* *

His saying: ﴿And Allah has reverted them for what they earned﴾ means: He returned them and cast them into error.

Ibn 'Abbas said: ﴿arkasahum﴾ means He cast them down. Qatadah said: He destroyed them. Al-Suddi said: He led them astray.

* *

This is only because of the intensity of their enmity and hatred toward you. For this reason He said: ﴿So do not take from among them allies until they emigrate in the cause of Allah. But if they turn away﴾, that is, they refuse to emigrate, as al-'Awfi reported from Ibn 'Abbas. Al-Suddi said: they openly show their disbelief. ﴿Then seize them and kill them wherever you find them, and do not take from among them an ally or a helper﴾, that is, do not befriend them, and do not seek their support against the enemies while they remain in that state.

They are those who come to the battle lines while their hearts are constricted, that is, their hearts are narrowed, resentful of fighting you, and it is also not easy for them to fight their own people alongside you. Rather, they are neither with you nor against you. ﴿And if Allah had willed, He would have given them power over you, and they would have fought you﴾, that is, by His kindness toward you, He restrained them from you. ﴿So if they keep away from you and do not fight you and offer you peace﴾, that is, reconciliation, ﴿then Allah has not made for you a way against them﴾, that is, you have no right to kill them as long as their condition is like this. These are like the group of Banu Hashim who went out with the polytheists on the day of Badr, who attended the fighting while unwilling, such as al-'Abbas and others. For this reason the Prophet (ﷺ) forbade the killing of al-'Abbas that day and ordered his capture.

* *

His saying: ﴿You will find others who wish to be safe from you and safe from their own people [every time they are returned to disbelief, they are plunged back into it]﴾, and the verse continues: these people in their outward appearance are like those who preceded them, but their intention is different from theirs. These are hypocrites who show Islam to the Prophet (ﷺ) and his Companions so that they may be safe among them regarding their lives, property and offspring, while they flatter the disbelievers inwardly, worshipping with them what they worship, so that they may be safe among them. Inwardly they are with those others, as Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And when they meet those who believe, they say, "We believe"; but when they are alone with their devils, they say, "Indeed we are with you; we were only mocking."﴾ [al-Baqarah: 14]. Here He said: ﴿Every time they are returned to disbelief, they are plunged back into it﴾, that is, they immerse themselves in it.

Al-Suddi said: Here "fitnah" means polytheism. Ibn Jarir related from Mujahid that it was revealed concerning a people from Mecca who used to come to the Prophet (ﷺ) and greet him with Islam out of hypocrisy, then return to Quraysh and plunge into idol worship, seeking by that to be safe on both sides. So He commanded that they be fought if they did not keep away and make peace. For this reason He, exalted is He, said: ﴿So if they do not keep away from you and offer you peace and restrain their hands﴾, that is, from fighting, ﴿then seize them and kill them wherever you overtake them﴾, that is, wherever you encounter them, ﴿and those – We have made for you against them a clear authority﴾, that is, a manifest and evident one.

He, exalted is He, says, rebuking the believers for their disagreement about the hypocrites, who were of two opinions. There is also disagreement over the cause of this. Imam Ahmad said: Bahz narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, 'Adi ibn Thabit said: 'Abdullah ibn Yazid informed me, from Zayd ibn Thabit, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out to Uhud, and some people who had gone out with him turned back. The Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) divided into two groups about them: one group said, "Let us kill them," and another group said, "No." So Allah revealed: ﴿So what is the matter with you that you have become two groups concerning the hypocrites?﴾ Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "It is Taybah (Medina), and it expels impurity as the fire expels the dross of silver."

Al-Bukhari and Muslim both recorded it in their Sahihs, from the narration of Shu'bah.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar mentioned, regarding the battle of Uhud, that 'Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul turned back that day with a third of the army: he turned back with three hundred, and the Prophet (ﷺ) remained with seven hundred.

Al-'Awfi said, from Ibn 'Abbas: It was revealed concerning a people in Mecca who had professed Islam and were supporting the polytheists. They went out of Mecca seeking something they needed, and they said: "If we meet the companions of Muhammad, there is no harm for us from them." When the believers were told that they had left Mecca, a group of the believers said: "Ride out against those cowards and kill them, for they are supporting your enemy against you." Another group of the believers said: "Glory be to Allah! Or as they said: Will you kill people who have spoken the same words as you have spoken? Is it because they did not emigrate and did not leave their homes, that their blood and property are made lawful?" Thus they were two groups, while the Messenger was among them and did not forbid either of the two groups from anything. So Allah revealed: ﴿So what is the matter with you that you have become two groups concerning the hypocrites?﴾

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it. Similar reports have also been transmitted from Abu Salamah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, 'Ikrimah, Mujahid, al-Dahhak and others.

Zayd ibn Aslam said, from a son of Sa'd ibn Mu'adh: It was revealed concerning the dispute between the Aws and the Khazraj about 'Abdullah ibn Ubayy, when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) asked for his removal from the pulpit in the affair of the slander.

This is a strange report, and it has been said that it was other than this.

* *

His saying: ﴿And Allah has reverted them for what they earned﴾ means: He returned them and cast them into error.

Ibn 'Abbas said: ﴿arkasahum﴾ means He cast them down. Qatadah said: He destroyed them. Al-Suddi said: He led them astray.

* *

His saying: ﴿for what they earned﴾ means: because of their disobedience, their opposition to the Messenger, and their following of falsehood.

﴿Do you wish to guide those whom Allah has led astray? And whomever Allah leads astray, you will not find for him a way.﴾ That is, there is no path for him to guidance and no escape for him to it.

Then He said: ﴿They wish that you would disbelieve as they have disbelieved, and that you would be alike.﴾ That is, they wish for you to be misguided so that you and they would be equal in it. This is only because of the intensity of their enmity and hatred toward you. For this reason He said: ﴿So do not take from among them allies until they emigrate in the cause of Allah. But if they turn away﴾, that is, they refuse to emigrate, as al-'Awfi reported from Ibn 'Abbas. Al-Suddi said: they openly show their disbelief. ﴿Then seize them and kill them wherever you find them, and do not take from among them an ally or a helper﴾, that is, do not befriend them, and do not seek their support against the enemies while they remain in that state.

Then Allah, glorified is He, made an exception from these people, saying: ﴿except for those who reach a people between whom and you there is a covenant﴾, that is, except those who take refuge with and join a people between whom and you there is a truce or a covenant of protection (dhimmah); so their ruling is to be like the ruling for them. This is the view of al-Suddi, Ibn Zayd and Ibn Jarir.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated: My father narrated to us, Abu Salamah narrated to us, Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from 'Ali ibn Zayd ibn Jud'an, from al-Hasan: that Suraqah ibn Malik al-Mudlaji related to them, saying: When (the Prophet (ﷺ)) prevailed over the people of Badr and Uhud, and those around them embraced Islam, Suraqah said: It reached me that he intends to send Khalid ibn al-Walid to my people, Banu Mudlij. So I went to him and said: "I beseech you by the blessing." They said: "Hush!" But the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Leave him. What do you want?" He said: "It has reached me that you intend to send someone to my people, and I want you to make a truce with them. If your people embrace Islam, they will embrace it too, and if they do not embrace Islam, the hearts of your people will not be harsh against them." So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) took the hand of Khalid ibn al-Walid and said: "Go with him and do what he wants." So Khalid made a treaty with them that they would not help against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and if Quraysh embraced Islam, they would embrace it with them, [and whoever reached them among the people would be on the same covenant as they were]. Then Allah revealed: ﴿They wish that you would disbelieve as they have disbelieved, and that you would be alike; so do not take from among them allies﴾.

Ibn Mardawayh also narrated it through the route of Hammad ibn Salamah, and in it he said: Then Allah revealed: ﴿except those who reach a people between whom and you there is a covenant﴾, so whoever reached them was with them under their covenant. [Ibn Abi Shaybah narrated it in al-Musannaf (14/232): Aswad ibn 'Amir narrated to us from Hammad ibn Salamah with it.] This is more suitable to the context of the discourse.

In Sahih al-Bukhari, in the account of the Treaty of al-Hudaybiyyah, it is stated: Whoever wished to enter into the agreement and covenant of Quraysh could do so, and whoever wished to enter into the agreement and covenant of Muhammad and his Companions could do so.

It has been narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: It was abrogated by His saying: ﴿Then when the sacred months have passed, kill the polytheists [wherever you find them]﴾ [al-Tawbah: 5].

* *

His saying: ﴿Or those who come to you, their hearts constricted [about fighting you or fighting their own people]﴾, and the verse continues: these are another group among those excepted from the command to fight them. They are those who come to the battle lines while their hearts are constricted, that is, their hearts are narrowed, resentful of fighting you, and it is also not easy for them to fight their own people alongside you. Rather, they are neither with you nor against you. ﴿And if Allah had willed, He would have given them power over you, and they would have fought you﴾, that is, by His kindness toward you, He restrained them from you. ﴿So if they keep away from you and do not fight you and offer you peace﴾, that is, reconciliation, ﴿then Allah has not made for you a way against them﴾, that is, you have no right to kill them as long as their condition is like this. These are like the group of Banu Hashim who went out with the polytheists on the day of Badr, who attended the fighting while unwilling, such as al-'Abbas and others. For this reason the Prophet (ﷺ) forbade the killing of al-'Abbas that day and ordered his capture.

* *

His saying: ﴿You will find others who wish to be safe from you and safe from their own people [every time they are returned to disbelief, they are plunged back into it]﴾, and the verse continues: these people in their outward appearance are like those who preceded them, but their intention is different from theirs. These are hypocrites who show Islam to the Prophet (ﷺ) and his Companions so that they may be safe among them regarding their lives, property and offspring, while they flatter the disbelievers inwardly, worshipping with them what they worship, so that they may be safe among them. Inwardly they are with those others, as Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And when they meet those who believe, they say, "We believe"; but when they are alone with their devils, they say, "Indeed we are with you; we were only mocking."﴾ [al-Baqarah: 14]. Here He said: ﴿Every time they are returned to disbelief, they are plunged back into it﴾, that is, they immerse themselves in it.

Al-Suddi said: Here "fitnah" means polytheism. Ibn Jarir related from Mujahid that it was revealed concerning a people from Mecca who used to come to the Prophet (ﷺ) and greet him with Islam out of hypocrisy, then return to Quraysh and plunge into idol worship, seeking by that to be safe on both sides. So He commanded that they be fought if they did not keep away and make peace. For this reason He, exalted is He, said: ﴿So if they do not keep away from you and offer you peace and restrain their hands﴾, that is, from fighting, ﴿then seize them and kill them wherever you overtake them﴾, that is, wherever you encounter them, ﴿and those – We have made for you against them a clear authority﴾, that is, a manifest and evident one.

Allah says: It is not for a believer to kill another believer under any circumstances, as is established in the two Sahihs (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim) from Ibn Mas'ud that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The blood of a Muslim man who testifies that there is no god but Allah and that I am the Messenger of Allah may not be shed except in one of three cases: a life for a life, a married person who commits adultery, and one who abandons his religion and separates from the community" [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (6878), and Sahih Muslim, no. (1676).]].
Then, when any one of these three cases occurs, it is not for any individual among the subjects to kill him; rather, that is for the Imam (ruler) or his deputy.
* *
As for His saying: ﴿except by mistake﴾, they said: it is an exceptive clause of the disconnected type (istithna' munqati', where what follows is not of the same kind as what precedes), like the saying of the poet [[He is Jarir ibn 'Atiyya al-Ghatafani, and the verse is in Tafsir al-Tabari (9/31).]]:
"Of the white women, she did not travel far nor did she tread on the earth except on a striped, folded cloth of the finest garment."
There are many examples of this.
The commentators differed concerning the occasion of revelation of this verse. Mujahid and others said: it was revealed concerning 'Ayyash ibn Abi Rabi'ah, the brother of Abu Jahl through their mother, whose mother was Asma' bint Makhribah. He killed a man who was tormenting him, along with his brother, for Islam; this man was al-Harith ibn Yazid al-'Amiri. 'Ayyash harbored ill will toward him. That man then embraced Islam and migrated, while 'Ayyash was unaware. When the day of the Conquest came, he saw him and thought that he was still upon his former religion, so he charged at him and killed him. Then Allah revealed this verse [[Narrated by al-Tabari in his Tafsir (9/33).]].
'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: It was revealed concerning Abu al-Darda', because he killed a man who had uttered the word of Islam when he raised the sword over him; he swung the sword at him, and he had said his statement. When this was mentioned to the Prophet (ﷺ), he said: "He only said it seeking refuge." So he said to him: "Did you split open his heart?" [[Narrated by al-Tabari in his Tafsir (9/34).]] [This story is in the Sahih for someone other than Abu al-Darda'.]
* *
As for His saying: ﴿And whoever kills a believer by mistake, then the freeing of a believing slave and a compensation (diyah) delivered to his family [unless they forgo it as charity]﴾: these are two obligations for killing by mistake. The first is expiation (kaffarah) for the great sin he committed, even though it was a mistake. Among its conditions is that it must be the freeing of a believing slave; a disbeliever is not sufficient.
Ibn Jarir related from Ibn 'Abbas, al-Sha'bi, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i and al-Hasan al-Basri that they said: a child is not sufficient unless he intends belief. It is also narrated through 'Abd al-Razzaq from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, who said: in the reading of Ubayy, "freeing a believing slave" — a child is not sufficient in it.
Ibn Jarir chose that if he was born between two Muslim parents, it is sufficient, and otherwise not. What the majority hold is that whenever he is a Muslim, his manumission for expiation is valid, whether he is a child or an adult.
Imam Ahmad said: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd Allah, from a man of the Ansar: that he came with a black slave girl and said: "O Messenger of Allah, upon me is a believing slave; if you see this one as a believer, I will free her." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to her: "Do you testify that there is no god but Allah?" She said: "Yes." He said: "Do you testify that I am the Messenger of Allah?" She said: "Yes." He said: "Do you believe in resurrection after death?" She said: "Yes." He said: "Free her."
This is a sound chain, and the ignorance of the Companion does not harm it [[Al-Musnad (3/451).]].
In the Muwatta' of Imam Malik, the Musnads of al-Shafi'i and Ahmad, Sahih Muslim, and the Sunan of Abu Dawud and al-Nasa'i, through the route of Hilal ibn Abi Maymunah, from 'Ata' ibn Yasar, from Mu'awiyah ibn al-Hakam: when he brought that black slave girl, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to her: "Where is Allah?" She said: "In the heaven." He said: "Who am I?" She said: "You are the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)." He said: "Free her, for she is a believer" [[Al-Muwatta' (2/777), Musnad al-Shafi'i no. (1196), Bada'i' al-Minan, Musnad Ahmad (5/447), Sahih Muslim no. (537), Sunan Abi Dawud no. (2384), Sunan al-Nasa'i (3/14).]].
* *
As for His saying: ﴿and a compensation (diyah) delivered to his family﴾: this is the second obligation, owed between the killer and the family of the slain, as compensation to them for what they lost of their relative. This compensation is due in fifths (akhmas), as related by Imam Ahmad and the authors of the Sunan, from the hadith of al-Hajjaj ibn Arta'ah, from Zayd ibn Jubayr, from Khashf ibn Malik, from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) decreed for the compensation for manslaughter: twenty daughters of a year (bint makhad), twenty sons of a year (ibn makhad), twenty daughters of two years (bint labun), twenty male camels of four years (jadha'ah), and twenty of five years (hiqqah).
This is the wording of al-Nasa'i. Al-Tirmidhi said: we do not know it as marfu' except through this route, and it has been narrated from 'Abd Allah as a mawquf report [[Al-Musnad (1/384), Sunan al-Nasa'i (8/43), Sunan Abi Dawud no. (4545), Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (1386), Sunan Ibn Majah no. (2631).]].
Likewise, it has been narrated from ['Ali and] a group of people.
It was also said: it is due in quarters. This compensation is owed by the killer's paternal kin ('aqilah), not from his own property. Al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, said: I know of no dissent that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) decreed the compensation to be borne by the 'aqilah, and this is more widely reported than the hadith of the particular individual [[Al-Umm (6/101).]]. What he, may Allah have mercy on him, pointed to has been established in more than one hadith. Among that is what is established in the two Sahihs from Abu Hurayrah, who said: Two women of Hudhayl fought, and one of them struck the other with a stone, killing her and the child in her womb. They brought the dispute to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he decreed that the compensation for her fetus was a ghurrah, a male or female slave, and he decreed the compensation for the woman upon her 'aqilah [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (6910) and Sahih Muslim no. (1681).]].
This implies that the ruling for semi-intentional killing (amd al-khata') is the ruling for pure mistake regarding the obligation of compensation; however, in this case the compensation is due in thirds, like intentional killing, because of its resemblance to it.
In Sahih al-Bukhari, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent Khalid ibn al-Walid to the Banu Judhaymah, and he invited them to Islam, but they did not properly say, "We have embraced Islam," instead they kept saying, "We have turned away, we have turned away." Khalid began killing them. This reached the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he raised his hands and said: "O Allah, I disavow before You what Khalid has done." He sent 'Ali, who paid the compensation for their slain and for what had been destroyed of their property, down to the lick of a dog's tongue [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (7189).]].
From this hadith it is taken that the mistake of the Imam or his deputy is paid from the public treasury (bayt al-mal).
* *
As for His saying: ﴿unless they forgo it as charity﴾, meaning: the compensation is due, delivered to his family, unless they give it up as charity, in which case it is not due.
* *
As for His saying: ﴿If he was from a people hostile to you, yet he was a believer, then the freeing of a believing slave﴾, meaning: if the slain was a believer, but his relatives were disbelievers at war with you, then they have no compensation, and the killer owes only the freeing of a believing slave.
* *
As for His saying: ﴿And if he was from a people between you and whom there is a covenant [then a compensation delivered to his family and the freeing of a believing slave]﴾, the verse continues, meaning: if the slain's relatives are people under protection (dhimmah) or truce (hudnah), then they have the compensation for their slain. If he was a believer, it is the full compensation. Likewise if he was a disbeliever, according to a group of scholars. It was also said: for a disbeliever the compensation is half the compensation for a Muslim, and it was said: a third of it, as is detailed in the Book of Rulings (Kitab al-Ahkam). The killer is also obligated to free a believing slave.
﴿Whoever cannot find one, then fasting for two consecutive months﴾, meaning: there is no breaking of the fast between them; rather, he must continue his fasting until they are complete. If he breaks it without an excuse, such as illness, menstruation or postnatal bleeding, he must begin again. The scholars differed over whether travel interrupts it, on two opinions.
* *
As for His saying: ﴿a repentance from Allah; and Allah is ever Knowing and Wise﴾, meaning: this is the repentance of one who killed by mistake when he cannot find a slave to free: he fasts two consecutive months.
The scholars differed concerning one who cannot fast: is it obligatory for him to feed sixty needy persons, as in the expiation for zihar? On two opinions. One: yes, as is explicitly stated in the expiation for zihar; and it was not mentioned here because this is a context of warning, intimidation and caution, so it is not fitting to mention feeding, which carries facilitation and leniency. The second opinion: he does not turn to feeding, because if it were obligatory, its explanation would not have been delayed beyond the time of need.
﴿And Allah is ever Knowing and Wise﴾: its explanation has already been given more than once.
Then, after Allah explained the ruling for killing by mistake, He began explaining the ruling for deliberate killing, saying: ﴿And whoever kills a believer intentionally [his recompense is Hell, abiding therein; and Allah will be angry with him and curse him and prepare for him a great punishment]﴾. This is a severe threat and a firm warning for whoever commits this great sin, which is linked to associating partners with Allah in more than one verse of the Book of Allah, where He, glorified is He, says in Surah al-Furqan: ﴿And those who do not invoke with Allah another deity, and do not kill the soul which Allah has forbidden except by right [and do not commit unlawful sexual intercourse]﴾ [al-Furqan: 68]. And Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Say: Come, I will recite what your Lord has forbidden you: that you associate nothing with Him [...] until He said:
﴿And do not kill the soul which Allah has forbidden, except by right. This He has instructed you, that you may use reason﴾ [al-An'am: 151].
The hadiths on the prohibition of killing are very numerous. Among them is what is established in the two Sahihs from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The first matter to be judged among people on the Day of Resurrection is concerning blood." In another hadith narrated by Abu Dawud, through 'Amr ibn al-Walid ibn 'Abadah al-Misri, from 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The believer remains in a state of latitude and righteousness so long as he has not shed unlawful blood; but if he sheds unlawful blood, he is ruined (balliha)" [[Sunan Abi Dawud no. (4270).]]. In another hadith: "The passing away of this world is less significant to Allah than the killing of a Muslim man" [[Narrated from the hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, and from the hadith of al-Bara' ibn 'Azib. As for the hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, al-Tirmidhi narrated it in his Sunan no. (1395), and al-Nasa'i in his Sunan (7/82), and this is its wording.]]. In another hadith: "If the people of the heavens and the earth were to join together in killing a Muslim man, Allah would throw them all into the Fire" [[Narrated by al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Saghir no. (565) through the route of Ja'far ibn Jubayr ibn Farqad, from his father, from al-Hasan, from Abu Bakrah (may Allah be pleased with him). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (7/297): "In it is Jisr ibn Farqad, and he is weak."]]. In another hadith: "Whoever helps in the killing of a Muslim, even with half a word, will come on the Day of Resurrection with written between his eyes: 'Despairing of the mercy of Allah.'" [[Narrated by Ibn Majah in his Sunan no. (2620), through the route of Yazid ibn Ziyad, from al-Zuhri, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, from Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him). Al-Dhahabi, may Allah have mercy on him, said: "This is a false, fabricated hadith."]].
Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with both of them, held that there is no repentance for one who deliberately kills a believer.

Al-Bukhari said: Adam narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, Mughirah ibn al-Nu'man narrated to us, saying: I heard Ibn Jubayr say: The people of Kufa differed concerning it (this verse), so I travelled to Ibn 'Abbas and asked him about it. He said: This verse, ﴿And whoever kills a believer intentionally, his recompense is Hell, [abiding therein]﴾, was the last of what was revealed, and nothing abrogated it.

It was also related in the same way by al-Bukhari himself, Muslim and al-Nasa'i through several routes, from Shu'bah, with the same wording. [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4590), Sahih Muslim no. (3023), Sunan al-Nasa'i (8/62).] Abu Dawud related it from Ahmad ibn Hanbal, from Ibn Mahdi, from Sufyan al-Thawri, from Mughirah ibn al-Nu'man, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas concerning his saying: ﴿And whoever kills a believer intentionally, his recompense is Hell, abiding therein forever﴾, and he said: Nothing has abrogated it.

[Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, Ibn Abi 'Adi narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Abu Bishr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr who said: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abza said: Ibn 'Abbas was asked about his saying: ﴿And whoever kills a believer intentionally, his recompense is Hell, abiding therein forever﴾, and he said: Nothing has abrogated it.] And he said concerning this verse: ﴿And those who do not invoke with Allah another deity [and do not kill the soul which Allah has forbidden, except by right, and do not commit unlawful sexual intercourse; and whoever does that will meet a penalty]﴾ [al-Furqan: 68]. He said: It was revealed concerning the people of polytheism. [Sunan Abi Dawud no. (4275).]

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, Jarir narrated to us, from Mansur, who narrated to me Sa'id ibn Jubayr, or al-Hakam narrated to me, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: I asked Ibn 'Abbas about His saying [Exalted is He]: ﴿And whoever kills a believer intentionally, his recompense is Hell﴾. He said: When a man knows Islam and its laws, then kills a believer intentionally, his recompense is Hell, and there is no repentance for him. I mentioned that to Mujahid, and he said: Except for the one who regrets.

Ibn Humayd and Ibn Wakr narrated to us, both saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Yahya al-Jabir, from Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd, who said: We were with Ibn 'Abbas after his sight had gone, when a man came to him and called out: O 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abbas, what do you say about a man who kills a believer intentionally? He said: ﴿His recompense is Hell, abiding therein; and Allah has become angry with him and has cursed him and prepared for him a great punishment﴾. The man said: What do you think if he repents, does righteous deeds, and then is guided? Ibn 'Abbas said: May his mother be bereaved of him! How can he have repentance and guidance? By Him in whose hand my soul is, I heard your Prophet ﷺ say: "May his mother be bereaved of him, the killer of a believer intentionally, he will come on the Day of Resurrection holding his killer by his right hand or his left, his veins gushing blood before the throne of the Most Merciful, and he will cling to his killer with his other hand, saying: Ask this one why he killed me." [Tafsir al-Tabari (9/62, 63).] By Him whose soul is in the hand of 'Abd Allah, this verse was revealed, and no verse abrogated it until your Prophet ﷺ passed away, and no revelation came after it.

Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, I heard Yahya ibn al-Muhajjar narrating from Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd, from Ibn 'Abbas, that a man came to him and said: What do you say about a man who killed a man intentionally? He said: ﴿His recompense is Hell, abiding therein [and Allah has become angry with him and has cursed him and prepared for him a great punishment]﴾. He said: It was revealed among the last of what was revealed; nothing abrogated it until the Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed away, and no revelation came after the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He said: What do you say if he repents, believes, does righteous deeds, and then is guided? He said: How can he have repentance? You have heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "May his mother be bereaved of him, a man who killed a man intentionally, he will come on the Day of Resurrection holding his killer by his right hand or his left, and holding his head by his right or left hand, his veins gushing blood from before the throne, saying: O Lord, ask Your servant why he killed me."

It was also related by al-Nasa'i from Qutaybah, and by Ibn Majah from Muhammad ibn al-Sabbah, from Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah, from 'Ammar al-Duhni, Yahya al-Jabir and Thabit al-Thumali, from Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd, from Ibn 'Abbas, and he mentioned it. [Al-Musnad (1/240), Sunan al-Nasa'i (8/63), Sunan Ibn Majah no. (2621).] This has been related from Ibn 'Abbas through many routes.

Among those from the early generations who held that the killer has no repentance were: Zayd ibn Thabit, Abu Hurayrah, 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar, Abu Salamah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, 'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr, al-Hasan, Qatadah, and al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim; Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted this.

On this topic there are many hadiths. Among them is what Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh al-Hafiz related in his Tafsir: Da'laj ibn Ahmad narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Sa'id al-Bushanji narrated to us, and 'Abd Allah ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn Fahd narrated to us, both saying: 'Ubayd ibn 'Ubaydah narrated to us, Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from his father, from al-A'mash, from Abu 'Amr ibn Shurahbil, from 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "The one who is killed will come on the Day of Resurrection clinging to his killer, holding his head in his other hand, and he will say: O Lord, ask this one why he killed me." He said: "He will say: I killed him so that the might would be Yours. He will say: Indeed it is Mine." He said: "And another will come clinging to his killer and say: O Lord, ask this one why he killed me. He will say: I killed him so that the might would be for so-and-so. He said: It is not for him; he will bear his sin." He said: "Then he will plunge into the Fire for seventy autumns."

It was also related by al-Nasa'i from Ibrahim ibn al-Mustamirr al-'Awfi, from 'Amr ibn 'Asim, from Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman, with the same. [Sunan al-Nasa'i (7/84). Abu Nu'aym related it in al-Hilyah (4/147) and al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (10/119). Abu Nu'aym said: "Gharib from the hadith of Sulayman al-Taymi from al-A'mash; none related it from him except his son Mu'tamir, and 'Amr ibn 'Asim related it from Mu'tamir in the same way."]

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Safwan ibn 'Isa narrated to us, Thawr ibn Yazid narrated to us, from Abu 'Awn, from Abu Idris who said: I heard Mu'awiyah, may Allah be pleased with him, say: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "Every sin, Allah may forgive it, except the man who dies a disbeliever, or the man who kills a believer intentionally."

Al-Nasa'i likewise related it from Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna, from Safwan ibn 'Isa, with the same. [Al-Musnad (4/99), Sunan al-Nasa'i (7/81).]

Ibn Mardawayh said: 'Abd Allah ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Sammawayh narrated to us, 'Abd al-A'la ibn Muhsir narrated to us, Sadaqah ibn Khalid narrated to us, Khalid ibn Dihqan narrated to us, Ibn Abi Zakariyya narrated to us, who said: I heard Umm al-Darda' say: I heard Abu al-Darda' say: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "Every sin, Allah may forgive it, except the one who dies associating others with Allah, or the one who kills a believer intentionally."

This is very strange from this route. The well-known (narration) is the hadith of Mu'awiyah mentioned earlier. [Abu Dawud related it in his Sunan no. (4270), Ibn Hibban in his Sahih no. (51), and al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan al-Kubra (8/21) through the route of Khalid ibn Dihqan with the same. And the statement of the Hafiz Ibn Kathir, may Allah have mercy on him, here: "very strange from this route," the reason for it has not become clear to me; however, the hadith of Abu al-Darda' is stronger than the hadith of Mu'awiyah, for in the chain of the hadith of Mu'awiyah (Abu 'Awn) none declared him reliable except Ibn Hibban, whereas the men of the hadith of Abu al-Darda' are all trustworthy.] So Allah knows best.

Then Ibn Mardawayh related through the route of Baqiyyah ibn al-Walid, from Nafi' ibn Yazid, who said: Ibn Jubayr al-Ansari narrated to me, from Dawud ibn al-Husayn, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "Whoever kills a believer intentionally has disbelieved in Allah, the Mighty and Majestic."

This hadith is also munkar, and its chain is severely criticized. [Ibn 'Adi related it in al-Kamil (3/203) through the route of Baqiyyah, then said: "These hadiths from Zayd, from Dawud, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar are not preserved; Zayd ibn Jubayrah narrates from Dawud alone," and Zayd ibn Jubayrah is munkar al-hadith and his narrations are not followed.]

Imam Ahmad said: al-Nadr narrated to us, Sulayman ibn al-Mughirah narrated to us, Humayd narrated to us, saying: Abu al-'Aliyah came to me, myself and a companion of mine, and said to us: Come, for you two are younger than me and more retentive of hadith than I am. So he took us to Bishr ibn 'Asim. Abu al-'Aliyah said to him: Narrate your hadith to these people. He said: 'Uqbah ibn Malik al-Laythi narrated to us, saying: The Prophet ﷺ sent a expedition, which raided a people, and a man from the people broke away, and a man from the expedition pursued him, drawing his sword. The man who had broken away said: I am a Muslim. But he did not consider what he said, and struck him and killed him. The news reached the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he spoke harshly about it, and it reached the killer. While the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was delivering a sermon, the killer said: By Allah, he only said what he said out of fear of being killed. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ turned away from him and from those of the people who had heard him, and continued his sermon. Then he (the killer) said again: O Messenger of Allah, he only said what he said out of fear of being killed. He turned away from him and from those of the people who had heard him, and continued his sermon. Then he could not hold back, and said a third time: By Allah, O Messenger of Allah, he only said it out of fear of being killed.

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ turned to him, and the displeasure was recognised in his face, and he said: "Indeed Allah refuses (to forgive) the one who kills a believer," three times.

Al-Nasa'i related it from the hadith of Sulayman ibn al-Mughirah. [Al-Musnad (5/288), Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra no. (8593).]

What the majority of the early and later generations of this Ummah hold is that the killer has repentance between himself and his Lord, the Mighty and Majestic. If he repents, turns back, humbles himself and submits, and does righteous deeds, Allah will replace his evil deeds with good deeds, and will compensate the slain for his wrong and satisfy him regarding his claim.

Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And those who do not invoke with Allah another deity [and do not kill the soul which Allah has forbidden, except by right, and do not commit unlawful sexual intercourse; and whoever does that will meet a penalty. Its punishment will be doubled for him on the Day of Resurrection, and he will abide therein in humiliation]﴾ [up to His saying]: ﴿Except for one who repents and believes and does righteous work; for those, Allah will replace their evil deeds with good, and ever is Allah Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [al-Furqan: 68–70]. This is a report that cannot be abrogated. Applying it to polytheists, and applying this verse to believers, is contrary to the apparent meaning, and such an application needs evidence. So Allah knows best.

And Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Say, O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah; indeed, Allah forgives all sins; indeed, it is He who is the Forgiving, the Merciful﴾ [al-Zumar: 53]. This is general concerning all sins, of disbelief and polytheism, doubt and hypocrisy, killing and wickedness, and other than these: whoever repents of any of them, Allah will accept his repentance.

And Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive that He be associated with; but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills﴾ [al-Nisa': 48]. This verse is general concerning all sins other than shirk, and it is mentioned in this noble surah both after this verse and before it, to strengthen hope. And Allah knows best.

It is well established in the two Sahihs (al-Sahihayn, i.e., Bukhari and Muslim) that the Israelite who killed one hundred souls then asked a scholar, "Is there any repentance for me?" He said, "Who could stand between you and repentance?!" Then he directed him to a land where Allah is worshipped, so he migrated there, but he died on the way, and the angels of mercy took his soul. As we have mentioned more than once, if this was the case among the Children of Israel, then acceptance of repentance in this Ummah is all the more fitting and deserving, because Allah has removed from us the shackles and burdens that were upon them, and sent our Prophet with the upright and easy monotheistic faith (al-hanifiyyah al-samhah).

As for the noble verse, which is His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Whoever kills a believer intentionally, his recompense is Hell, abiding therein forever, and Allah will be angry with him and curse him and prepare for him a great punishment﴾ [[Addition from R and A; in H: "the verse".]]. Abu Hurayrah and a group of the early generations said: "This is his recompense if Allah recompenses him." It was also transmitted by Ibn Mardawayh in a marfu' form, through Muhammad ibn Jami' al-Attar, from al-Ala' ibn Maymun al-Anbari, from Hajjaj al-Aswad, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, from Abu Hurayrah in a marfu' form, but it is not authentic. The meaning of this formula is that this is his recompense if he is requited for it, and likewise every threat for a sin. However, this may be counterbalanced by good deeds that prevent that recompense from reaching him, according to the view of the people of al-muwazanah (the weighing of deeds) or of al-ihbat (the nullification of deeds). This is the best approach to take in the matter of threats, and Allah knows best what is correct. And even on the assumption that the killer enters the Fire, either according to the view of Ibn Abbas and those who agree with him that he has no repentance, or according to the view of the majority where he has no righteous deed by which he may be saved, he will not remain in it forever; rather, "abiding" (khulud) means a long stay. The hadiths have been reported in succession from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that whoever has in his heart even the smallest particle of faith will be brought out of the Fire. As for the hadith of Mu'awiyah: "Every sin, Allah may forgive it, except a man who dies as a disbeliever, or a man who kills a believer intentionally," the word "'asa" (perhaps) indicates hope, so when hope is negated in these two cases, that does not negate the occurrence of that in one of them, namely killing, because of the evidences we have mentioned. As for the one who dies as a disbeliever, the explicit text says that he will never be forgiven at all. As for the demand of the slain against the killer on the Day of Resurrection, it is a right of the children of Adam, and such rights do not fall away through repentance. There is no difference between the slain and the one whose property was stolen, the one from whom something was seized by force, the one falsely accused, and all other rights of the children of Adam, for consensus (al-ijma') has been established that these rights do not fall away through repentance, and it is necessary to restore them to their owners for the repentance to be valid. If that is impossible, then there must be a demand for them on the Day of Resurrection. But the occurrence of the demand does not necessarily mean the occurrence of retribution. The killer may have good deeds that are transferred to the slain, or some of them are, and then he may have an excess of reward by which he enters Paradise, or Allah may compensate the slain from His bounty with whatever He wills, such as palaces of Paradise and its bliss, the raising of his rank therein, and the like. And Allah knows best.

Then, for intentional killing there are rulings in this world and rulings in the Hereafter. As for this world, the guardians of the slain are empowered over the killer. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And whoever is killed wrongfully, We have given his heir authority, but let him not commit excess in killing; indeed, he is supported﴾ [al-Isra' 33]. Then they have the choice between executing him, pardoning him, or taking blood money (diyah) made heavier, in three categories: thirty hiqqah (camels in their fourth year), thirty jadh'ah (camels in their fifth year), and forty khalifah (pregnant she-camels), as is established in the books of rulings.

The imams differed: is an expiation (kaffarah) of freeing a slave, or fasting two consecutive months, or feeding the poor, obligatory upon him? This is according to one of the two opinions, as was discussed earlier regarding the expiation for accidental killing, where there are two views. Al-Shafi'i and his companions and a group of scholars say: yes, it is obligatory upon him, because if expiation is obligatory for accidental killing, then it is all the more obligatory for intentional killing. They applied this same reasoning to the expiation for the oath of ghamus (the deliberate false oath), and they relied on the making up of prayers that were intentionally left out, just as they agreed on that in the case of accidental killing.

The companions of Imam Ahmad and others said: intentional killing is too grave to be expiated, so there is no expiation for it, and likewise for the ghamus oath. They have no way to distinguish between these two cases and the intentionally abandoned prayer, for they say that it must be made up even if it was intentionally abandoned.

Those who held that expiation is obligatory for intentional killing have argued with what Imam Ahmad narrated, where he said: Aarim ibn al-Fadl narrated to us, 'Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, from Ibrahim ibn Abi 'Ablah, from al-Gharif ibn 'Ayyash, from Wathilah ibn al-Asqa' who said: A group from Banu Sulaym came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: "A companion of ours has incurred the obligation (of Hell)." He said: "Let him free a slave; Allah will ransom with each of its limbs a limb of his from the Fire" [Musnad (4/107)].

And Ahmad said: Ibrahim ibn Ishaq narrated to us, Damrah ibn Rabi'ah narrated to us, from Ibrahim ibn Abi 'Ablah, from al-Gharif al-Daylami who said: We came to Wathilah ibn al-Asqa' al-Laythi and said: "Narrate to us a hadith that you heard from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ." He said: "We came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ concerning a companion of ours who had incurred (the obligation), and he said: 'Free (a slave) on his behalf; Allah will free from the Fire with each of its limbs a limb of his.'"

It was also transmitted by Abu Dawud and al-Nasa'i, through the hadith of Ibrahim ibn Abi 'Ablah, with the same chain [Musnad (3/491), Sunan Abi Dawud no. (3964), Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra no. (4892)]. The wording of Abu Dawud from al-Gharif al-Daylami is: He said: "We came to Wathilah ibn al-Asqa' and said: 'Narrate to us a hadith with no addition or subtraction.' He became angry and said: 'Indeed one of you recites while his mushaf is hanging in his house, and so he adds and subtracts.' We said: 'We only wanted a hadith you heard from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.' He said: 'We came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ concerning a companion of ours who had incurred (the obligation) — meaning the Fire — by killing, and he said: "Free (a slave) on his behalf; Allah will free from the Fire with each of its limbs a limb of his."' [Sunan Abi Dawud no. (3964)].

[The words of the Mighty and Majestic]

Allah says: It is not for a believer to kill another believer under any circumstances, as is established in the two Sahihs (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim) from Ibn Mas'ud that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The blood of a Muslim man who testifies that there is no god but Allah and that I am the Messenger of Allah may not be shed except in one of three cases: a life for a life, a married person who commits adultery, and one who abandons his religion and separates from the community" [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (6878), and Sahih Muslim, no. (1676).]].
Then, when any one of these three cases occurs, it is not for any individual among the subjects to kill him; rather, that is for the Imam (ruler) or his deputy.
* *
As for His saying: ﴿except by mistake﴾, they said: it is an exceptive clause of the disconnected type (istithna' munqati', where what follows is not of the same kind as what precedes), like the saying of the poet [[He is Jarir ibn 'Atiyya al-Ghatafani, and the verse is in Tafsir al-Tabari (9/31).]]:
"Of the white women, she did not travel far nor did she tread on the earth except on a striped, folded cloth of the finest garment."
There are many examples of this.
The commentators differed concerning the occasion of revelation of this verse. Mujahid and others said: it was revealed concerning 'Ayyash ibn Abi Rabi'ah, the brother of Abu Jahl through their mother, whose mother was Asma' bint Makhribah. He killed a man who was tormenting him, along with his brother, for Islam; this man was al-Harith ibn Yazid al-'Amiri. 'Ayyash harbored ill will toward him. That man then embraced Islam and migrated, while 'Ayyash was unaware. When the day of the Conquest came, he saw him and thought that he was still upon his former religion, so he charged at him and killed him. Then Allah revealed this verse [[Narrated by al-Tabari in his Tafsir (9/33).]].
'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: It was revealed concerning Abu al-Darda', because he killed a man who had uttered the word of Islam when he raised the sword over him; he swung the sword at him, and he had said his statement. When this was mentioned to the Prophet (ﷺ), he said: "He only said it seeking refuge." So he said to him: "Did you split open his heart?" [[Narrated by al-Tabari in his Tafsir (9/34).]] [This story is in the Sahih for someone other than Abu al-Darda'.]
* *
As for His saying: ﴿And whoever kills a believer by mistake, then the freeing of a believing slave and a compensation (diyah) delivered to his family [unless they forgo it as charity]﴾: these are two obligations for killing by mistake. The first is expiation (kaffarah) for the great sin he committed, even though it was a mistake. Among its conditions is that it must be the freeing of a believing slave; a disbeliever is not sufficient.
Ibn Jarir related from Ibn 'Abbas, al-Sha'bi, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i and al-Hasan al-Basri that they said: a child is not sufficient unless he intends belief. It is also narrated through 'Abd al-Razzaq from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, who said: in the reading of Ubayy, "freeing a believing slave" — a child is not sufficient in it.
Ibn Jarir chose that if he was born between two Muslim parents, it is sufficient, and otherwise not. What the majority hold is that whenever he is a Muslim, his manumission for expiation is valid, whether he is a child or an adult.
Imam Ahmad said: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd Allah, from a man of the Ansar: that he came with a black slave girl and said: "O Messenger of Allah, upon me is a believing slave; if you see this one as a believer, I will free her." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to her: "Do you testify that there is no god but Allah?" She said: "Yes." He said: "Do you testify that I am the Messenger of Allah?" She said: "Yes." He said: "Do you believe in resurrection after death?" She said: "Yes." He said: "Free her."
This is a sound chain, and the ignorance of the Companion does not harm it [[Al-Musnad (3/451).]].
In the Muwatta' of Imam Malik, the Musnads of al-Shafi'i and Ahmad, Sahih Muslim, and the Sunan of Abu Dawud and al-Nasa'i, through the route of Hilal ibn Abi Maymunah, from 'Ata' ibn Yasar, from Mu'awiyah ibn al-Hakam: when he brought that black slave girl, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to her: "Where is Allah?" She said: "In the heaven." He said: "Who am I?" She said: "You are the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)." He said: "Free her, for she is a believer" [[Al-Muwatta' (2/777), Musnad al-Shafi'i no. (1196), Bada'i' al-Minan, Musnad Ahmad (5/447), Sahih Muslim no. (537), Sunan Abi Dawud no. (2384), Sunan al-Nasa'i (3/14).]].
* *
As for His saying: ﴿and a compensation (diyah) delivered to his family﴾: this is the second obligation, owed between the killer and the family of the slain, as compensation to them for what they lost of their relative. This compensation is due in fifths (akhmas), as related by Imam Ahmad and the authors of the Sunan, from the hadith of al-Hajjaj ibn Arta'ah, from Zayd ibn Jubayr, from Khashf ibn Malik, from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) decreed for the compensation for manslaughter: twenty daughters of a year (bint makhad), twenty sons of a year (ibn makhad), twenty daughters of two years (bint labun), twenty male camels of four years (jadha'ah), and twenty of five years (hiqqah).
This is the wording of al-Nasa'i. Al-Tirmidhi said: we do not know it as marfu' except through this route, and it has been narrated from 'Abd Allah as a mawquf report [[Al-Musnad (1/384), Sunan al-Nasa'i (8/43), Sunan Abi Dawud no. (4545), Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (1386), Sunan Ibn Majah no. (2631).]].
Likewise, it has been narrated from ['Ali and] a group of people.
It was also said: it is due in quarters. This compensation is owed by the killer's paternal kin ('aqilah), not from his own property. Al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, said: I know of no dissent that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) decreed the compensation to be borne by the 'aqilah, and this is more widely reported than the hadith of the particular individual [[Al-Umm (6/101).]]. What he, may Allah have mercy on him, pointed to has been established in more than one hadith. Among that is what is established in the two Sahihs from Abu Hurayrah, who said: Two women of Hudhayl fought, and one of them struck the other with a stone, killing her and the child in her womb. They brought the dispute to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he decreed that the compensation for her fetus was a ghurrah, a male or female slave, and he decreed the compensation for the woman upon her 'aqilah [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (6910) and Sahih Muslim no. (1681).]].
This implies that the ruling for semi-intentional killing (amd al-khata') is the ruling for pure mistake regarding the obligation of compensation; however, in this case the compensation is due in thirds, like intentional killing, because of its resemblance to it.
In Sahih al-Bukhari, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent Khalid ibn al-Walid to the Banu Judhaymah, and he invited them to Islam, but they did not properly say, "We have embraced Islam," instead they kept saying, "We have turned away, we have turned away." Khalid began killing them. This reached the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he raised his hands and said: "O Allah, I disavow before You what Khalid has done." He sent 'Ali, who paid the compensation for their slain and for what had been destroyed of their property, down to the lick of a dog's tongue [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (7189).]].
From this hadith it is taken that the mistake of the Imam or his deputy is paid from the public treasury (bayt al-mal).
* *
As for His saying: ﴿unless they forgo it as charity﴾, meaning: the compensation is due, delivered to his family, unless they give it up as charity, in which case it is not due.
* *
As for His saying: ﴿If he was from a people hostile to you, yet he was a believer, then the freeing of a believing slave﴾, meaning: if the slain was a believer, but his relatives were disbelievers at war with you, then they have no compensation, and the killer owes only the freeing of a believing slave.
* *
As for His saying: ﴿And if he was from a people between you and whom there is a covenant [then a compensation delivered to his family and the freeing of a believing slave]﴾, the verse continues, meaning: if the slain's relatives are people under protection (dhimmah) or truce (hudnah), then they have the compensation for their slain. If he was a believer, it is the full compensation. Likewise if he was a disbeliever, according to a group of scholars. It was also said: for a disbeliever the compensation is half the compensation for a Muslim, and it was said: a third of it, as is detailed in the Book of Rulings (Kitab al-Ahkam). The killer is also obligated to free a believing slave.
﴿Whoever cannot find one, then fasting for two consecutive months﴾, meaning: there is no breaking of the fast between them; rather, he must continue his fasting until they are complete. If he breaks it without an excuse, such as illness, menstruation or postnatal bleeding, he must begin again. The scholars differed over whether travel interrupts it, on two opinions.
* *
As for His saying: ﴿a repentance from Allah; and Allah is ever Knowing and Wise﴾, meaning: this is the repentance of one who killed by mistake when he cannot find a slave to free: he fasts two consecutive months.
The scholars differed concerning one who cannot fast: is it obligatory for him to feed sixty needy persons, as in the expiation for zihar? On two opinions. One: yes, as is explicitly stated in the expiation for zihar; and it was not mentioned here because this is a context of warning, intimidation and caution, so it is not fitting to mention feeding, which carries facilitation and leniency. The second opinion: he does not turn to feeding, because if it were obligatory, its explanation would not have been delayed beyond the time of need.
﴿And Allah is ever Knowing and Wise﴾: its explanation has already been given more than once.
Then, after Allah explained the ruling for killing by mistake, He began explaining the ruling for deliberate killing, saying: ﴿And whoever kills a believer intentionally [his recompense is Hell, abiding therein; and Allah will be angry with him and curse him and prepare for him a great punishment]﴾. This is a severe threat and a firm warning for whoever commits this great sin, which is linked to associating partners with Allah in more than one verse of the Book of Allah, where He, glorified is He, says in Surah al-Furqan: ﴿And those who do not invoke with Allah another deity, and do not kill the soul which Allah has forbidden except by right [and do not commit unlawful sexual intercourse]﴾ [al-Furqan: 68]. And Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Say: Come, I will recite what your Lord has forbidden you: that you associate nothing with Him [...] until He said:
﴿And do not kill the soul which Allah has forbidden, except by right. This He has instructed you, that you may use reason﴾ [al-An'am: 151].
The hadiths on the prohibition of killing are very numerous. Among them is what is established in the two Sahihs from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The first matter to be judged among people on the Day of Resurrection is concerning blood." In another hadith narrated by Abu Dawud, through 'Amr ibn al-Walid ibn 'Abadah al-Misri, from 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The believer remains in a state of latitude and righteousness so long as he has not shed unlawful blood; but if he sheds unlawful blood, he is ruined (balliha)" [[Sunan Abi Dawud no. (4270).]]. In another hadith: "The passing away of this world is less significant to Allah than the killing of a Muslim man" [[Narrated from the hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, and from the hadith of al-Bara' ibn 'Azib. As for the hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, al-Tirmidhi narrated it in his Sunan no. (1395), and al-Nasa'i in his Sunan (7/82), and this is its wording.]]. In another hadith: "If the people of the heavens and the earth were to join together in killing a Muslim man, Allah would throw them all into the Fire" [[Narrated by al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Saghir no. (565) through the route of Ja'far ibn Jubayr ibn Farqad, from his father, from al-Hasan, from Abu Bakrah (may Allah be pleased with him). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (7/297): "In it is Jisr ibn Farqad, and he is weak."]].
