وَقَالَ ابْنُ أَبِي حَاتِمٍ: حَدَّثَنَا أَبِي، حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو مَعْمَرٍ الْمَقْرِيُّ [[في ر: "المنقري".]] حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ الْوَارِثِ، حَدَّثَنَا عَلِيِّ بْنِ زَيْدٍ، عَنْ سَعِيدِ بْنِ المسَّيب، عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ: أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ﷺ رَفَعَ يَدَهُ بَعْدَمَا سَلَّمَ، وَهُوَ مُسْتَقْبَلٌ الْقِبْلَةَ فَقَالَ: "اللَّهُمَّ خَلِّصِ الْوَلِيدَ بْنَ الْوَلِيدِ، وَعَيَّاشَ بْنَ أَبِي رَبِيعَةَ، وسَلَمة بْنَ هِشَامٍ، وَضَعَفَةَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ الَّذِينَ لَا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ حِيلَةً وَلَا يَهْتَدُونَ سَبِيلًا مِنْ أَيْدِي الْكُفَّارِ" [[وفي إسناده علي بن زيد بن عبد الله بن أبي مليكة ضعيف لا يحتج به، وقد اختلف عليه فيه، كما سيأتي في رواية الطبري.]] .

وَقَالَ ابْنُ جَرِيرٍ: حَدَّثَنَا الْمُثَنَّى، حَدَّثَنَا حَجَّاجٌ، حَدَّثَنَا حَمَّادٌ، عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ زَيْدٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ [[في ر، أ: "عبيد الله".]] -أَوْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ الْقُرَشِيِّ- عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ؛ أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ﷺ كَانَ يَدْعُو فِي دُبُرِ صَلَاةِ الظُّهْرِ: "اللَّهُمَّ خَلِّص الْوَلِيدِ، وَسَلَمَةَ بْنَ هِشَامٍ، وَعَيَّاشَ بْنَ أَبِي رَبِيعَةَ، وَضَعَفَةَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ مِنْ أَيْدِي الْمُشْرِكِينَ الَّذِينَ لَا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ حِيلَةً وَلَا يَهْتَدُونَ سَبِيلًا".

وَلِهَذَا الْحَدِيثِ شَاهِدٌ فِي الصَّحِيحِ مِنْ غَيْرِ هَذَا الْوَجْهِ كَمَا تَقَدَّمَ [[تفسير الطبري (٩/١١٠) وإسناده ضعيف.]] .

وَقَالَ عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ: أَنْبَأَنَا [[في أ: "أخبرنا".]] ابْنُ عُيَيْنَةَ، عَنْ عُبَيْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ أَبِي يَزِيدَ قَالَ: سَمِعْتُ ابْنَ عَبَّاسٍ يَقُولُ: كُنْتُ أَنَا وَأُمِّي مِنَ الْمُسْتَضْعَفِينَ مِنَ النِّسَاءِ وَالْوَلَدَانِ [[تفسير عبد الرزاق (١/١٦٦) .]]

وَقَالَ الْبُخَارِيُّ: أَنْبَأَنَا أَبُو النُّعْمَانِ، حَدَّثَنَا حَمَّادُ بْنُ زَيْدٍ، عَنْ أَيُّوبَ، عَنْ ابْنِ أَبِي مُلَيْكَة، عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ: ﴿إِلا الْمُسْتَضْعَفِينَ﴾ قَالَ: كَانَتْ أُمِّي مِمَّنْ عَذَر اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ [[صحيح البخاري برقم (٤٥٩٧) .]] .

* *

وَقَوْلُهُ: ﴿وَمَنْ يُهَاجِرْ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ يَجِدْ فِي الأرْضِ مُرَاغَمًا كَثِيرًا وَسَعَةً﴾ هذا تحريض على الْهِجْرَةِ، وَتَرْغِيبٌ فِي مُفَارَقَةِ الْمُشْرِكِينَ، وَأَنَّ الْمُؤْمِنَ حَيْثُمَا ذَهَبَ وَجَدَ عَنْهُمْ مَنْدُوحَةً وَمَلْجَأً يَتَحَصَّنُ فِيهِ، وَ"الْمُرَاغَمُ" مَصْدَرٌ، تَقُولُ الْعَرَبُ: رَاغَمَ فُلَانُ قَوْمَهُ مُرَاغَمًا وَمُرَاغَمَةً، قَالَ نَابِغَةُ [[في أ: "نابغة في بني جعدة.]] بَنِي جَعْدَةَ [[البيت في تفسير الطبري (١٠/١١٢) واللسان مادة (رغم) .]]

كَطَوْدٍ يُلاذُ بأرْكَانِه ... عَزيز المُرَاغَم وَالْمَهْربِ ...

وَقَالَ ابْنُ عَبَّاسٍ: "المراغَم": التَّحَوُّلُ مِنْ أَرْضٍ إِلَى أَرْضٍ. وَكَذَا رُوي عَنِ الضَّحَّاكِ وَالرَّبِيعِ بْنِ أَنَسٍ، الثَّوْرِيِّ، وَقَالَ مُجَاهِدٌ: ﴿مُرَاغَمًا كَثِيرًا﴾ يَعْنِي: مُتَزَحْزَحًا عَمَّا يُكْرَهُ. وَقَالَ سُفْيَانُ بْنُ عُيَيْنَةَ: ﴿مُرَاغَمًا كَثِيرًا﴾ يَعْنِي: بُرُوجًا.

وَالظَّاهِرُ -وَاللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ- أَنَّهُ [[في أ: "أن المراغم هو".]] التَّمَنُّعُ الَّذِي يُتَحصَّن بِهِ، وَيُرَاغَمُ بِهِ الْأَعْدَاءُ.

قَوْلُهُ: ﴿وَسَعَةً﴾ يَعْنِي: الرِّزْقَ. قَالَهُ غَيْرُ وَاحِدٍ، مِنْهُمْ: قَتَادَةُ، حَيْثُ قَالَ فِي قَوْلِهِ: ﴿يَجِدْ فِي الأرْضِ مُرَاغَمًا كَثِيرًا وَسَعَةً﴾ إِي، وَاللَّهِ، مِنَ الضَّلَالَةِ إِلَى الْهُدَى، وَمِنِ الْقِلَّةِ إِلَى الْغِنَى.

* *

وَقَوْلُهُ: ﴿وَمَنْ يَخْرُجْ مِنْ بَيْتِهِ مُهَاجِرًا إِلَى اللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ ثُمَّ يُدْرِكْهُ الْمَوْتُ فَقَدْ وَقَعَ أَجْرُهُ عَلَى اللَّهِ﴾ أَيْ: وَمَنْ خَرَجَ مِنْ مَنْزِلِهِ بِنِيَّةِ الْهِجْرَةِ، فَمَاتَ فِي أَثْنَاءِ الطَّرِيقِ، فَقَدْ حَصَلَ لَهُ مِنَ [[في أ: "عند".]] اللَّهِ ثَوَابُ مَنْ هَاجَرَ، كَمَا ثَبَتَ فِي الصَّحِيحَيْنِ وَغَيْرِهِمَا مِنَ الصِّحَاحِ وَالْمَسَانِيدِ وَالسُّنَنِ، مِنْ طَرِيقِ يَحْيَى بْنِ سَعِيدٍ الْأَنْصَارِيِّ [[في أ: "القطان".]] عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ التَّيْمِيِّ، عَنْ عَلْقَمَةَ بْنِ وَقّاص اللَّيْثِيِّ، عَنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ الْخَطَّابِ قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وسلم: "إنما الْأَعْمَالُ بِالنِّيَّاتِ، وَإِنَّمَا لِكُلِّ امْرِئٍ مَا نَوَى، فَمَنْ كَانَتْ هِجْرَتُهُ إِلَى اللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ، فَهِجْرَتُهُ إِلَى اللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ، وَمَنْ كَانَتْ هِجْرَتُهُ لِدُنْيَا يُصِيبُهَا، أَوِ امْرَأَةٍ يَتَزَوَّجُهَا، فَهِجْرَتُهُ إِلَى مَا هَاجَرَ إِلَيْهِ" [[صحيح البخاري برقم (١، ٥٤) وصحيح مسلم برقم (١٩٠٧) وسنن أبي داود برقم (٢٢٠١) وسن الترمذي برقم (١٦٤٧) ، وسنن النسائي (١/٥٩) وسنن ابن ماجه برقم (٤٢٢٧) ومسند أحمد (١/٢٥) ومسند الحميدي (١/١٦) ومسند الطيالسي (٢/٢٧) "منحة المعبود".]] .

وَهَذَا عَامٌّ فِي الْهِجْرَةِ وَفِي كُلِّ الْأَعْمَالِ. وَمِنْهُ الْحَدِيثُ الثَّابِتُ فِي الصَّحِيحَيْنِ [[صحيح البخاري برقم (٣٤٧٠) وصحيح مسلم برقم (٢٧٦٦) .]] فِي الرَّجُلِ الَّذِي قَتَلَ تِسْعَةً وَتِسْعِينَ نَفْسًا. ثُمَّ أَكْمَلَ بِذَلِكَ الْعَابِدِ الْمِائَةَ، ثُمَّ سَأَلَ عَالِمًا: هَلْ لَهُ مِنْ تَوْبَةٍ؟ فَقَالَ: وَمَنْ يَحُول بَيْنَكَ وَبَيْنَ التَّوْبَةِ؟ ثُمَّ أَرْشَدَهُ إِلَى أَنْ يَتَحَوَّلَ مِنْ بَلَدِهِ إِلَى بَلَدٍ آخَرَ يَعْبُدُ اللَّهَ فِيهِ، فَلَمَّا ارْتَحَلَ مِنْ بَلَدِهِ مُهَاجِرًا إِلَى الْبَلَدِ الْآخَرِ، أَدْرَكَهُ الْمَوْتُ فِي أَثْنَاءِ الطَّرِيقِ، فَاخْتَصَمَتْ فِيهِ مَلَائِكَةُ الرَّحْمَةِ وَمَلَائِكَةُ الْعَذَابِ، فَقَالَ هَؤُلَاءِ: إِنَّهُ جَاءَ تَائِبًا. وَقَالَ هَؤُلَاءِ: إِنَّهُ لَمْ يَصِلْ بَعْدُ. فَأُمِرُوا أَنَّ يَقِيسُوا مَا بَيْنَ الْأَرْضَيْنِ فَإِلَى أَيَّتِهِمَا [[في د، ر: "أيها"، وفي أ: "أيهما".]] كَانَ أَقْرَبُ كَانَ [[في د، ر: "فهو".]] مِنْهَا، فَأَمْرَ اللَّهُ هَذِهِ أَنْ يُقرب [[في د: "تقترب"، وفي ر: "تقرب".]] مِنْ هَذِهِ، وَهَذِهِ أَنْ تَبْعُدَ [[في د: "تبتعد".]] فَوَجَدُوهُ أَقْرَبَ إِلَى الْأَرْضِ الَّتِي هَاجَرَ إِلَيْهَا بِشِبْر، فَقَبَضَتْهُ مَلَائِكَةُ الرَّحْمَةِ. وَفِي رِوَايَةٍ: أَنَّهُ لَمَّا جَاءَهُ الْمَوْتُ نَاءَ بِصَدْرِهِ إِلَى الْأَرْضِ [[في د: "البلد".]] الَّتِي هَاجَرَ إِلَيْهَا.

Imam Ahmad said: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Atik, from his father Abdullah ibn Atik, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "Whoever leaves his house as an emigrant [in A: "as a mujahid"] in the way of Allah"—then he gestured with these three fingers, the middle, the index and the thumb, joined them together, and said: "and where are the mujahidun?"—"and he falls from his mount and dies, then his reward has fallen upon Allah; or a creature stings him and he dies, then his reward has fallen upon Allah; or he dies in his bed, then his reward has fallen upon Allah." By Allah, it is a word I have not heard from any of the Arabs before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. "And whoever is killed suddenly (qa'san), then he has merited the return (al-ma'ab)."

[Musnad (4/36). Al-Haythami said in Majma' al-Zawa'id (5/260): "In it is Muhammad ibn Ishaq, who is a mudallis, and the rest of its narrators are trustworthy."]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur'ah narrated to us, Abd al-Rahman ibn Abd al-Malik ibn Shaybah al-Hizami [in A: "al-Khuzami"] narrated to us, Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Mughirah al-Hizami [in A: "al-Khuzami"] narrated to me, from al-Mundhir ibn Abdullah, from Hisham ibn Urwah, from his father, that al-Zubayr ibn al-Awwam said: Khalid ibn Hizam [in A: "Ibn Haram"] emigrated to the land of Abyssinia, and a snake bit him on the way and he died. Concerning him was revealed: ﴿And whoever leaves his house as an emigrant to Allah and His Messenger, and then death overtakes him, his reward has indeed fallen upon Allah, and Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful﴾. Al-Zubayr said: I used to expect him and await his arrival while I was in the land of Abyssinia. Nothing grieved me as much as his death when it reached me, because few of those who emigrated from Quraysh were without some of their family or relatives with them, and there was no one with me from the Banu Asad ibn Abd al-'Uzza, nor did I hope for anyone other than him.

This report is very strange (gharib jiddan), for the reason of its strangeness is also as Ibn Hajar said: the one about whom this verse was revealed was Jundub ibn Damrah, and his report will come right after this. Moreover, this story is Meccan, while the revelation of this verse is Medinan. Perhaps he intended that the verse was revealed to encompass his ruling along with others, even if that was not the occasion of revelation. And Allah knows best.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Sulayman ibn Dawud, client of Abdullah ibn Ja'far, narrated to us, Sahl ibn Uthman narrated to us, Abd al-Rahman [in R: "Abd al-Rahim"] ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from al-Ash'ath [in R: "Ash'ath"]—he is Ibn Sawwar—from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Damrah ibn Jundub set out toward the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and died on the way before reaching the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, so this was revealed: ﴿And whoever leaves his house as an emigrant to Allah and His Messenger [then death overtakes him, his reward has indeed fallen upon Allah, and Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful]﴾.

[Abu Ya'la in his Musnad (5/81) and al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (11/272) narrated it through Ash'ath ibn Sawwar. Al-Haythami, after attributing it to Abu Ya'la alone, said: "Its narrators are trustworthy, but in its chain is Ash'ath ibn Sawwar, who is weak."]

And it was narrated to us by my father: Abdullah ibn Raja' narrated to us, Isra'il informed us, from Salim, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Abu Damrah ibn al-'Is al-Zuraqi, who was blind in his sight and was in Mecca. When the verse was revealed: ﴿except the oppressed men, women and children who are unable to devise a plan﴾, I said: "Indeed I am wealthy, and indeed I am capable of a plan." So he prepared himself, intending the Prophet ﷺ, but death overtook him at al-Tan'im, and this verse was revealed: ﴿And whoever leaves his house as an emigrant to Allah and His Messenger, then death overtakes him, [his reward has indeed fallen upon Allah, and Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful]﴾.

[Tafsir Ibn Abi Hatim (q.176). This report has also been narrated by other routes as a mursal (disconnected) report: Sa'id ibn Mansur in his Sunan, no. (685), said: Hushaym informed us, from Abu Bishr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, as a mursal. And al-Tabari in his Tafsir (9/118) narrated it through Qays ibn al-Rabi', from Salim, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, as a mursal.]

Al-Hafiz Abu Ya'la said: Ibrahim ibn Ziyad Sabalan narrated to us, Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, from Humayd ibn Abi Humayd, from Ata' ibn Yazid al-Laythi, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever sets out for Hajj and dies, the reward of the one performing Hajj will be recorded for him until the Day of Resurrection; whoever sets out for 'Umrah and dies, the reward of the one performing 'Umrah will be recorded for him until the Day of Resurrection; and whoever sets out as a warrior in the way of Allah and dies, the reward of the warrior will be recorded for him until the Day of Resurrection."

This is a strange hadith from this route (gharib min hadha al-wajh).

[Musnad Abi Ya'la (1/238). In its chain is Jamil ibn Abi Maymunah, whom none declared trustworthy except Ibn Hibban, and Ibn Ishaq is a mudallis who narrated with 'an'anah.]

قَالَ الْبُخَارِيُّ: حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ يَزِيدَ الْمُقْرِئُ، حَدَّثَنَا حَيْوَة وَغَيْرُهُ قَالَا حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ أَبُو الْأَسْوَدِ قَالَ: قُطِعَ عَلَى [[في أ: "من".]] أَهْلِ الْمَدِينَةِ بعْثٌ، فَاكْتَتَبْتُ فِيهِ، فلقيتُ عِكْرِمَةَ مَوْلَى ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ فَأَخْبَرْتُهُ، فَنَهَانِي عَنْ ذَلِكَ أَشَدَّ النَّهْيِ، ثُمَّ قَالَ: أَخْبَرَنِي ابْنُ عَبَّاسٍ أَنَّ نَاسًا مِنَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ كَانُوا مَعَ الْمُشْرِكِينَ، يُكَّثِرُونَ سَوَادَ الْمُشْرِكِينَ عَلَى رَسُولِ اللَّهِ ﷺ يَأْتِي السَّهْمُ فَيُرمى [[في د، ر أ: "يرمى".]] بِهِ، فَيُصِيبُ أَحَدَهُمْ فَيَقْتُلُهُ، أَوْ يُضْرَبُ عُنُقُهُ فَيُقْتَلُ، فَأَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ [عَزَّ وَجَلَّ] [[زيادة من ر.]] ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ تَوَفَّاهُمُ الْمَلائِكَةُ ظَالِمِي أَنْفُسِهِمْ﴾ رَوَاهُ اللَّيْثُ عَنْ أَبِي الْأَسْوَدِ [[صحيح البخاري برقم (٤٥٩٦) .]] .

وَقَالَ ابْنُ أَبِي حَاتِمٍ: حَدَّثَنَا أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مَنْصُورٍ الرَّمَادِي، حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو أَحْمَدَ -يعني الزبيري- حدثنا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ شَرِيك الْمَكِّيُّ، حَدَّثَنَا عَمْرِو بْنِ دِينَارٍ، عَنْ عِكْرِمَةَ عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ قَالَ: كَانَ قَوْمٌ مِنْ أَهْلِ مَكَّةَ أَسْلَمُوا، وَكَانُوا يَسْتَخِفُونَ بِالْإِسْلَامِ، فَأَخْرَجَهُمُ الْمُشْرِكُونَ يَوْمَ بَدْرٍ مَعَهُمْ، فَأُصِيبَ بَعْضُهُمْ بِفِعْلِ بَعْضٍ [[في ر، أ: "بنبل".]] قَالَ الْمُسْلِمُونَ: كَانَ أَصْحَابُنَا هَؤُلَاءِ مُسْلِمِينَ [[في ر: "مسلمون".]] وَأُكْرِهُوا، فاستَغْفَروا لَهُمْ، فَنَزَلَتْ: ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ تَوَفَّاهُمُ الْمَلائِكَةُ ظَالِمِي أَنْفُسِهِمْ [قَالُوا فِيمَ كُنْتُم﴾ إِلَى آخَرِ] [[زيادة من ر، أ.]] الْآيَةِ، قَالَ: فَكَتَبَ إِلَى مَنْ بَقِيَ مِنَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ بِهَذِهِ الْآيَةِ: لَا عُذْرَ لَهُمْ. قَالَ: فَخَرَجُوا فَلَحِقَهُمُ الْمُشْرِكُونَ فَأَعْطَوْهُمُ الْفِتْنَةَ، فَنَزَلَتْ هَذِهِ [[في أ: "فيهم".]] الْآيَةُ: ﴿وَمِنَ النَّاسِ مَنْ يَقُولُ آمَنَّا بِاللَّهِ﴾ الْآيَةَ [[ورواه الطبراني في تفسيره (٩/١٠٢) حدثنا أحمد بن منصور الرمادي به.]] [الْبَقَرَةِ: ٨] .

وَقَالَ عِكْرِمَةُ: نَزَلَتْ هَذِهِ الْآيَةُ فِي شَبَابٍ مِنْ قُرَيْشٍ، كَانُوا تَكَلَّمُوا بِالْإِسْلَامِ بِمَكَّةَ، مِنْهُمْ: عَلِيُّ بْنُ أُمَيَّةَ بْنِ خَلَف، وَأَبُو قَيْسِ بْنُ الْوَلِيدِ بْنِ الْمُغِيرَةِ، وَأَبُو الْعَاصِ بْنُ مُنَبِّهِ [[في د: "ابن منصور".]] بْنِ الْحَجَّاجِ، وَالْحَارِثُ بْنُ زَمْعة.

وَقَالَ الضَّحَّاكُ: نَزَلَتْ فِي نَاسٍ [[في د، ر: "أناس".]] مِنَ الْمُنَافِقِينَ، تَخَلَّفُوا عَنْ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ ﷺ بمكة، وَخَرَجُوا مَعَ الْمُشْرِكِينَ يَوْمَ بَدْرٍ، فَأُصِيبُوا فِيمَنْ أُصِيبَ فَنَزَلَتْ هَذِهِ [[في أ: "فهذه".]] الْآيَةُ الْكَرِيمَةُ عَامَّةً فِي كُلِّ مَنْ أَقَامَ بَيْنَ ظَهَرَانَيِ الْمُشْرِكِينَ وَهُوَ قَادِرٌ عَلَى الْهِجْرَةِ، وَلَيْسَ مُتَمَكِّنًا مِنْ إِقَامَةِ الدِّينِ، فَهُوَ ظَالِمٌ لِنَفْسِهِ مُرْتَكِبٌ حَرَامًا بِالْإِجْمَاعِ (consensus)، وَبِنَصِّ هَذِهِ الْآيَةِ حَيْثُ يَقُولُ تَعَالَى: ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ تَوَفَّاهُمُ الْمَلائِكَةُ ظَالِمِي أَنْفُسِهِمْ﴾ أَيْ: بِتَرْكِ الْهِجْرَةِ ﴿قَالُوا فِيمَ كُنْتُمْ﴾ أَيْ: لِمَ مَكَثْتُمْ هَاهُنَا وَتَرَكْتُمُ الْهِجْرَةَ؟ ﴿قَالُوا كُنَّا مُسْتَضْعَفِينَ فِي الأرْضِ﴾ أَيْ: لَا نَقْدِرُ عَلَى الْخُرُوجِ مِنَ الْبَلَدِ، وَلَا الذَّهَابِ فِي الْأَرْضِ ﴿قَالُوا أَلَمْ تَكُنْ أَرْضُ اللَّهِ وَاسِعَةً [فَتُهَاجِرُوا فِيهَا فَأُولَئِكَ مَأْوَاهُمْ جَهَنَّمُ وَسَاءَتْ مَصِيرًا] [[زيادة من د، ر، أ، وفي هـ: "الآية".]] ﴾ .

وَقَالَ أَبُو دَاوُدَ: حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ دَاوُدَ بْنِ سُفْيَانَ، حَدَّثَنِي يَحْيَى بْنُ حَسَّانَ، أَخْبَرَنَا سُلَيْمَانُ بْنُ مُوسَى أَبُو دَاوُدَ، حَدَّثَنَا جَعْفَرُ بْنُ سَعْدِ بْنِ سمرة بن جندب، حدثني خبيب [[في ر، أ: "حبيب".]] بن سليمان، عَنْ أَبِيهِ سُلَيْمَانَ بْنِ سَمُرَةَ، عَنْ سَمُرَةَ بن جندب: أما بعد، قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ: "مَنْ جَامَعَ الْمُشْرِكَ وَسَكَنَ مَعَهُ فَإِنَّهُ مِثْلُهُ" [[سنن أبي داود برقم (٢٧٨٧) .]] .

وَقَالَ السُّدِّيُّ: لَمَّا أُسِرَ الْعَبَّاسُ وَعقِيل ونَوْفَل، قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ لِلْعَبَّاسِ: "افْدِ نَفْسَكَ وَابْنَ أَخِيكَ" قَالَ: يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، أَلَمْ نُصَلِّ قِبْلَتَكَ، وَنَشْهَدْ شَهَادَتَكَ؟ قَالَ: "يَا عَبَّاسُ، إِنَّكُمْ خَاصَمْتُمْ فخُصمتم". ثُمَّ تَلَا عَلَيْهِ هَذِهِ الْآيَةَ: ﴿أَلَمْ تَكُنْ أَرْضُ اللَّهِ وَاسِعَةً [فَتُهَاجِرُوا فِيهَا فَأُولَئِكَ مَأْوَاهُمْ جَهَنَّمُ وَسَاءَتْ مَصِيرًا] [[زيادة من ر، أ، وفي هـ: "الآية".]] ﴾ رَوَاهُ ابْنُ أَبِي حَاتِمٍ.

* *

وَقَوْلُهُ: ﴿إِلا الْمُسْتَضْعَفِينَ [مِنَ الرِّجَالِ وَالنِّسَاءِ وَالْوِلْدَانِ لَا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ حِيلَةً وَلا يَهْتَدُونَ سَبِيلا [[زيادة من د، ر، أ، وفي هـ: "إلى آخر الآية".]] ] ﴾ هَذَا عُذْرٌ مِنَ اللَّهِ تَعَالَى لِهَؤُلَاءِ فِي تَرْكِ الْهِجْرَةِ، وَذَلِكَ أَنَّهُمْ لَا يَقْدِرُونَ عَلَى التَّخَلُّصِ مِنْ أَيْدِي الْمُشْرِكِينَ، وَلَوْ قَدَرُوا مَا عَرَفُوا يَسْلُكُونَ الطَّرِيقَ، وَلِهَذَا قَالَ: ﴿لَا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ حِيلَةً وَلا يَهْتَدُونَ سَبِيلا﴾ قَالَ مُجَاهِدٌ وَعِكْرِمَةُ، وَالسُّدِّيُّ: يَعْنِي طَرِيقًا.

* *

وَقَوْلُهُ تَعَالَى: ﴿فَأُولَئِكَ عَسَى اللَّهُ أَنْ يَعْفُوَ عَنْهُمْ﴾ أَيْ: يَتَجَاوَزَ عَنْهُمْ بِتَرْكِ [[في د، أ: "بتركهم".]] الْهِجْرَةِ، وَعَسَى مِنَ اللَّهِ مُوجِبَةٌ ﴿وَكَانَ اللَّهُ عَفُوًّا غَفُورًا [[في ر: "عفوا غفورا" وهو خطأ.]] ﴾ .

قَالَ الْبُخَارِيُّ: حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو نُعَيْم، حَدَّثَنَا شَيْبَان، عَنْ يَحْيَى، عَنْ أَبِي سَلَمَة، عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ قَالَ: بَيْنَا النَّبِيُّ ﷺ يُصَلِّي الْعِشَاءَ إِذْ قَالَ: "سَمِعَ اللَّهُ لِمَنْ حَمِدَهُ" ثُمَّ قَالَ قَبْلَ أَنْ يَسْجُدَ "اللَّهُمَّ نَج [[في ر، أ: "أنج".]] عَيَّاشَ بْنَ أَبِي رَبِيعَةَ، اللَّهُمَّ نَجِّ [[في ر، أ: "أنج".]] سَلَمَةَ بْنَ هِشَامٍ، اللَّهُمَّ نَجِّ [[في ر، أ: "أنج".]] الْوَلِيدَ بْنَ الْوَلِيدِ، اللَّهُمَّ نَج [[في ر، أ: "أنج".]] الْمُسْتَضْعَفِينَ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ، اللَّهُمَّ اشْدُدْ وَطْأَتَكَ عَلَى مُضَر، اللَّهُمَّ اجْعَلْهَا سِنِينَ كسِنِيِّ يُوسُفَ". [[صحيح البخاري برقم (٤٥٩٨) .]]

وَقَالَ ابْنُ أَبِي حَاتِمٍ: حَدَّثَنَا أَبِي، حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو مَعْمَرٍ الْمَقْرِيُّ [[في ر: "المنقري".]] حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ الْوَارِثِ، حَدَّثَنَا عَلِيِّ بْنِ زَيْدٍ، عَنْ سَعِيدِ بْنِ المسَّيب، عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ: أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ﷺ رَفَعَ يَدَهُ بَعْدَمَا سَلَّمَ، وَهُوَ مُسْتَقْبَلٌ الْقِبْلَةَ فَقَالَ: "اللَّهُمَّ خَلِّصِ الْوَلِيدَ بْنَ الْوَلِيدِ، وَعَيَّاشَ بْنَ أَبِي رَبِيعَةَ، وسَلَمة بْنَ هِشَامٍ، وَضَعَفَةَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ الَّذِينَ لَا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ حِيلَةً وَلَا يَهْتَدُونَ سَبِيلًا مِنْ أَيْدِي الْكُفَّارِ" [[وفي إسناده علي بن زيد بن عبد الله بن أبي مليكة ضعيف لا يحتج به، وقد اختلف عليه فيه، كما سيأتي في رواية الطبري.]] .

وَقَالَ ابْنُ جَرِيرٍ: حَدَّثَنَا الْمُثَنَّى، حَدَّثَنَا حَجَّاجٌ، حَدَّثَنَا حَمَّادٌ، عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ زَيْدٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ [[في ر، أ: "عبيد الله".]] -أَوْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ الْقُرَشِيِّ- عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ؛ أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ﷺ كَانَ يَدْعُو فِي دُبُرِ صَلَاةِ الظُّهْرِ: "اللَّهُمَّ خَلِّص الْوَلِيدِ، وَسَلَمَةَ بْنَ هِشَامٍ، وَعَيَّاشَ بْنَ أَبِي رَبِيعَةَ، وَضَعَفَةَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ مِنْ أَيْدِي الْمُشْرِكِينَ الَّذِينَ لَا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ حِيلَةً وَلَا يَهْتَدُونَ سَبِيلًا".

وَلِهَذَا الْحَدِيثِ شَاهِدٌ فِي الصَّحِيحِ مِنْ غَيْرِ هَذَا الْوَجْهِ كَمَا تَقَدَّمَ [[تفسير الطبري (٩/١١٠) وإسناده ضعيف.]] .

وَقَالَ عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ: أَنْبَأَنَا [[في أ: "أخبرنا".]] ابْنُ عُيَيْنَةَ، عَنْ عُبَيْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ أَبِي يَزِيدَ قَالَ: سَمِعْتُ ابْنَ عَبَّاسٍ يَقُولُ: كُنْتُ أَنَا وَأُمِّي مِنَ الْمُسْتَضْعَفِينَ مِنَ النِّسَاءِ وَالْوَلَدَانِ [[تفسير عبد الرزاق (١/١٦٦) .]]

وَقَالَ الْبُخَارِيُّ: أَنْبَأَنَا أَبُو النُّعْمَانِ، حَدَّثَنَا حَمَّادُ بْنُ زَيْدٍ، عَنْ أَيُّوبَ، عَنْ ابْنِ أَبِي مُلَيْكَة، عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ: ﴿إِلا الْمُسْتَضْعَفِينَ﴾ قَالَ: كَانَتْ أُمِّي مِمَّنْ عَذَر اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ [[صحيح البخاري برقم (٤٥٩٧) .]] .

* *

وَقَوْلُهُ: ﴿وَمَنْ يُهَاجِرْ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ يَجِدْ فِي الأرْضِ مُرَاغَمًا كَثِيرًا وَسَعَةً﴾ هذا تحريض على الْهِجْرَةِ، وَتَرْغِيبٌ فِي مُفَارَقَةِ الْمُشْرِكِينَ، وَأَنَّ الْمُؤْمِنَ حَيْثُمَا ذَهَبَ وَجَدَ عَنْهُمْ مَنْدُوحَةً وَمَلْجَأً يَتَحَصَّنُ فِيهِ، وَ"الْمُرَاغَمُ" مَصْدَرٌ، تَقُولُ الْعَرَبُ: رَاغَمَ فُلَانُ قَوْمَهُ مُرَاغَمًا وَمُرَاغَمَةً، قَالَ نَابِغَةُ [[في أ: "نابغة في بني جعدة.]] بَنِي جَعْدَةَ [[البيت في تفسير الطبري (١٠/١١٢) واللسان مادة (رغم) .]]

كَطَوْدٍ يُلاذُ بأرْكَانِه ... عَزيز المُرَاغَم وَالْمَهْربِ ...

وَقَالَ ابْنُ عَبَّاسٍ: "المراغَم": التَّحَوُّلُ مِنْ أَرْضٍ إِلَى أَرْضٍ. وَكَذَا رُوي عَنِ الضَّحَّاكِ وَالرَّبِيعِ بْنِ أَنَسٍ، الثَّوْرِيِّ، وَقَالَ مُجَاهِدٌ: ﴿مُرَاغَمًا كَثِيرًا﴾ يَعْنِي: مُتَزَحْزَحًا عَمَّا يُكْرَهُ. وَقَالَ سُفْيَانُ بْنُ عُيَيْنَةَ: ﴿مُرَاغَمًا كَثِيرًا﴾ يَعْنِي: بُرُوجًا.

وَالظَّاهِرُ -وَاللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ- أَنَّهُ [[في أ: "أن المراغم هو".]] التَّمَنُّعُ الَّذِي يُتَحصَّن بِهِ، وَيُرَاغَمُ بِهِ الْأَعْدَاءُ.

قَوْلُهُ: ﴿وَسَعَةً﴾ يَعْنِي: الرِّزْقَ. قَالَهُ غَيْرُ وَاحِدٍ، مِنْهُمْ: قَتَادَةُ، حَيْثُ قَالَ فِي قَوْلِهِ: ﴿يَجِدْ فِي الأرْضِ مُرَاغَمًا كَثِيرًا وَسَعَةً﴾ إِي، وَاللَّهِ، مِنَ الضَّلَالَةِ إِلَى الْهُدَى، وَمِنِ الْقِلَّةِ إِلَى الْغِنَى.

* *

وَقَوْلُهُ: ﴿وَمَنْ يَخْرُجْ مِنْ بَيْتِهِ مُهَاجِرًا إِلَى اللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ ثُمَّ يُدْرِكْهُ الْمَوْتُ فَقَدْ وَقَعَ أَجْرُهُ عَلَى اللَّهِ﴾ أَيْ: وَمَنْ خَرَجَ مِنْ مَنْزِلِهِ بِنِيَّةِ الْهِجْرَةِ، فَمَاتَ فِي أَثْنَاءِ الطَّرِيقِ، فَقَدْ حَصَلَ لَهُ مِنَ [[في أ: "عند".]] اللَّهِ ثَوَابُ مَنْ هَاجَرَ، كَمَا ثَبَتَ فِي الصَّحِيحَيْنِ وَغَيْرِهِمَا مِنَ الصِّحَاحِ وَالْمَسَانِيدِ وَالسُّنَنِ، مِنْ طَرِيقِ يَحْيَى بْنِ سَعِيدٍ الْأَنْصَارِيِّ [[في أ: "القطان".]] عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ التَّيْمِيِّ، عَنْ عَلْقَمَةَ بْنِ وَقّاص اللَّيْثِيِّ، عَنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ الْخَطَّابِ قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وسلم: "إنما الْأَعْمَالُ بِالنِّيَّاتِ، وَإِنَّمَا لِكُلِّ امْرِئٍ مَا نَوَى، فَمَنْ كَانَتْ هِجْرَتُهُ إِلَى اللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ، فَهِجْرَتُهُ إِلَى اللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ، وَمَنْ كَانَتْ هِجْرَتُهُ لِدُنْيَا يُصِيبُهَا، أَوِ امْرَأَةٍ يَتَزَوَّجُهَا، فَهِجْرَتُهُ إِلَى مَا هَاجَرَ إِلَيْهِ" [[صحيح البخاري برقم (١، ٥٤) وصحيح مسلم برقم (١٩٠٧) وسنن أبي داود برقم (٢٢٠١) وسن الترمذي برقم (١٦٤٧) ، وسنن النسائي (١/٥٩) وسنن ابن ماجه برقم (٤٢٢٧) ومسند أحمد (١/٢٥) ومسند الحميدي (١/١٦) ومسند الطيالسي (٢/٢٧) "منحة المعبود".]] .

وَهَذَا عَامٌّ فِي الْهِجْرَةِ وَفِي كُلِّ الْأَعْمَالِ. وَمِنْهُ الْحَدِيثُ الثَّابِتُ فِي الصَّحِيحَيْنِ [[صحيح البخاري برقم (٣٤٧٠) وصحيح مسلم برقم (٢٧٦٦) .]] فِي الرَّجُلِ الَّذِي قَتَلَ تِسْعَةً وَتِسْعِينَ نَفْسًا. ثُمَّ أَكْمَلَ بِذَلِكَ الْعَابِدِ الْمِائَةَ، ثُمَّ سَأَلَ عَالِمًا: هَلْ لَهُ مِنْ تَوْبَةٍ؟ فَقَالَ: وَمَنْ يَحُول بَيْنَكَ وَبَيْنَ التَّوْبَةِ؟ ثُمَّ أَرْشَدَهُ إِلَى أَنْ يَتَحَوَّلَ مِنْ بَلَدِهِ إِلَى بَلَدٍ آخَرَ يَعْبُدُ اللَّهَ فِيهِ، فَلَمَّا ارْتَحَلَ مِنْ بَلَدِهِ مُهَاجِرًا إِلَى الْبَلَدِ الْآخَرِ، أَدْرَكَهُ الْمَوْتُ فِي أَثْنَاءِ الطَّرِيقِ، فَاخْتَصَمَتْ فِيهِ مَلَائِكَةُ الرَّحْمَةِ وَمَلَائِكَةُ الْعَذَابِ، فَقَالَ هَؤُلَاءِ: إِنَّهُ جَاءَ تَائِبًا. وَقَالَ هَؤُلَاءِ: إِنَّهُ لَمْ يَصِلْ بَعْدُ. فَأُمِرُوا أَنَّ يَقِيسُوا مَا بَيْنَ الْأَرْضَيْنِ فَإِلَى أَيَّتِهِمَا [[في د، ر: "أيها"، وفي أ: "أيهما".]] كَانَ أَقْرَبُ كَانَ [[في د، ر: "فهو".]] مِنْهَا، فَأَمْرَ اللَّهُ هَذِهِ أَنْ يُقرب [[في د: "تقترب"، وفي ر: "تقرب".]] مِنْ هَذِهِ، وَهَذِهِ أَنْ تَبْعُدَ [[في د: "تبتعد".]] فَوَجَدُوهُ أَقْرَبَ إِلَى الْأَرْضِ الَّتِي هَاجَرَ إِلَيْهَا بِشِبْر، فَقَبَضَتْهُ مَلَائِكَةُ الرَّحْمَةِ. وَفِي رِوَايَةٍ: أَنَّهُ لَمَّا جَاءَهُ الْمَوْتُ نَاءَ بِصَدْرِهِ إِلَى الْأَرْضِ [[في د: "البلد".]] الَّتِي هَاجَرَ إِلَيْهَا.

Imam Ahmad said: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Atik, from his father Abdullah ibn Atik, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "Whoever leaves his house as an emigrant [in A: "as a mujahid"] in the way of Allah"—then he gestured with these three fingers, the middle, the index and the thumb, joined them together, and said: "and where are the mujahidun?"—"and he falls from his mount and dies, then his reward has fallen upon Allah; or a creature stings him and he dies, then his reward has fallen upon Allah; or he dies in his bed, then his reward has fallen upon Allah." By Allah, it is a word I have not heard from any of the Arabs before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. "And whoever is killed suddenly (qa'san), then he has merited the return (al-ma'ab)."

[Musnad (4/36). Al-Haythami said in Majma' al-Zawa'id (5/260): "In it is Muhammad ibn Ishaq, who is a mudallis, and the rest of its narrators are trustworthy."]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur'ah narrated to us, Abd al-Rahman ibn Abd al-Malik ibn Shaybah al-Hizami [in A: "al-Khuzami"] narrated to us, Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Mughirah al-Hizami [in A: "al-Khuzami"] narrated to me, from al-Mundhir ibn Abdullah, from Hisham ibn Urwah, from his father, that al-Zubayr ibn al-Awwam said: Khalid ibn Hizam [in A: "Ibn Haram"] emigrated to the land of Abyssinia, and a snake bit him on the way and he died. Concerning him was revealed: ﴿And whoever leaves his house as an emigrant to Allah and His Messenger, and then death overtakes him, his reward has indeed fallen upon Allah, and Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful﴾. Al-Zubayr said: I used to expect him and await his arrival while I was in the land of Abyssinia. Nothing grieved me as much as his death when it reached me, because few of those who emigrated from Quraysh were without some of their family or relatives with them, and there was no one with me from the Banu Asad ibn Abd al-'Uzza, nor did I hope for anyone other than him.

This report is very strange (gharib jiddan), for the reason of its strangeness is also as Ibn Hajar said: the one about whom this verse was revealed was Jundub ibn Damrah, and his report will come right after this. Moreover, this story is Meccan, while the revelation of this verse is Medinan. Perhaps he intended that the verse was revealed to encompass his ruling along with others, even if that was not the occasion of revelation. And Allah knows best.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Sulayman ibn Dawud, client of Abdullah ibn Ja'far, narrated to us, Sahl ibn Uthman narrated to us, Abd al-Rahman [in R: "Abd al-Rahim"] ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from al-Ash'ath [in R: "Ash'ath"]—he is Ibn Sawwar—from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Damrah ibn Jundub set out toward the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and died on the way before reaching the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, so this was revealed: ﴿And whoever leaves his house as an emigrant to Allah and His Messenger [then death overtakes him, his reward has indeed fallen upon Allah, and Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful]﴾.

[Abu Ya'la in his Musnad (5/81) and al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (11/272) narrated it through Ash'ath ibn Sawwar. Al-Haythami, after attributing it to Abu Ya'la alone, said: "Its narrators are trustworthy, but in its chain is Ash'ath ibn Sawwar, who is weak."]

And it was narrated to us by my father: Abdullah ibn Raja' narrated to us, Isra'il informed us, from Salim, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Abu Damrah ibn al-'Is al-Zuraqi, who was blind in his sight and was in Mecca. When the verse was revealed: ﴿except the oppressed men, women and children who are unable to devise a plan﴾, I said: "Indeed I am wealthy, and indeed I am capable of a plan." So he prepared himself, intending the Prophet ﷺ, but death overtook him at al-Tan'im, and this verse was revealed: ﴿And whoever leaves his house as an emigrant to Allah and His Messenger, then death overtakes him, [his reward has indeed fallen upon Allah, and Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful]﴾.

[Tafsir Ibn Abi Hatim (q.176). This report has also been narrated by other routes as a mursal (disconnected) report: Sa'id ibn Mansur in his Sunan, no. (685), said: Hushaym informed us, from Abu Bishr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, as a mursal. And al-Tabari in his Tafsir (9/118) narrated it through Qays ibn al-Rabi', from Salim, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, as a mursal.]

Al-Hafiz Abu Ya'la said: Ibrahim ibn Ziyad Sabalan narrated to us, Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, from Humayd ibn Abi Humayd, from Ata' ibn Yazid al-Laythi, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever sets out for Hajj and dies, the reward of the one performing Hajj will be recorded for him until the Day of Resurrection; whoever sets out for 'Umrah and dies, the reward of the one performing 'Umrah will be recorded for him until the Day of Resurrection; and whoever sets out as a warrior in the way of Allah and dies, the reward of the warrior will be recorded for him until the Day of Resurrection."

This is a strange hadith from this route (gharib min hadha al-wajh).

[Musnad Abi Ya'la (1/238). In its chain is Jamil ibn Abi Maymunah, whom none declared trustworthy except Ibn Hibban, and Ibn Ishaq is a mudallis who narrated with 'an'anah.]

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And when you travel in the land﴾, meaning, when you journey through the lands, as He says: ﴿He knows that there will be among you those who are ill, and others who travel through the land seeking of Allah's bounty, and others who fight in the cause of Allah [[Addition from manuscripts R and A.]]﴾ [Al-Muzzammil: 20].
* *
As for His saying: ﴿there is no blame upon you for shortening the prayer﴾, meaning, lightening it, either in its quantity, by reducing the four-rak'ah prayer to two rak'ahs, as the majority (al-Jumhur) understood from this verse. They used it as evidence for shortening the prayer during travel, though they differed on this:

Some said that the journey must be for an act of obedience, such as jihad, Hajj, 'Umrah, seeking knowledge, visiting (relatives), or other such purposes. This is narrated from Ibn 'Umar and 'Ata', and it is reported from Malik in one narration, for the apparent meaning of His saying: ﴿if you fear that those who disbelieve will attack you﴾.

Others said that a journey of obedience is not required, but it must be permissible (mubah), based on His saying: ﴿But whoever is compelled by necessity, neither desiring it nor exceeding the limit, then indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful [[Addition from manuscripts R and A.]]﴾ [Al-Ma'idah: 3], which permits him to eat carrion when compelled, on condition that he is not disobedient by his journey. This is the view of al-Shafi'i, Ahmad, and other imams.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah said: Waki' narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us, from Ibrahim, who said: A man came and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I am a merchant who frequently travels to Bahrain." "So he commanded him to pray two rak'ahs." This is a mursal report (one in which the Successor omits the Companion from the chain).

Others said that merely travelling suffices, whether it is permissible or forbidden. Even if someone went out to commit highway robbery and terrorize travellers, he may still shorten the prayer, because the essential travel exists. This is the view of Abu Hanifah, may Allah have mercy on him, al-Thawri, and Dawud, based on the generality of the verse. The majority disagreed with them. As for His saying: ﴿if you fear that those who disbelieve will attack you﴾, this may have been stated in the form of what usually happens at the time the verse was revealed, for at the beginning of Islam after the Hijrah, most of their journeys were fearful. Indeed, they would only set out for a general campaign (ghazw 'amm) or a specific expedition (sariyyah khassah), and at all other times there was war against Islam and its people. When a statement is made in the form of what usually happens, or in reference to a particular incident, it carries no implied restriction (mafhum), like His saying: ﴿And do not compel your slave girls to prostitution if they desire chastity﴾ [An-Nur: 33], and like His saying: ﴿and your stepdaughters who are in your guardianship, born of your wives...﴾ [An-Nisa': 23].

Imam Ahmad said: Ibn Idris narrated to us, Ibn Juraij narrated to us, from Ibn Abi 'Ammar, from 'Abdullah ibn Babayh, from Ya'la ibn Umayyah, who said: I asked 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, saying: "﴿There is no blame upon you for shortening the prayer if you fear that those who disbelieve will attack you﴾, and yet people are now secure?" 'Umar said to me: "I wondered about the same thing you wondered about, so I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about it, and he said: 'It is a charity which Allah has given you, so accept His charity.'"

Likewise Muslim and the authors of the Sunan related it from the hadith of Ibn Juraij, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Abdullah ibn Abi 'Ammar, with the same chain. At-Tirmidhi said: "This is a hasan sahih hadith." 'Ali ibn al-Madini said: "This is a sahih hadith from the narration of 'Umar, and it is not known except through this route, and its narrators are well known." [[Al-Musnad (1/25), Sahih Muslim no. (686), Sunan Abi Dawud no. (1199), Sunan al-Nasa'i (3/116), Sunan Ibn Majah no. (1065).]]

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah said: Abu Nu'aym narrated to us, Malik ibn Mighwal narrated to us, from Abu Hanzalah al-Haddha', who said: I asked Ibn 'Umar about the prayer during travel, and he said: "Two rak'ahs." I said: "Where is His saying: ﴿if you fear that those who disbelieve will attack you﴾, when we are secure?" He said: "It is the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ." [[Al-Musannaf (2/447), and Ahmad related it in his Musnad (2/31) through Yazid ibn Isma'il from Abu Hanzalah from Ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him.]]

Ibn Mardawayh said: 'Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa narrated to us, 'Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id narrated to us, Minjab narrated to us, Shurayk narrated to us, from Qays ibn Wahb, from Abu al-Waddak, who said: I asked Ibn 'Umar about the two rak'ahs in travel? He said: "It is a concession (rukhsah) that came down from heaven, so if you wish, reject it."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah said: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, Ibn 'Awn narrated to us, from Ibn Sirin, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "We prayed with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ between Makkah and Madinah, while we were secure and feared nothing between them, two rak'ahs, two rak'ahs."

Al-Nasa'i related it likewise from Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la, from Khalid al-Haddha', from 'Abdullah ibn 'Awn, with the same wording. [[Al-Musannaf (2/448) and Sunan al-Nasa'i (3/117).]] Abu 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-Barr said: "Likewise it was related by Ayyub, Hisham, and Yazid ibn Ibrahim al-Tustari, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, from the Prophet ﷺ, similarly."

I say: Likewise at-Tirmidhi and an-Nasa'i both related it from Qutaybah, from Hushaym, from Mansur ibn Zadhan, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, from Ibn 'Abbas, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ left Madinah for Makkah, fearing none but the Lord of the Worlds, and he prayed two rak'ahs. Then at-Tirmidhi said: "Sahih." [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (547) and Sunan al-Nasa'i (3/117).]]

Al-Bukhari said: Abu Ma'mar narrated to us, 'Abd al-Warith narrated to us, Yahya ibn Abi Ishaq narrated to us, who said: I heard Anas say: "We went out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ from Madinah to Makkah, and he prayed two rak'ahs, two rak'ahs, until we returned to Madinah." I asked: "Did you stay in Makkah for any length of time?" He said: "We stayed there ten (days)."

Likewise the rest of the group related it through various routes from Yahya ibn Abi Ishaq al-Hadrami, with the same wording. [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (1081), Sahih Muslim no. (693), Sunan Abi Dawud no. (1233), Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (548), Sunan al-Nasa'i (3/118), Sunan Ibn Majah no. (1077).]]

Imam Ahmad said: Waki' narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Haritha ibn Wahb al-Khuza'i, who said: "I prayed with the Prophet ﷺ the Zuhr and the 'Asr at Mina, when people were most numerous and most secure, two rak'ahs."

The group, except Ibn Majah, related it through various routes from Abu Ishaq al-Sabi'i, from him, with the same wording. [[Al-Musnad (4/306), Sahih al-Bukhari no. (1083), Sahih Muslim no. (696), Sunan Abi Dawud no. (1965), Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (882), Sunan al-Nasa'i (3/120).]] The wording of al-Bukhari is: Abu al-Walid narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, Abu Ishaq informed us, I heard Haritha ibn Wahb say: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ led us in prayer at Mina, when it was at its most secure, two rak'ahs."

Al-Bukhari said: Musaddad narrated to us, Yahya narrated to us, 'Ubaydullah narrated to us, Nafi' informed us, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar, who said: "I prayed with the Prophet ﷺ two rak'ahs, and with Abu Bakr and 'Umar, and with 'Uthman for the early part of his caliphate, then he completed it (four rak'ahs)."

Likewise Muslim related it from the hadith of Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Qattan [al-Ansari] [[Addition from manuscript A.]], with the same wording. [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (1082), Sahih Muslim no. (694), Sunan al-Nasa'i (3/121).]]

Al-Bukhari said: Qutaybah narrated to us, 'Abd al-Wahid narrated to us, from al-A'mash, Ibrahim narrated to us, I heard 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Yazid say: "'Uthman ibn 'Affan, may Allah be pleased with him, led us in prayer at Mina with four rak'ahs. This was mentioned to 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, and he said, 'Inna lillah wa inna ilayhi raji'un,' then said: 'I prayed with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at Mina two rak'ahs, and I prayed with Abu Bakr at Mina two rak'ahs, and I prayed with 'Umar ibn al-Khattab at Mina two rak'ahs. Would that my share of four rak'ahs were two accepted rak'ahs.'"

Al-Bukhari also related it from the hadith of al-Thawri, from al-A'mash, with the same wording. Muslim related it through various routes from him, among them from Qutaybah as previously mentioned. [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (1084) and (1657), Sahih Muslim no. (695).]]

These hadiths clearly indicate that the shortening of the prayer is not conditional upon the presence of fear. For this reason, some scholars said that the intended meaning of shortening here is the shortening of the manner (qasr al-kayfiyyah), not the quantity (qasr al-kammiyyah). This is the view of Mujahid, al-Dahhak, and al-Suddi, as will be explained later. They also relied on what Imam Malik related from Salih ibn Kaysan, from 'Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, from 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, that she said: "The prayer was prescribed as two rak'ahs, two rak'ahs, both in travel and at home. Then the travel prayer was left as it was, and the prayer at home was increased."

This hadith was related by al-Bukhari from 'Abdullah ibn Yusuf al-Tinnisi, by Muslim from Yahya ibn Yahya, by Abu Dawud from al-Qa'nabi, and by al-Nasa'i from Qutaybah, all four from Malik, with the same wording. [[Al-Muwatta', on shortening the prayer during travel, no. (8), (1/146), Sahih al-Bukhari no. (350), Sahih Muslim no. (685), Sunan Abi Dawud no. (1198), Sunan al-Nasa'i (1/225).]]

They said: If the original prayer during travel is two rak'ahs, then how can the intended meaning of shortening here be shortening in quantity? For what is the original form cannot be described with His saying: ﴿there is no blame upon you for shortening the prayer﴾?

Even clearer in indicating this is what Imam Ahmad related: Waki' narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, and 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Zubayd al-Yami, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, from 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "The travel prayer is two rak'ahs, the Adha prayer is two rak'ahs, the Fitr prayer is two rak'ahs, and the Friday prayer is two rak'ahs, a complete prayer, not shortened, upon the tongue of Muhammad ﷺ."

Likewise an-Nasa'i, Ibn Majah, and Ibn Hibban in his Sahih related it through various routes from Zubayd al-Yami, with the same wording. [[Al-Musnad (1/37), Sunan al-Nasa'i (3/111), Sunan Ibn Majah no. (1063), Sahih Ibn Hibban (4/197).]]

This is a chain that meets the conditions of Muslim. Muslim, in the introduction to his book, judged that Ibn Abi Layla heard from 'Umar. It is stated explicitly in this hadith and elsewhere, and this is the correct view, if Allah wills. However, Yahya ibn Ma'in, Abu Hatim, and al-Nasa'i said that he did not hear from him. In light of this as well, in some routes of Abu Ya'la al-Mawsili, through the route of al-Thawri, from Zubayd, from 'Abd al-Rahman [ibn Abi Layla] [[Addition from manuscript A.]], from a trustworthy narrator, from 'Umar, he mentioned it. In Ibn Majah's route through Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad ibn Abi al-Ja'd, from Zubayd, from 'Abd al-Rahman, from Ka'b ibn 'Ujrah, from 'Umar, with the same wording. And Allah knows best. [[See Sahih Muslim, introduction (1/34), al-Marasil of Ibn Abi Hatim (125), and the History of al-Duri from Yahya ibn Ma'in (2/356). The correct view is that 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla did not hear from 'Umar. Rather, Ibn Ma'in said in a narration of Ibn Abi Shaybah about him: he did not hear from 'Umar or 'Uthman, but he heard from 'Ali. See also Tahdhib al-Kamal of al-Mizzi (17/376) and the commentary of Dr. Bashshar 'Awwad upon it.]]

Muslim, in his Sahih, and Abu Dawud, al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah narrated from the hadith of Abu 'Awana al-Wadday ibn 'Abd Allah al-Yashkuri (Muslim and al-Nasa'i add: and Ayyub ibn 'A'idh), both from Bukayr ibn al-Akhnas, from Mujahid, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abbas, who said: "Allah prescribed the prayer through the tongue of your Prophet: four rak'ahs when at home, two rak'ahs when travelling, and one rak'ah in a time of fear." [This was narrated by Waki' and Rawh ibn 'Ubada from Usama ibn Zayd al-Laythi: "al-Hasan ibn Muslim ibn Yasaf narrated to me, from Tawus, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Allah and His Messenger ﷺ prescribed the prayer at home as four rak'ahs and while travelling as two rak'ahs."] [[Addition from A.]] Just as the prayer is performed at home with its sunnah prayers before and after, so it is performed while travelling. [[Sahih Muslim, no. 687; Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 1247; Sunan al-Nasa'i (3/169); Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 1068.]]

Ibn Majah also narrated it from the hadith of Usama ibn Zayd, from Tawus himself. [[Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 1072.]]

So this is established from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with both of them. [[In R: "from him."]] It does not contradict what was reported earlier from 'A'isha, because she reported that the original form of the prayer was two rak'ahs, but more was added to the prayer at home. Once that was settled, it is correct to say that the obligatory prayer at home is four rak'ahs, as Ibn 'Abbas said, and Allah knows best. However, the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas and that of 'A'isha agree that the prayer while travelling is two rak'ahs, and that it is complete, not shortened, as is stated explicitly in the hadith of 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him. If that is so, then the meaning of Allah's words ﴿So there is no blame upon you if you shorten the prayer﴾ is the shortening of its form (qasr al-kayfiyyah), as in the prayer of fear. For this reason He said: ﴿if you fear that those who disbelieve may attack you. Indeed, the disbelievers are to you a clear enemy﴾.

For this reason He said after it: ﴿And when you are among them and lead them in prayer, let a group of them stand with you﴾ [[Addition from R, A.]] and so on [[In R, A: "to its end."]]. So He clarified here the purpose of the shortening, and mentioned its description and manner. For this reason, when al-Bukhari (the author of the Sahih) arranged the chapter on the prayer of fear (salat al-khawf, the prayer performed in a state of danger), he opened it with Allah's words: ﴿And when you travel through the land, there is no blame upon you if you shorten the prayer﴾ up to His words: ﴿Indeed, Allah has prepared for the disbelievers a humiliating punishment﴾.

Juwaybir said, from al-Dahhak, regarding Allah's words ﴿So there is no blame upon you if you shorten the prayer﴾: "That is during combat, when a rider prays two takbirs wherever his face is directed."

Asbat said, from al-Suddi, regarding Allah's words ﴿And when you travel through the land, there is no blame upon you if you shorten the prayer, if you fear...﴾ up to the end of the verse: "When the prayer is performed as two rak'ahs while travelling, it is complete; shortening is not permissible, except if you fear that those who disbelieve may tempt you away from the prayer. Then the shortening is one rak'ah."

Ibn Abi Najih said, from Mujahid: ﴿So there is no blame upon you if you shorten the prayer﴾ refers to the day when the Prophet ﷺ and his companions were at 'Usfan while the polytheists were at Dajnan, and they met. The Prophet ﷺ then led his companions in the noon prayer as four rak'ahs, with their bowing, prostrating and standing all together. The polytheists then intended to raid their goods and baggage.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated this. Ibn Jarir also narrated it from Mujahid and al-Suddi, and from Jabir and Ibn 'Umar, and he chose this view too, for after citing the views on this matter he said: "And this is the correct view." Ibn Jarir also said: Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Hakam narrated to me, Ibn Abi Fudayk narrated to us, Ibn Abi Dhi'b narrated to us, from Ibn Shihab, from Umayya ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Khalid ibn Usayd, that he said to 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar: "We find in the Book of Allah the shortening of the prayer of fear, but we do not find the shortening of the prayer of the traveller?" 'Abd Allah replied: "We found our Prophet ﷺ doing an action, and we act by it."

So he called the prayer of fear "shortened" and applied the verse to it, not to the shortening of the traveller's prayer. Ibn 'Umar agreed with this, and he argued for shortening the prayer while travelling by the Lawgiver's practice, not by the explicit text of the Qur'an.

Clearer than this is what Ibn Jarir also narrated: Ahmad ibn al-Walid al-Qurashi narrated to me, Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Shu'ba narrated to us, from Simak al-Hanafi: "I asked Ibn 'Umar about the prayer while travelling, and he said: 'Two rak'ahs, complete, not shortened. Shortening is only the prayer of fear (salat al-makhafah).' I asked: 'And what is the prayer of fear?' He said: 'The imam leads one group in one rak'ah, then these go to the position of those, and those come to the position of these, and he leads them in one rak'ah. So the imam has two rak'ahs, and each group has one rak'ah, one rak'ah.'" [[Tafsir al-Tabari (9/134).]]

The prayer of fear has many forms. Sometimes the enemy is in the direction of the qiblah (Ka'bah), and sometimes it is not in that direction. The prayer may be four-unit (rak'ah), sometimes three-unit as in Maghrib, and sometimes two-unit as in Subh (Fajr) and the prayer of travel. Sometimes they pray in congregation (jama'ah), and sometimes the fighting is so close that they cannot gather in congregation. Instead, they pray individually (furada), facing the qiblah or not facing it, on foot or on horseback, and in this state they may walk and strike blow after blow during the prayer itself.

Some scholars said: in this state they pray one rak'ah, based on the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas mentioned earlier, and this was the view of Ahmad ibn Hanbal. Al-Mundhiri said in al-Hawashi: this was also the view of 'Ata', Jabir, al-Hasan, Mujahid, al-Hakam, Qatadah and Hammad. Tawus and al-Dahhak also held this view.

Abu 'Asim al-'Abbadi [in manuscript r: "al-'Adi"] related from Muhammad ibn Nasr al-Marwazi that he held that the Subh prayer is reduced to one rak'ah in times of fear. Ibn Hazm also held this view.

Ishaq ibn Rahawayh said: "At the time of close combat (musayafah), one rak'ah suffices for you, which you perform by gesturing (ima'). If you cannot do even that, then one prostration suffices, because it is a remembrance of Allah."

Others said: one takbir suffices. Perhaps he meant one rak'ah, as stated by Ahmad ibn Hanbal and his companions. However, those who relate this view relate it according to its apparent meaning, namely that one takbir is sufficient, as is the position of Ishaq ibn Rahawayh. This was also the view of al-Amir 'Abd al-Wahhab ibn Bukht al-Makki, to the point that he said: "If one is unable to perform the takbir, he should not abandon it in his heart," meaning with the intention (niyyah). This was related by Sa'id ibn Mansur in his Sunan from Isma'il ibn 'Ayyash, from Shu'ayb ibn Dinar, from him. And Allah knows best.

Some scholars permitted delaying the prayer because of the excuse of fighting and the urgency of engagement, as the Prophet (ﷺ) delayed the 'Asr prayer on the Day of the Confederates (al-Ahzab). It was said that he also delayed the Zuhr; he prayed both after sunset, then prayed Maghrib and then 'Isha' after them. He also said, after that, on the Day of Banu Qurayzah, when he dispatched the army to them: "None of you should pray 'Asr except at Banu Qurayzah." The time for prayer came upon them along the way. Some of them said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not intend for us to hasten the march only, and did not intend for us to delay the prayer beyond its time." So they prayed at its time on the road. Others delayed 'Asr and prayed it at Banu Qurayzah after sunset. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not rebuke either group. [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (946) and Sahih Muslim no. (1770) from the hadith of 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both.]

We have discussed this in the book on the Sirah, and we explained that those who prayed 'Asr at its proper time were closer to the truth in reality, although the others were also excused. The argument here concerns their excuse for delaying the prayer for the sake of jihad and hastening to besiege those who broke the covenant from the accursed group, the Jews.

As for the majority (jumhur), they said: all of this has been abrogated (mansukh) by the prayer of fear, because it had not yet been revealed. When it was revealed, the delay of the prayer for this reason was abrogated. This is clear in the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, which al-Shafi'i and the authors of the Sunan related. However, what al-Bukhari, may Allah have mercy on him, related in his Sahih creates a difficulty for this view, where he said:

"Chapter: Prayer at the time of storming fortresses and meeting the enemy." Al-Awza'i said: If the conquest has become imminent and they cannot pray, they should pray by gesture, each person for himself. If they cannot even gesture, they delay the prayer until the fighting subsides or they feel safe, and then they pray two rak'ahs. If they cannot do that, they pray one rak'ah and two prostrations. If they cannot do even that, the takbir does not suffice for them, and they delay it until they feel safe. Makhul also said this. Anas ibn Malik said: "I was present at the storming of the fortress of Tustar at the break of dawn, and the fighting intensified, so they could not pray. We did not pray until after the sun had risen high, and then we prayed it with Abu Musa, and it was opened for us." Anas said: "That prayer does not delight me more than the world and all that is in it." [Related by al-Bukhari as a suspended narration (ta'liq) (2/434).]

End of what he mentioned. Then he followed it with the hadith of the delay of the prayer on the Day of the Confederates, then with the hadith of his command to them not to pray 'Asr except at Banu Qurayzah, and it seems he preferred this, and Allah knows best.

For one who inclines to this view, he may argue from the conduct of Abu Musa and his companions on the day of the conquest of Tustar, since it is generally well known. However, that occurred during the caliphate (imarah) of 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, and it is not reported that he, or any of the Companions, denounced them. And Allah knows best.

[Wa] [addition from d.] These scholars said: the prayer of fear was legislated at the time of the Trench (al-Khandaq), because Dhat al-Riqa' took place before the Trench according to the view of the majority of the scholars of biography and military expeditions (siyar and maghazi). Among those who explicitly stated this were Muhammad ibn Ishaq, Musa ibn 'Uqbah, al-Waqidi, Muhammad ibn Sa'd his scribe, Khalifah ibn Khayyat, and others. [See: al-Sirah al-Nabawiyyah of Ibn Hisham (2/203), al-Maghazi of al-Waqidi (1/335), and al-Tabaqat al-Kubra of Ibn Sa'd (2/61).] But al-Bukhari and others said: Dhat al-Riqa' took place after the Trench, based on the hadith of Abu Musa, and he [Abu Musa] did not come except at Khaybar. And Allah knows best.

It is astonishing, utterly astonishing, that al-Muzani, Abu Yusuf the judge, and Ibrahim ibn Isma'il ibn 'Ulayyah went to the view that the prayer of fear was abrogated by the Prophet's delaying of the prayer on the day of the Trench. This is extremely strange. The hadiths have been established, after the Trench, concerning the prayer of fear. Delaying the prayer on that day is better and closer to being interpreted as what Makhul and al-Awza'i said. And Allah knows best.

So His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And when you are among them and establish prayer for them﴾ means: when you lead them in prayer during the prayer of fear. This is a different situation from the first, for that [situation] is shortened to one rak'ah, as the hadith indicates: individually, on foot, on horseback, facing the qiblah or not facing it. Then he mentioned the situation of gathering and following one imam. How excellent is the evidence used by those who hold that congregation is obligatory from this noble verse, since many actions were excused for the sake of congregation. Had it not been obligatory, that would not have been permissible. As for one who argues from this verse that the prayer of fear was abrogated after the Prophet (ﷺ), because of His saying ﴿And when you are among them﴾, and that after him this condition ceases to exist, this is a weak argument. It may be answered in the same way as the argument of those who withheld zakat, who relied on His saying: ﴿Take from their wealth a charity by which you purify them and cause them to grow, and invoke blessings upon them. Indeed, your invocation is a comfort for them﴾ [At-Tawbah: 103]. They said: "We do not give our zakat to anyone after him (ﷺ); rather we distribute it ourselves to whom we see fit, and we do not give it to one whose prayer (salah), meaning his supplication, is a comfort for us." Nevertheless, the Companions rebutted them, refused this argument, compelled them to pay zakat, and fought those among them who withheld it.

Let us first mention the occasion of revelation (sabab al-nuzul) of this noble verse before mentioning its description:

Ibn Jarir said: al-Muthanna related to me, Ishaq related to us, 'Abdullah ibn Hashim related to us, Sayf informed us [in manuscript a: "Sufyan"], from Abu Rawq, from Abu Ayyub, from 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: A group from Banu al-Najjar asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), saying: "O Messenger of Allah, we travel through the land, so how should we pray?" So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿And when you travel in the land, there is no blame upon you for shortening the prayer﴾. Then the revelation ceased. When a year had passed, the Prophet (ﷺ) went on a military expedition and prayed Zuhr. The polytheists said: "Muhammad and his companions have given you an opportunity from behind them. Why did you not press upon them?" One of them said: "Indeed, they have another [prayer] like it after it." He said: So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed between the two prayers: ﴿If you fear that those who disbelieve may attack you, indeed the disbelievers are ever to you a clear enemy. And when you are among them and establish prayer for them, let a group of them stand with you﴾, up to His saying: ﴿He has prepared for the disbelievers a humiliating punishment﴾ [addition from r and a; and in h: "the two verses"]. Then the prayer of fear was revealed.

This chain is very strange. However, part of it has a witness from the narration of Abu 'Ayyash al-Zuraqi, whose name is Zayd ibn al-Samit, may Allah be pleased with him. Imam Ahmad said:

We were related to by 'Abd al-Razzaq, who related to us al-Thawri, from Mansur, from Mujahid, from Abu 'Ayyash, who said: "We were with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) at 'Usfan. The polytheists faced us, led by Khalid ibn al-Walid, and they were between us and the qiblah. The Prophet (ﷺ) led us in Zuhr prayer. They said: 'We had a chance to strike them at a moment of negligence!' Then they said: 'Now a prayer will come upon them that is more beloved to them than their sons and themselves.' He said: So Jibril descended with these verses between Zuhr and 'Asr: ﴿And when you are among them and establish prayer for them﴾." He said: "So the time came, and the Prophet (ﷺ) commanded them, and they took up their weapons. We formed two rows behind him. He said: Then he bowed, and we all bowed; then he raised [his head], and we all raised [ours]. Then the Prophet (ﷺ) prostrated with the row that was next to him, while the others stood guarding them. When they had prostrated and stood up, the others sat down and prostrated in their places. Then these advanced to the positions of those, and those came to the positions of these. Then he bowed, and they all bowed; then he raised, and they all raised. Then the Prophet (ﷺ) prostrated with the row next to him, while the others stood guarding them. When they sat, the others sat down and prostrated. Then he gave the salam to them, and then he left." He said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) prayed it twice: once at 'Usfan, and once in the land of Banu Sulaym."

Then Ahmad related it from Ghundar, from Shu'bah, from Mansur, with similar wording. Likewise Abu Dawud related it from Sa'id ibn Mansur, from Jarir ibn 'Abd al-Hamid; and al-Nasa'i [related it] from the hadith of Shu'bah and 'Abd al-Aziz ibn 'Abd al-Samad, all of them from Mansur, with the same [chain]. [Al-Musnad (4/59, 60); Sunan Abi Dawud no. (1236); Sunan Sa'id ibn Mansur no. (686); Sunan al-Nasa'i (3/176).]

This chain is sound (sahih), and it has many supporting narrations. Among them is what al-Bukhari related, where he said: Hayawah ibn Shurayh related to us, Muhammad ibn Harb related to us, from al-Zubaydi, from al-Zuhri, from 'Ubaydullah ibn 'Abdullah ibn 'Utbah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "The Prophet (ﷺ) stood and the people stood with him. He said the takbir and they said the takbir with him. He bowed and a group of them bowed. Then he prostrated and they prostrated with him. Then he stood for the second [rak'ah], and those who had prostrated stood and guarded their brothers. Then the other group came and bowed and prostrated with him, while all the people were in the prayer, but some of them were guarding others." [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (944).]

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, Mu'adh ibn Hisham narrated to us, my father narrated to me, from Qatadah, from Sulayman al-Yashkuri, that he asked Jabir ibn Abdullah about the shortening (iqsar) of the prayer: "On which day was it revealed?" Or he said: "Which day was it?" Jabir said: "We set out to intercept the caravan of Quraysh coming from Syria. When we reached Nakhl, a man from the group came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: 'O Muhammad!' He said: 'Yes.' The man said: 'Do you fear me?' He said: 'No.' The man said: 'Then what protects you from me?' He said: 'Allah protects me from you.' So the man drew his sword, then threatened him and warned him. Then he called for departure and took up arms, and then the call to prayer was given. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) led a group of the people in prayer while another group stood guard over them. He prayed with those who were closest to him two rak'ahs, then those closest to him withdrew backward and stood in the ranks of their companions. Then the others came, and he prayed with them two rak'ahs while the first group guarded them, and then he gave the salam. So the Prophet (ﷺ) had four rak'ahs, and the people had two rak'ahs each. On that day, Allah revealed the verse about the shortening of the prayer and commanded the believers to take up arms."

Al-Imam Ahmad said: Suraij narrated to us, Abu Awanah narrated to us, from Abu Bishr, from Sulayman ibn Qays al-Yashkuri, from Jabir ibn Abdullah, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) fought the people of Khasafah (Muharib Khasafah). A man among them called Ghawrath ibn al-Harith came and stood over the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) with a sword and said: 'Who will protect you from me?' He said: 'Allah.' The sword fell from his hand, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) took it and said: 'And who will protect you from me?' He said: 'Be the best of takers.' He said: 'Do you testify that there is no god but Allah and that I am the Messenger of Allah?' He said: 'No, but I pledge to you that I will not fight you and will not be with a people who fight you.' So he let him go. He came to his people and said: 'I have come to you from the best of people.' When the prayer time came, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) prayed the prayer of fear (salat al-khawf). The people were in two groups: one group faced the enemy, and another group prayed with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He prayed with the group that was with him two rak'ahs, and they departed, and they took the place of those who were facing their enemy. Then those who were facing their enemy departed and prayed with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) two rak'ahs. So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had four rak'ahs, and the people had two rak'ahs each."

This narration is related by Ahmad alone through this route. [Al-Bukhari suspended a portion of it in his Sahih (7/476), and he narrated it through other routes with a similar wording (no. 4135): through al-Zuhri, from Sinan ibn Abi Sinan, from Jabir; and through Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from Abu Salamah, from Jabir.]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn Sinan narrated to us, Abu Qatan Amr ibn al-Haytham narrated to us, al-Mas'udi narrated to us, from Yazid al-Faqir, who said: "I asked Jabir ibn Abdullah about the two rak'ahs on a journey: Should one shorten them? He said: 'The two rak'ahs on a journey are complete; shortening is only one rak'ah during fighting. While we were with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in battle, the prayer was called, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood and arranged one group in rows, while another group faced the enemy. He prayed with them one rak'ah and prostrated twice with them. Then those who had stayed behind went to those others and took their place and position there, and those others came and stood behind the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He prayed with them one rak'ah and prostrated twice with them. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sat, and gave the salam, and those behind him gave the salam, and those others gave the salam. So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had two rak'ahs, and the people had one rak'ah each.'" Then he recited: ﴿And when you are among them and you establish the prayer for them﴾.

[Ibn Abi Shaybah related it in an abridged form (2/463) through Waki' from al-Mas'udi.]

Al-Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from al-Hakam, from Yazid al-Faqir, from Jabir ibn Abdullah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) led them in the prayer of fear: a row stood in front of him and a row behind him. He prayed with those behind him one rak'ah and two prostrations. Then these moved forward until they stood in the position of their companions, and those others came until they stood in the position of these. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) prayed with them one rak'ah and two prostrations, then gave the salam. So the Prophet (ﷺ) had two rak'ahs, and they had one rak'ah.

An-Nasa'i related it from the hadith of Shu'bah. This hadith has several routes from Jabir [Musnad (3/298) and Sunan an-Nasa'i (3/174)]. It is also in Sahih Muslim through another route with different wording [Muslim no. 840, through Abd al-Malik ibn Abi Sulayman, from Ata', from Jabir, may Allah be pleased with him]. A large group of narrators related it from Jabir in the Sahih collections, the Sunan and the Musnads.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Nu'aym ibn Hammad narrated to us, Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from Salim, from his father, who said regarding ﴿And when you are among them and you establish the prayer for them﴾: "It is the prayer of fear. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) prayed with one of the two groups one rak'ah, while the other group was facing the enemy. Then the other group, which had been facing the enemy, came and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) prayed with them another rak'ah, then gave the salam with them. Then each group stood and prayed one rak'ah each." The compilers all related this hadith in their books through the route of Ma'mar. This hadith has many routes from a number of the Companions. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh excelled in listing its routes and wordings, as did Ibn Jarir. We shall verify it in our book "al-Ahkam al-Kabir," if Allah wills, and with Allah is success.

As for the command to carry weapons during the prayer of fear, a group of scholars take it to be obligatory, based on the apparent meaning of the verse. This is one of the two opinions of al-Shafi'i, and it is indicated by His saying: ﴿There is no blame upon you if you put down your weapons due to rain or if you are ill; but take your precautions﴾, meaning: be in a state of readiness, so that when you need them you can put them on without difficulty. ﴿Indeed, Allah has prepared for the disbelievers a humiliating punishment.﴾

Allah, exalted is He, commands the frequent remembrance of Him (dhikr) immediately after the prayer of fear (salat al-khawf). Although remembrance is legislated and encouraged after other prayers as well, it is more emphatic here, because of the concessions made in the prayer regarding its pillars, and the allowance to move about during it, coming and going, and other things not found in other prayers. Just as He said concerning the sacred months: ﴿So do not wrong yourselves therein﴾ [At-Tawbah: 36]. Although wronging oneself is forbidden at all times, it is more emphatic during them, because of their great sanctity and importance. For this reason Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And when you have completed the prayer, remember Allah standing, sitting, and on your sides﴾, meaning, in all your conditions.

Then He said: ﴿So when you are secure, then establish the prayer﴾, meaning: when you are safe, the fear has gone, and tranquility has been attained, ﴿then establish the prayer﴾, meaning: complete it and perform it as you were commanded, with its limits, its humility (khushu'), its prostrations, its bowings, and all its matters.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Indeed, prayer has been decreed upon the believers a decree of specified times﴾, Ibn 'Abbas said: meaning, obligatory (mafrud). This was also related from Mujahid, Salim ibn 'Abd Allah, 'Ali ibn al-Husayn, Muhammad ibn 'Ali, al-Hasan, Muqatil, al-Suddi, and 'Atiyyah al-'Awfi.

'Abd al-Razzaq said, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿Indeed, prayer has been decreed upon the believers a decree of specified times﴾. Ibn Mas'ud said: "Indeed, for the prayer there is a time, like the time of Hajj."

Zayd ibn Aslam said: ﴿a decree of specified times﴾, he said: "Staggered (munajjaman), whenever one star set, another came to them", meaning: whenever one time passed, another time came.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And do not be weak in pursuit of the enemy﴾, meaning: do not weaken in seeking your enemy, but be earnest against them, fight them, and lie in wait for them at every place of ambush. ﴿If you are suffering, then indeed they are suffering as you are suffering﴾, meaning: just as wounds and killing afflict you, so they are afflicted too, as He said: ﴿If a wound touches you, a similar wound has touched the people﴾ [Al 'Imran: 140].

Then He said: ﴿but you hope from Allah that which they do not hope﴾, meaning: you and they are equal regarding what afflicts you and them of wounds and pains, but you hope from Allah for reward, victory, and support, while they hope for none of that. Therefore you are more deserving of jihad than they are, and more eager to establish the word of Allah and raise it.

﴿And ever is Allah Knowing and Wise﴾, meaning: He is most knowing and most wise in what He decrees, ordains, executes, and enforces, of His cosmic and legislative judgments, and He is praised in every condition.

Allah, exalted is He, commands the frequent remembrance of Him (dhikr) immediately after the prayer of fear (salat al-khawf). Although remembrance is legislated and encouraged after other prayers as well, it is more emphatic here, because of the concessions made in the prayer regarding its pillars, and the allowance to move about during it, coming and going, and other things not found in other prayers. Just as He said concerning the sacred months: ﴿So do not wrong yourselves therein﴾ [At-Tawbah: 36]. Although wronging oneself is forbidden at all times, it is more emphatic during them, because of their great sanctity and importance. For this reason Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And when you have completed the prayer, remember Allah standing, sitting, and on your sides﴾, meaning, in all your conditions.

Then He said: ﴿So when you are secure, then establish the prayer﴾, meaning: when you are safe, the fear has gone, and tranquility has been attained, ﴿then establish the prayer﴾, meaning: complete it and perform it as you were commanded, with its limits, its humility (khushu'), its prostrations, its bowings, and all its matters.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Indeed, prayer has been decreed upon the believers a decree of specified times﴾, Ibn 'Abbas said: meaning, obligatory (mafrud). This was also related from Mujahid, Salim ibn 'Abd Allah, 'Ali ibn al-Husayn, Muhammad ibn 'Ali, al-Hasan, Muqatil, al-Suddi, and 'Atiyyah al-'Awfi.

'Abd al-Razzaq said, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿Indeed, prayer has been decreed upon the believers a decree of specified times﴾. Ibn Mas'ud said: "Indeed, for the prayer there is a time, like the time of Hajj."

Zayd ibn Aslam said: ﴿a decree of specified times﴾, he said: "Staggered (munajjaman), whenever one star set, another came to them", meaning: whenever one time passed, another time came.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And do not be weak in pursuit of the enemy﴾, meaning: do not weaken in seeking your enemy, but be earnest against them, fight them, and lie in wait for them at every place of ambush. ﴿If you are suffering, then indeed they are suffering as you are suffering﴾, meaning: just as wounds and killing afflict you, so they are afflicted too, as He said: ﴿If a wound touches you, a similar wound has touched the people﴾ [Al 'Imran: 140].

Then He said: ﴿but you hope from Allah that which they do not hope﴾, meaning: you and they are equal regarding what afflicts you and them of wounds and pains, but you hope from Allah for reward, victory, and support, while they hope for none of that. Therefore you are more deserving of jihad than they are, and more eager to establish the word of Allah and raise it.

﴿And ever is Allah Knowing and Wise﴾, meaning: He is most knowing and most wise in what He decrees, ordains, executes, and enforces, of His cosmic and legislative judgments, and He is praised in every condition.

Ibn Kathir's Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim, on surah 4, verses 105–109 (part 1 of 2):

Allah, the Exalted, says, addressing His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book in truth﴾, meaning: it is the truth from Allah, and it contains truth in its information and its commands.

* *

His saying: ﴿that you may judge among the people by that which Allah has shown you﴾.
