Perhaps one of you is more eloquent in his argument than another, so I rule in his favour. Whoever I rule for from the right of a Muslim, it is only a piece of Fire, so let him take it or leave it." [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (2458) and Sahih Muslim no. (1713).]

Imam Ahmad said: Waki' narrated to us, Usamah ibn Zayd narrated to us, from 'Abdullah ibn Rafi', from Umm Salamah, who said: Two men from the Ansar came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) disputing over inheritances between them that had become obscure, and they had no evidence. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "You bring your disputes to me, and I am only a human being. Perhaps one of you is more eloquent in his argument than the other, and I judge between you according to what I hear. So whoever I give him something of his brother's right, let him not take it, for I am only cutting for him a piece of the Fire, which he will bring on his neck as a heavy burden on the Day of Resurrection." Then the two men wept, and each of them said: "My right belongs to my brother." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "As for when you have said this, then go and divide it equally, then seek out what is right, then draw lots, then each of you should absolve the other."

Abu Dawud narrated it from the hadith of Usamah ibn Zayd, with the same chain, and he added: "Indeed, I only judge between you by my opinion regarding that about which nothing has been revealed to me." [Al-Musnad (6/320) and Sunan Abi Dawud no. (3584).]

Ibn Mardawayh narrated, through the route of al-'Awfi, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: A group of the Ansar went out with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on one of his campaigns, and a coat of mail belonging to one of them was stolen. A man from the Ansar was suspected of it, so the owner of the coat of mail came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "Indeed, Tu'mah ibn Ubayriq has stolen my coat of mail." When the thief saw this, he went and placed it in the house of an innocent man, and he said to some of his tribe: "I have hidden the coat of mail and placed it in the house of so-and-so, and it will be found with him." So they went to the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) at night and said: "O Prophet of Allah, our companion is innocent, and the owner of the coat of mail is so-and-so, and we have full knowledge of this. So excuse our companion before the people and argue on his behalf, for if Allah does not protect him through you, he will be destroyed." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood up, cleared him and excused him before the people. Then Allah revealed: ﴿Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book in truth, that you may judge among the people by that which Allah has shown you, and do not be a advocate for the treacherous﴾ [He says: judge by what Allah has revealed to you in the Book] ﴿and seek forgiveness of Allah. Indeed, Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful. And do not argue on behalf of those who betray themselves. Indeed, Allah does not love one who is a betrayer and sinful﴾. Then He said concerning those who came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) concealing falsehood: ﴿They conceal from the people, but they cannot conceal from Allah, and He is with them when they plot by night that which He does not approve of in speech. And ever is Allah, of what they do, encompassing. Here you are, arguing on their behalf in the life of this world, but who will argue with Allah on their behalf on the Day of Resurrection, or who will be their guardian?﴾ Meaning: those who came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) concealing themselves, who argued on behalf of the treacherous. Then He said: ﴿And whoever commits an evil or wrongs himself [then seeks forgiveness of Allah will find Allah Forgiving and Merciful]﴾, meaning: those who came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) concealing falsehood. Then He said: ﴿And whoever earns a sin or an offence and then throws it onto an innocent person has certainly borne a slander and a manifest sin﴾, meaning: the thief and those who argued on behalf of the thief. This narration is strange [and similar was mentioned by Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, Qatadah, al-Suddi, Ibn Zayd and others regarding this verse, that it was revealed concerning the thief of Banu Ubayriq, though their narrations differ, and they are close in meaning].

Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated this story at length. Abu 'Isa al-Tirmidhi, in his Jami', when interpreting this verse, and Ibn Jarir in his Tafsir, said:

Al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn Abi Shu'ayb Abu Muslim al-Harrani narrated to us; Muhammad ibn Salamah al-Harrani narrated to us; Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, from 'Asim ibn 'Umar ibn Qatadah, from his father, from his grandfather Qatadah ibn al-Nu'man, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: There was a household among us called Banu Ubayriq: Bishr, Bushayr and Mubashshir. Bushayr was a hypocrite. He would compose poetry in which he satirised the companions of the Prophet (ﷺ), then attribute it to some of the Arabs, then say: "So-and-so said such-and-such, and so-and-so said such-and-such." When the companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) heard that poetry, they would say: "By Allah, no one composes this poetry except this wicked man," or as the man said. They said: "It is Ibn al-Ubayriq who said it." They said: They were a household of need and poverty in the Jahiliyyah and in Islam. The people of Madinah had only dates and barley as their food. A man who had wealth would, when a caravan (dafitah) came from Syria with fine wheat flour (al-darmak), buy from it and reserve it for himself, while his dependants had only dates and barley for food. A caravan came from Syria, and my uncle Rifa'ah ibn Zayd bought a load of fine flour and stored it in a storeroom (mashrubah) of his, in which there were weapons: a coat of mail and a sword. Then he was attacked from beneath the house; the storeroom was broken into, and the food and the weapons were taken. When morning came, my uncle Rifa'ah came to me and said: "O nephew, we were attacked during this night. Our storeroom was broken into, and our food and weapons were taken." He said: We searched the household and asked, and it was said to us: "We saw the Banu Ubayriq kindling a fire this night, and we think nothing but that it was from some of your food."

He said: The Banu Ubayriq had said, while we were asking in the household: "By Allah, we do not see your companion except Labid ibn Sahl, a man of ours who has piety and Islam." When Labid heard this, he drew his sword and said: "Am I a thief? By Allah, this sword will reach you, or you will make this theft clear." They said: "Leave us alone, O man, for you are not its perpetrator." We kept asking in the household until we did not doubt that they were its perpetrators.

My uncle said to me: "O nephew, if only you would go to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and mention that to him." Qatadah said: So I came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "Indeed, a household among us, people of harshness, deliberately attacked my uncle Rifa'ah ibn Zayd, broke into his storeroom, and took his weapons and his food. Let them return our weapons to us; as for the food, we have no need of it." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "I will consider this matter."

When the Banu Ubayriq heard, they came to a man among them called Usayr ibn 'Amr [in Dal and A: "ibn 'Urwah"] and spoke to him about it. Some people from the household gathered around this, and they said: "O Messenger of Allah, indeed Qatadah ibn al-Nu'man and his uncle have targeted a household of ours, a household of Islam and righteousness, accusing them of theft without any evidence or certainty." Qatadah said: So I came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and spoke to him, and he said: "You have targeted a household about whom Islam and righteousness are mentioned, accusing them of theft without certainty and without evidence?"

He said: So I returned, and I wished I had given up some of my wealth and had not spoken to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about it. My uncle Rifa'ah came to me and said: "O nephew, what have you done?" I informed him of what the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had said to me, and he said: "Allah is the One sought for help." We had not lingered long before the Qur'an was revealed: ﴿Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book in truth, that you may judge among the people by that which Allah has shown you, and do not be an advocate for the treacherous﴾, [concerning] the Banu Ubayriq; ﴿and seek forgiveness of Allah﴾ for what you said to Qatadah; ﴿indeed, Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful. And do not argue on behalf of those who betray themselves. Indeed, Allah does not love one who is a betrayer and sinful. They conceal from the people, but they cannot conceal from Allah, and He is with them﴾, up to His saying: ﴿Merciful﴾, meaning: if they had sought forgiveness of Allah, He would have forgiven them. ﴿And whoever earns a sin, he earns it only against himself﴾, up to His saying: ﴿a manifest sin﴾. And [the verses concerning] their saying to Labid: ﴿And if not for the grace of Allah upon you and His mercy...﴾, up to His saying: ﴿then We will give him a great reward﴾.

When the Qur'an was revealed, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) brought the weapons and returned them to Rifa'ah.

Qatadah said: When I brought the weapons to my uncle, he was an old man who had become weak in sight or in his bones (the doubt is from Abu 'Isa), in the Jahiliyyah. I had considered his Islam to be doubtful, but when I brought him the weapons he said: "O nephew, it is in the way of Allah." So I knew that his Islam was sound. When the Qur'an was revealed, Bushayr joined the polytheists, and he settled with Sulafah bint Sa'd ibn Sumayyah. Then Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿And whoever opposes the Messenger after guidance has become clear to him and follows other than the way of the believers, We will leave him in what he has taken and drive him into Hell, and evil is it as a destination. Indeed, Allah does not forgive association with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills. And whoever associates others with Allah has certainly strayed far astray﴾. When he settled with Sulafah, Hassan ibn Thabit attacked her with some verses of his poetry. She took his saddlebag, placed it on her head, went out with it and threw it into al-Abtah. Then she said: "You have brought me the poetry of Hassan? You were never bringing me any good."

This is the wording of al-Tirmidhi. Then al-Tirmidhi said: This is a strange hadith; we do not know of anyone who transmitted it with this chain except Muhammad ibn Salamah al-Harrani. Yunus ibn Bukayr and others narrated it from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from 'Asim ibn 'Umar ibn Qatadah, as a mursal (a narration with a missing companion in the chain), and they did not mention "from his father, from his grandfather" in it.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from Hashim ibn al-Qasim al-Harrani, from Muhammad ibn Salamah, in part.

Ibn al-Mundhir narrated it in his Tafsir: Muhammad ibn Isma'il, meaning al-Sa'igh, narrated to us; al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn Abi Shu'ayb al-Harrani narrated to us; Muhammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, and he mentioned it in full.

Abu al-Shaykh al-Asbahani narrated it in his Tafsir from Muhammad ibn al-'Abbas ibn Ayyub and al-Hasan ibn Ya'qub, both from al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn Abi Shu'ayb al-Harrani, from Muhammad ibn Salamah. Then he said at its end: Muhammad ibn Salamah said: Yahya ibn Ma'in, Ahmad ibn Hanbal and Ishaq ibn Isra'il heard this hadith from me. [Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3036) and Tafsir al-Tabari (9/177); see also the commentary of Shaykh Ahmad Shakir on this hadith (9/181).]

Al-Hakim Abu 'Abd Allah al-Naysaburi also narrated this hadith in his book *al-Mustadrak* (the "Supplement" to the hadith collections), from Abu al-'Abbas al-Asamm, from Ahmad ibn 'Abd al-Jabbar al-'Utaridi, from Yunus ibn Bukayr, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, with a fuller meaning than this version, and in it is the poetry. He then said: "This is a sound hadith according to the criteria of Muslim, though the two (al-Bukhari and Muslim) did not narrate it." [[al-Mustadrak (4/385–388), and al-Dhahabi agreed with him.]]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿They hide from people, but they cannot hide from Allah; He is with them when they devise at night what He does not approve of in speech [and Allah is ever encompassing of what they do]﴾ [[Addition from manuscripts R and A.]], this is a rebuke of the hypocrites for concealing their ugly deeds from people so that they will not be condemned for them, while they flaunt them before Allah, because He is aware of their inner secrets and knows what is in their hearts. For this reason He said: ﴿He is with them when they devise at night what He does not approve of in speech, and Allah is ever encompassing of what they do﴾. This is a threat and a warning to them.

Then He said: ﴿Here you are, those who argued on their behalf in the life of this world; but who will argue with Allah on their behalf on the Day of Resurrection, or who will be their guardian?﴾ [[Addition from manuscripts R and A; in manuscript H: "the verse".]] That is: suppose these people prevailed in this world by what they displayed, or what was displayed for them before the rulers who judge by the outward appearance, and who are bound to judge that way. What, then, will be their condition on the Day of Resurrection before Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, who knows the secret and what is even more hidden? And who will act as their advocate that day to advance their claim? That is: on that day no one will be their advocate. For this reason He said: ﴿or who will be their guardian?﴾

Ibn Kathir's Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim, on surah 4, verses 105–109 (part 1 of 2):

Allah, the Exalted, says, addressing His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book in truth﴾, meaning: it is the truth from Allah, and it contains truth in its information and its commands.

* *

His saying: ﴿that you may judge among the people by that which Allah has shown you﴾. Those scholars of usul (the foundations of jurisprudence) who hold that the Prophet (ﷺ) had the right to judge by ijtihad (independent reasoning) have cited this verse as evidence, along with what is established in the Sahihayn (the two Sahihs of al-Bukhari and Muslim) from the narration of Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from his father, from Zaynab bint Umm Salamah, from Umm Salamah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) heard the clamour of litigants at the door of his chamber, so he went out to them and said: "Indeed, I am only a human being, and I judge only according to what I hear. Perhaps one of you is more eloquent in his argument than another, so I rule in his favour. Whoever I rule for from the right of a Muslim, it is only a piece of Fire, so let him take it or leave it." [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (2458) and Sahih Muslim no. (1713).]

Imam Ahmad said: Waki' narrated to us, Usamah ibn Zayd narrated to us, from 'Abdullah ibn Rafi', from Umm Salamah, who said: Two men from the Ansar came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) disputing over inheritances between them that had become obscure, and they had no evidence. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "You bring your disputes to me, and I am only a human being. Perhaps one of you is more eloquent in his argument than the other, and I judge between you according to what I hear. So whoever I give him something of his brother's right, let him not take it, for I am only cutting for him a piece of the Fire, which he will bring on his neck as a heavy burden on the Day of Resurrection." Then the two men wept, and each of them said: "My right belongs to my brother." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "As for when you have said this, then go and divide it equally, then seek out what is right, then draw lots, then each of you should absolve the other."

Abu Dawud narrated it from the hadith of Usamah ibn Zayd, with the same chain, and he added: "Indeed, I only judge between you by my opinion regarding that about which nothing has been revealed to me." [Al-Musnad (6/320) and Sunan Abi Dawud no. (3584).]

Ibn Mardawayh narrated, through the route of al-'Awfi, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: A group of the Ansar went out with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on one of his campaigns, and a coat of mail belonging to one of them was stolen. A man from the Ansar was suspected of it, so the owner of the coat of mail came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "Indeed, Tu'mah ibn Ubayriq has stolen my coat of mail." When the thief saw this, he went and placed it in the house of an innocent man, and he said to some of his tribe: "I have hidden the coat of mail and placed it in the house of so-and-so, and it will be found with him." So they went to the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) at night and said: "O Prophet of Allah, our companion is innocent, and the owner of the coat of mail is so-and-so, and we have full knowledge of this. So excuse our companion before the people and argue on his behalf, for if Allah does not protect him through you, he will be destroyed." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood up, cleared him and excused him before the people. Then Allah revealed: ﴿Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book in truth, that you may judge among the people by that which Allah has shown you, and do not be a advocate for the treacherous﴾ [He says: judge by what Allah has revealed to you in the Book] ﴿and seek forgiveness of Allah. Indeed, Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful. And do not argue on behalf of those who betray themselves. Indeed, Allah does not love one who is a betrayer and sinful﴾. Then He said concerning those who came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) concealing falsehood: ﴿They conceal from the people, but they cannot conceal from Allah, and He is with them when they plot by night that which He does not approve of in speech. And ever is Allah, of what they do, encompassing. Here you are, arguing on their behalf in the life of this world, but who will argue with Allah on their behalf on the Day of Resurrection, or who will be their guardian?﴾ Meaning: those who came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) concealing themselves, who argued on behalf of the treacherous. Then He said: ﴿And whoever commits an evil or wrongs himself [then seeks forgiveness of Allah will find Allah Forgiving and Merciful]﴾, meaning: those who came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) concealing falsehood. Then He said: ﴿And whoever earns a sin or an offence and then throws it onto an innocent person has certainly borne a slander and a manifest sin﴾, meaning: the thief and those who argued on behalf of the thief. This narration is strange [and similar was mentioned by Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, Qatadah, al-Suddi, Ibn Zayd and others regarding this verse, that it was revealed concerning the thief of Banu Ubayriq, though their narrations differ, and they are close in meaning].

Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated this story at length. Abu 'Isa al-Tirmidhi, in his Jami', when interpreting this verse, and Ibn Jarir in his Tafsir, said:

Al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn Abi Shu'ayb Abu Muslim al-Harrani narrated to us; Muhammad ibn Salamah al-Harrani narrated to us; Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, from 'Asim ibn 'Umar ibn Qatadah, from his father, from his grandfather Qatadah ibn al-Nu'man, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: There was a household among us called Banu Ubayriq: Bishr, Bushayr and Mubashshir. Bushayr was a hypocrite. He would compose poetry in which he satirised the companions of the Prophet (ﷺ), then attribute it to some of the Arabs, then say: "So-and-so said such-and-such, and so-and-so said such-and-such." When the companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) heard that poetry, they would say: "By Allah, no one composes this poetry except this wicked man," or as the man said. They said: "It is Ibn al-Ubayriq who said it." They said: They were a household of need and poverty in the Jahiliyyah and in Islam. The people of Madinah had only dates and barley as their food. A man who had wealth would, when a caravan (dafitah) came from Syria with fine wheat flour (al-darmak), buy from it and reserve it for himself, while his dependants had only dates and barley for food. A caravan came from Syria, and my uncle Rifa'ah ibn Zayd bought a load of fine flour and stored it in a storeroom (mashrubah) of his, in which there were weapons: a coat of mail and a sword. Then he was attacked from beneath the house; the storeroom was broken into, and the food and the weapons were taken. When morning came, my uncle Rifa'ah came to me and said: "O nephew, we were attacked during this night. Our storeroom was broken into, and our food and weapons were taken." He said: We searched the household and asked, and it was said to us: "We saw the Banu Ubayriq kindling a fire this night, and we think nothing but that it was from some of your food."

He said: The Banu Ubayriq had said, while we were asking in the household: "By Allah, we do not see your companion except Labid ibn Sahl, a man of ours who has piety and Islam." When Labid heard this, he drew his sword and said: "Am I a thief? By Allah, this sword will reach you, or you will make this theft clear." They said: "Leave us alone, O man, for you are not its perpetrator." We kept asking in the household until we did not doubt that they were its perpetrators.

My uncle said to me: "O nephew, if only you would go to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and mention that to him." Qatadah said: So I came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "Indeed, a household among us, people of harshness, deliberately attacked my uncle Rifa'ah ibn Zayd, broke into his storeroom, and took his weapons and his food. Let them return our weapons to us; as for the food, we have no need of it." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "I will consider this matter."

When the Banu Ubayriq heard, they came to a man among them called Usayr ibn 'Amr [in Dal and A: "ibn 'Urwah"] and spoke to him about it. Some people from the household gathered around this, and they said: "O Messenger of Allah, indeed Qatadah ibn al-Nu'man and his uncle have targeted a household of ours, a household of Islam and righteousness, accusing them of theft without any evidence or certainty." Qatadah said: So I came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and spoke to him, and he said: "You have targeted a household about whom Islam and righteousness are mentioned, accusing them of theft without certainty and without evidence?"

He said: So I returned, and I wished I had given up some of my wealth and had not spoken to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about it. My uncle Rifa'ah came to me and said: "O nephew, what have you done?" I informed him of what the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had said to me, and he said: "Allah is the One sought for help." We had not lingered long before the Qur'an was revealed: ﴿Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book in truth, that you may judge among the people by that which Allah has shown you, and do not be an advocate for the treacherous﴾, [concerning] the Banu Ubayriq; ﴿and seek forgiveness of Allah﴾ for what you said to Qatadah; ﴿indeed, Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful. And do not argue on behalf of those who betray themselves. Indeed, Allah does not love one who is a betrayer and sinful. They conceal from the people, but they cannot conceal from Allah, and He is with them﴾, up to His saying: ﴿Merciful﴾, meaning: if they had sought forgiveness of Allah, He would have forgiven them. ﴿And whoever earns a sin, he earns it only against himself﴾, up to His saying: ﴿a manifest sin﴾. And [the verses concerning] their saying to Labid: ﴿And if not for the grace of Allah upon you and His mercy...﴾, up to His saying: ﴿then We will give him a great reward﴾.

When the Qur'an was revealed, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) brought the weapons and returned them to Rifa'ah.

Qatadah said: When I brought the weapons to my uncle, he was an old man who had become weak in sight or in his bones (the doubt is from Abu 'Isa), in the Jahiliyyah. I had considered his Islam to be doubtful, but when I brought him the weapons he said: "O nephew, it is in the way of Allah." So I knew that his Islam was sound. Then she said: "You have brought me the poetry of Hassan? You were never bringing me any good."

Ibn Kathir's commentary on Surah 4, verses 110–113:

He, exalted is He, informs of His generosity and bounty: whoever repents to Him, He will accept his repentance, whatever sin he has committed.

Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿And whoever does evil or wrongs himself, then seeks Allah's forgiveness, will find Allah Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that he said regarding this verse: Allah informed His servants of His forbearance, His pardon, His generosity, the vastness of His mercy and His forgiveness. Whoever commits a sin, whether small or great, ﴿then seeks Allah's forgiveness, will find Allah Forgiving and Merciful﴾, even if his sins were greater than the heavens, the earth and the mountains. Narrated by Ibn Jarir (al-Tabari).

Ibn Jarir also said: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Abi 'Adi narrated to us, from Shu'bah, from 'Asim, from Abu Wa'il, who said: 'Abd Allah (Ibn Mas'ud) said: "The Children of Israel, when one of them committed a sin, would find in the morning the expiation for that sin written on his door. And if urine touched any part of his body, he would cut it off with scissors." A man said: "Allah has indeed given the Children of Israel good." 'Abd Allah said: "What Allah has given you is better than what He gave them. He made water a purifier for you." And He said: ﴿And those who, when they commit an abomination or wrong themselves, remember Allah and seek forgiveness for their sins﴾ [Al 'Imran: 135], and He said: ﴿And whoever does evil or wrongs himself, then seeks Allah's forgiveness, will find Allah Forgiving and Merciful﴾.

He also said: Ya'qub narrated to me, Hushaym narrated to us, Ibn 'Awn narrated to us, from Habib ibn Abi Thabit, who said: A woman came to 'Abd Allah ibn Mughaffal and asked him about a woman who committed fornication, became pregnant, and when she gave birth, killed her child. 'Abd Allah ibn Mughaffal said: "What about her? She will be in the Fire!" So she left weeping. He called her back and said: "I do not see your case except as one of two matters: ﴿And whoever does evil or wrongs himself, then seeks Allah's forgiveness, will find Allah Forgiving and Merciful﴾." She said: She wiped her eyes and went on her way.

Imam Ahmad said: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from 'Uthman ibn al-Mughirah, who said: I heard 'Ali ibn Rabi'ah from Banu Asad narrate from Asma' (or Ibn Asma' from Banu Fazarah), who said: 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "When I heard anything from the Messenger of Allah, Allah benefited me from it as much as He willed. And Abu Bakr narrated to me, and Abu Bakr spoke the truth: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'There is no Muslim who commits a sin, then performs ablution, prays two rak'ahs, then seeks Allah's forgiveness for that sin, except that Allah forgives him.'" And he recited these two verses: ﴿And whoever does evil or wrongs himself [then seeks Allah's forgiveness, will find Allah Forgiving and Merciful]﴾ and ﴿And those who, when they commit an abomination or wrong themselves﴾, and the verse.

[Footnote: Al-Musnad (1/8). See its takhrij (sourcing) previously under Surah Al 'Imran, verse 135.]

We have discussed this hadith, attributed it to those who narrated it among the authors of the Sunan, and mentioned what is said about its chain in the Musnad of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him. Some of this has also been mentioned earlier in Surah Al 'Imran.

Ibn Mardawayh narrated it in his tafsir through another route from 'Ali, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ziyad narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Harbi narrated to us, Dawud ibn Mihran al-Dabbagh narrated to us, 'Umar ibn Yazid narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from 'Abd Khayr, from 'Ali, who said: I heard Abu Bakr, namely al-Siddiq, say: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "There is no servant who commits a sin, then stands and performs ablution, doing it well, then stands and prays and seeks forgiveness for his sin, except that it is binding upon Allah to forgive him, because He says: ﴿And whoever does evil or wrongs himself [then seeks Allah's forgiveness, will find Allah Forgiving and Merciful]﴾."

Then he narrated it through the route of Aban ibn Abi 'Ayyash, from Abu Ishaq al-Sabi'i, from al-Harith, from 'Ali, from al-Siddiq, similar to it. This chain is not sound.

[Footnote: Al-Daraqutni mentioned it in al-'Ilal (1/179) and narrated it in al-Afrad, as in al-Atraf of Ibn al-Qaysarani (folio 13), and said: "No one narrated it from him (i.e., 'Umar ibn Yazid) except Dawud ibn Mihran, and it is strange, from the hadith of Abu Ishaq from 'Abd Khayr." He also said in al-'Ilal (Defects): "The best of its chains and the most authentic is what al-Thawri and Mis'ar and those who followed them narrated from 'Uthman ibn al-Mughirah." This is the narration of the people of the Sunan.]

Ibn Mardawayh said: Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Duhaym narrated to us, Ahmad ibn Hazim narrated to us, Musa ibn Marwan al-Raqqi narrated to us, Mubashshir ibn Isma'il al-Halabi narrated to us, from Tammam ibn Najih, who said: Ka'b ibn Dhuhl al-Azdi narrated to me, who said: I heard Abu al-Darda' narrate, saying: "When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sat with us, and he had some need, he would rise to attend to it and intend to return, and he would leave his sandals in his place, or some of what was upon him. He rose once and left his sandals." Abu al-Darda' said: "So I took a water vessel and followed him. He went on for a while, then returned without having fulfilled his need, and said: 'A messenger came to me from my Lord and said to me: ﴿Whoever does evil or wrongs himself, then seeks Allah's forgiveness, will find Allah Forgiving and Merciful﴾, so I wanted to give good news to my companions.'" Abu al-Darda' said: "The verse before it had been difficult for people: ﴿Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it﴾. So I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, even if he fornicates, even if he steals, then seeks forgiveness from his Lord, will He forgive him?' He said: 'Yes.' I said a second time, he said: 'Yes.' Then I said a third time, and he said: 'Yes, even if he fornicates, even if he steals, then seeks forgiveness from Allah, He will forgive him, despite the nose of 'Uwaymir.'" He said: "I saw Abu al-Darda' striking his own nose with his finger."

This is a very strange hadith by this route and in this wording, and there is weakness in its chain.

[Footnote: Al-Tabarani narrated it in his Mu'jam, as in al-Majma' (7/11). Al-Haythami said: "In it is Mubashshir ibn Isma'il, whom Ibn Ma'in and others declared trustworthy, while al-Bukhari and others declared him weak." Abu Dawud also narrated it in his Sunan, no. (4854): Ibrahim ibn Musa al-Razi narrated to us, Mubashshir ibn Isma'il narrated to us, and he mentioned its beginning up to his words: "and left his sandals."]

* *

His saying: ﴿And whoever earns a sin, he earns it only against himself, and Allah is ever Knowing and Wise.﴾ is like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿No bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another, and if a heavily laden soul calls [another] to its load, nothing of it will be carried, even if he were a close relative﴾ [Fatir: 18]. It means that no one commits a crime against another; rather, every soul is accountable only for what it has done, and no one else bears its burden. For this reason He said: ﴿and Allah is ever Knowing and Wise﴾, meaning: this came from His knowledge and wisdom, and His justice and mercy.

Then He said: ﴿And whoever earns an error or sin and then throws it onto an innocent person has certainly borne a slander and a manifest sin.﴾ That is, just as the Banu Ubayriq accused that righteous man, Labid ibn Sahl, with their vile deed, as mentioned earlier in the hadith, or Zayd ibn al-Samin the Jew, according to what others have said. He was innocent, while they were the wrongdoers and traitors, as Allah informed His Messenger (ﷺ) of this. This rebuke and reproach is general to them and to others who share their attributes and commit a similar error, and for them is a similar punishment.

* *

His saying: ﴿Had it not been for Allah's bounty upon you and His mercy, a faction of them would have resolved to mislead you, but they do not mislead except themselves, and they do not harm you at all.﴾ Imam Ibn Abi Hatim said: Hashim ibn al-Qasim al-Harrani informed us, in what he wrote to me, Muhammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from 'Asim ibn 'Umar ibn Qatadah al-Ansari, from his father, from his grandfather Qatadah ibn al-Nu'man, and he mentioned the story of the Banu Ubayriq. So Allah revealed: ﴿A faction of them resolved to mislead you, but they do not mislead except themselves, and they do not harm you at all.﴾ This refers to Usayr ibn 'Urwah and his companions. It refers to when they praised the Banu Ubayriq and blamed Qatadah ibn al-Nu'man for accusing them, while they were righteous and innocent, and the matter was not as they had reported to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). For this reason Allah revealed the decisive resolution of the matter and its clarification to His Messenger (ﷺ).

Then He bestowed favour upon him by strengthening him in all circumstances, protecting him, and sending down to him the Book, which is the Qur'an, and the wisdom, which is the Sunnah: ﴿and taught you what you did not know﴾, that is, [what] before the revelation of that to you, as in His saying: ﴿And thus We revealed to you a Spirit of Our command. You did not know what the Book was, nor [what] faith [was]; but We made it a light by which We guide whom We will of Our servants. [Footnote: Al-Tabarani narrated it in his Mu'jam, as in al-Majma' (7/11). Al-Haythami said: "In it is Mubashshir ibn Isma'il, whom Ibn Ma'in and others declared trustworthy, while al-Bukhari and others declared him weak." Abu Dawud also narrated it in his Sunan, no. (4854): Ibrahim ibn Musa al-Razi narrated to us, Mubashshir ibn Isma'il narrated to us, and he mentioned its beginning up to his words: "and left his sandals."]

* *

His saying: ﴿And whoever earns a sin, he earns it only against himself, and Allah is ever Knowing and Wise.﴾ is like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿No bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another, and if a heavily laden soul calls [another] to its load, nothing of it will be carried, even if he were a close relative﴾ [Fatir: 18]. It means that no one commits a crime against another; rather, every soul is accountable only for what it has done, and no one else bears its burden. For this reason He said: ﴿and Allah is ever Knowing and Wise﴾, meaning: this came from His knowledge and wisdom, and His justice and mercy.

Then He said: ﴿And whoever earns an error or sin and then throws it onto an innocent person has certainly borne a slander and a manifest sin.﴾ That is, just as the Banu Ubayriq accused that righteous man, Labid ibn Sahl, with their vile deed, as mentioned earlier in the hadith, or Zayd ibn al-Samin the Jew, according to what others have said. He was innocent, while they were the wrongdoers and traitors, as Allah informed His Messenger (ﷺ) of this. This rebuke and reproach is general to them and to others who share their attributes and commit a similar error, and for them is a similar punishment.

* *

His saying: ﴿Had it not been for Allah's bounty upon you and His mercy, a faction of them would have resolved to mislead you, but they do not mislead except themselves, and they do not harm you at all.﴾ Imam Ibn Abi Hatim said: Hashim ibn al-Qasim al-Harrani informed us, in what he wrote to me, Muhammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from 'Asim ibn 'Umar ibn Qatadah al-Ansari, from his father, from his grandfather Qatadah ibn al-Nu'man, and he mentioned the story of the Banu Ubayriq. So Allah revealed: ﴿A faction of them resolved to mislead you, but they do not mislead except themselves, and they do not harm you at all.﴾ This refers to Usayr ibn 'Urwah and his companions. It refers to when they praised the Banu Ubayriq and blamed Qatadah ibn al-Nu'man for accusing them, while they were righteous and innocent, and the matter was not as they had reported to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). For this reason Allah revealed the decisive resolution of the matter and its clarification to His Messenger (ﷺ).

Then He bestowed favour upon him by strengthening him in all circumstances, protecting him, and sending down to him the Book, which is the Qur'an, and the wisdom, which is the Sunnah: ﴿and taught you what you did not know﴾, that is, [what] before the revelation of that to you, as in His saying: ﴿And thus We revealed to you a Spirit of Our command. You did not know what the Book was, nor [what] faith [was]; but We made it a light by which We guide whom We will of Our servants. And indeed, you guide to a straight path, the path of Allah, to whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. Unquestionably, to Allah do all matters return﴾ [Al-Shura: 52–53], and He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And you did not expect that the Book would be bestowed upon you, except as a mercy from your Lord﴾ [Al-Qasas: 86]. For this reason He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And the bounty of Allah upon you has been ever great.﴾

Allah the Exalted says: "There is no good in much of their secret talk" — meaning, the speech of people — "except for one who enjoins charity, or what is right, or reconciliation between people" — i.e., except the secret talk of one who says such things, as came in the hadith narrated by Ibn Mardawayh:

Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Ibrahim narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Sulayman ibn al-Harith narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Yazid ibn Khunays (in the copy of R: "Hunays") narrated to us, saying: We entered upon Sufyan al-Thawri to visit him — and he gestured towards the House of the Perfumers — and Sa'id ibn Hassan al-Makhzumi entered upon him. Sufyan al-Thawri said to him: "The hadith that you narrated to me from Umm Salih, repeat it to me." He said: Umm Salih narrated to me, from Safiyya bint Shayba, from Umm Habiba, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "All of the speech of the son of Adam is against him, not for him, except enjoining what is right, or forbidding what is wrong, or the remembrance of Allah, Mighty and Majestic." Sufyan said: So I urged him (in the copy of A: "and urged him"). Muhammad ibn Yazid said: "How severe is this hadith!" Sufyan said: "And what is the severity of this hadith? It was only brought by one woman from another woman. This is in the Book of Allah which your Prophet (ﷺ) was sent with. Did you not hear Allah say in His Book: ﴿There is no good in much of their secret talk, except for one who enjoins charity, or what is right, or reconciliation between people﴾ — this is exactly it. Or did you not hear Allah say: ﴿On the Day when the Spirit and the angels stand in rows, none will speak except one whom the Most Merciful permits, and he says what is correct﴾ [An-Naba: 38] — this is exactly it. Or did you not hear Allah say in His Book: ﴿By time, indeed mankind is in loss, except those who believe and do righteous deeds and advise each other to truth and advise each other to patience﴾ [Al-Asr] — this is exactly it."

Al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah narrated this hadith from the narration of Muhammad ibn Yazid ibn Khunays from Sa'id ibn Hassan, with the same. They did not mention the statements of al-Thawri to its end. Then al-Tirmidhi said: "Gharib (strange); we do not know it except from the hadith of Ibn Khunays."

Imam Ahmad said: Ya'qub narrated to us, my father narrated to us, Salih ibn Kaysan narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Muslim ibn 'Ubayd Allah ibn Shihab narrated to us: that Humayd ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf informed him, that his mother Umm Kulthum bint 'Uqba informed him: that she heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "The liar is not the one who reconciles between people, so that he brings about good, or says good." She said: "I did not hear him permit anything of what people say except in three: in war, in reconciliation between people, and the speech of a man to his wife and the speech of a woman to her husband." He said: Umm Kulthum bint 'Uqba was among the emigrant women who pledged allegiance to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

The group (of compilers), except Ibn Majah, narrated it through several chains, from al-Zuhri, with similar wording.

Imam Ahmad said: Abu Mu'awiya narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from 'Amr ibn Murra (in the copies of R and A: "Muhammad"), from Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd, from Umm al-Darda', from Abu al-Darda', who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Shall I inform you of something better in rank than prayer, fasting and charity?" They said: "Yes." He said: "Reconciling between people; for the corruption of relations between people is the shaver (that destroys religion)."

Abu Dawud and al-Tirmidhi narrated it from the hadith of Abu Mu'awiya, and al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan sahih."

The hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said: Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Rahim narrated to us, Suraij (in the copies of R and A: "Shurayh") ibn Yunus narrated to us, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar narrated to us, my father narrated to us, from Humayd, from Anas: that the Prophet (ﷺ) said to Abu Ayyub: "Shall I direct you to a trade?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Strive for reconciliation between people when they are at odds, and bring them closer when they are apart." Then al-Bazzar said: "'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Abd Allah al-'Umari is weak, and he narrated hadiths that were not followed by others in them."

Therefore He said: ﴿And whoever does that seeking the pleasure of Allah﴾ — meaning, sincerely in that, seeking reward for it from Allah, Mighty and Majestic — ﴿We will give him a great reward﴾ — meaning, abundant and vast reward.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And whoever opposes the Messenger after guidance has become clear to him﴾ — meaning, whoever follows a path other than the way of the Shari'ah that the Messenger (ﷺ) brought, so he becomes in one side while the Shari'ah is on the other side, and that deliberately, after the truth has become manifest to him, clear to him and evident to him. And His saying: ﴿and follows other than the way of the believers﴾ — this accompanies the first attribute, but the opposition may be to the explicit text of the Lawgiver, and it may be to what the Muhammadan Ummah has agreed upon, where their agreement is known with certainty; for they have been guaranteed protection from error in their consensus, as an honour to them and an exaltation of their Prophet (ﷺ). Many sound hadiths have come concerning this, of which we have mentioned a good portion in the book "Ahadith al-Usul." Some scholars have claimed that its meaning is mutawatir (widely transmitted). And the argument upon which al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, relied in proving that consensus is a proof whose opposition is forbidden is this noble verse, after long reflection and thought. It is among the finest and strongest deductions, although some have found this problematic and held that the indication from it is weak.

Therefore Allah, the Exalted, threatened for this by His saying: ﴿We will leave him to what he has turned to and burn him in Hell, and it is a wretched destination﴾ — meaning, if he takes this path, We will recompense him for it, by making it appealing in his heart and adorning it for him — as a gradual leading (istidraj) to him — as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿So leave Me with those who deny this statement; We will lead them step by step from where they do not know﴾ [Al-Qalam: 44]. And Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿So when they deviated, Allah caused their hearts to deviate﴾ [As-Saff: 5]. And His saying: ﴿and We leave them in their transgression, wandering blindly﴾ [Al-An'am: 110].

And He made Hell his destination in the Hereafter, because whoever departs from guidance has no path except to the Fire on the Day of Resurrection, as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Gather those who did wrong and their companions, and what they used to worship besides Allah, and guide them to the path of Hellfire﴾ [As-Saffat: 22-23]. And He said: ﴿And the criminals will see the Fire and will assume that they are going to fall into it, and will not find from it any escape﴾ [Al-Kahf: 53].

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 4, verse 116–122:

The discussion of this noble verse has already preceded, which is His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive association with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills﴾ [An-Nisa: 48], and we mentioned what relates to it of hadith at the beginning of this surah.

Al-Tirmidhi narrated the hadith of Thuwayr [in A: "Yazid"] ibn Abi Fakhita, Sa'id ibn 'Alaqa, from his father, from 'Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) that he said: "There is no verse in the Qur'an more beloved to me than this verse: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive association with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills﴾," and then he said: "Hasan gharib" [Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 3037].

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And whoever associates others with Allah has certainly strayed far astray﴾, meaning: he has taken a path other than the true path, strayed from guidance, moved far from what is correct, destroyed himself and lost himself [in A: "harmed it"] in this world and the Hereafter, and the happiness of this world and the Hereafter has escaped him.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿They invoke besides Him none but female [deities]﴾, Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Mahmud ibn Ghaylan narrated to us, al-Fadl ibn Musa informed us, al-Husayn [in R, A: "informed us al-Husayn"] ibn Waqid informed us, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, from Abu al-'Aliya, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b: ﴿They invoke besides Him none but female [deities]﴾, he said: "With every idol is a jinn-female."

And my father narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Salama al-Bahili narrated to us, from 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Muhammad, from Hisham — meaning Ibn 'Urwa — from his father, from 'A'isha: ﴿They invoke besides Him none but female [deities]﴾, she said: "Idols."

It was narrated similarly from Abu Salama ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, 'Urwa ibn al-Zubayr, Mujahid, Abu Malik, al-Suddi, and Muqatil ibn Hayyan.

Juwaybir narrated from al-Dahhak regarding His saying ﴿They invoke besides Him none but female [deities]﴾: "The polytheists said: 'The angels are the daughters of Allah, and we only worship them so that they bring us near to Allah in position.'" He said: "They took them as lords, and fashioned them in the forms of young women, and they judged and imitated, and they said: 'These resemble the daughters of Allah whom we worship,' meaning the angels."

This interpretation is similar to His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Have you considered al-Lat and al-'Uzza, and Manat, the third, the other? Is for you the male and for Him the female? That, then, is an unjust division. They are not but names you have named them, you and your fathers, for which Allah has sent down no authority﴾ [An-Najm: 19–23]. And He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And they have made the angels, who are servants of the Most Merciful, females [Did they witness their creation? Their testimony will be recorded, and they will be questioned]﴾ [Az-Zukhruf: 19]. And He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And they have made between Him and the jinn a relationship, but the jinn know that they will be brought forth [to account]. Exalted is Allah above what they describe﴾ [As-Saffat: 158–159].

'Ali ibn Abi Talha and al-Dahhak narrated from Ibn 'Abbas regarding ﴿They invoke besides Him none but female [deities]﴾: "He means the dead."

Mubarak [i.e., Ibn Fudala] narrated from al-Hasan regarding ﴿They invoke besides Him none but female [deities]﴾: al-Hasan said: "The females are everything dead that has no spirit in it, whether a dry piece of wood or a dry stone." Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Jarir narrated it, and it is gharib.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And they invoke none but Satan, a rebellious [devil]﴾, meaning: it is he who commanded them to that, made it appealing to them and adorned it for them, and in reality they are worshipping Iblis, as He said, the Exalted: ﴿Did I not charge you, O children of Adam, that you not worship Satan? Indeed, he is to you a clear enemy﴾ [Ya-Sin: 60]. And He, the Exalted, said, informing about the angels that they will say on the Day of Resurrection, concerning the polytheists who claimed to worship them in the world: ﴿Rather, they used to worship the jinn; most of them were believers in them﴾ [Saba: 41].

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Allah has cursed him﴾, meaning: He expelled him and removed him far from His mercy, and drove him out of His neighborhood.

And [Satan] said: ﴿I will surely take from Your servants an appointed portion﴾, meaning: a specified, determined, known share. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: "From every thousand, nine hundred and ninety-nine to the Fire, and one to Paradise."

﴿And I will surely mislead them﴾, meaning: from the truth. ﴿And I will surely arouse in them desires﴾, meaning: I will adorn for them the abandonment of repentance, promise them false hopes, command them to procrastinate and delay, and deceive them concerning themselves.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And I will surely command them, so they will slit the ears of cattle﴾, Qatada, al-Suddi and others said: it means splitting them and making them a mark and sign for the baheera and the sa'iba.

﴿And I will surely command them, so they will alter the creation of Allah﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: "By that is meant the castration of animals." Likewise it was narrated from Ibn 'Umar, Anas, Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, 'Ikrima, Abu 'Iyad, Abu Salih, Qatada, and al-Thawri. And there has come in a hadith the prohibition of that [Narrated by Ibn Abi Shayba in al-Musannaf (12/225) and al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan al-Kubra (10/24) through Nafi' from Ibn 'Umar who said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade the castration of horses and animals," and Ibn 'Umar said: "In it is the change of creation."].

Al-Hasan ibn Abi al-Hasan al-Basri said: "By that is meant tattooing." And in Sahih Muslim there is the prohibition of tattooing the face [Sahih Muslim, no. 2117, from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah that the Prophet ﷺ passed by a donkey whose face had been branded, and said: "May Allah curse the one who branded it."]. And in another wording: "May Allah curse whoever does that." And in the Sahih from Ibn Mas'ud that he said: "Allah has cursed the women who tattoo and those who have themselves tattooed, the women who pluck their facial hair and those who have it plucked, and those who file their teeth for beauty, who alter the creation of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic." Then he said: "Shall I not curse whom the Messenger of Allah ﷺ cursed, and who is in the Book of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic?" meaning His saying: ﴿And whatever the Messenger has given you, take; and what he has forbidden you, refrain from﴾ [Al-Hashr: 7] [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 5948].

Ibn 'Abbas in one narration, and Mujahid, 'Ikrima also, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, al-Hasan, Qatada, al-Hakam, al-Suddi, al-Dahhak, and 'Ata al-Khurasani said regarding His saying: ﴿And I will surely command them, so they will alter the creation of Allah﴾ that it means: the religion of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. This is like His saying, the Exalted: ﴿So direct your face toward the religion, inclining to truth. [Adhere to] the fitrah of Allah upon which He has created mankind. No change should there be to the creation of Allah﴾ [Ar-Rum: 30], according to those who take it as a command, meaning: do not change the fitrah of Allah, and leave people upon their fitrah, as established in the two Sahihs from Abu Hurayra who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Every child is born upon the fitrah; then his parents make him a Jew, or a Christian, or a Magian, just as an animal gives birth to a complete animal. Do you see any mutilation in it?" And in Sahih Muslim, from 'Iyad ibn Himar who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: Indeed, I created My servants as hanifs, but the devils came to them and led them astray from their religion, and made unlawful for them what I had made lawful for them" [Sahih Muslim, no. 2865].

* *

As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And whoever takes Satan as an ally instead of Allah has certainly suffered a clear loss﴾, meaning: he has lost this world and the Hereafter, and that is a loss for which there is no compensation and no recovery of what has been lost.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿He promises them and arouses desires in them, but Satan does not promise them except delusion﴾. This is a report about reality, because Satan promises his allies and gives them false hopes that they will be the winners in this world and the Hereafter, but he has lied and fabricated in that; therefore He said: ﴿And Satan does not promise them except delusion﴾, as He, the Exalted, said, reporting about Iblis on the Day of Return: ﴿And Satan will say when the matter has been decided: Indeed, Allah promised you a true promise, and I promised you, but I broke my promise to you. I had over you no authority except that I invited you, and you responded to me. So do not blame me but blame yourselves. I cannot help you, nor can you help me. Indeed, I deny your association of me [with Allah] before. Indeed, for the wrongdoers is a painful punishment﴾ [Ibrahim: 22].

* *

As for His saying: i.e., those who find his promises and desires appealing: ﴿Their refuge is Hell﴾, meaning: their destination and final abode on the Day of their reckoning. ﴿And they will not find for themselves any escape therefrom﴾, meaning: there is no way out for them from it, no turning away, no deliverance, and no refuge.

Then He mentioned the condition of the happy, the pious, and what they have in their final destiny of complete honor, saying: ﴿But those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾, meaning: their hearts affirm and their limbs act upon what they were commanded of good, and they abandon what they were forbidden of evil. ﴿We will admit them to gardens beneath which rivers flow﴾, meaning: they will direct them wherever they wish and wherever they desire. ﴿Abiding therein forever﴾, meaning: without cessation and without removal. ﴿The promise of Allah is true﴾, meaning: this is a promise from Allah, and the promise of Allah is known in reality to be certain to occur without doubt; for this He emphasized it with the verbal noun that confirms the certainty of the report, which is His saying: ﴿true﴾. Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 4, verse 116–122:

The discussion of this noble verse has already preceded, which is His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive association with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills﴾ [An-Nisa: 48], and we mentioned what relates to it of hadith at the beginning of this surah.

Al-Tirmidhi narrated the hadith of Thuwayr [in A: "Yazid"] ibn Abi Fakhita, Sa'id ibn 'Alaqa, from his father, from 'Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) that he said: "There is no verse in the Qur'an more beloved to me than this verse: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive association with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills﴾," and then he said: "Hasan gharib" [Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 3037].

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And whoever associates others with Allah has certainly strayed far astray﴾, meaning: he has taken a path other than the true path, strayed from guidance, moved far from what is correct, destroyed himself and lost himself [in A: "harmed it"] in this world and the Hereafter, and the happiness of this world and the Hereafter has escaped him.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿They invoke besides Him none but female [deities]﴾, Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Mahmud ibn Ghaylan narrated to us, al-Fadl ibn Musa informed us, al-Husayn [in R, A: "informed us al-Husayn"] ibn Waqid informed us, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, from Abu al-'Aliya, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b: ﴿They invoke besides Him none but female [deities]﴾, he said: "With every idol is a jinn-female."

And my father narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Salama al-Bahili narrated to us, from 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Muhammad, from Hisham — meaning Ibn 'Urwa — from his father, from 'A'isha: ﴿They invoke besides Him none but female [deities]﴾, she said: "Idols."

It was narrated similarly from Abu Salama ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, 'Urwa ibn al-Zubayr, Mujahid, Abu Malik, al-Suddi, and Muqatil ibn Hayyan.

Juwaybir narrated from al-Dahhak regarding His saying ﴿They invoke besides Him none but female [deities]﴾: "The polytheists said: 'The angels are the daughters of Allah, and we only worship them so that they bring us near to Allah in position.'" He said: "They took them as lords, and fashioned them in the forms of young women, and they judged and imitated, and they said: 'These resemble the daughters of Allah whom we worship,' meaning the angels."

This interpretation is similar to His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Have you considered al-Lat and al-'Uzza, and Manat, the third, the other? Is for you the male and for Him the female? That, then, is an unjust division. They are not but names you have named them, you and your fathers, for which Allah has sent down no authority﴾ [An-Najm: 19–23]. And He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And they have made the angels, who are servants of the Most Merciful, females [Did they witness their creation? Their testimony will be recorded, and they will be questioned]﴾ [Az-Zukhruf: 19]. And He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And they have made between Him and the jinn a relationship, but the jinn know that they will be brought forth [to account]. Exalted is Allah above what they describe﴾ [As-Saffat: 158–159].

'Ali ibn Abi Talha and al-Dahhak narrated from Ibn 'Abbas regarding ﴿They invoke besides Him none but female [deities]﴾: "He means the dead."

Mubarak [i.e., Ibn Fudala] narrated from al-Hasan regarding ﴿They invoke besides Him none but female [deities]﴾: al-Hasan said: "The females are everything dead that has no spirit in it, whether a dry piece of wood or a dry stone." Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Jarir narrated it, and it is gharib.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And they invoke none but Satan, a rebellious [devil]﴾, meaning: it is he who commanded them to that, made it appealing to them and adorned it for them, and in reality they are worshipping Iblis, as He said, the Exalted: ﴿Did I not charge you, O children of Adam, that you not worship Satan? Indeed, he is to you a clear enemy﴾ [Ya-Sin: 60]. And He, the Exalted, said, informing about the angels that they will say on the Day of Resurrection, concerning the polytheists who claimed to worship them in the world: ﴿Rather, they used to worship the jinn; most of them were believers in them﴾ [Saba: 41].

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Allah has cursed him﴾, meaning: He expelled him and removed him far from His mercy, and drove him out of His neighborhood.

And [Satan] said: ﴿I will surely take from Your servants an appointed portion﴾, meaning: a specified, determined, known share. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: "From every thousand, nine hundred and ninety-nine to the Fire, and one to Paradise."

﴿And I will surely mislead them﴾, meaning: from the truth. ﴿And I will surely arouse in them desires﴾, meaning: I will adorn for them the abandonment of repentance, promise them false hopes, command them to procrastinate and delay, and deceive them concerning themselves.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And I will surely command them, so they will slit the ears of cattle﴾, Qatada, al-Suddi and others said: it means splitting them and making them a mark and sign for the baheera and the sa'iba.

﴿And I will surely command them, so they will alter the creation of Allah﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: "By that is meant the castration of animals." Likewise it was narrated from Ibn 'Umar, Anas, Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, 'Ikrima, Abu 'Iyad, Abu Salih, Qatada, and al-Thawri. And there has come in a hadith the prohibition of that [Narrated by Ibn Abi Shayba in al-Musannaf (12/225) and al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan al-Kubra (10/24) through Nafi' from Ibn 'Umar who said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade the castration of horses and animals," and Ibn 'Umar said: "In it is the change of creation."].

Al-Hasan ibn Abi al-Hasan al-Basri said: "By that is meant tattooing." And in Sahih Muslim there is the prohibition of tattooing the face [Sahih Muslim, no. 2117, from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah that the Prophet ﷺ passed by a donkey whose face had been branded, and said: "May Allah curse the one who branded it."]. And in another wording: "May Allah curse whoever does that." And in the Sahih from Ibn Mas'ud that he said: "Allah has cursed the women who tattoo and those who have themselves tattooed, the women who pluck their facial hair and those who have it plucked, and those who file their teeth for beauty, who alter the creation of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic." Then he said: "Shall I not curse whom the Messenger of Allah ﷺ cursed, and who is in the Book of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic?" meaning His saying: ﴿And whatever the Messenger has given you, take; and what he has forbidden you, refrain from﴾ [Al-Hashr: 7] [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 5948].

Ibn 'Abbas in one narration, and Mujahid, 'Ikrima also, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, al-Hasan, Qatada, al-Hakam, al-Suddi, al-Dahhak, and 'Ata al-Khurasani said regarding His saying: ﴿And I will surely command them, so they will alter the creation of Allah﴾ that it means: the religion of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. This is like His saying, the Exalted: ﴿So direct your face toward the religion, inclining to truth. [Adhere to] the fitrah of Allah upon which He has created mankind. No change should there be to the creation of Allah﴾ [Ar-Rum: 30], according to those who take it as a command, meaning: do not change the fitrah of Allah, and leave people upon their fitrah, as established in the two Sahihs from Abu Hurayra who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Every child is born upon the fitrah; then his parents make him a Jew, or a Christian, or a Magian, just as an animal gives birth to a complete animal. Do you see any mutilation in it?" And in Sahih Muslim, from 'Iyad ibn Himar who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: Indeed, I created My servants as hanifs, but the devils came to them and led them astray from their religion, and made unlawful for them what I had made lawful for them" [Sahih Muslim, no. 2865].

* *

As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And whoever takes Satan as an ally instead of Allah has certainly suffered a clear loss﴾, meaning: he has lost this world and the Hereafter, and that is a loss for which there is no compensation and no recovery of what has been lost.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿He promises them and arouses desires in them, but Satan does not promise them except delusion﴾. This is a report about reality, because Satan promises his allies and gives them false hopes that they will be the winners in this world and the Hereafter, but he has lied and fabricated in that; therefore He said: ﴿And Satan does not promise them except delusion﴾, as He, the Exalted, said, reporting about Iblis on the Day of Return: ﴿And Satan will say when the matter has been decided: Indeed, Allah promised you a true promise, and I promised you, but I broke my promise to you. I had over you no authority except that I invited you, and you responded to me. So do not blame me but blame yourselves. I cannot help you, nor can you help me. Indeed, I deny your association of me [with Allah] before. Indeed, for the wrongdoers is a painful punishment﴾ [Ibrahim: 22].

* *

As for His saying: i.e., those who find his promises and desires appealing: ﴿Their refuge is Hell﴾, meaning: their destination and final abode on the Day of their reckoning. ﴿And they will not find for themselves any escape therefrom﴾, meaning: there is no way out for them from it, no turning away, no deliverance, and no refuge.

Then He mentioned the condition of the happy, the pious, and what they have in their final destiny of complete honor, saying: ﴿But those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾, meaning: their hearts affirm and their limbs act upon what they were commanded of good, and they abandon what they were forbidden of evil. ﴿We will admit them to gardens beneath which rivers flow﴾, meaning: they will direct them wherever they wish and wherever they desire. ﴿Abiding therein forever﴾, meaning: without cessation and without removal. ﴿The promise of Allah is true﴾, meaning: this is a promise from Allah, and the promise of Allah is known in reality to be certain to occur without doubt; for this He emphasized it with the verbal noun that confirms the certainty of the report, which is His saying: ﴿true﴾. Then He said: ﴿And who is more truthful than Allah in statement?﴾, meaning: no one is more truthful than Him in speech and report; there is no god but Him, and no lord other than Him.

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to say in his sermon: "Indeed, the truest speech is the Book of Allah, the best guidance is the guidance of Muhammad ﷺ, and the worst of matters are their newly invented ones, and every newly invented matter is an innovation, every innovation is a misguidance, and every misguidance is in the Fire."

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 4, verses 123–126 (part 1 of 3):

Qatadah said: It was mentioned to us that the Muslims and the People of the Scripture boasted. The People of the Scripture said: "Our prophet came before your prophet, and our book came before your book, so we are closer to Allah than you are." The Muslims said: "We are closer to Allah than you are. Our prophet is the Seal of the Prophets, and our book overrides the books that came before it." So Allah revealed: ﴿It is not by your wishful thinking, nor by the wishful thinking of the People of the Scripture. Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it.﴾ And: ﴿And who is better in religion than one who submits himself to Allah while being a doer of good [and follows the religion of Abraham, inclining toward truth]﴾ [[Addition from manuscripts R and A.]] ﴿...﴾ the verse. Thus Allah established the proof of the Muslims over those who opposed them among the people of the religions.

The same was narrated from al-Suddi, Masruq, al-Dahhak, Abu Salih and others. Al-Awfi also narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that he said regarding this verse: The people of the religions disputed. The People of the Torah said: "Our book is the best of books, and our prophet is the best of prophets." The People of the Gospel said the same. The People of Islam said: "There is no religion except Islam. Our book has abrogated every book, our prophet is the Seal of the Prophets, and you were commanded, and we were commanded, to believe in your book and act upon our book." So Allah judged between them, saying: ﴿It is not by your wishful thinking, nor by the wishful thinking of the People of the Scripture. Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it.﴾ And He gave them a choice between the religions, saying: ﴿And who is better in religion than one who submits himself to Allah while being a doer of good [and follows the religion of Abraham, inclining toward truth]﴾ [[Addition from manuscript R.]] ﴿...﴾ up to His saying: ﴿And Allah took Abraham as an intimate friend.﴾

Mujahid said: The Arabs said: "We will not be resurrected and we will not be punished." The Jews and Christians said: ﴿None will enter Paradise except those who are Jews or Christians﴾ [al-Baqarah: 111], and they said: ﴿The Fire will not touch us except for a few numbered days﴾ [al-Baqarah: 80].

The meaning of this verse is that religion is not by adornment nor by wishful thinking. Not everyone who claims something obtains it merely by his claim, and not everyone who says, "I am the one who is right," is heeded merely for saying so, until he has a proof from Allah. For this reason, the Exalted said: ﴿It is not by your wishful thinking, nor by the wishful thinking of the People of the Scripture.﴾ That is: salvation is not for you, nor for them, by mere wishing. Rather, what counts is obedience to Allah and following what He has legislated through the lips of His noble messengers. For this reason He said after it: ﴿Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it,﴾ like His saying: ﴿So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it﴾ [al-Zalzalah: 7–8].

It has been narrated that when this verse was revealed it was difficult for many of the Companions. Imam Ahmad said: 'Abd Allah ibn Numayr narrated to us, Isma'il narrated to us, from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Zuhayr, who said: I was informed that Abu Bakr said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is the good state after this verse: ﴿It is not by your wishful thinking, nor by the wishful thinking of the People of the Scripture. Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it﴾? Every evil we do, we will be recompensed for it?" The Prophet ﷺ said: "May Allah forgive you, O Abu Bakr. Do you not fall ill? Do you not become weary? Do you not grieve? Does not hardship (al-la'waa') befall you?" [[In manuscript A: "Does not harm befall you?"]] He said: "Yes." He said: "That is what you are recompensed with."

Sa'id ibn Mansur narrated it from Khalaf ibn Khalifah, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, with the same. Ibn Hibban narrated it in his Sahih from Abu Ya'la, from Abu Khaythamah, from Yahya ibn Sa'id, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, with the same. Al-Hakim narrated it through the route of Sufyan al-Thawri, from Isma'il, with the same. [[The Musnad (1/11), Sunan Sa'id ibn Mansur no. (696), Sahih Ibn Hibban no. (1734) "Mawarid," and al-Mustadrak (3/74).]]

Imam Ahmad also said: 'Abd al-Wahhab ibn 'Ata' narrated to us, from Ziyad al-Jassas, from 'Ali ibn Zayd, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Umar, who said: I heard Abu Bakr say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it in this world." [[Musnad (1/6).]]

Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh said: Ahmad ibn Hushaym ibn Juhaymah narrated to us, Yahya ibn Abi Talib narrated to us, 'Abd al-Wahhab ibn 'Ata' narrated to us, Ziyad al-Jassas narrated to us, from 'Ali ibn Zayd, from Mujahid, who said: 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar said: "Look at the place where 'Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr is crucified, and do not pass by it." He said: The boy forgot, and then Ibn 'Umar was looking at Ibn al-Zubayr. He said: "May Allah forgive you three times. By Allah, I did not know you except as one who fasted much, prayed much at night, and was much in maintaining the ties of kinship. By Allah, I truly hope that, with what you have suffered, Allah will not punish you after it." He said: Then he turned to me and said: I heard Abu Bakr al-Siddiq say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever does evil in this world will be recompensed for it."

Abu Bakr al-Bazzar narrated it in his Musnad, from al-Fadl ibn Sahl, from 'Abd al-Wahhab ibn 'Ata', with the same, abridged. [[Musnad al-Bazzar no. (21). Al-Daraqutni said in al-'Ilal (4/223): "Ziyad al-Jassas narrated it, and there was disagreement regarding him. 'Abd al-Wahhab ibn 'Ata' narrated it from Ziyad, from 'Ali ibn Zayd, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Umar, from Abu Bakr. But Abu 'Asim al-'Abbadani contradicted him, narrating it from Ziyad al-Jassas, from Salim, from Ibn 'Umar, from 'Umar. There is nothing in it that is established."]] And it is mentioned in the Musnad of Ibn al-Zubayr: Ibrahim ibn al-Mustamirr al-'Aufi narrated to us [[In manuscripts R and A: "al-'Awfi."]], 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Sulaym ibn Hayyan narrated to us, my father narrated to me, from my grandfather Hayyan ibn Bistam, who said: I was with Ibn 'Umar, and he passed by 'Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr while he was crucified. He said: "May Allah have mercy on you, Abu Khubayb. I heard your father—meaning al-Zubayr—say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it in this world and the Hereafter.'" Then he said: "We do not know it being narrated from al-Zubayr except through this route." [[Musnad al-Bazzar no. (962). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (7/12): "It contains 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Sulaym ibn Hayyan, whom I do not know, and the rest of its narrators are trustworthy." The apparent name is 'Abd al-Rahim, as in al-Daraqutni's al-'Ilal (4/223), when he was asked about the route of Sulaym ibn Hayyan from his father from Ibn 'Umar, and he said: "'Abd al-Rahman ibn Sulaym ibn Hayyan narrates it from his father from Ibn 'Umar," and at another time he said: "From his father from Nafi' from Ibn 'Umar." 'Abd al-Rahim is weak, and Ziyad is weak.]]

Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh said: Ahmad ibn Kamil narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Sa'd al-'Awfi narrated to us, Rawh ibn 'Ubadah narrated to us, Musa ibn 'Ubaydah narrated to us, a client of Ibn Sibaa' narrated to me, who said: I heard Ibn 'Umar narrate from Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, who said: I was with the Prophet ﷺ when this verse was revealed: ﴿Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it, and will not find for himself besides Allah any protector or helper.﴾ The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "O Abu Bakr, shall I recite to you a verse that was revealed to me?" I said: "Yes, O Messenger of Allah." So he recited it to me. I did not know except that I felt a breaking in my back until I stretched out. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "What is the matter with you, O Abu Bakr?" I said: "My father and mother be sacrificed for you, O Messenger of Allah! Which of us has not done evil? Will we really be recompensed for every evil we have done?!" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "As for you, O Abu Bakr, and your companions who are believers, you will be recompensed for it in this world until you meet Allah, and you will have no sins. As for the others, it will be gathered for them until they are recompensed for it on the Day of Resurrection."

Likewise al-Tirmidhi narrated it from Yahya ibn Musa, and 'Abd ibn Humayd, from Rawh ibn 'Ubadah, with the same. Then he said: Musa ibn 'Ubaydah is weak, and the client of Ibn Sibaa' is unknown. [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3039).]]

[Ibn Jarir said: al-Ghulam narrated to us, al-Husayn narrated to us, al-Hajjaj narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah informed me, who said: When it was revealed, Abu Bakr said: "O Messenger of Allah, the back-breaking verse has come!" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "It refers only to the calamities of this world."] [[Addition from manuscript A.]]

Another route from al-Siddiq: Ibn Mardawayh said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ishaq al-'Askari narrated to us, Muhammad ibn 'Amir al-Sa'di narrated to us, Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us, Fudayl ibn 'Iyad narrated to us, from Sulayman ibn Mihran, from Muslim ibn Subayh, from Masruq, who said: Abu Bakr [al-Siddiq] [[Addition from manuscript A.]] said: "O Messenger of Allah, how severe is this verse: ﴿Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it﴾!" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Calamities, illnesses and griefs in this world are a recompense." [[Abu Nu'aym narrated it in al-Hilyah (8/119) through this route, with the same, and in it is Muhammad al-Sa'di, who used to lie and fabricate.]]

Another route: Ibn Jarir said: 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Ziyad and Ahmad ibn Mansur narrated to me, both saying: Zayd ibn al-Hubab narrated to us, 'Abd al-Malik ibn al-Hasan al-Harithi narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Zayd ibn Qunfudh narrated to us, from 'A'ishah, from Abu Bakr, who said: When it was revealed: ﴿Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it,﴾ Abu Bakr said: "O Messenger of Allah, will we be held accountable for everything we do?" He said: "O Abu Bakr, does not what befalls you such-and-such? That is an expiation." [[Tafsir al-Tabari (9/240).]]

Another hadith: Sa'id ibn Mansur said: 'Abd Allah ibn Wahb informed us, 'Amr ibn al-Harith informed me, that Bakr ibn Sawadah narrated to him, that Yazid ibn Abi Yazid narrated to him, from 'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr, from 'A'ishah, that a man recited this verse: ﴿Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it,﴾ and said: "Are we really recompensed for every deed? Then we are ruined!" This reached the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said: "Yes. The believer is recompensed in this world, in his self, in his body, in what harms him." [[Sunan Sa'id ibn Mansur no. (699), and Ahmad in al-Musnad (6/65) through the route of 'Abd Allah ibn Wahb with the same.]]

Another route: Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Salamah ibn Bashir narrated to us, Hushaym narrated to us, from Abu 'Amir, from Ibn Abi Mulaykah, from 'A'ishah, who said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, I know the most severe verse in the Quran." He said: "What is it, O 'A'ishah?" I said: ﴿Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it.﴾ He said: "It is what befalls the believing servant, even the prick he is pricked with."

Ibn Jarir narrated it through the narration of Hushaym, with the same. Abu Dawud narrated it through the narration of Abu 'Amir Salih ibn Rustum al-Khazzaz, with the same. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (9/246) and Sunan Abi Dawud no. (3093).]]

Another route: Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said: Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from 'Ali ibn Zayd, from Umayyah, that she asked 'A'ishah about this verse: ﴿Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it.﴾ She said: "No one has asked me about this verse since I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about it. I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said: 'O 'A'ishah, this is Allah's transaction with the servant, for what befalls him of fever, prick, and thorn, even the merchandise a man places in his sleeve, then he searches for it and finds it in his pocket. Indeed, the believer comes out of his sins just as red gold comes out of the furnace.'" [[Musnad al-Tayalisi no. (1584), and Ahmad in al-Musnad (6/218) through the route of Hammad ibn Salamah with the same. Note: In al-Tayalisi it reads "mu'atabah" instead of "mubaya'ah," and in Ahmad it reads "mutabi'ah."]]

Another route: Ibn Mardawayh said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Abu al-Qasim narrated to us, Surayj [[In manuscripts R and A: "Shurayh."]] ibn Yunus narrated to us, Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Muhammad ibn Zayd ibn al-Muhajir, from 'A'ishah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asked about this verse: ﴿Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it.﴾ He said: "Indeed the believer is rewarded in everything, even in the al-faydh [[In manuscript R: "al-ghayd"; in manuscript A: "al-ghayt." Al-faydh means the departure of the soul.]] at the time of death."

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 4, verses 123–126 (part 2 of 3):

Imam Ahmad said: Husayn narrated to us, from Za'idah, from Layth, from Mujahid, from 'Aishah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When the sins of a servant become many, and he has nothing that expiates them, Allah tests him with grief so that He may expiate them for him." [[Al-Musnad (6/157).]]

Another hadith: Sa'id ibn Mansur said, from Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah, from 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhaysin, who heard Muhammad ibn Qays ibn Makhramah report that Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, said: When the verse ﴿Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it﴾ was revealed, it weighed heavily upon the Muslims. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to them: "Be steadfast, and draw near (to what is right), for in everything that afflicts a Muslim there is an expiation, even the thorn that pricks him and the stumble he suffers." [[Sunan Sa'id ibn Mansur (no. 694), al-Musnad (2/248), Sahih Muslim (no. 2574), Sunan al-Tirmidhi (no. 5029), and Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra (no. 11122).]]

Ahmad narrated it in the same way from Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah, and Muslim, al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i (narrated it) from the hadith of Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah, with the same chain.
