Ibn Mardawayh narrated it through Rawh and Mu'tamir, both from Ibrahim ibn Yazid [in A: "Zayd"], from 'Abd Allah ibn Ibrahim, who said: I heard Abu Hurayrah say: When this verse was revealed, ﴿It is not by your wishful thinking, nor by the wishful thinking of the People of the Book: whoever does evil will be recompensed for it﴾, we wept and grieved, and we said: "O Messenger of Allah, this verse has left nothing (for us)." He said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, it is indeed as it was revealed. But rejoice and draw near (to what is right) and be steadfast, for no one among you is afflicted in this world but that Allah expiates his sin by it, even the thorn that one of you pricks in his foot." [[In its chain is Ibrahim ibn Yazid al-Khawzami, who is weak.]]

'Ata' ibn Yasar said, from Abu Sa'id and Abu Hurayrah, that they both heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "No fatigue, nor illness, nor sickness, nor grief afflicts the believer, not even the worry that troubles him, but that some of his evil deeds are expiated by it." It was recorded by al-Bukhari and Muslim. [[Sahih al-Bukhari (nos. 5641, 5642) and Sahih Muslim (no. 2573).]]

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Yahya narrated to us, from Sa'd ibn Ishaq, who said: Zaynab bint Ka'b ibn 'Ujrah narrated to me, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: A man said to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "Do you see these illnesses that afflict us? What is their benefit for us?" He said: "They are expiations." Ubayy said: "Even if they are few?" He said: "Even if it is a thorn or something more than that." (The narrator) said: So Ubayy invoked (a curse) upon himself, that the fever would not leave him until he died, so that it would not distract him from Hajj, 'Umrah, jihad in the way of Allah, or the obligatory prayer in congregation. No one touched him but he felt its heat, until he died, may Allah be pleased with him. Ahmad alone narrated it. [[Al-Musnad (3/23). Abu Ya'la also narrated it in his Musnad (2/281), and al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (2/301): "Its narrators are trustworthy."]]

Another hadith: Ibn Mardawayh narrated through the route of Husayn ibn Waqid, from al-Kalbi, from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, (what about) ﴿whoever does evil will be recompensed for it﴾?" He said: "Yes. And whoever does a good deed will be rewarded for it tenfold. So he who is overcome by his single (bad deed) will be destroyed, (despite) his ten (good deeds)." [[Its chain is very weak, as was mentioned in the introduction.]]

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Humayd, from al-Hasan, regarding ﴿whoever does evil will be recompensed for it﴾, that he said: "(It refers to) the disbeliever," and then he recited: ﴿And do We recompense any but the ungrateful?﴾ [Saba': 17].

Similarly, it is reported from Ibn 'Abbas and Sa'id ibn Jubayr that they both interpreted "evil" here as "shirk" (associating partners with Allah).

* *

As for His saying: ﴿and he will not find for himself, besides Allah, any protector or any helper﴾: 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: "Except that he repents, and then Allah accepts his repentance." Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it.

The sound view is that this applies generally to all deeds, based on the hadiths that have preceded, and this is the view preferred by Ibn Jarir. And Allah knows best.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And whoever does righteous deeds, whether male or female, while being a believer [then those will enter Paradise and will not be wronged, even by the size of a naqir]﴾ [[Addition from the manuscripts Waw and A; in H it is written "the verse."]]: when He mentioned the recompense for evil deeds, and that it must take its due from the servant, either in this world (which is better for him) or in the Hereafter (and we seek refuge in Allah from that, and ask Him for well-being in this world and the Hereafter, and for pardon, forgiveness and forbearance), He began to explain His goodness, generosity and mercy in accepting the righteous deeds of His servants, both male and female, on condition of faith, and that He will admit them into Paradise and will not wrong them of their good deeds even by the size of the naqir. The naqir is the small hollow on the back of a date stone. The fatil (the thread in the split of a date stone) has already been discussed, and this naqir and the fatil are both in the date stone, and likewise the qitmir, which is the thin membrane over the date stone. These three are mentioned in the Qur'an.

Then He said, may He be exalted: ﴿And who is better in religion than one who submits his face to Allah﴾, sincerely dedicating his deed to his Lord, may He be mighty and majestic, acting in faith and seeking reward, ﴿while he is a doer of good﴾, meaning, following in his deed what Allah has prescribed for him and what He sent His Messenger with, of guidance and the religion of truth. These two conditions are such that no worker's deed is valid without them: it must be sincere (for Allah alone) and correct (in conformity with the Law). Sincerity means it is for Allah, and correctness means it follows the Shari'ah. Its outward aspect is valid through following (the Prophet), and its inward aspect through sincerity. Whoever lacks either of these two conditions, his deed is corrupt. Whoever lacks sincerity is a hypocrite, who show off to people. Whoever lacks following (the Prophet) is astray and ignorant. When both are combined, it is the deed of the believers: ﴿those from whom We accept the best of what they have done and overlook their evil deeds, among the companions of Paradise, a true promise which they had been promised﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 16]. For this reason He said: ﴿and follows the religion of Abraham, a hanif﴾. They are Muhammad and his followers until the Day of Resurrection, as He said: ﴿Indeed, the closest of people to Abraham are those who followed him, and this Prophet, and those who believe; and Allah is the ally of the believers﴾ [Al 'Imran: 68]. And He said: ﴿Say: Indeed, my Lord has guided me to a straight path, a correct religion, the religion of Abraham, a hanif, and he was not of those who associate partners with Allah﴾ [[Addition from A.]] [al-An'am: 161]. And: ﴿Then We revealed to you: Follow the religion of Abraham, a hanif, and he was not of those who associate partners with Allah﴾ [al-Nahl: 123]. The hanif is one who turns away from shirk with intent, that is, one who abandons it with insight, and turns entirely toward the truth, with nothing diverting him from it and no one turning him back from it.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And Allah took Abraham as an intimate friend (khalil)﴾: this is in the context of encouraging following him, because he is an imam to be emulated, for he reached the furthest point to which servants can draw near to Allah. He attained the rank of khullah (intimate friendship), which is the highest station of love, and this was only because of the abundance of his obedience to his Lord, as He described him in His saying: ﴿and Abraham who fulfilled (his commitments)﴾ [al-Najm: 37]. Many of the early scholars said: That is, he carried out all that he was commanded, and fulfilled every station of worship, so that no great matter distracted him from a small one, nor a big matter from a little one. And He said: ﴿And when Abraham was tested by his Lord with certain words, and he fulfilled them, (Allah) said: Indeed, I will make you an imam for the people﴾ [[Addition from R and A.]] [al-Baqarah: 124], to the end of the verse. And He said: ﴿Indeed, Abraham was a community, devoutly obedient to Allah, a hanif, and he was not of those who associate partners with Allah, grateful for His favors. He chose him and guided him to a straight path. And We gave him good in this world, and indeed, in the Hereafter he is among the righteous﴾ [[Addition from R.]] [al-Nahl: 120–122].

Al-Bukhari said: Sulayman ibn Harb narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Habib ibn Abi Thabit, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from 'Amr ibn Maymun, who said: When Mu'adh came to Yemen, he led them in the dawn prayer, and he recited: ﴿And Allah took Abraham as an intimate friend﴾. A man from the people said: "The eye of Abraham's mother has indeed been comforted."

Ibn Jarir mentioned in his tafsir, from some of them, that Allah named him khalil only because the people of his region suffered a drought, so he travelled to a khalil (friend) of his from the people of Mosul (and some of them said: from the people of Egypt) to obtain food for his family from him. But he did not find what he needed with him. When he drew near to his family, he passed through a sandy desert, and he said: "If only I could fill my sacks with this sand, so that I do not sadden my family by returning to them without provisions, and so that they may think that I have brought them what they love." So he did that, and the sand in his sacks turned into flour. When he reached his home, he slept, and his family rose and opened the sacks, and they found flour. They kneaded it and baked bread from it. He awoke and asked them about the flour from which they had baked, and they said: "From the flour you brought from your khalil." He said: "Yes, it is from my khalil, Allah." So Allah named him khalil because of this.

The authenticity and occurrence of this report are open to question. At best it is an Isra'iliyyat report, which is neither confirmed nor denied. Rather, he was named "Khalil of Allah" because of the intense love of his Lord, may He be mighty and majestic, for him, on account of the obedience he rendered, which Allah loves and is pleased with. For this reason it is established in the two Sahihs, from the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, that when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) addressed them in the last sermon he gave, he said: "To proceed: O people, if I were to take any of the people of the earth as a khalil, I would have taken Abu Bakr ibn Abi Quhafah as a khalil. But your companion is the khalil of Allah." [[Sahih al-Bukhari (no. 3654) and Sahih Muslim (no. 2382). The wording "your companion is the khalil of Allah" is from the hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, narrated by Muslim (no. 2383).]]

And it has come through the routes of Jundub ibn 'Abd Allah al-Bajali, 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As and 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, from the Prophet (ﷺ): "Indeed Allah has taken me as a khalil just as He took Abraham as a khalil." [[The hadith of Jundub ibn 'Abd Allah is narrated by Muslim in his Sahih (no. 532). The hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr is narrated by al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman (no. 9616). The hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud is narrated by Muslim in his Sahih (no. 2383).]]

Ibn Abi Hatim is not the only one to report this. Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh said: Abd al-Rahim ibn Muhammad ibn Muslim narrated to us, Isma'il ibn Ahmad ibn Usayd narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn Ya'qub al-Jawzajani narrated to us in Makkah, Ubayd Allah [[In MS. D and R: "Abd Allah".]] al-Hanafi narrated to us, Zam'ah ibn Salih narrated to us, from Salamah ibn Wahram, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Some of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ were sitting, waiting for him. He came out until he drew near them and heard them discussing. He heard their conversation, and some of them were saying: "How strange! If Allah has taken a khalil (intimate friend) from among His creation, then Ibrahim is His khalil!" Another said: "What is so remarkable about Allah speaking to Musa directly!" Another said: "Isa is the Spirit of Allah and His Word!" Another said: "Adam, whom Allah chose!" So he came out to them, greeted them, and said: "I have heard your talk and your amazement, that Ibrahim is the khalil of Allah, and so he is. Musa is His interlocutor (kalim), Isa is His Spirit and His Word, and Adam is one whom Allah chose, and so he is. Indeed, I am the beloved (habib) of Allah, and I say this without pride. I will bear the banner of praise on the Day of Resurrection, and I say this without pride. I will be the first intercessor and the first whose intercession is accepted, and I say this without pride. I will be the first to move the rings of Paradise, and Allah will open it for me and admit me into it, and with me will be the poor among the believers, and I say this without pride. I will be the most honoured of the first and the last on the Day of Resurrection, and I say this without pride."

This hadith is gharib (strange, with a weak or single chain) from this route, but parts of it have supporting narrations in the Sahih collections and elsewhere. [[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in his Sunan, no. 3616, and he said: "This is a gharib hadith."]]

Qatadah narrated from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, that he said: "Are you amazed that khullah (intimate friendship) was given to Ibrahim, speech to Musa, and vision to Muhammad? May the blessings and peace of Allah be upon them all."

Al-Hakim narrated it in his Mustadrak and said: "It is sahih (sound) according to the conditions of al-Bukhari, though they (al-Bukhari and Muslim) did not include it." It is also narrated similarly from Anas ibn Malik and from many Companions and Successors, and from the leading scholars of the earlier and later generations.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Yahya ibn Abdak al-Qazwini narrated to us, Muhammad, meaning Ibn Sa'id ibn Sabiq, narrated to us, Amr, meaning Ibn Abi Qays, narrated to us, from Asim, from Abu Rashid, from Ubayd ibn Umayr, who said: Ibrahim, peace be upon him, used to host people. One day he went out seeking someone to host, but he found no one to host, so he returned to his house and found a man standing in it. He said: "O servant of Allah, what brought you into my house without my permission?" He replied: "I entered it with the permission of its Lord." He said: "And who are you?" He replied: "I am the Angel of Death. My Lord sent me to one of His servants to give him the good news that Allah has taken him as a khalil." He said: "Who is he? By Allah, if you tell me about him, and he is in the farthest of lands, I will go to him, and I will not leave him as a neighbour until death separates us." He said: "That servant is you." He said: "Me?" He said: "Yes." He said: "For what reason has Allah taken me as a khalil?" He said: "Because you give to people and do not ask them." [[Its chain is mursal (broken).]]

And Mahmud ibn Khalid al-Sulami narrated to us, al-Walid narrated to us, from Ishaq ibn Yasar, who said: When Allah took Ibrahim as a khalil, He placed trembling (wajal) in his heart, to the extent that the pounding of his heart could be heard from a distance, like the fluttering of birds in the air. Likewise it has been described of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that the sound of weeping in his chest was heard like the boiling of a cauldron.

* *

His saying: ﴿And to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾ means: all of it is His possession, His servants and His creation, and He is the one who disposes of all of that. None can reject what He has decreed, none can overturn what He has judged, and He is not questioned about what He does, because of His greatness, His power, His justice, His wisdom, His kindness and His mercy.

* *

His saying: ﴿And Allah is ever, of all things, encompassing﴾ means: His knowledge pervades all of that. No secret of His servants is hidden from Him, and not even the weight of an atom in the heavens or on the earth escapes His knowledge, nor anything smaller than that or greater. No atom is hidden from Him, whether it is visible to observers or concealed.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 4, verses 123–126 (part 1 of 3):

Qatadah said: It was mentioned to us that the Muslims and the People of the Scripture boasted. The People of the Scripture said: "Our prophet came before your prophet, and our book came before your book, so we are closer to Allah than you are." The Muslims said: "We are closer to Allah than you are. Our prophet is the Seal of the Prophets, and our book overrides the books that came before it." So Allah revealed: ﴿It is not by your wishful thinking, nor by the wishful thinking of the People of the Scripture. Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it.﴾ And: ﴿And who is better in religion than one who submits himself to Allah while being a doer of good [and follows the religion of Abraham, inclining toward truth]﴾ [[Addition from manuscripts R and A.]] ﴿...﴾ the verse. Thus Allah established the proof of the Muslims over those who opposed them among the people of the religions.

The same was narrated from al-Suddi, Masruq, al-Dahhak, Abu Salih and others. Al-Awfi also narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that he said regarding this verse: The people of the religions disputed. The People of the Torah said: "Our book is the best of books, and our prophet is the best of prophets." The People of the Gospel said the same. The People of Islam said: "There is no religion except Islam. Our book has abrogated every book, our prophet is the Seal of the Prophets, and you were commanded, and we were commanded, to believe in your book and act upon our book." So Allah judged between them, saying: ﴿It is not by your wishful thinking, nor by the wishful thinking of the People of the Scripture. Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it.﴾ And He gave them a choice between the religions, saying: ﴿And who is better in religion than one who submits himself to Allah while being a doer of good [and follows the religion of Abraham, inclining toward truth]﴾ [[Addition from manuscript R.]] ﴿...﴾ up to His saying: ﴿And Allah took Abraham as an intimate friend.﴾

Mujahid said: The Arabs said: "We will not be resurrected and we will not be punished." The Jews and Christians said: ﴿None will enter Paradise except those who are Jews or Christians﴾ [al-Baqarah: 111], and they said: ﴿The Fire will not touch us except for a few numbered days﴾ [al-Baqarah: 80].

The meaning of this verse is that religion is not by adornment nor by wishful thinking. Not everyone who claims something obtains it merely by his claim, and not everyone who says, "I am the one who is right," is heeded merely for saying so, until he has a proof from Allah. For this reason, the Exalted said: ﴿It is not by your wishful thinking, nor by the wishful thinking of the People of the Scripture.﴾ That is: salvation is not for you, nor for them, by mere wishing. Rather, what counts is obedience to Allah and following what He has legislated through the lips of His noble messengers. For this reason He said after it: ﴿Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it,﴾ like His saying: ﴿So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it﴾ [al-Zalzalah: 7–8].

It has been narrated that when this verse was revealed it was difficult for many of the Companions. Imam Ahmad said: 'Abd Allah ibn Numayr narrated to us, Isma'il narrated to us, from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Zuhayr, who said: I was informed that Abu Bakr said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is the good state after this verse: ﴿It is not by your wishful thinking, nor by the wishful thinking of the People of the Scripture. Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it﴾? Every evil we do, we will be recompensed for it?" The Prophet ﷺ said: "May Allah forgive you, O Abu Bakr. Do you not fall ill? Do you not become weary? Do you not grieve? Does not hardship (al-la'waa') befall you?" [[In manuscript A: "Does not harm befall you?"]] He said: "Yes." He said: "That is what you are recompensed with."

Sa'id ibn Mansur narrated it from Khalaf ibn Khalifah, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, with the same. Ibn Hibban narrated it in his Sahih from Abu Ya'la, from Abu Khaythamah, from Yahya ibn Sa'id, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, with the same. Al-Hakim narrated it through the route of Sufyan al-Thawri, from Isma'il, with the same. [[The Musnad (1/11), Sunan Sa'id ibn Mansur no. (696), Sahih Ibn Hibban no. (1734) "Mawarid," and al-Mustadrak (3/74).]]

Imam Ahmad also said: 'Abd al-Wahhab ibn 'Ata' narrated to us, from Ziyad al-Jassas, from 'Ali ibn Zayd, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Umar, who said: I heard Abu Bakr say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it in this world." [[Musnad (1/6).]]

Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh said: Ahmad ibn Hushaym ibn Juhaymah narrated to us, Yahya ibn Abi Talib narrated to us, 'Abd al-Wahhab ibn 'Ata' narrated to us, Ziyad al-Jassas narrated to us, from 'Ali ibn Zayd, from Mujahid, who said: 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar said: "Look at the place where 'Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr is crucified, and do not pass by it." He said: The boy forgot, and then Ibn 'Umar was looking at Ibn al-Zubayr. He said: "May Allah forgive you three times. By Allah, I did not know you except as one who fasted much, prayed much at night, and was much in maintaining the ties of kinship. By Allah, I truly hope that, with what you have suffered, Allah will not punish you after it." He said: Then he turned to me and said: I heard Abu Bakr al-Siddiq say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever does evil in this world will be recompensed for it."

Abu Bakr al-Bazzar narrated it in his Musnad, from al-Fadl ibn Sahl, from 'Abd al-Wahhab ibn 'Ata', with the same, abridged. [[Musnad al-Bazzar no. (21). Al-Daraqutni said in al-'Ilal (4/223): "Ziyad al-Jassas narrated it, and there was disagreement regarding him. 'Abd al-Wahhab ibn 'Ata' narrated it from Ziyad, from 'Ali ibn Zayd, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Umar, from Abu Bakr. But Abu 'Asim al-'Abbadani contradicted him, narrating it from Ziyad al-Jassas, from Salim, from Ibn 'Umar, from 'Umar. There is nothing in it that is established."]] And it is mentioned in the Musnad of Ibn al-Zubayr: Ibrahim ibn al-Mustamirr al-'Aufi narrated to us [[In manuscripts R and A: "al-'Awfi."]], 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Sulaym ibn Hayyan narrated to us, my father narrated to me, from my grandfather Hayyan ibn Bistam, who said: I was with Ibn 'Umar, and he passed by 'Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr while he was crucified. He said: "May Allah have mercy on you, Abu Khubayb. I heard your father—meaning al-Zubayr—say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it in this world and the Hereafter.'" Then he said: "We do not know it being narrated from al-Zubayr except through this route." [[Musnad al-Bazzar no. (962). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (7/12): "It contains 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Sulaym ibn Hayyan, whom I do not know, and the rest of its narrators are trustworthy." The apparent name is 'Abd al-Rahim, as in al-Daraqutni's al-'Ilal (4/223), when he was asked about the route of Sulaym ibn Hayyan from his father from Ibn 'Umar, and he said: "'Abd al-Rahman ibn Sulaym ibn Hayyan narrates it from his father from Ibn 'Umar," and at another time he said: "From his father from Nafi' from Ibn 'Umar." 'Abd al-Rahim is weak, and Ziyad is weak.]]

Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh said: Ahmad ibn Kamil narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Sa'd al-'Awfi narrated to us, Rawh ibn 'Ubadah narrated to us, Musa ibn 'Ubaydah narrated to us, a client of Ibn Sibaa' narrated to me, who said: I heard Ibn 'Umar narrate from Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, who said: I was with the Prophet ﷺ when this verse was revealed: ﴿Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it, and will not find for himself besides Allah any protector or helper.﴾ The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "O Abu Bakr, shall I recite to you a verse that was revealed to me?" I said: "Yes, O Messenger of Allah." So he recited it to me. I did not know except that I felt a breaking in my back until I stretched out. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "What is the matter with you, O Abu Bakr?" I said: "My father and mother be sacrificed for you, O Messenger of Allah! Which of us has not done evil? Will we really be recompensed for every evil we have done?!" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "As for you, O Abu Bakr, and your companions who are believers, you will be recompensed for it in this world until you meet Allah, and you will have no sins. As for the others, it will be gathered for them until they are recompensed for it on the Day of Resurrection."

Likewise al-Tirmidhi narrated it from Yahya ibn Musa, and 'Abd ibn Humayd, from Rawh ibn 'Ubadah, with the same. Then he said: Musa ibn 'Ubaydah is weak, and the client of Ibn Sibaa' is unknown. [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3039).]]

[Ibn Jarir said: al-Ghulam narrated to us, al-Husayn narrated to us, al-Hajjaj narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah informed me, who said: When it was revealed, Abu Bakr said: "O Messenger of Allah, the back-breaking verse has come!" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "It refers only to the calamities of this world."] [[Addition from manuscript A.]]

Another route from al-Siddiq: Ibn Mardawayh said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ishaq al-'Askari narrated to us, Muhammad ibn 'Amir al-Sa'di narrated to us, Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us, Fudayl ibn 'Iyad narrated to us, from Sulayman ibn Mihran, from Muslim ibn Subayh, from Masruq, who said: Abu Bakr [al-Siddiq] [[Addition from manuscript A.]] said: "O Messenger of Allah, how severe is this verse: ﴿Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it﴾!" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Calamities, illnesses and griefs in this world are a recompense." [[Abu Nu'aym narrated it in al-Hilyah (8/119) through this route, with the same, and in it is Muhammad al-Sa'di, who used to lie and fabricate.]]

Another route: Ibn Jarir said: 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Ziyad and Ahmad ibn Mansur narrated to me, both saying: Zayd ibn al-Hubab narrated to us, 'Abd al-Malik ibn al-Hasan al-Harithi narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Zayd ibn Qunfudh narrated to us, from 'A'ishah, from Abu Bakr, who said: When it was revealed: ﴿Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it,﴾ Abu Bakr said: "O Messenger of Allah, will we be held accountable for everything we do?" He said: "O Abu Bakr, does not what befalls you such-and-such? That is an expiation." [[Tafsir al-Tabari (9/240).]]

Another hadith: Sa'id ibn Mansur said: 'Abd Allah ibn Wahb informed us, 'Amr ibn al-Harith informed me, that Bakr ibn Sawadah narrated to him, that Yazid ibn Abi Yazid narrated to him, from 'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr, from 'A'ishah, that a man recited this verse: ﴿Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it,﴾ and said: "Are we really recompensed for every deed? Then we are ruined!" This reached the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said: "Yes. The believer is recompensed in this world, in his self, in his body, in what harms him." [[Sunan Sa'id ibn Mansur no. (699), and Ahmad in al-Musnad (6/65) through the route of 'Abd Allah ibn Wahb with the same.]]

Another route: Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Salamah ibn Bashir narrated to us, Hushaym narrated to us, from Abu 'Amir, from Ibn Abi Mulaykah, from 'A'ishah, who said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, I know the most severe verse in the Quran." He said: "What is it, O 'A'ishah?" I said: ﴿Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it.﴾ He said: "It is what befalls the believing servant, even the prick he is pricked with."

Ibn Jarir narrated it through the narration of Hushaym, with the same. Abu Dawud narrated it through the narration of Abu 'Amir Salih ibn Rustum al-Khazzaz, with the same. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (9/246) and Sunan Abi Dawud no. (3093).]]

Another route: Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said: Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from 'Ali ibn Zayd, from Umayyah, that she asked 'A'ishah about this verse: ﴿Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it.﴾ She said: "No one has asked me about this verse since I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about it. I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said: 'O 'A'ishah, this is Allah's transaction with the servant, for what befalls him of fever, prick, and thorn, even the merchandise a man places in his sleeve, then he searches for it and finds it in his pocket. Indeed, the believer comes out of his sins just as red gold comes out of the furnace.'" [[Musnad al-Tayalisi no. (1584), and Ahmad in al-Musnad (6/218) through the route of Hammad ibn Salamah with the same. Note: In al-Tayalisi it reads "mu'atabah" instead of "mubaya'ah," and in Ahmad it reads "mutabi'ah."]]

Another route: Ibn Mardawayh said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Abu al-Qasim narrated to us, Surayj [[In manuscripts R and A: "Shurayh."]] ibn Yunus narrated to us, Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Muhammad ibn Zayd ibn al-Muhajir, from 'A'ishah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asked about this verse: ﴿Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it.﴾ He said: "Indeed the believer is rewarded in everything, even in the al-faydh [[In manuscript R: "al-ghayd"; in manuscript A: "al-ghayt." Al-faydh means the departure of the soul.]] at the time of death."

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 4, verses 123–126 (part 2 of 3):

Imam Ahmad said: Husayn narrated to us, from Za'idah, from Layth, from Mujahid, from 'Aishah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When the sins of a servant become many, and he has nothing that expiates them, Allah tests him with grief so that He may expiate them for him." [[Al-Musnad (6/157).]]

Another hadith: Sa'id ibn Mansur said, from Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah, from 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhaysin, who heard Muhammad ibn Qays ibn Makhramah report that Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, said: When the verse ﴿Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it﴾ was revealed, it weighed heavily upon the Muslims. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to them: "Be steadfast, and draw near (to what is right), for in everything that afflicts a Muslim there is an expiation, even the thorn that pricks him and the stumble he suffers." [[Sunan Sa'id ibn Mansur (no. 694), al-Musnad (2/248), Sahih Muslim (no. 2574), Sunan al-Tirmidhi (no. 5029), and Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra (no. 11122).]]

Ahmad narrated it in the same way from Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah, and Muslim, al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i (narrated it) from the hadith of Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah, with the same chain. Ibn Mardawayh narrated it through Rawh and Mu'tamir, both from Ibrahim ibn Yazid [in A: "Zayd"], from 'Abd Allah ibn Ibrahim, who said: I heard Abu Hurayrah say: When this verse was revealed, ﴿It is not by your wishful thinking, nor by the wishful thinking of the People of the Book: whoever does evil will be recompensed for it﴾, we wept and grieved, and we said: "O Messenger of Allah, this verse has left nothing (for us)." He said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, it is indeed as it was revealed. But rejoice and draw near (to what is right) and be steadfast, for no one among you is afflicted in this world but that Allah expiates his sin by it, even the thorn that one of you pricks in his foot." [[In its chain is Ibrahim ibn Yazid al-Khawzami, who is weak.]]

'Ata' ibn Yasar said, from Abu Sa'id and Abu Hurayrah, that they both heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "No fatigue, nor illness, nor sickness, nor grief afflicts the believer, not even the worry that troubles him, but that some of his evil deeds are expiated by it." It was recorded by al-Bukhari and Muslim. [[Sahih al-Bukhari (nos. 5641, 5642) and Sahih Muslim (no. 2573).]]

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Yahya narrated to us, from Sa'd ibn Ishaq, who said: Zaynab bint Ka'b ibn 'Ujrah narrated to me, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: A man said to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "Do you see these illnesses that afflict us? What is their benefit for us?" He said: "They are expiations." Ubayy said: "Even if they are few?" He said: "Even if it is a thorn or something more than that." (The narrator) said: So Ubayy invoked (a curse) upon himself, that the fever would not leave him until he died, so that it would not distract him from Hajj, 'Umrah, jihad in the way of Allah, or the obligatory prayer in congregation. No one touched him but he felt its heat, until he died, may Allah be pleased with him. Ahmad alone narrated it. [[Al-Musnad (3/23). Abu Ya'la also narrated it in his Musnad (2/281), and al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (2/301): "Its narrators are trustworthy."]]

Another hadith: Ibn Mardawayh narrated through the route of Husayn ibn Waqid, from al-Kalbi, from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, (what about) ﴿whoever does evil will be recompensed for it﴾?" He said: "Yes. And whoever does a good deed will be rewarded for it tenfold. So he who is overcome by his single (bad deed) will be destroyed, (despite) his ten (good deeds)." [[Its chain is very weak, as was mentioned in the introduction.]]

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Humayd, from al-Hasan, regarding ﴿whoever does evil will be recompensed for it﴾, that he said: "(It refers to) the disbeliever," and then he recited: ﴿And do We recompense any but the ungrateful?﴾ [Saba': 17].

Similarly, it is reported from Ibn 'Abbas and Sa'id ibn Jubayr that they both interpreted "evil" here as "shirk" (associating partners with Allah).

* *

As for His saying: ﴿and he will not find for himself, besides Allah, any protector or any helper﴾: 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: "Except that he repents, and then Allah accepts his repentance." Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it.

The sound view is that this applies generally to all deeds, based on the hadiths that have preceded, and this is the view preferred by Ibn Jarir. And Allah knows best.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And whoever does righteous deeds, whether male or female, while being a believer [then those will enter Paradise and will not be wronged, even by the size of a naqir]﴾ [[Addition from the manuscripts Waw and A; in H it is written "the verse."]]: when He mentioned the recompense for evil deeds, and that it must take its due from the servant, either in this world (which is better for him) or in the Hereafter (and we seek refuge in Allah from that, and ask Him for well-being in this world and the Hereafter, and for pardon, forgiveness and forbearance), He began to explain His goodness, generosity and mercy in accepting the righteous deeds of His servants, both male and female, on condition of faith, and that He will admit them into Paradise and will not wrong them of their good deeds even by the size of the naqir. The naqir is the small hollow on the back of a date stone. The fatil (the thread in the split of a date stone) has already been discussed, and this naqir and the fatil are both in the date stone, and likewise the qitmir, which is the thin membrane over the date stone. These three are mentioned in the Qur'an.

Then He said, may He be exalted: ﴿And who is better in religion than one who submits his face to Allah﴾, sincerely dedicating his deed to his Lord, may He be mighty and majestic, acting in faith and seeking reward, ﴿while he is a doer of good﴾, meaning, following in his deed what Allah has prescribed for him and what He sent His Messenger with, of guidance and the religion of truth. These two conditions are such that no worker's deed is valid without them: it must be sincere (for Allah alone) and correct (in conformity with the Law). Sincerity means it is for Allah, and correctness means it follows the Shari'ah. Its outward aspect is valid through following (the Prophet), and its inward aspect through sincerity. Whoever lacks either of these two conditions, his deed is corrupt. Whoever lacks sincerity is a hypocrite, who show off to people. Whoever lacks following (the Prophet) is astray and ignorant. When both are combined, it is the deed of the believers: ﴿those from whom We accept the best of what they have done and overlook their evil deeds, among the companions of Paradise, a true promise which they had been promised﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 16]. For this reason He said: ﴿and follows the religion of Abraham, a hanif﴾. They are Muhammad and his followers until the Day of Resurrection, as He said: ﴿Indeed, the closest of people to Abraham are those who followed him, and this Prophet, and those who believe; and Allah is the ally of the believers﴾ [Al 'Imran: 68]. And He said: ﴿Say: Indeed, my Lord has guided me to a straight path, a correct religion, the religion of Abraham, a hanif, and he was not of those who associate partners with Allah﴾ [[Addition from A.]] [al-An'am: 161]. And: ﴿Then We revealed to you: Follow the religion of Abraham, a hanif, and he was not of those who associate partners with Allah﴾ [al-Nahl: 123]. The hanif is one who turns away from shirk with intent, that is, one who abandons it with insight, and turns entirely toward the truth, with nothing diverting him from it and no one turning him back from it.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And Allah took Abraham as an intimate friend (khalil)﴾: this is in the context of encouraging following him, because he is an imam to be emulated, for he reached the furthest point to which servants can draw near to Allah. He attained the rank of khullah (intimate friendship), which is the highest station of love, and this was only because of the abundance of his obedience to his Lord, as He described him in His saying: ﴿and Abraham who fulfilled (his commitments)﴾ [al-Najm: 37]. Many of the early scholars said: That is, he carried out all that he was commanded, and fulfilled every station of worship, so that no great matter distracted him from a small one, nor a big matter from a little one. And He said: ﴿And when Abraham was tested by his Lord with certain words, and he fulfilled them, (Allah) said: Indeed, I will make you an imam for the people﴾ [[Addition from R and A.]] [al-Baqarah: 124], to the end of the verse. And He said: ﴿Indeed, Abraham was a community, devoutly obedient to Allah, a hanif, and he was not of those who associate partners with Allah, grateful for His favors. He chose him and guided him to a straight path. And We gave him good in this world, and indeed, in the Hereafter he is among the righteous﴾ [[Addition from R.]] [al-Nahl: 120–122].

Al-Bukhari said: Sulayman ibn Harb narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Habib ibn Abi Thabit, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from 'Amr ibn Maymun, who said: When Mu'adh came to Yemen, he led them in the dawn prayer, and he recited: ﴿And Allah took Abraham as an intimate friend﴾. A man from the people said: "The eye of Abraham's mother has indeed been comforted."

Ibn Jarir mentioned in his tafsir, from some of them, that Allah named him khalil only because the people of his region suffered a drought, so he travelled to a khalil (friend) of his from the people of Mosul (and some of them said: from the people of Egypt) to obtain food for his family from him. But he did not find what he needed with him. When he drew near to his family, he passed through a sandy desert, and he said: "If only I could fill my sacks with this sand, so that I do not sadden my family by returning to them without provisions, and so that they may think that I have brought them what they love." So he did that, and the sand in his sacks turned into flour. When he reached his home, he slept, and his family rose and opened the sacks, and they found flour. They kneaded it and baked bread from it. He awoke and asked them about the flour from which they had baked, and they said: "From the flour you brought from your khalil." He said: "Yes, it is from my khalil, Allah." So Allah named him khalil because of this.

The authenticity and occurrence of this report are open to question. At best it is an Isra'iliyyat report, which is neither confirmed nor denied. Rather, he was named "Khalil of Allah" because of the intense love of his Lord, may He be mighty and majestic, for him, on account of the obedience he rendered, which Allah loves and is pleased with. For this reason it is established in the two Sahihs, from the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, that when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) addressed them in the last sermon he gave, he said: "To proceed: O people, if I were to take any of the people of the earth as a khalil, I would have taken Abu Bakr ibn Abi Quhafah as a khalil. But your companion is the khalil of Allah." [[Sahih al-Bukhari (no. 3654) and Sahih Muslim (no. 2382). The wording "your companion is the khalil of Allah" is from the hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, narrated by Muslim (no. 2383).]]

And it has come through the routes of Jundub ibn 'Abd Allah al-Bajali, 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As and 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, from the Prophet (ﷺ): "Indeed Allah has taken me as a khalil just as He took Abraham as a khalil." [[The hadith of Jundub ibn 'Abd Allah is narrated by Muslim in his Sahih (no. 532). The hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr is narrated by al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman (no. 9616). The hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud is narrated by Muslim in his Sahih (no. 2383).]]

Ibn Abi Hatim is not the only one to report this. Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh said: Abd al-Rahim ibn Muhammad ibn Muslim narrated to us, Isma'il ibn Ahmad ibn Usayd narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn Ya'qub al-Jawzajani narrated to us in Makkah, Ubayd Allah [[In MS. D and R: "Abd Allah".]] al-Hanafi narrated to us, Zam'ah ibn Salih narrated to us, from Salamah ibn Wahram, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Some of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ were sitting, waiting for him. He came out until he drew near them and heard them discussing. He heard their conversation, and some of them were saying: "How strange! If Allah has taken a khalil (intimate friend) from among His creation, then Ibrahim is His khalil!" Another said: "What is so remarkable about Allah speaking to Musa directly!" Another said: "Isa is the Spirit of Allah and His Word!" Another said: "Adam, whom Allah chose!" So he came out to them, greeted them, and said: "I have heard your talk and your amazement, that Ibrahim is the khalil of Allah, and so he is. Musa is His interlocutor (kalim), Isa is His Spirit and His Word, and Adam is one whom Allah chose, and so he is. Indeed, I am the beloved (habib) of Allah, and I say this without pride. I will bear the banner of praise on the Day of Resurrection, and I say this without pride. I will be the first intercessor and the first whose intercession is accepted, and I say this without pride. I will be the first to move the rings of Paradise, and Allah will open it for me and admit me into it, and with me will be the poor among the believers, and I say this without pride. I will be the most honoured of the first and the last on the Day of Resurrection, and I say this without pride."

This hadith is gharib (strange, with a weak or single chain) from this route, but parts of it have supporting narrations in the Sahih collections and elsewhere. [[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in his Sunan, no. 3616, and he said: "This is a gharib hadith."]]

Qatadah narrated from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, that he said: "Are you amazed that khullah (intimate friendship) was given to Ibrahim, speech to Musa, and vision to Muhammad? May the blessings and peace of Allah be upon them all."

Al-Hakim narrated it in his Mustadrak and said: "It is sahih (sound) according to the conditions of al-Bukhari, though they (al-Bukhari and Muslim) did not include it." It is also narrated similarly from Anas ibn Malik and from many Companions and Successors, and from the leading scholars of the earlier and later generations.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Yahya ibn Abdak al-Qazwini narrated to us, Muhammad, meaning Ibn Sa'id ibn Sabiq, narrated to us, Amr, meaning Ibn Abi Qays, narrated to us, from Asim, from Abu Rashid, from Ubayd ibn Umayr, who said: Ibrahim, peace be upon him, used to host people. One day he went out seeking someone to host, but he found no one to host, so he returned to his house and found a man standing in it. He said: "O servant of Allah, what brought you into my house without my permission?" He replied: "I entered it with the permission of its Lord." He said: "And who are you?" He replied: "I am the Angel of Death. My Lord sent me to one of His servants to give him the good news that Allah has taken him as a khalil." He said: "Who is he? By Allah, if you tell me about him, and he is in the farthest of lands, I will go to him, and I will not leave him as a neighbour until death separates us." He said: "That servant is you." He said: "Me?" He said: "Yes." He said: "For what reason has Allah taken me as a khalil?" He said: "Because you give to people and do not ask them." [[Its chain is mursal (broken).]]

And Mahmud ibn Khalid al-Sulami narrated to us, al-Walid narrated to us, from Ishaq ibn Yasar, who said: When Allah took Ibrahim as a khalil, He placed trembling (wajal) in his heart, to the extent that the pounding of his heart could be heard from a distance, like the fluttering of birds in the air. Likewise it has been described of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that the sound of weeping in his chest was heard like the boiling of a cauldron.

* *

His saying: ﴿And to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾ means: all of it is His possession, His servants and His creation, and He is the one who disposes of all of that. None can reject what He has decreed, none can overturn what He has judged, and He is not questioned about what He does, because of His greatness, His power, His justice, His wisdom, His kindness and His mercy.

* *

His saying: ﴿And Allah is ever, of all things, encompassing﴾ means: His knowledge pervades all of that. No secret of His servants is hidden from Him, and not even the weight of an atom in the heavens or on the earth escapes His knowledge, nor anything smaller than that or greater. No atom is hidden from Him, whether it is visible to observers or concealed.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 4, verses 123–126 (part 1 of 3):

Qatadah said: It was mentioned to us that the Muslims and the People of the Scripture boasted. The People of the Scripture said: "Our prophet came before your prophet, and our book came before your book, so we are closer to Allah than you are." The Muslims said: "We are closer to Allah than you are. Our prophet is the Seal of the Prophets, and our book overrides the books that came before it." So Allah revealed: ﴿It is not by your wishful thinking, nor by the wishful thinking of the People of the Scripture. Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it.﴾ And: ﴿And who is better in religion than one who submits himself to Allah while being a doer of good [and follows the religion of Abraham, inclining toward truth]﴾ [[Addition from manuscripts R and A.]] ﴿...﴾ the verse. Thus Allah established the proof of the Muslims over those who opposed them among the people of the religions.

The same was narrated from al-Suddi, Masruq, al-Dahhak, Abu Salih and others. Al-Awfi also narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that he said regarding this verse: The people of the religions disputed. The People of the Torah said: "Our book is the best of books, and our prophet is the best of prophets." The People of the Gospel said the same. The People of Islam said: "There is no religion except Islam. Our book has abrogated every book, our prophet is the Seal of the Prophets, and you were commanded, and we were commanded, to believe in your book and act upon our book." So Allah judged between them, saying: ﴿It is not by your wishful thinking, nor by the wishful thinking of the People of the Scripture. Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it.﴾ And He gave them a choice between the religions, saying: ﴿And who is better in religion than one who submits himself to Allah while being a doer of good [and follows the religion of Abraham, inclining toward truth]﴾ [[Addition from manuscript R.]] ﴿...﴾ up to His saying: ﴿And Allah took Abraham as an intimate friend.﴾

Mujahid said: The Arabs said: "We will not be resurrected and we will not be punished." The Jews and Christians said: ﴿None will enter Paradise except those who are Jews or Christians﴾ [al-Baqarah: 111], and they said: ﴿The Fire will not touch us except for a few numbered days﴾ [al-Baqarah: 80].

The meaning of this verse is that religion is not by adornment nor by wishful thinking. Not everyone who claims something obtains it merely by his claim, and not everyone who says, "I am the one who is right," is heeded merely for saying so, until he has a proof from Allah. For this reason, the Exalted said: ﴿It is not by your wishful thinking, nor by the wishful thinking of the People of the Scripture.﴾ That is: salvation is not for you, nor for them, by mere wishing. Rather, what counts is obedience to Allah and following what He has legislated through the lips of His noble messengers. For this reason He said after it: ﴿Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it,﴾ like His saying: ﴿So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it﴾ [al-Zalzalah: 7–8].

It has been narrated that when this verse was revealed it was difficult for many of the Companions. Imam Ahmad said: 'Abd Allah ibn Numayr narrated to us, Isma'il narrated to us, from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Zuhayr, who said: I was informed that Abu Bakr said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is the good state after this verse: ﴿It is not by your wishful thinking, nor by the wishful thinking of the People of the Scripture. Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it﴾? Every evil we do, we will be recompensed for it?" The Prophet ﷺ said: "May Allah forgive you, O Abu Bakr. Do you not fall ill? Do you not become weary? Do you not grieve? Does not hardship (al-la'waa') befall you?" [[In manuscript A: "Does not harm befall you?"]] He said: "Yes." He said: "That is what you are recompensed with."

Sa'id ibn Mansur narrated it from Khalaf ibn Khalifah, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, with the same. Ibn Hibban narrated it in his Sahih from Abu Ya'la, from Abu Khaythamah, from Yahya ibn Sa'id, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, with the same. Al-Hakim narrated it through the route of Sufyan al-Thawri, from Isma'il, with the same. [[The Musnad (1/11), Sunan Sa'id ibn Mansur no. (696), Sahih Ibn Hibban no. (1734) "Mawarid," and al-Mustadrak (3/74).]]

Imam Ahmad also said: 'Abd al-Wahhab ibn 'Ata' narrated to us, from Ziyad al-Jassas, from 'Ali ibn Zayd, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Umar, who said: I heard Abu Bakr say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it in this world." [[Musnad (1/6).]]

Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh said: Ahmad ibn Hushaym ibn Juhaymah narrated to us, Yahya ibn Abi Talib narrated to us, 'Abd al-Wahhab ibn 'Ata' narrated to us, Ziyad al-Jassas narrated to us, from 'Ali ibn Zayd, from Mujahid, who said: 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar said: "Look at the place where 'Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr is crucified, and do not pass by it." He said: The boy forgot, and then Ibn 'Umar was looking at Ibn al-Zubayr. He said: "May Allah forgive you three times. By Allah, I did not know you except as one who fasted much, prayed much at night, and was much in maintaining the ties of kinship. By Allah, I truly hope that, with what you have suffered, Allah will not punish you after it." He said: Then he turned to me and said: I heard Abu Bakr al-Siddiq say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever does evil in this world will be recompensed for it."

Abu Bakr al-Bazzar narrated it in his Musnad, from al-Fadl ibn Sahl, from 'Abd al-Wahhab ibn 'Ata', with the same, abridged. [[Musnad al-Bazzar no. (21). Al-Daraqutni said in al-'Ilal (4/223): "Ziyad al-Jassas narrated it, and there was disagreement regarding him. 'Abd al-Wahhab ibn 'Ata' narrated it from Ziyad, from 'Ali ibn Zayd, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Umar, from Abu Bakr. But Abu 'Asim al-'Abbadani contradicted him, narrating it from Ziyad al-Jassas, from Salim, from Ibn 'Umar, from 'Umar. There is nothing in it that is established."]] And it is mentioned in the Musnad of Ibn al-Zubayr: Ibrahim ibn al-Mustamirr al-'Aufi narrated to us [[In manuscripts R and A: "al-'Awfi."]], 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Sulaym ibn Hayyan narrated to us, my father narrated to me, from my grandfather Hayyan ibn Bistam, who said: I was with Ibn 'Umar, and he passed by 'Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr while he was crucified. He said: "May Allah have mercy on you, Abu Khubayb. I heard your father—meaning al-Zubayr—say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it in this world and the Hereafter.'" Then he said: "We do not know it being narrated from al-Zubayr except through this route." [[Musnad al-Bazzar no. (962). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (7/12): "It contains 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Sulaym ibn Hayyan, whom I do not know, and the rest of its narrators are trustworthy." The apparent name is 'Abd al-Rahim, as in al-Daraqutni's al-'Ilal (4/223), when he was asked about the route of Sulaym ibn Hayyan from his father from Ibn 'Umar, and he said: "'Abd al-Rahman ibn Sulaym ibn Hayyan narrates it from his father from Ibn 'Umar," and at another time he said: "From his father from Nafi' from Ibn 'Umar." 'Abd al-Rahim is weak, and Ziyad is weak.]]

Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh said: Ahmad ibn Kamil narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Sa'd al-'Awfi narrated to us, Rawh ibn 'Ubadah narrated to us, Musa ibn 'Ubaydah narrated to us, a client of Ibn Sibaa' narrated to me, who said: I heard Ibn 'Umar narrate from Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, who said: I was with the Prophet ﷺ when this verse was revealed: ﴿Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it, and will not find for himself besides Allah any protector or helper.﴾ The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "O Abu Bakr, shall I recite to you a verse that was revealed to me?" I said: "Yes, O Messenger of Allah." So he recited it to me. I did not know except that I felt a breaking in my back until I stretched out. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "What is the matter with you, O Abu Bakr?" I said: "My father and mother be sacrificed for you, O Messenger of Allah! Which of us has not done evil? Will we really be recompensed for every evil we have done?!" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "As for you, O Abu Bakr, and your companions who are believers, you will be recompensed for it in this world until you meet Allah, and you will have no sins. As for the others, it will be gathered for them until they are recompensed for it on the Day of Resurrection."

Likewise al-Tirmidhi narrated it from Yahya ibn Musa, and 'Abd ibn Humayd, from Rawh ibn 'Ubadah, with the same. Then he said: Musa ibn 'Ubaydah is weak, and the client of Ibn Sibaa' is unknown. [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3039).]]

[Ibn Jarir said: al-Ghulam narrated to us, al-Husayn narrated to us, al-Hajjaj narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah informed me, who said: When it was revealed, Abu Bakr said: "O Messenger of Allah, the back-breaking verse has come!" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "It refers only to the calamities of this world."] [[Addition from manuscript A.]]

Another route from al-Siddiq: Ibn Mardawayh said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ishaq al-'Askari narrated to us, Muhammad ibn 'Amir al-Sa'di narrated to us, Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us, Fudayl ibn 'Iyad narrated to us, from Sulayman ibn Mihran, from Muslim ibn Subayh, from Masruq, who said: Abu Bakr [al-Siddiq] [[Addition from manuscript A.]] said: "O Messenger of Allah, how severe is this verse: ﴿Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it﴾!" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Calamities, illnesses and griefs in this world are a recompense." [[Abu Nu'aym narrated it in al-Hilyah (8/119) through this route, with the same, and in it is Muhammad al-Sa'di, who used to lie and fabricate.]]

Another route: Ibn Jarir said: 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Ziyad and Ahmad ibn Mansur narrated to me, both saying: Zayd ibn al-Hubab narrated to us, 'Abd al-Malik ibn al-Hasan al-Harithi narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Zayd ibn Qunfudh narrated to us, from 'A'ishah, from Abu Bakr, who said: When it was revealed: ﴿Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it,﴾ Abu Bakr said: "O Messenger of Allah, will we be held accountable for everything we do?" He said: "O Abu Bakr, does not what befalls you such-and-such? That is an expiation." [[Tafsir al-Tabari (9/240).]]

Another hadith: Sa'id ibn Mansur said: 'Abd Allah ibn Wahb informed us, 'Amr ibn al-Harith informed me, that Bakr ibn Sawadah narrated to him, that Yazid ibn Abi Yazid narrated to him, from 'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr, from 'A'ishah, that a man recited this verse: ﴿Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it,﴾ and said: "Are we really recompensed for every deed? Then we are ruined!" This reached the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said: "Yes. The believer is recompensed in this world, in his self, in his body, in what harms him." [[Sunan Sa'id ibn Mansur no. (699), and Ahmad in al-Musnad (6/65) through the route of 'Abd Allah ibn Wahb with the same.]]

Another route: Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Salamah ibn Bashir narrated to us, Hushaym narrated to us, from Abu 'Amir, from Ibn Abi Mulaykah, from 'A'ishah, who said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, I know the most severe verse in the Quran." He said: "What is it, O 'A'ishah?" I said: ﴿Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it.﴾ He said: "It is what befalls the believing servant, even the prick he is pricked with."

Ibn Jarir narrated it through the narration of Hushaym, with the same. Abu Dawud narrated it through the narration of Abu 'Amir Salih ibn Rustum al-Khazzaz, with the same. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (9/246) and Sunan Abi Dawud no. (3093).]]

Another route: Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said: Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from 'Ali ibn Zayd, from Umayyah, that she asked 'A'ishah about this verse: ﴿Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it.﴾ She said: "No one has asked me about this verse since I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about it. I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said: 'O 'A'ishah, this is Allah's transaction with the servant, for what befalls him of fever, prick, and thorn, even the merchandise a man places in his sleeve, then he searches for it and finds it in his pocket. Indeed, the believer comes out of his sins just as red gold comes out of the furnace.'" [[Musnad al-Tayalisi no. (1584), and Ahmad in al-Musnad (6/218) through the route of Hammad ibn Salamah with the same. Note: In al-Tayalisi it reads "mu'atabah" instead of "mubaya'ah," and in Ahmad it reads "mutabi'ah."]]

Another route: Ibn Mardawayh said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Abu al-Qasim narrated to us, Surayj [[In manuscripts R and A: "Shurayh."]] ibn Yunus narrated to us, Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Muhammad ibn Zayd ibn al-Muhajir, from 'A'ishah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asked about this verse: ﴿Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it.﴾ He said: "Indeed the believer is rewarded in everything, even in the al-faydh [[In manuscript R: "al-ghayd"; in manuscript A: "al-ghayt." Al-faydh means the departure of the soul.]] at the time of death."

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 4, verses 123–126 (part 2 of 3):

Imam Ahmad said: Husayn narrated to us, from Za'idah, from Layth, from Mujahid, from 'Aishah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When the sins of a servant become many, and he has nothing that expiates them, Allah tests him with grief so that He may expiate them for him." [[Al-Musnad (6/157).]]

Another hadith: Sa'id ibn Mansur said, from Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah, from 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhaysin, who heard Muhammad ibn Qays ibn Makhramah report that Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, said: When the verse ﴿Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it﴾ was revealed, it weighed heavily upon the Muslims. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to them: "Be steadfast, and draw near (to what is right), for in everything that afflicts a Muslim there is an expiation, even the thorn that pricks him and the stumble he suffers." [[Sunan Sa'id ibn Mansur (no. 694), al-Musnad (2/248), Sahih Muslim (no. 2574), Sunan al-Tirmidhi (no. 5029), and Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra (no. 11122).]]

Ahmad narrated it in the same way from Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah, and Muslim, al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i (narrated it) from the hadith of Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah, with the same chain. Ibn Mardawayh narrated it through Rawh and Mu'tamir, both from Ibrahim ibn Yazid [in A: "Zayd"], from 'Abd Allah ibn Ibrahim, who said: I heard Abu Hurayrah say: When this verse was revealed, ﴿It is not by your wishful thinking, nor by the wishful thinking of the People of the Book: whoever does evil will be recompensed for it﴾, we wept and grieved, and we said: "O Messenger of Allah, this verse has left nothing (for us)." He said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, it is indeed as it was revealed. But rejoice and draw near (to what is right) and be steadfast, for no one among you is afflicted in this world but that Allah expiates his sin by it, even the thorn that one of you pricks in his foot." [[In its chain is Ibrahim ibn Yazid al-Khawzami, who is weak.]]

'Ata' ibn Yasar said, from Abu Sa'id and Abu Hurayrah, that they both heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "No fatigue, nor illness, nor sickness, nor grief afflicts the believer, not even the worry that troubles him, but that some of his evil deeds are expiated by it." It was recorded by al-Bukhari and Muslim. [[Sahih al-Bukhari (nos. 5641, 5642) and Sahih Muslim (no. 2573).]]

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Yahya narrated to us, from Sa'd ibn Ishaq, who said: Zaynab bint Ka'b ibn 'Ujrah narrated to me, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: A man said to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "Do you see these illnesses that afflict us? What is their benefit for us?" He said: "They are expiations." Ubayy said: "Even if they are few?" He said: "Even if it is a thorn or something more than that." (The narrator) said: So Ubayy invoked (a curse) upon himself, that the fever would not leave him until he died, so that it would not distract him from Hajj, 'Umrah, jihad in the way of Allah, or the obligatory prayer in congregation. No one touched him but he felt its heat, until he died, may Allah be pleased with him. Ahmad alone narrated it. [[Al-Musnad (3/23). Abu Ya'la also narrated it in his Musnad (2/281), and al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (2/301): "Its narrators are trustworthy."]]

Another hadith: Ibn Mardawayh narrated through the route of Husayn ibn Waqid, from al-Kalbi, from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, (what about) ﴿whoever does evil will be recompensed for it﴾?" He said: "Yes. And whoever does a good deed will be rewarded for it tenfold. So he who is overcome by his single (bad deed) will be destroyed, (despite) his ten (good deeds)." [[Its chain is very weak, as was mentioned in the introduction.]]

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Humayd, from al-Hasan, regarding ﴿whoever does evil will be recompensed for it﴾, that he said: "(It refers to) the disbeliever," and then he recited: ﴿And do We recompense any but the ungrateful?﴾ [Saba': 17].

Similarly, it is reported from Ibn 'Abbas and Sa'id ibn Jubayr that they both interpreted "evil" here as "shirk" (associating partners with Allah).

* *

As for His saying: ﴿and he will not find for himself, besides Allah, any protector or any helper﴾: 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: "Except that he repents, and then Allah accepts his repentance." Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it.

The sound view is that this applies generally to all deeds, based on the hadiths that have preceded, and this is the view preferred by Ibn Jarir. And Allah knows best.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And whoever does righteous deeds, whether male or female, while being a believer [then those will enter Paradise and will not be wronged, even by the size of a naqir]﴾ [[Addition from the manuscripts Waw and A; in H it is written "the verse."]]: when He mentioned the recompense for evil deeds, and that it must take its due from the servant, either in this world (which is better for him) or in the Hereafter (and we seek refuge in Allah from that, and ask Him for well-being in this world and the Hereafter, and for pardon, forgiveness and forbearance), He began to explain His goodness, generosity and mercy in accepting the righteous deeds of His servants, both male and female, on condition of faith, and that He will admit them into Paradise and will not wrong them of their good deeds even by the size of the naqir. The naqir is the small hollow on the back of a date stone. The fatil (the thread in the split of a date stone) has already been discussed, and this naqir and the fatil are both in the date stone, and likewise the qitmir, which is the thin membrane over the date stone. These three are mentioned in the Qur'an.

Then He said, may He be exalted: ﴿And who is better in religion than one who submits his face to Allah﴾, sincerely dedicating his deed to his Lord, may He be mighty and majestic, acting in faith and seeking reward, ﴿while he is a doer of good﴾, meaning, following in his deed what Allah has prescribed for him and what He sent His Messenger with, of guidance and the religion of truth. These two conditions are such that no worker's deed is valid without them: it must be sincere (for Allah alone) and correct (in conformity with the Law). Sincerity means it is for Allah, and correctness means it follows the Shari'ah. Its outward aspect is valid through following (the Prophet), and its inward aspect through sincerity. Whoever lacks either of these two conditions, his deed is corrupt. Whoever lacks sincerity is a hypocrite, who show off to people. Whoever lacks following (the Prophet) is astray and ignorant. When both are combined, it is the deed of the believers: ﴿those from whom We accept the best of what they have done and overlook their evil deeds, among the companions of Paradise, a true promise which they had been promised﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 16]. For this reason He said: ﴿and follows the religion of Abraham, a hanif﴾. They are Muhammad and his followers until the Day of Resurrection, as He said: ﴿Indeed, the closest of people to Abraham are those who followed him, and this Prophet, and those who believe; and Allah is the ally of the believers﴾ [Al 'Imran: 68]. And He said: ﴿Say: Indeed, my Lord has guided me to a straight path, a correct religion, the religion of Abraham, a hanif, and he was not of those who associate partners with Allah﴾ [[Addition from A.]] [al-An'am: 161]. And: ﴿Then We revealed to you: Follow the religion of Abraham, a hanif, and he was not of those who associate partners with Allah﴾ [al-Nahl: 123]. The hanif is one who turns away from shirk with intent, that is, one who abandons it with insight, and turns entirely toward the truth, with nothing diverting him from it and no one turning him back from it.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And Allah took Abraham as an intimate friend (khalil)﴾: this is in the context of encouraging following him, because he is an imam to be emulated, for he reached the furthest point to which servants can draw near to Allah. He attained the rank of khullah (intimate friendship), which is the highest station of love, and this was only because of the abundance of his obedience to his Lord, as He described him in His saying: ﴿and Abraham who fulfilled (his commitments)﴾ [al-Najm: 37]. Many of the early scholars said: That is, he carried out all that he was commanded, and fulfilled every station of worship, so that no great matter distracted him from a small one, nor a big matter from a little one. And He said: ﴿And when Abraham was tested by his Lord with certain words, and he fulfilled them, (Allah) said: Indeed, I will make you an imam for the people﴾ [[Addition from R and A.]] [al-Baqarah: 124], to the end of the verse. And He said: ﴿Indeed, Abraham was a community, devoutly obedient to Allah, a hanif, and he was not of those who associate partners with Allah, grateful for His favors. He chose him and guided him to a straight path. And We gave him good in this world, and indeed, in the Hereafter he is among the righteous﴾ [[Addition from R.]] [al-Nahl: 120–122].

Al-Bukhari said: Sulayman ibn Harb narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Habib ibn Abi Thabit, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from 'Amr ibn Maymun, who said: When Mu'adh came to Yemen, he led them in the dawn prayer, and he recited: ﴿And Allah took Abraham as an intimate friend﴾. A man from the people said: "The eye of Abraham's mother has indeed been comforted."

Ibn Jarir mentioned in his tafsir, from some of them, that Allah named him khalil only because the people of his region suffered a drought, so he travelled to a khalil (friend) of his from the people of Mosul (and some of them said: from the people of Egypt) to obtain food for his family from him. But he did not find what he needed with him. When he drew near to his family, he passed through a sandy desert, and he said: "If only I could fill my sacks with this sand, so that I do not sadden my family by returning to them without provisions, and so that they may think that I have brought them what they love." So he did that, and the sand in his sacks turned into flour. When he reached his home, he slept, and his family rose and opened the sacks, and they found flour. They kneaded it and baked bread from it. He awoke and asked them about the flour from which they had baked, and they said: "From the flour you brought from your khalil." He said: "Yes, it is from my khalil, Allah." So Allah named him khalil because of this.

The authenticity and occurrence of this report are open to question. At best it is an Isra'iliyyat report, which is neither confirmed nor denied. Rather, he was named "Khalil of Allah" because of the intense love of his Lord, may He be mighty and majestic, for him, on account of the obedience he rendered, which Allah loves and is pleased with. For this reason it is established in the two Sahihs, from the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, that when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) addressed them in the last sermon he gave, he said: "To proceed: O people, if I were to take any of the people of the earth as a khalil, I would have taken Abu Bakr ibn Abi Quhafah as a khalil. But your companion is the khalil of Allah." [[Sahih al-Bukhari (no. 3654) and Sahih Muslim (no. 2382). The wording "your companion is the khalil of Allah" is from the hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, narrated by Muslim (no. 2383).]]

And it has come through the routes of Jundub ibn 'Abd Allah al-Bajali, 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As and 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, from the Prophet (ﷺ): "Indeed Allah has taken me as a khalil just as He took Abraham as a khalil." [[The hadith of Jundub ibn 'Abd Allah is narrated by Muslim in his Sahih (no. 532). The hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr is narrated by al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman (no. 9616). The hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud is narrated by Muslim in his Sahih (no. 2383).]]

Ibn Abi Hatim is not the only one to report this. Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh said: Abd al-Rahim ibn Muhammad ibn Muslim narrated to us, Isma'il ibn Ahmad ibn Usayd narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn Ya'qub al-Jawzajani narrated to us in Makkah, Ubayd Allah [[In MS. D and R: "Abd Allah".]] al-Hanafi narrated to us, Zam'ah ibn Salih narrated to us, from Salamah ibn Wahram, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Some of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ were sitting, waiting for him. He came out until he drew near them and heard them discussing. He heard their conversation, and some of them were saying: "How strange! If Allah has taken a khalil (intimate friend) from among His creation, then Ibrahim is His khalil!" Another said: "What is so remarkable about Allah speaking to Musa directly!" Another said: "Isa is the Spirit of Allah and His Word!" Another said: "Adam, whom Allah chose!" So he came out to them, greeted them, and said: "I have heard your talk and your amazement, that Ibrahim is the khalil of Allah, and so he is. Musa is His interlocutor (kalim), Isa is His Spirit and His Word, and Adam is one whom Allah chose, and so he is. Indeed, I am the beloved (habib) of Allah, and I say this without pride. I will bear the banner of praise on the Day of Resurrection, and I say this without pride. I will be the first intercessor and the first whose intercession is accepted, and I say this without pride. I will be the first to move the rings of Paradise, and Allah will open it for me and admit me into it, and with me will be the poor among the believers, and I say this without pride. I will be the most honoured of the first and the last on the Day of Resurrection, and I say this without pride."

This hadith is gharib (strange, with a weak or single chain) from this route, but parts of it have supporting narrations in the Sahih collections and elsewhere. [[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in his Sunan, no. 3616, and he said: "This is a gharib hadith."]]

Qatadah narrated from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, that he said: "Are you amazed that khullah (intimate friendship) was given to Ibrahim, speech to Musa, and vision to Muhammad? May the blessings and peace of Allah be upon them all."

Al-Hakim narrated it in his Mustadrak and said: "It is sahih (sound) according to the conditions of al-Bukhari, though they (al-Bukhari and Muslim) did not include it." It is also narrated similarly from Anas ibn Malik and from many Companions and Successors, and from the leading scholars of the earlier and later generations.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Yahya ibn Abdak al-Qazwini narrated to us, Muhammad, meaning Ibn Sa'id ibn Sabiq, narrated to us, Amr, meaning Ibn Abi Qays, narrated to us, from Asim, from Abu Rashid, from Ubayd ibn Umayr, who said: Ibrahim, peace be upon him, used to host people. One day he went out seeking someone to host, but he found no one to host, so he returned to his house and found a man standing in it. He said: "O servant of Allah, what brought you into my house without my permission?" He replied: "I entered it with the permission of its Lord." He said: "And who are you?" He replied: "I am the Angel of Death. My Lord sent me to one of His servants to give him the good news that Allah has taken him as a khalil." He said: "Who is he? By Allah, if you tell me about him, and he is in the farthest of lands, I will go to him, and I will not leave him as a neighbour until death separates us." He said: "That servant is you." He said: "Me?" He said: "Yes." He said: "For what reason has Allah taken me as a khalil?" He said: "Because you give to people and do not ask them." [[Its chain is mursal (broken).]]

And Mahmud ibn Khalid al-Sulami narrated to us, al-Walid narrated to us, from Ishaq ibn Yasar, who said: When Allah took Ibrahim as a khalil, He placed trembling (wajal) in his heart, to the extent that the pounding of his heart could be heard from a distance, like the fluttering of birds in the air. Likewise it has been described of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that the sound of weeping in his chest was heard like the boiling of a cauldron.

* *

His saying: ﴿And to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾ means: all of it is His possession, His servants and His creation, and He is the one who disposes of all of that. None can reject what He has decreed, none can overturn what He has judged, and He is not questioned about what He does, because of His greatness, His power, His justice, His wisdom, His kindness and His mercy.

* *

His saying: ﴿And Allah is ever, of all things, encompassing﴾ means: His knowledge pervades all of that. No secret of His servants is hidden from Him, and not even the weight of an atom in the heavens or on the earth escapes His knowledge, nor anything smaller than that or greater. No atom is hidden from Him, whether it is visible to observers or concealed.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 4, verses 123–126 (part 1 of 3):

Qatadah said: It was mentioned to us that the Muslims and the People of the Scripture boasted. The People of the Scripture said: "Our prophet came before your prophet, and our book came before your book, so we are closer to Allah than you are." The Muslims said: "We are closer to Allah than you are. Our prophet is the Seal of the Prophets, and our book overrides the books that came before it." So Allah revealed: ﴿It is not by your wishful thinking, nor by the wishful thinking of the People of the Scripture. Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it.﴾ And: ﴿And who is better in religion than one who submits himself to Allah while being a doer of good [and follows the religion of Abraham, inclining toward truth]﴾ [[Addition from manuscripts R and A.]] ﴿...﴾ the verse. Thus Allah established the proof of the Muslims over those who opposed them among the people of the religions.

The same was narrated from al-Suddi, Masruq, al-Dahhak, Abu Salih and others. Al-Awfi also narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that he said regarding this verse: The people of the religions disputed. The People of the Torah said: "Our book is the best of books, and our prophet is the best of prophets." The People of the Gospel said the same. The People of Islam said: "There is no religion except Islam. Our book has abrogated every book, our prophet is the Seal of the Prophets, and you were commanded, and we were commanded, to believe in your book and act upon our book." So Allah judged between them, saying: ﴿It is not by your wishful thinking, nor by the wishful thinking of the People of the Scripture. Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it.﴾ And He gave them a choice between the religions, saying: ﴿And who is better in religion than one who submits himself to Allah while being a doer of good [and follows the religion of Abraham, inclining toward truth]﴾ [[Addition from manuscript R.]] ﴿...﴾ up to His saying: ﴿And Allah took Abraham as an intimate friend.﴾

Mujahid said: The Arabs said: "We will not be resurrected and we will not be punished." The Jews and Christians said: ﴿None will enter Paradise except those who are Jews or Christians﴾ [al-Baqarah: 111], and they said: ﴿The Fire will not touch us except for a few numbered days﴾ [al-Baqarah: 80].

The meaning of this verse is that religion is not by adornment nor by wishful thinking. Not everyone who claims something obtains it merely by his claim, and not everyone who says, "I am the one who is right," is heeded merely for saying so, until he has a proof from Allah. For this reason, the Exalted said: ﴿It is not by your wishful thinking, nor by the wishful thinking of the People of the Scripture.﴾ That is: salvation is not for you, nor for them, by mere wishing. Rather, what counts is obedience to Allah and following what He has legislated through the lips of His noble messengers. For this reason He said after it: ﴿Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it,﴾ like His saying: ﴿So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it﴾ [al-Zalzalah: 7–8].

It has been narrated that when this verse was revealed it was difficult for many of the Companions. Imam Ahmad said: 'Abd Allah ibn Numayr narrated to us, Isma'il narrated to us, from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Zuhayr, who said: I was informed that Abu Bakr said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is the good state after this verse: ﴿It is not by your wishful thinking, nor by the wishful thinking of the People of the Scripture. Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it﴾? Every evil we do, we will be recompensed for it?" The Prophet ﷺ said: "May Allah forgive you, O Abu Bakr. Do you not fall ill? Do you not become weary? Do you not grieve? Does not hardship (al-la'waa') befall you?" [[In manuscript A: "Does not harm befall you?"]] He said: "Yes." He said: "That is what you are recompensed with."

Sa'id ibn Mansur narrated it from Khalaf ibn Khalifah, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, with the same.
