Ibn Hibban narrated it in his Sahih from Abu Ya'la, from Abu Khaythamah, from Yahya ibn Sa'id, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, with the same. Al-Hakim narrated it through the route of Sufyan al-Thawri, from Isma'il, with the same. [[The Musnad (1/11), Sunan Sa'id ibn Mansur no. (696), Sahih Ibn Hibban no. (1734) "Mawarid," and al-Mustadrak (3/74).]]

Imam Ahmad also said: 'Abd al-Wahhab ibn 'Ata' narrated to us, from Ziyad al-Jassas, from 'Ali ibn Zayd, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Umar, who said: I heard Abu Bakr say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it in this world." [[Musnad (1/6).]]

Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh said: Ahmad ibn Hushaym ibn Juhaymah narrated to us, Yahya ibn Abi Talib narrated to us, 'Abd al-Wahhab ibn 'Ata' narrated to us, Ziyad al-Jassas narrated to us, from 'Ali ibn Zayd, from Mujahid, who said: 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar said: "Look at the place where 'Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr is crucified, and do not pass by it." He said: The boy forgot, and then Ibn 'Umar was looking at Ibn al-Zubayr. He said: "May Allah forgive you three times. By Allah, I did not know you except as one who fasted much, prayed much at night, and was much in maintaining the ties of kinship. By Allah, I truly hope that, with what you have suffered, Allah will not punish you after it." He said: Then he turned to me and said: I heard Abu Bakr al-Siddiq say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever does evil in this world will be recompensed for it."

Abu Bakr al-Bazzar narrated it in his Musnad, from al-Fadl ibn Sahl, from 'Abd al-Wahhab ibn 'Ata', with the same, abridged. [[Musnad al-Bazzar no. (21). Al-Daraqutni said in al-'Ilal (4/223): "Ziyad al-Jassas narrated it, and there was disagreement regarding him. 'Abd al-Wahhab ibn 'Ata' narrated it from Ziyad, from 'Ali ibn Zayd, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Umar, from Abu Bakr. But Abu 'Asim al-'Abbadani contradicted him, narrating it from Ziyad al-Jassas, from Salim, from Ibn 'Umar, from 'Umar. There is nothing in it that is established."]] And it is mentioned in the Musnad of Ibn al-Zubayr: Ibrahim ibn al-Mustamirr al-'Aufi narrated to us [[In manuscripts R and A: "al-'Awfi."]], 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Sulaym ibn Hayyan narrated to us, my father narrated to me, from my grandfather Hayyan ibn Bistam, who said: I was with Ibn 'Umar, and he passed by 'Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr while he was crucified. He said: "May Allah have mercy on you, Abu Khubayb. I heard your father—meaning al-Zubayr—say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it in this world and the Hereafter.'" Then he said: "We do not know it being narrated from al-Zubayr except through this route." [[Musnad al-Bazzar no. (962). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (7/12): "It contains 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Sulaym ibn Hayyan, whom I do not know, and the rest of its narrators are trustworthy." The apparent name is 'Abd al-Rahim, as in al-Daraqutni's al-'Ilal (4/223), when he was asked about the route of Sulaym ibn Hayyan from his father from Ibn 'Umar, and he said: "'Abd al-Rahman ibn Sulaym ibn Hayyan narrates it from his father from Ibn 'Umar," and at another time he said: "From his father from Nafi' from Ibn 'Umar." 'Abd al-Rahim is weak, and Ziyad is weak.]]

Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh said: Ahmad ibn Kamil narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Sa'd al-'Awfi narrated to us, Rawh ibn 'Ubadah narrated to us, Musa ibn 'Ubaydah narrated to us, a client of Ibn Sibaa' narrated to me, who said: I heard Ibn 'Umar narrate from Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, who said: I was with the Prophet ﷺ when this verse was revealed: ﴿Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it, and will not find for himself besides Allah any protector or helper.﴾ The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "O Abu Bakr, shall I recite to you a verse that was revealed to me?" I said: "Yes, O Messenger of Allah." So he recited it to me. I did not know except that I felt a breaking in my back until I stretched out. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "What is the matter with you, O Abu Bakr?" I said: "My father and mother be sacrificed for you, O Messenger of Allah! Which of us has not done evil? Will we really be recompensed for every evil we have done?!" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "As for you, O Abu Bakr, and your companions who are believers, you will be recompensed for it in this world until you meet Allah, and you will have no sins. As for the others, it will be gathered for them until they are recompensed for it on the Day of Resurrection."

Likewise al-Tirmidhi narrated it from Yahya ibn Musa, and 'Abd ibn Humayd, from Rawh ibn 'Ubadah, with the same. Then he said: Musa ibn 'Ubaydah is weak, and the client of Ibn Sibaa' is unknown. [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3039).]]

[Ibn Jarir said: al-Ghulam narrated to us, al-Husayn narrated to us, al-Hajjaj narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah informed me, who said: When it was revealed, Abu Bakr said: "O Messenger of Allah, the back-breaking verse has come!" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "It refers only to the calamities of this world."] [[Addition from manuscript A.]]

Another route from al-Siddiq: Ibn Mardawayh said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ishaq al-'Askari narrated to us, Muhammad ibn 'Amir al-Sa'di narrated to us, Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us, Fudayl ibn 'Iyad narrated to us, from Sulayman ibn Mihran, from Muslim ibn Subayh, from Masruq, who said: Abu Bakr [al-Siddiq] [[Addition from manuscript A.]] said: "O Messenger of Allah, how severe is this verse: ﴿Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it﴾!" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Calamities, illnesses and griefs in this world are a recompense." [[Abu Nu'aym narrated it in al-Hilyah (8/119) through this route, with the same, and in it is Muhammad al-Sa'di, who used to lie and fabricate.]]

Another route: Ibn Jarir said: 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Ziyad and Ahmad ibn Mansur narrated to me, both saying: Zayd ibn al-Hubab narrated to us, 'Abd al-Malik ibn al-Hasan al-Harithi narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Zayd ibn Qunfudh narrated to us, from 'A'ishah, from Abu Bakr, who said: When it was revealed: ﴿Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it,﴾ Abu Bakr said: "O Messenger of Allah, will we be held accountable for everything we do?" He said: "O Abu Bakr, does not what befalls you such-and-such? That is an expiation." [[Tafsir al-Tabari (9/240).]]

Another hadith: Sa'id ibn Mansur said: 'Abd Allah ibn Wahb informed us, 'Amr ibn al-Harith informed me, that Bakr ibn Sawadah narrated to him, that Yazid ibn Abi Yazid narrated to him, from 'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr, from 'A'ishah, that a man recited this verse: ﴿Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it,﴾ and said: "Are we really recompensed for every deed? Then we are ruined!" This reached the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said: "Yes. The believer is recompensed in this world, in his self, in his body, in what harms him." [[Sunan Sa'id ibn Mansur no. (699), and Ahmad in al-Musnad (6/65) through the route of 'Abd Allah ibn Wahb with the same.]]

Another route: Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Salamah ibn Bashir narrated to us, Hushaym narrated to us, from Abu 'Amir, from Ibn Abi Mulaykah, from 'A'ishah, who said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, I know the most severe verse in the Quran." He said: "What is it, O 'A'ishah?" I said: ﴿Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it.﴾ He said: "It is what befalls the believing servant, even the prick he is pricked with."

Ibn Jarir narrated it through the narration of Hushaym, with the same. Abu Dawud narrated it through the narration of Abu 'Amir Salih ibn Rustum al-Khazzaz, with the same. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (9/246) and Sunan Abi Dawud no. (3093).]]

Another route: Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said: Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from 'Ali ibn Zayd, from Umayyah, that she asked 'A'ishah about this verse: ﴿Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it.﴾ She said: "No one has asked me about this verse since I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about it. I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said: 'O 'A'ishah, this is Allah's transaction with the servant, for what befalls him of fever, prick, and thorn, even the merchandise a man places in his sleeve, then he searches for it and finds it in his pocket. Indeed, the believer comes out of his sins just as red gold comes out of the furnace.'" [[Musnad al-Tayalisi no. (1584), and Ahmad in al-Musnad (6/218) through the route of Hammad ibn Salamah with the same. Note: In al-Tayalisi it reads "mu'atabah" instead of "mubaya'ah," and in Ahmad it reads "mutabi'ah."]]

Another route: Ibn Mardawayh said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Abu al-Qasim narrated to us, Surayj [[In manuscripts R and A: "Shurayh."]] ibn Yunus narrated to us, Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Muhammad ibn Zayd ibn al-Muhajir, from 'A'ishah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asked about this verse: ﴿Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it.﴾ He said: "Indeed the believer is rewarded in everything, even in the al-faydh [[In manuscript R: "al-ghayd"; in manuscript A: "al-ghayt." Al-faydh means the departure of the soul.]] at the time of death."

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 4, verses 123–126 (part 2 of 3):

Imam Ahmad said: Husayn narrated to us, from Za'idah, from Layth, from Mujahid, from 'Aishah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When the sins of a servant become many, and he has nothing that expiates them, Allah tests him with grief so that He may expiate them for him." [[Al-Musnad (6/157).]]

Another hadith: Sa'id ibn Mansur said, from Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah, from 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhaysin, who heard Muhammad ibn Qays ibn Makhramah report that Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, said: When the verse ﴿Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it﴾ was revealed, it weighed heavily upon the Muslims. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to them: "Be steadfast, and draw near (to what is right), for in everything that afflicts a Muslim there is an expiation, even the thorn that pricks him and the stumble he suffers." [[Sunan Sa'id ibn Mansur (no. 694), al-Musnad (2/248), Sahih Muslim (no. 2574), Sunan al-Tirmidhi (no. 5029), and Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra (no. 11122).]]

Ahmad narrated it in the same way from Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah, and Muslim, al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i (narrated it) from the hadith of Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah, with the same chain. Ibn Mardawayh narrated it through Rawh and Mu'tamir, both from Ibrahim ibn Yazid [in A: "Zayd"], from 'Abd Allah ibn Ibrahim, who said: I heard Abu Hurayrah say: When this verse was revealed, ﴿It is not by your wishful thinking, nor by the wishful thinking of the People of the Book: whoever does evil will be recompensed for it﴾, we wept and grieved, and we said: "O Messenger of Allah, this verse has left nothing (for us)." He said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, it is indeed as it was revealed. But rejoice and draw near (to what is right) and be steadfast, for no one among you is afflicted in this world but that Allah expiates his sin by it, even the thorn that one of you pricks in his foot." [[In its chain is Ibrahim ibn Yazid al-Khawzami, who is weak.]]

'Ata' ibn Yasar said, from Abu Sa'id and Abu Hurayrah, that they both heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "No fatigue, nor illness, nor sickness, nor grief afflicts the believer, not even the worry that troubles him, but that some of his evil deeds are expiated by it." It was recorded by al-Bukhari and Muslim. [[Sahih al-Bukhari (nos. 5641, 5642) and Sahih Muslim (no. 2573).]]

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Yahya narrated to us, from Sa'd ibn Ishaq, who said: Zaynab bint Ka'b ibn 'Ujrah narrated to me, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: A man said to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "Do you see these illnesses that afflict us? What is their benefit for us?" He said: "They are expiations." Ubayy said: "Even if they are few?" He said: "Even if it is a thorn or something more than that." (The narrator) said: So Ubayy invoked (a curse) upon himself, that the fever would not leave him until he died, so that it would not distract him from Hajj, 'Umrah, jihad in the way of Allah, or the obligatory prayer in congregation. No one touched him but he felt its heat, until he died, may Allah be pleased with him. Ahmad alone narrated it. [[Al-Musnad (3/23). Abu Ya'la also narrated it in his Musnad (2/281), and al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (2/301): "Its narrators are trustworthy."]]

Another hadith: Ibn Mardawayh narrated through the route of Husayn ibn Waqid, from al-Kalbi, from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, (what about) ﴿whoever does evil will be recompensed for it﴾?" He said: "Yes. And whoever does a good deed will be rewarded for it tenfold. So he who is overcome by his single (bad deed) will be destroyed, (despite) his ten (good deeds)." [[Its chain is very weak, as was mentioned in the introduction.]]

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Humayd, from al-Hasan, regarding ﴿whoever does evil will be recompensed for it﴾, that he said: "(It refers to) the disbeliever," and then he recited: ﴿And do We recompense any but the ungrateful?﴾ [Saba': 17].

Similarly, it is reported from Ibn 'Abbas and Sa'id ibn Jubayr that they both interpreted "evil" here as "shirk" (associating partners with Allah).

* *

As for His saying: ﴿and he will not find for himself, besides Allah, any protector or any helper﴾: 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: "Except that he repents, and then Allah accepts his repentance." Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it.

The sound view is that this applies generally to all deeds, based on the hadiths that have preceded, and this is the view preferred by Ibn Jarir. And Allah knows best.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And whoever does righteous deeds, whether male or female, while being a believer [then those will enter Paradise and will not be wronged, even by the size of a naqir]﴾ [[Addition from the manuscripts Waw and A; in H it is written "the verse."]]: when He mentioned the recompense for evil deeds, and that it must take its due from the servant, either in this world (which is better for him) or in the Hereafter (and we seek refuge in Allah from that, and ask Him for well-being in this world and the Hereafter, and for pardon, forgiveness and forbearance), He began to explain His goodness, generosity and mercy in accepting the righteous deeds of His servants, both male and female, on condition of faith, and that He will admit them into Paradise and will not wrong them of their good deeds even by the size of the naqir. The naqir is the small hollow on the back of a date stone. The fatil (the thread in the split of a date stone) has already been discussed, and this naqir and the fatil are both in the date stone, and likewise the qitmir, which is the thin membrane over the date stone. These three are mentioned in the Qur'an.

Then He said, may He be exalted: ﴿And who is better in religion than one who submits his face to Allah﴾, sincerely dedicating his deed to his Lord, may He be mighty and majestic, acting in faith and seeking reward, ﴿while he is a doer of good﴾, meaning, following in his deed what Allah has prescribed for him and what He sent His Messenger with, of guidance and the religion of truth. These two conditions are such that no worker's deed is valid without them: it must be sincere (for Allah alone) and correct (in conformity with the Law). Sincerity means it is for Allah, and correctness means it follows the Shari'ah. Its outward aspect is valid through following (the Prophet), and its inward aspect through sincerity. Whoever lacks either of these two conditions, his deed is corrupt. Whoever lacks sincerity is a hypocrite, who show off to people. Whoever lacks following (the Prophet) is astray and ignorant. When both are combined, it is the deed of the believers: ﴿those from whom We accept the best of what they have done and overlook their evil deeds, among the companions of Paradise, a true promise which they had been promised﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 16]. For this reason He said: ﴿and follows the religion of Abraham, a hanif﴾. They are Muhammad and his followers until the Day of Resurrection, as He said: ﴿Indeed, the closest of people to Abraham are those who followed him, and this Prophet, and those who believe; and Allah is the ally of the believers﴾ [Al 'Imran: 68]. And He said: ﴿Say: Indeed, my Lord has guided me to a straight path, a correct religion, the religion of Abraham, a hanif, and he was not of those who associate partners with Allah﴾ [[Addition from A.]] [al-An'am: 161]. And: ﴿Then We revealed to you: Follow the religion of Abraham, a hanif, and he was not of those who associate partners with Allah﴾ [al-Nahl: 123]. The hanif is one who turns away from shirk with intent, that is, one who abandons it with insight, and turns entirely toward the truth, with nothing diverting him from it and no one turning him back from it.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And Allah took Abraham as an intimate friend (khalil)﴾: this is in the context of encouraging following him, because he is an imam to be emulated, for he reached the furthest point to which servants can draw near to Allah. He attained the rank of khullah (intimate friendship), which is the highest station of love, and this was only because of the abundance of his obedience to his Lord, as He described him in His saying: ﴿and Abraham who fulfilled (his commitments)﴾ [al-Najm: 37]. Many of the early scholars said: That is, he carried out all that he was commanded, and fulfilled every station of worship, so that no great matter distracted him from a small one, nor a big matter from a little one. And He said: ﴿And when Abraham was tested by his Lord with certain words, and he fulfilled them, (Allah) said: Indeed, I will make you an imam for the people﴾ [[Addition from R and A.]] [al-Baqarah: 124], to the end of the verse. And He said: ﴿Indeed, Abraham was a community, devoutly obedient to Allah, a hanif, and he was not of those who associate partners with Allah, grateful for His favors. He chose him and guided him to a straight path. And We gave him good in this world, and indeed, in the Hereafter he is among the righteous﴾ [[Addition from R.]] [al-Nahl: 120–122].

Al-Bukhari said: Sulayman ibn Harb narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Habib ibn Abi Thabit, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from 'Amr ibn Maymun, who said: When Mu'adh came to Yemen, he led them in the dawn prayer, and he recited: ﴿And Allah took Abraham as an intimate friend﴾. A man from the people said: "The eye of Abraham's mother has indeed been comforted."

Ibn Jarir mentioned in his tafsir, from some of them, that Allah named him khalil only because the people of his region suffered a drought, so he travelled to a khalil (friend) of his from the people of Mosul (and some of them said: from the people of Egypt) to obtain food for his family from him. But he did not find what he needed with him. When he drew near to his family, he passed through a sandy desert, and he said: "If only I could fill my sacks with this sand, so that I do not sadden my family by returning to them without provisions, and so that they may think that I have brought them what they love." So he did that, and the sand in his sacks turned into flour. When he reached his home, he slept, and his family rose and opened the sacks, and they found flour. They kneaded it and baked bread from it. He awoke and asked them about the flour from which they had baked, and they said: "From the flour you brought from your khalil." He said: "Yes, it is from my khalil, Allah." So Allah named him khalil because of this.

The authenticity and occurrence of this report are open to question. At best it is an Isra'iliyyat report, which is neither confirmed nor denied. Rather, he was named "Khalil of Allah" because of the intense love of his Lord, may He be mighty and majestic, for him, on account of the obedience he rendered, which Allah loves and is pleased with. For this reason it is established in the two Sahihs, from the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, that when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) addressed them in the last sermon he gave, he said: "To proceed: O people, if I were to take any of the people of the earth as a khalil, I would have taken Abu Bakr ibn Abi Quhafah as a khalil. But your companion is the khalil of Allah." [[Sahih al-Bukhari (no. 3654) and Sahih Muslim (no. 2382). The wording "your companion is the khalil of Allah" is from the hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, narrated by Muslim (no. 2383).]]

And it has come through the routes of Jundub ibn 'Abd Allah al-Bajali, 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As and 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, from the Prophet (ﷺ): "Indeed Allah has taken me as a khalil just as He took Abraham as a khalil." [[The hadith of Jundub ibn 'Abd Allah is narrated by Muslim in his Sahih (no. 532). The hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr is narrated by al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman (no. 9616). The hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud is narrated by Muslim in his Sahih (no. 2383).]]

Ibn Abi Hatim is not the only one to report this. Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh said: Abd al-Rahim ibn Muhammad ibn Muslim narrated to us, Isma'il ibn Ahmad ibn Usayd narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn Ya'qub al-Jawzajani narrated to us in Makkah, Ubayd Allah [[In MS. D and R: "Abd Allah".]] al-Hanafi narrated to us, Zam'ah ibn Salih narrated to us, from Salamah ibn Wahram, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Some of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ were sitting, waiting for him. He came out until he drew near them and heard them discussing. He heard their conversation, and some of them were saying: "How strange! If Allah has taken a khalil (intimate friend) from among His creation, then Ibrahim is His khalil!" Another said: "What is so remarkable about Allah speaking to Musa directly!" Another said: "Isa is the Spirit of Allah and His Word!" Another said: "Adam, whom Allah chose!" So he came out to them, greeted them, and said: "I have heard your talk and your amazement, that Ibrahim is the khalil of Allah, and so he is. Musa is His interlocutor (kalim), Isa is His Spirit and His Word, and Adam is one whom Allah chose, and so he is. Indeed, I am the beloved (habib) of Allah, and I say this without pride. I will bear the banner of praise on the Day of Resurrection, and I say this without pride. I will be the first intercessor and the first whose intercession is accepted, and I say this without pride. I will be the first to move the rings of Paradise, and Allah will open it for me and admit me into it, and with me will be the poor among the believers, and I say this without pride. I will be the most honoured of the first and the last on the Day of Resurrection, and I say this without pride."

This hadith is gharib (strange, with a weak or single chain) from this route, but parts of it have supporting narrations in the Sahih collections and elsewhere. [[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in his Sunan, no. 3616, and he said: "This is a gharib hadith."]]

Qatadah narrated from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, that he said: "Are you amazed that khullah (intimate friendship) was given to Ibrahim, speech to Musa, and vision to Muhammad? May the blessings and peace of Allah be upon them all."

Al-Hakim narrated it in his Mustadrak and said: "It is sahih (sound) according to the conditions of al-Bukhari, though they (al-Bukhari and Muslim) did not include it." It is also narrated similarly from Anas ibn Malik and from many Companions and Successors, and from the leading scholars of the earlier and later generations.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Yahya ibn Abdak al-Qazwini narrated to us, Muhammad, meaning Ibn Sa'id ibn Sabiq, narrated to us, Amr, meaning Ibn Abi Qays, narrated to us, from Asim, from Abu Rashid, from Ubayd ibn Umayr, who said: Ibrahim, peace be upon him, used to host people. One day he went out seeking someone to host, but he found no one to host, so he returned to his house and found a man standing in it. He said: "O servant of Allah, what brought you into my house without my permission?" He replied: "I entered it with the permission of its Lord." He said: "And who are you?" He replied: "I am the Angel of Death. My Lord sent me to one of His servants to give him the good news that Allah has taken him as a khalil." He said: "Who is he? By Allah, if you tell me about him, and he is in the farthest of lands, I will go to him, and I will not leave him as a neighbour until death separates us." He said: "That servant is you." He said: "Me?" He said: "Yes." He said: "For what reason has Allah taken me as a khalil?" He said: "Because you give to people and do not ask them." [[Its chain is mursal (broken).]]

And Mahmud ibn Khalid al-Sulami narrated to us, al-Walid narrated to us, from Ishaq ibn Yasar, who said: When Allah took Ibrahim as a khalil, He placed trembling (wajal) in his heart, to the extent that the pounding of his heart could be heard from a distance, like the fluttering of birds in the air. Likewise it has been described of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that the sound of weeping in his chest was heard like the boiling of a cauldron.

* *

His saying: ﴿And to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾ means: all of it is His possession, His servants and His creation, and He is the one who disposes of all of that. None can reject what He has decreed, none can overturn what He has judged, and He is not questioned about what He does, because of His greatness, His power, His justice, His wisdom, His kindness and His mercy.

* *

His saying: ﴿And Allah is ever, of all things, encompassing﴾ means: His knowledge pervades all of that. No secret of His servants is hidden from Him, and not even the weight of an atom in the heavens or on the earth escapes His knowledge, nor anything smaller than that or greater. No atom is hidden from Him, whether it is visible to observers or concealed.

Al-Bukhari said: Ubayd ibn Isma'il narrated to us, Abu Usamah narrated to us, saying: Hisham ibn Urwah narrated to us, my father informed me [in another version: "from his father"], from Aisha, regarding ﴿They ask you for a ruling concerning women. Say, "Allah gives you His ruling concerning them"﴾ up to His saying ﴿and you desire to marry them﴾. She said: It concerns the man who has an orphan girl in his care, of whom he is the guardian and heir, and he has shared with her in his property, even in the date palm (al-'adhq). He desires to marry her, but he dislikes to marry her to another man lest that man share his property with her. So he prevents her (from marriage). Then this verse was revealed.

Muslim also narrated it in the same way, from Abu Kurayb and from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, both from Abu Usamah. [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 5131; Sahih Muslim, no. 3018.]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: I read to Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Hakam; Ibn Wahb informed us; Yunus informed me, from Ibn Shihab; Urwah ibn al-Zubayr informed me, that Aisha said: Then people asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) for a ruling about them after this verse, so Allah revealed ﴿They ask you for a ruling concerning women. Say, "Allah gives you His ruling concerning them, and what is recited to you in the Book"﴾ to the end of the verse. She said: As for what Allah mentioned, that is recited to them in the Book, it is the first verse in which Allah says ﴿If you fear that you will not deal justly with the orphan girls, then marry what seems good to you of women﴾ [An-Nisa 3].

With this same chain, from Aisha, she said: As for the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, ﴿and you desire to marry them﴾, it refers to the desire of one of you to avoid his orphan in his care when she is poor in wealth and beauty. So they were forbidden to marry those orphan women whom they desired for their wealth and beauty, except with justice, because of their aversion to them.

Its origin is established in the two Sahihs, through the route of Yunus ibn Yazid al-Ayli, with the same wording. [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 5064; Sahih Muslim, no. 3018.]

The meaning is that if a man has an orphan girl in his care, it is permitted for him to marry her. Sometimes he desires to marry her, so Allah, Mighty and Majestic, commands him to give her a dowry equal to that of women like her. If he does not do so, then he should turn to other women, for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has made it wide. This meaning is in the first verse at the beginning of the surah. Sometimes the man has no desire for her because she is unattractive in his eyes, or in reality, so Allah, Mighty and Majestic, forbids him to prevent her from marrying others out of fear that they would share the property between him and her. This is as 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying ﴿concerning the orphan women, to whom you do not give what is prescribed for them, and whom you desire to marry﴾ up to the end of the verse: In the Jahiliyyah, a man would have an orphan girl in his care, and he would throw his garment over her. When he did that, no one could marry her ever. If she was beautiful and he loved her, he would marry her and consume her property. If she was unattractive, he would prevent men from her forever until she died, and then he would inherit her. So Allah forbade that and prohibited it.

He also said regarding His saying ﴿and the oppressed among the children﴾: In the Jahiliyyah they did not give inheritance to young children or to girls. That is His saying ﴿you do not give them what is prescribed for them﴾. So Allah prohibited that, and specified for each one entitled his share, saying ﴿For the male is the equal of the portion of two females﴾ [An-Nisa 11], whether small or grown.

Likewise Sa'id ibn Jubayr and others said. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said regarding His saying ﴿and that you stand for the orphans with justice﴾: It is like when she has beauty and wealth, you marry her and keep her to yourself; likewise, when she has neither beauty nor wealth, marry her and keep her to yourself.

* *

His saying ﴿And whatever good you do, indeed Allah is ever Knowing of it﴾ is an incitement to doing good deeds and complying with the command, and that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is Knowing of all of that, and He will reward for it with the fullest and most complete reward.

The Exalted says, informing and legislating concerning the state of the spouses: at times in a state of the man's aversion from the woman, at times in a state of their agreement, and at times in a state of his separation from her.

The first state: if the woman fears from her husband that he will turn away from her or ignore her, then she may waive her right, or part of it, whether maintenance, clothing, sleeping (night) turn, or other rights over him, and he may accept that from her. There is no blame upon her for offering that to him, nor upon him for accepting it from her. For this reason the Exalted said: ﴿And there is no blame upon them both if they make terms of settlement between themselves, and settlement is best﴾, meaning: better than separation. And His saying: ﴿And souls are present with stinginess﴾ means: settlement when there is contention is better than separation. For this reason, when Sawdah bint Zam'ah grew old, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ resolved to divorce her, so she made terms with him that he would keep her and she would give up her day to 'A'ishah, and he accepted that from her and kept her on that basis.

Mention of the narration on this:

Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said: Sulayman ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, from Simak ibn Harb, from Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Sawdah feared that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would divorce her, so she said: "O Messenger of Allah, do not divorce me, and give my day to 'A'ishah." He did so, and this verse was revealed: ﴿And if a woman fears from her husband ill-treatment or aversion﴾ to the end of the verse. Ibn 'Abbas said: Whatever they agree upon of anything is permissible.

It was also related by al-Tirmidhi, from Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna, from Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi, with the same chain, and he said: "Hasan gharib."[1]

Al-Shafi'i said: Muslim informed us, from Ibn Jurayj, from 'Ata', from Ibn 'Abbas, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ died leaving nine wives, and he used to divide (his nights) among eight.[2]

In the Two Sahihs, from the hadith of Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from his father, from 'A'ishah, who said: When Sawdah bint Zam'ah grew old, she gave her day to 'A'ishah, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would spend her night with 'A'ishah in place of Sawdah's day.[3]

In Sahih al-Bukhari, from the hadith of al-Zuhri, from 'Urwah, from 'A'ishah, similar to it.

Sa'id ibn Mansur said: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi al-Zinad informed us, from Hisham, from his father 'Urwah, who said: Allah the Exalted revealed concerning Sawdah and her likes: ﴿And if a woman fears from her husband ill-treatment or aversion﴾. That was because Sawdah was a woman who had grown old, and she feared that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would part from her, and she was anxious about her place with him, and she knew of the Messenger of Allah's ﷺ love for 'A'ishah and her standing with him, so she gave her day from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to 'A'ishah, and the Prophet ﷺ accepted that.[4]

Al-Bayhaqi said: Ahmad ibn Yunus also narrated it from Ibn Abi al-Zinad, connected (to 'A'ishah). This chain was related by al-Hakim in his Mustadrak, where he said:

Abu Bakr ibn Ishaq al-Faqih informed us: al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Ziyad narrated to us: Ahmad ibn Yunus narrated to us: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi al-Zinad narrated to us, from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from his father, from 'A'ishah, that she said to him: "O nephew, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not favour some of us over others in his staying with us, and hardly a day passed but that he went round to us all, approaching each woman without intercourse, until he reached the one whose day it was, and he spent the night with her. Sawdah bint Zam'ah said, when she had grown old and feared that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would part from her: 'O Messenger of Allah, my day is for 'A'ishah.' The Messenger of Allah ﷺ accepted that." 'A'ishah said: "Concerning that Allah revealed: ﴿And if a woman fears from her husband ill-treatment or aversion﴾."

Likewise Abu Dawud related it from Ahmad ibn Yunus, with the same. Then al-Hakim said: "Sound chain, though the two (Shaykhs) did not record it."[5]

Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh also related it through Abu Bilal al-Ash'ari, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi al-Zinad, similar to it. And from the narration of 'Abd al-Aziz ibn Muhammad al-Darawardi, from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, similar to it, abridged. And Allah knows best.

Abu al-'Abbas Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Dughuli said at the beginning of his Mu'jam: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated to us: Muslim ibn Ibrahim narrated to us: Hisham al-Dastuwa'i narrated to us: al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazzah said: The Prophet ﷺ sent to Sawdah bint Zam'ah to divorce her. When his messenger came to her, she sat on the road of 'A'ishah. When she saw him she said: "I implore you by the One who sent down His speech to you and chose you over His creation, that you take me back, for I have grown old and have no need of men, but I wish to be raised on the Day of Resurrection among your wives." So he took her back, and she said: "I have made my day and my night for the love of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ." This is gharib and mursal.[6]

Al-Bukhari said: Muhammad ibn Muqatil narrated to us: 'Abd Allah informed us: Hisham ibn 'Urwah informed us, from his father, from 'A'ishah concerning ﴿And if a woman fears from her husband ill-treatment or aversion﴾, she said: "It is the man who has a wife with whom he is not inclined to remain, and he wants to part from her, so she says: 'I release you from any obligation concerning me.' Then this verse was revealed."

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Wakic narrated to us, from his father, from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from his father, from 'A'ishah concerning ﴿And if a woman fears from her husband ill-treatment or aversion, there is no blame upon them both if they make terms of settlement between themselves, and settlement is best﴾, she said: "This concerns the woman who is with a man, and perhaps he does not favour her much and she has no child, and she has companionship (with him), so she says: 'Do not divorce me, and you are free of any obligation concerning me.'"

Al-Muthanna narrated to me, from Hajjaj ibn Minhal, from Hammad ibn Salamah, from Hisham, from 'Urwah, from 'A'ishah concerning His saying ﴿And if a woman fears from her husband ill-treatment or aversion﴾, she said: "It is the man who has two wives, one of whom has grown old, or is ugly, and he does not favour her, so she says: 'Do not divorce me, and you are free of any obligation concerning me.'"

This hadith is established in the Two Sahihs, through more than one route, from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from his father, from 'A'ishah, in substance as preceded. To Allah belongs all praise and favour.

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Humayd and Ibn Wakic narrated to us, both saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Ash'ath, from Ibn Sirin, who said: A man came to 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, and asked him about a verse, and he disliked that and struck him with a whip. Then another asked him about this verse: ﴿And if a woman fears from her husband ill-treatment or aversion﴾, and he said: "Ask about the like of this." Then he said: "This is the woman who is with a man, who has passed beyond her age, and he marries a young woman seeking her children. Whatever they agree upon of anything is permissible."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: 'Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Hisinjani narrated to us: Musaddad narrated to us: Abu al-Ahwas narrated to us, from Simak ibn Harb, from Khalid ibn 'Ar'arah, who said: A man came to 'Ali ibn Abi Talib [may Allah be pleased with him] and asked him about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿And if a woman fears from her husband ill-treatment or aversion, there is no blame upon them both﴾. 'Ali said: "A man has a woman with him, and his eyes turn away from her because of her plainness, or her age, or her bad character, or her ugliness, and he dislikes parting from her. If she waives for him some of her dowry, it is lawful for him; and if she gives him some of her days, there is no harm."

Likewise Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi related it from Shu'bah, from Hammad ibn Salamah and Abu al-Ahwas. Ibn Jarir related it through Isra'il; all four from Simak, with the same. Thus Ibn 'Abbas explained it, as did 'Ubaydah al-Salmani, Mujahid ibn Jabr, al-Sha'bi, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, 'Ata', 'Atiyyah al-'Awfi, Makhul, al-Hakam ibn 'Utbah, al-Hasan, Qatadah, and many others of the early generations and the Imams. I know of no disagreement that this verse refers to this. And Allah knows best.

Al-Shafi'i said: Ibn 'Uyaynah informed us, from al-Zuhri, from Ibn al-Musayyab: that the daughter of Muhammad ibn Maslamah was with Rafi' ibn Khadij, and he disliked something in her, whether her age or otherwise, and wished to divorce her. She said: "Do not divorce me, and give me your share as you wish." So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿And if a woman fears from her husband ill-treatment or aversion﴾, the verse.

It was also related by al-Hakim in his Mustadrak, through 'Abd al-Razzaq, from Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab and Sulayman ibn Yasar, with a longer context than this.[7]

Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bayhaqi said: Abu Sa'id ibn Abi 'Amr informed us: Abu Muhammad Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Muzani narrated to us: 'Ali ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa informed us: Abu al-Yaman narrated to us: Shu'ayb ibn Abi Hamzah informed me, from al-Zuhri, who said: Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab and Sulayman ibn Yasar informed me that the sunnah concerning these two verses, in which Allah mentioned the man's ill-treatment and aversion towards his wife, in His saying ﴿And if a woman fears from her husband ill-treatment or aversion﴾ up to the end of the two verses, is that when a man turns away from his wife and prefers others over her, it is her right that he offer her either divorce or that she remain with him on the basis of his favouritism in sharing his wealth and himself. If she remains with him on that basis and dislikes that he divorce her, then there is no blame upon him for favouring others over her in that. If he does not offer her divorce, but makes terms with her to give her from his wealth what she is content with, and she remains with him despite the favouritism in sharing his wealth and himself, that is permissible for him and her settlement with him is valid. Thus Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab and Sulayman mentioned the settlement which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, spoke of: ﴿there is no blame upon them both if they make terms of settlement between themselves, and settlement is best﴾.

It has been mentioned to me that Rafi' ibn Khadij al-Ansari, one of the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ, had a wife who, when she grew old, he married a young girl, and favoured the young girl over her. She asked him for divorce, so he divorced her with one pronouncement. Then he left her until she was nearly to be released from her waiting period, then he took her back. Then he returned to favouring the young girl over her, and she asked him for divorce, so he divorced her with another pronouncement. Then he left her until she was nearly to be released, then took her back. Then he returned to favouring the young girl, and they asked him for divorce, so he said to her: "Whatever you wish. Only one pronouncement remains for you. If you wish, remain on the favouritism you see, or if you wish, I will part from you." She said: "No, rather I will remain on the favouritism." So he kept her on that basis, and that was their settlement. Rafi' did not consider it a sin upon him when she was content to remain with him despite the favouritism he showed her.

This too he narrated in full: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Ḥātim, from his father, from Abū al-Yamān, from Shuʿayb, from al-Zuhrī, from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab and Sulaymān ibn Yasār, and he mentioned it at length. And Allah knows best. [[Al-Sunan al-Kubrā (7/296).]]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And reconciliation is better﴾. ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥah related from Ibn ʿAbbās: it means the option (al-takhyīr, giving the wife a choice), that the husband gives her the choice between staying and separation, which is better than the husband persisting in favouring others over her.

The apparent meaning of the verse is that their reconciliation, by her giving up some of her right to the husband and his accepting that, is better than complete separation. Just as the Prophet ﷺ kept Sawdah bint Zamʿah when she gave up her day to ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, and did not divorce her but kept her among his wives. His doing so was so that his community would follow him in the lawfulness and permissibility of this. Thus it is superior in his case, peace and blessings be upon him. And since agreement (al-wifāq) is more beloved to Allah [ʿazza wa-jall] [[Addition from manuscript R.]] than separation, He said: ﴿And reconciliation is better﴾.

Rather, divorce is hateful to Him, glorified and exalted is He. This is why there came in the hadith narrated by Abū Dāwūd and Ibn Mājah both, from Kathīr ibn ʿUbayd, from Muḥammad ibn Khālid, from Muʿarraf ibn Wāṣil, from Muḥārib ibn Dithār, from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUmar who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The most hated of lawful things to Allah [[In manuscripts R and A: "Allah, glorified and exalted is He."]] is divorce."

Then Abū Dāwūd narrated it from Aḥmad ibn Yūnus, from Muʿarraf ibn Muḥārib, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said... and he mentioned its meaning as a mursal (a narration with a missing companion). [[Sunan Abī Dāwūd no. (2178) and Sunan Ibn Mājah no. (2018), from the hadith of Ibn ʿUmar.
Abū Ḥātim said: "It is only Muḥārib from the Prophet ﷺ, a mursal." (Al-ʿIlal (1/431)). The mursal route was narrated by Abū Dāwūd in his Sunan no. (2177). Shaykh Nāṣir al-Albānī discussed this hadith at length in his book Irwāʾ al-Ghalīl (2040), sufficiently, so let it be consulted.]]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And if you do good and fear Allah, then indeed Allah is ever Acquainted with what you do﴾ [i.e.] [[Addition from manuscripts R and A.]] and if you endure the hardship of patience with those among them whom you dislike, and divide equitably among them as their counterparts, then Allah knows that, and He will reward you for it with the fullest reward.

* *

And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And you will never be able to be equitable between wives, even if you should strive to do so﴾. That is: O people, you will never be able to equalize between wives in every respect. Even if the outward division is achieved, a night for one and a night for another, there must still be disparity in affection, desire and intercourse. This was said by Ibn ʿAbbās, ʿUbaydah al-Salmānī, Mujāhid, al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī and al-Ḍaḥḥāk ibn Muzāḥim.

Ibn Abī Ḥātim said: Abū Zurʿah related to us, Ibn Abī Shaybah related to us, Ḥusayn al-Juʿfī related to us, from Zāʾidah, from ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Rufayʿ, from Ibn Abī Mulaykah who said: This verse ﴿And you will never be able to be equitable between wives, even if you should strive to do so﴾ was revealed concerning ʿĀʾishah. That is, the Prophet ﷺ loved her more than the others, as came in the hadith narrated by Imam Aḥmad and the compilers of the Sunan, from the hadith of Ḥammād ibn Salamah, from Ayyūb, from Abū Qilābah, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Yazīd, from ʿĀʾishah who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to divide among his wives and be equitable, then he would say: "O Allah, this is my division in what I possess, so do not blame me for what You possess and I do not." That is, the heart.

This is the wording of Abū Dāwūd. Its chain is ṣaḥīḥ, but al-Tirmidhī said: Ḥammād ibn Zayd and others narrated it from Ayyūb, from Abū Qilābah, as a mursal. He said: And this is more authentic. [[Sunan Abī Dāwūd no. (2134), Sunan al-Tirmidhī no. (1140), Sunan al-Nasāʾī (7/63), and Sunan Ibn Mājah no. (1971).]]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿So do not incline completely [away from one], leaving her as if suspended﴾. That is: if you incline towards one of them [in manuscript R and A: "towards one of them" (the correct reading being "them")], then do not go to the extreme of complete inclination, leaving the other one suspended. Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujāhid, Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, al-Ḥasan, al-Ḍaḥḥāk, al-Rabīʿ ibn Anas, al-Suddī and Muqātil ibn Ḥayyān said: its meaning is that she is neither a married woman nor a divorced one.

Abū Dāwūd al-Ṭayālisī said: Hammām related to us, from Qatādah, from al-Naḍr ibn Anas, from Bashīr ibn Nahīk, from Abū Hurayrah who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever has two wives and inclines towards one of them will come on the Day of Resurrection with one of his sides fallen."

This was also narrated by Imam Aḥmad and the compilers of the Sunan, from the hadith of Hammām ibn Yaḥyā, from Qatādah, with the same wording. Al-Tirmidhī said: Hammām only transmitted it as a marfūʿ report, and Hishām al-Dastuwāʾī narrated it from Qatādah saying: "It used to be said." We do not know this hadith as marfūʿ except through Hammām. [[Musnad al-Ṭayālisī no. (1597), Al-Musnad (1/471), Sunan Abī Dāwūd no. (2133), Sunan al-Tirmidhī no. (1141), Sunan al-Nasāʾī (7/63), and Sunan Ibn Mājah no. (1969).]]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And if you reconcile and fear Allah, then indeed Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful﴾. That is: if you set your affairs right, divide justly in what you possess, and fear Allah in all circumstances, Allah will forgive you what inclination there was towards some wives over others.

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And if they separate, Allah will enrich each of them from His abundance. And ever is Allah All-Encompassing and Wise﴾. This is the third situation, the situation of separation. He, exalted is He, informed that if they separate, Allah will make the husband independent of her and her independent of him, by giving him in exchange one better for him than her, and giving her in exchange one better for her than him. ﴿And ever is Allah All-Encompassing and Wise﴾: that is, abundant in bounty, great in generosity, and wise in all His actions, decrees and legislation.

The Exalted says, informing and legislating concerning the state of the spouses: at times in a state of the man's aversion from the woman, at times in a state of their agreement, and at times in a state of his separation from her.

The first state: if the woman fears from her husband that he will turn away from her or ignore her, then she may waive her right, or part of it, whether maintenance, clothing, sleeping (night) turn, or other rights over him, and he may accept that from her. Al-Bukhari said: Muhammad ibn Muqatil narrated to us: 'Abd Allah informed us: Hisham ibn 'Urwah informed us, from his father, from 'A'ishah concerning ﴿And if a woman fears from her husband ill-treatment or aversion﴾, she said: "It is the man who has a wife with whom he is not inclined to remain, and he wants to part from her, so she says: 'I release you from any obligation concerning me.' Then this verse was revealed."

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Wakic narrated to us, from his father, from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from his father, from 'A'ishah concerning ﴿And if a woman fears from her husband ill-treatment or aversion, there is no blame upon them both if they make terms of settlement between themselves, and settlement is best﴾, she said: "This concerns the woman who is with a man, and perhaps he does not favour her much and she has no child, and she has companionship (with him), so she says: 'Do not divorce me, and you are free of any obligation concerning me.'"

Al-Muthanna narrated to me, from Hajjaj ibn Minhal, from Hammad ibn Salamah, from Hisham, from 'Urwah, from 'A'ishah concerning His saying ﴿And if a woman fears from her husband ill-treatment or aversion﴾, she said: "It is the man who has two wives, one of whom has grown old, or is ugly, and he does not favour her, so she says: 'Do not divorce me, and you are free of any obligation concerning me.'"

This hadith is established in the Two Sahihs, through more than one route, from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from his father, from 'A'ishah, in substance as preceded. To Allah belongs all praise and favour.

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Humayd and Ibn Wakic narrated to us, both saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Ash'ath, from Ibn Sirin, who said: A man came to 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, and asked him about a verse, and he disliked that and struck him with a whip. Then another asked him about this verse: ﴿And if a woman fears from her husband ill-treatment or aversion﴾, and he said: "Ask about the like of this." Then he said: "This is the woman who is with a man, who has passed beyond her age, and he marries a young woman seeking her children. Whatever they agree upon of anything is permissible."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: 'Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Hisinjani narrated to us: Musaddad narrated to us: Abu al-Ahwas narrated to us, from Simak ibn Harb, from Khalid ibn 'Ar'arah, who said: A man came to 'Ali ibn Abi Talib [may Allah be pleased with him] and asked him about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿And if a woman fears from her husband ill-treatment or aversion, there is no blame upon them both﴾. 'Ali said: "A man has a woman with him, and his eyes turn away from her because of her plainness, or her age, or her bad character, or her ugliness, and he dislikes parting from her. If she waives for him some of her dowry, it is lawful for him; and if she gives him some of her days, there is no harm."

Likewise Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi related it from Shu'bah, from Hammad ibn Salamah and Abu al-Ahwas. Ibn Jarir related it through Isra'il; all four from Simak, with the same. Thus Ibn 'Abbas explained it, as did 'Ubaydah al-Salmani, Mujahid ibn Jabr, al-Sha'bi, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, 'Ata', 'Atiyyah al-'Awfi, Makhul, al-Hakam ibn 'Utbah, al-Hasan, Qatadah, and many others of the early generations and the Imams. I know of no disagreement that this verse refers to this. And Allah knows best.

Al-Shafi'i said: Ibn 'Uyaynah informed us, from al-Zuhri, from Ibn al-Musayyab: that the daughter of Muhammad ibn Maslamah was with Rafi' ibn Khadij, and he disliked something in her, whether her age or otherwise, and wished to divorce her. She said: "Do not divorce me, and give me your share as you wish." So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿And if a woman fears from her husband ill-treatment or aversion﴾, the verse.

It was also related by al-Hakim in his Mustadrak, through 'Abd al-Razzaq, from Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab and Sulayman ibn Yasar, with a longer context than this.[7]

Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bayhaqi said: Abu Sa'id ibn Abi 'Amr informed us: Abu Muhammad Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Muzani narrated to us: 'Ali ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa informed us: Abu al-Yaman narrated to us: Shu'ayb ibn Abi Hamzah informed me, from al-Zuhri, who said: Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab and Sulayman ibn Yasar informed me that the sunnah concerning these two verses, in which Allah mentioned the man's ill-treatment and aversion towards his wife, in His saying ﴿And if a woman fears from her husband ill-treatment or aversion﴾ up to the end of the two verses, is that when a man turns away from his wife and prefers others over her, it is her right that he offer her either divorce or that she remain with him on the basis of his favouritism in sharing his wealth and himself. If she remains with him on that basis and dislikes that he divorce her, then there is no blame upon him for favouring others over her in that. If he does not offer her divorce, but makes terms with her to give her from his wealth what she is content with, and she remains with him despite the favouritism in sharing his wealth and himself, that is permissible for him and her settlement with him is valid. Thus Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab and Sulayman mentioned the settlement which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, spoke of: ﴿there is no blame upon them both if they make terms of settlement between themselves, and settlement is best﴾.

It has been mentioned to me that Rafi' ibn Khadij al-Ansari, one of the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ, had a wife who, when she grew old, he married a young girl, and favoured the young girl over her. She asked him for divorce, so he divorced her with one pronouncement. Then he left her until she was nearly to be released from her waiting period, then he took her back. Then he returned to favouring the young girl over her, and she asked him for divorce, so he divorced her with another pronouncement. Then he left her until she was nearly to be released, then took her back. Then he returned to favouring the young girl, and they asked him for divorce, so he said to her: "Whatever you wish. Only one pronouncement remains for you. If you wish, remain on the favouritism you see, or if you wish, I will part from you." She said: "No, rather I will remain on the favouritism." So he kept her on that basis, and that was their settlement. Rafi' did not consider it a sin upon him when she was content to remain with him despite the favouritism he showed her.

As for His saying: ﴿And reconciliation is better﴾. ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥah related from Ibn ʿAbbās: it means the option (al-takhyīr, giving the wife a choice), that the husband gives her the choice between staying and separation, which is better than the husband persisting in favouring others over her.

The apparent meaning of the verse is that their reconciliation, by her giving up some of her right to the husband and his accepting that, is better than complete separation. Just as the Prophet ﷺ kept Sawdah bint Zamʿah when she gave up her day to ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, and did not divorce her but kept her among his wives. His doing so was so that his community would follow him in the lawfulness and permissibility of this. Thus it is superior in his case, peace and blessings be upon him. And since agreement (al-wifāq) is more beloved to Allah [ʿazza wa-jall] [[Addition from manuscript R.]] than separation, He said: ﴿And reconciliation is better﴾.

Rather, divorce is hateful to Him, glorified and exalted is He. This is why there came in the hadith narrated by Abū Dāwūd and Ibn Mājah both, from Kathīr ibn ʿUbayd, from Muḥammad ibn Khālid, from Muʿarraf ibn Wāṣil, from Muḥārib ibn Dithār, from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUmar who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The most hated of lawful things to Allah [[In manuscripts R and A: "Allah, glorified and exalted is He."]] is divorce."

Then Abū Dāwūd narrated it from Aḥmad ibn Yūnus, from Muʿarraf ibn Muḥārib, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said... and he mentioned its meaning as a mursal (a narration with a missing companion). [[Sunan Abī Dāwūd no. (2178) and Sunan Ibn Mājah no. (2018), from the hadith of Ibn ʿUmar.
Abū Ḥātim said: "It is only Muḥārib from the Prophet ﷺ, a mursal." (Al-ʿIlal (1/431)). The mursal route was narrated by Abū Dāwūd in his Sunan no. (2177). Shaykh Nāṣir al-Albānī discussed this hadith at length in his book Irwāʾ al-Ghalīl (2040), sufficiently, so let it be consulted.]]

As for His saying: ﴿And if you do good and fear Allah, then indeed Allah is ever Acquainted with what you do﴾ [i.e.] [[Addition from manuscripts R and A.]] and if you endure the hardship of patience with those among them whom you dislike, and divide equitably among them as their counterparts, then Allah knows that, and He will reward you for it with the fullest reward.

* *

And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And you will never be able to be equitable between wives, even if you should strive to do so﴾. That is: O people, you will never be able to equalize between wives in every respect. Even if the outward division is achieved, a night for one and a night for another, there must still be disparity in affection, desire and intercourse. This was said by Ibn ʿAbbās, ʿUbaydah al-Salmānī, Mujāhid, al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī and al-Ḍaḥḥāk ibn Muzāḥim.

Ibn Abī Ḥātim said: Abū Zurʿah related to us, Ibn Abī Shaybah related to us, Ḥusayn al-Juʿfī related to us, from Zāʾidah, from ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Rufayʿ, from Ibn Abī Mulaykah who said: This verse ﴿And you will never be able to be equitable between wives, even if you should strive to do so﴾ was revealed concerning ʿĀʾishah. That is, the Prophet ﷺ loved her more than the others, as came in the hadith narrated by Imam Aḥmad and the compilers of the Sunan, from the hadith of Ḥammād ibn Salamah, from Ayyūb, from Abū Qilābah, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Yazīd, from ʿĀʾishah who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to divide among his wives and be equitable, then he would say: "O Allah, this is my division in what I possess, so do not blame me for what You possess and I do not." That is, the heart.

This is the wording of Abū Dāwūd. Its chain is ṣaḥīḥ, but al-Tirmidhī said: Ḥammād ibn Zayd and others narrated it from Ayyūb, from Abū Qilābah, as a mursal. He said: And this is more authentic. [[Sunan Abī Dāwūd no. (2134), Sunan al-Tirmidhī no. (1140), Sunan al-Nasāʾī (7/63), and Sunan Ibn Mājah no. (1971).]]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿So do not incline completely [away from one], leaving her as if suspended﴾. That is: if you incline towards one of them [in manuscript R and A: "towards one of them" (the correct reading being "them")], then do not go to the extreme of complete inclination, leaving the other one suspended. Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujāhid, Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, al-Ḥasan, al-Ḍaḥḥāk, al-Rabīʿ ibn Anas, al-Suddī and Muqātil ibn Ḥayyān said: its meaning is that she is neither a married woman nor a divorced one.

Abū Dāwūd al-Ṭayālisī said: Hammām related to us, from Qatādah, from al-Naḍr ibn Anas, from Bashīr ibn Nahīk, from Abū Hurayrah who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever has two wives and inclines towards one of them will come on the Day of Resurrection with one of his sides fallen."

This was also narrated by Imam Aḥmad and the compilers of the Sunan, from the hadith of Hammām ibn Yaḥyā, from Qatādah, with the same wording. Al-Tirmidhī said: Hammām only transmitted it as a marfūʿ report, and Hishām al-Dastuwāʾī narrated it from Qatādah saying: "It used to be said." We do not know this hadith as marfūʿ except through Hammām. [[Musnad al-Ṭayālisī no. (1597), Al-Musnad (1/471), Sunan Abī Dāwūd no. (2133), Sunan al-Tirmidhī no. (1141), Sunan al-Nasāʾī (7/63), and Sunan Ibn Mājah no. (1969).]]

As for His saying: ﴿And if you reconcile and fear Allah, then indeed Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful﴾. That is: if you set your affairs right, divide justly in what you possess, and fear Allah in all circumstances, Allah will forgive you what inclination there was towards some wives over others.

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And if they separate, Allah will enrich each of them from His abundance. And ever is Allah All-Encompassing and Wise﴾. This is the third situation, the situation of separation. He, exalted is He, informed that if they separate, Allah will make the husband independent of her and her independent of him, by giving him in exchange one better for him than her, and giving her in exchange one better for her than him. ﴿And ever is Allah All-Encompassing and Wise﴾: that is, abundant in bounty, great in generosity, and wise in all His actions, decrees and legislation.

The Exalted says, informing and legislating concerning the state of the spouses: at times in a state of the man's aversion from the woman, at times in a state of their agreement, and at times in a state of his separation from her.

The first state: if the woman fears from her husband that he will turn away from her or ignore her, then she may waive her right, or part of it, whether maintenance, clothing, sleeping (night) turn, or other rights over him, and he may accept that from her. There is no blame upon her for offering that to him, nor upon him for accepting it from her. For this reason the Exalted said: ﴿And there is no blame upon them both if they make terms of settlement between themselves, and settlement is best﴾, meaning: better than separation. And His saying: ﴿And souls are present with stinginess﴾ means: settlement when there is contention is better than separation. For this reason, when Sawdah bint Zam'ah grew old, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ resolved to divorce her, so she made terms with him that he would keep her and she would give up her day to 'A'ishah, and he accepted that from her and kept her on that basis.

Mention of the narration on this:

Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said: Sulayman ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, from Simak ibn Harb, from Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Sawdah feared that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would divorce her, so she said: "O Messenger of Allah, do not divorce me, and give my day to 'A'ishah." He did so, and this verse was revealed: ﴿And if a woman fears from her husband ill-treatment or aversion﴾ to the end of the verse. Ibn 'Abbas said: Whatever they agree upon of anything is permissible.

It was also related by al-Tirmidhi, from Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna, from Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi, with the same chain, and he said: "Hasan gharib."[1]

Al-Shafi'i said: Muslim informed us, from Ibn Jurayj, from 'Ata', from Ibn 'Abbas, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ died leaving nine wives, and he used to divide (his nights) among eight.[2]

In the Two Sahihs, from the hadith of Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from his father, from 'A'ishah, who said: When Sawdah bint Zam'ah grew old, she gave her day to 'A'ishah, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would spend her night with 'A'ishah in place of Sawdah's day.[3]

In Sahih al-Bukhari, from the hadith of al-Zuhri, from 'Urwah, from 'A'ishah, similar to it.

Sa'id ibn Mansur said: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi al-Zinad informed us, from Hisham, from his father 'Urwah, who said: Allah the Exalted revealed concerning Sawdah and her likes: ﴿And if a woman fears from her husband ill-treatment or aversion﴾. That was because Sawdah was a woman who had grown old, and she feared that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would part from her, and she was anxious about her place with him, and she knew of the Messenger of Allah's ﷺ love for 'A'ishah and her standing with him, so she gave her day from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to 'A'ishah, and the Prophet ﷺ accepted that.[4]

Al-Bayhaqi said: Ahmad ibn Yunus also narrated it from Ibn Abi al-Zinad, connected (to 'A'ishah). This chain was related by al-Hakim in his Mustadrak, where he said:

Abu Bakr ibn Ishaq al-Faqih informed us: al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Ziyad narrated to us: Ahmad ibn Yunus narrated to us: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi al-Zinad narrated to us, from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from his father, from 'A'ishah, that she said to him: "O nephew, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not favour some of us over others in his staying with us, and hardly a day passed but that he went round to us all, approaching each woman without intercourse, until he reached the one whose day it was, and he spent the night with her. Sawdah bint Zam'ah said, when she had grown old and feared that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would part from her: 'O Messenger of Allah, my day is for 'A'ishah.' The Messenger of Allah ﷺ accepted that." 'A'ishah said: "Concerning that Allah revealed: ﴿And if a woman fears from her husband ill-treatment or aversion﴾."

Likewise Abu Dawud related it from Ahmad ibn Yunus, with the same. Then al-Hakim said: "Sound chain, though the two (Shaykhs) did not record it."[5]

Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh also related it through Abu Bilal al-Ash'ari, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi al-Zinad, similar to it. And from the narration of 'Abd al-Aziz ibn Muhammad al-Darawardi, from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, similar to it, abridged. And Allah knows best.

Abu al-'Abbas Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Dughuli said at the beginning of his Mu'jam: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated to us: Muslim ibn Ibrahim narrated to us: Hisham al-Dastuwa'i narrated to us: al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazzah said: The Prophet ﷺ sent to Sawdah bint Zam'ah to divorce her. When his messenger came to her, she sat on the road of 'A'ishah. When she saw him she said: "I implore you by the One who sent down His speech to you and chose you over His creation, that you take me back, for I have grown old and have no need of men, but I wish to be raised on the Day of Resurrection among your wives." So he took her back, and she said: "I have made my day and my night for the love of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ." This is gharib and mursal.[6]

As for His saying: ﴿And reconciliation is better﴾. ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥah related from Ibn ʿAbbās: it means the option (al-takhyīr, giving the wife a choice), that the husband gives her the choice between staying and separation, which is better than the husband persisting in favouring others over her.

The apparent meaning of the verse is that their reconciliation, by her giving up some of her right to the husband and his accepting that, is better than complete separation. Just as the Prophet ﷺ kept Sawdah bint Zamʿah when she gave up her day to ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, and did not divorce her but kept her among his wives. His doing so was so that his community would follow him in the lawfulness and permissibility of this. Thus it is superior in his case, peace and blessings be upon him. And since agreement (al-wifāq) is more beloved to Allah [ʿazza wa-jall] [[Addition from manuscript R.]] than separation, He said: ﴿And reconciliation is better﴾.

Rather, divorce is hateful to Him, glorified and exalted is He. This is why there came in the hadith narrated by Abū Dāwūd and Ibn Mājah both, from Kathīr ibn ʿUbayd, from Muḥammad ibn Khālid, from Muʿarraf ibn Wāṣil, from Muḥārib ibn Dithār, from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUmar who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The most hated of lawful things to Allah [[In manuscripts R and A: "Allah, glorified and exalted is He."]] is divorce."

Then Abū Dāwūd narrated it from Aḥmad ibn Yūnus, from Muʿarraf ibn Muḥārib, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said... and he mentioned its meaning as a mursal (a narration with a missing companion). [[Sunan Abī Dāwūd no. (2178) and Sunan Ibn Mājah no. (2018), from the hadith of Ibn ʿUmar.
Abū Ḥātim said: "It is only Muḥārib from the Prophet ﷺ, a mursal." (Al-ʿIlal (1/431)). The mursal route was narrated by Abū Dāwūd in his Sunan no. (2177). Shaykh Nāṣir al-Albānī discussed this hadith at length in his book Irwāʾ al-Ghalīl (2040), sufficiently, so let it be consulted.]]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And if you do good and fear Allah, then indeed Allah is ever Acquainted with what you do﴾ [i.e.] [[Addition from manuscripts R and A.]] and if you endure the hardship of patience with those among them whom you dislike, and divide equitably among them as their counterparts, then Allah knows that, and He will reward you for it with the fullest reward.

* *

And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And you will never be able to be equitable between wives, even if you should strive to do so﴾. That is: O people, you will never be able to equalize between wives in every respect. Even if the outward division is achieved, a night for one and a night for another, there must still be disparity in affection, desire and intercourse. This was said by Ibn ʿAbbās, ʿUbaydah al-Salmānī, Mujāhid, al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī and al-Ḍaḥḥāk ibn Muzāḥim.

Ibn Abī Ḥātim said: Abū Zurʿah related to us, Ibn Abī Shaybah related to us, Ḥusayn al-Juʿfī related to us, from Zāʾidah, from ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Rufayʿ, from Ibn Abī Mulaykah who said: This verse ﴿And you will never be able to be equitable between wives, even if you should strive to do so﴾ was revealed concerning ʿĀʾishah. That is, the Prophet ﷺ loved her more than the others, as came in the hadith narrated by Imam Aḥmad and the compilers of the Sunan, from the hadith of Ḥammād ibn Salamah, from Ayyūb, from Abū Qilābah, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Yazīd, from ʿĀʾishah who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to divide among his wives and be equitable, then he would say: "O Allah, this is my division in what I possess, so do not blame me for what You possess and I do not." That is, the heart.

This is the wording of Abū Dāwūd. Its chain is ṣaḥīḥ, but al-Tirmidhī said: Ḥammād ibn Zayd and others narrated it from Ayyūb, from Abū Qilābah, as a mursal. He said: And this is more authentic. [[Sunan Abī Dāwūd no. (2134), Sunan al-Tirmidhī no. (1140), Sunan al-Nasāʾī (7/63), and Sunan Ibn Mājah no. (1971).]]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿So do not incline completely [away from one], leaving her as if suspended﴾. That is: if you incline towards one of them [in manuscript R and A: "towards one of them" (the correct reading being "them")], then do not go to the extreme of complete inclination, leaving the other one suspended. Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujāhid, Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, al-Ḥasan, al-Ḍaḥḥāk, al-Rabīʿ ibn Anas, al-Suddī and Muqātil ibn Ḥayyān said: its meaning is that she is neither a married woman nor a divorced one.

Abū Dāwūd al-Ṭayālisī said: Hammām related to us, from Qatādah, from al-Naḍr ibn Anas, from Bashīr ibn Nahīk, from Abū Hurayrah who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever has two wives and inclines towards one of them will come on the Day of Resurrection with one of his sides fallen."

This was also narrated by Imam Aḥmad and the compilers of the Sunan, from the hadith of Hammām ibn Yaḥyā, from Qatādah, with the same wording. Al-Tirmidhī said: Hammām only transmitted it as a marfūʿ report, and Hishām al-Dastuwāʾī narrated it from Qatādah saying: "It used to be said." We do not know this hadith as marfūʿ except through Hammām. [[Musnad al-Ṭayālisī no. (1597), Al-Musnad (1/471), Sunan Abī Dāwūd no. (2133), Sunan al-Tirmidhī no. (1141), Sunan al-Nasāʾī (7/63), and Sunan Ibn Mājah no. (1969).]]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And if you reconcile and fear Allah, then indeed Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful﴾. That is: if you set your affairs right, divide justly in what you possess, and fear Allah in all circumstances, Allah will forgive you what inclination there was towards some wives over others.

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And if they separate, Allah will enrich each of them from His abundance. And ever is Allah All-Encompassing and Wise﴾. This is the third situation, the situation of separation. He, exalted is He, informed that if they separate, Allah will make the husband independent of her and her independent of him, by giving him in exchange one better for him than her, and giving her in exchange one better for her than him. ﴿And ever is Allah All-Encompassing and Wise﴾: that is, abundant in bounty, great in generosity, and wise in all His actions, decrees and legislation.

ِAllah informs that He is the Owner of the heavens and the earth, and that He is the Judge over them both. Therefore He said: ﴿And We had already enjoined those who were given the Scripture before you, and [also] you, to fear Allah﴾, meaning: We enjoined on you what We enjoined on them, namely to fear Allah, Mighty and Majestic, by worshipping Him alone, with no partner.

Then He said: ﴿And if you disbelieve - then indeed, to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth [And ever is Allah Free of need and Praiseworthy]﴾ [[Addition from ر, أ; in هـ: "the verse".]], as Allah the Exalted said, reporting about Moses that he said to his people: ﴿If you disbelieve, you and whoever is on the earth entirely - then indeed, Allah is Free of need and Praiseworthy﴾ [Ibrahim: 8]. He also said: ﴿But they disbelieved and turned away, and Allah made [them] independent [of need], and Allah is Free of need and Praiseworthy﴾ [At-Taghabun: 6]. That is, He is Free of need of His servants. ﴿Praiseworthy﴾ means He is praised in all that He decrees and legislates.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and sufficient is Allah as Disposer of affairs﴾, meaning: He is the Overseer over every soul for what it has earned, the Watchful, the Witness over everything.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿If He wills, He can remove you, O people, and bring others; and ever is Allah competent to do that﴾, meaning: He is able to remove you and replace you with others if you disobey Him. As He said: ﴿And if you turn away, He will replace you with another people; then they will not be like you﴾ [Muhammad: 38]. Some of the early pious predecessors (al-Salaf) said: "How insignificant the servants are before Allah when they neglect His command!" Allah also said: ﴿If He wills, He can remove you and bring a new creation. And that is not difficult for Allah﴾ [Ibrahim: 19-20], meaning: it is not impossible for Him.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Whoever desires the reward of this world - then with Allah is the reward of this world and the Hereafter﴾, meaning: O you whose concern is only this world, know that with Allah is the reward of this world and the Hereafter. If you ask Him for both of these, He will give you, enrich you and satisfy you. As Allah said: ﴿Among the people is he who says, "Our Lord, give us in this world," and he will have no share in the Hereafter. And among them is he who says, "Our Lord, give us in this world good and in the Hereafter good and protect us from the punishment of the Fire." Those will have a share of what they have earned, and Allah is swift in account﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 200-202]. He also said: ﴿Whoever desires the harvest of the Hereafter, We will increase him in his harvest; and whoever desires the harvest of this world, We will give him of it, but he will have no share in the Hereafter﴾ [Ash-Shura: 20]. And He said: ﴿Whoever desires the immediate [world], We hasten for him therein what We will, for whom We intend. Then We have made for him Hell; he will burn therein, blamed and banished. And whoever desires the Hereafter and strives for it its due effort while he is a believer - those are the ones whose effort is appreciated. All - to these and to those - We extend from the gift of your Lord, and the gift of your Lord is not restricted. Look how We have preferred some of them over others; and the Hereafter is greater in degrees and greater in preference﴾ [Al-Isra: 18-21].

Ibn Jarir claimed that the meaning of this verse, ﴿Whoever desires the reward of this world﴾, refers to the hypocrites who displayed faith for that purpose, ﴿then with Allah is the reward of this world﴾, which is what they obtained of spoils and other things along with the Muslims. And His saying: ﴿and the Hereafter﴾ means: and with Allah [[In د، ر، أ: "i.e., and with Him".]] is the reward of the Hereafter, which is the punishment He has stored up for them in the Fire of Hell. He made this like His saying: ﴿Whoever desires the worldly life and its adornment - We will fully repay them for their deeds therein, and they therein will not be deprived. Those are the ones for whom there is nothing in the Hereafter except the Fire, and what they did therein will be nullified, and worthless is what they used to do﴾ [Hud: 15-16].

There is no doubt that the meaning of this verse is clear. But his interpretation of the first verse in this way is open to question. His saying ﴿then with Allah is the reward of this world and the Hereafter﴾ clearly indicates that good in this world and the Hereafter is present, meaning: both of these are in His hand. So let not one of limited aspiration confine himself to striving for this world alone; rather, let his aspiration be lofty, reaching for the high goals of this world and the Hereafter, for the return of all of that is to the One in whose hand is harm and benefit, Allah, there is no god but Him, who has apportioned happiness and misery in this world and the Hereafter among people, and has dealt justly among them in what He knows of them, with regard to those who deserve this and those who deserve this. Therefore He said: ﴿And ever is Allah Hearing and Seeing﴾.
