(5678), from Abu Hurayrah, with the wording: "Allah has not sent down any disease except that He has sent down its cure."] In his time, Allah will send forth Ya'juj and Ma'juj, and Allah will destroy them through the blessing of his supplication. Allah the Exalted has said: ﴿Until, when Gog and Magog are released, and they swarm from every elevated place. And the true promise draws near﴾ [al-Anbiya': 96-97], and the verse continues.

The description of 'Isa, peace be upon him:

It has already passed in the hadith of 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Adam, from Abu Hurayrah [may Allah be pleased with him]: "When you see him, recognise him: a man of medium height, inclining to redness and whiteness, wearing two garments dyed with saffron, as if his head were dripping, though no water has touched it." In the hadith of al-Nawwas ibn Sam'an: "He will descend at the white minaret east of Damascus, between two garments of saffron, placing his palms upon the wings of two angels. When he lowers his head, drops fall from it, and when he raises it, there flows from it like pearls of jewels. No disbeliever who smells his breath will be allowed to live, and his breath reaches as far as his gaze reaches."

Al-Bukhari and Muslim narrated, through the chain of al-Zuhri, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "On the night I was taken on the Night Journey, I met Musa (Moses)," and he described him: "Behold, a man, I think he said, [who was] agitated, curly-haired, as if he were one of the men of Shanu'ah." He said: "And I met 'Isa," and the Prophet (ﷺ) described him: "Of medium height, reddish, as if he had just come out of a bathhouse (dimas, meaning the hammam). And I saw Ibrahim, and I am the most similar of his offspring to him." [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (3437) and Sahih Muslim no. (168)]... the hadith.

Al-Bukhari narrated, from the hadith of Mujahid, from Ibn 'Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I saw Musa, 'Isa and Ibrahim. As for 'Isa, he is reddish, curly-haired, broad-chested. As for Musa, he is dark-skinned, tall, straight-haired, as if he were one of the men of al-Zutt." [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (3438). Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar, in Fath al-Bari (6/484), held that the correct attribution is from Ibn 'Abbas, not Ibn 'Umar, so refer there.]

And al-Bukhari and Muslim also narrated from the route of Musa ibn 'Uqbah, from Nafi', who said: 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar said: One day the Prophet (ﷺ) mentioned the Masih al-Dajjal among the people and said: "Allah is not one-eyed. Behold, the Masih al-Dajjal is blind in the right eye, as if his eye were a floating grape. Allah showed me at the Ka'bah in a dream: a man, brown-skinned, the best-looking brown-skinned man you have ever seen, with his hair hanging between his shoulders, straight-haired, water dripping from his head, placing his hands on the shoulders of two men, and he was circumambulating the House. I asked: 'Who is this?' They said: 'The Masih, son of Maryam.' Then I saw behind him a man, curly-haired, tightly curled, blind in the right eye, most resembling Ibn Qatan whom I have seen, placing his hands on the shoulders of a man circumambulating the House. I asked: 'Who is this?' They said: 'The Masih al-Dajjal.'" 'Ubayd Allah narrated the same from Nafi'. [Sahih al-Bukhari nos. (3439, 3440) and Sahih Muslim no. (169).]

Then al-Bukhari narrated it from Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Makki, from Ibrahim ibn Sa'd, from al-Zuhri, from Salim, from his father, who said: "No, by Allah, the Prophet (ﷺ) did not say that 'Isa was red. Rather he said: 'While I was sleeping, I was circumambulating the Ka'bah, and behold, a man, brown-skinned, straight-haired, being supported between two men, water dripping from his head or his head pouring water. I asked: "Who is this?" They said: "The son of Maryam." I turned to look, and behold, a red, tall man, curly-haired, blind in his right eye, as if his eye were a floating grape. I asked: "Who is this?" They said: "The Dajjal." And the closest person to him in resemblance is Ibn Qatan.'" Al-Zuhri said: He was a man from Khuza'ah who died in the pre-Islamic period. [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (3441).]

These are all the words of al-Bukhari (may Allah have mercy on him). It has already been mentioned in the hadith of Abd al-Rahman ibn Adam from Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him) that Isa (peace be upon him), after his descent to the earth, will remain on the earth for forty years, and then he will die and the Muslims will pray over him.

In the hadith of Abd Allah ibn Amr in Muslim, it is narrated that he will remain for seven years. So it is possible, and Allah knows best, that what is meant by his staying on the earth for forty years is the total of his residence there before his being raised up and after his descent, for he was raised up when he was thirty-three years old, according to the Sahih (the authentic collection). This is also mentioned in a hadith describing the people of Paradise: that they will be upon the form of Adam, and that the age of Isa at his birth was thirty-three years.

As for what Ibn Asakir related from some scholars, that he was raised up when he was one hundred and fifty years old, it is anomalous, strange and far-fetched.

The hafiz Abu al-Qasim ibn Asakir mentioned in the biography of Isa ibn Maryam in his History, from some of the early generation (salaf), that he will be buried with the Prophet (ﷺ) in his chamber. Allah knows best.
[Tarikh Dimashq (14/106, manuscript) and Mukhtasar Tarikh Dimashq by Ibn Manzur (20/154), with its chain of narration going back to Abd Allah ibn Salam (may Allah be pleased with him). Al-Bukhari said: "This is not authentic according to me, and no one corroborates it."]

* *

As for the Most High's saying: ﴿And on the Day of Resurrection he will be a witness against them﴾, Qatadah said: He will testify against them that he had conveyed the message of Allah to them, and that he acknowledged servanthood to Allah, Mighty and Majestic. This is like His saying, Most High, at the end of Surah al-Ma'idah: ﴿And when Allah says, "O Isa, son of Maryam, did you say to the people, 'Take me and my mother as two gods besides Allah'?" He will say, "Glory be to You, it is not for me to say what I have no right to. If I had said it, You would have known it. You know what is in my soul, and I do not know what is in Your soul. Indeed, You, You are the Knower of the unseen. I did not tell them except what You commanded me: 'Worship Allah, my Lord and your Lord.' And I was a witness over them while I was among them; but when You caused me to die, You were the Watcher over them, and You are Witness over all things. If You punish them, indeed they are Your servants; and if You forgive them, indeed You, You are the Exalted in Might, the Wise.'﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 116–118]

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 4, verses 155–159 (part 1 of 7):

These were among the sins they committed, which made their curse, their expulsion, and their distance from guidance necessary. This includes their breaking of the covenants and pacts that were taken from them, and their disbelief in the signs of Allah, that is, His proofs and evidences, and the miracles they witnessed through the hands of the Prophets, peace be upon them.

His saying: ﴿and their killing of the Prophets without right﴾. This is because of the magnitude of their crimes and their audacity against the Prophets of Allah. They killed a great multitude of the Prophets [without right], peace be upon them.

And their saying: ﴿Our hearts are uncovered﴾. Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, 'Ikrimah, al-Suddi, Qatadah, and others said: that is, they are in coverings. This is like the saying of the polytheists: ﴿And they say, "Our hearts are in coverings from what you call us to, and in our ears is deafness, and between us and you is a screen. So act, indeed we are acting."﴾ [Fussilat: 5]. It was also said that the meaning is that they claimed their hearts were "ghulf" (full) of knowledge, that is, receptacles containing knowledge which they had retained and acquired. This was related by al-Kalbi, from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas. A similar explanation has already been mentioned in his commentary on Surat al-Baqarah.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Rather, Allah has sealed over them because of their disbelief.﴾ According to the first view, it is as though they were offering an excuse to Him, claiming that their hearts do not comprehend what he says, because they are in coverings and in veils. Allah said: rather, He has sealed them because of their disbelief. According to the second view, what they claimed is reversed against them in every respect. The discussion of this kind of matter has already been presented in Surat al-Baqarah.

﴿So they do not believe, except a few.﴾ That is: their hearts became hardened in disbelief, rebellion, and scarcity of faith.

﴿And because of their disbelief and their saying against Maryam a tremendous slander.﴾ 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah related from Ibn 'Abbas: "That is, they accused her of fornication." Likewise said al-Suddi, Juwaybir, Muhammad ibn Ishaq, and others. It is apparent from the verse that they accused her and her son with enormous things, making her an adulteress, while she had conceived her child from that [some added: while she was menstruating]. So upon them be the continuous curses of Allah until the Day of Resurrection.

And their saying: ﴿Indeed, we killed the Messiah, 'Isa, son of Maryam, the Messenger of Allah.﴾ That is [after it in one manuscript: and with their claim of falsehood, lies, calumny, and transgression in their saying: "Indeed, we killed the Messiah, 'Isa, son of Maryam, the Messenger of Allah"]: this one who claims for himself this position, we killed him. This was from them by way of mockery and derision, like the saying of the polytheists: ﴿O you to whom the Reminder has been revealed, indeed you are a madman!﴾ [al-Hijr: 6].

The account of the Jews, may the curses, wrath, anger, and punishment of Allah be upon them, is that when Allah sent 'Isa son of Maryam with clear proofs and guidance, they envied him for what Allah had given him of prophethood and striking miracles. By these he healed the blind and the leper, and he brought the dead to life by the permission of Allah, and he shaped a bird from clay, then breathed into it, and it became a bird whose flight was witnessed, by the permission of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and other miracles with which Allah honored him and performed through his hands. Despite this, they denied him and opposed him, and they strove to harm him by every means they could, until the Prophet of Allah, 'Isa, peace be upon him, would not dwell among them in any town. Rather, he and his mother, peace be upon them both, traveled extensively. Even so, this did not satisfy them, until they went to the king of Damascus at that time, who was a polytheist, one of the worshippers of the stars, and whose people were called the Yunan. They informed him that in Bayt al-Maqdis there was a man who was seducing the people, misguiding them, and corrupting the king's subjects. The king became angry at this, and wrote to his deputy in Jerusalem to seize this man, to crucify him, to place thorns on his head, and to restrain his harm to the people. When the letter arrived, the governor of Bayt al-Maqdis [in another version: the governor of the city] carried out this order, and he went with a group of Jews to the house where 'Isa, peace be upon him, was, with a group of his companions, twelve or thirteen (it was also said seventeen men). That was on Friday after the 'Asr prayer, on the night of Saturday, so they besieged him there. When he sensed them, and realized there was no escape from their entering upon him or from his going out to them, he said to his companions: "Which of you will have my likeness cast upon him, and he will be my companion in Paradise?" A young man among them volunteered for this, but he seemed too young for it in their eyes, so he asked again a second and a third time, and each time only that young man volunteered. He said: "You are he." Allah cast the likeness of 'Isa upon him, so that he appeared to be him. An opening in the roof of the house was made, and sleep overtook 'Isa, peace be upon him, and he was raised to heaven while in that state, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿When Allah said, "O 'Isa, indeed I will take you and raise you to Myself and purify you from those who disbelieve"﴾ [Al 'Imran: 55], and the rest of the verse.

When he was raised, those men came out. When they saw that young man, they thought he was 'Isa, so they seized him at night and crucified him, and they placed thorns on his head. The Jews made known that they had striven to crucify him, and they boasted of this. Groups of the Christians accepted this from them, due to their ignorance and scarcity of intellect, except for those who had been in the house with the Messiah, for they had witnessed his being raised. As for the rest, they thought, just as the Jews thought, that the one crucified was the Messiah, 'Isa son of Maryam. It is said that Maryam sat beneath that crucified one and wept, and it is said that he spoke to her. And Allah knows best.

All of this is part of Allah's trial for His servants, for He has profound wisdom in it. Allah has clarified the matter, made it manifest, explained it, and revealed it in the Great Quran, which He sent down to His noble Messenger, supported by miracles, clear proofs, and evident signs. So the Exalted said, and He is the most truthful of speakers, the Lord of the worlds, who knows the secrets and the innermost thoughts, who knows the secret in the heavens and the earth, who knows what has been and what will be, and what would have been had it not been, how it would have been: ﴿And they did not kill him, nor did they crucify him, but it was made to appear so to them.﴾ That is: they saw his likeness and thought it was him. For this reason He said: ﴿Indeed, those who differ concerning it are in doubt about it. They have no knowledge of it except the following of assumption. And they did not kill him for certain. Rather, Allah raised him to Himself.﴾ By this He means that all of them, both the Jews who claimed his killing and the ignorant Christians who accepted it, are in doubt about that, in confusion, misguidance, and bewilderment. For this reason He said: ﴿And they did not kill him for certain﴾, that is: they did not kill him being certain that he was he, but rather doubting and supposing. ﴿Rather, Allah raised him to Himself. And Allah is ever Mighty and Wise.﴾ That is: Mighty in His dominion, whose sanctuary cannot be violated, and who does not wrong whoever seeks refuge at His door. ﴿Wise﴾, that is: in all that He decrees and ordains of matters that He creates, and His is the perfect wisdom, the conclusive proof, the great authority, and the eternal command.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn Sinan narrated to us, Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from al-Minhal ibn 'Amr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: When Allah wished to raise 'Isa to heaven, he came out to his companions, and in the house were twelve men from the disciples (al-Hawariyyun). He came out to them from a spring in the house, and his head was dripping with water. He said: "Indeed among you is one who will disbelieve in me twelve times after having believed in me." Then he said: "Which of you will have my likeness cast upon him, so that he will be killed in my place and be with me in my rank?" A young man, the youngest of them in age, stood up. He said to him: "Sit down." Then he repeated it to them, and that young man stood up again, and he said: "Sit down." Then he repeated it to them, and the young man stood up and said: "I." He said: "You are he, that one." So the likeness of 'Isa was cast upon him, and 'Isa was raised from an opening in the house to heaven. He said: The Jews came in pursuit and seized the one who resembled him, and they killed him, then crucified him. Some of them disbelieved in him twelve times after having believed in him, and they split into three sects. One group said: "God was among us as long as He willed, then He ascended to heaven." These are the Ya'qubiyyah. Another group said: "The son of God was among us as long as He willed, then God raised him to Himself." These are the Nestorians. Another group said: "The servant of God and His Messenger was among us as long as God willed, then God raised him to Himself." These are the Muslims. Thus the two disbelieving sects allied against the Muslim sect and killed her. Islam remained obscured until Allah sent Muhammad (ﷺ).

This is a sound chain of narration back to Ibn 'Abbas. It was also related by al-Nasa'i from Abu Kurayb, from Abu Mu'awiyah, with similar wording (Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. 11591). Likewise, a number of the early scholars mentioned that he said to them: "Which of you will have my likeness cast upon him, so that he will be killed in my place, and he will be my companion in Paradise?"

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, from Ya'qub al-Qummi, from Harun ibn 'Antara, from Wahb ibn Munabbih, who said: Jesus was approached while he was in a house with seventeen of the disciples (al-Hawariyyun), and they surrounded them. When they entered upon him, God, exalted and majestic is He, made all of them take the form of Jesus. They said to them: "You have bewitched us. Either Jesus must come out to us, or we will kill all of you." Jesus said to his companions: "Which of you will sell his soul today for Paradise?" A man among them said: "I will." So he went out to them and said: "I am Jesus," and God had made him in the form of Jesus. They seized him, killed him, and crucified him. From that point, it was made to appear to them (shubbiha lahum), so they thought they had killed Jesus. The Christians likewise thought that he was Jesus. God raised Jesus up that same day. This is a very strange account (siyaq gharib jiddan). [Tafsir al-Tabari (9/368). He approved the statement of Wahb ibn Munabbih, although the Hafiz here considered it strange. See: Tafsir al-Tabari (9/374).]

Ibn Jarir said: A similar statement has been related from Wahb, namely what al-Muthanna narrated to me: Ishaq narrated to us, Isma'il ibn 'Abd al-Karim narrated to us, 'Abd al-Samad ibn Ma'qil narrated to me, that he heard Wahb say: When God informed Jesus, son of Mary, that he was about to depart from the world, he dreaded death and it weighed heavily on him. He summoned the disciples and prepared food for them, and said: "Attend me tonight, for I have a need of you." When they gathered to him at night, he fed them and began serving them. When they finished eating, he began washing their hands and performing ablution for them with his own hand, and wiping their hands with his garments. They found this great and disliked it. He said: "Whoever objects to anything I do tonight, he is not of me, nor am I of him." So they acquiesced. When he had finished that, he said: "As for what I have done with you tonight, serving you at the meal and washing your hands with my own hand, let there be for you an example in me, for you see that I am the best of you. Let none of you exalt himself over another, and let each of you give himself for another, as I have given myself for you. As for my need tonight, which I ask your help with, it is that you call upon God for me, and strive in supplication that my term be postponed." When they set themselves to supplication and intended to exert themselves, sleep overcame them until they could not manage any supplication. He kept waking them and saying: "Glory be to God! Will you not bear with me for one night, helping me in it?" They said: "By God, we do not know what has happened to us. We used to converse and talk at length, but tonight we cannot endure conversation, and whenever we want to supplicate, something comes between us and it." He said: "The shepherd is taken away and the sheep are scattered." He continued to speak words similar to this, lamenting himself. Then he said: "Truly, one of you will disbelieve in me before the rooster crows three times, and one of you will sell me for a small sum of dirhams and will eat my price." They went out and dispersed. The Jews were seeking him, and they seized Shim'un, one of the disciples, and said: "This man is one of his companions." He denied it and said: "I am not his companion," so they left him. Then others seized him, and he denied it likewise. Then he heard the crowing of a rooster, and he wept and was grieved. When morning came, one of the disciples went to the Jews and said: "What will you give me if I guide you to the Messiah?" They offered him thirty dirhams. He took them and guided them to him. He had been made to resemble (shubbiha 'alayhim) before that. They seized him, made him secure, bound him with rope, and began leading him, saying to him: "You used to revive the dead, drive out the devil, and heal the madman; will you not save yourself from this rope?" They spat upon him, cast thorns upon him, until they brought him to the wood on which they intended to crucify him. God raised him up to Himself, and they crucified what had been made to resemble him. He remained for seven [days]. Then his mother and the woman whom Jesus, peace be upon him, had been treating, whom God had cured of madness, came weeping at the place of the crucified one. Jesus came to them and said: "Why are you weeping?" They said: "For you." He said: "God has raised me up to Himself, and nothing but good has befallen me. This was made to resemble them. So command the disciples to meet me at such-and-such a place." Eleven of them met him at that place, and they lost the one who had sold him and pointed the Jews to him. He asked his companions about him, and they said: "He regretted what he had done, hanged himself, and killed himself." He said: "Had he repented, God would have accepted his repentance." Then he asked them about a boy who had nearly followed them, called Yahya. He said: "He is with you. Go, for every person will awake speaking the language of his people, so let him warn them and let him call them." [This is a very strange account (siyaq gharib jiddan). Tafsir al-Tabari (9/368).]

Then Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, Salama narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: The name of the king of the Children of Israel who was sent to Jesus to kill him was a man among them called Dawud. When they resolved upon that concerning him, no servant of God's servants was ever terrified of death as he was terrified, and he did not lament it as he lamented, nor did he cease supplicating God to turn it away from him, so much so that, it is claimed, he would say: "O God, if You are turning this cup away from anyone of Your creation, then turn it away from me," and his skin would sweat blood from the anguish of it. He entered the place where they had agreed to enter upon him to kill him, he and his companions, who were thirteen with Jesus, peace be upon him. When he became certain that they were entering upon him, he said to his companions among the disciples, who were twelve men: Futrus, Ya'qub ibn Zabdi, Yuhannas the brother of Ya'qub, Andarabis, Filibs, Abartulma, Mana, Tumas, Ya'qub ibn Halfiya, Tada'usis, Qathaniya, Yuwadis Zakariya Yutta.

Ibn Humayd said: Salama said, Ibn Ishaq said: Among them, as was mentioned to me, was a man named Sirjis. They were thirteen men besides Jesus, peace be upon him. The Christians deny him, because he was the one who was made to resemble Jesus for the Jews. He said: "I do not know whether he was among these twelve or was the thirteenth," and they denied him when they acknowledged to the Jews the crucifixion of Jesus, and disbelieved in what Muhammad ﷺ had reported about him. If they were thirteen, then when they entered the place they were fourteen with Jesus; and if they were twelve, then when they entered the place they were thirteen.

Ibn Ishaq said: A man who had been a Christian and then embraced Islam related to me that when revelation came to Jesus from God, "Indeed I will cause you to die and raise you to Me" [Qur'an 3:55], he said: "O assembly of the disciples, which of you loves to be my companion in Paradise on condition that he is made to resemble me in form before the people, and they kill him in my place?" Sirjis said: "I, O Spirit of God." He said: "Then sit in my seat." So he sat in it, and Jesus, peace be upon him, was raised. They entered upon him, seized him and crucified him, and he was the one they crucified, and it was made to appear to them as him. Their number when they entered with Jesus was known; they had seen them and counted them. When they entered upon him to seize him, they found Jesus, as they thought, and his companions, but they were missing one man from the count; he was the one about whom they disagreed, and they did not recognize Jesus, until they gave Yudas Zakariya Yutta thirty dirhams on condition that he guide them to him and identify him for them. He said to them: "When you enter upon him, I will approach him, and he is the one I kiss; so seize him." When they entered, Jesus had been raised, and he saw Sirjis in the form of Jesus, and no doubt entered his mind that he was Jesus. He bent over him and kissed him, [and they killed him]; they seized him and crucified him.

Then Yudas Zakariya Yutta regretted what he had done, and he hanged himself with a rope until he killed himself. He is cursed among the Christians, and he had been counted among his companions. Some Christians claim that Yudas Zakariya Yutta was the one made to resemble him, so they crucified him while he was saying: "I am not your companion; I am the one who guided you to him." And God knows best which of these was the case. [Related by al-Tabari in his commentary (9/371) by way of Salama from Ibn Ishaq.]

Ibn Jarir said, from Mujahid: They crucified a man whom they made to resemble Jesus, and God, exalted and majestic is He, raised Jesus to the heaven alive.

Ibn Jarir chose the view that the likeness of Jesus was cast upon all of his companions.

* *

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And there is none of the People of the Scripture but that he will surely believe in him before his death. And on the Day of Resurrection he will be against them a witness﴾

Ibn Jarir said: The interpreters differed regarding the meaning of this. Some of them said: The meaning of that: ﴿And there is none of the People of the Scripture but that he will surely believe in him﴾, meaning in Jesus, ﴿before his death﴾, meaning: before the death of Jesus. This is directed to the view that all of them will affirm him when he descends to kill the Dajjal, and then all the religions will become one, which is the religion of Islam, the upright religion of Abraham, peace be upon him.

Mention of those who said that:

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu Husayn, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿And there is none of the People of the Scripture but that he will surely believe in him before his death﴾, he said: before the death of Jesus son of Mary. Al-'Awfi also related similarly from Ibn 'Abbas [Tafsir al-Tabari (9/380)].

Abu Malik said regarding His saying: ﴿but that he will surely believe in him before his death﴾: That is at the descent of Jesus son of Mary, peace be upon him; no one of the People of the Scripture will remain but that he will believe in him.

Al-Dahhak said, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿And there is none of the People of the Scripture but that he will surely believe in him before his death﴾, meaning: the Jews specifically. Al-Hasan al-Basri said: meaning the Negus (al-Najashi) and his companions. Ibn Abi Hatim related both.

Ibn Jarir said: Ya'qub narrated to me, Ibn 'Ulayya narrated to us, Abu Raja' narrated to us, from al-Hasan: ﴿And there is none of the People of the Scripture but that he will surely believe in him before his death﴾, he said: before the death of Jesus. By God, he is now alive with God, but when he descends they will all believe in him.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, 'Ali ibn 'Uthman al-Lahiqi narrated to us, Juwayriya ibn Bishr narrated to us, who said: I heard a man say to al-Hasan: "O Abu Sa'id, the saying of God, exalted is He: ﴿And there is none of the People of the Scripture but that he will surely believe in him before his death﴾" He said: "Before the death of Jesus. God raised Jesus to Himself, and He will send him before the Day of Resurrection to a station in which the righteous and the wicked will all believe in him."

Likewise said Qatada, and 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, and others. This statement is the truth, as we will clarify afterward with the decisive proof, God willing, and in Him is trust, and upon Him is reliance.

Ibn Jarir said: Others said: The meaning of that: ﴿And there is none of the People of the Scripture but that he will surely believe in him﴾, before the death of the Scripturist (al-kitabi). This refers to those who held that when he sees death he knows truth from falsehood, because everyone whom death approaches, his soul does not depart until the truth becomes clear to him from falsehood in his religion.

'Ali ibn Abi Talha said, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿And there is none of the People of the Scripture but that he will surely believe in him before his death﴾: He said: No Jew dies until he believes in Jesus.

Ibn Kathir's commentary (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on Surah an-Nisa', verses 155–159 (part 3 of 7):

Al-Muthanna narrated to me: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His words: ﴿And there is none of the People of the Scripture but that he will surely believe in him before his death﴾: "Every person of the Scripture believes in 'Isa before his death," meaning before the death of the person of the Scripture. Ibn 'Abbas said: "If you struck his neck, his soul would not leave until he believed in 'Isa."

Ibn Humayd narrated to us: Abu Numaylah Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us: Husayn ibn Waqid narrated to us, from Yazid al-Nahwi, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "No Jew dies until he testifies that 'Isa is the servant of Allah and His Messenger, even if he is struck with weapons."

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim ibn Habib ibn al-Shahid narrated to me: 'Attab ibn Bashir narrated to us, from Khusayf, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning ﴿And there is none of the People of the Scripture but that he will surely believe in him before his death﴾. He said: "It is in the recitation of Ubayy: ﴿before their death﴾. No Jew ever dies without believing in 'Isa." It was said to Ibn 'Abbas: "What if he falls from the top of a house?" He said: "He will speak of it while falling." It was said: "What if one of them has his neck struck?" He said: "His tongue will stammer over it."

Similarly, Sufyan al-Thawri narrated from Khusayf, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning ﴿And there is none of the People of the Scripture but that he will surely believe in him before his death﴾, that he said: "No Jew dies until he believes in 'Isa, peace be upon him. Even if he is struck with a sword, he will speak of it. And if he falls, he will speak of it while falling."

Similarly, Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi narrated from Shu'bah, from Abu Harun al-Ghanawi (in one copy: al-'Awfi), from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas. All of these are sound chains (asanid sahihah) to Ibn 'Abbas. Similarly, this has been authentically reported from Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, and Muhammad ibn Sirin. This is also the view of al-Dahhak, Juwaybir, and al-Suddi, who attributed it to Ibn 'Abbas and cited the recitation of Ubayy ibn Ka'b: "before their death."

'Abd al-Razzaq said, from Isra'il, from Furat al-Qazzaz, from al-Hasan, concerning His words: ﴿And there is none of the People of the Scripture but that he will surely believe in him before his death﴾: "None of them dies until he believes in 'Isa before he dies."

This may be what al-Hasan meant by what was reported earlier from him, and it may be that he meant what these others meant. [Tafsir 'Abd al-Razzaq (1/170).]

Ibn Jarir (al-Tabari) said: "Others said that the meaning is: 'And there is none of the People of the Scripture but that he will surely believe in Muhammad ﷺ before the death of the scripturist.'"

Mention of those who said this:

Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to me: al-Hajjaj ibn Minhal narrated to us: Hammad narrated to us, from Humayd, who said: 'Ikrimah said: "No Christian or Jew dies until he believes in Muhammad ﷺ," concerning His words: ﴿And there is none of the People of the Scripture but that he will surely believe in him before his death﴾.

Then Ibn Jarir said: "The most correct of these views is the first, namely that none of the People of the Scripture will remain after the descent of 'Isa, peace be upon him, except that he believes in him before his death, that is, before the death of 'Isa, peace be upon him." There is no doubt that what Ibn Jarir said, may Allah have mercy on him, is correct, because it is the purpose of the context of these verses, which establish the falsehood of what the Jews claimed, namely that they killed 'Isa and crucified him, and which show that the ignorant Christians who accepted this were wrong. Allah informs that the matter was not so, but it was made to appear so to them, and they killed the one who resembled him while they were not certain of it. Then He raised him to Himself, and he is alive, and he will descend before the Day of Resurrection, as indicated by the mutawatir (widely transmitted) hadiths, which we will cite shortly, if Allah wills. He will kill the Dajjal (false messiah), break the cross, kill the swine, and abolish the jizyah (poll tax), meaning that he will not accept it from anyone of any religion, rather he will accept only Islam or the sword. This noble verse informs that all the People of the Scripture will believe in him at that time, and not one of them will fail to affirm him. For this reason He said: ﴿And there is none of the People of the Scripture but that he will surely believe in him before his death﴾, that is, before the death of 'Isa, whom the Jews and those who agreed with them among the Christians claimed was killed and crucified.

﴿And on the Day of Resurrection he will be a witness against them﴾, that is, concerning their deeds, which he witnessed from them before his ascension to heaven and after his descent to earth.

As for the one who interpreted this verse to mean that every scripturist does not die until he believes in 'Isa or in Muhammad ﷺ, peace be upon them both, this is what actually happens, because at the time of death everyone sees what he was ignorant of, and so believes in it. But this will not be a beneficial faith for him, since he has already witnessed the angel, as Allah, the Exalted, said at the beginning of this surah: ﴿And repentance is not accepted from those who continue to do evil until, when death approaches one of them, he says, "Indeed, I have repented now," nor from those who die while they are disbelievers﴾ [An-Nisa' 18]. And Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿So when they saw Our punishment, they said, "We believe in Allah alone and reject what we used to associate with Him." But their faith was not going to benefit them when they saw Our punishment﴾ [Ghafir 84–85]. This shows the weakness of what Ibn Jarir argued in rejecting this view, when he said: "If this verse meant this, then everyone who believed in Muhammad or in the Messiah, from among those who had disbelieved in them, would be upon their religion, and then his relatives from among the people of his religion would not inherit from him, because the Truthful One has informed that he believes in him before his death." This is not sound, because it does not follow that if his faith at a time when it does not benefit him, he thereby becomes a Muslim. Do you not see the saying of Ibn 'Abbas: "Even if he falls from a high place, or is struck with a sword, or is seized by a predator, he will surely believe in 'Isa." Faith in such circumstances is not beneficial, and it does not move its holder from his disbelief, for the reason we have already mentioned. And Allah knows best.

Whoever reflects on this carefully and considers it deeply will find clear that although this is what actually happens, it does not follow that this is the meaning of the verse. Rather, its meaning is what we have mentioned: the establishment of the existence of 'Isa, peace be upon him, the continuation of his life in heaven, and that he will descend to earth before the Day of Resurrection. This is to refute both groups, the Jews and the Christians, whose statements about him conflicted, opposed one another, contradicted, and were devoid of truth. The Jews fell short, and the Christians exceeded the limit. The Jews belittled him by accusing him of what they accused him of and of great wrongs against his mother, while the Christians praised him excessively, claiming for him what is not his. In opposition to those, they elevated him from the station of prophethood to the station of divinity. Allah is exalted far above the words of these and those, and He is glorified, sanctified, and there is no god but Him.

The Hadiths Concerning the Descent of 'Isa ibn Maryam to Earth from Heaven at the End of Time, Before the Day of Resurrection, and that He Calls to the Worship of Allah Alone, without Partner:

Al-Bukhari, may Allah have mercy on him, said in the Book of Mentioning the Prophets of his Sahih, which has been received with acceptance: "The Descent of 'Isa ibn Maryam, peace be upon him": Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us: Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to us: my father narrated to us, from Salih, from Ibn Shihab, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "By the One in whose hand is my soul, the son of Maryam will surely descend among you as a just judge. He will break the cross, kill the swine, abolish the jizyah, and wealth will abound until no one accepts it, until a prostration will be better than this world and whatever is in it." Then Abu Hurayrah said: "Recite if you wish: ﴿And there is none of the People of the Scripture but that he will surely believe in him before his death, and on the Day of Resurrection he will be a witness against them﴾."

Similarly, Muslim narrated it from al-Hasan al-Hulwani and 'Abd ibn Humayd, both from Ya'qub, with the same wording. [Sahih al-Bukhari no. 3448, and Sahih Muslim no. 155.] Al-Bukhari and Muslim also narrated it from the hadith of Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah, from al-Zuhri, with the same wording. [Sahih al-Bukhari no. 2476, and Sahih Muslim no. 155.] They also narrated it through al-Layth from al-Zuhri with the same wording. [Sahih al-Bukhari no. 2222, and Sahih Muslim no. 155.] Ibn Mardawayh narrated it through Muhammad ibn Abi Hafsah, from al-Zuhri, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "It is near that the son of Maryam will be among you as a just judge. He will kill the Dajjal, kill the swine, break the cross, abolish the jizyah, wealth will abound, and there will be one prostration to Allah, Lord of the worlds." Abu Hurayrah said: "Recite if you wish: ﴿And there is none of the People of the Scripture but that he will surely believe in him before his death﴾," meaning before the death of 'Isa ibn Maryam. Then Abu Hurayrah repeated it three times. [Al-Suyuti mentioned it in al-Durr al-Manthur (2/735).]

Another route from Abu Hurayrah: Imam Ahmad said: Rawh narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Abi Hafsah narrated to us, from al-Zuhri, from Handhalah ibn 'Ali al-Aslami, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "'Isa ibn Maryam will surely assume the state of ihram at Fajj al-Rawha' for Hajj or 'Umrah, or he will combine both together."

Similarly, Muslim narrated it alone from the hadiths of Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah, al-Layth ibn Sa'd, and Yunus ibn Yazid, all three from al-Zuhri with the same wording. [Al-Musnad (2/513) and Sahih Muslim no. 1252.]

Ahmad also said: Yazid narrated to us: Sufyan, that is Ibn Husayn, narrated to us, from al-Zuhri, from Handhalah, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "'Isa ibn Maryam will descend, kill the swine, erase the cross, the prayer will be gathered for him, he will give wealth until it is not accepted, he will abolish the kharaj (land tax), and he will descend at al-Rawha' and perform Hajj or 'Umrah from there, or combine both." He said: Abu Hurayrah recited: ﴿And there is none of the People of the Scripture but that he will surely believe in him before his death [and on the Day of Resurrection he will be a witness against them]﴾. Handhalah claimed that Abu Hurayrah said: "He will believe in him before the death of 'Isa." I do not know whether all of this is the hadith of the Prophet ﷺ or something Abu Hurayrah said.

Similarly, Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from his father, from Abu Musa Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna, from Yazid ibn Harun, from Sufyan ibn Husayn, from al-Zuhri, with the same wording. [Al-Musnad (2/290).]

Another route: al-Bukhari said: Ibn Bukayr narrated to us: al-Layth narrated to us, from Yunus, from Ibn Shihab, from Nafi', client of Abu Qatadah al-Ansari, that Abu Hurayrah said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "How will you be when the Messiah, the son of Maryam, descends among you, and your imam is from among you?" 'Uqayl and al-Awza'i followed him in this.

Similarly, Imam Ahmad narrated it from 'Abd al-Razzaq, from Ma'mar, and from 'Uthman ibn 'Umar, from Ibn Abi Dhi'b, both from al-Zuhri, with the same wording. Muslim also narrated it from the narrations of Yunus, al-Awza'i, and Ibn Abi Dhi'b, with the same wording. [Sahih al-Bukhari no. 3449, al-Musnad (2/272) through 'Abd al-Razzaq, (2/336) through 'Uthman ibn 'Umar, and Sahih Muslim no. 155.]

Another route: Imam Ahmad said: Affan narrated to us, Hammam narrated to us, Qatadah informed us, from Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The prophets are brothers by different mothers (ʿallāt), their religion is one, and I am the closest of people to Jesus, son of Mary, because there was no prophet between me and him. He will descend, so when you see him, recognize him: a man of medium height, inclining to redness and whiteness, wearing two light yellow garments, as if his head is dripping water even though no moisture has touched it. He will break the cross, kill the swine, abolish the jizyah, and call people to Islam. In his time Allah will destroy all religions except Islam, and Allah will destroy in his time the Messiah ad-Dajjal. Then security will spread over the earth, so that lions will graze with camels, panthers with cattle, and wolves with sheep, and children will play with snakes without being harmed. He will remain forty years, then he will die, and the Muslims will pray over him."

Abu Dawud related it similarly, from Hudbah ibn Khalid, from Hammam ibn Yahya. Ibn Jarir related it, and he did not mention anything else at this verse, from Bishr ibn Muadh, from Yazid ibn Harun, from Saeed ibn Abi ʿArubah, both of them from Qatadah, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Adam, the client of Umm Burthun, the one in charge of the water-supply, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), and he mentioned something similar, and said: "Then people will fight for Islam."

Al-Bukhari related from Abu al-Yaman, from Shuʿayb, from al-Zuhri, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "I am the closest of people to Jesus, son of Mary, and the prophets are ʿallāt brothers (awlād ʿallāt), there is no prophet between me and him."

Then he related from Muhammad ibn Sinan: from Fulayh ibn Sulayman, from Hilal ibn Ali, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi ʿAmrah, from Abu Hurayrah who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I am the closest of people to Jesus, son of Mary, in this world and the Hereafter, and the prophets are brothers by different mothers, their religion is one." Ibrahim ibn Tahman said, from Musa ibn Uqbah, from Safwan ibn Sulaym, from Ata ibn Yasar, from Abu Hurayrah who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said.

Another hadith: Muslim said in his Sahih: Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me, Muʿalla ibn Mansur narrated to us, Sulayman ibn Bilal narrated to us, Suhayl narrated to us, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The Hour will not come until the Romans land at al-Aʿmaq or Dabiq. An army from Madinah, of the best people of the earth on that day, will go out to them. When they line up, the Romans will say: 'Leave us and those who took captives from us, so we may fight them.' The Muslims will say: 'No, by Allah, we will not leave you between us and our brothers.' So they will fight, and a third will flee, whom Allah will never forgive, and a third will be killed, the best of martyrs with Allah [Mighty and Majestic], and a third will be victorious, who will never be tested, and they will conquer Constantinople. While they are dividing the spoils, having hung their swords on the olive trees, Satan will shout among them: 'The Messiah has taken your place among your families!' They will go out, but it is false. When they come to Syria, he will emerge, and while they are preparing for battle, arranging the rows, the prayer will be called, and Jesus, son of Mary, will descend and lead them. When the enemy of Allah sees him, he will melt as salt melts in water; if he left him, he would melt away until he perished, but Allah will kill him by his hand, and show them his blood on his spear."

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Hushaym narrated to us, from al-Awwam ibn Hawshab, from Jabalah ibn Suhaym, from Mu'thir ibn Afazah, from Ibn Masʿud, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) who said: "On the night I was taken on the Night Journey, I met Ibrahim, Musa and Isa, peace be upon them. They discussed the matter of the Hour, and referred their question to Ibrahim, who said: 'I have no knowledge of it.' They referred it to Musa, who said: 'I have no knowledge of it.' They referred it to Isa, who said: 'As for its appointed time, none knows it except Allah. My Lord has charged me that the Dajjal will emerge.' He said: 'I will have with me two staves; when he sees me he will melt as lead melts. Allah will destroy him when he sees me, until even the stone and the tree will say: O Muslim, there is a disbeliever beneath me, come and kill him.' He said: 'Allah will destroy them, then people will return to their lands and homelands. At that time Yajuj and Majuj will emerge, and they are from every slope, swarming. They will trample their lands, and they will leave nothing they pass without destroying it, and they will not pass by water without drinking it. He said: Then people will return to me complaining of them, and I will call upon Allah against them, and He will destroy and kill them, until the earth is filled with the stench of their smell. Allah will send rain which will sweep their bodies until We cast them into the sea. Concerning this my Lord has charged me that when this happens, the Hour will be like a pregnant woman near term, whose family does not know when her birth will surprise them, by night or by day.'"

Ibn Majah related it, from Muhammad ibn Bashshar, from Yazid ibn Harun, from al-Awwam ibn Hawshab, with it in similar form.

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, Hammad ibn Salamah informed us, from Ali ibn Zayd, from Abu Nadrah who said: We came to Uthman ibn Abi al-As on a Friday, to present to him our copy of the Qur'an against his copy. When Friday came, he ordered us, so we performed ghusl, then he brought us perfume, so we perfumed ourselves, then we went to the mosque and sat with a man who told us about the Dajjal. Then Uthman ibn Abi al-As came, so we stood up for him, and we sat. He said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "The Muslims will have three cities: a city at the meeting of the two seas, a city at al-Hirah, and a city in Syria. People will be struck with three panics. The Dajjal will emerge among the people's honour, and he will be defeated from the east. The first city he will reach is the city at the meeting of the two seas, and its people will become three groups: one group will remain saying: 'We will see what this is'; one group will join the Bedouins; and one group will join the city next to them. With the Dajjal will be seventy thousand men wearing shawls, and most of those with him will be Jews and women. Then he will come to the next city, and its people will become three groups: one group says: 'We will smell it and see what it is'; one group joins the Bedouins; and one group joins the city next to them, in the west of Syria. The Muslims will withdraw to the Aqabah of Afiq and send out a detachment, which will be struck, and this will grieve them, and they will suffer severe hunger and hardship, so that one of them will burn the string of his bow and eat it. While they are in this state, a caller will call from the dawn: 'O people, help has come to you,' three times. Some will say to others: 'This is the voice of a satisfied man.' Then Isa, son of Maryam, peace be upon him, will descend at the time of the Fajr prayer, and their leader will say to him: 'Spirit of Allah, go forward and lead the prayer.' He will say: 'This community are leaders over one another.' So their leader will go forward and pray. When he finishes his prayer, Isa will take his spear and go toward the Dajjal. When the Dajjal sees him, he will melt as lead melts, and Isa will place his spear between his chest and throat, and kill him, and his companions will be defeated. On that day there will be nothing to hide anyone, until even the tree will say: 'O believer, this is a disbeliever.' And the stone will say: 'O believer, this is a disbeliever.'" Ahmad alone related it through this route.

Another hadith: Abu Abd Allah Muhammad ibn Yazid ibn Majah said in his famous Sunan: Ali ibn Muhammad narrated to us, Abd al-Rahman al-Muharibi narrated to us, from Ismail ibn Rafi Abu Rafi, from Abu Zurʿah al-Shaybani Yahya ibn Abi Amr, from Abu Umamah al-Bahili who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) addressed us, and most of his sermon was a narration about the Dajjal, which he warned us about. Among what he said was:

"There has never been a trial on earth since Allah created the offspring of Adam, greater than the trial of the Dajjal. Allah has never sent a prophet without warning his nation about the Dajjal. I am the last of the prophets, and you are the last of the nations, and he will certainly emerge among you. If he emerges while I am among you, I will be a disputant for every Muslim; and if he emerges after me, each person will be his own disputant, and Allah is my successor over every Muslim. He will emerge from a passage between Syria and Iraq, and will spread corruption right and left. O servants of Allah, O people, stand firm. I will describe him to you in a way no prophet before me has described him: he will begin by saying, 'I am a prophet,' but there is no prophet after me; then he will say, 'I am your lord,' but you will not see your Lord until you die. He is one-eyed, while your Lord, Mighty and Majestic, is not one-eyed. Written between his eyes is 'disbeliever,' which every believer will read, whether literate or illiterate. Among his trials is that he has a garden and a fire: his fire is a garden and his garden is a fire. Whoever is tested by his fire, let him call upon Allah and recite the opening verses of Surat al-Kahf, and it will become cool and safe for him, as the fire became cool and safe for Ibrahim. Among his trials is that he will say to a Bedouin: 'Tell me, if I bring your father and mother back to life, will you testify that I am your lord?' He will say: 'Yes.' Then two devils will take the form of his father and mother and say: 'My son, follow him, for he is your lord.' Among his trials is that he will be given power over one soul, kill it, and saw it in two with a saw, until it is thrown in two halves; then he will say: 'Look at this servant of mine, for I will now raise him,' yet he will claim that he has a lord other than me. Allah will raise him, and the wicked one will say to him: 'Who is your lord?' He will say: 'My Lord is Allah, and you are the enemy of Allah, the Dajjal. By Allah, I have never been more certain of you than I am today.'"

Abu al-Hasan al-Tanafisi said: Al-Muharibi narrated to us, Ubayd Allah ibn al-Walid al-Wassafi narrated to us, from Atiyyah, from Abu Sa'id who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "That man will be the highest in rank of my nation in Paradise."

He said: Abu Sa'id said: "By Allah, we did not think that man was anyone but Umar ibn al-Khattab, until he passed on to his path."

Al-Muharibi said: Then we returned to the hadith of Abu Rafi'. He said: "Among his trials is that he will command the sky to rain, and it will rain, and he will command the earth to grow, and it will grow. [Among his trials is that he will pass by a tribe and they will deny him, and no grazing animal of theirs will be left but it will perish.]" [Addition from A and Ibn Majah.] "And among his trials is that he will pass by a tribe and they will believe him. He will command the sky to rain, and it will rain, and he will command the earth to grow, and it will grow, until their livestock come home that day fatter and larger than they have ever been, with their flanks at their fullest and their udders at their most abundant. Nothing on earth will remain that he does not tread upon and overcome, except Makkah and Madinah. No entrance of theirs through any of their passes will be open to him except that the angels will meet him with drawn swords, until he descends at the red sand dune, at the end of the salt marsh. Then Madinah will shake with its people three times, and no hypocrite, man or woman, will remain but will go out to him. It will expel the impurity from it as the furnace expels the impurity of iron. That day will be called the Day of Deliverance."

Umm Sharik bint Abi al-'Akr [variant in R: "al-'Akam"] said: "O Messenger of Allah, where will the Arabs be on that day?" He said: "They will be few, and most of them will be in Bayt al-Maqdis, and their imam will be a righteous man. While their imam has come forward to lead them in the dawn prayer, 'Isa the son of Maryam (peace be upon him) descends upon them [addition from A and Ibn Majah]. The imam turns back, walking backwards, so that 'Isa may come forward and lead the people in prayer. 'Isa (peace be upon him) places his hand between his shoulders and says: 'Go forward and lead, for the prayer was called for you.' So their imam leads them in prayer. When he finishes, 'Isa (peace be upon him) says: 'Open the gate.' It is opened, and behind it is the Dajjal, with seventy thousand Jews, each of them carrying a decorated sword and a shawl. When the Dajjal sees him, he melts as salt melts in water and flees, and 'Isa (peace be upon him) says: 'I have a blow for you that you will not escape.' He overtakes him at the eastern gate of Ludd and kills him. Allah defeats the Jews, and nothing that Allah has created remains behind which a Jew might hide but that Allah will make that thing speak, be it a stone, a tree, a wall, or an animal, except the gharqad tree, which is of their trees and does not speak. Each will say: 'O servant of Allah, the Muslim, here is a Jew; come and kill him.'"

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "His days will be forty years: a year is like half a year, a year is like a month, a month is like a week, and the last of his days will be like a spark. One of you will rise in the morning at the gate of Madinah and will not reach its other gate before evening." It was said to him: "O Prophet of Allah, how should we pray in those short days?" He said: "Estimate the prayer in them as you estimate it in these long days, and then pray."

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "'Isa the son of Maryam will then be among my community as a just judge and an equitable leader. He will break the cross, kill the pig [variant in D and A: "slaughter"], abolish the jizyah, and leave the zakat, so that no one will go to collect it for a sheep or a camel. Rancour and hatred will be removed, and the venom of every venomous creature will be extracted, so that a child can put his hand into a snake without being harmed, and a young girl can drive off a lion without it harming her. The wolf will be among the sheep as if it were their dog, and the earth will be filled with peace as a vessel is filled with water. The word will be one, so none will be worshipped but Allah. War will lay down its burdens, Quraysh will be stripped of its kingdom, and the earth will be like a silver platter, producing its plants as in the time of Adam, so that a group of people will gather over a bunch of grapes and it will satisfy them, and a group will gather over a pomegranate and it will satisfy them. A bull will cost so-and-so much in wealth, and a horse will be sold for a few dirhams."

It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, what will make the horse cheap?" He said: "It will never be ridden for war." It was said to him: "What will make the bull expensive?" He said: "The whole earth will be ploughed."

Before the emergence of the Dajjal there will be three years of severe hardship, during which people will suffer intense hunger. In the first year Allah will command the sky to withhold a third of its rain, and He will command the earth to withhold a third of its produce. Then He will command the sky in the second year to withhold two-thirds of its rain, and He will command the earth to withhold two-thirds of its produce. Then Allah will command the sky in the third year [addition from D, R and Ibn Majah] to withhold all its rain, so that not a drop falls, and He will command the earth to withhold all its produce, so that nothing green grows. No hoofed animal will remain but it will perish, except what Allah wills."

It was said: "Then how will people survive in that time?" He said: "By tahlil, takbir, tasbih and tahmid, and this will take the place of food for them."

Ibn Majah said: I heard Abu al-Hasan al-Tanafisi say: I heard 'Abd al-Rahman al-Muharibi say: "This hadith should be given to the teacher, so that he may teach it to the children in the kuttab."

This is a very strange hadith from this route, but parts of it have corroborating reports from other hadiths. We shall mention here the hadith of al-Nawwas ibn Sam'an, because of its resemblance in context to this hadith. Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj said in his Sahih:

Abu Khaythamah Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to us: al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Yazid ibn Jabir narrated to me: Yahya ibn Jabir al-Ta'i, judge of Homs, narrated to me: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr narrated to me, from his father Jubayr ibn Nufayr al-Hadrami, that he heard al-Nawwas ibn Sam'an al-Kilabi (ḥ). And Muhammad ibn Mihran al-Razzi narrated to us: al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Yazid ibn Jabir narrated to us, from Yahya ibn Jabir al-Ta'i, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr, from his father Jubayr ibn Nufayr, from al-Nawwas ibn Sam'an, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) mentioned the Dajjal one morning, lowering and raising his voice about him, until we thought he was in a grove of palm trees. When we went to him, he perceived that in us and said: 'What is wrong with you?' We said: 'O Messenger of Allah, you mentioned the Dajjal this morning, lowering and raising your voice, until we thought he was in a grove of palms.' He said: 'What I fear for you is other than the Dajjal. If he emerges while I am among you, then I will be your opponent in argument on your behalf. If he emerges while I am not among you, then each man will have to argue for himself, and Allah will be my successor over every Muslim. He is a young man with curly hair, his eye bulging out. I liken him to 'Abd al-'Uzza ibn Qatan. Whoever of you meets him should recite over him the opening verses of Surat al-Kahf. He will emerge from a valley between Syria and Iraq and will spread corruption to the right and to the left. O servants of Allah, stand firm!'" We said: "O Messenger of Allah, how long will he remain on earth?" He said: "Forty days: one day is like a year, one day is like a month, one day is like a week, and the rest of his days are like your days."

We said: "O Messenger of Allah, will the day that is like a year be enough for us to pray one day's prayers in it?" He said: "No, estimate its proper measure." We said: "O Messenger of Allah, how fast will he travel on the earth?" He said: "Like rain driven on by the wind. He will come to a people and call them, and they will believe in him and respond to him. He will command the sky and it will rain, and the earth and it will grow, and their grazing animals will return to them with their humps at their longest, their udders at their fullest, and their flanks at their largest. Then he will come to another people and call them, but they will reject his words, and he will depart from them. They will awake in drought, with nothing of their wealth left in their hands. He will pass by a ruin and say to it: 'Bring out your treasures,' and its treasures will follow him like swarms of bees. Then he will call a young man, full of youth, and strike him with a sword, cutting him into two pieces as far apart as the distance of an archery target. Then he will call him, and he will come forward with a face radiant and smiling. While he is doing this, Allah will send the Messiah, the son of Maryam (peace be upon him), who will descend at the white minaret east of Damascus, between two yellow garments, placing his palms on the wings of two angels. When he lowers his head, drops fall, and when he raises it, pearls like beads of light fall from it. No disbeliever who smells his breath will live, and his breath will reach as far as his sight. He will pursue the Dajjal until he overtakes him at the gate of Ludd and kills him."

Then 'Isa (peace be upon him) will come to a people whom Allah has protected from him, and he will wipe their faces and tell them of their ranks in Paradise. While he is doing this, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will reveal to 'Isa: "I have brought out servants of Mine whom no one has the power to fight. So take My servants to Mount Tur."

Allah will send forth Ya'juj and Ma'juj, "and they will swarm down from every mound" [Q 21:96]. The first of them will pass by the lake of Tiberias and drink all its water, and when the last of them passes, they will say: "There was once water here." The Prophet of Allah, 'Isa, and his companions will be besieged, until the head of a bull will be more valuable to one of them than a hundred dinars is to any of you today. The Prophet of Allah, 'Isa, and his companions will supplicate, and Allah will send a worm upon their necks, and they will die in the same instant, like one soul.

Then the Prophet of Allah, 'Isa, and his companions will descend to the earth, and they will find no spot of a hand's breadth on the earth that is not filled with their fat and stench. The Prophet of Allah, 'Isa, and his companions will turn to Allah, and Allah will send birds like the necks of Bukht camels, which will carry them and cast them wherever Allah wills.

Then Allah will send rain that no house of clay or wool can keep out, and it will wash the earth until it leaves it like a mirror. Then it will be said to the earth: "Bring forth your fruit and restore your blessing." On that day a group will eat from one pomegranate and shelter under its peel, and Allah will bless the milk, so that a she-camel in milk will suffice a large band of people, and a she-camel's milk will suffice a clan. While they are in this state, Allah will send a good wind which will take them under their armpits, and it will take the soul of every believer and every Muslim. The worst of people will remain, copulating in public like donkeys, and upon them the Hour will be established."

[Sahih Muslim, no. 2137; al-Musnad 4/182; Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 4321; Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 2240; al-Sunan al-Kubra of al-Nasa'i, no. 10783; Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 4075.]

Imam Ahmad and the authors of the Sunan also narrated it through 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Yazid ibn Jabir, with the same chain. We shall also mention it through Ahmad's route when we reach Allah's words in Surat al-Anbiya': ﴿Until, when Gog and Magog are released, and they swarm down from every mound﴾ [al-Anbiya' 21:96]. [Addition from R and A; in H: "the verse".]

Another hadith: Muslim also said in his Sahih: Ubayd Allah [in some copies: "Abd Allah"] ibn Mu'adh ibn Mu'adh al-'Anbari narrated to us, my father narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from al-Nu'man ibn Salim, who said: I heard Ya'qub ibn 'Asim ibn 'Urwah ibn Mas'ud al-Thaqafi saying: I heard 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, and a man came to him and said: "What is this hadith that you narrate, that you say: 'The Hour will be established at such and such'?" He said: "Subhan Allah! Or: La ilaha illa Allah, or a similar phrase! I had almost resolved never to narrate anything to anyone ever again. I only said: 'You will soon see a great matter: the House will be burned, and such and such will happen.'" Then he said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The Dajjal (the Antichrist) will emerge among my ummah (community) and will remain forty, I do not know whether forty days, or forty months, or forty years. Then Allah the Exalted will send 'Isa ibn Maryam (Jesus, son of Mary), who will resemble 'Urwah ibn Mas'ud. He will seek him out and destroy him. Then the people will remain for seven years with no enmity between any two. Then Allah will send a cold wind from the direction of al-Sham (the Levant), and there will not remain on the face of the earth anyone who has in his heart even an atom's weight of good [in some copies: "a grain of mustard"] or faith, except that it will take him, until if one of you were to enter into the core of a mountain, it would enter after him until it takes him." He said: I heard it from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He (ﷺ) said: "Then the worst of people will remain, with the lightness of birds and the minds of beasts, not recognising good nor denouncing evil. Then Satan will appear to them and say: 'Will you not respond?' They will say: 'What do you command us?' He will command them to worship idols, and they will be in that state with abundant provision and good living. Then the Trumpet will be blown, and no one who hears it will fail to incline his neck and raise it. He said: The first to hear it will be a man who is repairing the water trough of his camels. He said: He will swoon, and the people will swoon. Then Allah will send down [or: He said, will cause to descend] rain like dew, or like shade [he was in doubt, al-Nu'man], and from it the bodies of the people will grow. Then it will be blown into a second time, and behold, they will be standing, looking. Then it will be said: 'O people, come to your Lord,' and: ﴿Stop them, for they are to be questioned﴾ [al-Saffat: 24]." He (ﷺ) said: "Then it will be said: 'Bring forth the portion of the Fire.' It will be said: 'From how many?' It will be said: 'From every thousand, nine hundred and ninety-nine.'" He said: ﴿That will make the children grey-haired﴾ [al-Muzzammil: 17], and that is ﴿the Day when the shin will be uncovered﴾ [al-Qalam: 42].

Then Muslim and al-Nasa'i in his Tafsir both narrated it together from Muhammad ibn Bashshar, from Ghundar, from Shu'bah, from al-Nu'man ibn Salim, with the same chain. [Sahih Muslim no. (2940) and Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra no. (11629).]

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Ubayd Allah [in some copies: "Ubayd Allah ibn 'Abd Allah"] ibn Ta'labah al-Ansari, from 'Abd Allah ibn Yazid [in one copy: Zayd] al-Ansari, from Mujammi' ibn Jariyah [in one copy: "Harithah"], who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "The son of Maryam will kill the Masih (Messiah) al-Dajjal at the gate of Lud" [or: "beside Lud"]. [Al-Musnad (3/420).]

Ahmad also narrated it from Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah, from the hadith of al-Layth and al-Awza'i, all three from al-Zuhri, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Ubayd Allah ibn Ta'labah, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Yazid, from his paternal uncle Mujammi' ibn Jariyah [in one copy: "Harithah"], from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "The son of Maryam will kill al-Dajjal at the gate of Lud."

Similarly al-Tirmidhi narrated it from Qutaybah, from al-Layth, with the same chain, and said: "This is a sahih hadith." He said: "On this topic there are also narrations from 'Imran ibn Husayn, Nafi' ibn 'Utbah, Abu Barzah, Hudhayfah ibn Usayd, Abu Hurayrah, Kaysan, 'Uthman ibn Abi al-'As, Jabir, Abu Umamah, Ibn Mas'ud, 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, Samurah ibn Jundub, al-Nawwas ibn Sam'an, 'Amr ibn 'Awf, and Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman, may Allah be pleased with them [in one copy: "may Allah be pleased with them all"]." [Al-Musnad (3/420) and Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (2244).]

The purpose of the narrations of these people is what contains mention of al-Dajjal and the killing of him by 'Isa ibn Maryam, peace be upon him. As for the hadiths mentioning only al-Dajjal, they are very numerous, more than can be counted, due to their wide circulation and the abundance of their narrators in the Sahih, Hasan and Musnad collections and elsewhere. [The author, the Hafiz Ibn Kathir, mentioned these hadiths and discussed them at length in his book: al-Nihayah fi al-Fitan wa al-Malahim.]

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Sufyan narrated to us, from Furat, from Abu al-Tufayl, from Hudhayfah ibn Usayd al-Ghifari, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) looked down upon us from an upper room while we were discussing the Hour, and he said: "The Hour will not be established until you see ten signs: the rising of the sun from its west, the smoke, the Beast, the emergence of Ya'juj and Ma'juj (Gog and Magog), the descent of 'Isa ibn Maryam, the Dajjal, and three eclipses: an eclipse in the East, an eclipse in the West, and an eclipse in the Arabian Peninsula. And a fire will emerge from the bottom of 'Adan, driving [or: gathering] the people; it will spend the night with them wherever they spend the night, and rest at noon with them wherever they rest."

Thus it was narrated by Muslim and the authors of the Sunan from the hadith of Furat al-Qazzaz, with the same chain. [Al-Musnad (4/6), with a different wording; this is the wording of Ibn Mahdi's narration from Sufyan, found in al-Musnad (4/7). Also narrated by Muslim in his Sahih no. (2901), Abu Dawud in al-Sunan no. (4311), al-Tirmidhi in al-Sunan no. (2183), and Ibn Majah in al-Sunan no. (4055).] Muslim also narrated it from the narration of 'Abd al-Aziz ibn Rufay' from Abu al-Tufayl, from Abu Sarihah Hudhayfah ibn Usayd al-Ghifari, as a mawquf (ending with a companion) report. [Sahih Muslim no. (2901).] And Allah knows best.

These are mutawatir (widely transmitted) hadiths from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), narrated through Abu Hurayrah, Ibn Mas'ud, 'Uthman ibn Abi al-'As, Abu Umamah, al-Nawwas ibn Sam'an, 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As, Mujammi' ibn Jariyah [in one copy: "Harithah"], Abu Sarihah and Hudhayfah ibn Usayd, may Allah be pleased with them.

In them is evidence of the manner and place of his descent: that it is in al-Sham (the Levant), indeed in Damascus, at the eastern minaret. And that this will occur at the time of the call to the dawn prayer [in another copy: "at the iqamah (second call) for the dawn prayer"]. In these times, in the year 741 AH, a white minaret was built for the Umayyad Mosque, of carved stone, in place of the minaret that was destroyed by the fire attributed to the handiwork of the Christians, may the continuous curses of Allah be upon them until the Day of Resurrection. Most of its construction was funded by their wealth. Strong suspicions arose that it is the one upon which 'Isa ibn Maryam (the Messiah), peace be upon him, will descend, and will kill the pig, break the cross, and abolish the jizyah (poll tax), accepting nothing but Islam, as has passed in the two Sahihs. This is an announcement from the Prophet (ﷺ) of that, and an affirmation, legislation and permission for it in that time, when their defects will be removed and their doubts lifted from their souls. For this reason, all of them will enter the religion of Islam, following 'Isa, peace be upon him, and at his hands. For this reason Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And there is none of the People of the Scripture but that he will surely believe in him before his death, and on the Day of Resurrection he will be a witness against them﴾ [Ibn Kathir's addition: "And on the Day of Resurrection he will be a witness against them."].

This verse is like His saying: ﴿And indeed, it is a sign [ilm] for the Hour﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 61]. It is also read as "'alam" with a vowel on the first letter, meaning a sign and an indication of the nearness of the Hour. That is because he will descend after the emergence of the Messiah al-Dajjal, and Allah will kill him at his hands, as is established in the Sahih: "Allah has not sent down any disease except that He has sent down its cure." [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (5678), from Abu Hurayrah, with the wording: "Allah has not sent down any disease except that He has sent down its cure."] In his time, Allah will send forth Ya'juj and Ma'juj, and Allah will destroy them through the blessing of his supplication. Allah the Exalted has said: ﴿Until, when Gog and Magog are released, and they swarm from every elevated place. And the true promise draws near﴾ [al-Anbiya': 96-97], and the verse continues.

The description of 'Isa, peace be upon him:

It has already passed in the hadith of 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Adam, from Abu Hurayrah [may Allah be pleased with him]: "When you see him, recognise him: a man of medium height, inclining to redness and whiteness, wearing two garments dyed with saffron, as if his head were dripping, though no water has touched it." In the hadith of al-Nawwas ibn Sam'an: "He will descend at the white minaret east of Damascus, between two garments of saffron, placing his palms upon the wings of two angels. When he lowers his head, drops fall from it, and when he raises it, there flows from it like pearls of jewels. No disbeliever who smells his breath will be allowed to live, and his breath reaches as far as his gaze reaches."

Al-Bukhari and Muslim narrated, through the chain of al-Zuhri, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "On the night I was taken on the Night Journey, I met Musa (Moses)," and he described him: "Behold, a man, I think he said, [who was] agitated, curly-haired, as if he were one of the men of Shanu'ah." He said: "And I met 'Isa," and the Prophet (ﷺ) described him: "Of medium height, reddish, as if he had just come out of a bathhouse (dimas, meaning the hammam). And I saw Ibrahim, and I am the most similar of his offspring to him." [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (3437) and Sahih Muslim no. (168)]... the hadith.

Al-Bukhari narrated, from the hadith of Mujahid, from Ibn 'Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I saw Musa, 'Isa and Ibrahim. As for 'Isa, he is reddish, curly-haired, broad-chested. As for Musa, he is dark-skinned, tall, straight-haired, as if he were one of the men of al-Zutt." [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (3438). Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar, in Fath al-Bari (6/484), held that the correct attribution is from Ibn 'Abbas, not Ibn 'Umar, so refer there.]

And al-Bukhari and Muslim also narrated from the route of Musa ibn 'Uqbah, from Nafi', who said: 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar said: One day the Prophet (ﷺ) mentioned the Masih al-Dajjal among the people and said: "Allah is not one-eyed. Behold, the Masih al-Dajjal is blind in the right eye, as if his eye were a floating grape. Allah showed me at the Ka'bah in a dream: a man, brown-skinned, the best-looking brown-skinned man you have ever seen, with his hair hanging between his shoulders, straight-haired, water dripping from his head, placing his hands on the shoulders of two men, and he was circumambulating the House. I asked: 'Who is this?' They said: 'The Masih, son of Maryam.' Then I saw behind him a man, curly-haired, tightly curled, blind in the right eye, most resembling Ibn Qatan whom I have seen, placing his hands on the shoulders of a man circumambulating the House. I asked: 'Who is this?' They said: 'The Masih al-Dajjal.'" 'Ubayd Allah narrated the same from Nafi'. [Sahih al-Bukhari nos. (3439, 3440) and Sahih Muslim no. (169).]

Then al-Bukhari narrated it from Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Makki, from Ibrahim ibn Sa'd, from al-Zuhri, from Salim, from his father, who said: "No, by Allah, the Prophet (ﷺ) did not say that 'Isa was red. Rather he said: 'While I was sleeping, I was circumambulating the Ka'bah, and behold, a man, brown-skinned, straight-haired, being supported between two men, water dripping from his head or his head pouring water. I asked: "Who is this?" They said: "The son of Maryam." I turned to look, and behold, a red, tall man, curly-haired, blind in his right eye, as if his eye were a floating grape. I asked: "Who is this?" They said: "The Dajjal." And the closest person to him in resemblance is Ibn Qatan.'" Al-Zuhri said: He was a man from Khuza'ah who died in the pre-Islamic period. [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (3441).]

These are all the words of al-Bukhari (may Allah have mercy on him). It has already been mentioned in the hadith of Abd al-Rahman ibn Adam from Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him) that Isa (peace be upon him), after his descent to the earth, will remain on the earth for forty years, and then he will die and the Muslims will pray over him.

In the hadith of Abd Allah ibn Amr in Muslim, it is narrated that he will remain for seven years. So it is possible, and Allah knows best, that what is meant by his staying on the earth for forty years is the total of his residence there before his being raised up and after his descent, for he was raised up when he was thirty-three years old, according to the Sahih (the authentic collection). This is also mentioned in a hadith describing the people of Paradise: that they will be upon the form of Adam, and that the age of Isa at his birth was thirty-three years.

As for what Ibn Asakir related from some scholars, that he was raised up when he was one hundred and fifty years old, it is anomalous, strange and far-fetched.

The hafiz Abu al-Qasim ibn Asakir mentioned in the biography of Isa ibn Maryam in his History, from some of the early generation (salaf), that he will be buried with the Prophet (ﷺ) in his chamber. Allah knows best.
[Tarikh Dimashq (14/106, manuscript) and Mukhtasar Tarikh Dimashq by Ibn Manzur (20/154), with its chain of narration going back to Abd Allah ibn Salam (may Allah be pleased with him). Al-Bukhari said: "This is not authentic according to me, and no one corroborates it."]

* *

As for the Most High's saying: ﴿And on the Day of Resurrection he will be a witness against them﴾, Qatadah said: He will testify against them that he had conveyed the message of Allah to them, and that he acknowledged servanthood to Allah, Mighty and Majestic. This is like His saying, Most High, at the end of Surah al-Ma'idah: ﴿And when Allah says, "O Isa, son of Maryam, did you say to the people, 'Take me and my mother as two gods besides Allah'?" He will say, "Glory be to You, it is not for me to say what I have no right to. If I had said it, You would have known it. You know what is in my soul, and I do not know what is in Your soul.
