Indeed, You, You are the Knower of the unseen. I did not tell them except what You commanded me: 'Worship Allah, my Lord and your Lord.' And I was a witness over them while I was among them; but when You caused me to die, You were the Watcher over them, and You are Witness over all things. If You punish them, indeed they are Your servants; and if You forgive them, indeed You, You are the Exalted in Might, the Wise.'﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 116–118]

Ibn Kathir, *Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim*, on Surah 4, verses 160–162:

He, exalted is He, informs that, because of the wrongdoing of the Jews and the great sins they committed, He forbade them good things that He had previously made lawful for them. As Ibn Abi Hatim said:

Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Yazid al-Muqri narrated to us: Sufyan ibn 'Uyayna narrated to us, from 'Amr, and said: Ibn 'Abbas recited: "good things that had been made lawful for them."

This prohibition may be *qadari* (divinely decreed), meaning that God allowed them to distort and alter in their Book things that had been lawful for them, and they then forbade these to themselves, out of excessive strictness toward themselves, constriction, and extremism (*tanaqqu'*). It may also be *shar'i* (legislated), meaning that God forbade them in the Torah things that had been lawful for them before that, as He says: ﴿All food was lawful to the Children of Israel, except what Israel made unlawful for himself before the Torah was revealed﴾ [Al 'Imran: 93]. We have already discussed this verse, and the meaning is that all foods had been lawful for them before the Torah was revealed, except what Israel (Ya'qub) had forbidden himself, namely the flesh and milk of camels. Then God forbade many things in the Torah, as He says in Surah al-An'am: ﴿And for those who were Jews We forbade every animal with claws. And of cattle and sheep We forbade them their fat, except what their backs carry or the entrails or what is mixed with bone. That was their recompense for their rebellion. And indeed, We are truthful﴾ [Al-An'am: 146]. That is, We forbade them this only because they deserved it through their rebellion, their transgression, their opposition to their messenger, and their disputing with him. For this reason He says: ﴿For the wrongdoing of those who were Jews, We forbade them good things that had been lawful for them, and for their hindering many from the way of God﴾. That is, they turned people away and turned themselves away from following the truth. This was their disposition, which they have characterized since ancient times and in recent times. For this reason they were enemies of the messengers, killed a number of the prophets, and denied both 'Isa and Muhammad, may the blessings and peace of God be upon them both.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿and their taking of usury, although they had been forbidden from it﴾, that is, God had forbidden them usury, yet they engaged in it and took it, and they devised various tricks and forms of pretext to get around it, and they consumed people's wealth falsely. He says: ﴿And We have prepared for the disbelievers among them a painful punishment﴾.

Then He says: ﴿But those firm in knowledge among them﴾, that is, those established in the religion, who have firm footing in beneficial knowledge. This matter has already been discussed in Surah Al 'Imran.

﴿And the believers﴾ is a conjunction (*'atf*) on "those firm in knowledge," and its predicate is ﴿believe in what has been revealed to you and what was revealed before you﴾.

Ibn 'Abbas said: It was revealed concerning 'Abdullah ibn Salam, Tha'laba ibn Sa'ya, Asad and Zayd ibn Sa'ya, and Asad ibn 'Ubayd, who entered Islam and affirmed what God sent Muhammad (ﷺ) with.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿and those who establish prayer﴾, it is written this way in all the standard codices, and likewise in the codex of Ubayy ibn Ka'b. Ibn Jarir mentioned that in the codex of Ibn Mas'ud it reads: "and those who establish prayer" (*wal-muqimuna al-salah*), and he said: The correct view is the recitation of all of them. Then he refuted those who claimed that this was an error of the scribes. Then he mentioned the differences of opinion among people. Some said: It is in the accusative (*nasb*) by way of praise, as in His saying: ﴿and those who fulfill their covenant when they make one, and the patient in misfortune and hardship and in the time of battle; those are the ones who have been true﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 177]. They said: This is permissible in Arabic speech, as the poet said:

"Let not my people be far away, those who are
the poison of the enemies and the ruin of the ... ,
Those who alight in every battle,
and who are the best at tying the knots of the loincloths."

Others said: It is in the genitive (*khafd*) by conjunction with His saying: ﴿in what has been revealed to you and what was revealed before you﴾, meaning: and in those who establish prayer.

It is as if he is saying: and in the establishment of prayer, that is, they acknowledge its obligation and that it has been prescribed for them. Or it may be that what is meant by "those who establish prayer" are the angels. This is the view preferred by Ibn Jarir, meaning: they believe in what has been revealed to you, what was revealed before you, and in the angels. But this is open to question, and God knows best.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿and those who give zakah﴾, it may mean the zakah on wealth, it may mean the purification of souls, or it may include both, and God knows best.

﴿And those who believe in God and the Last Day﴾, that is, they affirm that there is no god but God, and they believe in resurrection after death and in recompense for deeds, whether good or evil.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿those﴾, it is the predicate for what came before. ﴿We will give them a great reward﴾, that is, Paradise.

Ibn Kathir, *Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim*, on Surah 4, verses 160–162:

He, exalted is He, informs that, because of the wrongdoing of the Jews and the great sins they committed, He forbade them good things that He had previously made lawful for them. As Ibn Abi Hatim said:

Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Yazid al-Muqri narrated to us: Sufyan ibn 'Uyayna narrated to us, from 'Amr, and said: Ibn 'Abbas recited: "good things that had been made lawful for them."

This prohibition may be *qadari* (divinely decreed), meaning that God allowed them to distort and alter in their Book things that had been lawful for them, and they then forbade these to themselves, out of excessive strictness toward themselves, constriction, and extremism (*tanaqqu'*). It may also be *shar'i* (legislated), meaning that God forbade them in the Torah things that had been lawful for them before that, as He says: ﴿All food was lawful to the Children of Israel, except what Israel made unlawful for himself before the Torah was revealed﴾ [Al 'Imran: 93]. We have already discussed this verse, and the meaning is that all foods had been lawful for them before the Torah was revealed, except what Israel (Ya'qub) had forbidden himself, namely the flesh and milk of camels. Then God forbade many things in the Torah, as He says in Surah al-An'am: ﴿And for those who were Jews We forbade every animal with claws. And of cattle and sheep We forbade them their fat, except what their backs carry or the entrails or what is mixed with bone. That was their recompense for their rebellion. And indeed, We are truthful﴾ [Al-An'am: 146]. That is, We forbade them this only because they deserved it through their rebellion, their transgression, their opposition to their messenger, and their disputing with him. For this reason He says: ﴿For the wrongdoing of those who were Jews, We forbade them good things that had been lawful for them, and for their hindering many from the way of God﴾. That is, they turned people away and turned themselves away from following the truth. This was their disposition, which they have characterized since ancient times and in recent times. For this reason they were enemies of the messengers, killed a number of the prophets, and denied both 'Isa and Muhammad, may the blessings and peace of God be upon them both.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿and their taking of usury, although they had been forbidden from it﴾, that is, God had forbidden them usury, yet they engaged in it and took it, and they devised various tricks and forms of pretext to get around it, and they consumed people's wealth falsely. He says: ﴿And We have prepared for the disbelievers among them a painful punishment﴾.

Then He says: ﴿But those firm in knowledge among them﴾, that is, those established in the religion, who have firm footing in beneficial knowledge. This matter has already been discussed in Surah Al 'Imran.

﴿And the believers﴾ is a conjunction (*'atf*) on "those firm in knowledge," and its predicate is ﴿believe in what has been revealed to you and what was revealed before you﴾.

Ibn 'Abbas said: It was revealed concerning 'Abdullah ibn Salam, Tha'laba ibn Sa'ya, Asad and Zayd ibn Sa'ya, and Asad ibn 'Ubayd, who entered Islam and affirmed what God sent Muhammad (ﷺ) with.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿and those who establish prayer﴾, it is written this way in all the standard codices, and likewise in the codex of Ubayy ibn Ka'b. Ibn Jarir mentioned that in the codex of Ibn Mas'ud it reads: "and those who establish prayer" (*wal-muqimuna al-salah*), and he said: The correct view is the recitation of all of them. Then he refuted those who claimed that this was an error of the scribes. Then he mentioned the differences of opinion among people. Some said: It is in the accusative (*nasb*) by way of praise, as in His saying: ﴿and those who fulfill their covenant when they make one, and the patient in misfortune and hardship and in the time of battle; those are the ones who have been true﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 177]. They said: This is permissible in Arabic speech, as the poet said:

"Let not my people be far away, those who are
the poison of the enemies and the ruin of the ... ,
Those who alight in every battle,
and who are the best at tying the knots of the loincloths."

Others said: It is in the genitive (*khafd*) by conjunction with His saying: ﴿in what has been revealed to you and what was revealed before you﴾, meaning: and in those who establish prayer.

It is as if he is saying: and in the establishment of prayer, that is, they acknowledge its obligation and that it has been prescribed for them. Or it may be that what is meant by "those who establish prayer" are the angels. This is the view preferred by Ibn Jarir, meaning: they believe in what has been revealed to you, what was revealed before you, and in the angels. But this is open to question, and God knows best.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿and those who give zakah﴾, it may mean the zakah on wealth, it may mean the purification of souls, or it may include both, and God knows best.

﴿And those who believe in God and the Last Day﴾, that is, they affirm that there is no god but God, and they believe in resurrection after death and in recompense for deeds, whether good or evil.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿those﴾, it is the predicate for what came before. ﴿We will give them a great reward﴾, that is, Paradise.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 4, verse 163–165 (part 1 of 3):

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said, from Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, from Ikrimah or Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Sukayn and 'Adi ibn Zayd said: "O Muhammad, we do not know that God has sent down anything to a human being after Moses." So God revealed in response to their words: ﴿Indeed, We have revealed to you as We revealed to Noah and the prophets after him﴾, to the end of the verses.

Ibn Jarir said: al-Harith narrated to us, 'Abd al-'Aziz narrated to us, Abu Ma'shar narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, who said: God revealed: ﴿The People of the Book ask you to bring down to them a Book from heaven﴾, to His words ﴿and their saying against Mary a tremendous slander﴾. So he (the Prophet) recited it to them, meaning to the Jews, and informed them of their wicked deeds. They denied everything God had sent down and said: "God has not sent down anything to a human being, neither to Moses nor to Jesus, nor to any prophet." He said: So he (the Prophet) became angry and said: "Nor to anyone." Then God, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿They did not esteem God with the esteem due to Him when they said, "God has not sent down anything to a human being"﴾ [al-An'am: 91].

Concerning what Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi said, there is an objection: this verse is Meccan in Surah al-An'am, whereas this verse in Surah an-Nisa' is Medinan, and it is a response to them when they asked the Prophet ﷺ to bring down to them a Book from heaven. God the Exalted said: ﴿They asked Moses for greater than that﴾ [an-Nisa': 153]. Then He mentioned their disgraces, their faults, what they were upon, and what they are upon now of lying and fabrication. Then He mentioned that He revealed to His servant and messenger Muhammad ﷺ just as He revealed to the other earlier prophets, saying: ﴿Indeed, We have revealed to you as We revealed to Noah and the prophets after him, and We revealed to Abraham and Ishmael and Isaac and Jacob and the Descendants and Jesus and Job and Jonah and Aaron and Solomon, and We gave David the Psalms﴾.

Az-Zabur: it is the name of the Book that God revealed to David, peace be upon him. We will mention the biography of each of these prophets, may the most excellent of God's blessings and peace be upon them, when recounting their stories in the coming surahs, if God wills. And in Him is trust, and upon Him is reliance.

* *

His saying ﴿And messengers We have related to you before, and messengers We have not related to you﴾, meaning: before this verse, i.e., in the Meccan surahs and others.

These are the names of the prophets whose names are specified in the Qur'an: Adam, Idris, Noah, Hud, Salih, Abraham, Lot, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, Joseph, Job, Shu'ayb, Moses, Aaron, Jonah, David, Solomon, Elias, Elisha, Zechariah, John, and Jesus, peace be upon them; and likewise Dhul-Kifl according to many exegetes; and their master is Muhammad ﷺ.

* *

His saying: ﴿And messengers We have not related to you﴾, meaning: other created beings not mentioned in the Qur'an. The number of prophets and messengers has been disputed, and the most well-known in this regard is the lengthy hadith of Abu Dharr, as narrated by Ibn Mardawayh, may God have mercy on him, in his Tafsir, where he said: Ibrahim ibn Muhammad narrated to us, Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan and al-Husayn ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Yazid narrated to us, both saying: Ibrahim ibn Hisham ibn Yahya al-Ghassani narrated to us, my father narrated to me from my grandfather, from Abu Idris al-Khawlani, from Abu Dharr, who said: I said: "O Messenger of God, how many are the prophets?" He said: "One hundred and twenty-four thousand." I said: "O Messenger of God, how many of them are messengers?" He said: "Three hundred and thirteen, a great throng." I said: "O Messenger of God, who was the first of them?" He said: "Adam." I said: "O Messenger of God, was he a prophet and messenger?" He said: "Yes, God created him with His own hand, breathed into him of His spirit, then formed him directly." Then he said: "O Abu Dharr, four are Syriac: Adam, Seth, Noah, and Kanukh—who is Idris, and he was the first to write with a pen—and four are Arabs: Hud, Salih, Shu'ayb, and your Prophet, O Abu Dharr. The first of the prophets of the Children of Israel was Moses, and the last of them was Jesus. The first of the prophets was Adam, and the last of them is your Prophet."

This hadith in its entirety was narrated by the Hafiz Abu Hatim Ibn Hibban al-Busti in his book "al-Anwa' wa'l-Taqasim," and he graded it as sound. Ibn al-Jawzi disagreed with him, mentioning this hadith in his book "al-Mawdu'at" (Fabricated Hadiths), and accused Ibrahim ibn Hisham of fabricating it. There is no doubt that more than one of the imams of criticism and authentication spoke about him because of this hadith [Sahih Ibn Hibban, no. (94) "Mawarid"; Abu Nu'aym narrated it in al-Hilyah (1/166) through the route of Ibrahim ibn Hisham ibn Yahya with the same chain.
Ibrahim ibn Hisham al-Ghassani was declared a liar by Abu Hatim and Abu Zur'ah, and al-Dhahabi said: "He is the transmitter of the lengthy hadith of Abu Dharr; he alone narrated it from his father from his grandfather."]. And God knows best.

This hadith has also been narrated through another route, from a different Companion. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn 'Awf narrated to us, Abu al-Mughirah narrated to us, Mu'an ibn Rifa'ah narrated to us, from 'Ali ibn Yazid, from al-Qasim, from Abu Umamah, who said: I said: "O Prophet of God, how many are the prophets?" He said: "One hundred and twenty-four thousand, of whom three hundred and fifteen are a great throng."

Mu'an ibn Rifa'ah al-Salami is weak, 'Ali ibn Yazid is weak, and al-Qasim Abu 'Abd al-Rahman is also weak [mentioned by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur (2/746)].

The Hafiz Abu Ya'la al-Mawsili said: Ahmad ibn Ishaq Abu 'Abd Allah al-Jawhari al-Basri narrated to us, Makki ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Musa ibn 'Ubaydah al-Rabadhi narrated to us, from Yazid al-Raqqashi, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "God sent eight thousand prophets: four thousand to the Children of Israel, and four thousand to the rest of mankind."

This is also a weak chain, in which al-Rabadhi is weak, and his teacher al-Raqqashi is weaker still [Musnad Abi Ya'la (7/160); Abu Nu'aym narrated it in al-Hilyah (3/53) through the route of Makki ibn Ibrahim; al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (8/210): "In it is Musa ibn 'Ubaydah al-Rabadhi, who is very weak."]. And God knows best.

Abu Ya'la also said: Abu al-Rabi' narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Thabit al-'Abdi narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Ansari narrated to us, from Yazid al-Raqqashi, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "Among my brothers among the prophets who passed away were eight thousand prophets, then came Jesus son of Mary, then I." [Musnad Abi Ya'la (7/131); al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (8/211): "In it is Muhammad ibn Thabit al-'Abdi, who is weak."]

We have also narrated it from Anas through another route: al-Hafiz Abu 'Abd Allah al-Dhahabi informed us, Abu al-Fadl ibn 'Asakir informed us, Imam Abu Bakr al-Qasim ibn Abi Sa'id al-Saffar informed us, my paternal aunt 'A'ishah bint Ahmad ibn Mansur ibn al-Saffar informed us, al-Sharif Abu al-Sanabik Hibat Allah ibn Abi al-Sahba' Muhammad ibn Haydar al-Qurashi informed us, Imam al-Ustadh Abu Ishaq al-Isfara'ini said: Imam Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Isma'ili informed us, Muhammad ibn 'Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, Ahmad ibn Tariq narrated to us, Muslim ibn Khalid narrated to us, Ziyad ibn Sa'd narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Safwan ibn Sulaym, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "I was sent after three thousand prophets from the Children of Israel." This is strange from this route, and its chain is acceptable; all its narrators are known except this Ahmad ibn Tariq, for I do not know him to be either trustworthy or defective [narrated by Abu Nu'aym in al-Hilyah (3/162) through the route of Muslim ibn Khalid al-Zanji, and he said: "Strange."]. And God knows best.

The lengthy hadith of Abu Dharr al-Ghifari concerning the number of the prophets, peace be upon them:

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 4, verses 163–165 (part 2 of 3):

Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Ajurri said: Abu Bakr Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn al-Firyabi narrated to us by dictation in the month of Rajab, in the year 297 AH. Ibrahim ibn Hisham ibn Yahya al-Ghassani narrated to us, my father narrated to us, from his grandfather, from Abu Idris al-Khawlani, from Abu Dharr, who said: I entered the mosque and found the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sitting alone, so I sat down with him and said: "O Messenger of Allah, you commanded me to pray." He said: "Prayer is the best of undertakings, so increase it or reduce it." He said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, which deed is best?" He said: "Belief in Allah and striving (jihad) in His cause." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, which of the believers is best?" He said: "The one with the best character." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, which of the Muslims is the most secure (from harm)?" He said: "The one from whose tongue and hand people are safe." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, which migration is best?" He said: "The one who abandons evil deeds." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, which prayer is best?" He said: "Lengthy standing (qunut)." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, which fasting is best?" He said: "An obligatory fast that is sufficient, and with Allah there are many multiples." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, which jihad is best?" He said: "The one whose mount is hamstrung and whose blood is shed." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, which slaves (freed) are best?" He said: "The most expensive in price and the most precious to their owners." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, which charity is best?" He said: "Effort from one who has little, and secret giving to a poor person." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, which verse of what was revealed to you is the greatest?" He said: "The Verse of the Throne (Ayat al-Kursi)." Then he said: "O Abu Dharr, the seven heavens compared to the Kursi are nothing but a ring thrown down in a desert, and the excellence of the Throne over the Kursi is like the excellence of the desert over the ring." He said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, how many prophets are there?" He said: "One hundred and twenty-four thousand." He said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, how many of them were messengers?" He said: "Three hundred and thirteen, a great, abundant, numerous, good company." I said: "Who was the first of them?" He said: "Adam." I said: "Was he a prophet sent (with a message)?" He said: "Yes, Allah created him with His own hand, breathed into him of His spirit, and fashioned him properly (qabilan)." Then he said: "O Abu Dharr, four are Syriac: Adam, Shith, Khanukh (who is Idris, and he was the first to write with a pen), and Nuh. And four are Arab: Hud, Shu'ayb, Salih, and your Prophet, O Abu Dharr. The first prophets of the Children of Israel was Musa, and the last of them was Isa. The first of the messengers was Adam, and the last of them was Muhammad." He said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, how many books did Allah send down?" He said: "One hundred and four books. Allah sent down to Shith fifty scrolls, to Khanukh thirty scrolls, to Ibrahim ten scrolls, and He sent down to Musa, before the Torah, ten scrolls, and (He sent) the Injil, the Zabur, and the Furqan." He said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, what were the scrolls of Ibrahim?" He said: "They were entirely: O you powerful, afflicted, deceived king, I did not send you to gather the world, some of it upon others, but I sent you to turn away from Me the supplication of the oppressed, for I do not reject it even if it comes from a disbeliever. And in them was a parable: a wise person should have times: a time in which he communes with his Lord, a time in which he takes account of his soul, a time in which he reflects on the handiwork of Allah, and a time in which he is alone for his needs of food and drink. And a wise person should not be hostile except for three things: provision for the Hereafter, repair of livelihood, or pleasure that is not forbidden. And a wise person should be aware of his time, attentive to his affairs, and guarding his tongue. Whoever counts his speech as part of his deeds will speak little, except about what concerns him." He said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, what were the scrolls of Musa?" He said: "They were entirely lessons: I wonder at one who is certain of death and yet rejoices; I wonder at one who is certain of divine decree and yet toils; I wonder at one who sees the world and its turning over its people and yet is at ease with it; and I wonder at one who is certain of the reckoning tomorrow and yet does not act." He said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, is there anything in our hands from what was in the hands of Ibrahim and Musa, and what Allah sent down to you?" He said: "Yes. Recite, O Abu Dharr: ﴿He has certainly succeeded who purifies himself, and remembers the name of his Lord and prays. Rather, you prefer the worldly life, while the Hereafter is better and more lasting. Indeed, this is in the former scriptures, the scriptures of Ibrahim and Musa﴾ [Al-A'la: 14–19]."

He said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, advise me." He said: "I advise you to have fear of Allah, for it is the head of your affair."

He said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, increase (my knowledge) for me." He said: "Upon you is recitation of the Qur'an and remembrance of Allah, for it is a remembrance for you in the heavens and a light for you on the earth."

He said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, increase (my knowledge) for me." He said: "Beware of excessive laughter, for it kills the heart and takes away the light of the face." I said: "Increase for me." He said: "Upon you is jihad, for it is the monasticism of my Ummah." I said: "Increase for me." He said: "Upon you is silence except for good, for it repels Satan and is a help for you in the matter of your religion."

I said: "Increase for me." He said: "Look at one who is below you, and do not look at one who is above you, for that is more fitting for you so that you do not belittle the blessing of Allah upon you."

I said: "Increase for me." He said: "Love the poor and sit with them, for that is more fitting that you do not belittle the blessing of Allah upon you." I said: "Increase for me." He said: "Maintain your kinship ties even if they sever them from you." I said: "Increase for me." He said: "Speak the truth even if it is bitter."

I said: "Increase for me." He said: "Do not fear the blame of any blamer in (the cause of) Allah."

I said: "Increase for me." He said: "Let what you know about yourself keep you from (criticizing) people, and do not seek fault in them for what you love (in yourself). It is enough of a defect for you that you know from people what you are ignorant of in yourself, or that you seek fault in them for what you love."

Then he struck my chest with his hand and said: "O Abu Dharr, there is no intellect like forethought, no piety like restraint, and no lineage like good character."

[Al-Shari'a of al-Ajurri (p. 404). In its chain is Ibrahim ibn Hisham al-Ghassani, whom Abu Hatim and Abu Zur'a declared a liar, and he is the only one who narrated it from his father, from his grandfather.]

Imam Ahmad narrated from Abu al-Mughira, from Mu'an ibn Rifa'a, from Ali ibn Yazid, from al-Qasim, from Abu Umama, that Abu Dharr asked the Prophet (ﷺ), and he mentioned the matter of prayer, fasting, charity, the excellence of the Verse of the Throne, "there is no power and no strength except with Allah," the best of martyrs, the best of slaves (freed), the prophethood of Adam, that he was spoken to, and the number of prophets and messengers, similar to what has preceded.

[Al-Musnad (5/265).]

Abdullah ibn Imam Ahmad said: I found in my father's book, in his handwriting: Abd al-Muta'ali ibn Abd al-Wahhab narrated to me, Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Umawi narrated to us, Mujalid narrated to us, from Abu al-Wadda, who said: Abu Sa'id said: "Do the Kharijites say that the Dajjal (Antichrist) is real?" I said: "No." He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I am the seal of a thousand prophets or more, and no prophet was sent whose followers were not warned by him about him. And I have been shown what was not shown to anyone. He is one-eyed, and your Lord is not one-eyed. His right eye is blind, bulging, and not hidden, as if it were a spittle on a plastered wall, and his left eye is like a shining star. With him is the likeness of every tongue, and with him is the image of Paradise, green, in which water flows, and the image of the Fire, black, smoking."

[Al-Musnad (3/79). Al-Haythami said in Al-Majma' (7/346): "In it is Mujalid ibn Sa'id, whom al-Nasa'i declared reliable in one narration, and in another said: 'not strong.' A group declared him weak."]

This (hadith) has also been narrated to us in the part containing the narration of Abu Ya'la al-Mawsili, from Yahya ibn Ma'in, who said: Marwan ibn Mu'awiya narrated to us, Mujalid narrated to us, from Abu al-Wadda, from Abu Sa'id, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I am sealing a thousand thousand prophets or more. Allah has not sent a prophet to his people except that he warned them of the Dajjal..." and he mentioned the rest of the hadith. This is his wording with the addition of "alf" (thousand), and it may be an interpolation. [Al-Hakim narrated it in Al-Mustadrak (2/597) by the route of Yahya ibn Ma'in, and al-Dhahabi said: Mujalid is weak, and it does not have the addition of "alf," which is an interpolation as the author mentioned.] And Allah knows best. The wording of Imam Ahmad's narration is more established and more deserving of authenticity. The men in the chain of this hadith are acceptable. This hadith has also been narrated through Jabir ibn Abdullah, may Allah be pleased with him. The hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said:

Amr ibn Ali narrated to us, Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us, Mujalid narrated to us, from al-Sha'bi, from Jabir, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I am indeed the seal of a thousand prophets or more, and there is no prophet among them except that he warned his people of the Dajjal. And I have been shown what was not shown to any of them. He is one-eyed, and your Lord is not one-eyed."

[Musnad al-Bazzar, no. 3380, Kashf al-Astar.]

* *

His saying (Most High): ﴿And Allah spoke to Musa directly﴾. This is an honor for Musa, peace be upon him, through this attribute; for this reason he is called "al-Kalim" (the one who was spoken to). The hafiz Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sulayman al-Maliki narrated to us, Masih ibn Hatim narrated to us, Abd al-Jabbar ibn Abd Allah narrated to us, who said: A man came to Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash and said: "I heard a man reciting: 'And Allah spoke to Musa directly.'" Abu Bakr said: "None recites this except a disbeliever. I read it to al-A'mash, al-A'mash read it to Yahya ibn Wathhab, Yahya ibn Wathhab read it to Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, Abu Abd al-Rahman read it to Ali ibn Abi Talib, and Ali ibn Abi Talib read it to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): ﴿And Allah spoke to Musa directly﴾."

[Al-Tabarani narrated it in Al-Awsat (no. 3325), Majma' al-Bahrayn, by the route of Masih ibn Hatim. Al-Tabarani said: "No one narrated it from al-A'mash except Abu Bakr; Abd al-Jabbar ibn Abd Allah is alone in it, I do not know him, and the rest of its narrators are reliable."]

Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash, may Allah have mercy on him, was extremely angry at the one who recited this way, because he distorted the wording and meaning of the Qur'an. This was from the Mu'tazila, who deny that Allah spoke to Musa, peace be upon him, or speaks to any of His creation. Similarly, it has been related to us that one of the Mu'tazila recited to one of the shaykhs: "And Allah spoke to Musa directly," and he said to him: "O son of the wretched (ibn al-lakhna'), how will you deal with His saying, Most High: ﴿And when Musa came at Our appointed time and his Lord spoke to him﴾ [Al-A'raf: 143]?" Meaning: this does not admit distortion or interpretation.

Ibn Mardawayh said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Ahmad ibn al-Husayn ibn Bahram narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Marzuq narrated to us, Hani ibn Yahya narrated to us, from al-Hasan ibn Abi Ja'far, from Qatada, from Yahya ibn Wathhab, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When Allah spoke to Musa, he could see the crawling of an ant on the rock in a dark night." This is a strange hadith, and its chain is not authentic. If it is authentic as a statement of a Companion (mawquf), it is good.

[Al-Tabarani narrated it in Al-Mu'jam al-Saghir (no. 77) by the route of Ahmad ibn al-Husayn ibn Bahram. Al-Haythami said in Al-Majma' (8/203): "In it is al-Husayn ibn Abi Ja'far al-Jafri, who is abandoned (matruk)."]

Ibn Kathir's commentary on Surah 4, verses 163–165 (part 3 of 3):

Al-Hakim related in his Mustadrak, and Ibn Mardawayh, from the hadith of Humayd ibn Qays al-A'raj, from Abdullah ibn al-Harith, from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When your Lord spoke to Musa, Musa had on a woolen robe (jubbat suf), a woolen cloak (kisa' suf), woolen trousers (sarawil suf), and two sandals of donkey hide that had not been tanned." [[Al-Mustadrak (2/379). It was also related by al-Tirmidhi in his Sunan, no. 1734, through the route of Humayd al-A'raj.
Al-Hakim said: "It meets the conditions of al-Bukhari." Al-Dhahabi criticised him, saying: "Rather, it does not meet his conditions. What deceived him is that its chain contains Humayd ibn Qays, and that is an error. It is Humayd al-A'raj al-Kufi, son of Ali or son of Ammar, one of those who are abandoned (matrukun), and he thought he was the Meccan, the truthful one."]]

Ibn Mardawayh also said, with his chain, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Allah conversed with Musa with one hundred thousand and forty thousand words, over three days, all of them admonitions. When Musa heard the speech of the children of Adam, he despised them because of what had reached his ears of the speech of the Lord, Mighty and Majestic.

This chain is also weak, for Juwaybir is weak, and al-Dahhak did not meet Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him.

As for the report related by Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh and others through the route of al-Fadl ibn Isa al-Raqqashi, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Jabir ibn Abdullah, who said: When Allah spoke to Musa on the Mount of Tur, He spoke to him with other than the speech with which He had spoken to him on the day He called him. Musa said to Him: "O Lord, is this Your speech with which You spoke to me?" He said: "No, O Musa. I spoke to you with the strength of ten thousand tongues, and I have the strength of all tongues, and I am stronger than that." When Musa returned to the Children of Israel, they said: "O Musa, describe to us the speech of the Merciful." He said: "I cannot." They said: "Then liken it for us." He said: "Have you not heard the sound of thunderbolts? They are close to it, yet it is not it."

This chain is weak, for this al-Fadl al-Raqqashi is extremely weak.

Abd al-Razzaq said: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from Abu Bakr ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Harith, from Jaz' ibn Jabir al-Khath'ami, from Ka'b, who said: When Allah spoke to Musa, He spoke to him in all tongues apart from His own speech. Musa said to Him: "O Lord, is this Your speech?" He said: "No. Even if I had spoken to you with My speech, you would not have been able to bear it." He said: "O Lord, is there any of Your creation that resembles Your speech?" He said: "No. The creature most like My speech is the most intense of the thunderbolts you hear."

This is a report halted at Ka'b al-Ahbar (mawquf), and he is relating from the earlier books that contain the narratives of the Children of Israel, in which there is both the worthless and the valuable.

* *

As for His saying, ﴿Messengers as bringers of good tidings and as warners﴾, meaning: they give glad tidings to whoever obeys Allah and follows His good pleasure with good things, and they warn whoever opposes His command and denies His messengers with punishment and torment.

* *

As for His saying, ﴿So that mankind will have no argument against Allah after the messengers. And Allah is ever Exalted in Might and Wise﴾, meaning: He, the Exalted, sent down His scriptures and dispatched His messengers with good tidings and warning, and explained what He loves and is pleased with, and what He dislikes and rejects, so that no excuse remains for one who makes excuses, as He said, the Exalted: ﴿And if We had destroyed them with a punishment before it, they would have said, "Our Lord, why did You not send to us a messenger so we could follow Your verses before we were humiliated and disgraced?"﴾ [Ta-Ha: 134]. Likewise His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And if not that a misfortune should strike them for what their hands have sent forth, they would say, "Our Lord, why did You not send to us a messenger so we could follow Your verses and be among the believers?"﴾ [Al-Qasas: 47].

It is established in the two Sahihs [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4634, and Sahih Muslim, no. 2760.]] from Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "There is no one more jealous (aghyar) than Allah; for this reason He forbade indecencies, both what is apparent of them and what is hidden. And there is no one who loves praise more than Allah; for this reason He praised Himself. And there is no one who loves excuse more than Allah; for this reason He sent the Prophets as bringers of good tidings and warners." In another wording: "For this reason He sent His messengers and sent down His scriptures."

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 4, verse 163–165 (part 1 of 3):

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said, from Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, from Ikrimah or Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Sukayn and 'Adi ibn Zayd said: "O Muhammad, we do not know that God has sent down anything to a human being after Moses." So God revealed in response to their words: ﴿Indeed, We have revealed to you as We revealed to Noah and the prophets after him﴾, to the end of the verses.

Ibn Jarir said: al-Harith narrated to us, 'Abd al-'Aziz narrated to us, Abu Ma'shar narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, who said: God revealed: ﴿The People of the Book ask you to bring down to them a Book from heaven﴾, to His words ﴿and their saying against Mary a tremendous slander﴾. So he (the Prophet) recited it to them, meaning to the Jews, and informed them of their wicked deeds. They denied everything God had sent down and said: "God has not sent down anything to a human being, neither to Moses nor to Jesus, nor to any prophet." He said: So he (the Prophet) became angry and said: "Nor to anyone." Then God, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿They did not esteem God with the esteem due to Him when they said, "God has not sent down anything to a human being"﴾ [al-An'am: 91].

Concerning what Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi said, there is an objection: this verse is Meccan in Surah al-An'am, whereas this verse in Surah an-Nisa' is Medinan, and it is a response to them when they asked the Prophet ﷺ to bring down to them a Book from heaven. God the Exalted said: ﴿They asked Moses for greater than that﴾ [an-Nisa': 153]. Then He mentioned their disgraces, their faults, what they were upon, and what they are upon now of lying and fabrication. Then He mentioned that He revealed to His servant and messenger Muhammad ﷺ just as He revealed to the other earlier prophets, saying: ﴿Indeed, We have revealed to you as We revealed to Noah and the prophets after him, and We revealed to Abraham and Ishmael and Isaac and Jacob and the Descendants and Jesus and Job and Jonah and Aaron and Solomon, and We gave David the Psalms﴾.

Az-Zabur: it is the name of the Book that God revealed to David, peace be upon him. We will mention the biography of each of these prophets, may the most excellent of God's blessings and peace be upon them, when recounting their stories in the coming surahs, if God wills. And in Him is trust, and upon Him is reliance.

* *

His saying ﴿And messengers We have related to you before, and messengers We have not related to you﴾, meaning: before this verse, i.e., in the Meccan surahs and others.

These are the names of the prophets whose names are specified in the Qur'an: Adam, Idris, Noah, Hud, Salih, Abraham, Lot, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, Joseph, Job, Shu'ayb, Moses, Aaron, Jonah, David, Solomon, Elias, Elisha, Zechariah, John, and Jesus, peace be upon them; and likewise Dhul-Kifl according to many exegetes; and their master is Muhammad ﷺ.

* *

His saying: ﴿And messengers We have not related to you﴾, meaning: other created beings not mentioned in the Qur'an. The number of prophets and messengers has been disputed, and the most well-known in this regard is the lengthy hadith of Abu Dharr, as narrated by Ibn Mardawayh, may God have mercy on him, in his Tafsir, where he said: Ibrahim ibn Muhammad narrated to us, Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan and al-Husayn ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Yazid narrated to us, both saying: Ibrahim ibn Hisham ibn Yahya al-Ghassani narrated to us, my father narrated to me from my grandfather, from Abu Idris al-Khawlani, from Abu Dharr, who said: I said: "O Messenger of God, how many are the prophets?" He said: "One hundred and twenty-four thousand." I said: "O Messenger of God, how many of them are messengers?" He said: "Three hundred and thirteen, a great throng." I said: "O Messenger of God, who was the first of them?" He said: "Adam." I said: "O Messenger of God, was he a prophet and messenger?" He said: "Yes, God created him with His own hand, breathed into him of His spirit, then formed him directly." Then he said: "O Abu Dharr, four are Syriac: Adam, Seth, Noah, and Kanukh—who is Idris, and he was the first to write with a pen—and four are Arabs: Hud, Salih, Shu'ayb, and your Prophet, O Abu Dharr. The first of the prophets of the Children of Israel was Moses, and the last of them was Jesus. The first of the prophets was Adam, and the last of them is your Prophet."

This hadith in its entirety was narrated by the Hafiz Abu Hatim Ibn Hibban al-Busti in his book "al-Anwa' wa'l-Taqasim," and he graded it as sound. Ibn al-Jawzi disagreed with him, mentioning this hadith in his book "al-Mawdu'at" (Fabricated Hadiths), and accused Ibrahim ibn Hisham of fabricating it. There is no doubt that more than one of the imams of criticism and authentication spoke about him because of this hadith [Sahih Ibn Hibban, no. (94) "Mawarid"; Abu Nu'aym narrated it in al-Hilyah (1/166) through the route of Ibrahim ibn Hisham ibn Yahya with the same chain.
Ibrahim ibn Hisham al-Ghassani was declared a liar by Abu Hatim and Abu Zur'ah, and al-Dhahabi said: "He is the transmitter of the lengthy hadith of Abu Dharr; he alone narrated it from his father from his grandfather."]. And God knows best.

This hadith has also been narrated through another route, from a different Companion. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn 'Awf narrated to us, Abu al-Mughirah narrated to us, Mu'an ibn Rifa'ah narrated to us, from 'Ali ibn Yazid, from al-Qasim, from Abu Umamah, who said: I said: "O Prophet of God, how many are the prophets?" He said: "One hundred and twenty-four thousand, of whom three hundred and fifteen are a great throng."

Mu'an ibn Rifa'ah al-Salami is weak, 'Ali ibn Yazid is weak, and al-Qasim Abu 'Abd al-Rahman is also weak [mentioned by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur (2/746)].

The Hafiz Abu Ya'la al-Mawsili said: Ahmad ibn Ishaq Abu 'Abd Allah al-Jawhari al-Basri narrated to us, Makki ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Musa ibn 'Ubaydah al-Rabadhi narrated to us, from Yazid al-Raqqashi, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "God sent eight thousand prophets: four thousand to the Children of Israel, and four thousand to the rest of mankind."

This is also a weak chain, in which al-Rabadhi is weak, and his teacher al-Raqqashi is weaker still [Musnad Abi Ya'la (7/160); Abu Nu'aym narrated it in al-Hilyah (3/53) through the route of Makki ibn Ibrahim; al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (8/210): "In it is Musa ibn 'Ubaydah al-Rabadhi, who is very weak."]. And God knows best.

Abu Ya'la also said: Abu al-Rabi' narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Thabit al-'Abdi narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Ansari narrated to us, from Yazid al-Raqqashi, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "Among my brothers among the prophets who passed away were eight thousand prophets, then came Jesus son of Mary, then I." [Musnad Abi Ya'la (7/131); al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (8/211): "In it is Muhammad ibn Thabit al-'Abdi, who is weak."]

We have also narrated it from Anas through another route: al-Hafiz Abu 'Abd Allah al-Dhahabi informed us, Abu al-Fadl ibn 'Asakir informed us, Imam Abu Bakr al-Qasim ibn Abi Sa'id al-Saffar informed us, my paternal aunt 'A'ishah bint Ahmad ibn Mansur ibn al-Saffar informed us, al-Sharif Abu al-Sanabik Hibat Allah ibn Abi al-Sahba' Muhammad ibn Haydar al-Qurashi informed us, Imam al-Ustadh Abu Ishaq al-Isfara'ini said: Imam Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Isma'ili informed us, Muhammad ibn 'Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, Ahmad ibn Tariq narrated to us, Muslim ibn Khalid narrated to us, Ziyad ibn Sa'd narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Safwan ibn Sulaym, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "I was sent after three thousand prophets from the Children of Israel." This is strange from this route, and its chain is acceptable; all its narrators are known except this Ahmad ibn Tariq, for I do not know him to be either trustworthy or defective [narrated by Abu Nu'aym in al-Hilyah (3/162) through the route of Muslim ibn Khalid al-Zanji, and he said: "Strange."]. And God knows best.

The lengthy hadith of Abu Dharr al-Ghifari concerning the number of the prophets, peace be upon them:

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 4, verses 163–165 (part 2 of 3):

Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Ajurri said: Abu Bakr Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn al-Firyabi narrated to us by dictation in the month of Rajab, in the year 297 AH. Ibrahim ibn Hisham ibn Yahya al-Ghassani narrated to us, my father narrated to us, from his grandfather, from Abu Idris al-Khawlani, from Abu Dharr, who said: I entered the mosque and found the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sitting alone, so I sat down with him and said: "O Messenger of Allah, you commanded me to pray." He said: "Prayer is the best of undertakings, so increase it or reduce it." He said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, which deed is best?" He said: "Belief in Allah and striving (jihad) in His cause." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, which of the believers is best?" He said: "The one with the best character." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, which of the Muslims is the most secure (from harm)?" He said: "The one from whose tongue and hand people are safe." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, which migration is best?" He said: "The one who abandons evil deeds." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, which prayer is best?" He said: "Lengthy standing (qunut)." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, which fasting is best?" He said: "An obligatory fast that is sufficient, and with Allah there are many multiples." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, which jihad is best?" He said: "The one whose mount is hamstrung and whose blood is shed." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, which slaves (freed) are best?" He said: "The most expensive in price and the most precious to their owners." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, which charity is best?" He said: "Effort from one who has little, and secret giving to a poor person." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, which verse of what was revealed to you is the greatest?" He said: "The Verse of the Throne (Ayat al-Kursi)." Then he said: "O Abu Dharr, the seven heavens compared to the Kursi are nothing but a ring thrown down in a desert, and the excellence of the Throne over the Kursi is like the excellence of the desert over the ring." He said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, how many prophets are there?" He said: "One hundred and twenty-four thousand." He said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, how many of them were messengers?" He said: "Three hundred and thirteen, a great, abundant, numerous, good company." I said: "Who was the first of them?" He said: "Adam." I said: "Was he a prophet sent (with a message)?" He said: "Yes, Allah created him with His own hand, breathed into him of His spirit, and fashioned him properly (qabilan)." Then he said: "O Abu Dharr, four are Syriac: Adam, Shith, Khanukh (who is Idris, and he was the first to write with a pen), and Nuh. And four are Arab: Hud, Shu'ayb, Salih, and your Prophet, O Abu Dharr. The first prophets of the Children of Israel was Musa, and the last of them was Isa. The first of the messengers was Adam, and the last of them was Muhammad." He said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, how many books did Allah send down?" He said: "One hundred and four books. Allah sent down to Shith fifty scrolls, to Khanukh thirty scrolls, to Ibrahim ten scrolls, and He sent down to Musa, before the Torah, ten scrolls, and (He sent) the Injil, the Zabur, and the Furqan." He said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, what were the scrolls of Ibrahim?" He said: "They were entirely: O you powerful, afflicted, deceived king, I did not send you to gather the world, some of it upon others, but I sent you to turn away from Me the supplication of the oppressed, for I do not reject it even if it comes from a disbeliever. And in them was a parable: a wise person should have times: a time in which he communes with his Lord, a time in which he takes account of his soul, a time in which he reflects on the handiwork of Allah, and a time in which he is alone for his needs of food and drink. And a wise person should not be hostile except for three things: provision for the Hereafter, repair of livelihood, or pleasure that is not forbidden. And a wise person should be aware of his time, attentive to his affairs, and guarding his tongue. Whoever counts his speech as part of his deeds will speak little, except about what concerns him." He said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, what were the scrolls of Musa?" He said: "They were entirely lessons: I wonder at one who is certain of death and yet rejoices; I wonder at one who is certain of divine decree and yet toils; I wonder at one who sees the world and its turning over its people and yet is at ease with it; and I wonder at one who is certain of the reckoning tomorrow and yet does not act." He said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, is there anything in our hands from what was in the hands of Ibrahim and Musa, and what Allah sent down to you?" He said: "Yes. Recite, O Abu Dharr: ﴿He has certainly succeeded who purifies himself, and remembers the name of his Lord and prays. Rather, you prefer the worldly life, while the Hereafter is better and more lasting. Indeed, this is in the former scriptures, the scriptures of Ibrahim and Musa﴾ [Al-A'la: 14–19]."

He said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, advise me." He said: "I advise you to have fear of Allah, for it is the head of your affair."

He said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, increase (my knowledge) for me." He said: "Upon you is recitation of the Qur'an and remembrance of Allah, for it is a remembrance for you in the heavens and a light for you on the earth."

He said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, increase (my knowledge) for me." He said: "Beware of excessive laughter, for it kills the heart and takes away the light of the face." I said: "Increase for me." He said: "Upon you is jihad, for it is the monasticism of my Ummah." I said: "Increase for me." He said: "Upon you is silence except for good, for it repels Satan and is a help for you in the matter of your religion."

I said: "Increase for me." He said: "Look at one who is below you, and do not look at one who is above you, for that is more fitting for you so that you do not belittle the blessing of Allah upon you."

I said: "Increase for me." He said: "Love the poor and sit with them, for that is more fitting that you do not belittle the blessing of Allah upon you." I said: "Increase for me." He said: "Maintain your kinship ties even if they sever them from you." I said: "Increase for me." He said: "Speak the truth even if it is bitter."

I said: "Increase for me." He said: "Do not fear the blame of any blamer in (the cause of) Allah."

I said: "Increase for me." He said: "Let what you know about yourself keep you from (criticizing) people, and do not seek fault in them for what you love (in yourself). It is enough of a defect for you that you know from people what you are ignorant of in yourself, or that you seek fault in them for what you love."

Then he struck my chest with his hand and said: "O Abu Dharr, there is no intellect like forethought, no piety like restraint, and no lineage like good character."

[Al-Shari'a of al-Ajurri (p. 404). In its chain is Ibrahim ibn Hisham al-Ghassani, whom Abu Hatim and Abu Zur'a declared a liar, and he is the only one who narrated it from his father, from his grandfather.]

Imam Ahmad narrated from Abu al-Mughira, from Mu'an ibn Rifa'a, from Ali ibn Yazid, from al-Qasim, from Abu Umama, that Abu Dharr asked the Prophet (ﷺ), and he mentioned the matter of prayer, fasting, charity, the excellence of the Verse of the Throne, "there is no power and no strength except with Allah," the best of martyrs, the best of slaves (freed), the prophethood of Adam, that he was spoken to, and the number of prophets and messengers, similar to what has preceded.

[Al-Musnad (5/265).]

Abdullah ibn Imam Ahmad said: I found in my father's book, in his handwriting: Abd al-Muta'ali ibn Abd al-Wahhab narrated to me, Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Umawi narrated to us, Mujalid narrated to us, from Abu al-Wadda, who said: Abu Sa'id said: "Do the Kharijites say that the Dajjal (Antichrist) is real?" I said: "No." He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I am the seal of a thousand prophets or more, and no prophet was sent whose followers were not warned by him about him. And I have been shown what was not shown to anyone. He is one-eyed, and your Lord is not one-eyed. His right eye is blind, bulging, and not hidden, as if it were a spittle on a plastered wall, and his left eye is like a shining star. With him is the likeness of every tongue, and with him is the image of Paradise, green, in which water flows, and the image of the Fire, black, smoking."

[Al-Musnad (3/79). Al-Haythami said in Al-Majma' (7/346): "In it is Mujalid ibn Sa'id, whom al-Nasa'i declared reliable in one narration, and in another said: 'not strong.' A group declared him weak."]

This (hadith) has also been narrated to us in the part containing the narration of Abu Ya'la al-Mawsili, from Yahya ibn Ma'in, who said: Marwan ibn Mu'awiya narrated to us, Mujalid narrated to us, from Abu al-Wadda, from Abu Sa'id, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I am sealing a thousand thousand prophets or more. Allah has not sent a prophet to his people except that he warned them of the Dajjal..." and he mentioned the rest of the hadith. This is his wording with the addition of "alf" (thousand), and it may be an interpolation. [Al-Hakim narrated it in Al-Mustadrak (2/597) by the route of Yahya ibn Ma'in, and al-Dhahabi said: Mujalid is weak, and it does not have the addition of "alf," which is an interpolation as the author mentioned.] And Allah knows best. The wording of Imam Ahmad's narration is more established and more deserving of authenticity. The men in the chain of this hadith are acceptable. This hadith has also been narrated through Jabir ibn Abdullah, may Allah be pleased with him. The hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said:

Amr ibn Ali narrated to us, Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us, Mujalid narrated to us, from al-Sha'bi, from Jabir, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I am indeed the seal of a thousand prophets or more, and there is no prophet among them except that he warned his people of the Dajjal. And I have been shown what was not shown to any of them. He is one-eyed, and your Lord is not one-eyed."

[Musnad al-Bazzar, no. 3380, Kashf al-Astar.]

* *

His saying (Most High): ﴿And Allah spoke to Musa directly﴾. This is an honor for Musa, peace be upon him, through this attribute; for this reason he is called "al-Kalim" (the one who was spoken to). The hafiz Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sulayman al-Maliki narrated to us, Masih ibn Hatim narrated to us, Abd al-Jabbar ibn Abd Allah narrated to us, who said: A man came to Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash and said: "I heard a man reciting: 'And Allah spoke to Musa directly.'" Abu Bakr said: "None recites this except a disbeliever. I read it to al-A'mash, al-A'mash read it to Yahya ibn Wathhab, Yahya ibn Wathhab read it to Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, Abu Abd al-Rahman read it to Ali ibn Abi Talib, and Ali ibn Abi Talib read it to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): ﴿And Allah spoke to Musa directly﴾."

[Al-Tabarani narrated it in Al-Awsat (no. 3325), Majma' al-Bahrayn, by the route of Masih ibn Hatim. Al-Tabarani said: "No one narrated it from al-A'mash except Abu Bakr; Abd al-Jabbar ibn Abd Allah is alone in it, I do not know him, and the rest of its narrators are reliable."]

Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash, may Allah have mercy on him, was extremely angry at the one who recited this way, because he distorted the wording and meaning of the Qur'an. This was from the Mu'tazila, who deny that Allah spoke to Musa, peace be upon him, or speaks to any of His creation. Similarly, it has been related to us that one of the Mu'tazila recited to one of the shaykhs: "And Allah spoke to Musa directly," and he said to him: "O son of the wretched (ibn al-lakhna'), how will you deal with His saying, Most High: ﴿And when Musa came at Our appointed time and his Lord spoke to him﴾ [Al-A'raf: 143]?" Meaning: this does not admit distortion or interpretation.

Ibn Mardawayh said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Ahmad ibn al-Husayn ibn Bahram narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Marzuq narrated to us, Hani ibn Yahya narrated to us, from al-Hasan ibn Abi Ja'far, from Qatada, from Yahya ibn Wathhab, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When Allah spoke to Musa, he could see the crawling of an ant on the rock in a dark night." This is a strange hadith, and its chain is not authentic. If it is authentic as a statement of a Companion (mawquf), it is good.

[Al-Tabarani narrated it in Al-Mu'jam al-Saghir (no. 77) by the route of Ahmad ibn al-Husayn ibn Bahram. Al-Haythami said in Al-Majma' (8/203): "In it is al-Husayn ibn Abi Ja'far al-Jafri, who is abandoned (matruk)."]

Ibn Kathir's commentary on Surah 4, verses 163–165 (part 3 of 3):

Al-Hakim related in his Mustadrak, and Ibn Mardawayh, from the hadith of Humayd ibn Qays al-A'raj, from Abdullah ibn al-Harith, from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When your Lord spoke to Musa, Musa had on a woolen robe (jubbat suf), a woolen cloak (kisa' suf), woolen trousers (sarawil suf), and two sandals of donkey hide that had not been tanned." [[Al-Mustadrak (2/379). It was also related by al-Tirmidhi in his Sunan, no. 1734, through the route of Humayd al-A'raj.
Al-Hakim said: "It meets the conditions of al-Bukhari." Al-Dhahabi criticised him, saying: "Rather, it does not meet his conditions. What deceived him is that its chain contains Humayd ibn Qays, and that is an error. It is Humayd al-A'raj al-Kufi, son of Ali or son of Ammar, one of those who are abandoned (matrukun), and he thought he was the Meccan, the truthful one."]]

Ibn Mardawayh also said, with his chain, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Allah conversed with Musa with one hundred thousand and forty thousand words, over three days, all of them admonitions. When Musa heard the speech of the children of Adam, he despised them because of what had reached his ears of the speech of the Lord, Mighty and Majestic.

This chain is also weak, for Juwaybir is weak, and al-Dahhak did not meet Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him.

As for the report related by Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh and others through the route of al-Fadl ibn Isa al-Raqqashi, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Jabir ibn Abdullah, who said: When Allah spoke to Musa on the Mount of Tur, He spoke to him with other than the speech with which He had spoken to him on the day He called him. Musa said to Him: "O Lord, is this Your speech with which You spoke to me?" He said: "No, O Musa. I spoke to you with the strength of ten thousand tongues, and I have the strength of all tongues, and I am stronger than that." When Musa returned to the Children of Israel, they said: "O Musa, describe to us the speech of the Merciful." He said: "I cannot." They said: "Then liken it for us." He said: "Have you not heard the sound of thunderbolts? They are close to it, yet it is not it."

This chain is weak, for this al-Fadl al-Raqqashi is extremely weak.

Abd al-Razzaq said: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from Abu Bakr ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Harith, from Jaz' ibn Jabir al-Khath'ami, from Ka'b, who said: When Allah spoke to Musa, He spoke to him in all tongues apart from His own speech. Musa said to Him: "O Lord, is this Your speech?" He said: "No. Even if I had spoken to you with My speech, you would not have been able to bear it." He said: "O Lord, is there any of Your creation that resembles Your speech?" He said: "No. The creature most like My speech is the most intense of the thunderbolts you hear."

This is a report halted at Ka'b al-Ahbar (mawquf), and he is relating from the earlier books that contain the narratives of the Children of Israel, in which there is both the worthless and the valuable.

* *

As for His saying, ﴿Messengers as bringers of good tidings and as warners﴾, meaning: they give glad tidings to whoever obeys Allah and follows His good pleasure with good things, and they warn whoever opposes His command and denies His messengers with punishment and torment.

* *

As for His saying, ﴿So that mankind will have no argument against Allah after the messengers. And Allah is ever Exalted in Might and Wise﴾, meaning: He, the Exalted, sent down His scriptures and dispatched His messengers with good tidings and warning, and explained what He loves and is pleased with, and what He dislikes and rejects, so that no excuse remains for one who makes excuses, as He said, the Exalted: ﴿And if We had destroyed them with a punishment before it, they would have said, "Our Lord, why did You not send to us a messenger so we could follow Your verses before we were humiliated and disgraced?"﴾ [Ta-Ha: 134]. Likewise His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And if not that a misfortune should strike them for what their hands have sent forth, they would say, "Our Lord, why did You not send to us a messenger so we could follow Your verses and be among the believers?"﴾ [Al-Qasas: 47].

It is established in the two Sahihs [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4634, and Sahih Muslim, no. 2760.]] from Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "There is no one more jealous (aghyar) than Allah; for this reason He forbade indecencies, both what is apparent of them and what is hidden. And there is no one who loves praise more than Allah; for this reason He praised Himself. And there is no one who loves excuse more than Allah; for this reason He sent the Prophets as bringers of good tidings and warners." In another wording: "For this reason He sent His messengers and sent down His scriptures."

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 4, verse 163–165 (part 1 of 3):

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said, from Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, from Ikrimah or Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Sukayn and 'Adi ibn Zayd said: "O Muhammad, we do not know that God has sent down anything to a human being after Moses." So God revealed in response to their words: ﴿Indeed, We have revealed to you as We revealed to Noah and the prophets after him﴾, to the end of the verses.

Ibn Jarir said: al-Harith narrated to us, 'Abd al-'Aziz narrated to us, Abu Ma'shar narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, who said: God revealed: ﴿The People of the Book ask you to bring down to them a Book from heaven﴾, to His words ﴿and their saying against Mary a tremendous slander﴾. So he (the Prophet) recited it to them, meaning to the Jews, and informed them of their wicked deeds. They denied everything God had sent down and said: "God has not sent down anything to a human being, neither to Moses nor to Jesus, nor to any prophet." He said: So he (the Prophet) became angry and said: "Nor to anyone." Then God, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿They did not esteem God with the esteem due to Him when they said, "God has not sent down anything to a human being"﴾ [al-An'am: 91].

Concerning what Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi said, there is an objection: this verse is Meccan in Surah al-An'am, whereas this verse in Surah an-Nisa' is Medinan, and it is a response to them when they asked the Prophet ﷺ to bring down to them a Book from heaven. God the Exalted said: ﴿They asked Moses for greater than that﴾ [an-Nisa': 153]. Then He mentioned their disgraces, their faults, what they were upon, and what they are upon now of lying and fabrication. Then He mentioned that He revealed to His servant and messenger Muhammad ﷺ just as He revealed to the other earlier prophets, saying: ﴿Indeed, We have revealed to you as We revealed to Noah and the prophets after him, and We revealed to Abraham and Ishmael and Isaac and Jacob and the Descendants and Jesus and Job and Jonah and Aaron and Solomon, and We gave David the Psalms﴾.

Az-Zabur: it is the name of the Book that God revealed to David, peace be upon him. We will mention the biography of each of these prophets, may the most excellent of God's blessings and peace be upon them, when recounting their stories in the coming surahs, if God wills. And in Him is trust, and upon Him is reliance.

* *

His saying ﴿And messengers We have related to you before, and messengers We have not related to you﴾, meaning: before this verse, i.e., in the Meccan surahs and others.

These are the names of the prophets whose names are specified in the Qur'an: Adam, Idris, Noah, Hud, Salih, Abraham, Lot, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, Joseph, Job, Shu'ayb, Moses, Aaron, Jonah, David, Solomon, Elias, Elisha, Zechariah, John, and Jesus, peace be upon them; and likewise Dhul-Kifl according to many exegetes; and their master is Muhammad ﷺ.

* *

His saying: ﴿And messengers We have not related to you﴾, meaning: other created beings not mentioned in the Qur'an. The number of prophets and messengers has been disputed, and the most well-known in this regard is the lengthy hadith of Abu Dharr, as narrated by Ibn Mardawayh, may God have mercy on him, in his Tafsir, where he said: Ibrahim ibn Muhammad narrated to us, Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan and al-Husayn ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Yazid narrated to us, both saying: Ibrahim ibn Hisham ibn Yahya al-Ghassani narrated to us, my father narrated to me from my grandfather, from Abu Idris al-Khawlani, from Abu Dharr, who said: I said: "O Messenger of God, how many are the prophets?" He said: "One hundred and twenty-four thousand." I said: "O Messenger of God, how many of them are messengers?" He said: "Three hundred and thirteen, a great throng." I said: "O Messenger of God, who was the first of them?" He said: "Adam." I said: "O Messenger of God, was he a prophet and messenger?" He said: "Yes, God created him with His own hand, breathed into him of His spirit, then formed him directly." Then he said: "O Abu Dharr, four are Syriac: Adam, Seth, Noah, and Kanukh—who is Idris, and he was the first to write with a pen—and four are Arabs: Hud, Salih, Shu'ayb, and your Prophet, O Abu Dharr. The first of the prophets of the Children of Israel was Moses, and the last of them was Jesus. The first of the prophets was Adam, and the last of them is your Prophet."

This hadith in its entirety was narrated by the Hafiz Abu Hatim Ibn Hibban al-Busti in his book "al-Anwa' wa'l-Taqasim," and he graded it as sound. Ibn al-Jawzi disagreed with him, mentioning this hadith in his book "al-Mawdu'at" (Fabricated Hadiths), and accused Ibrahim ibn Hisham of fabricating it. There is no doubt that more than one of the imams of criticism and authentication spoke about him because of this hadith [Sahih Ibn Hibban, no. (94) "Mawarid"; Abu Nu'aym narrated it in al-Hilyah (1/166) through the route of Ibrahim ibn Hisham ibn Yahya with the same chain.
Ibrahim ibn Hisham al-Ghassani was declared a liar by Abu Hatim and Abu Zur'ah, and al-Dhahabi said: "He is the transmitter of the lengthy hadith of Abu Dharr; he alone narrated it from his father from his grandfather."]. And God knows best.

This hadith has also been narrated through another route, from a different Companion. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn 'Awf narrated to us, Abu al-Mughirah narrated to us, Mu'an ibn Rifa'ah narrated to us, from 'Ali ibn Yazid, from al-Qasim, from Abu Umamah, who said: I said: "O Prophet of God, how many are the prophets?" He said: "One hundred and twenty-four thousand, of whom three hundred and fifteen are a great throng."

Mu'an ibn Rifa'ah al-Salami is weak, 'Ali ibn Yazid is weak, and al-Qasim Abu 'Abd al-Rahman is also weak [mentioned by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur (2/746)].

The Hafiz Abu Ya'la al-Mawsili said: Ahmad ibn Ishaq Abu 'Abd Allah al-Jawhari al-Basri narrated to us, Makki ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Musa ibn 'Ubaydah al-Rabadhi narrated to us, from Yazid al-Raqqashi, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "God sent eight thousand prophets: four thousand to the Children of Israel, and four thousand to the rest of mankind."

This is also a weak chain, in which al-Rabadhi is weak, and his teacher al-Raqqashi is weaker still [Musnad Abi Ya'la (7/160); Abu Nu'aym narrated it in al-Hilyah (3/53) through the route of Makki ibn Ibrahim; al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (8/210): "In it is Musa ibn 'Ubaydah al-Rabadhi, who is very weak."]. And God knows best.

Abu Ya'la also said: Abu al-Rabi' narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Thabit al-'Abdi narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Ansari narrated to us, from Yazid al-Raqqashi, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "Among my brothers among the prophets who passed away were eight thousand prophets, then came Jesus son of Mary, then I." [Musnad Abi Ya'la (7/131); al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (8/211): "In it is Muhammad ibn Thabit al-'Abdi, who is weak."]

We have also narrated it from Anas through another route: al-Hafiz Abu 'Abd Allah al-Dhahabi informed us, Abu al-Fadl ibn 'Asakir informed us, Imam Abu Bakr al-Qasim ibn Abi Sa'id al-Saffar informed us, my paternal aunt 'A'ishah bint Ahmad ibn Mansur ibn al-Saffar informed us, al-Sharif Abu al-Sanabik Hibat Allah ibn Abi al-Sahba' Muhammad ibn Haydar al-Qurashi informed us, Imam al-Ustadh Abu Ishaq al-Isfara'ini said: Imam Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Isma'ili informed us, Muhammad ibn 'Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, Ahmad ibn Tariq narrated to us, Muslim ibn Khalid narrated to us, Ziyad ibn Sa'd narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Safwan ibn Sulaym, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "I was sent after three thousand prophets from the Children of Israel." This is strange from this route, and its chain is acceptable; all its narrators are known except this Ahmad ibn Tariq, for I do not know him to be either trustworthy or defective [narrated by Abu Nu'aym in al-Hilyah (3/162) through the route of Muslim ibn Khalid al-Zanji, and he said: "Strange."]. And God knows best.

The lengthy hadith of Abu Dharr al-Ghifari concerning the number of the prophets, peace be upon them:

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 4, verses 163–165 (part 2 of 3):

Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Ajurri said: Abu Bakr Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn al-Firyabi narrated to us by dictation in the month of Rajab, in the year 297 AH. Ibrahim ibn Hisham ibn Yahya al-Ghassani narrated to us, my father narrated to us, from his grandfather, from Abu Idris al-Khawlani, from Abu Dharr, who said: I entered the mosque and found the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sitting alone, so I sat down with him and said: "O Messenger of Allah, you commanded me to pray." He said: "Prayer is the best of undertakings, so increase it or reduce it." He said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, which deed is best?" He said: "Belief in Allah and striving (jihad) in His cause." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, which of the believers is best?" He said: "The one with the best character." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, which of the Muslims is the most secure (from harm)?" He said: "The one from whose tongue and hand people are safe." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, which migration is best?" He said: "The one who abandons evil deeds." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, which prayer is best?" He said: "Lengthy standing (qunut)." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, which fasting is best?" He said: "An obligatory fast that is sufficient, and with Allah there are many multiples." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, which jihad is best?" He said: "The one whose mount is hamstrung and whose blood is shed." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, which slaves (freed) are best?" He said: "The most expensive in price and the most precious to their owners." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, which charity is best?" He said: "Effort from one who has little, and secret giving to a poor person." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, which verse of what was revealed to you is the greatest?" He said: "The Verse of the Throne (Ayat al-Kursi)." Then he said: "O Abu Dharr, the seven heavens compared to the Kursi are nothing but a ring thrown down in a desert, and the excellence of the Throne over the Kursi is like the excellence of the desert over the ring." He said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, how many prophets are there?" He said: "One hundred and twenty-four thousand." He said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, how many of them were messengers?" He said: "Three hundred and thirteen, a great, abundant, numerous, good company." I said: "Who was the first of them?" He said: "Adam." I said: "Was he a prophet sent (with a message)?" He said: "Yes, Allah created him with His own hand, breathed into him of His spirit, and fashioned him properly (qabilan)." Then he said: "O Abu Dharr, four are Syriac: Adam, Shith, Khanukh (who is Idris, and he was the first to write with a pen), and Nuh. And four are Arab: Hud, Shu'ayb, Salih, and your Prophet, O Abu Dharr. The first prophets of the Children of Israel was Musa, and the last of them was Isa. The first of the messengers was Adam, and the last of them was Muhammad." He said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, how many books did Allah send down?" He said: "One hundred and four books. Allah sent down to Shith fifty scrolls, to Khanukh thirty scrolls, to Ibrahim ten scrolls, and He sent down to Musa, before the Torah, ten scrolls, and (He sent) the Injil, the Zabur, and the Furqan." He said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, what were the scrolls of Ibrahim?" He said: "They were entirely: O you powerful, afflicted, deceived king, I did not send you to gather the world, some of it upon others, but I sent you to turn away from Me the supplication of the oppressed, for I do not reject it even if it comes from a disbeliever. And in them was a parable: a wise person should have times: a time in which he communes with his Lord, a time in which he takes account of his soul, a time in which he reflects on the handiwork of Allah, and a time in which he is alone for his needs of food and drink. And a wise person should not be hostile except for three things: provision for the Hereafter, repair of livelihood, or pleasure that is not forbidden. And a wise person should be aware of his time, attentive to his affairs, and guarding his tongue. Whoever counts his speech as part of his deeds will speak little, except about what concerns him." He said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, what were the scrolls of Musa?" He said: "They were entirely lessons: I wonder at one who is certain of death and yet rejoices; I wonder at one who is certain of divine decree and yet toils; I wonder at one who sees the world and its turning over its people and yet is at ease with it; and I wonder at one who is certain of the reckoning tomorrow and yet does not act." He said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, is there anything in our hands from what was in the hands of Ibrahim and Musa, and what Allah sent down to you?" He said: "Yes. Recite, O Abu Dharr: ﴿He has certainly succeeded who purifies himself, and remembers the name of his Lord and prays. Rather, you prefer the worldly life, while the Hereafter is better and more lasting. Indeed, this is in the former scriptures, the scriptures of Ibrahim and Musa﴾ [Al-A'la: 14–19]."

He said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, advise me." He said: "I advise you to have fear of Allah, for it is the head of your affair."

He said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, increase (my knowledge) for me." He said: "Upon you is recitation of the Qur'an and remembrance of Allah, for it is a remembrance for you in the heavens and a light for you on the earth."

He said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, increase (my knowledge) for me." He said: "Beware of excessive laughter, for it kills the heart and takes away the light of the face." I said: "Increase for me." He said: "Upon you is jihad, for it is the monasticism of my Ummah." I said: "Increase for me." He said: "Upon you is silence except for good, for it repels Satan and is a help for you in the matter of your religion."

I said: "Increase for me." He said: "Look at one who is below you, and do not look at one who is above you, for that is more fitting for you so that you do not belittle the blessing of Allah upon you."

I said: "Increase for me." He said: "Love the poor and sit with them, for that is more fitting that you do not belittle the blessing of Allah upon you." I said: "Increase for me." He said: "Maintain your kinship ties even if they sever them from you." I said: "Increase for me." He said: "Speak the truth even if it is bitter."

I said: "Increase for me." He said: "Do not fear the blame of any blamer in (the cause of) Allah."

I said: "Increase for me." He said: "Let what you know about yourself keep you from (criticizing) people, and do not seek fault in them for what you love (in yourself). It is enough of a defect for you that you know from people what you are ignorant of in yourself, or that you seek fault in them for what you love."

Then he struck my chest with his hand and said: "O Abu Dharr, there is no intellect like forethought, no piety like restraint, and no lineage like good character."

[Al-Shari'a of al-Ajurri (p. 404). In its chain is Ibrahim ibn Hisham al-Ghassani, whom Abu Hatim and Abu Zur'a declared a liar, and he is the only one who narrated it from his father, from his grandfather.]

Imam Ahmad narrated from Abu al-Mughira, from Mu'an ibn Rifa'a, from Ali ibn Yazid, from al-Qasim, from Abu Umama, that Abu Dharr asked the Prophet (ﷺ), and he mentioned the matter of prayer, fasting, charity, the excellence of the Verse of the Throne, "there is no power and no strength except with Allah," the best of martyrs, the best of slaves (freed), the prophethood of Adam, that he was spoken to, and the number of prophets and messengers, similar to what has preceded.

[Al-Musnad (5/265).]

Abdullah ibn Imam Ahmad said: I found in my father's book, in his handwriting: Abd al-Muta'ali ibn Abd al-Wahhab narrated to me, Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Umawi narrated to us, Mujalid narrated to us, from Abu al-Wadda, who said: Abu Sa'id said: "Do the Kharijites say that the Dajjal (Antichrist) is real?" I said: "No." He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I am the seal of a thousand prophets or more, and no prophet was sent whose followers were not warned by him about him. And I have been shown what was not shown to anyone. He is one-eyed, and your Lord is not one-eyed. His right eye is blind, bulging, and not hidden, as if it were a spittle on a plastered wall, and his left eye is like a shining star.
