With him is the likeness of every tongue, and with him is the image of Paradise, green, in which water flows, and the image of the Fire, black, smoking."

[Al-Musnad (3/79). Al-Haythami said in Al-Majma' (7/346): "In it is Mujalid ibn Sa'id, whom al-Nasa'i declared reliable in one narration, and in another said: 'not strong.' A group declared him weak."]

This (hadith) has also been narrated to us in the part containing the narration of Abu Ya'la al-Mawsili, from Yahya ibn Ma'in, who said: Marwan ibn Mu'awiya narrated to us, Mujalid narrated to us, from Abu al-Wadda, from Abu Sa'id, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I am sealing a thousand thousand prophets or more. Allah has not sent a prophet to his people except that he warned them of the Dajjal..." and he mentioned the rest of the hadith. This is his wording with the addition of "alf" (thousand), and it may be an interpolation. [Al-Hakim narrated it in Al-Mustadrak (2/597) by the route of Yahya ibn Ma'in, and al-Dhahabi said: Mujalid is weak, and it does not have the addition of "alf," which is an interpolation as the author mentioned.] And Allah knows best. The wording of Imam Ahmad's narration is more established and more deserving of authenticity. The men in the chain of this hadith are acceptable. This hadith has also been narrated through Jabir ibn Abdullah, may Allah be pleased with him. The hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said:

Amr ibn Ali narrated to us, Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us, Mujalid narrated to us, from al-Sha'bi, from Jabir, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I am indeed the seal of a thousand prophets or more, and there is no prophet among them except that he warned his people of the Dajjal. And I have been shown what was not shown to any of them. He is one-eyed, and your Lord is not one-eyed."

[Musnad al-Bazzar, no. 3380, Kashf al-Astar.]

* *

His saying (Most High): ﴿And Allah spoke to Musa directly﴾. This is an honor for Musa, peace be upon him, through this attribute; for this reason he is called "al-Kalim" (the one who was spoken to). The hafiz Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sulayman al-Maliki narrated to us, Masih ibn Hatim narrated to us, Abd al-Jabbar ibn Abd Allah narrated to us, who said: A man came to Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash and said: "I heard a man reciting: 'And Allah spoke to Musa directly.'" Abu Bakr said: "None recites this except a disbeliever. I read it to al-A'mash, al-A'mash read it to Yahya ibn Wathhab, Yahya ibn Wathhab read it to Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, Abu Abd al-Rahman read it to Ali ibn Abi Talib, and Ali ibn Abi Talib read it to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): ﴿And Allah spoke to Musa directly﴾."

[Al-Tabarani narrated it in Al-Awsat (no. 3325), Majma' al-Bahrayn, by the route of Masih ibn Hatim. Al-Tabarani said: "No one narrated it from al-A'mash except Abu Bakr; Abd al-Jabbar ibn Abd Allah is alone in it, I do not know him, and the rest of its narrators are reliable."]

Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash, may Allah have mercy on him, was extremely angry at the one who recited this way, because he distorted the wording and meaning of the Qur'an. This was from the Mu'tazila, who deny that Allah spoke to Musa, peace be upon him, or speaks to any of His creation. Similarly, it has been related to us that one of the Mu'tazila recited to one of the shaykhs: "And Allah spoke to Musa directly," and he said to him: "O son of the wretched (ibn al-lakhna'), how will you deal with His saying, Most High: ﴿And when Musa came at Our appointed time and his Lord spoke to him﴾ [Al-A'raf: 143]?" Meaning: this does not admit distortion or interpretation.

Ibn Mardawayh said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Ahmad ibn al-Husayn ibn Bahram narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Marzuq narrated to us, Hani ibn Yahya narrated to us, from al-Hasan ibn Abi Ja'far, from Qatada, from Yahya ibn Wathhab, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When Allah spoke to Musa, he could see the crawling of an ant on the rock in a dark night." This is a strange hadith, and its chain is not authentic. If it is authentic as a statement of a Companion (mawquf), it is good.

[Al-Tabarani narrated it in Al-Mu'jam al-Saghir (no. 77) by the route of Ahmad ibn al-Husayn ibn Bahram. Al-Haythami said in Al-Majma' (8/203): "In it is al-Husayn ibn Abi Ja'far al-Jafri, who is abandoned (matruk)."]

Ibn Kathir's commentary on Surah 4, verses 163–165 (part 3 of 3):

Al-Hakim related in his Mustadrak, and Ibn Mardawayh, from the hadith of Humayd ibn Qays al-A'raj, from Abdullah ibn al-Harith, from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When your Lord spoke to Musa, Musa had on a woolen robe (jubbat suf), a woolen cloak (kisa' suf), woolen trousers (sarawil suf), and two sandals of donkey hide that had not been tanned." [[Al-Mustadrak (2/379). It was also related by al-Tirmidhi in his Sunan, no. 1734, through the route of Humayd al-A'raj.
Al-Hakim said: "It meets the conditions of al-Bukhari." Al-Dhahabi criticised him, saying: "Rather, it does not meet his conditions. What deceived him is that its chain contains Humayd ibn Qays, and that is an error. It is Humayd al-A'raj al-Kufi, son of Ali or son of Ammar, one of those who are abandoned (matrukun), and he thought he was the Meccan, the truthful one."]]

Ibn Mardawayh also said, with his chain, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Allah conversed with Musa with one hundred thousand and forty thousand words, over three days, all of them admonitions. When Musa heard the speech of the children of Adam, he despised them because of what had reached his ears of the speech of the Lord, Mighty and Majestic.

This chain is also weak, for Juwaybir is weak, and al-Dahhak did not meet Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him.

As for the report related by Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh and others through the route of al-Fadl ibn Isa al-Raqqashi, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Jabir ibn Abdullah, who said: When Allah spoke to Musa on the Mount of Tur, He spoke to him with other than the speech with which He had spoken to him on the day He called him. Musa said to Him: "O Lord, is this Your speech with which You spoke to me?" He said: "No, O Musa. I spoke to you with the strength of ten thousand tongues, and I have the strength of all tongues, and I am stronger than that." When Musa returned to the Children of Israel, they said: "O Musa, describe to us the speech of the Merciful." He said: "I cannot." They said: "Then liken it for us." He said: "Have you not heard the sound of thunderbolts? They are close to it, yet it is not it."

This chain is weak, for this al-Fadl al-Raqqashi is extremely weak.

Abd al-Razzaq said: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from Abu Bakr ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Harith, from Jaz' ibn Jabir al-Khath'ami, from Ka'b, who said: When Allah spoke to Musa, He spoke to him in all tongues apart from His own speech. Musa said to Him: "O Lord, is this Your speech?" He said: "No. Even if I had spoken to you with My speech, you would not have been able to bear it." He said: "O Lord, is there any of Your creation that resembles Your speech?" He said: "No. The creature most like My speech is the most intense of the thunderbolts you hear."

This is a report halted at Ka'b al-Ahbar (mawquf), and he is relating from the earlier books that contain the narratives of the Children of Israel, in which there is both the worthless and the valuable.

* *

As for His saying, ﴿Messengers as bringers of good tidings and as warners﴾, meaning: they give glad tidings to whoever obeys Allah and follows His good pleasure with good things, and they warn whoever opposes His command and denies His messengers with punishment and torment.

* *

As for His saying, ﴿So that mankind will have no argument against Allah after the messengers. And Allah is ever Exalted in Might and Wise﴾, meaning: He, the Exalted, sent down His scriptures and dispatched His messengers with good tidings and warning, and explained what He loves and is pleased with, and what He dislikes and rejects, so that no excuse remains for one who makes excuses, as He said, the Exalted: ﴿And if We had destroyed them with a punishment before it, they would have said, "Our Lord, why did You not send to us a messenger so we could follow Your verses before we were humiliated and disgraced?"﴾ [Ta-Ha: 134]. Likewise His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And if not that a misfortune should strike them for what their hands have sent forth, they would say, "Our Lord, why did You not send to us a messenger so we could follow Your verses and be among the believers?"﴾ [Al-Qasas: 47].

It is established in the two Sahihs [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4634, and Sahih Muslim, no. 2760.]] from Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "There is no one more jealous (aghyar) than Allah; for this reason He forbade indecencies, both what is apparent of them and what is hidden. And there is no one who loves praise more than Allah; for this reason He praised Himself. And there is no one who loves excuse more than Allah; for this reason He sent the Prophets as bringers of good tidings and warners." In another wording: "For this reason He sent His messengers and sent down His scriptures."

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 4, verse 166–170:

When His saying, ﴿Indeed, We have revealed to you as We revealed to Noah and the prophets after him﴾ up to the end of the context, included the affirmation of his prophethood (ﷺ) [[In A: "with his prophethood, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him."]] and the refutation of those among the polytheists and the People of the Book who denied his prophethood, Allah the Exalted said: ﴿But Allah bears witness to what He has sent down to you﴾. That is: even if whoever disbelieved in it among those who denied you and opposed you disbelieves, Allah bears witness for you that you are His Messenger, to whom He sent down the Book, which is the Great Qur'an, ﴿falsehood cannot approach it from before it or from behind it; it is a revelation from One Wise and Praiseworthy﴾ [Fussilat: 42]. Therefore He said: ﴿He has sent it down with His knowledge﴾. That is: within it is His knowledge, which He wished to make the servants aware of, of the clear proofs, guidance, and criterion, and what Allah loves and is pleased with, and what He dislikes and rejects, and what it contains of knowledge of the unseen, of the past and the future, and what it contains of the mention of His holy attributes, which no prophet sent nor any near-stationed angel knows, except what Allah informs him of, as He said: ﴿And they do not encompass anything of His knowledge except what He wills﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 255], and He said: ﴿and they do not encompass it in knowledge﴾ [Taha: 110].

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, al-Hasan ibn Sahl al-Ja'fari and Khazaz ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, both said: Imran ibn Uyaynah narrated to us, Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib narrated to us, he said: Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami taught me the Qur'an, and whenever one of us recited the Qur'an to him he would say: "You have taken the knowledge of Allah; there is no one today more excellent than you except by action," then he would recite: ﴿He has sent it down with His knowledge, and the angels bear witness, and sufficient is Allah as a witness﴾. And His saying ﴿and the angels bear witness﴾ means: to the truth of what came to you, was revealed to you, and was sent down upon you, along with Allah the Exalted's testimony to you of that, ﴿and sufficient is Allah as a witness﴾.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said, from Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, from Ikrimah or Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: A group of Jews entered upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he said to them: "Indeed I know—by Allah—that you know that I am the Messenger of Allah." They said: "We do not know that." So Allah the Mighty and Majestic revealed: ﴿But Allah bears witness to what He has sent down to you; He has sent it down with His knowledge [and the angels bear witness, and sufficient is Allah as a witness]﴾ [[From A, and in H: "the verse."]].

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieved and averted [others] from the way of Allah have certainly strayed far astray﴾. That is: they disbelieved within themselves, so they did not follow the truth, and they strove to turn people away from following it and emulating it. They have departed from the truth and strayed from it, and gone far from it, a great and distant remoteness.

Then Allah the Exalted informed of His ruling regarding those who disbelieve in His signs, His Book, and His Messenger, wronging themselves thereby and by averting from His way and committing its sins and violating its sanctities: that He will not forgive them, ﴿nor will He guide them to a path﴾, that is, a way to good, ﴿except the path of Hell﴾, and this is a disconnected exception, ﴿abiding therein forever [and that is ever easy for Allah]﴾ [[From A.]].

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿O mankind, there has certainly come to you the Messenger with the truth from your Lord, so believe; it is better for you﴾. That is: Muhammad (ﷺ) has certainly come to you with guidance, the religion of truth, and the healing explanation from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, so believe in what he has brought you and follow him; it will be better for you.

Then He said: ﴿But if you disbelieve, then indeed to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth﴾. That is: He is free of need of you and of your faith, and He is not harmed by your disbelief, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And Moses said, "If you disbelieve, you and whoever is on earth entirely, then indeed Allah is Free of need, Praiseworthy"﴾ [Ibrahim: 8]. And here He said: ﴿And ever is Allah Knowing and Wise﴾. That is: of who among you deserves guidance so He guides him, and of who deserves misguidance so He misguides him. ﴿Wise﴾ means: in His statements, His actions, His legislation, and His decree.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, al-Hasan ibn Sahl al-Ja'fari and Khazaz ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, both said: Imran ibn Uyaynah narrated to us, Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib narrated to us, he said: Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami taught me the Qur'an, and whenever one of us recited the Qur'an to him he would say: "You have taken the knowledge of Allah; there is no one today more excellent than you except by action," then he would recite: ﴿He has sent it down with His knowledge, and the angels bear witness, and sufficient is Allah as a witness﴾. And His saying ﴿and the angels bear witness﴾ means: to the truth of what came to you, was revealed to you, and was sent down upon you, along with Allah the Exalted's testimony to you of that, ﴿and sufficient is Allah as a witness﴾.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said, from Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, from Ikrimah or Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: A group of Jews entered upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he said to them: "Indeed I know—by Allah—that you know that I am the Messenger of Allah." They said: "We do not know that." So Allah the Mighty and Majestic revealed: ﴿But Allah bears witness to what He has sent down to you; He has sent it down with His knowledge [and the angels bear witness, and sufficient is Allah as a witness]﴾ [[From A, and in H: "the verse."]].

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieved and averted [others] from the way of Allah have certainly strayed far astray﴾. That is: they disbelieved within themselves, so they did not follow the truth, and they strove to turn people away from following it and emulating it. They have departed from the truth and strayed from it, and gone far from it, a great and distant remoteness.

Then Allah the Exalted informed of His ruling regarding those who disbelieve in His signs, His Book, and His Messenger, wronging themselves thereby and by averting from His way and committing its sins and violating its sanctities: that He will not forgive them, ﴿nor will He guide them to a path﴾, that is, a way to good, ﴿except the path of Hell﴾, and this is a disconnected exception, ﴿abiding therein forever [and that is ever easy for Allah]﴾ [[From A.]].

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿O mankind, there has certainly come to you the Messenger with the truth from your Lord, so believe; it is better for you﴾. That is: Muhammad (ﷺ) has certainly come to you with guidance, the religion of truth, and the healing explanation from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, so believe in what he has brought you and follow him; it will be better for you.

Then He said: ﴿But if you disbelieve, then indeed to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth﴾. That is: He is free of need of you and of your faith, and He is not harmed by your disbelief, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And Moses said, "If you disbelieve, you and whoever is on earth entirely, then indeed Allah is Free of need, Praiseworthy"﴾ [Ibrahim: 8]. And here He said: ﴿And ever is Allah Knowing and Wise﴾. That is: of who among you deserves guidance so He guides him, and of who deserves misguidance so He misguides him. ﴿Wise﴾ means: in His statements, His actions, His legislation, and His decree.

He, may He be exalted, forbids the People of the Book from exaggeration (*ghuluww*) and excessive praise (*iṭrā'*). This is common among the Christians, for they went beyond the bounds of affirming Jesus, until they raised him above the rank that Allah had granted him. They moved him from the sphere of prophethood to the point of taking him as a god besides Allah, worshipping him as they worship Him. Moreover, they exaggerated regarding his followers and adherents, those who claimed to be upon his religion. They ascribed infallibility (*'iṣma*) to them and followed them in everything they said, whether it was true or false, misguidance or right guidance, correct or a lie. For this reason He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿They took their rabbis and their monks as lords besides Allah, and [also] the Messiah, son of Mary. Yet they were commanded only to worship one God. There is no god except Him. Glorified is He above what they associate with Him.﴾ [At-Tawbah: 31].

Imam Ahmad said: Hushaim narrated to us, saying: Az-Zuhri claimed, from 'Ubaydullah ibn 'Abdullah ibn 'Utbah ibn Mas'ud, from Ibn 'Abbas, from 'Umar, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Do not overpraise me as the Christians overpraised Jesus, son of Mary. I am only a servant of Allah and His Messenger."

Then he (Ahmad) and 'Ali ibn al-Madini narrated it from Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah, from az-Zuhri, likewise. 'Ali ibn al-Madini said: "This is a sound hadith in its chain (*sanaduhu*)." [In A: "musnad".] Likewise al-Bukhari narrated it from al-Humaydi, from Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah, from az-Zuhri, with it, and its wording is: "I am only a servant, so say: 'the servant of Allah and His Messenger.'" [Musnad (1/23, 24) and Sahih al-Bukhari no. (3445).]

Imam Ahmad also said: Hasan ibn Musa narrated to us, saying: Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Thabit al-Bunani, from Anas ibn Malik, that a man said: "Muhammad, O our master and son of our master, and our best and son of our best!" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "O people, stick to your words, and let not Satan lead you astray. I am Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah, the servant of Allah and His Messenger. By Allah, I do not like that you raise me above my station which Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has placed me." Ahmad alone narrated it through this route. [Musnad (3/153), and it is according to the condition of Muslim.]

* *

His saying: ﴿And do not say about Allah except the truth﴾ means: do not fabricate against Him and do not ascribe to Him a consort or a son. — Allah is exalted far above that, high beyond measure — and He is glorified, sanctified, and singled out in His lordship, majesty, and greatness. — There is no god but Him, and no lord besides Him. For this reason He said: ﴿The Messiah, Jesus, son of Mary, was only a messenger of Allah and His word which He directed to Mary and a spirit from Him.﴾ That is: he is only a servant of Allah's servants and a creation of His creatures. He said to him "Be," and he was. And he was a messenger of His messengers. And His word, which He directed to Mary, means: He created him by the word with which He sent Gabriel, upon him be peace, to Mary. So he breathed into her from His spirit by the permission of her Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, and Jesus came into being by the permission of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. That breath which he blew into the collar of her garment descended until it entered her private part, in the manner of the father's seed (*liqāḥ*) to the mother. Everything is created by Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. For this reason it was said of Jesus that he is the word of Allah and a spirit from Him, because he had no father from whom he was born; rather, he came into being from the word by which He said to him "Be," and he was. And the spirit with which Gabriel was sent. Allah, may He be exalted, said: ﴿The Messiah, son of Mary, was only a messenger; messengers had passed before him, and his mother was a truthful woman. They both used to eat food.﴾ [Al-Ma'idah: 75]. He, may He be exalted, also said: ﴿Indeed, the likeness of Jesus with Allah is like the likeness of Adam. He created him from dust, then said to him, "Be," and he is.﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 59]. And He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And [mention] she who guarded her chastity, so We breathed into her of Our spirit and made her and her son a sign for the worlds.﴾ [Al-Anbiya': 91]. And He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And Mary, daughter of 'Imran, who guarded her chastity, so We breathed into it of Our spirit, and she believed in the words of her Lord and His scriptures, and she was among the devoutly obedient.﴾ [At-Tahrim: 12] [Addition from R and A; in H: "the verse".]. And He, may He be exalted, said, reporting about the Messiah: ﴿He was not but a servant upon whom We bestowed favor, and We made him an example for the Children of Israel.﴾ [Az-Zukhruf: 59] [Addition from R and A; in H: "the verse".].

'Abd ar-Razzaq said, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿And His word which He directed to Mary﴾ is like His saying: "Be," and he was. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn Sinan al-Wasiti narrated to us, saying: I heard Shadhdh ibn Yahya say concerning the saying of Allah: ﴿And His word which He directed to Mary and a spirit from Him﴾: "The word did not become Jesus; rather, through the word Jesus came into being."

This is better than what Ibn Jarir [Tafsir al-Tabari (9/418)] claimed concerning His saying: ﴿which He directed to Mary﴾, meaning: He informed her of it, as he claimed concerning His saying: ﴿When the angels said, "O Mary, indeed Allah gives you good tidings of a word from Him"﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 45], meaning: He informs you of a word from Him, and He makes that like what He said, exalted is He: ﴿And you did not expect that the Book would be delivered to you, except as a mercy from your Lord﴾ [Al-Qasas: 86]. Rather, the correct view is that it is the word which Gabriel brought to Mary, and he breathed into her by the permission of Allah, and so Jesus, upon him be peace, came into being.

Al-Bukhari said: Sadaqah ibn al-Fadl narrated to us, saying: al-Walid narrated to us, saying: al-Awza'i narrated to us, saying: 'Umayr ibn Hani' narrated to me, saying: Junadah ibn Abi Umayyah narrated to me, from 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "Whoever testifies that there is no god but Allah alone, with no partner, and that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger, and that Jesus is the servant of Allah and His Messenger, and His word which He directed to Mary, and a spirit from Him, and that Paradise is true and the Fire is true, Allah will admit him into Paradise according to whatever deeds he had." Al-Walid said: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Yazid ibn Jabir narrated to me, from 'Umayr ibn Hani', from Junadah, adding: "from whichever of the eight gates of Paradise he wishes."

Likewise Muslim narrated it from Dawud ibn Rashid, from al-Walid, from Ibn Jabir, with it. [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (3435) and Sahih Muslim no. (28).] And by another route, from al-Awza'i, with it. [Sahih Muslim no. (28).]

So His saying in the verse and the hadith: ﴿and a spirit from Him﴾ is like His saying: ﴿And He subjected to you whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, all from Him﴾ [Al-Jathiyah: 13]. That is: from His creation and from His presence. The "min" (from) here is not partitive, as the Christians say — upon them be the continuous curses of Allah — rather it indicates the starting point (*ibtidā' al-ghāyah*), as in the other verse.

Mujahid said concerning His saying: ﴿and a spirit from Him﴾: meaning "and a messenger from Him." Others said: "and a mercy from Him." The more apparent is the first: that he was created from a created spirit, and the spirit was attributed to Allah as a mark of honor, just as the she-camel and the House were attributed to Allah, in His saying: ﴿This is the she-camel of Allah﴾ [Hud: 64], and His saying: ﴿Purify My House for those who circumambulate﴾ [Al-Hajj: 26], and as in the sound hadith: "Then I enter upon my Lord in His house," attributing it to Him as an attribution of honor for it. All of this is of one kind and one pattern.

* *

His saying: ﴿So believe in Allah and His messengers﴾ means: affirm that Allah is one, the Unique, having no consort and no son, and know and be certain that Jesus is the servant of Allah and His Messenger. For this reason He said: ﴿And do not say, "Three."﴾ That is: do not make Jesus and his mother partners with Allah. Allah is exalted far above that, high beyond measure.

This verse and the one that comes in Surah al-Ma'idah, where He, may He be exalted, says: ﴿They have certainly disbelieved who say, "Indeed, Allah is the third of three," and there is no god except one God﴾ [Al-Ma'idah: 73]. And as He said at the end of the mentioned surah: ﴿And [beware the Day] when Allah will say, "O Jesus, son of Mary, did you say to the people, 'Take me and my mother as two gods besides Allah?'" He will say, "Exalted are You! [Addition from R, A.]﴾ — the verse. [Al-Ma'idah: 116]. And He said at its beginning: ﴿They have certainly disbelieved who say, "Indeed, Allah is the Messiah, son of Mary"﴾ — the verse [Al-Ma'idah: 72]. So the Christians — upon them be the curse of Allah — out of their ignorance have no fixed standard, and their disbelief has no limit. Rather, their statements and their misguidance are widespread. Among them are those who believe him to be a god, among them those who believe him to be a partner, and among them those who believe him to be a son. They are many sects with differing opinions and incompatible statements. Some of the scholars (*mutakallimūn*) have aptly said: "If ten Christians gathered, they would split into eleven opinions."

Some of their well-known scholars, namely Sa'id ibn Bitriq, the Patriarch of Alexandria, around the year four hundred after the Prophetic migration, mentioned that they gathered in the great assembly (*majma'*) in which they drew up the great "creed" (*amānah*) which they have — and it is in fact a small, petty betrayal — and that was in the days of Constantine, builder of the famous city. They disagreed among themselves in an uncontrollable and unlimited disagreement, so that they were more than two thousand bishops (*asqufs*), forming many factions: every fifty of them were upon one doctrine, twenty upon one doctrine, a hundred upon one doctrine, seventy upon one doctrine, and more or fewer than that. When a group of them, who had exceeded three hundred by eighteen persons, saw that they had agreed upon one doctrine, the king took it, supported and strengthened it — he was a philosopher of great bearing — and he eradicated all the other statements. The "creed" of those three hundred and eighteen was established, churches were built for them, and they composed books and canons for them. They introduced the creed which they teach to young children, so that they would believe it, and they baptize them upon it. The followers of these are the Melkites. Then they gathered a second assembly, and the Jacobites arose among them; then a third assembly, and the Nestorians arose among them. All these sects affirm the three hypostases (*aqānīm*) in the Messiah, and they differ concerning the manner of this, and concerning divinity (*lāhūt*) and humanity (*nāsūt*) according to their claim: Did the two unite, or did they not unite? Did they blend, or did it dwell within him? — on three doctrines. Each of them declares the other sect to be unbelieving, and we declare all three to be unbelieving.

For this reason He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿Cease — it is better for you.﴾ That is: let it be better for you. ﴿Indeed, Allah is but one God; exalted is He above having a son.﴾ That is: exalted and sanctified is He far above that, high beyond measure. ﴿To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And sufficient is Allah as Disposer of affairs.﴾

That is: all of it is His possession and His creation, and all that is in them are His servants, who are under His management and control, and He is Guardian over all things. So how could there be for Him from them a consort or a son? As He said in another verse: ﴿Originator of the heavens and the earth; how could He have a son when there is not for Him a companion, and He created all things, and He is, of all things, Knowing?﴾ [Al-An'am: 101] [Addition from R, A; in H: "the verse".]. And He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And they say, "The Most Merciful has taken a son." You have certainly produced a terrible thing. [The heavens almost split from it, the earth splits open, and the mountains collapse in ruin, that they attribute to the Most Merciful a son. And it is not befitting for the Most Merciful to take a son. There is none in the heavens and the earth but that he comes to the Most Merciful as a servant. He has enumerated them and counted them with a precise counting. And all of them will come to Him on the Day of Resurrection, alone.]﴾ [Maryam: 88–95] [Addition from R, A; in H: "up to His saying: 'alone'".].

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 4, verse 172–173:

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn Musa narrated to us, Hisham narrated to us, from Ibn Juraij, from ʿAṭāʾ, from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding His saying: ﴿The Messiah will never disdain to be a servant of Allah﴾, that he would never be arrogant.

Qatadah said: ﴿The Messiah will never disdain to be a servant of Allah, nor will the angels brought near [to Allah]﴾, meaning, he will never feel shy. Some of those who hold that the angels are superior to humans have used this verse as evidence, since He said: ﴿nor will the angels brought near﴾. However, there is no proof in it for that, because He only mentioned the angels after the Messiah because disdaining (istinkaf) means refusing, and the angels are more capable of that than the Messiah. Therefore He said: ﴿nor will the angels brought near﴾. Yet being stronger and more capable of refusing does not necessarily make them superior.

It was also said: They were mentioned only because they were taken as gods alongside Allah, just as the Messiah was taken [as a god]. So Allah, exalted is He, informed that they are servants among His servants and creatures among His creation, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And they say, "The Most Merciful has taken a son." Exalted is He! Rather, they are [but] honored servants. They do not precede Him in speech, and they act by His command. He knows what is before them and what is behind them, and they do not intercede except for one whom He approves, and they are, out of fear of Him, apprehensive. And whoever of them should say, "Indeed, I am a deity other than Him," then such We will recompense with Hell. Thus do We recompense the wrongdoers﴾ [al-Anbiya' 26–29].

Then He said: ﴿And whoever disdains His worship and is arrogant – He will gather them to Himself all together﴾, meaning: He will assemble them to Himself on the Day of Resurrection and will judge between them with His just judgment, in which there is no injustice and no wrongdoing. Therefore He said: ﴿As for those who believed and did righteous deeds, He will give them their rewards in full and will increase them from His bounty﴾, meaning: He will give them reward in accordance with their righteous deeds, and will increase them beyond that from His bounty, His grace, the vastness of His mercy, and His generosity.

Ibn Mardawayh narrated through the route of Baqiyyah, from Isma'il ibn 'Abd Allah al-Kindi, from al-A'mash, from Sufyan [in A: "Shaqiq"], from ʿAbd Allah who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: ﴿He will give them their rewards in full and will increase them from His bounty﴾ – "Their rewards: He will admit them to Paradise." ﴿And will increase them from His bounty﴾ – "Intercession for those who were deserving of the Fire, from among those who had shown them kindness in their worldly life" [in A: "in the world"].

This is a chain that is not established. If it is narrated from Ibn Mas'ud as a statement of his own (mawquf), then it is good. [Al-Tabarani narrated it in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (10/248) through the route of Baqiyyah from Isma'il al-Kindi with the same.

Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (7/13): "In it is Isma'il ibn 'Abd Allah al-Kindi, whom al-Dhahabi declared weak on his own account, saying: he brought a munkar report; and the rest of its narrators are deemed trustworthy."

Abu Nu'aym narrated it in al-Hilyah (4/108) through the route of Ibn Humayr from al-Thawri from Shaqiq from ʿAbd Allah ibn Mas'ud with similar wording, and said: "Gharib from the hadith of al-A'mash; 'aziz 'ajib from the hadith of al-Thawri; Isma'il ibn 'Ubayd Allah al-Kindi alone narrated it from al-A'mash, and from Isma'il, Baqiyyah ibn al-Walid narrated it; and we have not written the hadith of al-Thawri except from this shaykh."]

﴿And as for those who disdained and were arrogant﴾, meaning: they refused to obey Allah and worship Him and were arrogant about that, ﴿He will punish them with a painful punishment, and they will not find for themselves besides Allah any protector or helper﴾. As Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, those who are too arrogant to worship Me will enter Hell disgraced﴾ [Ghafir: 60], meaning: humiliated, belittled, abased, just as they were refusing and arrogant.

Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim, on Surah an-Nisa' 4:174–175:

Allah, the Exalted, says, addressing all of mankind and informing them that there has come to them from Him a great proof (burhan), which is the decisive evidence that removes every excuse and the argument that dispels every doubt. Therefore He said: ﴿And We have sent down to you a manifest light﴾, meaning a clear radiance upon the truth. Ibn Jurayj and others said: It is the Qur'an.

﴿As for those who believed in Allah and held fast to Him﴾, meaning they combined the station of worship with reliance upon Allah in all their affairs. Ibn Jurayj said: They believed in Allah and held fast to the Qur'an. Ibn Jarir narrated it.

﴿Then He will admit them to mercy from Him and bounty﴾, meaning He will show them mercy, admitting them to Paradise, increasing them in reward, multiplying it, and raising them in ranks, out of His bounty toward them and His kindness to them. ﴿And guide them to Himself on a straight path﴾, meaning a clear, direct, upright, and moderate way, with no crookedness or deviation in it. This is the description of the believers in this world and the Hereafter: in this world they are upon the path of uprightness and the way of safety in all beliefs and deeds, and in the Hereafter they are upon the straight path of Allah that leads to the gardens of Paradise.

In the hadith of al-Harith al-A'war, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib (radiya Allahu 'anhu), from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he said: "The Qur'an is the straight path of Allah and the firm rope of Allah." The full hadith has already been mentioned at the beginning of the tafsir, and to Allah belongs all praise and grace.

Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim, on Surah an-Nisa' 4:174–175:

This is the description of the believers in this world and the Hereafter: in this world they are upon the path of uprightness and the way of safety in all beliefs and deeds, and in the Hereafter they are upon the straight path of Allah that leads to the gardens of Paradise.

In the hadith of al-Harith al-A'war, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib (radiya Allahu 'anhu), from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he said: "The Qur'an is the straight path of Allah and the firm rope of Allah." The full hadith has already been mentioned at the beginning of the tafsir, and to Allah belongs all praise and grace.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 4, verse 176 (part 1 of 2):

Al-Bukhari said: Sulayman ibn Harb narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, who said: I heard al-Bara' say: "The last surah to be revealed was Bara'ah (Surat al-Tawbah), and the last verse to be revealed was ﴿They ask you for a ruling﴾." [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (2605).]]

And Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, who said: I heard Jabir ibn Abdullah say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered upon me while I was ill and had lost my senses. He performed wudu', then poured (water) over me, or said: "Pour it over him." I regained my senses and said: "Indeed, none inherits from me except a kalalah. So how is the inheritance?" He said: Then the verse of the inheritance was revealed. [[Gloss: "the verse of the inheritance" (ayat al-fara'id).]]

Both of them (al-Bukhari and Muslim) recorded it in their Sahihs through the narration of Shu'bah. [[Musnad (3/298); Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (6743); Sahih Muslim, no. (1616).]] The group (of compilers) also narrated it through the chain of Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Jabir, with the same wording. [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (6723); Sahih Muslim, no. (1616); Sunan Abu Dawud, no. (2886); Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (2097); Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. (11134); Sunan Ibn Majah, no. (1436).]] In some wordings: Then the verse of the inheritance was revealed: ﴿They ask you for a ruling. Say: Allah gives you a ruling concerning the kalalah﴾, to the end of the verse.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Yazid narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, and Ibn al-Zubayr said: He (meaning Jabir) said: "It was revealed concerning me: ﴿They ask you for a ruling. Say: Allah gives you a ruling concerning the kalalah﴾."

It seems that the meaning of the statement, and Allah knows best, is: ﴿They ask you for a ruling﴾ concerning the kalalah. Say: Allah gives you a ruling concerning it. Thus what is mentioned indicates what is omitted.

The discussion of the kalalah and its derivation has already preceded, and that it is derived from the crown (iklil) that surrounds the head from its sides. For this reason, most of the scholars have explained it as: one who dies while having neither a child nor a parent. Some people say: the kalalah is one who has no child, as this verse indicates: ﴿If a man dies [i.e., perishes] ﴾ [[Addition from manuscript A.]] ﴿leaving no child﴾.

The ruling on the kalalah was unclear to the Commander of the Faithful, Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, as it is established from him in the two Sahihs that he said: "There are three matters I wished that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had made a firm covenant with us about, a definite decision we could rely upon: the grandfather, the kalalah, and some aspects of usury."

Imam Ahmad said: Isma'il narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah, from Qatadah, from Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd, from Ma'dan ibn Abi Talhah, who said: Umar ibn al-Khattab said: "I did not ask the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about anything more often than I asked him about the kalalah, until he struck my chest with his finger and said: 'The verse of summer that is at the end of Surat al-Nisa' will suffice you.'"

Thus he narrated it in abridged form, and Muslim recorded it in a much longer form than this. [[Musnad (1/26); Sahih Muslim, no. (1617).]]

Another chain: Imam Ahmad said: Abu Nu'aym narrated to us, Malik (meaning Ibn Mighl) narrated to us: I heard al-Fadl ibn Amr, from Ibrahim, from Umar, who said: "I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about the kalalah, and he said: 'The verse of summer will suffice you.'" Then he said: "To have asked the Prophet ﷺ about it would be dearer to me than having red camels." This is a good chain, except that there is a break (inqita') between Ibrahim and Umar, for he did not meet him. [[Musnad (1/38).]]

Imam Ahmad also said: Yahya ibn Adam narrated to us, Abu Bakr narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Bara' ibn 'Azib, who said: A man came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and asked him about the kalalah, and he said: "The verse of summer will suffice you." This is a good chain. Abu Dawud and al-Tirmidhi narrated it through the hadith of Abu Bakr ibn 'Ayyash, with the same chain. [[Musnad (4/293); Sunan Abu Dawud, no. (2889); Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (3042).]] It seems that what is meant by "the verse of summer" is that it was revealed in the season of summer, and Allah knows best.

When the Prophet ﷺ guided him to understand it, for it contains sufficiency, he forgot to ask the Prophet ﷺ about its meaning. For this reason he said: "To have asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about it would be dearer to me than having red camels."

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn WakI' narrated to us, Jarir narrated to us, from al-Shaybani, from Amr ibn Murrah, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, who said: Umar ibn al-Khattab asked the Prophet ﷺ about the kalalah, and he said: "Has Allah not already made that clear?" Then the verse was revealed: ﴿They ask you for a ruling. Say: Allah gives you a ruling concerning the kalalah﴾, to the end of the verse. Qatadah said: It was mentioned to us that Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him, said in his sermon: "Beware! The verse that was revealed at the beginning of Surat al-Nisa' concerning the fara'id (the shares of inheritance) was revealed by Allah concerning the child and the parent. The second verse he revealed concerning the husband, the wife, and the brothers from the mother. The verse with which he concluded Surat al-Nisa' he revealed concerning the brothers and sisters from the father and mother, and the verse with which he concluded Surat al-Anfal he revealed concerning those with kinship ties (ulu al-arham): some of them are closer to others in the Book of Allah than the relatives by blood (al-'asabah) are." Ibn Jarir narrated it. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (9/431).]]

Discussion of its meaning, and with Allah is the help sought, and upon Him is reliance:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿If a man dies﴾, meaning: dies. Allah Almighty said: ﴿Everything will perish except His Face﴾ [al-Qasas: 88], meaning everything passes away and does not remain except Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, as He said: ﴿Everyone upon it will perish. And there will remain the Face of your Lord, Full of Majesty and Honor﴾ [al-Rahman: 26, 27].

* *

His saying: ﴿leaving no child﴾. Whoever holds that it is not a condition of the kalalah that there be no parent, but that the absence of a child suffices for the existence of the kalalah, has relied upon this. This is a narration from Umar ibn al-Khattab, which Ibn Jarir transmitted from him with a sound chain to him. However, what the majority adopted, and the judgment of al-Siddiq, is that it is one who has neither child nor parent. This is indicated by His saying: ﴿And he has a sister, so for her is half of what he left﴾. If there were a father with her, she would inherit nothing, because he excludes her by consensus. This indicates that the deceased has no child by the explicit text of the Qur'an, and no parent by the text as well upon reflection, because the sister is not assigned half when there is a parent; rather she has no inheritance at all.

Imam Ahmad said: al-Hakam ibn Nafi' narrated to us, Abu Bakr ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Makhul, 'Atiyyah, Hamzah and Rashid, from Zayd ibn Thabit: that he was asked about a husband and a full sister (from the same father and mother), and he gave the husband half and the sister half. He was challenged about this, and he said: "I was present with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when he decided that."

Ahmad alone narrated it through this route. [[Musnad (5/188).]] Ibn Jarir and others transmitted from Ibn 'Abbas and Ibn al-Zubayr that they used to say concerning a deceased who left a daughter and a sister: the sister has nothing, because of His saying: ﴿If a man dies leaving no child and he has a sister, for her is half of what he left﴾. They said: when he leaves a daughter, he has left a child, so the sister has nothing. The majority disagreed with them, and said in this matter: the daughter has half by fixed share (fard), and the sister has the other half by agnatic residue (ta'sib), by evidence other than this verse; and this is a case in which a share is assigned to her. As for her inheritance by agnatic residue: it is because al-Bukhari narrated through the chain of Sulayman, from Ibrahim, from al-Aswad, who said: Mu'adh ibn Jabal judged among us during the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: half for the daughter and half for the sister. Then Sulayman said: "He judged among us," and did not mention "during the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ." [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (6734).]] Also in Sahih al-Bukhari, from Huzayl ibn Shurahbil, who said: Abu Musa al-Ash'ari was asked about a daughter, a son's daughter, and a sister, and he said: "For the daughter is half, and for the sister is half; go to Ibn Mas'ud, and he will agree with me." Ibn Mas'ud was asked, and was informed of Abu Musa's statement, and he said: "Then I would have gone astray, and I would not be among the guided. I judge concerning it by what the Prophet ﷺ judged: for the daughter half, for the son's daughter a sixth, completing the two-thirds, and what remains is for the sister." We went to Abu Musa and informed him of Ibn Mas'ud's statement, and he said: "Do not ask me as long as this scholar is among you." [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (6736).]]

* *

His saying: ﴿And he inherits her if she has no child﴾, meaning: the brother inherits all of her property if she dies as a kalalah and has no child, that is, no parent either; for if she had a parent, the brother would inherit nothing. If it is assumed that there is with him someone who has a fixed share, his share is given to him, such as a husband or a maternal brother, and the remainder goes to the brother; this is based on what is established in the two Sahihs from Ibn 'Abbas, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Give the fara'id to their people, and whatever remains of the fara'id goes to the nearest male relative."[[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (6735); Sahih Muslim, no. (1615).]]

* *

His saying: ﴿If they were two sisters, then for them are two-thirds of what he left﴾, meaning: if the one who dies as a kalalah has two sisters, two-thirds is assigned to them, and likewise whatever exceeds two sisters is in their ruling. From here the majority derived the ruling for two daughters, just as the ruling for sisters was derived from the daughters in His saying: ﴿If they are women more than two, then for them are two-thirds of what he left﴾.

* *

His saying: ﴿And if they are brothers and sisters, men and women, then for the male is the equivalent of the share of two females﴾. This is the ruling for the agnatic heirs from the sons, the sons' sons, and the brothers, when their males and females combine: the male receives the equivalent of the share of two females.

* *

His saying: ﴿Allah makes clear to you﴾, meaning: He prescribes for you His obligations, sets for you His limits, and clarifies for you His laws.

* *

His saying: ﴿Lest you go astray﴾, meaning: lest you deviate from the truth after the clarification. ﴿And Allah is Knowing of all things﴾, meaning: He knows the consequences of matters, their benefits, and the good in them for His servants, and what each of the relatives deserves according to his closeness to the deceased.

Abu Ja'far Ibn Jarir said: Ya'qub narrated to me, Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to me, Ibn 'Awn informed us, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, who said: They were on a journey, and the rear of Hudhayfah's mount was beside the saddle-rear of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the rear of Umar's mount was beside the saddle-rear of Hudhayfah's mount. He said: And ﴿They ask you for a ruling. Say: Allah gives you a ruling concerning the kalalah﴾ was revealed, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ whispered it to Hudhayfah, and Hudhayfah whispered it to Umar. Later, Umar asked Hudhayfah about it, and he said: "By Allah, you are truly foolish if you thought that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ whispered it to me, and I whispered it to you as he whispered it to me. By Allah, I will never add anything to it for you ever." He said: So Umar used to say: "O Allah, if You made it clear to him, then it has not been made clear to me."

Ibn Jarir narrated this in the same way. He also narrated it from al-Hasan ibn Yahya [[In A: "Muhammad".]], from ʿAbd al-Razzaq, from Maʿmar, from Ayyub, from Ibn Sirin, similarly, with similar wording. It is a broken chain (munqati') between Ibn Sirin and Hudhayfah [[Tafsir al-Tabari (9/435).]]. The Hafiz Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn ʿAmr al-Bazzar said in his Musnad: Yusuf ibn Hammad al-Maʿnii and Muhammad ibn Marzuq narrated to us, both saying: ʿAbd al-Aʿla ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla informed us, Hisham ibn Hassan narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, from Abu ʿUbaydah ibn Hudhayfah, from his father, who said: "The kalalah [[Kalalah: a person who dies leaving neither a father nor a child (ascendant or descendant) as heir.]] was revealed to the Prophet ﷺ while he was on a journey. The Prophet ﷺ stopped, and he saw Hudhayfah, and the head of Hudhayfah's camel was at the waist-wrap of the Prophet ﷺ. He [the Prophet] met it [the question] with him [Hudhayfah]. Hudhayfah looked and it was ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, and he met it with him. When ʿUmar was caliph, ʿUmar considered the kalalah, so he called Hudhayfah and asked him about it. Hudhayfah said: 'The Messenger of Allah ﷺ indeed gave it to me, and I give it to you as he gave it to me. By Allah, I am truthful, and by Allah I will never add anything to that, ever.'"

Al-Bazzar then said: "We do not know anyone who narrated this hadith except Hudhayfah, and we do not know any route for it from Hudhayfah except this route, and no one narrated it from Hisham except ʿAbd al-Aʿla." Ibn Mardawayh similarly narrated it from the hadith of ʿAbd al-Aʿla [[Musnad al-Bazzar, no. 2206 (Kashf al-Astar). Al-Haythami said in al-Majmaʿ (7/13): "Its narrators are the narrators of the Sahih except Abu ʿUbaydah ibn Hudhayfah, and Ibn Hibban declared him trustworthy."]].

ʿUthman ibn Abi Shaybah said: Jarir narrated to us, from al-Shaybani, from ʿAmr ibn Murrah, from Saʿid [that is, Ibn al-Musayyab] [[Addition from R and A.]], that ʿUmar asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "How is the kalalah inherited?" He said: then Allah revealed: ﴿They ask you for a ruling. Say: "Allah gives you a ruling concerning the kalalah"﴾ [[Addition from R and A.]] ﴾ the verse [[In R and A: "to its end".]]. He said: "It seems ʿUmar did not understand. So he said to Hafsah: 'When you see the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in good spirits, ask him about it.' She saw him in good spirits and asked him about it [[In R: "about him".]], and he said: 'Did your father mention this to you? I do not think your father knows it.'" He said: "ʿUmar used to say: 'I do not think I know it, although the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said what he said.'"

Ibn Mardawayh narrated it [[Ishaq ibn Rahawayh also narrated it in his Musnad, as in al-Durr al-Manthur (2/753).]], and then narrated it through Ibn ʿUyaynah, from ʿAmr, from Tawus: that ʿUmar ordered Hafsah to ask the Prophet ﷺ about the kalalah, so he dictated it to her on a shoulder-blade. He said: "Who ordered you to do this? ʿUmar? I do not think he will keep it upright. Is not the verse of summer [[In R: "And".]] enough for him?" Sufyan said: "The verse of summer, which is in al-Nisa', is: ﴿If a man leaves neither ascendant nor descendant as heir, or a woman﴾. When they asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, the verse that is the conclusion of al-Nisa' was revealed, and ʿUmar threw away the shoulder-blade." Thus he said in this hadith, and it is mursal [[Sa'id ibn Mansur narrated it in al-Sunan, no. 587, and ʿAbd al-Razzaq in al-Musannaf, no. 19194, through the route of Sufyan ibn ʿUyaynah.]].

Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, ʿAththam narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Qays ibn Muslim, from Tariq ibn Shihab, who said: "ʿUmar took a shoulder-blade and gathered the companions of the Prophet ﷺ, then said: 'I will surely decide on the kalalah with a ruling that women will talk about in their chambers.' Then a snake came out of the house, and they scattered. He said: 'If Allah, Mighty and Majestic, had wanted to complete this matter, He would have completed it.'" This is a sahih chain [[Tafsir al-Tabari (9/439).]].

Al-Hakim Abu ʿAbd Allah al-Nisaburi said: ʿAli ibn Muhammad ibn ʿUqbah al-Shaybani narrated to us in Kufah, al-Haytham ibn Khalid narrated to us, Abu Nuʿaym narrated to us, Ibn ʿUyaynah narrated to us, from ʿAmr ibn Dinar, I heard Muhammad ibn Talhah ibn Yazid ibn Rukanah narrate from ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab, who said: "To have asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about three things is dearer to me than red camels: who is the successor after him? And about a people who say: 'We pay zakat from our wealth but do not give it to you; is it permissible to fight them?' And about the kalalah." Then he said: "Sahih according to the criteria of the two Shaykhs [al-Bukhari and Muslim], but they did not record it [[Al-Mustadrak (2/303). Al-Dhahabi responded: "Rather, they did not record anything from Muhammad, nor did he meet ʿUmar," so the chain has a break.]]." Then it was narrated with this chain to Sufyan ibn ʿUyaynah, from ʿAmr ibn Murrah, from Murrah, from ʿUmar, who said: "Three things, that the Prophet ﷺ had explained them to us, would be dearer to me than the world and what is in it: the caliphate, the kalalah, and usury (riba)." Then he said: "Sahih according to the criteria of the two Shaykhs, but they did not record it [[Al-Mustadrak (2/304); al-Dhahabi agreed.]]."

With this chain to Sufyan ibn ʿUyaynah, he said: I heard Sulayman al-Ahwal narrate, from Tawus, who said: I heard Ibn ʿAbbas say: "I was the last of the people to meet ʿUmar, and I heard him say: 'The saying is what I said.' I said: 'And what did you say?' He said: 'I said: the kalalah is the one who has no child.'" Then he said: "Sahih according to their criteria, but they did not record it."

In the same way Ibn Mardawayh narrated it through the route of Zamʿah ibn Salih, from ʿAmr ibn Dinar and Sulayman al-Ahwal, from Tawus, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: "I was the last of the people to meet ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab. He said: 'I and Abu Bakr disagreed about the kalalah, and the saying is what I said.'" He said: "It is mentioned that ʿUmar made the brothers of the same father and mother share with the brothers of the mother alone in the third when they gathered, and Abu Bakr disagreed with him, may Allah be pleased with both of them [[In R: "may Allah be pleased with them both".]] [[Al-Mustadrak (2/303). Sa'id ibn Mansur narrated it in al-Sunan, no. 589, from the hadith of Sufyan from Sulayman al-Ahwal.]]."

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Wakiʿ narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Humayd al-Maʿmari [[In R: "al-ʿUmari".]] narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhri, from Saʿid ibn al-Musayyab: that ʿUmar wrote a document concerning the grandfather and the kalalah. He remained seeking Allah's guidance (istikhara) about it, saying: "O Allah, if You know good in it, then carry it out." Until, when he was stabbed, he called for the document and it was erased, and no one knew what he had written in it. He said: "I had written a document concerning the grandfather and the kalalah, and I had sought Allah's guidance about it, and I saw that I should leave you upon what you were upon" [[Tafsir al-Tabari (9/438).]].

Ibn Jarir said: It has also been narrated from ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: "I am indeed ashamed to oppose Abu Bakr in it." It seems that Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, was saying: it is whatever excludes the child and the parent [[Sa'id ibn Mansur narrated it in al-Sunan, no. 591, and from his route al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan al-Kubra (6/224), through the route of Sufyan from ʿAsim from al-Shaʿbi who said: "ʿUmar said" and mentioned it. It is mungati' (broken).]].

What al-Siddiq [Abu Bakr] said is the view upon which the majority of the Companions, the Successors, and the Imams agree, in earlier and later times. It is the position of the four Imams and the seven jurists, and the opinion of the scholars of all the regions. It is also what the Qur'an indicates, as Allah guided that He has made this clear and explained it in His saying: ﴿Allah makes clear to you, lest you go astray, and Allah has knowledge of all things.﴾
